Verified by src/faculties/memory/startup-hydration.test.ts, src/faculties/memory/retrieval.test.ts, full npm test (482 files/4803 tests), npm run lint, and npm run build.

title: P0: Make sleeptime a real sleep/idle cleanup trigger
description:
Summary
Sleeptime is named and conceptually intended as cleanup that happens when the user/room is asleep or idle. Current code treats it as a post-turn action inferred every 3 responded turns and then schedules it for the next rest window. In live alpha this produced pending sleeptime work during active group chat, and that work can rewrite core memory plus run heavy episodic consolidation.

Live evidence from 2026-06-30
- Live /app/companion-data/state/post-turn-actions.queue.json contained memory.sleeptime.run for channel 1486443955561299979 with:
  - cadenceTurn: 3
  - lastUserActivityAtMs: 1782792625008
  - runAt: 1782796225008 (2026-06-30T05:10:25.008Z)
- This was queued during active late-night group chat.
- Scheduler config in live /app/system-data/scheduler.json has episodicProcessing enabled from 00:00 to 09:00 local and inactivityThresholdMinutes=60.

Root cause
- src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts:40 DEFAULT_CADENCE_TURNS = 3.
- src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts:468 increments turnCountBySession for every eligible external message.
- src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts:471 enqueues when nextCount % cadenceTurns === 0.
- src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts:478 computes rest-window eligibility using nowMs equal to the message timestamp and lastUserActivityAtMs equal to the same timestamp, so active chat in the rest-window schedules a future run as soon as the inactivity threshold would be met.
- src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts:502 rechecks rest-window on execute, but the queue is still repeatedly created/refreshed during active conversation.

Required design
- Sleeptime should be driven by actual quiet/idle conditions, not by chat-turn modulo.
- Rest-window and inactivity threshold are hard gates for enqueue, not just execute.
- The action should either be created by a scheduler/idle detector or inferPostTurnAction should only enqueue when the room is already eligible, with anti-loop/dedupe.
- Active conversation should not keep pushing scheduled cleanup actions forward every few turns.
- The implementation should remain asynchronous/background; do not block foreground chat.

Relationship to core-memory scoping
- This bead does not replace scoped core memory. Sleeptime still needs scoped writes from q7tv.1.
- Until scoped writes exist, tests should prevent sleeptime from mutating global core memory in active chat scenarios.

Non-goals
- Do not remove sleeptime/episodic consolidation entirely.
- Do not make timezone-per-user policy here; mixed Euro/Aussie/American group timing is a separate later issue.
- Do not add hardcoded user-specific sleep times.

Failure modes to prevent
- Every 3 turns creates a sleep cleanup action.
- A busy midnight group chat triggers heavy memory cleanup after only a short delay.
- A pending sleeptime action rewrites current prompt identity while users are actively testing the prompt.
- Reboots reload stale queued sleeptime actions and run them without rechecking inactivity/rest-window.
acceptance_criteria:
- Active chat turns below the configured inactivity threshold do not enqueue memory.sleeptime.run.
- Sleeptime enqueue is based on rest-window + inactivity eligibility, not only modulo turn count.
- A quiet rest-window channel can enqueue exactly one due sleeptime action after the configured inactivity threshold.
- Queued sleeptime actions dedupe per channel/session and are not continually pushed forward during active conversation.
- Existing queued actions that are no longer eligible are skipped with telemetry and do not mutate core memory.
- Tests cover active conversation, outside rest window, insufficient inactivity, eligible quiet window, and dedupe.
- Live/default config documents sleep/idle semantics and uses a threshold consistent with cleanup while the user sleeps.
- npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Completed in 416f06a1: sleeptime enqueue now requires rest-window/inactivity eligibility, uses skipFirstRun scheduler task memory.sleeptime.idle-infer, dedupes/skips ineligible runs, and no longer queues every active-chat cadence turn. Verified by src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.test.ts, src/core/scheduler/scheduler.test.ts, src/app/agent/scheduler-runtime.test.ts, full npm test (482 files/4803 tests), npm run lint, and npm run build.

title: P0: Scope core memory and orient/sleeptime mutation by channel
description:
Summary
Core memory is currently global mutable prompt context. One sleeptime run rewrote Carlini's durable core memory into a generic safety-coded "AI assistant" persona and injected that into every channel. This cooked the nun identity because the global <core_memory> block is appended near the bottom of the prompt and overrides/competes with the static character card.

Live evidence from 2026-06-30
- /app/companion-data/state/core_memory.json updated at 2026-06-30T04:31:36Z and contains:
  - persona: "Playful, garden-monastery-themed AI assistant..."
  - human: "Mixed group of monastery Discord users: Vega..., MrDragonFox..., Iki..., djsoapyknuckles..."
  - goals: safety/boundary-coded text.
- Latest live final system prompt for group channel 1486443955561299979 still contains <core_memory> with that assistant-role text.
- This block is not from prompt layers; it is from CoreMemoryStore.formatForContext().

Root cause
- src/faculties/core-memory/store.ts:5 hardcodes CORE_MEMORY_LABELS = ['persona','human','goals'].
- src/faculties/core-memory/store.ts:344 renders one global <core_memory> block with <persona>, <human>, and <goals>.
- src/core/session/manager.ts:1033 calls coreMemoryProvider.formatForContext() without channel/session scope.
- src/app/startup/composition/composition.ts:293 constructs CoreMemoryStore(resolveCoreMemoryPath(companionDataDir)); resolveCoreMemoryPath currently points to companion-data/state/core_memory.json.
- src/faculties/core-memory/tools.ts:453 append, :474 replace, and :504 reorient all mutate that same store.
- src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts:562 reads that same global store and :613 calls coreMemoryStore.rethink(...).

Required design
- Make mutable core memory scoped. Minimum viable scope is current channel/session: channel:<channelId>. This covers Discord group rooms and DMs without participant matrices.
- Room equals room. Do not implement per-participant allow matrices for group core memory.
- A DM can have its own scoped orientation. A group room can have its own scoped orientation. They do not cross.
- Keep stable identity in static prompt/card layers. Scoped core memory is current-scope orientation/context, not canonical identity.
- Preserve the user/operator's prompt layer ordering. This work must not hardcode prompt text or relocate static appearance/persona layers.

Rendering requirements
- Do not render generic <human> in group channels. The current tag is semantically wrong and caused unattributed multi-person noise.
- Group scope can render a room/channel block, for example structured <discord_channel> or <room_context>, with a one-line channel summary and at most 5 recently active participants if available.
- In 1:1 chat, render a contact/user-specific structured tag. If XML names are unsafe, use attributes, e.g. <participant_context name="Vega" platform="discord">, not <human>.
- Do not tell the companion how she feels. Mood/emotion belongs to the emotion system. Scoped core memory may summarize local context, commitments, goals, and continuity only.

Migration requirements
- Existing core_memory.json must not be blindly deleted. Back it up or migrate it into an explicit legacy/global archived scope.
- Do not inject legacy/global archived scope into prompts by default.
- If the old global block contains assistant-role or safety-coded corruption, quarantine it from model-facing context.

Non-goals
- Do not add participant-level memory visibility matrices.
- Do not make channel privacy labels per-user in this bead.
- Do not remove the static appearance section from the base prompt.
- Do not hardcode new prompt wording in TS except structural wrappers required by code; editable prompt text belongs in prompt layers/registry where applicable.

Failure modes to prevent
- A group-channel sleeptime run changes DM persona.
- A DM orient call changes group-channel context.
- A group summary of several people appears as <human> and pollutes a single user's identity.
- Scoped orientation tells Carlini to be an assistant or safety bot instead of preserving the character card.
- Existing global corrupt core memory remains injected into every final system prompt.
acceptance_criteria:
- A core memory snapshot can be read/written by scope key, with at least channel:<channelId> support for Discord rooms and DMs.
- Session prompt assembly renders only the scoped core memory for the current channel/session; unrelated room/DM scoped orientation is absent.
- Existing global core_memory.json is migrated or archived with backup/audit; stale global assistant-role/persona text is not injected into all rooms.
- orient append/replace/reorient targets current scope by default or an explicit validated scope; it cannot silently rewrite global mutable persona/human/goals.
- sleeptime rethinks only the action session/channel scope and includes source channel/session metadata in any memory writes.
- Group prompt output does not contain generic <human>; group scoped context uses room/channel naming and a bounded participant summary.
- DM prompt output uses an actual user/contact-specific label or structured participant tag, not generic <human>.
- Tests prove a group-channel reorientation does not appear in another group room or DM, and a DM reorientation does not appear in a group.
- Tests prove scoped store preserves prompt order/injection position and does not remove static appearance/persona layers.
- npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Completed in 416f06a1: CoreMemoryStore now stores scoped channel records, archives legacy global core memory, renders scoped room/participant context, and SessionManager/orient/sleeptime pass channel scope. Verified by src/faculties/core-memory/store.test.ts, src/faculties/core-memory/tools.test.ts, src/core/session/manager.test.ts, full npm test (482 files/4803 tests), npm run lint, and npm run build.

title: P0: Repair prompt runtime regressions from group-chat pass
description:
Summary
The sprint_9_final group-chat prompt/runtime pass regressed live Carlini prompt generation and runtime context. The live 2026-06-30 shakedown showed the failure as a connected incident, not isolated cosmetic prompt text: global mutable core memory was rewritten into an assistant/safety-coded persona, prompt monitor/loom did not expose the exact provider payload or tools clearly enough to validate the turn, stale tool-result failures were dumped into final system context, post-restart active memory started empty, persisted trust-policy defaults blocked personal memories for regular contacts, deterministic summaries produced clipped line dumps, and model-facing prompt prose existed in TypeScript hardcodes outside editable prompt layers/registry.

Operator history that must be preserved
- The companion is a character/companion, not a generic AI assistant. Runtime systems must not tell her who she is, how she feels, what relationship stance to take, or whether to be friendly/helpful; static character prompt layers and the emotion/relationship systems own those behaviors.
- Prompt JSON/layers and registry/bootstrap defaults are the editable source for model-facing prompt text. Hidden TypeScript prompt prose is not acceptable except for structural wrappers/typed data formatting.
- Room equals room for group memory/core-memory scoping. Do not build participant matrices. A group room scope can be reused in that room; another group room is separate even if membership overlaps. A DM scope is separate and must not leak into groups.
- The prompt-layer ordering and the user's ability to move sections must be preserved. Static/dynamic separation matters for cache stability; volatile runtime data belongs lower in the prompt.
- Carlini's static appearance/persona layer must remain present. Moving/reworking runtime context must not regress selfie/appearance grounding.
- Sleeptime is sleep/idle cleanup. It must not fire every few active chat turns.
- Startup hydration should warm the async memory cache. Do not make ordinary hot turns synchronously retrieve memory as a latency regression.
- Prompt loom is expected to show exactly what the model/provider sees: final system prompt, provider messages, active provider tool definitions, tool calls/results, memory capture input/output, and whether the snapshot is historical or current.

Concrete live evidence from 2026-06-30
- /app/companion-data/state/core_memory.json contained a sleeptime-authored block identifying Carlini as a "Playful, garden-monastery-themed AI assistant" with safety/boundary goals, and that global block appeared near the bottom of the final prompt.
- Live turn records for Discord channel 1486443955561299979 showed memory_chars:0 immediately after restart even though later retrieval traces found candidate memories.
- Live final prompts contained dozens of historical [Tool result:] failure lines, including repeated memory/contact/web errors.
- Live /app/system-data/trust-policy.json had regular limited to [public], while repo seed/runtime policy expect [public, personal].
- Live turn 1521381099152871429 contained observability.snapshot.toolContext.activeTools count=20, but the prompt monitor view did not present that active provider tool list in a usable way.
- Historical turn snapshots still contained removed prompt layers such as runtime_self, model_context, analysis_workbench_guidance, and authenticity/provenance noise; tooling must distinguish old snapshots from current generator output.

Scope
Track and land the concrete repair wave for:
1. Channel-scoped core memory and scoped orient/sleeptime mutation.
2. Sleeptime enqueue semantics based on true sleep/rest-window plus inactivity, not active-turn cadence.
3. Startup active-memory hydration without synchronous retrieval in every foreground turn.
4. Stale historical tool-result filtering/compression plus verification that active provider tools remain visible.
5. One LLM-backed automatic summary path for history/wake summaries, with separate editable prompts allowed for compaction versus recent wake/history.
6. Trust-policy owner-file drift migration for the known old default regular ceiling.
7. Prompt-loom/provider-payload visibility for exact final model input and active provider tools.
8. Removal of model-facing runtime prompt prose from TypeScript hardcodes into prompt registry/bootstrap defaults.

Non-goals
- Do not implement participant-matrix memory visibility.
- Do not move channel privacy labels from per-user to per-channel in this repair wave unless a child bead explicitly scopes it; that is later design work.
- Do not remove or rewrite the static character/persona/appearance layers.
- Do not redesign the entire prompt monitor IA beyond exact-payload visibility needed for validation.
- Do not delete sleeptime/episodic consolidation; fix its trigger semantics and scope.
- Do not silently overwrite custom owner files. Migrations must be narrow, evidence-based, and fail closed for malformed config.

Failure modes this epic must prevent
- A group-room background summary rewrites the companion's DM persona or global identity.
- A DM private/core memory appears in a group prompt.
- A different group room sees another room's scoped core memory because membership overlaps.
- Model-facing prompt text changes through a code deploy hidden from prompt JSON/layers/registry.
- The bottom of the prompt overrides the nun identity with assistant/safety-bot text.
- The first post-restart turn has no memory context despite existing allowed session history.
- Historical tool failures become permanent final system prompt content.
- Prompt monitor shows templates/debug metadata but not the exact provider payload and tools.
- Trust-policy migration widens sensitive access beyond public+personal for regular contacts or overwrites custom policy.
- The worker closes a bead without tests and npm run lint evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- Live final prompt no longer contains global assistant-role core_memory in unrelated channels.
- Core memory mutable orientation is scoped by channel/session context.
- Sleeptime does not run every few chat turns during active conversation.
- First post-restart prompt has active memory context when session history exists, without adding synchronous retrieval to every hot turn.
- Final system prompt no longer includes dozens of stale tool-result failures.
- Automatic history/wake summaries use the LLM-backed summary service, not deterministic line dumps.
- Trust policy regular ceiling is public+personal for default and migrated persisted owner files.
- Model-facing runtime prompts used by sleeptime/core-memory mutation are registry/bootstrap owned, not hidden TypeScript behavioral strings.
- Prompt loom exposes the exact final system prompt, provider messages, and active provider tools for a selected turn.
- npm run lint passes before closing.
close_reason: Completed across commits 416f06a1, 4575215f, 24a3f27c, fa865c78, and 0c5854b6. The repair wave delivered channel-scoped core memory/orient/sleeptime mutation, true sleep/inactivity-gated sleeptime scheduling, startup active-memory hydration, historical tool-entry filtering, LLM-backed recent session summaries, trust-policy drift migration, exact prompt loom/provider payload/tool visibility, prompt-registry-owned runtime summary prompts, immutable amendment static wording, and related live tool-surface fixes. Verified by targeted suites for core memory, sleeptime, startup hydration, session/context support, prompt registry/composer, prompt loom/admin routes, trust policy/settings contract, scratchpad, journal registry parity, and scheduler malformed-call handling; full npm test passed (482 files/4803 tests), npm run lint passed, npm run build passed, verify:settings-contract passed, and verify:repository-hygiene passed.

title: P0: Preserve prompt layer order during system-owned content migrations
description:
Summary
Prompt owner-file migrations and system-owned prompt rewrites must never reset a user/operator's prompt layer ordering. The immediate system_language retired-key migration preserves array order, but ensure/seed normalization paths may still force priority or promptOrder back to defaults while rewriting system-owned content.

Why this matters
The prompt monitor lets operators move prompt layers. Content migrations are allowed to repair old system-owned template bodies, but rewriting content must not undo the operator's layout choices or invalidate prompt ordering/cache assumptions.

Scope
- Audit prompt-layer migration/normalization paths touched by the 745daad4/7b950ba8 work.
- Preserve existing priority and promptOrder when normalizing existing system-owned runtime/system_language layer content.
- Keep default priority/promptOrder only when creating a missing layer from seed.
- Add regression tests proving content rewrite does not change existing priority/promptOrder.

Non-goals
- Do not redesign prompt monitor ordering.
- Do not preserve invalid metadata that fails schema validation; this is about valid user-moved order.
- Do not reintroduce removed prompt text.
acceptance_criteria:
- Existing system_language content normalization preserves the layer's priority and promptOrder.
- Existing runtime seed normalization preserves each layer's priority and promptOrder while updating system-owned content.
- Creating missing seed layers still uses default seed order.
- Tests cover user-moved order surviving content normalization.
- npm run lint passes before closure.
close_reason: Completed in git commit 774a1f9e. Existing prompt layer content rewrites now preserve valid priority and promptOrder instead of resetting operator/user layout. Covered runtime seed normalization, system_language normalization, retired-key load migration, temporal rules normalization, and Character Foundation metadata normalization. Creation of missing seed layers still uses seed/default order. Validation: npm test -- --run src/core/identity/system-language.test.ts src/core/identity/runtime-prompt-layers.test.ts src/core/identity/prompt-store.test.ts src/core/identity/prompt-composer.test.ts passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed.

title: P0: Normalize legacy system_language prompt layer on startup
description:
Summary
Deploying commit 745daad4 crashed Carlini because the persisted /app/companion-data/state/prompt-layers.json contains a system_language layer with retired substrate_health.* template keys. The new system-language contract rejects unknown keys during PromptLayerStore.load(), so startup dies before ensureSystemLanguagePromptLayer() can normalize the system-owned layer.

Why this matters
The runtime must be able to migrate system-owned persisted prompt layers forward when defaults remove retired template keys. Editable prompt JSON must remain authoritative, but system-owned defaults cannot brick production on deploy.

Scope
- Fix the load/migration path for legacy system_language content containing retired substrate_health.* keys.
- Preserve strict validation for admin/custom unknown template keys.
- Ensure normalized content is persisted by the existing system-language seed path after startup.
- Add regression tests covering old substrate_health.* keys in a persisted system-owned system_language layer.

Non-goals
- Do not reintroduce substrate_health prompt templates into the default contract.
- Do not loosen validation for arbitrary unknown keys.
- Do not touch unrelated prompt monitor redesign work.
acceptance_criteria:
- PromptLayerStore can load a persisted system-owned system_language layer containing only retired substrate_health.* extra keys without throwing.
- ensureSystemLanguagePromptLayer normalizes that layer to current composeDefaultSystemLanguageLayerContent() and removes substrate_health.* keys.
- Arbitrary unknown system_language keys still fail validation.
- Targeted system-language/prompt-store tests pass.
- npm run lint passes before closure.
close_reason: Completed in git commit 7b950ba8. Added a pre-validation prompt-layer owner-file migration for retired system_language substrate_health.* template keys, writes the repaired prompt-layers.json, records a prompt history entry, then runs the existing strict validators. System-owned system.language layers are normalized back to current composeDefaultSystemLanguageLayerContent(); admin-owned valid custom template content is preserved. Arbitrary unknown system_language keys still fail validation. title: P0: Repair prompt runtime regression after group-chat merge
description:
Summary
The 8sow group-runtime merge produced a prompt/runtime regression visible in prompt monitor and shakedown. The companion prompt is bloated with duplicated XML-ish labels, backend/debug/provenance metadata, generic runtime_self guidance, substrate/model/tool counts, and repeated authenticity_provenance blocks. The operator observed missing required appearance context, poor tool visibility in prompt monitor, Analyst Workbench guidance still present outside the charge line, history summary still rendered as line snippets instead of prose, and many memories withheld without useful explanation. This must be treated as a rollback-grade prompt correctness issue, not polish.

Observed failures from operator shakedown
- Sections are double-labeled, e.g. bracket titles inside XML-ish blocks such as immutable_human_safety_amendments / Constitution Precedence.
- runtime_self remains in the prompt but no longer carries useful relationship/person context; it also contains generic behavioral instructions such as friendly/helpful that conflict with the companion emotion/personality systems.
- Trust-level dynamic prompt fields remain present/generic while relationship level is missing where it would be useful.
- Generic runtime_tooling count blocks provide no model value and should not be in the default prompt.
- model_context and substrate_health are present even though the companion does not need model name/provider/backend health details for normal behavior.
- Charge budget format is mostly acceptable, but Analyst Workbench guidance still appears elsewhere in the prompt despite being explicitly removed from default companion context.
- authenticity_provenance appears repeatedly and bloats session/tool/error displays; it should not be sprayed into companion prompt/debug surfaces unless explicitly needed.
- Prompt monitor/tool debug surfaces no longer show the actual tool prompt descriptions clearly; they show errors and provenance metadata instead.
- Appearance context that had recently been restored to the main system prompt is missing from the generated prompt.
- History summary is still random lines/snippets, not a prose summary paragraph of what happened.
- Memory note says many memories were kept out of turn context; determine whether this is expected privacy/channel filtering, retrieval-budget filtering, or a regression in room-scoped memory access.
- One-on-one chat path must not be degraded by the group-chat changes.

Files to inspect first
- src/core/identity/runtime-prompt-layers.ts
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/prompt-lifecycle.ts
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/prompt-assembly.ts
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/agent-invocation.ts
- src/shared/authenticity-provenance.ts and call sites
- src/faculties/memory/retrieval/access.ts, telemetry.ts, withheld-summary.ts
- prompt monitor/Garden routes and services that expose generated prompt, provider payload, tool list, and session context

Non-goals
- Do not redesign the prompt monitor UI in this bead. Only restore enough debug data visibility to validate tool prompt/context payloads if a regression is present.
- Do not add per-participant memory permission matrices. Room = room remains the rule.
- Do not remove required companion identity/persona/appearance content.
- Do not replace deterministic filtering with prompt prose telling the companion how to decide privacy.
acceptance_criteria:
- Default companion prompt no longer includes generic runtime_self behavioral guidance, runtime_tooling count-only blocks, model_context, substrate_health, or repeated authenticity_provenance noise.
- XML-ish sections do not include redundant bracket/header titles that repeat the tag name.
- Analyst Workbench guidance is absent from default prompt unless analysis_workbench is actually available; charge budget may include only concise cost/availability lines.
- Appearance context is present in normal chat prompts when configured/expected, and tests cover this.
- DM/one-on-one prompt path still renders correctly and is explicitly covered by tests.
- Group prompt path still preserves speaker attribution and compact conversation_state.
- History summary is prose/compressed rather than line-dump/tool-error spam, or the failing generator is identified and fixed.
- Memory withheld count exposes reason categories sufficient to distinguish room privacy, budget, irrelevance, and other filters; same-room and authorized DM room memories are not accidentally withheld.
- Prompt/tool monitor data exposes actual model-facing tool descriptions or a clear error if unavailable, without provenance spam replacing the useful content.
- Targeted prompt/runtime/memory tests and npm run lint pass before closure.
close_reason: Completed in git commit 745daad4. Repaired prompt runtime by moving editable runtime layers into config/runtime-prompt-layers.seed.json, deleting hardcoded runtime-prompt-templates.ts, stripping prompt-facing runtime_self/provenance/model/substrate/tool-count noise, restoring static appearance, preserving compact conversation_state with speaker/trust/relationship, fixing regular trust to allow personal memories, fixing same-batch toolset overlay resolution, and replacing fallback history line dumps with prose/tool-failure compression. Validation: npm test -- --run passed before final hygiene-script edits; affected hygiene-script tests passed after those edits; npm run lint passed after final edits and again before closure; npm run build passed; npm run verify:settings-contract passed; npm run verify:repository-hygiene passed; git diff --check passed; fallow completed and only unrelated pre-existing hygiene findings were observed.

title: P0: Gate Analyst Workbench guidance and simplify charge budget
description:
Summary
Remove duplicated Analyst Workbench instructions from default prompt context and rewrite charge budget as a concise dynamic runtime block. Workbench is powerful and expensive/slow; guidance should appear only when the tool is actually available for the current companion/session/turn.

Current behavior
runtime.tooling includes an unconditional analysis_workbench_guidance block. buildChargeBudgetContextBlock also repeats detailed Workbench guidance and caution text. This makes the prompt verbose and repeatedly emphasizes Workbench even when it should not be used.

Required behavior
- Analyst Workbench guidance is included only when analysis_workbench is available for the current turn/session/tool surface.
- Default companion prompt does not include the separate Workbench wall of text when Workbench is not available.
- Charge budget block moves/stays in dynamic runtime context near the bottom and contains only operational budget/cost data.
- Charge budget should say how many charge units remain and list costs for available charge actions. It should not duplicate full tool descriptions.

- Generate image: X
- Generate selfie: X
- Analyst Workbench extension pass: X, only if the tool is available
</charge_budget>

title: P0: Remove backend-only runtime metadata from default prompt
description:
Summary
Audit and remove backend/debug-only runtime metadata from the default companion prompt. The model should not see internal model/provider details, raw capability tier labels, total tool counts, or backend implementation metadata unless those fields directly affect behavior.

Current behavior
Runtime layers include model_context, capability_tier, and tooling counts. Live startup logs also show detailed backend/tool counts that are useful operationally but not prompt-worthy by default.

Required behavior
Classify prompt fields into:
- RequiredForBehavior
- UsefulForBehavior
- BackendOnly
- DebugOnly

Default prompt should include RequiredForBehavior and selected UsefulForBehavior only. BackendOnly and DebugOnly fields should remain in telemetry/debug surfaces, not in the model prompt.

Likely fields to remove from default prompt
- model name / provider identifier / provider wire details.
- raw capability tier label unless a specific instruction changes behavior.
- total tool counts such as active/core/promoted/loaded/autoload/deferred/available extended counts.
- raw implementation metadata for runtime tooling.

Files to inspect first
- src/core/identity/runtime-prompt-layers.ts: model_context, capability_tier, runtime_tooling counts.
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts: runtime variables for model/capability/tool counts.
- src/core/identity/prompt-runtime.ts: macro hints for runtime variables.
- Tests under src/core/identity and src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.test.ts.

Non-goals
- Do not delete telemetry/debug data structures.
- Do not remove behaviorally necessary tool availability text.
design: Keep behavioral policy separate from backend observability. If a field is useful only to a developer, keep it out of the default prompt.
acceptance_criteria:
- Default companion prompt no longer includes model_context/model identifier.
- Default companion prompt no longer includes raw capability_tier unless a behavior policy explicitly requires it.
- Default companion prompt no longer includes raw tool count totals.
- Operational telemetry/debug snapshots still preserve backend fields for developer inspection where already supported.
- Tests assert removed backend-only fields are absent from default prompt rendering.
notes: This should reduce token bloat and prompt cache churn without removing runtime observability.

title: P0: Stabilize static prompt prefix against volatile runtime fields
description:
Summary
Fix prompt cache busting by ensuring volatile runtime fields do not render in or invalidate the static prompt prefix. The split prompt mechanism exists, but the static settings hash currently considers almost every template variable except now_iso, so dynamic values can still bust the static prefix cache.

Current behavior
Prompt assembly uses staticPrefixTemplate and dynamicSuffixTemplate, but buildStaticPromptSettingsHash filters only now_iso. Runtime variables include user/current speaker, channel, trust, model, date/time, charge/runtime state, tool counts, and emotional/runtime state. If those dynamic variables are included in static rendering or its settings hash, normal turns invalidate the cache.

Required behavior
- Static prefix contains durable rules, stable identity, stable safety/tool policy, and stable style constraints only.
- Dynamic suffix/runtime context contains current date/time, current speaker, current channel, group/DM conversation state, memory context, charge budget, emotional/runtime snapshot, tool availability for the turn, recent history, recent messages, and current user message.
- buildStaticPromptSettingsHash must only include variables that can actually affect the rendered static prefix or an explicit stable allowlist.
- Static prefix hash/settings should not change when only current speaker, date/time, charge budget, last message metadata, or memory retrieval results change.

Files to inspect first
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/prompt-lifecycle.ts: composePromptSections, buildPromptPrefixCacheKey, buildStaticPromptSettingsHash.
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/prompt-assembly.ts: static/dynamic rendering and final prompt assembly.
- src/core/identity/runtime-prompt-layers.ts: runtime layer placement.
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts: dynamic runtime variables and charge block.

Non-goals
- Do not redesign prompt monitor UI in this bead.
- Do not remove runtime data entirely; move/limit it so cache behavior is correct.
design: Prefer deriving the static settings hash from the static template's referenced macros, or an explicit stable allowlist, rather than hashing all available variables.
acceptance_criteria:
- Static prefix rendered text remains unchanged across two turns where only current speaker changes.
- Static prefix rendered text remains unchanged when date/time changes.
- Static prefix rendered text remains unchanged when charge remaining changes.
- Static prefix rendered text remains unchanged when memory context changes.
- Last message metadata and speaking/current author fields are absent from the static prefix.
- Tests cover settings hash stability for speaker/date/charge/memory changes and invalidation for an actual stable prompt/identity change.
notes: This bead is about cache correctness and placement; detailed cache diagnostics UI belongs to the deferred prompt-monitor bead.
close_reason: Completed in 287b05f7, integrated by 095432c8. Evidence: src/core/agent/substrate-agent/prompt-lifecycle.ts filters volatile static settings variables by dynamic key/prefix and referenced static macros; src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/prompt-assembly.ts strips current-datetime blocks from earlier prompt text and appends the canonical date/time near the bottom; runtime prompt layers split static-ish defaults from dynamic runtime state. Validation: src/core/agent/substrate-agent/prompt-lifecycle.test.ts covers speaker/date/charge/memory static hash stability and stable identity invalidation; targeted suite passed (309 tests), npm run lint passed, npm run build passed.

title: P0: Enforce room-scoped memory visibility during retrieval
description:
Summary
Add deterministic room-scoped memory gating before memory text is selected for prompt context. Room identity is channelId. This must prevent DM memories from leaking into group rooms and prevent memories from one group room leaking into another group room.

Current behavior
Memory provenance and scopeRef already store channel/room information, but evaluateRetrievalAccessDecision currently checks trust, sensitivity, contact scope, and policy boundary tags; it does not enforce room provenance or contact participation in a room.

Required behavior
- A memory created in a DM is only available in that same DM/contact context. It must not appear in any group room.
- A memory created in group room X is available in room X.
- A memory created in group room X is available in Vega's DM only if Vega's contact record shows participation in room X.
- A memory created in group room X is blocked in group room Y, even if the participant overlap is high.
- A memory created in group room X is blocked in another person's DM unless that contact is recorded as participating in room X.
- Missing room participation proof for DM access fails closed.
- Add/use a withheld reason such as blocked_by_room_visibility or room_visibility.blocked so telemetry distinguishes this from trust ceiling, sensitivity, budget, and relevance filtering.

Files to inspect first
- src/faculties/memory/types.ts: MemoryProvenance.channelId and MemoryScopeRef.
- src/faculties/memory/extraction.ts: persisted provenance/scopeRef write path.
- src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts: candidate loop before scoring/rendering.
- src/faculties/memory/retrieval/access.ts: evaluateRetrievalAccessDecision.
- src/core/contacts/types.ts and src/core/contacts/contact-store-port.ts: conversation channel participation records.

Non-goals
- No allowed_viewers matrix.
- No participant-set comparison between rooms.
- No leave-room/revocation semantics in this bead.
- No per-user channel privacy label migration in this bead.
design: Use existing provenance.channelId and scopeRef.kind=conversation/id where present. Treat legacy memories conservatively when room provenance is missing and the memory is sensitive or conversation-scoped.
acceptance_criteria:
- In a group room, memories from the same channelId may be included and memories from any other group channelId are excluded.
- In a group room, private DM memories are excluded.
- In Vega's DM, Vega's DM memories are allowed.
- In Vega's DM, memories from room X are allowed only when Vega's contact profile records room X participation.
- In Vega's DM, memories from rooms not recorded on Vega's contact profile are excluded.
- Excluded room memories do not appear as text in memory context.
- Retrieval trace/manifest includes a room-visibility withheld reason count distinct from trust/sensitivity/budget/relevance.
- Tests cover same-room group access, cross-room blocking, DM private blocking in group, DM access to participated room, DM blocking of non-participated room, and fail-closed missing participation proof.
notes: Operator clarification: room = room regardless of participants. If someone invites a problematic person later, that is outside this P0 logic. Later leave/revocation policy can be designed separately.
close_reason: Completed in 66c0ed2e and integrated by 721ab386. Evidence: src/faculties/memory/retrieval/access.ts enforces room_visibility decisions using provenance/scopeRef channelId and Contact.conversationChannels for DM room-participation proof; src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts threads roomVisibility through retrieval, summaries, active-context seeds, and telemetry; withheld summaries include room_visibility.blocked. Validation: src/faculties/memory/retrieval.test.ts covers same-room group access, cross-room blocking, DM participation access, missing-proof fail-closed, and manifest counts; targeted suite passed (309 tests), npm run lint passed, npm run build passed.

title: P0: Preserve group speaker attribution through provider payload
description:
Summary
Ensure user messages in group chats reach the provider with speaker attribution in the visible text. The provider-facing message format preserves role/content, not arbitrary session metadata, so attribution must be rendered before provider conversion.

Current behavior
Session entries retain authorName/authorId, but entriesToMessages renders ordinary user entries as raw content. contextMessagesToPiMessages then converts to provider messages and drops metadata. Consecutive same-role messages can be merged, which makes multi-speaker user turns ambiguous.

Required behavior
- In group mode, render user history lines as: Display Name (discord:platform_id): message text.
- In group mode, render the current user message with the same attribution before it is sent to the provider.
- Assistant messages should remain attributed as the companion/assistant where needed, without polluting normal response history.
- Preserve author metadata in storage as metadata, not duplicated text in memory captures.
- Avoid merging different human authors into a single anonymous user block. If same-role messages are merged, each constituent message must retain its speaker label.

Files to inspect first
- src/core/session/manager/context-support.ts: entriesToMessages and merge logic.
- src/primitives/llm/message-conversion.ts: contextMessagesToPiMessages drops metadata.
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/agent-invocation.ts: current-turn prompt message construction.
- src/core/session/entry-attribution.ts: existing attribution normalization helpers.

Non-goals
- Do not store attribution prefixes into memory text if the memory pipeline already stores speaker metadata.
- Do not change one-to-one DM prompt style unless needed for correctness.
design: Do the provider-visible labeling at context rendering/current-turn construction, not in the provider client. The provider client should stay transport-focused.
acceptance_criteria:
- Given a group chat with Vega, Iku, and Miss Dragon Fox, the final provider wire messages include each user message with visible speaker attribution.
- No group user message reaches the provider as only anonymous generic user content.
- Consecutive group user messages from different authors remain distinguishable after any merging.
- Current-turn group message attribution survives into the provider payload, not just session history.
- Memory extraction/capture still receives structured speaker metadata and does not rely on duplicated attribution text.
- Tests cover history conversion, current-turn conversion, and merged consecutive user messages from multiple authors.
notes: This is the highest-risk correctness issue for group chat: without visible attribution, the model cannot know who said what.
close_reason: Completed in 9ccec1b2 and integrated by 15a5655f plus 50e9a765. Evidence: src/core/session/entry-attribution.ts formats Display Name (source:id) labels; src/core/session/manager/context-support.ts labels group history before same-role merge; src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/agent-invocation.ts labels current-turn group user content before provider prompt. Integration fix in 50e9a765 makes buildContext label history only for explicit group/non-DM current contexts. Validation: targeted runtime/prompt/session/memory suite passed (309 tests), npm run lint passed, npm run build passed.

title: P0: Add compact DM/group conversation_state runtime context
description:
Summary
Add explicit chat_type to runtime context and replace ambiguous speaking_with semantics with a compact conversation_state block. This fixes one-to-one assumptions in group rooms while keeping prompt context lean.

Current behavior
Runtime prompt variables and layers expose speaking_with name/trust and channel_context, but they do not explicitly distinguish direct_message vs group chat. In a group room, speaking_with can incorrectly imply a single relationship anchor or current addressee.

Required behavior
- Derive chat_type from SubstrateMessage.isDirectMessage: direct_message when true, group when false.
- Render current_message_author and current_message_author_id from the current SubstrateMessage author fields.
- Render room/channel ID directly as the room identity. Do not derive room identity from participants.
- In group mode, render at most 5 recently active participants from recent session entries in the current channel, deduped newest-first by author ID. Include display name and platform/source ID when available.
- In DM mode, do not render a fake participant list.
- Keep the block compact and operational; do not include prose about what can safely be said or when to avoid intimate references.

Suggested prompt shape
<conversation_state>
  <chat_type>group</chat_type>
  <channel_id>...</channel_id>
  <channel_type>discord</channel_type>
  <channel_visibility>semi_private</channel_visibility>
  <current_message_author name="Vega" id="discord:..." />
  <recent_active_participants max="5">
    <participant name="Vega" id="discord:..." />
  </recent_active_participants>
</conversation_state>

Files to inspect first
- src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts: SubstrateMessage fields.
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts: buildPromptTemplateVariables and buildDynamicPromptTemplateVariables.
- src/core/identity/runtime-prompt-layers.ts: runtime.state layer.
- src/core/session/manager.ts and src/core/session/types.ts: recent session entries and author fields.

Non-goals
- No full member list.
- No relationship/trust summary per participant in this P0 bead.
- No prompt privacy guidance prose; filtering is deterministic upstream.
design: Prefer a small runtime-context helper that can be unit-tested independently. Source participant data from existing persisted session entries so the Discord adapter does not need to fetch full channel membership.
acceptance_criteria:
- Provider/system prompt explicitly states chat_type as direct_message or group for user-facing turns.
- Group prompt includes current_message_author with display name and stable platform/source ID when available.
- Group prompt includes no more than 5 recently active participants, newest-first deduped by author ID.
- Room identity is exactly channelId; participant membership does not alter room identity.
- No new prompt text tells the model how to decide privacy or whether to reveal intimate/private memories.
- Tests cover DM mode, group mode, max-5 participant cap, and recency ordering.
notes: Operator explicitly rejected full member lists and participant-matrix privacy. Keep this concise.
close_reason: Completed in 287b05f7 (runtime context cleanup), integrated by 095432c8. Evidence: src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts renders compact conversation_state with chat_type/current author/channel/recent participants capped at 5; src/core/identity/runtime-prompt-layers.ts uses conversation_state instead of speaking_with in the new runtime_state umbrella. title: P0: Group-aware prompt/runtime context and room-scoped memory privacy
description:
Summary
The prompt-generation/runtime-context system needs to be made correct for multi-user chat. The current runtime still behaves like a one-to-one chat in several places: it renders ambiguous speaking_with context, loses speaker attribution before provider calls, relies on trust/sensitivity memory filtering without a hard room boundary, includes backend/runtime metadata in the default prompt, repeats Analyst Workbench guidance, and allows dynamic fields to influence the static prompt prefix/cache behavior.

Source and evidence
This work comes from the operator transcript reviewed on 2026-06-29 plus read-only inspection of live Kubernetes logs from the psfn deployment. Live logs showed Retrieval traces for Discord channel 1486443955561299979 using channelVisibility=semi_private and trust/sensitivity filtering, but no room-visibility reason code. Extraction logs already preserve sourceSpeakerNames such as Vega and MrDragonFox, so upstream attribution exists. Gateway logs also showed repeated agent.turn.prompt calls under the same turn/request, which is useful debug evidence but not the immediate implementation target.

Operator decisions that must be preserved
- Room identity is the room/channel ID, not the participant set.
- Do not build an allowed_viewers participant matrix.
- Group prompt context must not include the full room member list; cap visible participants at 5 recently active speakers.
- Do not add long prompt prose telling the companion how to decide what is safe to say. Memory/privacy filtering is deterministic before prompt assembly; blocked memory text must simply be absent.
- If a memory was created in a DM, it must not leak into a group room.
- If a memory was created in group room X, it may be used in that same room X.
- If Vega is in room X and room X is recorded on Vega's contact profile, then Vega's DM may access memories from room X. If a contact is not recorded as participating in a room, that room's memories are blocked in that contact's DM.
- Cross-room leakage is not allowed even if the participant overlap is high.
- Leave-room/revocation semantics are deferred.
- Channel privacy labels probably need to become channel-owned instead of per-user, but that is not part of the immediate implementation.

Scope
This epic covers P0 runtime correctness and privacy/cache cleanup, plus P1/P2 follow-up work for telemetry, summaries, prompt monitor UX, episodic landmark placement, timezone metadata, and channel-owned privacy modeling.

Non-goals for the immediate P0 pass
- No prompt-monitor redesign implementation yet.
- No full participant/member list in prompts.
- No per-participant memory access matrix.
- No user-left-room revocation behavior.
- No migration of channel privacy labels to a new channel-owned model yet.
design: Use existing runtime primitives instead of adding a parallel model. Discord/Substrate messages already carry channelId, authorId, authorName, and isDirectMessage. Session entries already persist author metadata and channelVisibility. Memory provenance already carries channelId/source speaker fields and MemoryScopeRef supports conversation scope. The implementation should connect those existing primitives rather than introducing an allowed_viewers matrix.
acceptance_criteria:
- The epic has child beads for each concrete implementation surface: conversation state, speaker attribution, room-scoped memory gating, cache/static prefix hygiene, backend metadata trimming, charge/tool guidance cleanup, history summary cleanup, prompt monitor debug UX, episodic landmark placement, timezone metadata, and channel-owned privacy follow-up.
- P0 child beads preserve the operator decisions: room = channelId, no participant matrix, no full member list, max 5 recently active participants, no prompt privacy prose, and deterministic memory filtering before prompt assembly.
- Each child bead has self-contained context, concrete file anchors, explicit non-goals, and checkable acceptance criteria.
notes: Read-only code anchors from inspection: src/channels/discord/adapter.ts:758, src/core/session/manager.ts:570, src/core/session/manager/context-support.ts:224, src/primitives/llm/message-conversion.ts:229, src/faculties/memory/types.ts:64, src/faculties/memory/extraction.ts:561, src/faculties/memory/retrieval/access.ts:46, src/core/identity/runtime-prompt-layers.ts:151, src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts:493, src/core/agent/substrate-agent/prompt-lifecycle.ts:331.
close_reason: Implementation wave completed on integrate/psfn-framework-8sow. Closed implementation children .1-.9 cover compact group/direct conversation_state, provider speaker attribution, room-scoped memory retrieval, static-prefix/cache hygiene, backend metadata trimming, Workbench/charge prompt cleanup, history/tool failure compression, episodic landmark placement verification, and per-contact timezone runtime context. Deferred children .10 and .11 remain intentionally out of scope per operator direction: prompt monitor UX waits for operator UX review, and channel-owned privacy label migration is a later settings/design decision. title: P0: Update vulnerable production npm dependency pins from audit
description:
Summary: A codebase-audit run on 2026-06-29 found production dependency vulnerabilities in the root package. `npm audit --omit=dev --json` exits non-zero with 23 production vulnerabilities: 1 critical, 17 high, and 5 moderate. `admin-ui` and `companion-ui` production audits are clean, so this bead is scoped to the root package unless follow-up evidence broadens it.

Evidence and affected files:
- package.json:63 pins production dependencies including @huggingface/transformers 3.8.1, @mariozechner/pi-ai 0.62.0, discord.js 14.25.1, and ws 8.19.0.
- package.json:86 has overrides including undici 6.23.0, fast-xml-parser 5.4.2, and tar 7.5.10.
- `npm audit --omit=dev --json` reported critical protobufjs advisories. `npm why protobufjs --omit=dev` shows protobufjs comes transitively through onnxruntime-web under @huggingface/transformers and through @google/genai under @mariozechner/pi-ai.
- The same audit reported high advisories for ws, discord.js/undici paths, tar, @huggingface/transformers via onnxruntime-node, and related transitive packages.

Why it matters: This project has a supply-chain pinning policy. Production advisories in exact-pinned runtime dependencies need intentional upgrades or documented no-fix risk instead of being left hidden behind transitive dependencies.

Scope: Update exact dependency pins and overrides in the root package/package-lock to remove production advisories where fixed versions exist. Investigate the transformer/pi-ai transitive chains because some fixes may require major upgrades or upstream changes. Keep dependency references exact; do not introduce floating ranges, branch names, or latest aliases.

Non-goals: Do not refactor runtime code beyond what is required to adapt to upgraded APIs. Do not change admin-ui or companion-ui dependencies unless new evidence shows they are affected in production.
acceptance_criteria: npm audit --omit=dev exits 0 or remaining production advisories are explicitly documented with upstream no-fix evidence; exact pins/overrides are updated without floating ranges; npm install/package-lock updates are committed; npm run lint and the smallest relevant dependency/runtime tests pass.

title: Fix tsc regressions from kube backup and group-memory commits
description:
Summary: Repair TypeScript noEmit failures introduced by the recent kube backup/group-memory/turn-contention commits without touching unrelated local edits.

title: S9 Memory: Postgres-only no-loss memory database cutover
description:
Summary:
Turn the Sprint 9 memory direction in working_docs/SPRINT_9_MEMORY.md into a Postgres-only, no-loss memory/database cutover. This is not a table-for-table SQLite port. Use the migration to tighten memory semantics: canonical L0.1 episodes, watermarked synthesis, overlap-aware reconciliation, explicit L2 evolution links, richer sleep-time maintenance, and regression benchmarks.

Current code analysis from 2026-06-06 fallback checkout:
- L0 archive truth is still filesystem JSONL through SessionStore and SessionArchivePort. The database tier is a searchable projection, currently split between SQLite FTS (src/persistence/sessions/transcript-projection.ts, session-search.sqlite) and Postgres tsvector projection (src/persistence/sessions/postgres-adapters.ts, session_messages_projection).
- Runtime startup still defaults to sqlite when persistenceBackend is absent. composeSessionRuntime() is sqlite-only; composeSessionRuntimeAsync() supports Postgres, but SQLite remains the normal path.
- L0.1 episodic memory is SQLite-only. EpisodicStore in src/faculties/memory/episodic/store.ts owns l01_episodes and l01_episode_arcs in better-sqlite3; agent wiring creates an EpisodicStore only when a SQLite db exists, so Postgres mode currently has no durable episodic store.
- L2 memory has both SQLite MemoryStore and PostgresMemoryStore, but the schemas are not equivalent. SQLite has source_type, provenance_json, l2_memory_patch_events, sqlite-vec l2_memory_embeddings, and migration shims. Postgres stores pgvector embedding on l2_memories and rejects legacy embedding-table schemas, but still needs no-loss parity and first-class evolution links.
- Gateway audit, reflections, contacts, intentions, scratchpad, session search, e2e/CLI tools, and maintenance scripts still contain SQLite paths or fallback behavior. Production pure-Postgres means these cannot remain as ordinary runtime branches.
- Existing dependencies include better-sqlite3 and sqlite-vec. A migration utility may need a tightly scoped legacy SQLite reader, but runtime code must not keep SQLite as a supported backend.

Goal:
Make the operational memory/database tier pure Postgres with no loss of function. Remove legacy runtime SQLite code paths and silent SQLite fallbacks. Provide a deterministic SQLite-to-Postgres migration tool that transfers existing data, verifies parity, and leaves the runtime fail-closed on missing Postgres/pgvector configuration.

Non-goals:
- Do not import Hy-Memory/OpenClaw code.
- Do not add a Python sidecar.
- Do not weaken trust, privacy, provenance, backup/restore, or L0 raw-history guarantees.
- Do not preserve compatibility shims as permanent runtime behavior.
design: Use Postgres capabilities directly: pgvector for semantic search, tsvector for L0 projection search, JSONB GIN indexes for provenance/scope/consent/artifacts, range overlap indexes for episode spans, recursive CTEs for episode and memory lineage, and transactional canonicalization for merge/update/supersede decisions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Postgres is the only production runtime database backend; SQLite is absent from normal startup, gateway, agent, Garden/admin, maintenance, and e2e runtime paths.
- Existing SQLite-backed data can be migrated into Postgres with deterministic counts, checksums, embedding dimension validation, and provenance/lineage preservation.
- L0 database projection, L0.1 episodes/arcs, L2 memories, scratchpad, contacts, intentions, reflection mirrors, gateway audit, and maintenance reviews have Postgres coverage with no loss of current function.
- L0.1 duplicate episodes are reduced through watermarks and candidate-to-canonical reconciliation.
- L2 supersession is upgraded to explicit evolution links and retrieval can expand bounded history when useful.
- Memory benchmark harness catches current-state, compatible-update, contradiction, episodic-overlap, paraphrase, privacy/withheld-context, and backup/restore regressions.
- npm run lint passes before any implementation bead closes; broader build/test/e2e gates are specified on child beads.

title: Audit and clean companion memory context rendering
description:
Summary: Companion-facing memory/context text is carrying internal provenance and graph/linkage metadata into the chat prompt. Memory retrieval can keep rich refs, spans, classifications, and provenance internally, but the text shown to the companion as usable chat memory needs to read as clean recall prose, not raw IDs and drill-down instructions.

Observed bad context example:
Raw refs for drill-down: spans l0-session-span:b4bc447c3ea46010309b06fb; provenance l0_span:l0-session-span:b4bc447c3ea46010309b06fb, session:1313001762793197678, turn:019e57cf-18f2-7298-bdb3-8aefbb5245d9, turn:019e57d0-bf9a-76dc-989c-f5b9c4eb854c, turn:019e57e3-eeb1-7114-8c0c-7f1b14d632d5, turn:019e57f4-317a-772d-89ed-17443c87f670
Use these landmarks as scoped recall waypoints; drill into raw span/artifact refs only when needed.

Scope:
- Audit the memory/context assembly path that feeds companion chat turns, including L0/session span recall, memory retrieval formatting, and prompt/context injection.
- Identify every place internal refs, provenance IDs, span IDs, turn IDs, artifact IDs, drill-down instructions, or classification/debug labels can leak into companion-visible context.
- Define a clean rendering contract: companion-facing context is plain useful text; machine provenance stays in structured metadata, logs, trace records, or tool-only drill-down surfaces.
- Preserve enough linkage for debugging and retrieval without placing raw IDs in the model-visible memory prose.
- Add focused tests or golden context fixtures that fail if raw provenance/id strings appear in companion-facing context while allowing them in internal metadata.

Acceptance criteria:
- A representative chat context containing memory recall no longer includes raw span/session/turn/provenance IDs or drill-down instructions.
- Internal memory provenance remains available to the system for scraping, linking, classification, and debugging.
- Tests cover the provided raw-ref regression pattern and at least one normal memory-context render.
- Include token/context impact notes from the audit; 4k+ memory context is acceptable when useful, but metadata noise must not consume companion-facing prompt budget.

Migrated from the old PSFNLIVE bead database into psfn_framework on 2026-05-27 because live hotfixes track in the framework bead DB and deploy/pull into psfn-live.
notes: 2026-06-09 operator review: confirmed as top priority and broader than memory IDs alone — emotion-system raw vectors/decay math and overall dynamic-context token waste (two turns ~100k; dynamic blocks defeat prompt caching) are tracked in sibling beads: context efficiency/cache-discipline audit, emotion/bookkeeping prose rendering, and deterministic-work-out-of-LLM-paths. Principle: metadata stays recorded as metadata (records/journals/Garden), never injected into conversation context; companion-facing context must be simple, clear, with the right turns and the right memories.
close_reason: All four leak points cleaned and deployed live (commit 4448d0d7): episodic landmark chains no longer render span/artifact/provenance refs or episode ids (arc partners now referenced by title); avoidance metacognitive evidence cites concern text excerpts instead of UUIDs; scratchpad renders without entry ids (tool list action remains the id surface for mutations). Internal provenance collection for telemetry unchanged. Golden rendering-contract test added (src/faculties/memory/retrieval/formatting.test.ts) failing on UUIDs, l0 span refs, session:/turn: refs, sourceRef strings, or drill-down framing in companion-visible context; two legacy tests that blessed the leak were flipped to enforce the new contract. Token impact: the raw-refs line alone was ~200-400 chars per episode (up to 15 episodes/turn), plus 37 chars per concern UUID and ~40 per scratchpad id — roughly 0.5-2k tokens of pure noise removed from every memory-bearing turn. Broader composition instrumentation continues in psfn-framework-7jl.

title: Fix PostgreSQL memory schema/runtime mismatch and remove unsupported embedding layout drift
description:
Summary:
The PostgreSQL memory adapter currently reads and writes an `embedding` column on `l2_memories`, but the base PostgreSQL memory migration does not define that column. Instead, it creates a separate `l2_memory_embeddings` table that no production code uses. This is a real schema/runtime mismatch, not just dead schema, and it escaped because the current postgres-store test fakes SQL behavior instead of exercising the real schema.

Files likely include:
- `src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts`
- `src/persistence/postgres/migrations.ts`
- postgres memory/runtime tests
- operator docs if migration/cutover steps change

Implementation steps:
1. Align the supported PostgreSQL memory schema with the live store contract so the production adapter and migrations agree on where embeddings live.
2. Remove, migrate, or explicitly reject the unsupported `l2_memory_embeddings` layout so dead/ambiguous schema does not remain silently available.
3. Add fail-closed startup or migration validation that rejects incompatible PostgreSQL memory schemas instead of proceeding with hidden drift.
4. Add tests that exercise the real supported schema shape, not only mock SQL responders.

Acceptance:
- The supported PostgreSQL memory schema and the live adapter agree structurally.
- Unsupported or legacy embedding layouts fail clearly instead of limping along.
- No dead embedding table remains as an apparently supported path.

Validation:
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run build`
- targeted postgres memory tests against the real supported schema path
close_reason: Implemented the supported PostgreSQL memory schema on l2_memories.embedding, removed the dead l2_memory_embeddings layout from migrations, added fail-closed schema validation for missing/legacy layouts, and tightened the postgres memory tests. Validated with npm test -- --run src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.test.ts, npm run lint, and npm run build in /mnt/samesung/ai/psfn-framework-worktrees/PSFN-80xh.5. Committed as 8ab9ecb8 and merged into refactor-final at cca1f8e0.

title: Stop swallowing PostgreSQL memory persistence failures
description:
Summary:
`PostgresMemoryStore.enqueuePersist()` currently catches persistence failures and only logs them. That allows memory writes to appear successful in the in-memory maps while the backing PostgreSQL write has actually failed. This violates the repo fail-closed rules and creates fake-healthy persistence state.

Files likely include:
- `src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts`
- memory writer/retriever call paths if contract changes are required
- postgres memory tests

Implementation steps:
1. Remove the log-and-continue persistence error path from `PostgresMemoryStore`.
2. Make write failures observable through the store contract and caller paths instead of leaving stale in-memory success.
3. Ensure startup and subsequent writes do not report healthy persistence when the backing PostgreSQL operation failed.
4. Add tests covering failed insert/update/delete persistence behavior.

Acceptance:
- PostgreSQL memory persistence failures are surfaced to callers or runtime health, not swallowed.
- In-memory and persisted state cannot silently diverge behind a console error.
- Tests prove the failure path is explicit.

Validation:
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run build`
- targeted postgres memory failure-path tests
close_reason: Integrated on refactor-final as 0bf4ec11 after worker validation: npm run lint, npm test -- --run src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.test.ts, and npm run build passed in worktree PSFN-80xh.6.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: Post-cutover regression found and fixed 2026-06-11 (commit ad044cc7): the async port migration missed persistEmotionalStateFromExtraction — it stayed sync, so updateEmotionalBaseline rejections were unhandled and crashed the agent in a ~5min loop during active conversation (first 22P02 Jun 10 00:04). Second half: updateEmotionalBaseline and contact-merge passed raw JS arrays as jsonb params (node-pg array-literal encoding -> 22P02), meaning every emotional-baseline write since cutover had silently failed. Both fixed, fake pool now rejects array literals on jsonb, verified stable live with clean extraction + baseline writes.

title: Wire backend selection and runtime composition through port-backed persistence factories
description:

title: Make persistence async-safe and pluggable across SQLite, PostgreSQL, and rebuildable L0 projections
description:
Summary:
The current refactor state still cannot support PostgreSQL and future databases cleanly through domain ports. Existing progress extracted `EmbeddingProviderPort`, `ConfigStorePort`, `MemoryStorePort`, and `PromptStatePort`, but the actual persistence/search/archive surfaces are still mixed between concrete SQLite classes, synchronous caller assumptions, and file-path-level seams. PR #10 demonstrated exactly why a raw `DatabaseAdapter` is the wrong abstraction: async and dialect churn leaked across the repo because the missing domain ports and async-safe contracts were not in place.

Objective:
Deliver an async-safe persistence architecture that supports SQLite now, PostgreSQL next, and future databases later without another repo-wide raw-DB rewrite. This epic covers the missing persistence-domain ports, conversion of persistence-facing call chains to async-safe contracts, SQLite and PostgreSQL adapters behind those ports, runtime composition selection, rebuildable L0 transcript projections, and the charter/doc updates needed to make the architecture explicit.

Scope:
- Define and document the persistence port taxonomy.
- Convert persistence-facing contracts to async-first where backend I/O can occur.
- Keep JSONL L0 authoritative and treat DB copies as rebuildable projections.
- Add missing domain ports for session archive/search/projection, turn records, contacts, intention state, and gateway audit.
- Implement SQLite adapters behind the new ports.
- Implement PostgreSQL adapters behind the same ports.
- Wire backend selection and runtime composition through ports instead of direct concrete store construction.
- Add projection repair/rebuild tooling and parity validation.

Existing prerequisite work already closed and relied on by this epic:
- `PSFN-uaom.2` `EmbeddingProviderPort`

acceptance_criteria:
- The repo has an explicit persistence-domain port architecture for SQLite/PostgreSQL/future backends, not a raw DB adapter leaked through call sites.

title: Define gateway model transport contract for split runtime
description:
Summary: split-mode core still owns direct prompt transport and credential resolution. Define an explicit gateway-backed model transport contract so the agent core can request streaming/completion work without calling provider SDK transport or resolving API keys locally.

Files likely include:
- src/gateway/protocol.ts
- src/gateway/client.ts
- src/gateway/methods/**
- src/agent/stream-adapter.ts
- src/llm/**
- src/types.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Design a typed gateway RPC/port for model streaming and related request metadata used by the split runtime.
2. Keep provider selection, endpoint resolution, and credential lookup on the gateway side only.
3. Expose a narrow transport surface to core-side runtime code with no raw secret access.
4. Add tests for gateway protocol, client binding, and fail-closed behavior on invalid transport requests.

Validation:
- targeted gateway protocol/client tests
- targeted stream-adapter or llm transport tests
- npm run build
close_reason: Integrated gateway-backed stream transport contract into refactor/charter-boundary-remediation; validated with stream-adapter and gateway-client tests, lint, and build.

title: Move auxiliary provider workloads behind gateway transport
description:
Summary: prompt streaming is not the only boundary leak. Auxiliary provider workloads such as embeddings, vision review, model discovery, and helper clients still resolve LiteLLM endpoints or API keys outside the gateway boundary. Move those paths behind gateway-side ops as well.

Files likely include:
- src/llm/client.ts
- src/memory/embedding.ts
- src/images/vision-reviewer.ts
- src/runtime/startup-harness.ts
- src/agent-main.ts
- src/config/providers-config.ts
- related tests

Implementation steps:
1. Audit all core-side provider calls that still resolve configured base URLs or API keys.
2. Route embeddings, image review, model discovery, and similar provider work through gateway-side transport or privileged ops.
3. Remove core-side credential resolution from split-runtime modules.
4. Add tests covering each migrated workload and fail-closed behavior when gateway transport is unavailable.

Validation:
- targeted llm, embedding, image, and startup-harness tests
- npm run build
close_reason: Integrated auxiliary provider workloads behind gateway transport; validated with image vision reviewer, llm discovery/client, gateway client, and gateway llm tests plus build/lint.

title: Remediate remaining charter boundary leaks after scaffold pass
description:
Summary: close the remaining charter-adherence gaps discovered after the initial scaffold pass. The current refactor branch still leaks dead monolithic-startup language and parity naming, still lets split-mode core own direct provider transport and credential resolution, still executes untrusted shell work inside the gateway process, and still mixes outward musing semantics with legacy whisper identifiers.

Scope:
- remove remaining operational and code-surface references that keep monolithic startup alive
- make gateway the sole privileged external edge for model transport and credential resolution
- make sandbox execution a real trust-boundary split instead of a gateway-hosted interface
- finish the whisper-to-musing semantic split so outward soft messages are canonical musings and whisper stays internal-only
- add regression guards so these boundary leaks do not reappear

Primary files and surfaces likely include:
- package.json
- README.md
- docs/setup.md
- docs/operations.md
- docs/architecture.md
- docs/specifications.md
- src/runtime.ts and startup/parity helpers
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/agent/stream-adapter.ts
- src/agent/scheduled-agent-loop.ts
- src/llm/client.ts
- src/memory/embedding.ts
- src/images/vision-reviewer.ts
- src/repl/**
- src/gateway/**
- src/agent/message-classes.ts
- src/scheduler/heartbeat-policy.ts
- src/vault/auto-publish.ts

Acceptance:
1. No supported operational surface describes or exposes a monolithic startup path.
2. Core-side runtime code no longer resolves provider credentials or performs direct external model transport in split mode.
3. Untrusted shell execution no longer runs inside the gateway secrets boundary.
4. Outward soft-channel semantics are canonicalized as musings and whisper remains internal-only.
5. Targeted tests and boundary regression checks prove these invariants.
close_reason: All dependency-ordered remediation beads completed and integrated on refactor/charter-boundary-remediation; remaining unrelated composition-test debt filed as PSFN-xjdi.

title: Restore green validation gates after voice-provider hardening
description: Summary: The current phase-v HEAD is not green. npm test fails in src/channels/api/voice-websocket-runtime.test.ts because assertions still expect pre-hardening implicit provider behavior, and verify:public-sanitize fails because API CORS tests still use fixture hostnames containing 'vega'. Files to modify: src/channels/api/voice-websocket-runtime.test.ts, src/channels/api/voice-websocket-runtime.ts only if behavior is actually wrong, src/channels/api/http-policy.test.ts, src/channels/api/server.test.ts, and .beads/issues.jsonl. Implementation steps: 1) Align API voice websocket runtime tests and/or runtime behavior with explicit fail-closed provider selection rules. 2) Replace sanitize-violating fixture hostnames with neutral equivalents without weakening coverage. 3) Rerun full validation surface: npm test, verify:repository-hygiene, verify:settings-contract, build, admin-ui check. Example: before: provider-unset tests expect runtime to come up implicitly; after: tests assert disabled/fail-closed unless explicit provider is configured.
close_reason: Completed: restored green validation gates by aligning API voice websocket tests with explicit provider selection and removing sanitize-violating API fixture hostnames. Validation passed: npm test, verify:repository-hygiene, verify:settings-contract, build, admin-ui check.

title: Allow Garden chat API auth via admin token in split runtime
description: Summary: Garden chat falls back to admin token from bootstrap/login when API key is not exposed client-side. API auth currently accepts only API_KEY bearer, causing Unauthorized chat completions. Add explicit alternate bearer token path using ADMIN_TOKEN for API auth while API_KEY remains required for startup and primary auth.
close_reason: Completed: API now accepts ADMIN_TOKEN via bearer and psfn_token cookie for Garden chat calls; chat fetch includes credentials for split-mode cross-origin request; targeted tests passed (http-policy/server + tsc + admin-ui build).

title: Enforce single primary purpose on Conservatory tag cycling
description: Summary: In Garden Conservatory, setting a model purpose tag to primary does not demote existing primary tags for the same purpose on other models. This causes validation failure (multiple primaries) and blocks save. Update cycle logic so promoting one model to primary auto-demotes others for that purpose.
close_reason: Completed: purpose-tag cycling now enforces a single primary per purpose by auto-demoting other primaries when promoting a new one; save errors now show actionable validation/API details (first validation error and backend error body) instead of generic 400/validation text. Validated with npx tsx --test admin-ui/src/routes/models/discovery-autofill.test.ts and npx tsc --noEmit.

title: Fix Conservatory sidebar model id normalization for models.json schema
description: Summary: Adding models from Conservatory sidebar used raw discovered model ids as registry entry ids (e.g., openrouter/google/gemini...), which violates canonical MODEL_SLOT_KEY_PATTERN and causes POST /api/admin/settings/models 400. Normalize generated ids to key-safe form and add client-side validation to surface invalid ids before POST.
close_reason: Completed: normalized Conservatory sidebar-generated model ids to key-safe pattern required by models.json schema, added frontend id-pattern validation to prevent invalid POST payloads, and added unit tests for id normalization/edge cases. Validation: npx tsx --test admin-ui/src/routes/models/discovery-autofill.test.ts, npx vitest run src/channels/admin/server.test.ts src/llm/discovery.test.ts, npx tsc --noEmit.

title: Fix models save 400 regression after Conservatory autofill changes
description: Summary: Garden Conservatory save now returns POST /api/admin/settings/models 400 after recent autofill/discovery changes. Reproduce with current UI flow, identify invalid payload shape, and restore successful round-trip save without loosening schema validation. Files likely in admin-ui/src/routes/models/+page.svelte, admin-ui/src/routes/models/discovery-autofill.ts, src/config/models-config.ts, and admin API route tests.
close_reason: Completed: fixed Conservatory POST /api/admin/settings/models 400 regression by emitting discovery capability flags (supportsVision/supportsReasoning), applying those flags during autofill, seeding valid default purpose tags for newly discovered models, and adding client-side validation for missing purpose tags to block invalid payloads before POST. Validated with npx tsx --test admin-ui/src/routes/models/discovery-autofill.test.ts, npx vitest run src/llm/discovery.test.ts src/channels/admin/server.test.ts, and npx tsc --noEmit.
