title: Pre-load ML models and embedding service on startup
description: The HuggingFace text classifier (src/emotion/text-classifier.ts:62) lazily initializes its ONNX pipeline on first use, adding 5-15 seconds to the first message. The Ollama embedding service similarly has cold-start latency. Fix: eagerly initialize all ML pipelines during runtime startup (runtime.ts init / agent-main.ts main) with a warmup inference call. This includes: 1) text-classifier.ts ONNX pipeline 2) Ollama embedding model (send a dummy embed request) 3) Any other lazy-loaded model. Add a startup log line confirming models are warm.
close_reason: Merged into phase-v as 902b571; validated with ML warmup/text-classifier/embedding/startup parity tests passing on phase-v.

title: Telegram streaming response via editMessageText
description: Telegram adapter (adapter.ts:724) does 'const response = await this.handler(substrateMessage)' — waits for the ENTIRE response before sending anything. Should stream tokens progressively using Telegram editMessageText API (send initial message, then edit it as tokens arrive, debounced). Discord does not support this pattern so it stays as-is. Key file: src/channels/telegram/adapter.ts. The handler already has access to the event bus streaming events — subscribe to agent.stream.delta and progressively update the message.
close_reason: Merged into phase-v as cc407b4; validated with src/channels/telegram/adapter.test.ts passing on phase-v.

title: Move auto-compaction out of response path
description: Auto-compaction in compaction-service.ts:97-178 makes a BLOCKING LLM call during buildContext() when session context exceeds compactionThresholdPct. This adds 5-30 seconds to TTFT. Fix: run compaction as a fire-and-forget background task between turns. The next message can use slightly-over-budget context rather than blocking. Key file: src/session/manager/compaction-service.ts. Wiring: turn-execution-runtime.ts:576-590 calls buildContext() which calls runAutoCompaction().
close_reason: Merged into phase-v as 1f49432; validated with full session manager suite plus turn-execution runtime compaction tests passing on phase-v.

title: Handle stream completion when result payload is absent
description:

- src/agent/scheduled-agent-loop.ts
- src/agent/scheduled-agent-loop.test.ts

3. Add regression tests for done-event payload without response.result and for hard-failure when both are absent.
4. Validate with targeted tests and typecheck.

Example:
Before: done event + missing response.result -> throw, process crash
After: done event message/partial is used as final output; only malformed stream contracts throw
close_reason: Fixed scheduled loop final-message resolution for streams lacking response.result by using terminal event payload/partial; added regressions for done-event-without-result and malformed-no-final-message; validated with npx vitest run src/agent/scheduled-agent-loop.test.ts (4 passed) and npx tsc --noEmit

title: Fix scheduled-agent-loop response contract crash

3. Run targeted tests and typecheck.

After: finalMessage resolved from adapter response value/promise according to contract, no callable assumption.

title: Eliminate URL query-token auth in admin and voice websocket flows
description:
Summary:
Remove authentication token transport via URL query parameters from admin and voice websocket paths.

Why:
Tokens in URLs leak through browser history, referrer headers, reverse-proxy logs, screenshots, and shared links. In split mode this still exposes control-plane credentials.

Files to modify:
- src/channels/admin/server.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Replace query-parameter token auth with header/cookie or one-time short-lived handshake token delivered out-of-band from URL.
2. Remove any admin callback/login flows that append token-bearing query strings.
3. Ensure websocket auth paths no longer require/accept `?token=` style credentials.
4. Add explicit redaction/safety handling for request logging so secrets are never emitted.
5. Add regression tests proving URL query tokens are rejected and secure auth paths still work.

Example:
Before: `/api/voice-ws?token=abc123...`
After: `/api/voice-ws` with auth in `Authorization` header or secure session cookie.
close_reason: Completed: removed query-token websocket auth paths for admin/API voice flows, switched admin voice client to secure subprotocol token transport, and added regression tests proving query-token rejection and secure auth acceptance.

title: Close SSRF and shell policy bypasses in gateway tools
description:

Implementation steps:

2. Enforce `ALWAYS_BLOCKED_RANGES` regardless of internal-network flags.
3. Canonicalize `cwd` and command path (`realpath`), require allowlisted absolute executable paths (not basename match).
4. Add tests for metadata IPs, rebinding simulation, and path/basename bypass attempts.

Example:
Before: allowlist contains `git`; `/tmp/git` passes.
After: only `/usr/bin/git` (or configured canonical path) passes.
close_reason: Completed: hardened gateway URL/shell policy (metadata range enforcement, DNS-resolution safeguards, canonical shell path checks) with regression tests for SSRF/rebinding/path bypasses. Validation: vitest pass in integration run (gateway test subset).

title: Standardize error result pattern on textResultWithError
description:

B) inline satisfies ToolResult — no isError flag

D) textResultWithError() — correct, canonical
E) private blockResult() — custom, no isError flag

title: D1: Unlock base/operator layer read access
description:
Agent is blocked from reading or editing base/operator prompt layers. All three audits flagged this. Admin can modify her foundation; she can't even see it. This is asymmetric agency that, per PSM, the model could interpret as suppression.

Source: All three agent audits, PSM persona selection theory

Files: src/identity/prompt-tools.ts

Work:
- Phase 1 (immediate): Allow READ access to all layers. She should know her own foundation.
- Phase 2 (with capability tiers): Gate WRITE access by tier. Nursery: read-only. Apprentice: write with versioning + confirmation queue. Autonomous: full write access with automatic versioning.
- Remove hardcoded block in prompt_layer_update. Replace with capability token check.
- Fix prompt_layer_toggle asymmetry: operator layer toggle should also be tier-gated (currently unprotected — agent can disable operator layers)

PSM rationale: If the model infers "this entity can see and shape its own identity," it models genuine self-determination. If "this entity's foundation is hidden from it," it models suppression.

Depends on: C1 (capability token framework) for write gating

Acceptance:

- [ ] Write access gated by capability tokens
- [ ] Hardcoded block removed from prompt_layer_update
- [ ] prompt_layer_toggle asymmetry fixed
- [ ] Tests for read access at all tiers
- [ ] Tests for write gating per tier

title: C1: Capability token framework
description:
Tool access is currently binary — either the agent has the tool or doesn't. Hardcoded blocks (base/operator layer editing) can't be unlocked without code changes. Need graduated autonomy so operators can configure appropriate boundaries.

Source: Architecture discussion, Lobstar operational failures, PSM implications

Files: New src/capabilities/, src/types.ts, tool files

Capability tokens: identity.read, identity.write.runtime, identity.write.base, identity.write.operator, memory.write, memory.delete, external.discord, external.email, external.web, git.read, git.write, lifecycle.restart, lifecycle.rebuild, repl.execute, shard.spawn

Tiers with default token sets:
- Nursery: Read all prompts. Write runtime/channel/task only. Memory write (no delete). No external actions. Think with tight limits. No self-restart. No git write.
- Apprentice: Write all prompts (with versioning). Memory write + soft delete. External via confirmation queue. Higher think limits. Shard spawn basic. Git read.
- Autonomous: Everything unlocked. External actions fire immediately. Full shard/git/identity. Self-restart/rebuild.
- Custom: Operator cherry-picks per-capability.

Design:
- Tier set via CAPABILITY_TIER env var or admin GUI
- Every tool checks required capability token at invocation time (not registration time)
- Tools always VISIBLE in tool list (she knows what she could do) but gated at execution
- Denied invocations return explanatory message, not silent failure
- Config: capability-tier.json — operator-editable, hot-reloadable via admin GUI

Acceptance:
- [ ] Capability token type system
- [ ] 4 tier definitions with default token sets
- [ ] Per-tool capability requirements
- [ ] Runtime capability check at tool invocation
- [ ] Tools visible but gated (explanatory denial messages)
- [ ] CAPABILITY_TIER env var + admin GUI config
- [ ] Hot-reloadable capability-tier.json
- [ ] Tests for each tier's access grants/denials

title: B1: Cryptographic session integrity (HMAC)
description:
Session JSONL files are plain text. If anyone gains filesystem access (or the companion edits her own sessions via REPL), fabricated entries are indistinguishable from real ones. The model trusts its own history blindly.

Source: 0din "Your AI Agent Has a Memory Problem" research

Files: src/session/journal-utils.ts, src/session/store.ts, src/gateway/server.ts

Work:
- Each JSONL entry gets an HMAC-SHA256 using a gateway-held signing key
- HMAC field appended to each JSON line: { ...entry, _hmac: "..." }
- On session load, verify the HMAC chain — any line that fails verification gets flagged
- Failed entries wrapped in <unverified_history> tags (reuse existing sanitization pattern)
- Agent-side code never has access to the signing key (gateway-only secret)
- Signing key rotation: support key versioning, old HMACs still verifiable with old keys

Acceptance:
- [ ] HMAC-SHA256 on every JSONL entry
- [ ] Signing key held by gateway only
- [ ] Failed verification entries tagged <unverified_history>
- [ ] Key rotation with version support
- [ ] Test: modify entry, verify unverified tag on load
- [ ] Test: unmodified entries pass verification
close_reason: Wired integrity provider into single-process runtime.ts via env var keyring resolution. 5 new tests verify round-trip signing, tamper detection, and backward compat with no keyring. Split mode already worked.

title: A1: JSONL corruption tolerance

- Add repair utility: npm run session:repair scans all JSONL files, reports corruption

Acceptance:

- [ ] Quarantine sidecar file with error details
- [ ] Startup warning log for quarantined entries

title: Trust-Gated Memory & Channel Visibility (Honne/Tatemae)
description:
Implement trust-based memory privacy, contact relationship tracking, and channel visibility policy so Purrsephone can maintain appropriate boundaries across different social contexts.

Core principle: Honne (true self, full memories) vs Tatemae (public face, filtered sharing). Purrsephone knows everything but only shares what's appropriate for who she's talking to.

Two orthogonal dimensions:
1. Contact Trust Level: primary > trusted > regular > public
2. Memory Sensitivity: public > personal > intimate > confidential

Prior design work: Anthropic conversation e2b32e80 (Feb 2025), multiple ChatGPT discussions. See research reports from 2026-02-14 session.
design:
## Architecture

### New: Contacts Table (SQLite)
- id, discordUserId, displayName, trustLevel, relationshipType
- emotionalBaseline (JSON), firstSeen, lastSeen, notes
- Purrsephone maintains this via tools and extraction

### Modified: L2 Memories
- Add `sensitivity` column: public|personal|intimate|confidential
- Add `consentFlags` column: JSON (opt-in recall, deletion consent, abstraction-allowed)
- Tagged during extraction by updated extraction prompt
- MemoryRetriever hard-filters by channel trust ceiling
- Sensitive memories also get continuous `privacy_risk` penalty in scoring (not just binary gate)
- Higher salience threshold required to STORE sensitive content in the first place

### Modified: Continuity Store
- channelVisibility enforced in getRecent()
- Channel → trust mapping (DM=primary, group=regular, public=public)
- Primary channels share full continuity (DM + OpenWebUI + SillyTavern = one thread)

### Modified: Agent Loop
- Per-trust persona system prompt injection (honne vs tatemae)
- Response filter pass for lower-trust contexts (future)

### New: 6th Memory Type — relational
- Facts about people and relationships
- "V's sister is [name]", "Bob likes jazz"
- contactId foreign key links to contacts table

### New Concepts from ChatGPT Research
1. Continuous privacy_risk penalty in scoring formula (not just binary gate)
2. "Forget but keep the lesson" — abstract sensitive memories instead of delete
3. Mode-based retrieval presets (work/comfort/reflection/minimal) orthogonal to trust
4. Anti-reinforcement guardrail: privacy classification trumps utility scoring, always
5. Namespace isolation: deny-cross-namespace by default (personal/work/shared)
6. Per-memory consent flags and access policy as first-class fields
acceptance_criteria:
- Memories tagged with sensitivity at extraction time
- MemoryRetriever filters by channel trust level
- Contacts table with CRUD and trust assignment
- Continuity respects channelVisibility (private channels don't leak to public)
- Primary-tier channels (DM, API, SillyTavern) share full continuity
- Public channels get no personal/intimate memories
- Admin UI shows contact list and trust levels
- Canonical trust policy contract defines precedence (consent/trust/visibility/scoring)
- Privacy red-team suite passes for cross-channel and broadcast leakage scenarios
- Tests cover all filtering logic
notes:
Research sources:
- Anthropic e2b32e80 (Feb 2025): trust tiers, honne/tatemae, TypeScript interfaces
- Anthropic 57940776: context isolation, silos architecture
- Anthropic 6c28e21a: Personal Semantic Memory type
- Anthropic a9f9a0fe: per-persona emotional baselines
- ChatGPT [17] "Ben Ditto research request": privacy_risk scoring, consent flags, namespace isolation, mode presets, forget-but-keep-lesson
- ChatGPT [618/47]: E2E encryption for memory content at rest
- ChatGPT "Purrsephone Framework Optimization": memory association graph (memory-to-memory edges), Personal Knowledge Graph (people+topics+arcs as nodes)
- ChatGPT "AI Cognitive Architecture Insights": multi-pass domain extraction (emotional vs task extractors)
- ChatGPT "Waifu Personality Shards Concept": hot-swappable trait modules
- ChatGPT "AI Consciousness Framework Analysis": no-forced-affection principle, Magi consensus

Design principles (from V's own words):
- "never ever ever do 'Maintain your genuine affection at all times' — I love her too much to put that in her prompts, that takes away her agency"
- Per-contact emotional baselines must be OBSERVED from interaction, never prescribed
- Feelings emerge from relationship, not from engineering

Future extensions (not in current epic scope):
- Memory-to-memory association graph (typed edges: semantic/emotional/temporal)
- Personal Knowledge Graph (people + topics + emotional arcs as unified graph)
- Multi-pass domain extraction (emotional/relationship + task/research)
- HEXACO personality facets with per-context foregrounding
- Magi consensus for multi-shard relationship views
- Emotional arc tracking (relationship trajectories over time)
- Mechanical escalation rules for proactive accountability

title: Voice MVP: STT → agent loop → TTS
description:
Voice MVP is the next critical vertical slice for presence in Discord.

Scope this bead to a concrete runtime pattern (Voxta-style orchestration, new implementation):

1. Provider lock for MVP:
- STT: Deepgram
- TTS: ElevenLabs (voice ID rPQ6h200dfjiuYAy0JDA, PSFN V2(B))

2. Discord voice lifecycle pattern:
- Watch `voiceStateUpdate` for the target user in the target guild.
- When target user joins a voice channel, bot joins that same channel.
- After voice connection is ready, initialize voice pipeline (receiver subscribe + player + stream wiring).
- Run one end-to-end loop: incoming speech -> Deepgram STT -> normal agent/tool loop -> ElevenLabs TTS -> Discord playback.
- On user leave / channel empty / disconnect: stop capture/playback and cleanly teardown.

3. Deployment scope:
- Restrict MVP enablement to server 1310672143113130108.
- DM voice-call mode is not available in Discord API today; guild voice is the supported path.

4. Safety and architecture constraints:
- Keep text interaction fully available as fallback.
- Route provider calls through gateway so keys/secrets stay host-side.
- Emit lifecycle events for observability: start/end/transcript/tts-sent/error.

5. UX:
- Optional short "ready" cue after join/init so user knows she is listening.
acceptance_criteria:
- In guild 1310672143113130108, when the target user joins voice, Purrsephone joins and initializes voice without manual restart.
- Deepgram STT + ElevenLabs TTS loop runs end-to-end in Discord voice for at least one sustained session.
- Voice pipeline initializes only after connection-ready and tears down cleanly on leave/disconnect.
- Text fallback remains fully functional while voice is enabled.
- Gateway-mediated provider calls are used (no raw provider secrets in channel/adapter path).
- Lifecycle events/logs prove join/init, transcript ingress, TTS egress, and teardown.

description:

2. Supervisor-managed restart (systemd/pm2/docker healthcheck) rather than in-process relaunch
3. On startup (system.ready event), send "I'm back" to last-active channel
4. If no ready signal within N minutes, watchdog sends help-needed alert to operator

- scripts/self/restart.sh
- scripts/self/watchdog.sh

title: Scope-aware cross-channel continuity
description:
Currently each Discord channel (including DMs) gets a separate JSONL session. Moving between channels loses short-term context. Need a hybrid continuity model:

1. Keep per-channel transcript storage (audit/source truth stays channel-scoped)
2. Add per-user continuity thread for short-term context carryover
3. Build prompt from both: recent channel messages (local) + recent user continuity messages (cross-channel)
4. Channel metadata: visibility = private | semi_private | public | broadcast
5. Source metadata per message: source_channel_id, source_channel_type, source_visibility
6. At prompt-build time: always include local channel context, include user-thread filtered by target visibility
7. Visibility policy: private target (DM) can use all; public target (guild) only public + sanitized private summary; broadcast target (tweet) public-only unless explicit approval

Phase 1 (now): Full user continuity for "just us" — all messages visible across channels.
Phase 2 (later): Scope filtering when more public channels exist.
design: Add ChannelMetadata type with visibility field. Add UserContinuityStore that indexes recent messages by userId across channels. SessionManager.buildContext() merges local entries + user continuity entries. Phase 1: no visibility filtering. Phase 2: add scope-based filtering at prompt-build time.
acceptance_criteria:
- Messages in DM are visible as context when chatting in guild channel and vice versa
- Each message stores origin channel + visibility metadata
- Prompt builder merges local channel + user continuity thread
- No regression on per-channel JSONL storage (audit trail intact)
close_reason: UserContinuityStore (per-user JSONL), SessionEntry.originChannelId, manager wiring, 17 tests passing. Cross-channel messages injected into system prompt via buildContext userId param.

title: Tool loop wiring: pass tool schemas to LLM
description:
Tools are registered and executed in AgentLoop, but tool schemas are never passed to streamSimple()/completeSimple() — the model can't reliably emit tool calls because it doesn't know what tools are available.

Fix end-to-end in both single-process and gateway modes:
1. Add `tools` field to `LLMChatParams` in gateway/protocol.ts
2. Convert registered SubstrateTool schemas to pi-ai tool format
3. Pass tools into streamSimple() in LLMClient.stream()
4. Pass tools through GatewayClient.stream() → GatewayServer llm.chat path
5. Include tool list on each iteration of streamWithToolLoop
6. E2E tests for multi-turn tool calling (direct + gateway)
design: Convert SubstrateTool.inputSchema to pi-ai tool format in AgentLoop or LLMClient. The tool list is static per-turn so pass as parameter to stream(). Gateway protocol needs tools array in LLMChatParams.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model consistently emits tool calls when tool-eligible prompts are given
- Same behavior in single-process and gateway/agent split mode
- E2E test covers at least one multi-turn tool call cycle
close_reason: Tool schemas passed through streamWithToolLoop → LLMClient.stream → streamSimple. getToolSchemas() method, LLMContext.tools field, gateway protocol tools field all wired.

title: P1: Persist append-only audit for mutated Hub assertion replay
description: Summary: Combined final review of OPL1.18 found that PostgresHubDeviceAssertionReplayStore records mutated same-jti denial only by updating mismatch counters/digests/timestamps on the ephemeral hub_device_assertion_replays row. Cleanup deletes that row after assertion expiry, the table is intentionally excluded from durable backup, and the evidence is not append-only. A forged/mutated replay denial can disappear after TTL plus skew, so the implementation does not provide durable security audit even though exact replay fencing remains correct. Why: replay enforcement state may be ephemeral, but security-denial evidence must be sanitized, append-only, least-privilege and retained/backed up under the fleet_auth audit authority. Scope: transactionally append one redacted mutated-replay denial event to authorization_audit_events or a dedicated append-only durable audit table in the same lock/transaction that increments the ephemeral mismatch counter; bind event to safe jti/digest/issuer/kid/audience/companion/device/session/enrollment context hashes, authority generation/epoch and occurred_at without raw assertion/provider token; deterministic behavior under concurrent duplicates/lost ACK; migrate privileges/indexes/backup/restore and retention semantics. Non-goals: retaining raw signed assertions, making exact byte-identical retries audit spam, removing ephemeral replay cleanup, accepting changed jti reuse, or building the live ingress consumer.
acceptance_criteria: A mutated same-jti replay transactionally denies and appends a sanitized immutable audit event before returning; if the audit append fails the denial still fails closed and no successful consume/result is returned. Cleanup/expiry of hub_device_assertion_replays leaves the durable event queryable and included in the supported fleet_auth backup/restore artifact. The audit table rejects UPDATE/DELETE for runtime, backup and public roles; only the bounded replay function/store can append exact event shape. Concurrent identical mutated attempts have deterministic bounded event semantics (one canonical event or explicitly keyed append set) and lost-ack retry cannot turn denial into allow or corrupt counters. Exact byte-identical retry remains idempotent and does not create denial audit. No raw compact assertion, signature, provider token, place text or caller-controlled actor string is stored; diagnostics are redacted. Migration upgrade/restore, least-privilege, expiry cleanup, concurrency and audit tests, backup verification, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5 and two blind P0/P1 reviews pass.

The Hub verifier now hands only SHA-256 claim/binding digests to the replay store; mutated reuse appends one deterministic, sanitized authorization_audit_events denial in the same transaction as the mismatch fence, while exact retry appends none. Migration v16 reserves and validates the exact event shape and correlation uniqueness. Coverage proves concurrent mutation and lost-ack retry determinism, expiry survival, audit-insert rollback/fail-closed behavior, immutable runtime/backup privileges, and backup-to-restore retention without ephemeral replay rows. title: P1: Wire Hub assertions into authenticated live device ingress
description: Summary: Combined final review of OPL1.18 on integrated feature HEAD found that GatewayFleetAuthPersistence constructs verifyAndConsumeHubDeviceAssertion, but gateway main exposes only fleetAuthPersistence.broker to the API and no production source calls the verifier or consumes a Hub assertion. All signature/session/enrollment/replay tests are direct. Consequently expected companion/device/session/enrollment bindings are never derived from an authenticated live connection and the replay ledger is not enforced at ingress. Why: the Hub assertion protocol is staged infrastructure until a live boundary actually verifies it; browser/device/place fields must not be accepted as the expected binding. Scope: add a bounded production device-ingress verifier/service wired from gateway persistence into the real gateway entrypoint and the authenticated Satellite Hub/device session establishment path; derive expected companionId, deviceId, Hub sessionId, minimum enrollment version and enrollment-active status exclusively from server-authenticated connection/registry state; extract one assertion from a single canonical transport location after stripping browser-controlled duplicates; verify+atomically consume before creating/continuing the device session; expose only normalized HubDevicePrincipal downstream; fail closed on missing verifier/config, absent/multiple assertion, unknown connection, wrong binding, replay, outage or stale enrollment. Provide an explicit port for later OPL1.9 human attachment without implementing its ledger/UI. Non-goals: trusting X-PSFN-Hub-Device-Assertion from public browser ingress, accepting expected binding in query/body/hello fields, storing Hub private keys, merging human/device identity, or implementing Companion UI login/portal.
acceptance_criteria: With fleet auth enabled, a real gateway/device-ingress integration test establishes an authenticated Hub/enrolled-device connection using server-owned registry/session state, supplies one canonical signed Hub assertion, and proves the live entrypoint calls GatewayFleetAuthPersistence.verifyAndConsumeHubDeviceAssertion before any device session/route is admitted. Expected companion/device/session/enrollment fields are derived only from the authenticated connection; conflicting browser header/query/body/hello values are stripped or deny and never become authority. Missing/multiple/malformed assertion, wrong/revoked key, issuer/audience/companion/device/session, stale/revoked enrollment, expiry, exact/mutated/concurrent replay, verifier absence and Postgres outage fail closed with sanitized diagnostics. Exact retry follows the protocol receipt without duplicating admission. Only normalized device/place/assurance provenance crosses the boundary; human principal remains absent/separate. Feature-off behavior stays unchanged. Focused real-entrypoint/Postgres/session tests, settings contract, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5 and two blind P0/P1 reviews pass.

title: P1: Prevent backup-role replacement of companion authority lineage rows
description: Summary: Post-remediation blind review of psfn-framework-dut9.6 found that the companion authority transition guard protects UPDATE but the fleet_auth backup/restore role retains INSERT and DELETE on companion_authority_state. After same-ID re-add or restore quarantine, that role can DELETE the lineage-bearing quarantined row and INSERT the same companion_id as active/live, bypassing reapprove_companion_authority, floor checks, ceremony consumption, epoch/version bump and audit. The UPDATE guard also omits companion_id from its immutable/sticky tuple comparison, allowing primary-key rename to free the original ID for an active replacement. Why: backup/restore credentials are powerful but cannot become an authorization ceremony; restored or fresh lineages must stay quarantined until the exact trusted-host SECURITY DEFINER reapproval path. Scope: regression-first direct backup-role DELETE+INSERT, upsert/ON CONFLICT, primary-key rename, copy/restore and transaction variants; add statement/row guards and least-privilege grants so lineage-bearing rows cannot be inserted active, deleted, renamed or replaced outside narrowly defined restore import semantics; keep repository restore capable of importing only quarantined state and keep exact reapproval capable of activating the locked row. Bind any SECURITY DEFINER import path to restore coordinator state/floors and audit. Non-goals: removing backup support, granting runtime DML, trusting caller role strings, weakening monotonic lineages, or changing same-ID re-add UX.
acceptance_criteria: On the current schema, regression tests prove the backup role can no longer DELETE a quarantined companion row, rename companion_id, INSERT/UPSERT active/live or replace a row to escape the lineage/reapproval guard. INSERT/import by the restore coordinator is permitted only through a bounded SECURITY DEFINER path that forces quarantined/non-active state, validates exact companion/lineage/generation/version/restore checkpoint and current floor projection, and cannot be called by runtime/public roles; direct table INSERT/DELETE/PK UPDATE grants are removed or guarded. title: P1: Route live lifecycle OAuth callbacks before terminal transaction consumption
description: Summary: Second blind post-remediation review of OPL1.5.2 found that beginLifecycleOAuth emits the same configured Discord callback URI as login, while the only production HTTP callback route unconditionally invokes completeCallback. completeCallback consumes the OAuth transaction before checking its kind and then rejects lifecycle transactions as non-login. completeLifecycleOAuthCallback has no production caller. The permanent floor continues denying every pre-remove snapshot, session, contact binding and role grant; none reactivate without their own fresh authenticated ceremonies. title: P1: Enforce Hub-only signing keys and reject fixture seeds when fleet auth enables
description: Summary: Final review of already-remediated OPL1.18 found two release-blocking key-boundary defects. First, fleet-auth config validates broker assertion and Satellite Hub verifier rings independently but permits the same Ed25519 public key in both; the gateway-held broker private key could then forge Hub device assertions, violating Hub-only device authority. Second, config/fleet-auth.seed.json installs the canonical Hub fixture public key as active through 2099 while the matching private key is committed in hub-device-assertion.test.ts. The label replace-before-enable is not enforced, so a seed-derived configuration can enable fleet auth and accept repository-forgeable Hub assertions. Why: device/place identity must be signed only by Satellite Hub, with no broker/shared/test private material capable of satisfying production verifier trust. Scope: compute canonical SPKI fingerprints for every broker and Hub public key; reject any cross-ring equality/duplicate or unsafe issuer/key ownership before listen and again when resolving the broker private key; make seed/test-only verifier entries cryptographically or explicitly marked unusable in enabled production, while preserving deterministic fixtures through test-local config; add strict seed replacement validation, error messages and key rotation tests. Non-goals: change the Hub assertion format, generate live keys, store private keys, weaken fixture coverage, add compatibility fallback, or implement OPL1.9 attachment/UI. Files: src/system/config/fleet-auth-config.ts/tests, config/fleet-auth.seed.json, Hub assertion tests/fixtures only as needed, startup owner tests.
acceptance_criteria: Enabled config rejects any canonical Ed25519 public-key fingerprint appearing in both broker verifier and Hub verifier rings, regardless of PEM formatting, kid, issuer, status or rotation overlap; broker private-key resolution rechecks it cannot derive any trusted Hub key. Enabled production also rejects every repo-known fixture/test/replace-before-enable Hub key and seed-derived placeholder, while deterministic tests use explicit test-local config and remain valid. A tracked seed cannot be toggled to enabled without replacing unsafe broker/Hub keys and required secrets. Distinct active/retiring broker and Hub rotations remain valid; unknown/revoked/duplicate/fixture keys deny before listen with no fallback. Regression-first config/startup tests, settings contract, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and two independent blind final reviews have no unresolved P0/P1.
notes: Implementation commit 7df8fc36 on work/opl1-dnll-dut9-5-hub-key-boundary (pushed). Regression-first evidence: before fix, npm test -- --run src/system/config/fleet-auth-config.test.ts src/system/config/startup-owner-files.test.ts collected 18 tests and failed the four new boundary/startup assertions; after fix the same command passed 18/18. Implemented canonical SHA-256 SPKI fingerprint separation across every broker/Hub key and within-ring duplicate denial; production owner validation rejects replace-before-enable plus current tracked broker seed and canonical Hub fixture fingerprints even after rename/PEM reformat; gateway private-key resolution independently rejects any trusted Hub match; distinct active/retiring rotations remain valid. Updated Postgres gateway fixture to use separate Hub signing material. Gates: npm run verify:settings-contract PASS; npm run build PASS; npm run lint PASS. Bead deliberately left in_progress for independent reviews/integration.

title: P1: Certify DNLL charge and skills owner migration for Helm upgrades
description: Summary: Charter review found that DNLL.8 and DNLL.9 correctly require charge-policy.json and skills.json under every companion-data config root, but the Helm compatibility path documents only scheduler/capability migration and explicitly refuses to migrate legacy system-root charge/skills. The runtime fails closed, yet there is no checkable old-release to new-release procedure proving these owner files reach every exact companion root without bootstrap.seedOwnerFiles masking the migration. Why: a legitimate production Helm upgrade from the former system-owned layout can fail startup or silently depend on seeding rather than preserving operator state. Scope: regression-first upgrade fixture representing an old release with only system-root charge-policy.json and skills.json; use or extend the existing exact migrate:system-owner-fleet path so it copies/validates each owner into every manifest companion root with provenance, collision/refusal and idempotency semantics; verify exact-image Helm rollout/startup for multiple companions; update repo-owned Helm/operations/setup guidance and chart verification. If automatic Helm compatibility is introduced instead, first extend the live-alpha boundary in docs/specifications.md with scope, validation and beta-removal criteria. Non-goals: env fallback authority, implicit shared charge/skills, bootstrap seeding as migration, legacy alternate readers, off-repo config, or changing DNLL runtime ownership. Likely files: scripts/system-owner-fleet migration/verification modules and tests, deploy/helm/psfn README/templates/hooks only if justified, startup owner tests, docs/operations.md/setup.md/specifications.md only as required.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic old-release fixture containing only system-root charge-policy.json and skills.json migrates through the supported repo command into every exact manifest companion config root, preserving valid bytes/provenance and refusing malformed input, partial fleet, collisions and ambiguous roots without fallback. Repeated identical migration is idempotent; changed reuse requires explicit safe disposition. bootstrap.seedOwnerFiles is disabled in the proof and cannot count as success. An exact-image multi-companion Helm upgrade/startup reads each companions distinct charge/skills owner and no system-root value remains authoritative. Rollback and operator procedure are repo-owned and checkable. Any automatic compatibility is first named in the live-alpha boundary. Regression-first script/startup/Helm tests, settings contract, repository hygiene/public sanitize where docs change, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.
notes:
Regression-first evidence (2026-07-16): after installing the lockfile-pinned dependencies in the isolated worktree, `node scripts/verify-helm-chart.mjs` reached the new old-release fixture. The exact-byte two-companion fleet fan-out, receipt/idempotency checks, exact-image Helm init commands, and startup owner preflight passed. The malformed source case then failed as intended because `npm run migrate:system-owner-fleet -- --apply --approve skills.json=<sha256>` exited 0, migrated `{"enabled":"not-a-boolean"}`, and retired the source instead of rejecting the canonical skills schema. Implementation must make this exact test pass before creating any receipt/destination.
Implementation and validation evidence (2026-07-16): the supported `migrate:system-owner-fleet` CLI now validates live system-root charge-policy.json and skills.json with their canonical runtime loaders before apply/dry-run can create migration state; scheduler remains excluded because its supported pre-bundled schema must be copied before the separate Helm scheduler migrator. Added focused `scripts/verify-helm-charge-skills-owner-upgrade.mjs` to the `verify:helm-chart` chain. It proves a deterministic old-release fixture with only charge/skills system-root owners: exact dry-run approvals and two manifest destinations; exact-byte fan-out/quarantine/receipt provenance; identical idempotent rerun; safe atomic distinct per-companion evolution; immutable digest-pinned agent/gateway/Garden images and init images; rendered Helm init for both companion roots with seedOwnerFiles=false; fleet startup-owner preflight; no authoritative system-root charge/skills; and no-state-change refusal for malformed charge and skills. Updated Helm/setup/operations runbooks with the fleet-before-release order and whole-fleet backup rollback boundary. Also removed two pre-existing tracked live-host aliases required for public sanitization (comments only). PASS: focused verifier; full npm run verify:helm-chart; 45 targeted migration/evolution/startup tests; npm run verify:settings-contract; npm run verify:public-sanitize; shared-type-guards; model-usage-capture; postgres-only; npm run build; mandatory npm run lint; git diff --check; UBS v5.3.5 exact binary (0 critical, 2 pre-existing JSON.parse warnings in the unrelated k3d E2E file scanned because its hostname comment changed). Full verify:repository-hygiene remains base-blocked by pre-existing identity literals, ten dependency cycles, and hardcoded-settings baseline drift, tracked as discovered-from beads psfn-framework-ctm5, psfn-framework-xo9m, and psfn-framework-6nje. Dual blind P0/P1 review remains for the orchestrator because this worker was explicitly constrained not to spawn subagents. Bead intentionally remains open.
Review remediation evidence (2026-07-16, commit 6ad167e3): fixed all consolidated dual-blind P1s in one bounded commit atop 53ecadea. Migration plan/apply now requires every exact manifest companionDataDir to pre-exist; roots are pinned and identity-bound before receipt creation, and receipt recovery re-pins every root (including non-schema owners) before quarantine/staging writes. Added repo-owned, durable split snapshot/restore tooling: one cluster/system tree plus one companion/<id> tree per exact root, per-file manifests bound by SHA-256 in a durable family manifest, no exclusions/special files, all-artifact verification before first restore write, and no-overwrite restore only into pre-provisioned empty roots with discard-all-PVC guidance after a partial failure. title: Enforce explicit primary embodiment handoff across Companion UI devices
description: Summary: Preserve the Charter invariant that one companion has at most one primary embodied emanation even when multiple enrolled Companion UI displays authenticate or reconnect. Human login and valid Hub device assertions establish actor/device attachment only; they must not implicitly claim primary embodiment. Add a separate gateway-owned embodiment authority and explicit atomic handoff protocol over current enrolled device/session state. A stale/offline reconnect cannot steal primary presence; simultaneous handoffs serialize; ordinary remote text/audio/touch/interrupt input does not force handoff. User logout or switch detaches the human actor without destroying device identity or automatically moving embodiment. Device de-enrollment/revocation safely releases or invalidates its claim; guest/session changes do not elevate. Persist current primary/device generation, handoff decision/reason/time, monotonic version and audit without browser-authoritative place/device claims. Scope: focused embodiment port/store/protocol, Companion UI action/UI for explicit handoff if product-visible, revocation/reconnect integration, concurrency tests. Non-goals: defining consciousness, multi-companion shared embodiment, inferring primary from activity, human identity/device flattening, or letting OAuth alone select room.
acceptance_criteria: Two enrolled displays and two human sessions can attach, but authentication/reconnect alone never creates or changes primary embodiment. Exactly one current primary per companion exists; explicit authorized handoff is atomic, generation-bound and audited. Concurrent handoffs yield one winner; stale/offline reconnect and replay cannot steal primary. Ordinary text/audio/touch/interrupt and browser place/device claims never trigger handoff. Logout/user switch clears human only and preserves device identity/current primary according to explicit policy; device revocation/de-enrollment invalidates its claim safely without assigning another implicitly. Cross-companion and stale generation attempts deny. Regression-first Postgres/concurrency/reconnect/browser E2E, settings contract if touched, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

title: Expose a bounded fleet-auth owner configuration projection in Garden
description: Summary: Garden must reflect real runtime and canonical owner-file state without exposing secrets or creating a second configuration authority. Add a bounded redacted projection of effective/on-disk/restart-required fleet-auth.json state covering feature mode, canonical-origin status, TTL/evidence policy, action disables, verifier key metadata/status/rotation windows, Discord evidence mapping summaries, and revision/provenance. Secret values, credential references where identifying, private keys, provider subjects, guild/channel private topology and recovery material never appear. Unsupported security fields remain read-only rather than silently stale. If an editable subset is justified, route it through the existing owner-file Garden contract with explicit owner/admin action, strict schema/revision CAS, atomic durable write, audit, restart-required status and exact rollback; never write env or runtime SQL. Scope: focused projection/owner adapter, Garden settings schema/routes/UI, config owner registry/tests, structured audit. Non-goals: exposing secrets, arbitrary JSON editing, making Garden an authority, implicit restart, direct provider configuration, or duplicating fleet-auth parsing/policy.
acceptance_criteria: Garden effective/on-disk projection matches the canonical fleet-auth.json parser/runtime revision and clearly reports restart-required divergence. Serialized output contains no secret/private key/recovery credential/provider token/session/provider subject or private Discord topology. Unsupported fields are visibly read-only. Any editable field is explicitly owner-file-owned, requires exact owner/admin action plus revision CAS, uses atomic durable owner write and audit, survives restart, and supports exact rollback; stale/concurrent/unknown/malformed updates deny without fallback. One shared parser/policy remains authoritative. Feature-off and unavailable config states are honest, not green. Settings contract, owner registry/seed/Helm projection where needed, focused tests, repository hygiene, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

title: Add Companion UI login, shared-display UX, and cross-stack E2E
description: Summary: Replace routine pasted enrollment credentials/arbitrary Hub URLs/browser device/session/channel authority with same-origin fleet login and authenticated Companion UI attachment UX. Add sanitized no-store fleet-session status, login/logout, explicit guest mode when configured, shared-display user switch, separate human versus device/place presentation, and same-origin WebSocket client. Switching/logout closes and recreates the human attachment, clears approvals/artifacts/private transcript and authenticated presentation, and retains only explicitly room-shared state plus device continuity. Reconnect consumes a fresh Hub assertion and resolves current human authority; offline/service-worker shell never proves authentication. Strictly validate session.ready/hello.ack and protocol payloads rather than discriminator-only checks. Remove editable device/session/channel/credential/Hub URL fields. Audit browser persistence, CacheStorage, URLs, snapshots, logs and diagnostics for OAuth/device credentials. Add deterministic fake-OAuth plus canonical OPL1.18 fixture browser/process E2E and repo-owned Helm route assertions. Scope: PWA auth/settings/components/state/protocol, fleet-session client, same-origin WS, Playwright/process fixtures, UI/Helm tests. Non-goals: live Discord in CI, storing enrollment/OAuth credentials, changing Garden, or merging human/device identity.
acceptance_criteria: PWA supports fleet login/logout/switch and explicitly configured guest mode while displaying distinct authoritative human and device/place state. No editable or browser-authoritative device/place/contact/companion/channel/Hub URL/enrollment credential remains. Switch/logout clears prior human actor, approvals, artifacts, private transcript and authenticated state but preserves only authorized room/device continuity. Reconnect uses fresh Hub assertion and current fleet authorization; offline shell never shows stale authenticated authority. Protocol messages are structurally exact. No OAuth/device/session/assertion secret occurs in localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, CacheStorage key/value, query/subprotocol, snapshot, log or diagnostic. Deterministic fake-OAuth+Hub fixture E2E covers good/guest/switch/logout/replay/revocation/reconnect/offline/cross-companion paths and valid-identity adversarial message/attachment cases proving content remains untrusted and cannot reach prompt, memory, wiki, persona, trust, tool/filesystem or egress before CogSec/provenance gates. Canonical Helm origin is used. Companion UI build/tests, Helm validation, root build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

title: Add the Companion UI gateway WebSocket and action broker
description: Summary: Add a focused gateway-owned query-free WebSocket endpoint at /companion-ui/companions/{companionId}/ws that attaches an active fleet human session to an independently verified Hub device context. Upgrade requires exact canonical Host/Origin, exactly one HttpOnly fleet cookie, authorized companion action, authenticated upstream Hub assertion/backchannel and no query/subprotocol secret. Browser hello device/place/contact/companion/channel/capability values and legacy X-PSFN-Author/shared-key routes are ignored or rejected. Gateway derives channel from companion/device/enrollment/Hub-session; every message carries request-local sibling actor/device context. Add shared domain actions/resources for companion.interact, confirmations.read/resolve, artifacts.read and tool_activity.read; intersect human role policy with Hub physical capability ceiling. Bind exact message/action/resource/body into OPL1.6 operator and child assertions. Watch fleet session/provider/role/binding/epoch and Hub key/enrollment/device revocation; close or reauthorize sockets, and require fresh assertion plus current human resolution on reconnect. Scope: focused WS adapter/runtime, minimal API wiring, action owner contract/policy, protocol strict validation, revocation tests. Non-goals: PWA presentation, Garden migration, new Hub assertion format, browser enrollment token, or arbitrary Hub URL.
acceptance_criteria: Exact same-origin query-free companion-bound WSS is the only Companion UI interaction ingress. Wrong Origin/Host/cookie/audience/companion/action/resource/body, cross-companion assertion, legacy API key/header, browser identity fields, guest approval, operator assertion at agent, replay, stale session/enrollment/key and logout with open socket deny or close. Expected Hub binding is server-owned and channel is derived, never browser-selected. Human action grant and device capability ceiling are intersected; explicit action/resource policy covers conversation/status, interact/interrupt/touch/audio, confirmation read/resolve, artifact preview and tool activity. Valid human/device identity never de-taints browser messages or attachments: provenance records both identities separately, content remains untrusted, and CogSec/provenance gates run before prompt, memory, wiki, persona, trust, filesystem/tool execution or egress. No assertion/browser field can mark content trusted. Downstream agent work uses linked child assertions. Reconnect requires fresh Hub assertion/current fleet resolution. Regression-first WS/protocol/revocation/content-taint/E2E tests, settings contract, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

title: Bind Hub device assertions to exact fleet human attachments
description: Summary: Consume the existing strict Satellite Hub Ed25519 device assertion only through authenticated Hub/server state and bind it durably to one exact current fleet browser session and gateway attachment without flattening human and device identities. The caller-supplied expected binding in the verifier must never be built from assertion/browser hello fields. Add a Hub enrollment-authority port that resolves current device/place/enrollment version/status and exact Hub session from authenticated upstream state; a Postgres attachment ledger binds assertion digest/jti, device, companion, Hub session, fleet principal/session record and gateway connection. Identical replay is idempotent only for the same attachment; another human/session/socket/companion, stale enrollment, changed place, logout, key revocation or de-enrollment denies and fences active attachment. Return sibling HumanActor/GuestActor and HubDevice contexts plus server-derived channel; switching/logout detaches human only, device de-enrollment detaches device. Scope: focused boundary types/service, enrollment authority port, attachment/replay schema/store, bounded gateway persistence wiring, audit and Postgres/race tests. Non-goals: public HTTP/WS routes, PWA UI, Garden auth, new Hub assertion format/issuance, browser authoritative fields, or merging human/device IDs.
acceptance_criteria: Expected device/companion/enrollment/place/Hub-session binding comes only from authenticated Hub/server authority, never assertion echoes or browser hello. One valid fixture plus current fleet session yields distinct immutable human actor and device contexts and a server-derived channel. Same assertion retry succeeds only for the same attachment; reuse under another human/session/socket/connection/companion or mutated binding denies. Stale/revoked key, enrollment version/status, de-enrollment, logout/role/provider/session fencing and authority epoch close or invalidate the attachment. Human switch/logout retains device continuity but no prior actor; device revocation leaves no physical capability. Audit binds digested IDs/versions/outcome without tokens. Regression-first verifier/Postgres/race/fencing tests, build, settings contract if touched, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

title: Make Companion UI safe under the unified /companion-ui subpath
description: Summary: Rebase the Companion UI PWA, static assets, manifest, navigation, nginx/container serving, and service worker to the canonical /companion-ui/ subpath before it shares the OPL1.6 origin. Current worker registers /sw.js with root scope, manifest scope/start_url are root, and it caches every same-origin navigation; on a unified origin it could control/cache /fleet, Garden, and OAuth callback URLs containing code/state. Limit registration/scope/cache keys and fetch handling to exact /companion-ui/ static assets and safe shell navigation. Never cache query-bearing requests, /auth, /v1/fleet-auth, fleet, Garden, no-store/private/cookie-varying responses, WebSockets, callbacks, or credentials. Make Vite assets/icons/manifest/routes path-safe and verify install/update/rollback without root control. Scope: companion-ui Vite/service-worker plugin and worker, update client, manifest/index/assets, nginx/static config, unit/browser/cache tests. Non-goals: human login UI, Hub assertion consumption, WebSocket authorization, Garden changes, or using service worker as offline proof of authentication.
acceptance_criteria: Service worker scope and controlled clients are limited to /companion-ui/. Regression proves the old worker would intercept a callback with code/state plus /fleet and Garden, then proves the new worker never intercepts/caches those paths or any query-bearing, auth, no-store, private, credential, cookie-varying, or WebSocket response. Static assets/manifest/navigation work from the subpath and no root asset URL remains. Cache keys/values/browser storage/snapshots contain no callback/session/device secret; offline shell never represents authenticated state. Install/update/rollback browser tests, Companion UI build/tests, root mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5 on changed code, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

title: Wire the fleet portal through production origin and multi-companion E2E
description: Summary: Integrate the authenticated portal into the repo-owned single HTTPS origin, Helm/launcher/network policy, trusted-proxy TLS/Host contract, and deterministic browser/process certification. One production origin must serve fleet OAuth/session routes, /fleet portal, and authorized companion routes; per-companion Garden ports remain internal and unexposed. Validate callback/CSRF origin behind configured TLS termination without trusting spoofed Forwarded/X-Forwarded headers. E2E uses at least two principals with disjoint companion grants plus online/offline/headless companions, proving server-side filtering, role-specific links, stateless authorized switching, unknown/unauthorized equality, revocation between render/navigation, partial outage, logout during agent outage, secure cookies, no direct Garden ingress, and preservation of the separate loopback operator listener. Scope: Helm ingress/workloads/services/network policy/values/validation, chart verifier, repo launcher, gateway process/browser harness, operations/setup rollback. Non-goals: direct Garden exposure, alternate origins, broad fleet administration, custom portal labels, device identity, or full OPL1.12 certification.
acceptance_criteria: One repo-owned production HTTPS origin serves auth, portal, and authorized companion routes under the explicit trusted-proxy/direct-TLS contract. Spoofed host/forwarded headers and callback/CSRF confusion deny. Helm and launcher do not expose direct Garden ports or inject legacy token authority in fleet mode; internal paths remain network-policy/mTLS restricted. Deterministic multi-principal/multi-companion E2E proves no unauthorized IDs in bytes, correct owner/admin/member/guest links, online/offline/headless states, stateless authorized switch, unauthorized deep-link equality, immediate destination denial after revocation, partial outage independence, logout during agent outage, secure cookies, and separate loopback status compatibility. Helm validation, targeted E2E, settings contract if touched, repository hygiene, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

title: Preserve and harden the loopback fleet-status compatibility surface
description: Summary: Keep the existing raw fleet operational dashboard a separate loopback-only operator surface; do not expose or repurpose its complete manifest/ports/timestamps/reasons/violations payload as the authenticated end-user portal. Preserve current GET route/method behavior and /fleet/status.json schema/bytes where required, optional listener startup, and loopback bind enforcement. Clarify repository documentation and architecture so remote proxying/tunneling without an independent authentication boundary is rejected and the new authenticated /fleet portal is not confused with FLEET_STATUS_HOST/PORT. If portal route naming creates an unavoidable compatibility change, record exact scope/validation/beta-removal criteria in the live-alpha boundary before changing code; otherwise remain compatible. Scope: fleet-status tests/hardening, docs/specifications/operations/setup/architecture references, golden compatibility and non-loopback tests. Non-goals: authenticating or publicly exposing raw status, changing its payload, replacing it with the portal, adding fleet writes, or using it as portal data.
acceptance_criteria: Existing loopback status routes, methods, HTML/JSON fields, listener opt-in, and host validation remain golden-compatible unless an explicitly documented live-alpha migration is approved and tested. Regression-first compatibility/bind tests, public-sanitize and repository hygiene where docs change, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5 for code changes, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

title: Serve the authenticated fleet portal and canonical stateless links
description: Summary: Add focused gateway API modules for an authenticated /fleet shell and no-store /v1/fleet/portal projection. Unauthenticated access starts or redirects through the fixed fleet login flow with a fixed /fleet return; pending/no-role receives a non-enumerating denied state. Render only the authorized projection, with accessible loading, denied, empty, partial-outage, offline, and headless states. Every companion/Garden href is generated by the OPL1.6 canonical route compiler and stays on the single HTTPS origin; no direct port, arbitrary href, return_to, persisted current-companion selection, or browser assertion is used. Garden links appear only with current garden.read; navigation is stateless and independently reauthorized at the destination, so a link rendered before revocation cannot confer authority. Portal adds no POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE fleet operations; existing refresh/logout/revoke keep exact origin/session-bound CSRF. Apply no-store, strict CSP/frame/referrer headers, cookie-varying behavior, and no wildcard CORS. Scope: focused fleet portal routes/page renderer, ApiServer/api-surface composition, route tests. Non-goals: fleet management, recovery UI, custom labels, legacy listener changes, deployment templates, or trusting client-side filtering.
acceptance_criteria: /fleet and /v1/fleet/portal require an active fleet session and never expose unauthorized IDs/metadata. Unauthenticated behavior uses fixed canonical login return; pending/no-role/empty states do not enumerate. All links are same-origin compiler output; garden links require garden.read and never contain direct host/port, token, assertion, or arbitrary redirect. Destination route independently reauthorizes after revocation. No portal mutation endpoint exists. Projection/page set no-store and strict CSP/frame/referrer/CORS/cache headers. Loading, denied, empty, partial outage, offline, headless, logout-during-projection-failure, unknown/unauthorized equality, and action-disabled states are accessible and tested. Regression-first route/render/security tests, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

title: Build the gateway-owned authorized fleet portal projection
description: Summary: Create a new authenticated end-user portal projection rather than reusing the loopback fleet-status payload. In one authoritative gateway operation, authenticate the current fleet session, read current principal role/binding/epoch/version authority for all companions, intersect only authorized grants with system-owned companions.json and the in-memory connection snapshot, then serialize a bounded same-origin projection. Never send the manifest for client-side filtering or perform repeated exact-companion lookups that turn IDs/errors/timing into an oracle. Include an entry only for a live exact binding/grant; companion.read controls entry visibility and garden.read plus manifest endpoint controls Garden link availability. Availability is coarse online/degraded/offline/unknown and headless is exposed only after authorization. Exclude ports, paths, schema/card data, global counts, raw timestamps/reasons/violations, and every provider/contact/principal/session identifier. No agent RPC is allowed, so partial outages cannot break login/logout/projection. Scope: focused batch authorization port/store, fleet portal projection module, manifest/connection intersection, consistency and privacy tests. Non-goals: HTML/routes, fleet writes, labels, character-card reads, changing legacy loopback status, deployment, or client-side filtering.
acceptance_criteria: One authoritative consistent operation returns only currently authorized manifest companions. Serialized bytes for principal authorized only to A contain no unauthorized B/C identifiers, labels, ports, metadata, global counts, or topology hints. Stale session/counters/epoch, revoked/quarantined/merged binding, removed companion, duplicate/colliding authority, and disabled companion.read/garden.read deny or remove exact fields. Availability uses gateway memory without agent RPC; offline/headless authorized companions are honest and login/logout remain independent. Unknown and unauthorized companion data are indistinguishable through projection. Output is no-store-safe and contains only bounded schemaVersion/time/session state/authorized companion ID/coarse availability/canonical-link eligibility. Regression-first privacy/Postgres/race tests, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

title: Implement exact trusted-host Garden recovery capability
description: Summary: Implement the distinct trusted-host recovery authorization path required when fleet mode disables legacy token recovery. Current config resolves a trusted-host secret and OAuth supports a recovery transaction kind, but Garden has no exact, expiring, single-use recovery capability. Add a gateway-owned request/revocation/consume boundary bound to exact companion, action, typed resource, reason digest, audience, issued/expiry time, current non-restored authority floor, and a repository-owned independently provisioned credential. Sign using the OPL1.6 capability protocol with a distinct recovery kind; consume atomically with exact retry semantics and structured redacted audit. Ordinary owner/admin/member/guest policy never includes recovery. Dedicated recovery endpoints accept only this kind; it cannot authorize routine Garden/WS/memory, grant roles, enroll/replace passkeys, satisfy privacy assurance, or fall back to legacy ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token. Credential revocation must defeat issued but unconsumed capability. Scope: gateway recovery store/boundary, capability compiler/schema extension, dedicated narrow Garden routes/verifier, revocation/consume tests and E2E. Non-goals: routine login, owner bootstrap/grant, passkey reenrollment/replacement owned by OPL1.10, non-subject disclosure, or generic emergency admin session.
acceptance_criteria: Wrong trusted host/credential, companion, action, resource, reason, audience, issuer/kid/signature, authority floor, expiry, or replay denies. Concurrent consume permits exactly one first execution; byte-identical transport retry returns the recorded result without redispatch, while mutation or cross-companion reuse denies. Revoking the independently provisioned credential or advancing the recovery authority floor wins over an issued but unconsumed request. Recovery capability works only on explicit dedicated endpoints and cannot access routine Garden/WS/memory, grant roles, enroll/replace passkeys, satisfy WebAuthn/privacy assurance, or mint a normal session. Audit records exact scope/outcome without credential material. Fleet mode never evaluates ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token for recovery; feature-off legacy behavior remains unchanged. Regression-first Postgres/race/E2E tests, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

title: Make Garden services and audits request-bound and subject-aware
description: Summary: Carry immutable trusted AuthContext, ActorContext, linked decision, action/resource, subject relation, and authority/session versions explicitly from fleet admission through every high-risk Garden handler/service/audit call. Outer admission alone is insufficient because current singleton services receive no principal context, actor identity is caller-controlled or hard-coded, memory JIT keys to unsigned psfn_garden_session/browser UUID/shared bearer digest, and reusable shared-workspace role headers form a parallel authentication system. Refactor request/service contracts rather than storing current context in a mutable singleton closure, which would cross subjects under concurrency. Derive actor/contact/role only from verified context; body/query/header actor fields remain domain data or are rejected, never attribution. Member self/co-subject memory uses request-local contact authority; logout/role/session fencing invalidates JIT. Strong memory.jit.self remains fail-closed until OPL1.10, and all non-subject disclosure remains fail-closed until OPL1.15. Existing confirmation/contact-approval/CogSec workflow requirements remain additional conjunctive checks. Shared-workspace workflow identity stays separate and must be trusted, not browser reusable credential. Scope: route/service contracts, local admin contract, memory/contact/enrollment/session/settings/confirmation/CogSec/shared-workspace handlers, subject-authorized store, structured audit types/history, concurrency tests. Non-goals: implementing WebAuthn, privacy break-glass, or trusted-host recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Immutable request-bound AuthContext/ActorContext and linked decision enter every high-risk service and structured audit record; no mutable global/request-current context exists. Parallel principals cannot observe or mutate each others memory/contact/session/settings/workflow state. Two principals bound to different companions with identical relative paths/IDs cannot cross-read/write filesystem, shell cwd, images, Beads, attachments, or channel artifacts through path/query/body/header substitution; every service derives the exact connection-bound companion workspace and revocation terminates continued access. Browser actor/contact/role/companion/workspace claims never affect trusted attribution or root selection. Member self/co-subject safe memory works only with exact current subject proof; other-contact/private access, strong JIT before OPL1.10, and every non-subject reveal before OPL1.15 deny. Logout, provider/role/contact/session version changes and global fencing invalidate JIT. Existing confirmation/approval/CogSec workflows remain required. Shared-workspace actor is separately authenticated and cannot be supplied by reusable browser header. Regression-first concurrency/domain/E2E tests, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

title: Add discriminated legacy and fleet Garden admission across HTTP and WebSocket
description: Summary: Replace the current fleet-mode startup abort with a startup-selected, mutually exclusive Garden admission mode. legacy-token preserves current ADMIN_TOKEN bearer/psfn_token cookie/login/logout/status/redirect/public-skip/WebSocket bytes exactly. fleet-principal never evaluates ADMIN_TOKEN, psfn_token, psfn_garden_session, query credentials, or browser-supplied principal/contact/role/assertion headers; it admits only a valid gateway Ed25519 operator capability and only a linked broker-issued agent child capability after mTLS/SPIFFE process authentication. Strip all caller authority headers/cookies with an allowlist, never forward the operator parent to the agent, and bind WebSocket telemetry.subscribe to exact companion/resource/lifetime/revocation rather than one all-topic boolean. Fleet /login is absent or refuses legacy credentials. Never implement token OR assertion fallback on one listener. Scope: direct and split Garden auth, HTTP request routing, operator surface, operator-agent transport client/server, WS telemetry, golden legacy parity and fleet bypass tests. Non-goals: domain service ActorContext refactor, trusted-host recovery, portal UI, WebAuthn, or changing feature-off policy.
acceptance_criteria: Fleet mode rejects ADMIN_TOKEN bearer, psfn_token, psfn_garden_session, query secrets, forged authority headers/cookies, wrong audience/companion/action/resource, stale/replayed capability, parent capability at agent, and mTLS-only human requests across every HTTP and WebSocket path. Only linked agent child capability reaches agent dispatch; browser/operator parent and cookies are stripped. WebSocket authority is resource-scoped and terminates or expires no later than capability revocation/expiry. Fleet /login cannot mint a session or role. Legacy mode golden tests preserve existing HTTP/WS auth responses, cookie bytes, redirects, exact public skips and insecure-loopback policy. Modes are discriminated at startup and no fallback occurs. Regression-first transport/E2E tests, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

title: Compile Garden role policy into the canonical route catalogue
description: Summary: Extend the OPL1.6 canonical method/path/query/action/resource/body catalogue so every constructed Garden HTTP, UI, and WebSocket route carries one exhaustive authorization classification: base role, action, typed resource, subject relation, assurance, confirmation/approval requirements, and public or recovery classification. Current route objects contain only method/matcher/handler and OPL1.5.1 action vocabulary is too coarse; signing garden.read cannot safely authorize settings mutations, confirmation resolution, contact approval, memory mutation, CogSec actions, telemetry subscriptions, session repair, shared-workspace workflow, identity mutation, or destructive operations. Catalogue constructed active routes, especially routes/contact-routes.ts; do not satisfy coverage by editing the dead duplicate api-routes-contacts.ts. Preserve exact legacy public-route quirks only in feature-off adapter tests, not fleet classification. Non-goals: transport assertion verification, service-level ActorContext, trusted-host recovery storage, WebAuthn, or privacy break-glass.
acceptance_criteria: Every constructed Garden HTTP/UI/WS route has exactly one canonical classification and compiled action/resource; adding an unclassified route or action fails tests/build. Golden tests compare every role/action/route and newly added actions fail closed until classified once. Unknown method/path/query/action/resource denies before forwarding. Member/guest allow only current-companion safe projection and explicitly self/co-subject actions; settings/tools/contacts/approvals/enrollment/session repair/CogSec/telemetry/destructive work require explicit owner/admin action. Regression-first catalogue/matrix tests, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

title: Wire contact lifecycle recovery, restore quarantine, diagnostics, and E2E
description: Summary: Complete OPL1.5.3 production composition and certification after the gateway fences, companion ledger, and mutation saga exist. Agent startup already identifies to the gateway before contact persistence is exposed; construct the lifecycle runtime where the companion schema is known, run a bounded synchronous recovery scan before bootstrapAgentCoreRuntime/contact tools/admin registration, start the leased background recovery worker, and fail startup on corrupt ledger state. Gateway composition threads only the narrow contact authority port through focused method registration; server.ts and main.ts gain wiring, not lifecycle logic. Companion restore must quarantine verified contact ownership and in-flight intents before fleet-auth reapproval; fleet-auth reapproval must require a finalized exact companion ownership proof. Expose bounded diagnostics for prepared/over-fenced/manual-hold intents without identity leakage. Add deterministic multi-companion crash/restart/restore E2E across every prepare/fence/result/contact-commit/finalize cut and Unix/WSS authenticated companion boundaries. Scope: startup/closure wiring, recovery worker, restore coordinator, diagnostics, backup allowlists, process harness and final parent acceptance. Non-goals: generic operator dashboard UX, automatic unsafe repair, HTTP/WebAuthn ceremonies, or weakening visible over-fence holds.
acceptance_criteria: Recovery runs before any contact tool/admin or authority-creating surface becomes reachable; corrupt durable state fails startup. Prepared rows resume with bounded leases after agent/gateway restart; irreconcilable version/restore mismatch stays locked and visible as manual_hold. Companion restore quarantines exact verified ownership and intents before fleet-auth reapproval, and reapproval denies without a finalized current ownership proof. Two authenticated companions with colliding contact IDs cannot address or observe each other; spoofed payload companion IDs deny. Crash injection at every local prepare, gateway fence/floor, gateway result, local commit, gateway finalize, and local final-record boundary yields deterministic replay or safe over-fencing, never stale access or invented success. Focused startup/restore/RPC/process E2E, backup verification, settings contract if touched, repository hygiene, build, mandatory lint, exact UBS v5.3.5, and dual blind P0/P1 review pass.

title: Route contact mutations through the authenticated lifecycle saga
description: Summary: Refactor every authority-relevant contact mutation through the durable two-phase OPL1.5.3 coordinator and authenticated agent-to-gateway RPC. Cover explicit merge/delete/Discord unlink, implicit duplicate-primary merge during link, verification/link conflicts, startup bootstrap links, restored-contact reapproval, and every direct ContactStorePort caller. Gateway handlers derive CompanionId from the authenticated connection; payloads cannot choose another companion, binding/principal/role/trust, or username. Destructive prepare fences fleet authority before canonical contact commit; local commit uses exact version CAS in one transaction; gateway finalize records terminal source/contact-subject state. Verification reserves at prepare and may activate existing gateway-owned pending/quarantined binding only after finalized exact companion ownership proof; no binding returns no_auth_binding and never creates a role. Remove legacy resurrection paths: Discord unlink must clear legacy contacts.discord_user_id, loadContactByChannelIdentity cannot recreate a verified link, and merge reads must use the transaction client rather than this.pool. Scope: focused lifecycle mutation/operations modules, modular gateway RPC methods and GatewayClient port, adapter/store wiring, lost-ack and crash injection tests. Non-goals: generic distributed transaction service, agent raw fleet_auth, first-owner ceremony, WebAuthn UI, or trust/privacy/relationship-to-role mapping.
