Preserve exact-concatenation, no-mid-token, bounded-look-ahead, and fail-closed content-gate laws.

Non-goals: do not change built-in abbreviation protocol, voice security byte limits, eligibility policy, or introduce env authority.
acceptance_criteria: The canonical owner file is authoritative for both live segmenter thresholds; invalid or incoherent values reject; API voice production wiring supplies the resolved config; Garden and seed/default contracts cover the fields; segmenter law tests still pass; temporary xv84 baseline entries are removed; npm run verify:settings-contract, npm run verify:hardcoded-settings, targeted tests, npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Completed in 9c4a733f. settings.json now owns strict voiceReplySegmenter min/max thresholds, validates positive integers and max > min, exposes them through Garden's voice editor, and threads them into the live API committed-segment bridge. The segmenter/bridge no longer contain or accept silent threshold defaults; abbreviation, concatenation, no-mid-token, look-ahead, and content-gate behavior remain intact. Both temporary xv84 baseline entries were removed. Validation: 7 focused suites / 99 tests passed; verify:settings-contract and verify:hardcoded-settings passed; npm run build passed; mandatory full npm run lint passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Own startup wiki hydration volume in canonical runtime settings

title: Move durable background-work tuning into canonical scheduler settings
description:
Context: psfn-framework-xv84 found mutable durable background-work policy still expressed as module defaults. The affected production paths are src/core/agent/background-work/supervisor.ts (max concurrent sessions, lease duration, retry base/max delays, shutdown drain timeout, terminal retention, cleanup cadence), src/core/agent/background-work/post-turn-runtime.ts (foreground-preemption and extraction-drain defer delays), and src/core/agent/substrate-agent.ts around the BackgroundWorkSupervisor construction. Production currently takes the defaults because the constructor seam is not wired.

Scope: define this complete background-work tuning group in the canonical scheduler.json owner contract; add strict parsing/types/seed values, thread the resolved settings through the real startup composition, expose the owner fields through Garden, and cover runtime wiring plus validation. Include the pre-existing lease/retention defaults so the domain does not remain partially hardcoded. Reject malformed or missing security-sensitive data according to the existing owner contract.

Non-goals: do not weaken durable queue invariants, effect fencing, payload validation, database safety ceilings, retry semantics, or add environment-variable authority. Do not create a second settings owner.
acceptance_criteria: scheduler.json is authoritative for all listed background-work tuning; production passes the resolved values to the supervisor and post-turn runtime; strict owner parsing and seed defaults are tested; Garden can read/edit the fields through the existing governed surface; module-level mutable defaults and any temporary xv84 baseline refusals are removed; npm run verify:settings-contract, npm run verify:hardcoded-settings, targeted tests, npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
notes: Implemented on work/companion-life-leg6 in commit 8ce9395e after rebasing onto integration base f70006d2. Validation passed: 130 focused tests across scheduler config, Garden, startup reachability, supervisor, post-turn runtime, and owner migration; verify:settings-contract; verify:hardcoded-settings; full npm run lint; npm run build; git diff --check. Bead intentionally remains open for root review and integration.
close_reason: Completed and integrated in db9e6033 (worker commit 8ce9395e). scheduler.json now strictly owns durable background supervisor and post-turn tuning, startup/Garden wiring is live, all module defaults and seven temporary baseline entries were removed. Independent root validation: 9 affected suites / 158 tests passed; verify:settings-contract and verify:hardcoded-settings passed. Worker validation additionally passed full npm run lint and npm run build after rebasing onto f70006d2.

title: P1: Restore companion-bound ICP cost certification profiles
description: Summary: DNLL updates the ICP harness to load charge-policy.json from companion roots, but src/app/e2e/icp-certification/fixture.ts still applies lowered_warning/lowered_hard profiles only to the leftover system-root charge-policy.json after copying per-companion owners. The harness therefore observes default companion policies and fleet cost-boundary assertions no longer prove distinct warning/hard behavior. Scope: mutate the exact intended companion owner file(s) in the fixture, delete/forbid the system-root decoy, and strengthen certification assertions so each profile proves the companion ID and threshold source actually used. Non-goals: no production fallback, no shared policy, and no test-only bypass of the real gateway resolver.
acceptance_criteria: ICP certification creates no system-root charge-policy.json decoy; lowered_warning and lowered_hard are written to explicit companion roots and produce distinct companion-bound decisions through the production gateway policy resolver. A regression that edits only system root has no effect and fails the certification expectation. Focused fixture/harness integration tests and npm run lint pass.
notes: Fixture now seeds per-companion owner files directly into companion roots and creates no system-root charge-policy/scheduler/capability/skills decoys. lowered_warning/lowered_hard apply only to companion B while A retains the baseline. Extracted createGatewayFleetChargePolicyResolver from gateway main and reused it in the certification harness; integration assertions prove A/B identities, distinct thresholds, and companion-B blocked decisions. Focused fixture + real process harness command passed 4/4 selected tests; npm run lint passed.

title: P1: Verify startup owner files for every companion root
description: Summary: canonical scripts/verify-startup-owner-files.ts passes only config.dataDir (SYSTEM_DATA_DIR) and omits companionDataDir, causing src/system/config/startup-owner-files.ts to default per-companion capability-tier.json, scheduler.json, charge-policy.json, and skills.json back to the system root. Correct split deployments fail preflight, system-root decoys can falsely pass, and the verifier never iterates config.companionFleet. Scope: make the canonical verifier load the resolved fleet and validate system-owner files once plus every per-companion owner file in each exact companionDataDir, with stable companion-specific errors and no fallback. Update startup owner contract/tests and operations references. Non-goals: no single-companion shortcut in fleet mode and no system-root compatibility copy.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight passes only when system owner files exist in SYSTEM_DATA_DIR and every PER_COMPANION_OWNER_FILES entry exists and validates in each configured companionDataDir. Missing/malformed companion A names A and fails; companion B cannot satisfy A; system-root decoys do not help; unknown/duplicate/overlapping fleet roots deny. Focused multi-companion verifier tests, verify:startup-owner-files, and npm run lint pass.
notes: Added verifyStartupFleetOwnerFiles: global owners validate once, then scheduler/capability-tier/charge-policy/skills validate at every exact root in the canonically resolved fleet with companion-specific errors. Canonical script now selects fleet verification or the explicit single companion root. New multi-companion cases (all three) passed; verify:startup-owner-files and npm run lint passed. The focused test file exited 1 only because the pre-existing stale scheduler-drift assertion expected artifactLifecycle while the current validator reports episodicProcessing first; tracked separately for isolated repair and not rerun per one-pass instruction.

Commit 001395ea wires the real runtime preflight to this authority. Reconciled focused owner/launcher tests passed 65/65, verify:startup-owner-files, build, and npm run lint passed.

title: P1: Remove system-root scheduler decoy from standard launcher
description: Summary: after DNLL moves scheduler.json to per-companion ownership, scripts/start-gateway-agent.sh still unconditionally invokes src/app/maintenance/migrate-scheduler-owner.ts before startup. That maintenance command resolves SYSTEM_DATA_DIR and reads SYSTEM_DATA_DIR/scheduler.json, so a correctly provisioned/migrated split deployment with scheduler only in COMPANION_DATA_DIR fails ENOENT before runtime begins. Scope: replace/remove the unconditional legacy scheduler migration in the standard launcher and route any explicitly allowed live-alpha scheduler migration through the canonical per-companion owner/cutover contract. Update launcher tests, setup/operations, and live-alpha boundary if compatibility remains. Non-goals: no system-root decoy, fallback reader, or shared scheduler authority.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh and migrated production split deployments boot through scripts/start-gateway-agent.sh with scheduler.json only in every intended companion root and no system-root scheduler.json. Any named alpha migration is explicit, exact-root, fail-closed, and removable by beta. Missing/malformed per-companion scheduler still fails. Launcher/startup regression tests, verify:startup-owner-files, and npm run lint pass.
notes: Removed unconditional scheduler owner migration from scripts/start-gateway-agent.sh; retained the manual alpha command with a required exact companion --data-dir and documented its beta-removal boundary. Launcher regression suite passed (46 tests) and verify:startup-owner-files passed. The commit-scoped npm run lint invocation found the bxso no-unnecessary-condition issue tracked as psfn-framework-z9z7; that isolated fix then passed focused ESLint and full npm run lint in this same worktree. Per one-pass instructions, the original lint invocation was not rerun.
close_reason: Completed and integrated: commit 39fa6dc5 removes scheduler migration from scripts/start-gateway-agent.sh and makes the operator-only CLI require --data-dir for one exact companion root with no SYSTEM_DATA_DIR/DATA_DIR inference. docs/specifications.md names the temporary alpha boundary. The reconciliation retained Helm explicit-root invocation and added CLI tests proving all layout env without --data-dir denies unchanged and explicit --data-dir mutates only that companion. Focused owner/launcher tests passed 65/65, verify:startup-owner-files, build, and npm run lint passed.

title: P1: Make fleet owner migration crash-atomic and durable
description: Summary: blind DNLL review found src/persistence/system-owner-fleet-migration.ts copies each owner file directly to its final destination with COPYFILE_EXCL. A process or host crash during copy can leave a truncated final file while the receipt remains pending; retry sees an existing digest mismatch and rejects permanently rather than recovering. Existing retry coverage injects only after verification/receipt persistence, missing this window. Destination bytes/metadata are also not durably synced before the system-root source is unlinked. Scope: copy to a same-directory uniquely owned temporary regular file with exclusive creation, fsync it, re-verify exact source/destination digest and size, atomically publish without overwrite, fsync the destination directory, durably advance the receipt, and make retry clean or safely resume only migration-owned temp artifacts. Protect against symlinks, attacker/pre-existing temp/final files, changed source, cross-filesystem rename, and crash windows before/after publish/receipt/source retirement. Non-goals: no overwrite/merge, no shared fallback, and no weakening exact digest approvals.
acceptance_criteria: Injected failures during partial temp copy, after temp fsync, after atomic publish, before receipt update, after receipt update, before source retirement, and after unlink all retry deterministically without data loss or accepting a conflicting file. Only exact durable copies reach final paths; pre-existing final/temp conflicts and symlinks deny; source change denies; source is retired only after every destination and receipt are durably verified. Focused crash/retry tests and npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Completed and integrated: commit 6e057c5b adds exclusive same-directory temporary copies, fsync, atomic publication, destination-directory sync, durable receipt advancement, and deterministic fault-injection coverage for copy/publish/receipt/retirement windows in src/persistence/system-owner-fleet-migration.ts and its test. Subsequent commits 9a1618a2 and 5d15967b preserve and strengthen this contract with pinned directories and receipt-owned staging/recovery; 8427741b closes recovered-quarantine durability. All are ancestors of the feature branch; final DNLL review found no remaining blocker and reconciled build/lint pass.

title: Repair hardcoded-settings verifier drift on main
description: Discovered during combined-branch validation at origin/main e41a20fb plus the companion-life commits. npm run verify:hardcoded-settings fails before any target-feature setting change. It reports 47 unowned/unbaselined module constants across operator Kubernetes transports, gateway confirmation/auth limits, background-work scheduling, emotion bounds, scheduler wake timing, memory coverage/backfill bounds, wiki hydration, Garden auth limits, persistence limits, voice segmentation, lifecycle commands/rollouts, plus one stale baseline entry for DEFAULT_POST_TURN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS. The full exact output is reproducible with npm run verify:hardcoded-settings. Why it matters: repository hygiene fails closed and cannot distinguish new feature regressions while this drift remains. Scope: inspect each reported constant against the live owner-file contract; migrate genuinely mutable tuning/policy values through canonical JSON owner settings, Garden exposure, validation, and tests; record only genuinely code-owned protocol/safety/DoS/error-coupled limits in scripts/hardcoded-settings-baseline.json with a one-line justification; remove the stale baseline entry. Split follow-up beads if settings migrations are independently substantial, but leave this verifier green. Non-goals: do not weaken the scanner, add blanket ignores, restore env authority, or mechanically baseline mutable behavior without review.
acceptance_criteria: npm run verify:hardcoded-settings passes from a clean checkout; every previously reported constant is either settings-owned end to end or has a specific one-line code-ownership justification in scripts/hardcoded-settings-baseline.json; the stale DEFAULT_POST_TURN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS entry is gone; npm run verify:settings-contract passes if owner files change; npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass. Any intentionally deferred settings migration is a linked self-contained P1 bead and cannot leave the verifier red.
notes: Hygiene classification completed in git commit aef6b727. The regenerated baseline removes stale turn-support DEFAULT_POST_TURN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS and adds 46 current findings with one-line rationales: 21 are code-owned protocol/security/DoS/resource ceilings; 25 are temporary owner-plumbing deferrals. Linked P1 follow-ups: psfn-framework-leg6 (background-work scheduler policy), psfn-framework-6n8w (wiki hydration volume), psfn-framework-4k3h (voice segmenter thresholds), and psfn-framework-zhg9 (lifecycle/Kubernetes operational limits). Validation: npm run verify:hardcoded-settings passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed. verify:settings-contract was not applicable because no owner setting or settings UI changed. Bead intentionally remains in progress for parent integration.
close_reason: Completed in integrated commit 5521b9f0. Audited all 46 reported constants: 21 protocol/security/DoS/resource guards now have specific code-ownership notes, 25 mutable values are explicitly linked to P1 owner-plumbing migrations leg6/6n8w/4k3h/zhg9, and the stale turn-support entry is removed. Worker lint/build/diff-check passed; independent combined-branch verify:hardcoded-settings passed. The four linked migrations remain required before the broader branch is P1-clean.

title: P1: Restore Garden type-check and production build gates
description: Summary: the one-shot validation for dependency remediation e41a20fb..a33f887c exposed a broken Garden baseline/upgrade surface: npm --prefix admin-ui run check reports seven TypeScript diagnostics and npm --prefix admin-ui run build cannot parse a TypeScript optional parameter in a Svelte component. Garden is foundational under docs/PSFN_PROJECT_CHARTER.md sections 3.2 and 12.5; a branch whose real Garden cannot type-check or build has a P1 functionality/No-Bullshit-Tests blocker even if the cited source predates the dependency update. Exact diagnostics: src/core/session/icp-recovery-fatigue-metadata.ts:466 and :473 assign string to ObservabilityCallType; :487 assigns string to RequesterProvenance. src/core/cogsec/intake/scanners/rule-engine.ts:22 and :28 duplicate isRecord (must reuse src/shared/utils/types.ts). admin-ui/src/lib/events/prompt-monitor.ts:336 passes TurnSnapshotRecord where AdminTurnSnapshotData requires providerWireMessages; prompt-monitor.test.ts:257 has possibly undefined access. Admin build fails at admin-ui/src/routes/chat/+page.svelte:1086:54 parsing function formatSessionTimestamp(ts?: string | number), reporting Expected comma, got ?. Scope: correct the real shared types/guards, Garden snapshot adapter/test typing, and Svelte preprocessing/component placement/config so Garden check and static production build pass on the security-patched supported dependency graph. Add focused regression coverage where needed. Non-goals: do not roll back the patched exact Kit/Svelte/Vite graph, suppress diagnostics, add any-casts, weaken snapshot contracts, or paper over build output.
acceptance_criteria: npm --prefix admin-ui run check passes with zero diagnostics; npm --prefix admin-ui run build produces the static Garden bundle; the cited shared runtime assignments use canonical enum/union values; rule-engine has one imported shared isRecord guard; prompt-monitor explicitly and truthfully normalizes optional providerWireMessages and its test has safe setup; the chat timestamp helper compiles through the canonical Svelte preprocessing path without stripping types unsafely. Focused tests and npm run lint pass, no new P0/P1 findings or Charter 3.2/12.5 violations remain.
notes:

Garden check ran once and exposed 4 diagnostics (canonical tuple name collision/use-before-declaration, optional wire-message spread, overly canonical adapter input); final commit corrects them via aliasing, a UI-boundary input shape, and explicit normalization, not rerun. title: Prevent reflection grounding notes from becoming companion self-memories
description: Discovered while integrating psfn-framework-jy6s with psfn-framework-0ggv.1. The jy6s deliberation path appends a read-only evidence-grounding assistant turn to the same internal:reflection:<template> session before the final reflection. The 0ggv.1 extraction lane currently treats every assistant entry in internal:reflection:* as experiential evidence. Its lexical gate accepts text such as 'I found that Alice prefers blue' because it contains first-person language plus a preference word and is an exact assistant excerpt. That can misclassify a tool-grounding summary about another subject as companion-owned durable self experience; the resulting companion_private self_experience can later be recalled in a different primary DM. Scope: add a typed, durable distinction between intermediate grounding/tool-worker turns and final experiential reflection output, and make extraction accept only final experiential assistant turns. Preserve legitimate daily/weekly reflection and free-time extraction. Do not rely on model wording or a prompt-only rule, do not weaken subject authorization, and do not create a legacy text-pattern shim. Relevant files: src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts, session turn persistence/metadata contracts, src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts, src/faculties/memory/extraction/self-directed.ts. Link to both parent findings.
acceptance_criteria: A regression models one internal reflection session containing an intermediate assistant grounding note such as 'I found that Alice prefers blue' and a later genuine first-person final reflection. Extraction rejects the grounding note even when exact-cited and lexical checks would otherwise pass, accepts the final experiential reflection, and cannot persist or recall the other subject fact as companion_private self_experience. The distinction is structured and validated at the session/turn boundary rather than inferred from prose. Existing free-time and daily/weekly reflection extraction tests pass; npm run lint and build pass.
close_reason: Completed and integrated in b46f8527 (worker commit a8c4771b). Root review confirmed canonical reflection-journal final output is projected through a typed final_output seam, intermediate tool_grounding turns are rejected, and ordinary reflection session persistence remains disabled. Independent validation: 7 affected test files, 114 tests passed, including persist/recall regression proving 'I found that Alice prefers blue' is neither persisted nor recalled while genuine final reflection is companion_private self_experience.

title: P1: Route ordinary MoA turns through authoritative system prompt composition
description: Summary: src/core/agent/substrate-agent/moa-turn.ts:176-235 invokes runDeliberation for MoA reference voices and aggregation without passing an authoritativeSystemPrompt. buildMoaPrompt at moa-turn.ts:86-104 instead serializes context.systemPrompt into the reflection topic/user-message payload. The provider calls therefore receive only the generic analytical/background/synthesis deliberation system instructions from src/primitives/llm/deliberation.ts, while the canonical identity, immutable policy, companion values, and live runtime affect are demoted into user content. Why it matters: system-role identity and safety policy lose precedence on every MoA-enabled ordinary turn, the same defect class fixed for scheduled reflections by psfn-framework-hgpo. Concrete scope: route the exact canonical prompt-stack/runtime prefix already assembled for the ordinary turn into every MoA voice and aggregator request through runDeliberation.authoritativeSystemPrompt; keep conversation/history/current-turn material in user messages; remove the duplicate/demoted system-in-user representation from buildMoaPrompt if it is no longer needed; preserve MoA reference-model hints, caps, charge accounting, correlation, telemetry, and output behavior. Files: src/core/agent/substrate-agent/moa-turn.ts, src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/agent-invocation.ts, and focused MoA tests. Non-goals: do not change MoA model selection, budgets, charge policy, or scheduler reflection behavior; do not create another identity source or copy character-card persona fields into user content.
acceptance_criteria: Every MoA provider voice and aggregator request begins with the canonical authoritative identity/policy/runtime system prefix and retains its stage-specific instruction; canonical system instructions are not embedded or duplicated in user messages; reference/aggregator model hints, budgets, charge accounting, correlation, telemetry, and output semantics remain passing; focused provider-context tests cover voice and aggregator requests; npm run lint passes.
notes: Implemented in commit d3bc9b85. Ordinary-turn MoA now receives the exact promptAssembly.fullPrompt as runDeliberation.authoritativeSystemPrompt for every reference voice and aggregator; canonical system content was removed from the MoA user message while explicit session prompt blocks, transcript, and current turn remain. Provider-boundary regression verifies all three calls preserve canonical prefix, stage prompts, model hints, token budgets, output, and rounds. Validation: 99 focused Vitest tests passed (moa-turn, provider-context, full turn-execution-runtime); npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed. Bead intentionally left open for parent integration/closure.
close_reason: Completed by integrated implementation 5230b681 plus lint correction f70006d2. The MoA authority behavior passed 99/99 tests; the typed handoff assertion now uses a correctly typed SessionManager buildContext mock and direct non-null call tuples. Independent full npm run lint passed after correction, and the exact regression test passed. This supersedes the earlier incorrect lint handoff.

title: P1: Refresh Discord evidence on authority changes and expiry
description: Summary: blind review of opl1.4 commit 2ecb15d6 found that positive Discord room evidence is refreshed only in the active-principal OAuth callback. There is no production listener or bounded renewal path for guild membership, member roles, channel overwrites/deletion, or private-thread membership changes, and session rotation does not refresh. Positive evidence can therefore remain accepted until its configured TTL (currently potentially one hour), while an expired or startup-time bot_absent snapshot cannot recover without another full login. src/boundary/gateway/fleet-auth-broker.ts refreshes only at callback; src/channels/discord/adapter.ts has no evidence authority-change listeners; src/boundary/fleet-auth/discord-evidence-types.ts accepts positive snapshots until expiry; gateway main starts the OAuth API before Discord clients, making a permanent-for-session bot_absent snapshot possible. Scope: add a production evidence lifecycle coordinator that revokes/replaces evidence promptly on bot-observed guild/member/role/channel/overwrite/thread changes, performs bounded scheduled renewal before/at TTL for active sessions/subjects without leaking OAuth tokens, and provides an explicit safe reauth requirement where provider OAuth evidence cannot be refreshed from custody. Close the startup ordering gap so bot readiness can renew prior bot_absent evidence. Tests must exercise the production lifecycle rather than manually calling refresh twice. Non-goals: do not extend evidence TTL, persist browser-readable provider tokens, turn Discord events into PSFN role/trust/contact authority, or add a permissive cache fallback.
acceptance_criteria: While a fleet session remains active, removal or change of guild membership, member roles, mapped channel/overwrites, bot membership/readiness, or private-thread membership causes prompt fail-closed evidence replacement/revocation. Evidence at or before expiry has a bounded automatic renewal path when current provider evidence is securely available, otherwise the session is explicitly required to reauthenticate and old evidence remains denied. A login before the Discord bot is ready can recover after readiness without a second silent authorization gap. Regression tests drive the actual production coordinator/listeners/scheduler, prove stale positive evidence cannot authorize after change/expiry, prove cross-companion isolation, and prove no provider token leaves gateway custody. Targeted lifecycle tests, PostgreSQL denial coverage, build, and npm run lint pass.
notes:
2026-07-16 remediation commit 3b348c56 adds production lifecycle coordination, bot authority-change hooks, startup/session/renewal/reauth handling, bounded non-secret membership custody, and DB authority denial coverage. One-pass focused lifecycle/runtime/DB run passed 13/13; npm run build passed. npm run lint failed once on 5 unnecessary-condition assertions; all 5 final-diff assertions were corrected afterward and lint was intentionally not rerun. Blind re-review and integration lint remain required before closure.
2026-07-16 second blind review rejected 3b348c56 with three P1s: reauthenticationReason has no production enforcement before cookie/session use (zhn1); bot self-role/disconnect authority changes can leave stale positives (sitf); coordinator and PostgreSQL replace/revoke races lack shared serialization/generation fencing and can orphan positives (y1rw). Confirmed correct: production reachability/start-before-serve, GuildMembers intent/partials, ready recovery, companion isolation, revoke-first shape, non-secret bounded membership custody, unchanged TTL, permission math/veto/private-thread, exact store bindings, and no role/trust/contact/memory conversion.
close_reason: Completed by 3b348c56 with P1 follow-up remediations 63632fba, 36d8833c, and aef5b3b2, all integrated at d92e1357. Evidence: commit history and current production coordinator/event/store wiring were read; lifecycle renewal, bot readiness and authority-change revocation, session reauthentication fencing, shared serialization/generations, and companion isolation are present. Worker focused lifecycle/runtime/Postgres tests passed; follow-up focused suites/build/lint passed as recorded; the later full integration npm run lint/build passed and no OPL1.4 tests failed in the first feature-branch suite. Final independent review reported PASS with no P0/P1 or Charter issue.

title: P1: Migrate shared owner files safely across existing split fleets
description: Summary: the registry-driven legacy cutover moves a file from one legacy root to one companion and retires the source, but existing split fleets currently keep charge-policy.json and skills.json in SYSTEM_DATA_DIR. The default cutover does not discover that source, and pointing legacy-data-dir at SYSTEM_DATA_DIR can copy to only one companion before deleting it, leaving the rest unable to start. Scope: add an explicit receipt-bearing system-owner re-root migration for current split fleets. It must identify one source by exact digest, enumerate the configured companions, copy without overwrite or merge to every companion root, verify every destination, survive partial failure/retry deterministically, and retire the source only after all destinations are verified. Name the temporary support in docs/specifications.md Live Alpha Migration Boundary with validation and beta-removal criteria; update operations/setup. Non-goals: no silent startup hydration, no dual-read fallback, and no automatic conflict resolution. Discovered by blind review of dnll.6/.8/.9.
acceptance_criteria: A current split fleet with system-root charge-policy.json and skills.json can run one explicit migration that copies exact bytes to every configured companion root, records source/destination digests and completion, refuses conflicts or changed source, retries partial completion safely, and removes or retires the source only after all companions verify. Startup then passes for every companion. Live-alpha boundary and operator docs name scope, validation, and beta removal. Focused migration/conflict/retry tests, verify:startup-owner-files, and npm run lint pass.
notes: 2026-07-16 remediation commit bc4953b5: focused migration suite passed 3 tests; verify:startup-owner-files passed; npm run lint passed. No gates rerun. Blind full-range re-review pending.
close_reason: Completed and integrated: commit bc4953b5 adds the explicit approval-bound migrate:system-owner-fleet command, registry-driven fan-out to every resolved exact companion root, no-overwrite/digest checks, durable receipt/retry semantics, source retirement only after all destinations verify, and named live-alpha removal criteria. Regression coverage lives in src/persistence/system-owner-fleet-migration.test.ts. Follow-up P1 hardening landed in 6e057c5b, 9a1618a2, 5d15967b, and 8427741b. Worker evidence records focused migration 3/3, verify:startup-owner-files, and npm run lint passing; assembled DNLL final review passed.

title: P1: Seed per-companion owner files into companion roots in Helm
description: Summary: dnll.8 and dnll.9 make charge-policy.json and skills.json required per-companion files, but deploy/helm/psfn/templates/_helpers.tpl still copies every bootstrap seed to systemDataDir. The chart verifier explicitly asserts that obsolete placement, so a documented first install with bootstrap.seedOwnerFiles=true writes system-root decoys and then startup fails closed for missing companion files. Scope: make Helm seed placement derive from the same canonical per-companion owner-file registry or a generated parity artifact, seed each configured companion root without fallback, update chart verification, and correct deploy/helm values/README plus top-level README/docs/setup ownership text. Add a drift gate so Helm and TypeScript owner registries cannot diverge silently. Non-goals: no runtime fallback reader and no shared-root production support. Discovered by blind review of dnll.8/.9 commits 3708f592 and 5c0bd909.
acceptance_criteria: For a multi-companion Helm render with bootstrap.seedOwnerFiles=true, system owner files seed only systemDataDir and every PER_COMPANION_OWNER_FILES entry seeds each intended companionDataDir. No per-companion decoy is written to systemDataDir. Helm verification fails on ownership drift, docs match live ownership, verify:helm-chart, verify:startup-owner-files, repository hygiene, and npm run lint pass.
notes: 2026-07-16 remediation commit 50758bc7: verify:helm-chart passed; verify:startup-owner-files passed; npm run lint passed. verify:repository-hygiene stopped on pre-existing psfn-shard live-host-alias findings at docs/operations.md:309 and src/app/e2e/kube-self-update-e2e.test.ts:24; not rerun. title: P1: Restore Garden skills administration through per-companion owner adapter
description: Summary: dnll.9 removes SkillsRuntime.toggleSkill and getDisabledSkills to prevent model/runtime mutation of operator-owned skills.json, but the live Garden admin contract still requires and calls both methods. src/operator/garden/admin-contract.ts and api-routes.ts retain the methods while local-admin-contract.ts passes SkillsRuntime directly, causing type/build failure and runtime throws on Garden skills GET/toggle. Scope: introduce a Garden-owned AdminSkillsApi adapter that reads and writes the exact companion skills.json through the canonical ConfigStorePort, validates the owner-file contract, invalidates or refreshes SkillsRuntime after an operator edit, and supplies the existing Garden methods. Add route-level tests proving authorized operator reads/toggles only the current companion file while model/runtime code has no enablement mutation method. Non-goals: do not restore self-enablement on SkillsRuntime, add env authority, or share skill sets across companions. Files: src/operator/garden/admin-contract.ts, api-routes.ts, local-admin-contract.ts, src/faculties/skills/runtime.ts and focused tests. Discovered by blind review of dnll.9 commit 5c0bd909.
acceptance_criteria: The repository builds; Garden skills GET/toggle routes use a Garden-owned per-companion owner-file adapter and never call removed SkillsRuntime mutation methods. Toggling companion A cannot change companion B; malformed or missing owner data fails closed; runtime/model code cannot enable or disable skills. Route-level regression tests, verify:settings-contract, and npm run lint pass.
notes: 2026-07-16 remediation commit dbe3e511: focused Garden route run passed 2 tests with 47 skipped; verify:settings-contract passed; npm run lint passed. No gates rerun. Blind full-range re-review pending.

title: P1: Resolve gateway conversation cost-breaker charge policy per companion
description: Summary: dnll.8 moves charge-policy.json to each companion, but the gateway IcpConversationCostBreaker still holds one process-wide chargePolicy and applies it to every correlation. In a fleet, a correlation for companion B can therefore be admitted or denied using companion A or the gateway bootstrap companion budget, contradicting per-companion fatigue individuation and measuring per-companion ledgers against the wrong policy. Scope: bind gateway cost-breaker evaluation to the authoritative companion identity carried by each correlation and resolve that companion's charge policy from its companion data root. Fail closed when a correlation has no valid companion identity or no policy. Add a regression test with two companions and distinct budgets. Non-goals: no changes to agent-side fatigue ledgers or unrelated gateway capability-tier checks. Files: inspect src/app/gateway/main.ts and the IcpConversationCostBreaker construction/evaluation modules plus fleet correlation routing. Discovered during the dnll.8 post-commit adversarial audit.
acceptance_criteria: Two simultaneous fleet correlations for different companion IDs are evaluated against their own charge-policy.json budgets; changing companion A policy cannot alter companion B decision. Missing, unknown, or mismatched companion identity/policy denies without a default-companion fallback. A focused regression test, npm run lint, and relevant type/build checks pass.
close_reason: Completed and integrated: commit 27eb4c59 binds IcpConversationCostBreaker policy lookup to parsed correlation.localCompanionId in src/primitives/llm/icp-conversation-cost-breaker.ts and constructs a fail-closed known-companion resolver from each companionDataDir in src/app/gateway/main.ts. Unknown/missing policies throw instead of using a default companion. Regression coverage is in src/primitives/llm/icp-conversation-cost-breaker.test.ts. Worker evidence recorded focused 8/8 and npm run lint passing; assembled DNLL final independent review reported no remaining P0/P1/Charter finding.

title: P1: Route deliberation-mode reflections through the base identity prompt stack
description: Summary: Scheduled reflection templates configured with mode=deliberation bypass SubstrateAgent prompt assembly and call LLMProviderPort directly. In src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts:614-634, runTemplateDeliberation passes the narrative prompt to runExperientialTemplateDeliberation/runDeliberation; src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime/experiential-deliberation.ts:38-96 supplies bespoke stage system prompts. Unlike the ordinary-agent path at heartbeat-template-runtime.ts:888-910 and free-time turns at src/app/agent/main.ts:1138-1150, these provider calls do not compose the constitution, north star, companion values, character-card identity/personality, current emotions, or other default system-prompt layers. Why it matters: psfn-framework-i3yx removes duplicate persona text from reflection user messages based on the invariant that the base identity system stack remains present, but default daily-review and weekly-review templates are deliberation-mode when llmProvider is wired, so their identity grounding would be weaker and the issue acceptance cannot be proven for those turns. Scope: design and implement one canonical route that preserves the bounded multi-stage deliberation behavior while applying the same authoritative base identity/policy stack required for ordinary companion turns; add regression coverage that inspects provider system prompts for deliberation reflection stages. Non-goals: do not restore persona/description/scenario copies to reflection user messages, do not add an alternate identity source, and do not weaken deliberation budgets or grounding policy.
acceptance_criteria: For daily-review and weekly-review deliberation turns with llmProvider wired, every provider request includes the canonical base identity stack (including character-card identity/personality plus immutable policy layers and current runtime identity/affect context where applicable); reflection user messages do not contain separately injected persona, description, or scenario blocks; focused tests fail if deliberation bypasses prompt composition; existing bounded stage, budget, provenance, and contradiction behavior remains passing; npm run lint passes.
notes: 2026-07-16 implementation completed on work/companion-life-hgpo as 93c6ae40 (based on d3248000). Captures the exact canonical prompt-stack/runtime prefix at ordinary default prompt assembly, requires it fail-closed for reflection deliberation, and prepends it to every experiential stage plus non-experiential voice/aggregator system prompt without copying identity into user messages. Validation: heartbeat-template-runtime + deliberation suites 33/33 passed; composed identity handoff test 2/2 passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed. title: P1: Make scheduled full-family verification exercise the canonical restore path
description: Final integration check after psfn-framework-kl7y.2 remediation found that src/persistence/backups/fleet-restore.ts:679 verifyFleetAuthConsistentFamilyRestore restores raw companion/cluster slices into the scratch database using only the backup credential, then verifies fleet_auth transactionally. It does not call restoreFleetAuthConsistentFamily, does not accept or authenticate schema-owner URLs, does not apply/verify the manifest access contracts, and derives expected schemas only from the recovery manifest. The real PostgreSQL fixture in src/persistence/backups/fleet-auth-family-restore.integration.test.ts packages only companion_one even though the coordinator family contains companion_one, companion_two, and shared, yet the scheduled verifier can still report familyRestoreVerified=true. Therefore a missing companion recovery slice or broken owner/access mapping can pass the production scheduled verification while the canonical restore would fail. Scope: make the scheduled verifier compare the coordinator and recovery families exactly and exercise the canonical owner-authenticated database restore/access/isolation path in an isolated scratch target, while retaining complete filesystem and Helm verification and leaving production floors/destinations untouched. Wire validated scratch owner credentials/contracts from the gateway scheduler. Non-goals: the shared-schema migration-authority redesign tracked by psfn-framework-kl7y.4, production restore execution, or weakening dedicated scratch routing.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Scheduled verification rejects any missing/extra/duplicated companion or shared recovery slice relative to the authenticated coordinator family before mutation. 2. The verifier exercises the same schema-owner authentication, access-contract application, isolation checks, and rollback-safe database path as restoreFleetAuthConsistentFamily in a dedicated scratch database. 3. Missing, routed, mismatched, or unusable scratch owner credentials fail verification and familyRestoreVerified remains false. 4. Real PostgreSQL coverage includes at least two companions plus shared and proves a broken owner mapping and an omitted companion both fail; valid full-family verification leaves production authority floors and all scratch schemas clean. 5. Focused tests, npm run lint, build, backup verification, settings contract where applicable, and diff check pass.

title: Wire end-to-end voice-stream cancellation through the production gateway path (make barge-in actually cancel the model)
description:
EPIC-LEVEL / COMPOSITE gap surfaced by the mmo9.6.2 blind review (2026-07-15). mmo9.6.1 (cancellation identity + cancelTurn + provider-port signal) and mmo9.6.2 (WS interrupt frame bypass) are each correct in isolation and both PASSED per-bead review, but the COMPOSITE does NOT deliver barge-in in production.

Root cause (in a production-glue file neither bead owns): the production voice composition src/app/gateway/api-surface.ts:310-325 constructs createApiVoiceWebSocketRuntime with a handleAssistantTurn override that calls gateway.requestAgentVoiceStream(message, {signal}) — BYPASSING runAgentAssistantTurn (which is what the unit/e2e tests exercise). requestAgentVoiceStream (src/boundary/gateway/voice-stream-request.ts:170-205) mints a cancellationId into the routed message (so the agent turn IS addressable by cancelTurn) BUT only polls options.signal?.aborted inside the text-chunk loop (:178-183); during model generation it is blocked awaiting the voice.stream.end RPC (:191-199) with NO signal.addEventListener('abort') and NO sendCancel.

So when a WS interrupt fires handleInterrupt -> cancelInFlight -> state.abortController.abort (runtime.ts:355), the abort mirrors into the stage controller but neither rejects the in-flight JSON-RPC nor sends voice.stream.cancel. Result: local WS state is released (feels responsive, ack sent) but the AGENT KEEPS GENERATING until the end RPC resolves; the LLM stage locally hangs until the 45s llm budget times out; a follow-up barge-in turn queues behind the still-active uncancelled turn. This defeats mmo9.6's core stated goal (preemptive interrupts).

Scope: in requestAgentVoiceStream, attach an abort listener on options.signal for the WHOLE turn (not just the chunk-loop poll) that sends voice.stream.cancel / rejects the in-flight voice.stream.end RPC so the gateway aborts the agent turn (cancelTurn) and tears down the upstream provider stream during generation. Confirm the gateway voice.stream.cancel handler actually reaches SubstrateAgent.cancelTurn(cancellationId) + the provider-port cancel signal (mmo9.6.1's seam) so remote model+TTS generation stops, not just local state. This also subsumes mmo9.6.1's flagged split-process follow-up (an llm.chat.cancel-style reverse RPC) for the voice path.

Regression test: a PRODUCTION-composition test (voice-websocket-runtime.test.ts currently has ZERO interrupt/cancel coverage) that drives requestAgentVoiceStream, aborts mid-generation, and asserts voice.stream.cancel is sent + the agent turn is cancelled + no follow-up turn queues behind a still-active turn.

Non-goals: no new RPC redesign beyond the cancel path; do not touch mmo9.6.2's frame-bypass (correct) or mmo9.6.1's identity (correct).

Base: feat/mmo9-performance. This is the piece that makes 6.1+6.2 add up to working barge-in — a textbook epic-seam defect (both beads correct, composite broken, gap in an unowned glue file).
close_reason: Implemented on work/mmo9perf-mmo9.6.5 (f7192794e0..fe9a7dca4d), integrated to feat/mmo9-performance@51f1a4c0e4 (pushed; clean merge). THE COMPOSITE barge-in fix (closes the gap between 6.1+6.2 flagged by the 6.2 review). requestAgentVoiceStream (voice-stream-request.ts) now attaches a WHOLE-TURN abort listener that (a) sends voice.stream.cancel once (idempotent cancelSent guard), (b) rejects the in-flight reverse RPC via an abort-race so the await unblocks instead of hanging to the agent timeout; losing RPC .catch-guarded (no dangling); listener detached in finally on every exit path (no per-turn leak). Full chain verified: WS interrupt (6.2) -> abort -> voice.stream.cancel -> GatewayClient.handleVoiceStreamCancel aborts the same per-stream controller threaded into the model dispatch (handleVoiceStreamEnd) -> SubstrateAgent.cancelTurn(cancellationId) (6.1, identity-guarded, untouched) -> abort() -> provider-port cancel at the agent; the cancelled turn is released so the follow-up barge-in dispatches (not queued). Evidence at worker head: new production-composition test (real requestAgentVoiceStream <-> real GatewayClient over in-memory JSON-RPC bridge) FAILS pre-fix (hang->timeout, rejects 'timed out' not 'abort'), PASSES post-fix (voice.stream.cancel sent + dispatch signal aborted + cancellationId present + follow-up dispatches); 5 files 203 tests; integrated revalidation @51f1a4c0e4: 69 tests + lint clean. UBS range: no new critical/warning. Pi (GLM 5.2 @high) blind adversarial review: PASS, 0 blocking — traced remote-generation-stops in split topology, no abort-race promise leak/double-settle, idempotent cancel, listener cleanup on all paths, follow-up dispatch, benign json-rpc aborted log. Nonblocking (handoff): lost-cancel-frame on host<->agent partition = agent turn runs to completion (best-effort distributed cancel, acknowledged in code, not a regression); the agent's requestWithAbortSignal rejects local llm.chat but does NOT propagate a cancel to the gateway so an already-in-flight gateway->provider fetch isn't torn down (wasted tokens, no user-visible output — SAME split-process residual as 6.1's llm.chat.cancel follow-up; user-perceived barge-in works); timeoutRace setTimeout not cleared (pre-existing, bounded); new test proxies reservation-release via mock dispatch (cancel seam + follow-up faithfully exercised). Completes mmo9.6 barge-in end-to-end.

title: P1: Fail shutdown when safe background claims cannot be requeued
description: Source: independent review of PR #79 / psfn-framework-mmo9.3 at commit 5686ed21467ecf7c7624ffaba017428c2a662e73. src/core/agent/background-work/supervisor.ts:352-388 catches requeuePreBoundaryClaims failure, logs, and resolves stop(). src/app/agent/control-plane.ts:179-201 then proceeds to close PostgreSQL. Scope: make shutdown fail closed or retry boundedly until safe claims are durably released before database closure; preserve outcome-unknown treatment after the write boundary. Non-goals: no process supervisor/deployment changes or unlimited shutdown wait.
acceptance_criteria: 1. An injected requeuePreBoundaryClaims failure makes stop/shutdown observably fail and prevents database close, or succeeds through a bounded retry before close. 2. Pre-boundary claims are durably queued without consuming an attempt; started/applied receipts are never replayed. 3. A max-attempt pre-boundary claim cannot become retry_exhausted solely because graceful requeue failed silently. 4. Focused supervisor/control-plane and disposable-Postgres tests, npm run lint, build, and diff-check pass.

title: P1: Recover record-first background handoffs after live enqueue failures

Scope: provide bounded same-process recovery/retry for record-first handoffs, retaining atomic batch/fingerprint semantics and privacy/eligibility fences. acceptance_criteria: 1. Injected enqueue failure after startup recovery records the canonical manifest, reports the failure, and causes a later bounded recovery attempt in the same process to enqueue the exact jobs once. 2. Duplicate recovery across concurrent ticks/supervisors is idempotent and fingerprint mismatches fail closed. 3. Recovery is bounded/indexed and does not scan all historical TurnRecords on every tick. 4. Tombstoned/duplicate/ineligible source turns never enqueue. 5. Focused turn/supervisor and disposable-Postgres tests, npm run lint, build, and diff-check pass.

title: P1: Stop renewing foreground leases after ownership loss
description: Source: independent review of PR #79 / psfn-framework-mmo9.3 at commit 5686ed21467ecf7c7624ffaba017428c2a662e73. In src/core/agent/background-work/supervisor.ts:750-809, markForegroundLeaseLost aborts the local signal but leaves the lease ID in readyForegroundLeaseIds. src/persistence/postgres/background-work-store.ts:568-589 extends an observed-expired row for one quarantine window while omitting it from the renewed IDs. The next heartbeat retries the same ID during that extension, sees it as unexpired, and renews it indefinitely; a wedged foreground turn can therefore permanently fence same-session memory/compaction. Scope: terminally remove/fence locally lost foreground leases while preserving one bounded durable quarantine and safe endForeground cleanup. Non-goals: no scheduler redesign, provider preemption, or lease-duration tuning.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Regression first: after one lease expires, two subsequent heartbeats cannot renew or extend it beyond the single quarantine window. 2. A second supervisor can claim same-session background work after that bounded window even if the first foreground operation ignores abort. 3. endForeground remains idempotent after local loss and cannot delete another owner lease. 4. Existing foreground isolation and disposable-Postgres suites pass, plus npm run lint, build, and diff-check.

title: Sub-tick scheduling via adaptive next-wake
description: mmo9.5 child C (independent seam). ROOT CAUSE: scheduler.ts:347-425 + scheduler.seed.json:2 — start() arms one setInterval(tick, tickIntervalMs=60000); runTick(:408) is the ONLY due-ness evaluator, so every per-task intervalMs/runAt (incl. the executor's own intervalMs:Math.max(50,...) task @post-turn-actions.ts:1299 and rescheduleAt @:926-951) is checked only on the 60s edge — a job asking to run in 250ms waits up to 60s. The interval is a hard granularity FLOOR. CHANGE (no second scheduler — doc 9 / non-goal): scheduler.ts start()/runTick(): after each runTick compute nextWakeAt = min over tasks of (every: lastRun+intervalMs | wall-clock next | one-shot runAt), clamp to [minWakeMs~50ms, tickIntervalMs (stays coarse ceiling/safety net)], arm setTimeout. Add requestWake(atMs) to re-arm earlier when a near-term task is registered/updated. updateConfig/stop must clear the timer. OPTIONAL cross-file: post-turn-actions.ts rescheduleAt path (@926-951) calls scheduler.requestWake(rescheduleAt) so a 250ms defer is honored — this is the ONLY cross-file edit; can be deferred to keep C in one file (adaptive next-wake needs no executor change). AC: with tickIntervalMs:60000, a task/one-shot due in 250ms fires within a small tolerance of 250ms not at the 60s edge; periodic tasks still fire on cadence; no busy-loop (idle system arms a single timer at the true next due). Regression-first: scheduler.test.ts register one-shot runAt=now+250, fake timers, advance 300ms, assert fired (fails today, fires only at 60s); assert idle scheduler arms exactly one wake at next real boundary (no tight loop). Base: feat/mmo9-performance. Repo rules: fail closed, no swallowed errors, no real names.
close_reason: Implemented on work/mmo9perf-mmo9.5.3 (5686ed2146..b2ecd2a6b2), integrated to feat/mmo9-performance@f4cee18b64 (pushed; isolated scheduler.ts + scheduler.test.ts, clean non-overlapping merge). Replaced the fixed 60s setInterval with a self-rescheduling setTimeout: after each tick computeNextWakeAt takes min over idle tasks of next-due times (every-relative lastRun+intervalMs or now if lastRun=0; wall-clock coarse ceiling when not due; one-shot runAt), clamped to [MIN_WAKE_MS=50ms, tickIntervalMs ceiling]; public requestWake(atMs) re-arms earlier; updateConfig/stop clear the timer; running flag makes start() idempotent. Evidence at worker head + integrated @f4cee18b64: scheduler.test.ts + scheduler-local-timezone.test.ts 50/50 (5 new regression tests incl. 250ms one-shot fires within 300ms [fails on old fixed-interval], requestWake honored, idle arms one coarse wake no tight loop, periodic cadence, stop clears timer) + lint + build/DTS + diff-check clean. UBS range scan: no new critical/warning. Pi (GLM 5.2 @high) blind adversarial review: PASS, 0 blocking — traced every taskNextDueAt x computeNextWakeAt x armNextWake branch (no missed/late fire, no busy-loop [overdue clamps to 50ms], no double-arm/leak [clear-before-arm + tickInFlight gate + running/stopping gates], correct timer lifecycle, no double/wrong-fire, unref parity). IMPORTANT FOLLOW-UP (leading mmo9.5 handoff item): register() never calls requestWake, so a sub-minute one-shot REGISTERED AT RUNTIME while the scheduler is idle still waits up to the 60s ceiling for first evaluation (no worse than base, task fires late not never/wrong) — the adaptive mechanism is correct+tested but the executor rescheduleAt->requestWake / register()->requestWake wiring was deferred per spec; wire it before mmo9.5 admission responsiveness is considered end-to-end delivered. Nonblocking: updateConfig now eager-rearms on any update (harmless); start()-during-stop()-drain can leave scheduler running (matches pre-existing behavior, requires caller misuse).

title: Enforce requiresForegroundIdle from the lane profile (close policy/executor drift)
description: mmo9.5 child B (tiny, mechanical, high-confidence, land first). ROOT CAUSE (drift): post-turn-actions.ts:914-919 computes requiresForegroundIdle = registeredHandlers.some(executionMode !== 'background') and awaits agentLoop.waitForIdle on that. The authoritative field RuntimeLaneBudgetProfile.requiresForegroundIdle (worker-lanes.ts:87, true only for maintenance_reflection @:141) is NEVER read. Every registered post-turn handler currently passes executionMode:'background' (all call sites in heartbeat-post-turn-runtime*.ts, context-feedback/runtime.ts, tools/lifecycle.ts), so some(...) is false -> maintenance_reflection lanes that DECLARE foreground-idle never actually wait; conversely a non-background handler would force idle even for post_turn_appraisal. Dead policy = Law 12.4 one-home violation. CHANGE: post-turn-actions.ts:914-919 -> requiresForegroundIdle = resolveRuntimeLaneBudgetProfile(entry.runtimeClass).requiresForegroundIdle (drop the executionMode-derived computation). entry.runtimeClass already available (@821,@851). Do NOT delete executionMode (still meaningful for other wiring) but strip it of the overlap decision. Add a registration-time consistency assertion/startup validation: a handler registered executionMode:'foreground' maps only to a lane whose profile requiresForegroundIdle is true (prevent silent re-drift). AC: a maintenance_reflection action whose handler declares executionMode:'background' PROVABLY awaits waitForIdle (never overlaps foreground); a post_turn_appraisal action does NOT await idle; behavior driven solely by the profile field. Regression-first: register (a) maintenance_reflection + background-mode handler, assert waitForIdle IS called (fails today); (b) post_turn_appraisal + foreground-mode handler, assert waitForIdle is NOT called (fails today). Base: feat/mmo9-performance. Repo rules: fail closed, no real names.
close_reason: Implemented on work/mmo9perf-mmo9.5.2 (5686ed2146..fc6847c9b6), integrated to feat/mmo9-performance@f648d5bee7 (pushed; clean non-overlapping ort merge of exactly the reviewed diff — 2 files, post-turn-actions.ts + its test). title: Preemptable and reservable provider capacity at the model-call gate
description: mmo9.5 child A (hard core). Replace the single-boolean active slot with capacity-aware, preemption-capable admission; plumb a gate-owned cancel signal into the LLM transport; forward the supervisor per-job signal into background LLM calls; map preemption to the supervisor pre-boundary defer. ROOT CAUSE: model-call-gate.ts:25-168 ResourceQueue has one active:boolean per resourceKey; acquire() grants only when !active && pending empty; selectNextPendingIndex (:145) reorders WAITERS by lane priority but preemption is structurally impossible (gate holds only a release closure, no handle to cancel the running execute); caller signal (:74-90) only removes a WAITING acquire. So foreground voice waits behind an in-flight background extraction. NOTE resolveModelCallResourceKey (client.ts:517-531) returns a key ONLY for request_base_url/configured_litellm_proxy/litellm/local_endpoint; cloud providers return null and bypass the gate (already non-contended) — this defect bites shared-endpoint/local-substrate (Pi) deployments. CHANGES: model-call-gate.ts ResourceQueue gains capacity:number (default 1) + active:ActiveCall[] {runtimeClass, preemptController:AbortController, sequence}; run() passes execute a gate-owned preemptSignal; on acquire, grant immediately if active<capacity AND interactive-reservation invariant holds (keep >=1 slot free for foreground_chat unless acquirer IS foreground); else if acquirer higher-priority than lowest-priority active AND that lane is preemptable, abort that call's preemptController(PreemptError) and grant; else park (existing reorder). worker-lanes.ts: add preemptable:boolean to RuntimeLaneBudgetProfile (foreground_chat:false, post_turn_appraisal:false, background_continuation:true, maintenance_reflection:true — single home, Law 12.4). client.ts: thread gate preemptSignal through runWithModelCallGate(@584); complete path(@1058-1073) + stream path build transport signal = AbortSignal.any([options.signal, preemptSignal]) — MUST cover llm.stream path (mmo9.8 needs it; RE-VERIFY line numbers on the feat branch, ~35 hunks there). Capacity config goes in routing/model OWNER config (a provider property), NOT scheduler.seed.json (feat branch already edited it — conflict risk); default capacity 1 for local_endpoint/litellm shared keys (fail-closed). background-work/post-turn-runtime.ts: forward input.signal (currently unused) into extractor.maybeExtract / emotionRuntime.triggerEmotionAppraisal / sessionManager.scheduleAutoCompactionBetweenTurns; map a preemption-reason abort to BackgroundWorkDeferredError('foreground_active', delayMs) (defer, NO attempt consumed) not failOrRetry. SAFETY (load-bearing): for all four job classes the LLM call is BEFORE commitEffectBoundary, so aborting is always pre-boundary = supervisor-safe (receipt pending, abandonEffect drops it, job requeues revision-bumped, no duplicate write). Never preempt a non-preemptable lane; a test must assert an abort AFTER boundary crossing fails closed via outcome_unknown (no replay). AC: (i) capacity 1, in-flight background_continuation on key K aborted within budget when foreground_chat acquire on K arrives, foreground execute starts without waiting; (ii) capacity 2 + reserve-1, background holds one slot, foreground gets reserved slot with NO preemption; (iii) foreground_chat never itself preempted; (iv) preempted background job -> supervisor deferred, no attempt consumed, later resumes; (v) preemption telemetry {reason, resourceKey, preemptedRuntimeClass, waitedMs}. Regression-first: model-call-gate.test.ts fake execute blocking on a deferred — assert current code FAILS 'foreground starts before background completes' then passes; capacity/reservation test; streaming-path preemptSignal composition test; supervisor-integration preempt mid-extraction (pre-commitEffectBoundary) -> requeues cleanly no duplicate. OPEN RISK (verify, flag if true): ModelCallGate is per-LLMClient (client.ts:195); if each companion is a separate agent process, in-process gate can't coordinate two companions on the same endpoint (proxy-side concurrency limit is the cross-process control) — this bead fully solves multi-CHANNEL within one companion, not cross-process multi-companion. Base: feat/mmo9-performance. Repo rules: fail closed, no swallowed errors, no shims, no second budget system (Law 12.4), no real names.
close_reason: Implemented on work/mmo9perf-mmo9.5.1 (5686ed2146..52ca6fba7f) + one remediation (..98face9bfa), integrated to feat/mmo9-performance@97125b38a1 (pushed; delegated signal-compose merge with mmo9.6.1). Capacity-aware preemption-capable model-call gate: ResourceQueue{capacity, reservedForegroundSlots, active[]}; higher-priority foreground acquire preempts the lowest-priority PREEMPTABLE background call it strictly outranks (aborts its preemptController = ModelCallPreemptedError); gate provides execute a preemptSignal; foreground/post_turn_appraisal never preempted; config via ProviderRegistryEntry.capacity/reservedForegroundSlots (fail-closed). Preempt maps to supervisor BackgroundWorkDeferredError('foreground_active') pre-boundary defer (no attempt consumed). REVIEW FAIL@xhigh->remediated->verified: Pi found P1 — ModelCallPreemptedError flattened to -32603 across the gateway->agent JSON-RPC boundary (name lost), so preempted background job hit failOrRetry -> permanently failed after maxAttempts=5 (LOST cognition job in production split topology); in-process mock-transport tests missed it. Orchestrator confirmed against code. Remediation: dedicated GatewayErrors.MODEL_CALL_PREEMPTED=-32018, mapped in exposeModelCallGateBlocks (both llm.chat+llm.complete), reconstructed on GatewayClient (both complete+stream via modelCallPreemptedErrorFromRpc) so .name+instanceof hold across the wire -> defers correctly; new real-boundary regression test (JSON round-trip -> production mapping -> executePostTurnBackgroundWork asserts deferred not failed). INTEGRATION SEAM: 5.1 preempt signal + 6.1 caller-cancellation signal both thread the stream path; delegated merge composed both (composeTransportSignal(options?.signal, preemptSignal), adopted options-object signature across LLMProviderPort/LLMClient/transport/GatewayClient) and caught a LATENT trap in stream-adapter.ts (auto-merged clean but would have dropped caller cancellation in both topologies via undefined options.signal) — fixed + both-signal regression test added. Evidence: 5.1 remediation 190+17+3; merge validation 366 (306 6.1-cancellation suite + 59 5.1-preemption suite + 1 compose test) + lint + build/DTS + diff-check clean. UBS range: no new critical/warning. Pi (GLM 5.2 @xhigh) blind adversarial review of 5.1: selection/reservation/config-fail-closed/fallback-wrapping all verified correct. Nonblocking (handoff): input.signal forwarding into background handlers deferred (shutdown-latency only, preemption independent via gate signal); per-process gate scope (solves multi-channel not cross-process multi-companion, documented limitation); gate-preempt of a LIVE stream not reachable today (chat forced FOREGROUND_CHAT, never a victim) — forward-looking for mmo9.8 streaming reservation. Completes mmo9.5 (with 5.2, 5.3) -> unblocks mmo9.7.

title: Separate TTS first-byte budget from playback budget
description: mmo9.6 child 4/4 (independent seam; shares src/channels/discord/voice-turn-runtime.ts with mmo9.6.3 — different functions, expect small textual merge; also touches primitives/voice/policy/reliability.ts + websocket runtime.ts — grep VoiceRuntimeStage usages before editing the union). Root cause: one budget spans request-to-first-byte AND playback-duration, and retry has no 'cancel prior attempt first' guarantee. Discord: speakVoiceText (:464) wraps the ENTIRE synth+playback (playWithTtsConnector->playTtsSession->playReadableAudio, awaits entersState(Idle,120s)) in a single stage-tts budget (reliability.ts:18: 25s timeout, maxRetries 1) — a reply whose playback exceeds 25s trips the timeout and RETRIES the whole synth+playback while the first playback is not guaranteed cancelled => double-speak. WebSocket: streamPlayback (runtime.ts:459) budgets only synthesizeStream (session open) under stage-tts; the first audible chunk arrives lazily in the unbudgeted for-await loop => NO first-byte budget at all. Scope: add a tts_first_byte stage (short, retry-safe) to VoiceRuntimeStage/DEFAULT_VOICE_RELIABILITY_BUDGETS (reliability.ts:4,:14); keep tts/output as long non-retryable playback. Discord: split speakVoiceText/playWithTtsConnector (:434-529) — budget synth-request->first chunk under tts_first_byte; playback under output with maxRetries 0; on first-byte retry, assertActiveVoiceTurn + cancel prior turn.ttsSession BEFORE re-synth (use existing voice.tts.first-byte events :513,:566 as the budget boundary). WebSocket: streamPlayback (runtime.ts:459) wrap the FIRST for-await chunk (:469) in tts_first_byte, keep per-chunk output. GATED sub-task (only with new incremental-MP3 decoder-boundary tests): remove the one-chunk look-ahead in connectors/tts/elevenlabs-stream.ts:85 (responseBodyToAudioChunks holds 'pending' and yields the previous chunk, delaying first audible byte by one network read). AC: (a) a reply whose playback exceeds the old 25s does NOT trigger a second synth (no double-speak) — assert single synth call; (b) a synth that never returns a first byte times out under the short budget and its retry cancels the prior session first; (c) TTFA p50/p95 improvement in mmo9.2 telemetry. Base: feat/mmo9-performance. Repo rules: fail closed, no swallowed errors, no real names.
close_reason: Implemented on work/mmo9perf-mmo9.6.4 (e5ff7eee28..0476645322), integrated to feat/mmo9-performance@f7192794e0 (pushed; clean merge). Split the TTS budget: new retry-safe tts_first_byte stage (8s/maxRetries 1) budgets synth-request->first audible chunk; tts reconfigured to long non-retryable playback (125s/0) alongside output. Discord acquireTtsFirstByte + WS streamPlayback both cancel the prior ttsSession (await, synchronously) BEFORE re-synth on a first-byte retry (attempt-counter guard); playback runs under output (maxRetries 0). Eliminates the double-speak where a >25s playback tripped the old single tts budget and re-synthesized over an uncancelled first playback; adds a first-byte budget to the WS path (previously none). ElevenLabs one-chunk look-ahead removal DEFERRED (gated on incremental-MP3 decoder tests). Evidence at worker head: voice-tts-first-byte 3 (AC a/b/c) + WS runtime 8 (incl. cancel-prior-on-retry) + reliability + voice 45 + full voice sweep 155; integrated revalidation @f7192794e0: 147 voice tests + lint clean. UBS range: no new critical/warning. Pi (GLM 5.2 @high) blind adversarial review: PASS, 0 blocking — verified double-speak eliminated (cancel-prior awaited before re-synth; tts_first_byte provably can't fire once playback begins since first_audible_playback emits under output AFTER acquireTtsFirstByte returns), stage union clean (no exhaustive switch), budget correctness (never-returning first byte times out ~16s not hang; 30-119s reply completes without retry), resource safety. Nonblocking (handoff): buffered fallback fires on a PLAYBACK error too (>120s reply only, pre-existing, sequential replay not concurrent double-speak — candidate follow-up: gate fallback on acquisition-only errors); dead tts stage config (unused post-rewire); tts_first_byte 8s stricter than old 25s window (fail-fast, fine for normal <2s TTFA); telemetry double-count on orphan-timeout race; WS first-byte reads exactly one chunk (doesn't skip empty leading — pre-existing hang shape).

title: Preemptive WebSocket voice control frames
description: mmo9.6 child 2/4. DEPENDS ON mmo9.6.1 (interrupt must reach the model via cancellationId, not just cancel local playback). Root cause: primitives/voice/transports/websocket/server.ts:165 drainFrameQueue processes ALL frames strictly serially (processingFrames flag + await fireHook('onFrame') per frame), so an 'interrupt' frame queues behind a session.end frame whose onFrame is still awaiting the full model+TTS pipeline (runtime.ts:287 handleSessionEnd awaits onAssistantTurn then streamPlayback). The interrupt handler (runtime.ts:351 handleInterrupt) is correct but never runs until the in-flight frame resolves — control-plane and data-plane share one FIFO. Scope: route control frames (interrupt, ping) out of the data-plane FIFO so they dispatch synchronously on receipt (server.ts drainFrameQueue/handleMessage:68), bypassing frameQueue, while keeping session.start/audio.chunk/session.end ordered. Ensure handleInterrupt drives the mmo9.6.1 cancellationId so the MODEL turn (not just local playback) aborts; confirm handleSessionEnd's onAssistantTurn signal (runtime.ts:317) reaches the agent via .6.1. AC: test enqueues session.end (long model) then interrupt; assert interrupt is handled BEFORE end resolves and the model/TTS abort fires (criterion: stops remote model/TTS generation, not merely local playback). Base: feat/mmo9-performance. Repo rules: fail closed, no swallowed errors, no real names.
close_reason: Implemented on work/mmo9perf-mmo9.6.2 (68d505dfc3..0b6a71f291), integrated to feat/mmo9-performance@50f5a9ef86 (pushed; clean merge). Control-frame classifier (interrupt, ping) splits handleMessage: control frames dispatch synchronously via fireHook on receipt, bypassing the data-plane frameQueue + its backpressure ceiling; session.start/audio.chunk/session.end stay strictly ordered through drainFrameQueue. So an interrupt runs concurrently with a blocked in-flight session.end instead of queuing behind the full model+TTS pipeline. Evidence at worker head: websocket 24 (server 10 incl. interrupt+ping-ahead-of-blocked-session.end + saturated-queue, runtime 8, serializer 6) + gateway client + substrate-agent 181 (6.1 seam intact); integrated revalidation @50f5a9ef86: 24 WS tests pass. UBS range: 1 new listener-imbalance warning = TEST-ONLY (once:true mock in runtime.test.ts, self-cleans; production server.ts adds no listeners). Pi (GLM 5.2 @high) blind adversarial review: PASS, 0 blocking — traced ordering integrity (all 5 frame types accounted, data frames still FIFO, control bypass safe), interrupt-during-session.start no-ops (SESSION_NOT_FOUND), interrupt-mid-session.end idempotent (no double-cancel/free), no 6.1 identity-clobber reintroduced (control path never touches activeTurnCancellationId), no new swallowed error. IMPORTANT COMPOSITE FINDING (-> fix bead mmo9.6.5): 6.2's frame bypass is a NECESSARY PREREQUISITE for barge-in but does NOT by itself deliver production remote-model cancellation — the production voice composition (api-surface.ts requestAgentVoiceStream) mints a cancellationId but only polls signal.aborted in the chunk loop and does NOT observe the abort during the voice.stream.end generation RPC, so a WS interrupt releases local state (feels responsive) while the agent keeps generating. Neither 6.1 nor 6.2 per-bead review could flag this as blocking (each bead correct in its own scope; gap in an unowned glue file). Tracked as mmo9.6.5 (P1). title: End-to-end voice turn-cancellation identity (keystone)
description: mmo9.6 child 1/4 (KEYSTONE — land first; mmo9.6.2 and mmo9.8 depend on it). Mint one cancellationId at transport ingress and thread it transport->gateway->agent model->TTS, with a real abort keyed to it at each layer, closing the cancel-after-dispatch gap. Root cause: SubstrateAgent.abort() (substrate-agent.ts ~:1097) works and is exercised by API text (chat-completions.ts:294) but NO voice path threads a turn identity to it. MessageHandler (channels/backplane/types.ts:4) has no signal param; Discord handleVoiceUtterance wraps handler(message) but the signal only unblocks the local Promise.race, not the agent turn (uncancellable model calls). Gateway handleVoiceStreamCancel (client.ts:1248) only sets cancelled=true/deletes state AFTER handleVoiceStreamEnd (client.ts:1219->dispatchHandleMessage:1120, no signal) already dispatched the model. Scope: add turn-cancellation registry + cancelTurn(cancellationId) (identity-guarded over abort()) on SubstrateAgent; extend MessageHandler to carry {signal,cancellationId}; add cancellationId to SubstrateMessage.routing (survives serializeMessage:242); VoiceStreamState gains cancellationId+AbortController; handleVoiceStreamEnd threads signal into dispatchHandleMessage; handleVoiceStreamCancel aborts the controller / calls cancelTurn instead of only deleting state; voice-stream-request.ts carries cancellationId. Abort order on barge-in: model turn first, then TTS session, then transport state. cancelTurn(id) aborts IFF active turn id matches (a stale late cancel must NOT kill the next turn — critical for mmo9.8 rapid segment turns). VERIFY FIRST (open risk): whether inner Agent.abort() (substrate-agent.ts:514 inner Agent) truly cancels the upstream provider HTTP stream mid-generation or only stops local consumption; if only local, .1 grows to thread a provider-port cancel signal. AC: unit test dispatches a voice turn, cancels AFTER model dispatch, asserts (a) inner provider stream receives abort, (b) cancelTurn fires for that id and no other, (c) a late stale-id cancel does NOT abort a newer turn; cancellation observed at gateway state + agent turn + TTS session. Keep identity transport-agnostic (mmo9.8 reuses it); do NOT rename voice.stream.* RPCs (that's mmo9.8). Base: feat/mmo9-performance.
