title: Turn-record userMessage/assistantMessage frozen copies ignore CogSec tombstones
description: Discovered during eb14 remediation (2026-07-15). TurnRecord.userMessage.content (and by symmetry assistantMessage.content) is a frozen verbatim copy of partner/companion text persisted on the turn record at write time (turn-records.ts ~363, sessionEntryId + content). A CogSec tombstone of the backing L0 entry does not scrub it: the eb14 wave gated recentEntries (9ree/hgw3.10), plan.messages (9ree), memory candidates (jsi9), and capturedWirePayload (eb14), but the top-level userMessage/assistantMessage fields are served ungated by every turn-record read exit — consumers include introspection source.ts (reads userMessage/assistantMessage), Garden session views (buildTurnData), and telemetry sanitizers. Same partner-data retention class as eb14. The eb14 remediation deliberately did not expand scope (its withhold key now USES userMessage.sessionEntryId, so the plumbing to resolve the entry's L0 state at read time already exists — likely a small symmetric gate). Coordinate with ervg (cross-channel continuity) so the family lands coherently. Non-goals: wirebody (eb14, done), continuity surfaces (ervg).
acceptance_criteria: A CogSec tombstone of the L0 entry backing userMessage (or assistantMessage) results in the frozen copy no longer being served verbatim from any turn-record read exit or Garden/introspection surface (masked with the redaction marker, consistent with the 9ree convention); live text byte-identical; heal/telemetry consistent with hgw3.10; regression test: append turn, tombstone the current-turn partner entry, assert userMessage.content serves the marker not plaintext across getRecentTurnRecords/findTurnRecord/Garden session views; sessions + garden + introspection suites green.

title: P1: Close fleet-auth authority and reapproval bypasses
description: Sources: psfn-framework-opl1.2.3, opl1.2.4, and opl1.2.5; discovered during independent validation of PR #78 at feat/opl1-fleet-sso@fa336f2910. Verified failures: schema.ts rejects five direct PostgreSQL attributes but permits membership/SET ROLE into arbitrary predefined or external powerful roles and leaves inheritance/expiry/connection/database-owner posture unspecified; the runtime role has full DML on authority_state and reapproval trusts that mutable database copy; reapproval-sql.ts ignores trusted_host_ceremonies.exact_scope, so a ceremony for a lower role can promote a quarantined owner grant, and compares expiry to caller-controlled p_at; migrations v4 backfills history but post-migration restore can insert history-only provider ownership without updating provider_subject_registry, allowing later reassignment; fleet-auth-config.ts compares lexical URL host/port/path while libpq routing query overrides can redirect one credential; reapproval.ts swallows rollback failure. Scope: deny all role memberships/SET ROLE targets and enforce a documented exact safe login posture; remove ordinary runtime authority_state mutation while retaining bounded coordinator reconciliation; bind reapproval to exact principal/provider/companion/contact/binding/grant/role/current lineage+generation+checkpoint and database time; register every appended immutable history row; reject connection-routing overrides before identity comparison; surface rollback failure. Non-goals: OAuth/UI/passkey enrollment, backup filesystem/restore orchestration (sibling fix beads), production/Pi, or speculative refactors. Current working tree with regression-first draft: feat/opl1-fleet-sso worktree based fa336f2910.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Every fleet role rejects SUPERUSER/CREATEROLE/CREATEDB/REPLICATION/BYPASSRLS, any direct or transitive membership/SET ROLE target including predefined server roles, target database ownership, unsafe inheritance, expired credentials, and unbounded/unusable connection posture before schema/data work; valid dedicated roles pass. 2. Runtime SQL has SELECT-only authority_state access and cannot rewrite/delete the current floor projection; startup/restore coordinator reconciliation remains bounded and green. 3. Reapproval uses database time for expiry and requires exact JSON scope binding principal, provider subject, companion/contact, binding ID, grant ID, role, authority lineage/generation/restore checkpoint; wrong-role, stale, backdated-expiry, replay, and direct-SQL attempts deny with no mutation. 4. Restored/appended history-only provider evidence permanently registers its original principal and rejects reassignment. 5. Fleet database URLs reject query parameters that can override host/hostaddr/port/dbname/user/service or authentication target before same-database comparison. 6. Rollback errors are surfaced or aggregated, never swallowed. 7. Disposable-PG and config regressions, focused tests, npm run lint, build, settings contract, and diff check pass.

Both reviewers independently reproduced account reapproval accepting a ceremony that expired while waiting on row locks because v_now is captured before locking. Reviewer A additionally reproduced v4-to-v5 migration installing the history trigger without backfilling history appended after v4, allowing an existing subject binding to be permanently reassigned; orchestrator verified the migration lacks a backfill. One bounded remediation assigned on fix/opl1-security-authority-remediation; no successive inline cycle after final check.

title: Cross-channel continuity content ignores CogSec redaction on every persisted surface: wirebody.system, continuityEntries, Loom continuity views
description: Discovered during eb14 dual blind review (Opus reviewer, line-verified + mechanical repro; Pi independently confirmed the wirebody gating family). Cross-channel continuity entries (context-builder.ts:298 xmlElement('text', entry.content) -> body.system at :1072; persisted sessionContext.continuityEntries at :638) carry verbatim partner content from OTHER channels' journals with real L0 ids, but: (1) they are never plan.messages, so eb14's wire-body gate cannot key on them; (2) the origin channel's L0 state is unreadable from the consuming store's resolver (the exact reason 9ree excluded continuityEntries from the diet); (3) the un-gated continuityEntries surface renders in Loom continuityProvenance views independent of the wirebody. Concrete leak: partner message M in channel A -> turn T in channel B embeds M via continuity -> CogSec tombstone of M in channel A -> Loom read of T serves M verbatim from BOTH body.system and continuityEntries. Scope: one coherent cross-channel redaction propagation design covering all continuity-persisting surfaces (wirebody.system withhold key, continuityEntries gating, Loom views) — likely needs an origin-channel L0 resolution seam or a tombstone-fanout index; coordinate with the 9ree/hgw3.10 heal/telemetry conventions. Non-goals: same-channel gating (eb14), memory-store redaction (jsi9, shipped). Related: eb14 carve-out documented in that bead's close evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A CogSec tombstone applied in the origin channel results in the affected continuity content no longer being served verbatim from any persisted turn-record surface of any OTHER channel (wirebody.system, sessionContext.continuityEntries, Loom continuity/raw-wire views) — masked/withheld with telemetry; cross-channel resolution failures heal loudly rather than serving stale plaintext or breaking channel reads; regression test spans two channels (tombstone in A, assert gated reads in B); lint + sessions + garden suites green.

title: CogSec redaction must reach _shared/wirebodies: tombstoned partner content persists in capturedWirePayload and renders in Loom
description: Reclassified P1 by operator review of the wave-20260715 handoff (PR #77). The 80f6 wire capture persists the COMPLETE provider request body (system prompt, memories, partner messages) content-addressed under _shared/wirebodies/<sha>.json, resolves it unconditionally on turn-record reads (turn-record-shared-store resolveSerialized via turn-records.ts read compose chain), and renders it in the Loom 'Raw Wire Body' panel. The 9ree/hgw3.10 redaction propagation gates recentEntries and plan.messages only — a partner message tombstoned/redacted in L0 AFTER capture remains verbatim in capturedWirePayload.body and is served to the Garden. This is partner-data redaction/retention risk (Blocking Risk Standard: partner-data privacy), not report-only. Context: content-addressed dedup means one wirebody file may be shared across turns, so per-turn redaction is non-trivial (re-intern rewritten body vs dangle-and-heal); the read path currently fails closed on dangling refs (whole-channel), so naive deletion breaks Garden reads — the fix must handle refs (heal-on-absent for wirebodies, or rewrite+re-ref). Discovered-from: psfn-framework-80f6 (capture, Pi review observation #2/#4) and psfn-framework-hgw3.10 (which closed the sibling recentEntries surface). Non-goals: GC/retention policy (separate concern, coordinate), MoA turns (no capture).
acceptance_criteria: A CogSec tombstone/redaction applied to an L0 entry whose content appears in a captured wirebody results in that content no longer being served from any turn-record read or Loom surface (masked, healed, or rewritten — never verbatim); dangling/rewritten wirebody refs do not break whole-channel reads (heal path with telemetry, consistent with hgw3.10 semantics); regression test: capture a turn, tombstone a partner entry in L0, assert the Loom raw-wire view and getRecentTurnRecords no longer return the tombstoned plaintext; existing wirebody byte-identity tests updated to reflect the gated contract; lint + sessions suite green.
close_reason: Implemented @ e5f54ba6ab + remediation f79bf1a737 on fix/eb14-wirebody-cogsec, squash-merged to main @ 5656dcf2b2 (PR #80, agent-pair validated+merged). Read-time whole-body withhold ({withheld:'cogsec-redaction'} + safe metadata) at the SessionStore boundary on the union of three signals from the existing single L0 range read: plan.messages provenance suppression, current-turn partner entry (userMessage.sessionEntryId — structurally excluded from plan.messages per prompt-assembly.ts:499 guard) redacted/absent, and any window redaction/heal-drop; empty-plan bypass removed; sidecar files never touched (shared refs + fail-closed dangling semantics intact); telemetry turn_record_wire_body_withheld. Review gate (P1 dual blind + UBS clean): BOTH reviewers FAILed the first cut with different verified blockers — Pi: current-turn exclusion gap (confirmed at every line; original test used production-impossible shape); Opus: cross-channel continuity leak in body.system (line-verified + repro). Single remediation fixed the current-turn gap with production-shape regressions; continuity carved out per orchestrator ruling to P1 psfn-framework-ervg (all three continuity surfaces coherently — identical content leaks independently via un-gated continuityEntries) with docstrings corrected to claim exactly what is gated. Also discovered → P1 psfn-framework-sm9l (frozen userMessage/assistantMessage copies ignore tombstones). Final gates: 496 sessions+garden tests, 8/8 regression file incl. current-turn-tombstone→withheld, lint, build, validator-confirmed on the PR.

title: Fail queued durable extraction closed when shutdown begins
description: Final Standards review of u5bv.8 range cd0c8b9b6c..017b518eda reproduced a shutdown race that can mark a durable snapshot covered without writing it. MemoryExtractor.trackExtraction serializes bounded B behind existing same-session work at src/faculties/memory/extraction.ts:454-491. If BackgroundWorkSupervisor shutdown times out and MemoryExtractor.stop flips acceptingExtractions before B's chained run starts, the extraction orchestrator skips fact writes at src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts:476 but resolves normally. maybeExtract then advances B coverage and the effect receipt completes. Scope: distinguish not-started/draining from successfully consumed; queued durable work must either finish its exact snapshot or fail/defer so the job and receipt remain retryable. Non-goals: no forced process hang, no receipt deletion after a possibly committed effect, no weakening graceful shutdown timeouts.
design: Recheck acceptance at the start of each serialized bounded run and return a typed not-executed outcome or throw the existing retryable/deferred signal before any coverage/receipt advancement. If execution has crossed a durable sink boundary, preserve idempotent receipt semantics; never report an unexecuted snapshot as covered.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Deterministic race: A holds same-session extraction, B queues, stop/drain flips acceptance before B starts; B performs no write and its background effect/job is not marked applied/completed. 2. On restart/retry, B's exact snapshot runs once and only then advances coverage. 3. Shutdown after B starts either drains successfully or leaves an explicit retry-safe/indeterminate state; no duplicate durable fact and no silent loss. 4. Foreground/manual/group extraction stop behavior remains intentional and tested. 5. Focused extractor/supervisor/receipt plus disposable-Postgres race tests, mandatory npm run lint, build/DTS, and diff check pass.
close_reason: Implemented on work/mmo9-u5bv.11 (227355717c..969d9fcd59), integrated to feat/mmo9-background-supervisor@5686ed2146 (pushed; orchestrator resolved post-turn-runtime.ts + extraction.ts conflicts with u5bv.6, combining the drain-signal translation with u5bv.6's non-crossing pre-write fence so the drain guard fires before the boundary crosses). New ExtractionDrainRequeueError (drain-signal.ts): runExtraction throws it for a receipt-bound run when acceptingExtractions is false BEFORE crossing the effect boundary/advancing coverage; orchestrator closes the mid-flight-drain window (drain after cross but before any write throws instead of a covered no-op); post-turn-runtime translates the signal (matched by .name, no core->faculties import) into a retryable BackgroundWorkDeferredError('source_not_ready') so the untouched pending receipt is abandoned and the job defers with no consumed attempt; foreground/manual/group drains (no receipt) keep intentional silent skip. Evidence at worker head: extraction+orchestrator+post-turn-runtime+supervisor+runtime-helpers 123 tests (incl. extractor-level race fail-closed, retry-runs-once-advances-coverage, post-turn defer translation) + disposable-PG receipt test (abandoned on defer, applied exactly once on retry, attemptCount 0); integrated revalidation @5686ed2146: 147 background-work+extraction tests + lint + build/DTS + diff-check clean. UBS range scan: no new critical/warning. Pi (GLM 5.2 @high) blind adversarial review: PASS, 0 blocking — traced all 4 drain windows; a/b/c fail-closed (coverage never advances, receipt retryable), receipt-bound vs no-receipt distinction correct (only prod caller passes assertEffectAllowed), signal translation robust across the boundary. Nonblocking (handoff only): window-(d) partial-multi-write coverage-advance is PRE-EXISTING/out-of-scope (same accepted fail-closed boundary as u5bv.6; per-fact idempotency = candidate follow-up); telemetry start-without-end on window c; window c not directly unit-tested; non-exhausting defer (matches existing source_not_ready); add no-write-yet contract comment at 2nd throw site.

title: Make configured extraction intervals reachable from bounded post-turn snapshots
description: Final review of u5bv.8 combined range cd0c8b9b6c..017b518eda found a configuration/core-path mismatch. executePostTurnBackgroundWork requests at most ten entries in src/core/agent/background-work/post-turn-runtime.ts:184-192, while settings permits extractionInterval 1-50 in src/system/settings/form.ts:46. evaluateExtractionTriggerForSnapshot sees only the current snapshot and coverage advances only after a trigger, so a valid low-token interval of 11-50 can never interval-trigger: every sliding snapshot has at most ten uncovered messages and each job receipt completes as a no-op indefinitely. Scope: make every accepted extractionInterval reachable using bounded exact snapshots while retaining consumed-TurnID fencing and deterministic LLM-call gates. Non-goals: do not lower configured intervals silently, read unbounded history, or fall back to newer live session state.
design: Either size the source-bounded snapshot to the validated interval under the existing 512-TurnID fence cap, or durably accumulate an exact pending range that a later job can consume. The job that fires must enumerate, lock, re-read, and pass every content-bearing entry influencing the extraction. Coordinate with exact noncontiguous coverage rather than using a scalar live count.
acceptance_criteria: 1. For each valid interval boundary 1, 10, 11, and 50 with low token counts, deterministic post-turn execution fires at the configured message count and not earlier. 2. The firing extraction consumes every uncovered bounded entry exactly once even across sliding windows, retries, redactions, restore, and out-of-order claims. 3. The consumed TurnID set remains bounded, canonically ordered, projected through ICP delivery, and re-read under lock before any durable sink. 4. Threshold-trigger behavior and direct foreground undefined fallback remain unchanged. 5. Focused settings/helper/extractor/post-turn and disposable-Postgres races, mandatory npm run lint, build/DTS, settings-contract verification, and diff check pass.

title: Track exact noncontiguous durable extraction coverage
description: Final review of u5bv.8 combined range cd0c8b9b6c..017b518eda reproduced durable memory loss when bounded jobs execute out of order. src/faculties/memory/extraction/runtime-helpers.ts:145-164 and :189-211 model coverage as one count plus maximum coveredUpToMessageId. Sequence: A-B extracts IDs 1-4; C-E jobs are temporarily unavailable; later J runs a valid ten-entry snapshot for IDs 11-20 and advances the marker to 20; delayed C-E snapshots for IDs 5-10 then report zero uncovered entries, return without extraction, and their durable receipts complete. BackgroundWorkStore claim/retry ordering permits this. Scope: represent exact noncontiguous covered ranges or an equivalently strong durable/session-local coverage model so a later high ID never proves lower gaps consumed. Preserve exact fenced recoveredEntries, no live-history fallback, and bounded memory. Non-goals: no session-wide unbounded history scan, no weakening interval policy, no duplicate durable facts as a substitute.
design: Use a bounded interval/range set or monotonic contiguous-prefix plus explicit pending gaps keyed by logical session. Coverage advances only for entries actually processed successfully. Trigger evaluation counts exactly uncovered, countable entries even when snapshots arrive out of order; compaction/pruning may collapse only proven contiguous coverage.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Deterministic order B→J→C/D/E proves IDs 5-10 remain triggerable and are processed exactly once after J advances higher coverage. 2. All permutations of overlapping, duplicate, retried, and sparse snapshots preserve gaps and never double-count already covered entries. 3. Coverage storage is bounded/pruned without converting gaps into coverage and remains scoped by logical session. 4. Trigger/token evaluation consults only the exact fenced snapshot; direct undefined fallback is unchanged. 5. Focused helper/extractor/post-turn plus disposable-Postgres receipt tests, mandatory npm run lint, build/DTS, and diff check pass.

New coverage-ranges.ts models exact covered-id set as sorted disjoint inclusive intervals (binary-search membership, bounded 128 intervals dropping lowest = safe re-extraction direction); runtime-helpers.ts trigger eval + watermark advance rewired to exact set membership so an out-of-order high snapshot can no longer prove a lower gap consumed. Evidence: 117 focused tests (incl. coverage-ranges unit, B->J->C-E wiring) + 1 disposable real-PG receipt test (out-of-order 5-10 gap yields a real third extraction, exactly once); lint/build(DTS)/diff-check clean. UBS range scan: no new critical/warning vs base. Pi (GLM 5.2 @high) blind adversarial review: PASS, 0 blocking (traced interval-merge boundaries, prune safe-direction, failure-path idempotency, restart ephemerality = not a regression). Nonblocking observations in wave handoff only (leading: crash-recovery.ts:110 durable watermark has same contiguous-only shape on an unwired path). Unblocks u5bv.10.

title: Keep kube operator credentials out of the agent approval path
description: Final Spec review of x5rt.4 range 2128dca325..4035e2df64 reproduced an operator-boundary bypass in the one allowed remediation. src/operator/garden/api-routes.ts forwards the browser's ADMIN_TOKEN Authorization/Cookie through the agent-hosted Garden admin transport; src/app/agent/admin-surface.ts wires src/app/startup/support/gateway-operator-confirmation-client.ts so the agent process relays that credential to the gateway operator endpoint. Even though ADMIN_TOKEN is absent from the agent environment, the less-trusted agent can capture and replay the credential, then resolve its own kube mutation. Scope: move the credential-bearing gateway confirmation call into the independently authenticated Garden operator process, which already owns ADMIN_TOKEN, while keeping companion/agent RPC resolution denied for operator-only kube entries. Remove credential forwarding, operator endpoint client authority, related env, and related network access from the agent. Preserve the separate gateway ADMIN_TOKEN endpoint, exact resolver identity audit, ServiceAccount token rotation, and executed-but-result-audit-failed semantics delivered by x5rt.4. Files: src/operator/garden/operator-surface.ts and/or transport proxy boundary, src/operator/garden/api-routes.ts, src/app/agent/admin-surface.ts, src/app/startup/support/gateway-operator-confirmation-client.ts, src/channels/api/server.ts, deployment Helm/network policy and verification tests. Non-goals: no broad SSO redesign, no shared admin token in agent env, no off-repo proxy, no enabling production kube mutations, no live deployment.
design: The operator process must originate the gateway operator confirmation request only after its own authenticated Garden HTTP boundary succeeds. Credential bytes must not traverse the agent process or its admin transport. Agent-local confirmation listing may remain sanitized, but operator-only resolution must route directly from operator to gateway using repo-owned endpoint configuration and existing ADMIN_TOKEN ownership. The gateway continues to bind resolver {kind:operator,id:garden-admin}; normal agent RPC supplies companion identity and is rejected for resolutionAuthority=operator.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Tests prove ADMIN_TOKEN Authorization/Cookie bytes never reach agent-side handlers, agent env, agent admin transport payloads, logs, or audit. 2. An authenticated Garden operator can resolve an operator-only kube confirmation through a direct operator-to-gateway path; unauthenticated, agent-RPC, and cross-companion attempts fail closed and leave the entry pending. 3. Agent deployment/env/NetworkPolicy has no operator-confirmation credential relay authority or extra gateway API egress introduced solely for resolution. 4. Exact resolver identity remains in confirmation/audit history; request parameter binding and single-use behavior remain intact. 5. ServiceAccount token rotation and executed-but-result-audit-failed regressions remain green. 6. Focused operator/gateway/confirmation/kube tests, verify:helm-chart, mandatory npm run lint, build/DTS, and diff check pass. No Pi or production deployment is required.
close_reason: Implemented on work/x5rt-x5rt.10 (8345a741a4..2e2fc6350e), integrated to feat/x5rt-kube-self-management@07b6d387e7 (pushed). Browser ADMIN_TOKEN no longer traverses the agent: (1) buildProxyHeaders in transport-client.ts strips Authorization + psfn_token cookie on every operator->agent admin-transport request; (2) GardenOperatorSurface resolves operator-owned gateway confirmations on a direct operator->gateway path carrying the operator's own credential, credential-stripped agent-local fallback only on not_found; (3) agent-hosted surface resolves agent-local entries only, fails closed (not_found) for operator-owned entries, builds no operator gateway client; (4) Helm/NetworkPolicy: GATEWAY_OPERATOR_API_BASE_URL + gateway-API access moved agent->garden workload, agent lost gateway-API egress, gateway lost agent->gatewayApi ingress. Preserves resolver identity {kind:operator,id:garden-admin}, param binding, single-use, SA token rotation, executed-but-audit-failed. Evidence at worker head: 16 focused + 108 broader operator/gateway/confirmation/kube tests, verify:helm-chart, lint, build(DTS), diff-check all pass; integrated-branch revalidation @07b6d387e7: verify:helm-chart PASS, lint clean, 14 confirmation tests pass. UBS range scan: 2 new criticals triaged as UBS false positives (prototype-pollution flag on a plain field assignment with no merge; token-compare pattern not present in any production file). Pi (GLM 5.2 @high) blind adversarial review: PASS, 0 blocking — traced credential-strip coverage on all request builders, agent-side fail-closed, gateway-first fallback safety, resolver/single-use preservation, and NetworkPolicy egress removal. Nonblocking observations in wave handoff only. Unblocks x5rt.5/.6/.8.

title: Enforce trusted-host reapproval through a constrained fleet-auth authority API
description: Fresh final review of opl1.2 combined range 5d1785dcb1..464be9d9cd found restore quarantine can be bypassed by ordinary gateway SQL. GatewayFleetAuthPersistence exports a raw Pool at src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/gateway-persistence.ts:20-23; the runtime role receives unrestricted UPDATE on all mutable authority tables in src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/schema.ts:159-164. The restore integration test directly activates a quarantined principal, contact binding, and role using three UPDATE statements at schema.integration.test.ts:849-863, without trusted-host ceremony, current floor/lineage/generation checks, conflict checks, version/epoch updates, or an audit event. Scope: replace direct authority-state mutation with one constrained transactional reapproval API and database privilege boundary. Non-goals: no OAuth routes/UI, no passkey promotion, no approval-only provider relink, and no broad raw SQL escape hatch for future broker code.
design: Keep the gateway-owned persistence module deep: do not export its unrestricted Pool as the authority interface. Revoke ordinary runtime direct updates of lifecycle/restore/authority columns and expose narrow transactional operations or SECURITY DEFINER procedures with exact input validation. Reapproval must consume a current trusted-host ceremony, bind lineage/generation/principal/provider/companion/contact/role, recheck conflicts and tombstones under lock, bump versions/auth epoch as required, audit atomically, and never touch passkey authority.

title: Make fleet-auth lifecycle witness transitions monotonic across replicas
description: Fresh final review of opl1.2 combined range 5d1785dcb1..464be9d9cd reproduced a lost disable-to-re-enable transition across gateway replicas. FleetAuthLifecycleWitnessStore.prepareEnable at src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/lifecycle-witness.ts:93-109 releases its file lock before floor/DB reconciliation; recordEnabled at :112-123 later overwrites the witness unconditionally. initializeGatewayFleetAuthPersistence spans prepare, floor open, database reconcile, and record across src/persistence/postgres/fleet-auth/gateway-persistence.ts:243-256. Race: enabled replica A prepares with no transition; feature-off replica B records disabled; stale A records enabled; the next enable sees enabled and skips checkpoint/epoch fencing, so old sessions survive. Scope: make lifecycle transitions monotonic and replica-safe through the complete startup publish boundary. Non-goals: no global singleton gateway assumption, no long-held filesystem lock across network I/O, no feature-off state for never-enabled installs, and no loss of ordinary same-generation restart sessions.
design: Use a versioned transition token/CAS or equivalent two-phase witness protocol. prepareEnable returns the exact witness version it observed. recordEnabled may publish only if that version and phase remain unchanged; a concurrent disabled transition wins, stale startup must fail before listen, and its next retry consumes the disable transition through the non-restored floor. All writes remain durable/atomic and lineage-bound.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Deterministic two-replica interleaving A prepare-enabled, B record-disabled, A stale publish cannot erase disabled; A rejects before listen and the next enable advances restore checkpoint/auth epoch and clears ephemerals. 2. Simultaneous enabled restarts converge idempotently without revoking valid sessions or corrupting the witness. 3. Repeated disable calls and crash at every prepare/floor/DB/publish boundary over-fence or recover; no transition is lost. 4. Never-enabled feature-off remains state-free; lineage mismatch/missing floor fails closed. 5. Focused lifecycle/unit plus disposable-Postgres startup races, npm run lint, build/DTS, and diff check pass.

title: Treat empty bounded post-turn snapshots as authoritative
description: Final review of immutable u5bv.4 range fa2fdde0a4..cd0c8b9b6c reproduced the original cross-turn redaction race through an empty-snapshot fallback. SessionStore.withStableTurnRecordEligibilitySnapshot at src/persistence/sessions/store.ts:1164-1219 accepts an empty content snapshot when requiredTurnIds contains the canonical source TurnID, locks that source, rechecks empty equals empty, and invokes the effect. Non-goals: no live fallback for a durable job, no process-local dedupe, and no weakening of source or consumed-record eligibility.
design: Represent snapshot presence explicitly rather than overloading array length. When a durable handler supplies recoveredEntries, an empty array is authoritative: either the operation deterministically skips with no sink write or raises the existing source-not-ready/source-missing classification. Any fallback live read is permitted only for legacy foreground call sites that did not supply a snapshot at all.

Undefined snapshot retains the intentionally supported foreground behavior, while [] is never reinterpreted as undefined anywhere in memory extraction, emotion appraisal, or compaction. 3. Missing/reduced history during a durable job deterministically skips, defers, or fails closed with an operator-visible reason and preserves retry semantics. 4. title: Project bounded post-turn snapshots through ICP delivery status
description: Final review of immutable u5bv.4 range fa2fdde0a4..cd0c8b9b6c reproduced durable ingestion of failed or undelivered ICP assistant output. createIcpDeliveryProjectionStore in src/core/session/manager/icp-delivery-projection-store.ts:89-128 filters getRecent and getEntriesInRange but forwards getEntriesBefore directly to the raw journal. Scope: apply the canonical ICP delivery projection to every bounded ordinary extraction, emotion, and compaction read before the consumed TurnID set is derived and fenced. All bounded SessionStore read methods used by ordinary context/extraction/compaction honor the canonical delivery projection; raw access is named and limited to delivery recovery. 4. title: Make multi-write post-turn effects retry-safe
description: Final review of immutable mmo9.3 range 5d1785dcb1..fa2fdde0a4 reproduced duplicate durable effects after an ordinary post-write exception. src/core/agent/background-work/post-turn-runtime.ts:147-156 wraps an entire handler in one receipt; memory extraction performs multiple fact writes at src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts:682-799. src/core/agent/background-work/supervisor.ts:574-600 deletes the started receipt whenever the operation throws, and :470-477 schedules a generic retry. A real supervisor plus Postgres job store and durable sink wrote the same logical effect twice: first execution wrote then threw, receipt was removed, retry repeated the write and succeeded. MemoryExtractor also launches contact-profile/emotional persistence after maybeExtract returns at orchestrator.ts:860-880, extraction.ts:853-918, runtime-helpers.ts:269-292, and profile-synthesis.ts:288-295, allowing the outer receipt/fence to become applied and release while durable children remain in flight. Scope: give every durable child write an idempotent/transactional boundary that survives exceptions and keep the job receipt/fence open until all durable children settle. Non-goals: no swallowing handler errors, no blanket terminal failure for safely retryable pre-effect work, no reliance on process-local dedupe, and no detaching durable writes from job lifecycle.
design: Use stable per-logical-effect idempotency keys and sink-level atomic insert/upsert or per-child durable receipts. Never delete evidence that an effect may have occurred merely because the enclosing operation threw. Convert detached profile/emotional writes into awaited job-owned work or separately durable child jobs with their own receipts and eligibility fences. The parent job may become applied only when every owned durable child is applied; ambiguous children quarantine, while proven unapplied children can retry.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Failure injected after the first durable child write but before parent completion produces exactly one logical sink row across retry and restart; no started/ambiguous receipt is deleted into a duplicate-capable state. 2. Multi-fact memory extraction, emotion/reflection/compaction, profile synthesis, and any other multi-write handler use stable per-effect idempotency or one atomic transaction. 3. No durable child remains detached after the parent receipt is applied or its TurnRecord eligibility fence is released; shutdown waits/requeues or persists the child independently. 4. Pre-write exceptions remain retryable, post-write unknown outcomes fail closed, and fully applied receipts short-circuit duplicates. 5. Real-Postgres crash/exception/retry tests, focused handler tests, mandatory npm run lint, npm run build/DTS, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Implemented on work/mmo9-u5bv.6 (dfa9a0c7e2..69f1d81b6f), integrated to feat/mmo9-background-supervisor@e41f818086 (pushed; orchestrator resolved a post-turn-runtime.ts conflict with u5bv.10 snapshot-limit wiring, keeping both the interval sizing and the boundary-fence semantics). Three coupled fixes: (1) abandonEffect deletes ONLY a pending receipt — a boundary-crossed 'started' receipt survives, so a post-write exception fails closed as outcome_unknown on retry instead of replaying (closes the reproduced duplicate); (2) memory extraction crosses its durable boundary at the FIRST real durable write via a threaded non-crossing pre-write fence (input.effects.assertOwned), not at handler entry, so pre-write transient failures stay retryable; (3) detached contact-profile/emotional children now awaited inside the effect-guarded region (each self-swallows best-effort failure). Evidence at worker head: background-work integration 26/26; combined focused+integration 314 + 309 pass (extraction, writer, contacts incl. postgres-adapter, post-turn-runtime 14, supervisor 11) incl. new real-supervisor+PG+durable-sink exactly-once-across-retry test, store-level abandon-never-deletes-started, orchestrator await-ordering; integrated revalidation @e41f818086: 143 background-work+extraction tests + lint + build/DTS + diff-check clean. UBS range scan: no new critical/warning. Pi (GLM 5.2 @high) blind adversarial review: PASS, 0 blocking — traced every receipt-mutating path (no path deletes/downgrades a started receipt), confirmed every durable write from maybeExtract crosses the boundary first, detached children run post-cross so a retry cannot re-enter them. Nonblocking (handoff only): retry_exhausted vs effect_outcome_unknown reason-code labeling on max_attempts=1 (no duplicate); beginEffect same-owner+revision 'execute' resume is a latent footgun if a future handler calls effects.run twice per claim (pre-existing from u5bv.5); multi-fact partial-write fail-closed (1..k persist, k+1..N not retried) = accepted AC2 fail-closed design; scheduleProfileRefresh coalescing widens receipt-open window (no duplicate).

title: Requeue pre-effect jobs safely during graceful shutdown
description: Final review of immutable mmo9.3 range 5d1785dcb1..fa2fdde0a4 reproduced loss of work that had not crossed any side-effect boundary. src/core/agent/background-work/supervisor.ts:554-576 writes an effects.run started receipt before provider/compute begins. Supervisor stop at :330-347 waits five seconds but does not release or requeue claims; production closes stores at src/app/agent/control-plane.ts:172-202 and src/app/agent/main.ts:889-892. On restart src/persistence/postgres/background-work-store.ts:1164-1204 converts every expired job with a started receipt into terminal effect_outcome_unknown, even when sinkWrites=0. Scope: distinguish safely cancelable/pre-effect work from genuinely outcome-ambiguous work, and make graceful stop durably requeue or release only the former before closing stores. Preserve fail-closed handling once any externally durable effect may have occurred. Non-goals: no process-wide kill semantics, no assuming provider cancellation proves an external side effect absent, no infinite shutdown wait, and no weakening multi-replica lease ownership.
design: Introduce an explicit durable phase boundary rather than treating handler entry as effect entry. A job canceled before that boundary can be returned to pending/retry state under its claim token during graceful shutdown; a job at or beyond the boundary retains outcome-unknown quarantine unless an idempotent receipt proves completion. Supervisor stop must coordinate active AbortSignals, bounded drain, and claim release/requeue before Postgres close. Recovery must classify from the durable phase, not merely receipt existence.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A real-Postgres graceful-shutdown race with a blocked provider/compute step and zero sink writes stops within the configured bound, durably requeues the job, and a new supervisor completes it exactly once. 2. A crash or shutdown after crossing the possible-effect boundary remains fail closed as effect_outcome_unknown unless an applied receipt proves completion. 3. Shutdown never releases a claim while the old worker can still cross the effect boundary; cancellation and ownership checks are ordered and tested. 4. Multi-replica claim recovery, lease expiry, bounded quarantine/crash recovery, and normal drain behavior remain correct. 5. Focused unit and disposable Postgres tests, mandatory npm run lint, npm run build/DTS, and git diff --check pass.

title: Fence every TurnRecord consumed by a post-turn effect
description: Final review of immutable mmo9.3 range 5d1785dcb1..fa2fdde0a4 reproduced a stale-source write across turns. src/persistence/postgres/turn-record-eligibility-fence.ts:14-20 keys the advisory fence by logicalSessionId plus the durable job source turnId, and src/core/agent/background-work/post-turn-runtime.ts:133-142 holds only that source fence. Memory extraction reads the whole recent session window at src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts:285-292 and writes derived facts at :682-799; emotion and compaction handlers also consume multi-turn windows. Concrete failure: older turn A contains content later redacted; newer turn B schedules extraction; B holds only its own fence while redaction of A completes under a different key; B then persists A-derived content. Scope: make every TurnRecord whose content can influence a durable post-turn effect participate in the same eligibility serialization/recheck as that effect, using stable lock ordering and bounded consumed sets or an equally strong source-only design. Preserve canonical fingerprint, duplicate, tombstone, restore, and queue ownership checks inside the effect boundary. Non-goals: no broad extraction redesign, no weakening redaction, no content-bearing diagnostics, and no unbounded session-wide lock.
design: At the point the handler forms its bounded input snapshot, identify the exact consumed TurnIDs. Serialize with TurnRecord redact/restore/tombstone writers for every consumed ID in deterministic order, then re-read/revalidate the snapshot while fenced and keep the fence through the effect receipt/sink boundary. If a handler cannot enumerate exact consumed records, fail closed or narrow it to an enumerable source; never assume the durable job source TurnID covers the whole recent window. Audit lock ordering against foreground/session fences and prove no reverse acquisition.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A deterministic real-Postgres race with turn A in the recent window and source turn B proves redaction/restore of A cannot complete while a B effect can still consume A; after redaction wins, B rechecks and performs no A-derived write. 2. Memory, emotion, reflection/compaction, and every other multi-turn post-turn handler enumerate and fence all content-bearing TurnIDs or are explicitly source-only with tests. 3. Duplicate TurnRecords, source tombstones, sibling-store redactions, and restore remain exact and fail closed. 4. Advisory locks acquire in stable order with bounded cardinality; cross-session work remains concurrent and no deadlock/reverse-order path is found. 5. Focused unit and disposable Postgres races, mandatory npm run lint, npm run build/DTS, and git diff --check pass.
notes:
Implemented in cd0c8b9b6c on isolated range fa2fdde0a4..cd0c8b9b6c. Class-6 TOCTOU fix: bounded exact session snapshots enumerate every consumed TurnID, acquire deduplicated Postgres advisory fences in canonical order, re-read exact content under lock, revalidate physical-source ownership/tombstone/duplicate eligibility, and hold all fences through effect receipt and durable sink. Memory, emotion, and auto-compaction now consume their exact source-bounded snapshots; the sole production intention hook was audited source-only because it consumes only the canonical source message/response pair. Lock audit found eligibility outer, queue-effect/session-tail/filesystem locks inner, no reverse acquisition; 512 unique-TurnID cap fails closed. Deterministic disposable-Postgres race proves A redaction wins over B stale capture with no stale sink write, restore blocks through the consuming effect, reverse-order overlap completes, unrelated sessions remain concurrent, and duplicate TurnRecords fail closed. Validation: 122 tests across Postgres integration/supervisor/turn execution; 247 focused post-turn/session/memory/wiring tests; 3 emotion-scoping tests; npm run lint; npm run build including DTS; git diff --check. Sibling beads u5bv.5 and u5bv.6 untouched. No Pi or production access.
2026-07-15 fresh final review of fa2fdde0a4..cd0c8b9b6c verified two residual P1 interactions after implementation/lint/build passed: bounded getEntriesBefore/compaction reads bypass the ICP delivery projection, and authoritative empty recoveredEntries falls back to live unfenced history. No second inline remediation was started. Fresh children psfn-framework-u5bv.7 and .8 own the verified leftovers; .4 remains isolated pending integration into the mmo9.3 candidate.

Exact bounded consumed-TurnID fencing, deterministic multi-lock ordering, under-lock snapshot/physical TurnRecord revalidation, 512-key fail-closed cap, and source-only intention audit shipped on the integration branch. title: Add versioned owner-file migration preflight to Kubernetes rollouts
description: The first live rollout of merged 5d1785dcb1 failed closed twice before application readiness because existing canonical owner files predated newly mandatory schema fields. /app/system-data/scheduler.json lacked scheduler.icpAutonomy; after an atomic disabled-default migration, /app/system-data/charge-policy.json lacked companion_social, companionSocialContinuation, icpCostBreaker, and fatigue.socialRegulation. A merge-missing-defaults one-shot allowed the new image to start, but rollback to the prior image then correctly rejected the new icpCostBreaker key until only the newly added fields were removed again. This demonstrates that required owner-schema changes currently have no versioned deploy preflight or reversible cutover contract. Scope: design and implement an explicit alpha migration lane for canonical JSON owner files used by scripts/ops/ship-kube-update.sh and live Kubernetes deployment; include dry-run, exact old/new schema recognition, operator-value preservation, atomic writes, audit evidence, forward validation by the target image, and rollback compatibility/snapshot restoration. Add the temporary support to the named live alpha migration boundary in docs/specifications.md with beta-removal criteria before enabling it. Files likely include focused scripts/ops migration modules/tests, config validators/seed metadata, ship/validate scripts, and specifications/operations docs only where contractually required. Non-goals: no generic recursive seed merge, no silent startup fallback, no overwriting existing operator values, no acceptance of unknown/malformed keys, no parallel config roots, and no automatic production mutation without an explicit approved release step.
design: Use a small versioned migration registry keyed by owner file and exact from/to schema fingerprint, not ad hoc default merging. Each migration declares preconditions, additions/removals/transforms, invariant checks, and reverse/restore strategy. The ship preflight runs target-image validation against a read-only snapshot, emits a content-safe plan, requires the existing deployment authorization boundary, then performs an atomic in-volume transaction and records before/after digests without values. If Helm rollout fails, rollback restores the exact pre-migration owner bytes before starting the old image. Unknown source shapes or operator-modified migration fields fail closed for manual review.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Fixtures matching the pre-5d1785 live scheduler and charge-policy shapes migrate to the target schemas while preserving every pre-existing JSON value, including custom run-charge quotas; only declared fields are added. 2. Forward migration is atomic, fsyncs file+directory, emits only file/version/digests/changed paths, and target validators accept the result; malformed/unknown/already-modified shapes fail without changing bytes. 3. A forced Helm failure restores exact pre-migration bytes before old pods restart, and the prior validators accept them; successful rollout retains the new schema. 4. ship-kube-update integrates the preflight without remote git resets or off-repo authoritative config, and validate-kube-rollout verifies the expected schema/version. 5. docs/specifications.md names the temporary alpha boundary, validation, and beta-removal criteria. 6. Focused migration/ship tests, verify:settings-contract where applicable, verify:helm-chart, mandatory npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Duplicate of existing psfn-framework-m82u. The full 2026-07-15 scheduler/charge-policy rollout and rollback incident, versioned registry design, target-image preflight, exact-byte rollback, custom-value preservation, alpha-boundary requirement, and acceptance criteria were merged into m82u; relation to 5vhi added.

title: Wire the audit opaque-ID HMAC dependency into the Kubernetes agent
description: Live rollout of merged framework commit 5d1785dcb1 failed after successful scheduler/charge-policy owner migrations: psfn-agent initialized, then src/operator/garden/local-admin-contract.ts failed closed because Garden audit history opaque IDs required key material. The first candidate f7d924e9 wired the gateway root GATEWAY_SESSION_HMAC_KEY into the agent; independent security review correctly rejected that because src/boundary/gateway/companion-auth.ts can use the root keyring to mint arbitrary companion/role proofs. The agent already receives a distinct role-bound GATEWAY_SESSION_INTEGRITY_AUTH_TOKEN in Helm and from the scrubbed split launcher. Scope: derive a dedicated Garden audit opaque-ID keyring from that worker proof with a one-way domain-separated transform, remove the gateway root from the agent, preserve fail-closed validation, and prove both rendered Helm and env-i split-launch boundaries. Relevant files: src/operator/garden/audit-opaque-id-keyring.ts, src/operator/garden/local-admin-contract.ts, deploy/helm/psfn/templates/workloads.yaml, scripts/verify-helm-chart.mjs, and focused script-verification tests. Non-goals: do not expose or copy the gateway root, add a parallel live secret lifecycle, weaken audit key requirements, change gateway proof verification, move audit history ownership, or redesign the session-integrity RPC.
design: Treat the already-delegated internal_session_integrity proof as pseudorandom input material, not as the audit key itself. Validate the canonical version.hex64 proof shape; HMAC the proof digest under the fixed psfn-garden-audit-opaque-id-key-v1 domain plus key version; expose the result only as an AuditOpaqueIdKeyring to the Garden audit service. Local admin construction consumes config.gatewaySessionIntegrityAuthToken, which agent-mode config already requires and sanitizes from public admin config. Kubernetes keeps GATEWAY_SESSION_HMAC_KEY only in gateway; agent keeps its existing GATEWAY_SESSION_INTEGRITY_AUTH_TOKEN Secret reference, and Garden gets neither. npm run split already derives/passes the worker proof through its env-i allowlist; the regression executes a real derivation probe inside that scrubbed child and proves the root is absent. Rotating the worker proof intentionally changes opaque IDs while preserving the underlying audit records.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Parsed rendered Helm container env shows GATEWAY_SESSION_HMAC_KEY exactly in gateway and absent from agent/Garden; agent retains only its role-bound GATEWAY_SESSION_INTEGRITY_AUTH_TOKEN dependency. 2. A stable known-vector test proves domain-separated audit-key derivation; absent/malformed proofs fail closed, and a proof minted with the derived audit key is rejected by the gateway root keyring. 3. A real env-i split-launch regression proves the scrubbed agent receives the worker proof, never receives the gateway root, and can derive the expected audit keyring. 4. In-process Garden server/API and audit-history suites pass with the scoped derivation; no literal production secret, fallback to root, new secret owner path, or Garden exposure is introduced. 5. helm lint, parsed rendered-manifest test, npm run verify:helm-chart including provenance, mandatory npm run lint, npm run build including DTS, targeted tests, and git diff --check pass. 6. After merge, an exact-image rollout to the operator-directed local k3d cluster reaches Ready for agent/gateway/Garden; Garden health and authenticated audit-history API pass without audit-key startup errors; rendered live env still keeps the root gateway-only. Production rollout is explicitly out of scope after the operator directed that psfn-shard receive no further deployment testing.

title: Fence TurnRecord eligibility through content-consuming background effects
description: Final independent review of the frozen mmo9.3 candidate at d7179bd1d0 reproduced a privacy-relevant TOCTOU race. src/core/agent/background-work/post-turn-runtime.ts requireCanonicalTurnRecord() checks source eligibility/tombstone state once before raw TurnRecord rehydration, then later effect fencing checks only queue-claim ownership. A concurrent tombstone or uniqueness revocation after rehydration can therefore allow raw user/assistant content to reach intention effects; src/core/intention/runtime-wiring.ts passes assistant content to src/core/intention/postgres-adapters/intention-record-adapter.ts, which can persist a private excerpt. Repro: tombstone immediately after lookup yielded eligibilityCalls=1, eligibleAtEffect=false, persisted=private-response. Scope: make canonical source eligibility authoritative through every content-consuming/durable effect boundary for all four mmo9.3 job kinds, coordinated with tombstone/uniqueness writes and queue ownership. Preserve minimal-reference queue rows and exact-once effects. Likely files: post-turn-runtime.ts, TurnRecord/session persistence ports and Postgres adapters/migrations, effect fencing, and deterministic tests. Non-goals: no second raw-content store, no polling-only/uncoordinated boolean recheck presented as atomic fencing, no changes to retention policy, handler business logic, or mmo9.5 cadence.
design: Introduce a coordinated source-eligibility fence (for example an eligibility generation/epoch or transaction/advisory-lock protocol) that tombstone/uniqueness writers advance under the same durable serialization used by the background effect. Rehydrated content is a candidate, not authority: immediately before a content-consuming effect commits, the worker must atomically prove queue-claim ownership, the expected source identity/fingerprint, and current eligibility. Eligibility loss produces a privacy-safe stale/deferred terminal transition with no raw error/content telemetry and no durable handler effect.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A deterministic test rehydrates an eligible TurnRecord, tombstones it before the intention effect boundary, and proves no response strategy/private excerpt or other handler effect persists; lifecycle output contains no partner content. 2. Equivalent uniqueness/source-supersession interleavings fail closed, while an unchanged eligible source executes exactly once. 3. A disposable real-Postgres race coordinates tombstone/uniqueness mutation against a claimed job across two stores and proves either the effect commits before the revocation transaction or revocation wins and the effect is absent—never revoked source content after the fence. 4. All four job kinds retain correct stale/defer policy, minimal queue payloads, fingerprints, effect receipts, retries, and restart recovery. 5. Focused post-turn/session/TurnRecord/supervisor tests, disposable real-Postgres integration, touched SubstrateAgent tests, mandatory npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
notes: Implementation committed as adf8fff536 on fix/u5bv-eligibility-fence from immutable base d7179bd1d03c10a4c6a52a621cdd810ae5a6d2eb. RED: npm test -- --run src/core/agent/background-work/post-turn-runtime.test.ts reproduced the race; the intention job resolved and persisted private response after source revocation rather than rejecting. GREEN: added a Postgres session advisory-lock eligibility fence keyed by companion scope, logical session, and TurnID; production session composition requires it; canonical TurnRecord append plus redact/restore mutations share it; all four post-turn handlers now re-prove claim ownership, canonical fingerprint/source eligibility, and finish effect receipt handling while the fence remains held. The consumer API fails closed when the fence is absent. Deterministic unit proof persists no intention response after revocation. Disposable real-Postgres proof coordinates two background stores plus separate fence pools and proves effect-first ordering, tombstone-first absence, and duplicate/uniqueness-first absence. Validation: final race/session/Postgres set 3 files and 111 tests passed, including 14 real-Postgres integration tests; startup/adapter/runtime wiring set 3 files and 19 tests passed; earlier full touched-path set 9 files and 434 tests passed; mandatory npm run lint passed; npm run build including DTS passed; git diff --check passed. Local standards/spec and static lock-order audit found no remaining P0/P1; source advisory fence is outer to queue effect receipts and filesystem locks, and no reverse production acquisition was found. Bead intentionally remains in_progress for parent integration and fresh review.

title: Fence same-session foreground ownership through background side-effect boundaries
description: Final independent review of the frozen mmo9.3 candidate at d7179bd1d0 reproduced three fail-open interleavings in the durable BackgroundWorkSupervisor. (1) src/persistence/postgres/background-work-store.ts beginForeground() takes a per-session advisory lock but claimNext() does not, so replica B can claim while replica A foreground acquisition is in flight; the foreground commit then leaves the already-running claim untouched. (2) src/core/agent/background-work/supervisor.ts executeClaim() checks foreground state only once; effects.assertOwned() checks queue ownership but not foreground leases, so a foreground turn arriving before the side-effect boundary can overlap a background durable effect. (3) foreground renewal loss is only logged by ensureHeartbeat(); ForegroundWorkLease exposes no ownership-loss signal, so after lease expiry another replica can claim while the original foreground turn is still local. Scope: make the per-session foreground fence authoritative across acquisition, claim, every content/durable side-effect boundary, renewal loss, defer/retry, and cross-replica operation; preserve cross-session concurrency and the existing record-first handoff. Likely files: src/persistence/postgres/background-work-store.ts and its integration tests; src/core/agent/background-work/supervisor.ts, types/ports, and tests. Non-goals: no provider preemption or reserved capacity, no sub-tick scheduler/cadence work from mmo9.5, no broad supervisor rewrite, and no change to the four handler semantics.
design: Use one durable session-serialization/ownership contract shared by foreground acquisition, background claim, and effect fencing. A background claim must not cross a durable effect boundary unless it can prove both queue-claim ownership and absence of a current same-session foreground lease. Foreground lease renewal loss must become an observable ownership-loss signal to the local turn/supervisor rather than a log-only condition. Safe pre-effect work should durably defer and resume under the same idempotency key; already-committed effects must not be duplicated. Keep telemetry content-free and fail closed on store/check errors.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A deterministic disposable-Postgres two-store test pauses foreground acquisition after its lock begins, races claimNext on replica B, and proves no same-session job becomes running before/after foreground commit. 2. A deterministic supervisor test lets a claim pass its initial check, begins foreground work before effects.assertOwned, and proves the background effect does not run; the same idempotency key durably defers and resumes exactly once after foreground release. 3. A forced renewForeground ownership-loss/expiry test proves the original local foreground lease receives a loss signal and no second replica can execute a same-session background effect while that foreground work remains active. 4. Cross-session claims remain concurrent; retry deadlines/idempotency/effect receipts and shutdown behavior remain correct. 5. Focused supervisor/store tests, disposable real-Postgres integration, touched SubstrateAgent tests, mandatory npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
notes: Implemented one authoritative per-session Postgres advisory fence across foreground begin/renew/end, background claim, and effect receipt start. claimNext uses try-lock session selection so an in-flight same-session foreground acquisition cannot be crossed while unrelated sessions remain claimable. Effect checkpoints now classify queue lease loss versus foreground activity; safe pre-effect work durably defers under the original idempotency key and resumes once, while an operation that already returned success commits its receipt exactly once. ForegroundWorkLease now exposes an AbortSignal. Renewal loss aborts the exact request-owned active agent run and observed expiry leaves a bounded durable quarantine; a crashed owner recovers after that bounded window. Red/green evidence: reproduced claim during paused foreground acquisition, effect execution after foreground arrival, log-only renewal loss, unconsumed turn-lifecycle loss, and post-effect duplicate/defer behavior before the fixes. Validation: 250 focused supervisor, post-turn, turn-support, full touched turn-execution, full SubstrateAgent, and disposable real-Postgres tests passed; the 9 highest-risk interleavings passed 10 consecutive runs (90 assertions); npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed. The broad tsconfig.eslint noEmit check remains unusable on the unchanged baseline because it reports thousands of unrelated pre-existing test-fixture errors; production build/DTS and touched tests are clean.

title: Fence passkey revocation across fleet-auth restore
description:
## Summary
Correct the canonical Fleet SSO decision so an old fleet_auth backup cannot resurrect a revoked or replaced WebAuthn passkey. Current gap: opl1.2 persists passkey_credentials in the restorable artifact, but its authority_generation covers provider/link/tombstone/contact binding/role and global_auth_epoch invalidates only session/grant/challenge/evidence state. opl1.1 restore design and AC14, the opl1 parent restore prose, opl1.10 strong JIT/passkey replacement, and opl1.12 restore certification omit passkey credentials and their revocation history from the non-restored monotonic fence.

## Rationale
Concrete P1 failure: back up with passkey A active; A is stolen; trusted-host recovery revokes A and enrolls B; restore the old artifact; exact legitimate account/binding/role reapproval later makes restored A registered again unless credential authority is independent. A can then satisfy user-verifying strong JIT or trusted-ingress opl1.15 privacy break-glass. An auth epoch bump is insufficient because resurrected A can mint new current-epoch sessions and grants. This is partner-data/privacy exposure and account-recovery rollback, so old A must remain denied even after legitimate account authority is reapproved.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Rely on global_auth_epoch: rejected because it invalidates existing ephemeral authority but does not make restored credential A revoked when A authenticates again. 2. Let exact account/binding/role reapproval also promote restored passkeys: rejected because it conflates independent account and credential ceremonies and recreates the exploit. 3. Merge restored passkey rows into the current fleet_auth table: rejected because a restorable table cannot be the monotonic authority that decides which side wins. 4. Keep the authoritative current verifier and lifecycle ledger in a non-restored PasskeyAuthorityFloor, quarantine every restored row, and require a distinct exact current credential ceremony when no exact current verifier survives: selected because current B/tombstones remain authoritative while restored A cannot return.

## Scope and Non-goals
Update the canonical parent and every affected child design/acceptance field so current passkey authority is monotonic outside restorable state and restored passkeys fail closed. No code. Preserve accepted provider/role/Discord/privacy decisions, gateway-only authority, safe first-owner bootstrap, current-plus-new provider authentication, the ban on enabled legacy recovery tokens, and all opl1.19/.19.2/.19.3 decisions. Do not create a reusable recovery token or weaken user-verifying WebAuthn requirements.
design: Use a trusted-host-owned non-restored monotonic `PasskeyAuthorityFloor`/credential-revocation registry integrated with `TrustedHostAuthorityFloor`. It is the sole authoritative source for current credential identity/fingerprint, public-key verifier and RP/principal/expected-provider binding, generation/status, counter/backup signals, and revocation/replacement tombstones; authenticator private material is never stored. Any `fleet_auth.passkey_credentials` row is a non-authoritative projection/import candidate. Enrollment, compromise, revocation, replacement, and recovery advance/bind the floor before an old credential can remain usable; failure over-fences. Restore/disable-to-re-enable advances the account restore checkpoint and auth epoch while preserving the current credential floor, quarantines every restored passkey, and merges restored credential history without replacing or rolling back later entries. Account/binding/role reapproval does not promote passkeys. Current replacement B remains usable only through an exact non-restored credential/floor match. If current verifier state is missing, unavailable, or inconsistent, passkey authentication and strong assurance deny until a separate expected-provider one-time trusted-host nonce plus matching OAuth and live WebAuthn origin/RP/user-verification registration creates a new generation. Replacement atomically tombstones the prior credential, revokes superseded sessions/grants/challenges, advances generation, and audits. Restored or tombstoned A can never become current.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Canonical fields explicitly bind passkey credentials and revocation/replacement history to a non-restored monotonic `PasskeyAuthorityFloor`; global auth epoch is not claimed sufficient. 2. Every restored passkey is quarantined and cannot authenticate, step up, mint JIT, or satisfy opl1.15 privacy assurance; account/binding/role reapproval never promotes it. 3. Backup with A→trusted-host revoke/replace A with B→restore old backup→reapprove account/binding/role→attempt A denies before and after reapproval. Restored rows/history cannot erase current B or current tombstones. B works only from an exact current non-restored floor entry; missing/unavailable/mismatched verifier state fails closed. 4. Distinct re-enrollment/recovery requires expected stable provider subject, trusted-host one-time nonce, matching OAuth, live origin/RP/user-verification validation, atomic consume/generation/audit, and revocation of superseded sessions/grants/challenges; the new generation never reactivates A. 5. opl1 parent/.1/.2/.10/.12 design and acceptance agree, threat certification includes the exact sequence and JIT/privacy assertions, graph cycles remain empty, .2 stays blocked by .1, targeted lint is zero, and fresh final P0/P1 review is CLEAN.

title: Make member-specific deny a PSFN hard veto for Discord administrators
description:
## Summary
Resolve the final ambiguity between Discord ADMINISTRATOR semantics and PSFN room-evidence policy. Discord normally lets ADMINISTRATOR bypass channel overwrites, but PSFN treats an explicit member-specific channel deny as a hard evidence veto even for an administrator. When that veto is absent, current ADMINISTRATOR may otherwise contribute to proven Discord visibility and private-thread moderator evidence. It never creates or widens PSFN role, trust, contact binding, memory access, or other authority.

## Rationale
The previous opl1.1 and opl1.4 wording simultaneously said member-specific deny always denies and ADMINISTRATOR may satisfy visibility according to Discord semantics. In the combined case, those statements choose opposite outcomes. Leaving that ambiguity could expose a companion room despite an explicit per-member veto. Separating the native Discord calculation from PSFN final evidence preserves useful administrator visibility/moderator signals while keeping the stricter PSFN denial boundary fail closed.

## Scope
Update tracker decision fields in opl1.1, opl1.4, the opl1.12 certification fixtures, and exact equivalent opl1 wording. Persist or expose the native Discord result, explicit member-specific-deny veto, and final PSFN evidence result separately. Require a combined ADMINISTRATOR plus member-specific deny => deny regression alongside ordinary administrator and ordinary member-deny fixtures. Preserve every opl1.19.1 and opl1.19.2 authority, bootstrap, recovery, privacy, restore, and no-fallback decision.

## Non-goals
No product code, live Discord change, OAuth-scope change, removal of ADMINISTRATOR from all visibility evidence, PSFN role redesign, reopening other fleet-auth decisions, or unrelated editorial cleanup. Do not close opl1.19.3, opl1.19.2, opl1.19.1, opl1.19, or opl1.1 until one fresh independent P0/P1 review accepts the frozen candidate.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Mirror Discord exactly and let ADMINISTRATOR bypass the member overwrite: rejected because PSFN deliberately treats the explicit member-specific deny as a stricter operator safety veto. 2. Ignore ADMINISTRATOR entirely: rejected because current administrator status remains valid Discord visibility and private-thread moderator evidence when no PSFN hard veto exists. 3. Clarify only the certification test: rejected because canonical decision and implementation beads would remain internally contradictory even if one fixture happened to choose deny.
design: Treat Discord's native effective-permission calculation as an input to PSFN evidence, not the final PSFN admission decision. Preserve the native Discord result, then apply an explicit PSFN member-specific-channel-deny hard veto before producing the final evidence result. If the veto is absent, current Discord ADMINISTRATOR may contribute to visibility and private-thread moderator evidence according to Discord semantics. It never creates or widens PSFN role, trust, contact binding, memory access, or other authority. Require the three-way executable fixture matrix: ordinary ADMINISTRATOR positive evidence, ordinary member-specific deny, and ADMINISTRATOR plus member-specific deny => deny.
acceptance_criteria: 1. opl1.1 and opl1.4 explicitly state member-specific deny is a PSFN hard veto even when the principal has Discord ADMINISTRATOR. 2. ADMINISTRATOR may otherwise affect proven Discord visibility/private-thread moderator evidence but never PSFN role/trust/memory. 3. Certification requires an ADMINISTRATOR plus member-specific deny yields deny fixture, alongside ordinary administrator and member-deny cases. 4. Search finds no contradictory fallback across opl1, bd lint is clean, dependency cycles are empty, and a fresh final P0/P1 review is CLEAN before opl1.1 closes.

Frozen tracker-only decision candidate prepared 2026-07-15 for one fresh independent P0/P1 review. No product code, lint, build, git commit, or PR is part of this remediation lane. Do not close opl1.19.3, opl1.19.2, opl1.19.1, opl1.19, or opl1.1 until that review is CLEAN.

Exact changed fields:
- psfn-framework-opl1.1: design and acceptance_criteria. The canonical DiscordEvidenceSnapshot now separates native Discord permission result, member-specific-deny veto, and final PSFN evidence result; the design, threat matrix, and executable acceptance matrix state ADMINISTRATOR plus member-specific deny => deny.
- psfn-framework-opl1.4: description, design, and acceptance_criteria. A member-specific channel deny is an explicit PSFN hard veto even for ADMINISTRATOR; absent that veto, current ADMINISTRATOR may contribute only to Discord visibility/private-thread moderator evidence. Persistence and tests distinguish the native result, veto bit, and final result.
- psfn-framework-opl1.12: design and acceptance_criteria. Deterministic certification requires ordinary ADMINISTRATOR positive evidence, ordinary member-specific denial, and combined ADMINISTRATOR plus member-specific deny => deny fixtures.
- psfn-framework-opl1.19.2: description and acceptance_criteria received only the equivalent hard-veto clarification; an appended note records that opl1.19.2's no-fallback decision is unchanged.

Preserved decisions: every opl1.19.1 gateway-only broker, recovery, first-owner bootstrap, provider replacement, privacy, durable-restore, assertion, credential-separation, and feature-off decision remains unchanged. opl1.19.2's complete-current-bot-evidence and no-PSFN-fallback decision remains unchanged. No configured role, PSFN role, or other authority can substitute for missing/unknown/expired Discord evidence or override any denial.

Canonical opl1 through opl1.18 had zero occurrences of the old active forms: 'Discord ADMINISTRATOR can satisfy', 'Discord ADMINISTRATOR may satisfy Discord visibility', 'Discord ADMINISTRATOR affects only', 'permissionInputs/result', 'absent private-thread membership', 'deny or require explicit PSFN authorization', and 'bot-observed overwrites or explicit configured role rules'. title: Remove the last Discord visibility fallback from fleet SSO
description:
## Summary
The fresh final review of opl1.19.1 found one remaining P1 contradiction in psfn-framework-opl1.4 description. That field said channel evidence could use bot-observed overwrites or explicit configured role rules, and that unproven private-thread visibility could deny or require explicit PSFN authorization. Those phrases create a fallback where configured PSFN authority can admit someone despite missing Discord overwrite evidence or private-thread membership.

## Rationale
The stale phrases conflict with opl1.4 own adversarial correction and acceptance plus canonical opl1.1. Configured mappings may only narrow a complete current bot-observed Discord effective-permission result. A member-specific deny, missing or unknown overwrite input, expired evidence, absent bot observation, and a private thread with neither explicit current membership nor current MANAGE_THREADS must deny deterministically. Under the subsequent psfn-framework-opl1.19.3 clarification, Discord ADMINISTRATOR may otherwise contribute to Discord visibility and private-thread moderator evidence, but a member-specific channel deny remains a PSFN hard veto even for ADMINISTRATOR; it never grants PSFN authority. Leaving contradictory prose gives an implementer two incompatible security contracts and risks a fail-open room-access path.

## Scope
Correct opl1.4 description, design, and acceptance so the evidence prerequisite, deny cases, private-thread rule, and Discord ADMINISTRATOR boundary are unambiguous. Search the complete opl1 graph across description, design, acceptance, and notes for equivalent stale fallback wording. Update the canonical parent or another child only if equivalent fallback language actually exists.

## Non-goals
No code, OAuth-scope change, PSFN role redesign, reopening of the six opl1.19.1 authority/bootstrap/restore fixes, or unrelated editorial cleanup. Keep opl1.19.2, opl1.19.1, opl1.19, and opl1.1 open until a fresh independent final review accepts the frozen decision candidate.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Leave the corrected adversarial paragraph while retaining the contradictory summary: rejected because an implementation bead must be internally consistent. 2. Permit an explicit PSFN role or configured Discord-role rule to substitute for incomplete bot evidence: rejected because it converts narrowing policy into a fail-open visibility authority. 3. Rewrite every Discord mention in the epic: rejected because the rest of the canonical graph already expresses the accepted fail-closed contract and unrelated edits would risk reopening settled decisions.
acceptance_criteria: 1. opl1.4 description, design, and acceptance unambiguously require a complete current bot-observed Discord effective-permission result before PSFN mapping can narrow access. 2. No explicit configured role rule, PSFN role, or other PSFN authorization can substitute for missing or unknown overwrite evidence, a member-specific deny, expired evidence, absent bot observation, or a private thread lacking both proven current membership and proven current MANAGE_THREADS; every such case denies. 3. Discord ADMINISTRATOR may otherwise contribute only to Discord visibility/private-thread moderator evidence; a member-specific channel deny remains a PSFN hard veto even for ADMINISTRATOR, and ADMINISTRATOR never grants PSFN authority. 4. A search across every opl1 bead description, design, acceptance, and notes finds no equivalent fallback contradiction. 5. Targeted bd lint is clean, bd dep cycles is empty, and a fresh independent P0/P1 final review of the canonical decision is CLEAN before opl1.1 closes.

title: Make gateway notification receipts transport-truthful
description: Summary: The 343f notification-ack change counts ready/healthy gateway connections, but GatewayRpcConnection.send returns whether the transport accepted the frame. GatewayServer.notifyAll currently ignores that result and increments anyway; notifyChannelMessage multi-companion routing also returns 1 unconditionally. A socket can close after health refresh but before send, so Discord receives forwarded_to_agent and suppresses its error even though no agent received the turn. Relevant files: src/boundary/gateway/server.ts notifyAll/notifyOne/notifyChannelMessage; src/boundary/gateway/transport.ts GatewayRpcConnection and NDJSON/WebSocket implementations; src/boundary/gateway/channel-surfaces.ts; server/channel tests. Important transport nuance: WebSocket send false means closed/not-open/rejected. Node net.Socket.write false means backpressure after the frame was accepted, not rejection, so do not treat NDJSON backpressure as message loss. Define an unambiguous accepted-versus-rejected send contract or normalize implementations so the receipt count means frame accepted for delivery. Scope: single and multi-companion notification paths only, deterministic close-race tests, preserve exact companion routing and current health checks. Why: otherwise a broken core Discord path loses partner turns while emitting a false success acknowledgement. Non-goals: end-to-end agent processing acknowledgement, retry/queue redesign, Satellite Hub diagnosis, provider fallback, or changes to blocked_by_policy/authored/noReply semantics.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A single-companion ready/healthy connection whose transport rejects the frame yields recipient count zero and the Discord boundary emits no forwarded_to_agent acknowledgement. 2. A multi-companion exact route whose selected connection rejects the frame likewise fails closed without rerouting or broadcasting. 3. An NDJSON socket write that returns false solely for backpressure still counts as accepted because Node already queued the frame; a destroyed socket does not. WebSocket closed/not-open/send-throw does not count. 4.
