title: Resolve final fleet SSO authority and bootstrap contradictions
description:
Correct the six residual P1 contradictions from the final psfn-framework-opl1.1 decision review. Update the canonical bead fields, not product code.

1. Gateway ownership: remove every opl1.3 allowance for an operator-side broker. OAuth exchange, session authority, fleet_auth DML and all secret/private signing/pepper resolution belong only to the unified HTTPS gateway's dedicated fleet-auth broker; the per-companion operator is a verifier/proxy.
2. Recovery credential: remove admin-token break-glass wording from opl1 parent and opl1.3. In enabled mode legacy ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token is never recovery. Use only the independently provisioned trusted-ingress recovery credential defined by .1/.7/.10.
3. First-owner bootstrap: specify a fail-closed trusted-host ceremony that pre-binds a one-time nonce to the expected stable provider subject, companion, intended contact binding and initial owner grant. Require matching OAuth plus UV WebAuthn, explicit local operator confirmation, atomic consume/audit, and no existing active owner. Subsequent owner grants use ordinary privileged policy; the ceremony cannot be replayed after an owner exists.
4. Provider replacement: remove where-possible ambiguity. Ordinary link/replacement must authenticate current and new identities; inability to authenticate current forces the trusted-host recovery ceremony, never approval-only relink.
5. Privacy grants: update opl1.11 summary/design/acceptance so routine JIT grants are only self/co-subject. Every non-subject owner/admin reveal is exclusively opl1.15 privacy break-glass with trusted ingress and UV WebAuthn.
6. Durable restore fencing: define a concrete authoritative rule. After restore or re-enable, all restored durable provider links, contact bindings and role grants are quarantined/suspended until trusted-host reapproval against current companion/contact state; tombstone/revocation authority must be monotonic outside the restored snapshot or re-established by that ceremony. Regression: backup, revoke/unlink, restore old backup, fresh OAuth login remains denied.

Update opl1.1 acceptance/threat matrix and children .2/.3/.5/.11/.12 as necessary. Search the whole opl1 epic for stale contradictory phrases. Keep .17/.18 blocking graph and all previously accepted decisions unchanged. Record exact changed bead fields and run bd dep cycles.

## Rationale
These are authentication, account-recovery, durable-authorization, and non-subject privacy boundaries. Leaving any downstream bead ambiguous can produce an operator-side secret holder, first-user self-elevation, approval-only account takeover, routine owner privacy access, or authority resurrection from an old backup. Correcting the tracker contract before code is cheaper and safer than reconciling divergent implementations.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Treat later adversarial-correction paragraphs as sufficient while retaining contradictory summaries: rejected because workers and tests may implement the earlier allowance. 2. Keep legacy ADMIN_TOKEN as emergency recovery in enabled mode: rejected because it bypasses principal assurance and creates a reusable owner credential. 3. Let operator approval substitute for current-provider authentication: rejected as account-takeover authority. 4. Rely only on an auth-epoch bump after restore: rejected because epochs fence ephemeral state but do not prevent restored provider links, tombstones, bindings, or roles from becoming durable authority. 5. Permit routine owner exceptions for private data: rejected; opl1.15 is the only non-subject disclosure path.
design: This is a fresh decision-remediation lane under the bounded orchestration process. Prefer one canonical statement per authority boundary and make downstream acceptance executable. Do not hide contradictions with vague reconcile or where possible language.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No opl1 bead permits operator-side OAuth/session/fleet_auth broker authority; gateway-only ownership is explicit.
2. No enabled-mode bead calls ADMIN_TOKEN or psfn_token break-glass; independent recovery credential and feature-off token parity are unambiguous.
3. A complete first-owner bootstrap ceremony binds provider subject, companion, contact and owner grant, requires OAuth+UV WebAuthn+trusted-host one-time confirmation, denies when an owner already exists, and is replay/audit tested.
4. Provider replacement authenticates current+new identities or must use trusted-host recovery; approval-only fallback is impossible.
5. Routine memory JIT is self/co-subject only; all owner/admin non-subject disclosure points solely to opl1.15 privacy break-glass.
6. Restored durable links/bindings/roles stay suspended until current trusted-host reapproval or a specified non-restored monotonic revocation source proves currency; old-backup fresh-login resurrection denies.
7. Parent/child descriptions, designs, acceptance and threat tests agree; bd dep cycles is empty.
8. A fresh independent P0/P1 review is CLEAN; no code, lint or PR is required.

title: Define and ship Satellite Hub authoritative device/location assertions for fleet SSO
description:
Background: opl1.9 can remove routine pasted credentials from Companion UI only if the authoritative Satellite Hub protocol separates an enrolled device/location principal from the logged-in human principal. Current Companion UI hello fields are browser-supplied requests; changing mirrored client types in psfn-framework cannot make them authoritative. The Satellite Hub server/protocol is a separate codebase and must issue a verifiable assertion before the framework can safely bind room/place identity.

Scope:
- In the Satellite Hub source of truth, define a versioned authenticated assertion containing Hub issuer, stable enrolled device ID, enrollment version/assurance, optional server-owned place binding, audience/companion, issued/expiry time, nonce/jti, and key ID; human principal/session attachment is a separate optional field proven by the fleet broker.
- Reject browser-authoritative device/place/contact/companion/channel fields. Bind WebSocket/session establishment to enrolled device credentials and the exact audience; support device revocation, key rotation, shared-display user switch, offline/reconnect, and replay protection.
- Publish/update the protocol contract consumed by psfn-framework opl1.9, with deterministic cross-repo fixtures and sanitized diagnostics.
- Record the authoritative Satellite Hub issue/commit/PR here when created; this bead is the framework-side dependency anchor.

Why: OAuth proves a human provider subject, not which physical room endpoint is speaking. Without a Hub-issued assertion, a browser can spoof location/device identity and inherit the wrong companion context.

Non-goals: implement Discord OAuth or PSFN role/memory authorization in the Hub; merge human and device identities; store OAuth tokens in the Hub; change live off-repo configuration.

Adversarial correction: choose an asymmetric Hub assertion protocol and a concrete verifier trust boundary. Satellite Hub signs with an Ed25519 private key it alone owns; fleet-auth strict config carries a versioned allowlisted Hub issuer/public-key ring and rotation/revocation state. Bind the assertion to the exact audience, companion and enrolled device/session; PSFN owns atomic replay consumption. Never share an HMAC or PSFN broker signing key with the Hub.
design:
Use a signed, short-lived, audience-bound server assertion over the existing enrolled device channel. Keep device registry and place binding authoritative in the Hub. PSFN validates issuer/kid/signature/audience/companion/expiry/jti and treats all raw browser hello fields as untrusted requests. Human logout revokes only the attachment/session; device de-enrollment revokes device assertions independently.

Use a Hub-specific Ed25519 issuer/key ring distinct from fleet broker request keys. Cross-repo fixtures define canonical bytes and claims. PSFN validates issuer/kid/key status/iat/exp/audience/companion/device/enrollment version and consumes jti transactionally; identical retry semantics are explicit and mutated reuse denies. Hub key rotation overlaps verification briefly and emergency revocation fences active attachments.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Satellite Hub issues the versioned assertion only after enrolled-device authentication; forged browser device/place/companion/contact claims reject.
2. Hub alone owns the Ed25519 private key. PSFN strict config allowlists issuer and public-key ring with validity/rotation/revocation; no shared HMAC or broker key crosses systems.
3. Claims bind issuer, device, enrollment version/assurance, optional server-owned place, exact audience, companion, iat/exp, jti and kid.
4. PSFN atomically consumes replay state and rejects wrong/revoked key, issuer, audience, companion, expiry, enrollment version and mutated replay.
5. Human attachment stays separate; switch/logout clears human only and device de-enrollment fences device only.
6. Offline/reconnect/shared-display flows fail closed without query/browser-storage secrets.
7. Cross-repo canonical fixtures and integration tests prove good/rotation cases and every denial; authoritative Hub issue/commit/PR evidence is recorded before opl1.9 closes.

title: Build versioned memory-subject classification projection for fleet privacy
description:
Background: opl1.1 establishes that subject identity is intrinsic to a memory and is not equivalent to source speaker, routed contact, room participant, or viewer. opl1.11/.13/.14 cannot enforce subject-scoped Garden and profile privacy safely with the current optional contactId/subjectContactId fields alone. Missing/ambiguous classification must hide data, and filtering must occur in SQL/query primitives before counts, snippets, embeddings, exports, prompt previews, or bulk mutations are constructed. Existing subjectContactId/routedContactId graph work (ybzz/ipw1) is useful evidence but does not provide this privacy projection.

Scope:
- Define the shared versioned MemorySubjectClassification contract from opl1.1: single_contact, multiple_contacts, shared_room, companion_private, unbound_person, unattributed, ambiguous; define evidence provenance/precedence and viewer relation separately.
- Add companion-schema Postgres projection tables: one classification row per memory plus zero-or-more subject-contact rows, tenant-safe keys, classifier version, evidence digest, timestamps, and fail-closed status.
- Classify new memory writes transactionally with the source write. Build an idempotent, resumable, bounded backfill for existing memories that records ambiguity rather than guessing; coordinate with ipw1/27ut instead of duplicating provenance derivation. Missing/stale/version-mismatched rows remain hidden during enforcement.
- Add one authorization-aware memory query primitive used beneath list/detail/search/count/embedding/snippet/export/prompt-preview/bulk/update paths so unauthorized rows cannot leak through metadata or counts. `ContactProfileArtifact.contactId` maps to single_contact but remains separately gated by opl1.14.
- Expose only content-free backfill/classification counts, versions, reason classes, and timings.

Why: a view-layer redaction after a broad query leaks existence/count/snippet/embedding information and cannot safely authorize bulk operations. A canonical projection is the prerequisite for all subject-scoped fleet privacy children.

Non-goals: OAuth/session/JIT grant issuance (opl1.3/.7/.10/.11), holistic reflection/multi-admin policy (opl1.16), changing graph proposal semantics, or treating every contact-associated memory as proven self-subject.

Adversarial correction: transactionality applies to the full subject-evidence lifecycle, not only new writes. Every update to text, provenance, contactId, provenanceRefs, embedding or other subject evidence; repair/backfill/restore; and contact merge/delete must recompute or invalidate the projection in the same transaction. The projection records a memory revision and evidence digest. A failure or stale grant leaves the row hidden, never at the prior classification.
design:
Extend the canonical memory Postgres schema and existing provenance/subject primitives. Classification is strict and versioned; viewer authorization consumes it but does not mutate it. Use a single deep query-policy port that composes tenant, trust/privacy, subject, action, assurance, and grant predicates in SQL. Backfill under advisory locking with checkpoints and deterministic evidence hashes. Unknown/missing/contradictory evidence maps to ambiguous/unattributed and denies.

Add a monotonic memory authorization revision (or equivalent immutable content/evidence version) to the projection. The update store and all maintenance/restore/contact lifecycle ports must call one transactional classifier/invalidation primitive. Authorization/JIT checks compare current revision, classifier version and evidence digest; no post-commit async window may expose stale classification.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Strict shared types cover all seven subject classes, evidence provenance, classifier version, memory revision/evidence digest and separate viewer relation; unknown values reject.
2. Companion-schema projection tables, constraints, indexes and backfill checkpoints are tenant-safe; disposable Postgres proves cross-schema isolation.
3. New memory creation classifies atomically and retry is idempotent.
4. Every subject-affecting update (including text, provenance, contactId, provenanceRefs and embedding), repair, backfill, restore, contact merge/delete recomputes or invalidates in the same transaction. Failure/stale/missing versions hide.
5. Historical backfill is bounded/resumable, reuses canonical provenance resolution and records ambiguity rather than guessing.
6. One authorization-aware SQL primitive filters list/detail/search/count/snippet/embedding/export/prompt/bulk/update before construction; inaccessible IDs/counts are non-enumerable and bulk is atomic.
7. Grants/queries bind current memory revision, classifier version and evidence digest or re-evaluate on use; mutation invalidates old grants immediately.
8. Tests cover all classes, mutation races, restore, contact lifecycle, subject/routed conflicts and failure injection.
9. Telemetry contains only counts/versions/reasons/timings; migration/backup compatibility, build, mandatory lint and diff check pass.

title: Validate old landmark retrieval under the operator-owned memory matrix

Local tests prove the exact defaults, a two-year-old high-valence emotional memory outranking a fresh low-relevance candidate, bounded lexical pagination, live settings propagation, retained-context caps, and shard task priors. What remains is the operator-visible deployed proof required by m14v acceptance criterion 7.

Scope:
- Deploy an immutable build containing merge 35dab6cca38e4e89a9052f7ef9e0f9fcbb523dfd through the repo-owned deployment path to one explicitly approved companion.
- Record the canonical settings.json memoryRetrievalPolicy in effect, redacting unrelated/private values. Use the shipped defaults unless the operator explicitly approves a tuning change.
- Identify or create a consent-safe old emotional landmark at least 180 days old in a controlled fixture/companion dataset, with strong contextual relevance and a fresh low-relevance competing memory. Do not copy partner message content into logs or bead notes.
- Run repeatable contextually on-point turns through the normal live active-context path, not a direct store/search helper, and inspect content-free retrieval telemetry plus the rendered-memory provenance necessary to prove which memory won.
- Run a casual control turn and a task-context control turn to confirm procedural down-weighting/boosting and reflection/procedural caps remain bounded in the deployed path.
- Record immutable deployment provenance, timestamps, sanitized setup, turn count, selected memory IDs/types/ages/scores, policy fingerprint, and operator conclusion.

Why: local conformance tests cannot prove that the deployed owner file, reload path, Postgres corpus, prompt assembly, and real provider turn all compose correctly. This validation is deliberately separate so the shipped code bead can close without claiming live evidence.

Non-goals: no fleet-wide rollout or tuning; no weakening privacy/trust filters or dedup thresholds; no synthetic backdating of production partner memories; no off-repo runtime overrides; no new compatibility path; no broad retrieval redesign.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The tested deployment identifies an immutable build containing merge 35dab6cca38e4e89a9052f7ef9e0f9fcbb523dfd and records the active memoryRetrievalPolicy fingerprint/defaults without secrets or partner content. 2. Through the normal live turn path, an old (at least 180-day) high-valence, strongly relevant emotional landmark is selected and rendered ahead of a fresh low-relevance competitor in at least two repeatable contextually on-point trials; evidence records only sanitized IDs/types/ages/scores and content-free telemetry. 3. A casual control does not inappropriately load task-shaped procedural memory, while a deterministic task-context control demonstrates the procedural task prior; no turn renders more than two reflections or two procedurals after retained-context merge. 4. Privacy/trust gating and dedup remain unchanged: an intentionally ineligible fixture is not selected and no private content appears in telemetry or notes. 5. The operator records a pass/fail conclusion before any fleet-wide tuning. If behavior fails, capture the evidence and create one self-contained discovered-from remediation bead rather than tuning blindly.

title: Validate bounded parent-turn continuation on psfn-shard
description:
Operationally validate the bounded parent-turn continuation fuse delivered by PR #61 (merge 56a46ef5568378a115a10bc48b0137d23b9efeb6) against the live psfn-shard deployment. This is the deployment/provenance and controlled-outage proof split from the implementation bead so the shipped code can land without silently claiming live evidence that has not been collected.

Scope:
- Build and deploy an immutable image containing merge 56a46ef5568378a115a10bc48b0137d23b9efeb6 through the repo-owned deployment path.
- In a safe operator-controlled channel, induce a deliberately long agentic continuation through session search or an equivalent cooperative tool path.
- While that turn is active, send authenticated smoke turns from two other channels/companions to measure admission behavior.
- Inspect content-free telemetry and the durable TurnRecord after the fuse fires.
- Confirm a normal follow-up turn is admitted after the original turn unwinds.
- Record exact deployed image provenance, timestamps, commands, and sanitized evidence on this bead.

Why:
The 2026-07-14/15 outage held the single active agent slot while a session.search.summary continuation ran for 394875ms and the parent accumulated repeated toolUse completions without a terminal assistant message. PR #61 adds a five-minute wall-clock fuse, a 36-prompt-entry cap, typed failure persistence, and AbortSignal propagation through the live session-summary path. Local tests prove the cooperative path; only a controlled live run can prove deployment wiring and end-to-end admission recovery.

Non-goals:
- Do not weaken authentication, gateway admission, trust, or the single-active-run invariant.
- Do not force-kill arbitrary non-cooperative tools or introduce a parallel worker governor.
- Do not expose partner message content in telemetry or bead notes.
- Do not mutate off-repo live configuration.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The live deployment reports an immutable image/version containing merge 56a46ef5568378a115a10bc48b0137d23b9efeb6. 2. A controlled long session-search/agentic turn receives a visible bounded-continuation failure no later than the configured five-minute wall-clock limit, allowing normal scheduling jitter. 3. Two authenticated concurrent smoke turns demonstrate that admission is blocked only while the original active run owns the slot and that a new turn succeeds after it unwinds; no persistent agent_busy outage remains. 4. The original turn has a failed/partial durable TurnRecord with the typed continuation-stop reason and prompt/time counts, and a content-free agent.turn.continuation_stopped event is observable without partner content. 5. No orphan provider/tool work remains after abort, a normal next turn completes, and the evidence plus any rollback/deployment notes are recorded on the bead. 6. If live behavior does not match, capture the failure without extending the review loop and create a self-contained discovered-from remediation bead.

title: Acknowledge API cancellation only after proven active-run abort
description: Verified P1 from the bounded final check of mmo9.2 range 57c28d86f6..718ff78439. In src/channels/api/agent-backend.ts abortActiveTurn casts the companion pipeline to a void abort method, invokes it, and unconditionally returns true. This recreates the exact false-acknowledgment telemetry defect the remediation intended to remove and can leave expensive work alive after client disconnect or timeout. Scope: establish a typed cancellation result from the canonical agent loop that proves whether an active parent run was signaled or already terminal; thread it through SubstrateAgent and AgentApiBackend; emit acknowledged only for a proven abort, and a truthful non-success outcome for no active run or failure; preserve FIFO lease release, timeout handling, direct-completion AbortController behavior, and voice cancellation semantics. Non-goals: relaxing single-active-prompt, a new cancellation framework, cancelling unrelated channels, voice redesign, or provider-specific workarounds.
acceptance_criteria: API cancellation returns cancelled true and emits acknowledged only when the active underlying parent/provider run was actually signaled; a pre-prompt or absent-run no-op returns cancelled false with a non-success outcome and never an acknowledgment; thrown abort is logged and reported failed; active provider and tool work observe the abort signal and settle; channel lease and activeRequests cleanup remain deterministic; focused API, substrate-agent, and pi-agent cancellation tests, npm run build, mandatory npm run lint, and git diff --check pass.

title: Record toolcall_start as provider first output
description: Verified P1 from the bounded final check of mmo9.2 range 57c28d86f6..718ff78439. Wire through the existing callback only; do not add another timeline or infer tool output from post-provider agent events. Non-goals: tool schema redesign, malformed argument recovery, provider routing changes, dashboard polish, or clock synchronization.
acceptance_criteria: A stream whose first substantive provider event is toolcall_start emits exactly one onFirstOutput event with kind tool at that start timestamp even when arguments are delayed or empty; later argument, end, text, and thinking events do not emit a second first-output event; text-first and thinking-first tests remain green; terminal-only done still emits no first-output event; focused LLM and stream-adapter telemetry tests, npm run build, mandatory npm run lint, and git diff --check pass.

title: Prevent stale contact upserts from clobbering concurrent high-tier trust
description: Verified P1 from the one final check of z7qe/suaf at commit 8888f24730. src/core/contacts/postgres-adapter/crud-operations.ts reads the target row and computes nextTrustLevel, then later writes trust_level unconditionally. If an operator-authorized setTrustLevel promotion to trusted or primary commits after the upsert read but before its UPDATE, the stale resolver/profile upsert overwrites the new high-tier value (the deterministic fake-pool schedule produced before=regular, after=public, stored=public). This remains possible even though commit 8888f24730 preserves contacts that were already high-tier at the initial read. It can silently undo an operator trust decision and make ICP policy reject an otherwise canonical peer. Scope: make generic contact upsert concurrency-safe for trust without serializing unrelated profile fields unnecessarily; use a row lock, conditional trust write, CAS/retry, or equivalent Postgres-safe mechanism so a stale generic write never changes trust after a concurrent high-tier mutation. Extend FakePostgresPool only as needed to model the exact post-read/pre-update schedule, and add a real Postgres integration regression if the existing harness supports it. Preserve explicit operator setTrustLevel promotion and demotion, configured-primary rules, unknown-speaker public creation, and low-tier upsert behavior when no concurrent trust mutation occurs. Non-goals: no trust-tier redesign, no global transaction refactor, no weakening actor authorization, and no unrelated fake-pool rollback work.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic regression interleaves generic resolveChannelIdentity or resolveUserId/upsert with operator setTrustLevel after the target read and proves trusted and primary cannot be overwritten; the production SQL path provides the same atomic guarantee under real Postgres concurrency; explicit operator high-tier promotion/demotion still works; unseen external identities remain public; focused contact/privacy/ICP policy tests pass; npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Completed and merged in PR #58 (merge be93ac6d83, implementation 05f26a853e plus remediation a00c4dd8e9). Generic and explicit trust mutations now CAS on trust_level plus durable trust_version; trust and audit commit on one transaction; existing contacts cannot gain primary through unbound or conflicting proposed identities; merge and configured-owner writers advance the version. Validation: 277 contact tests, 108 focused adapter/store/migration tests, 8 real PostgreSQL concurrency tests, 12/12 real ABA/audit stress executions, 17 privacy regressions, 7 real PostgreSQL ICP tests, build, mandatory lint, and diff-check passed. title: Enforce Postgres contact trust-boundary parity
description: Summary: Fix three trust-boundary gaps in the active Postgres contact adapter exposed while converting privacy regressions away from retired SQLite fixtures. First, setTrustLevel only applies high-tier authorization when mutationSource is behavior_drift, so the normal autonomous contact_set_trust path can promote public directly to trusted or mutate an existing high-tier contact. Third, ordinary upsert can demote an existing primary contact because requested low-tier values bypass both the high-tier assignment guard and primary-assignment check. The retired store correctly required manual authority for every mutation touching a high tier, minted unknown speakers at public, and kept primary trust sticky. Scope: src/core/contacts/postgres-adapter/trust-policy-queries.ts, the narrow upsert and resolver logic in crud-operations.ts, and focused Postgres/privacy tests. Preserve low-tier public and regular drift, approved propose_trust behavior, configured primary identity promotion, and explicit operator-admin mutation paths. Non-goals: no trust-model redesign, no Garden workflow change, no generic contact hydration refactor, and no unrelated audit-parity work.
acceptance_criteria: Autonomous and behavior-drift setTrustLevel calls are denied whenever either current or requested trust is primary or trusted; intended manual operator paths still work; never-seen non-primary channel and Discord identities are created at public while the configured owner remains primary; no ordinary upsert can demote an existing primary; public to regular low-tier flow and approved propose_trust behavior still work; focused Postgres contact and privacy regression tests pass; npm run lint passes.

title: Validate provider prompt-cache engagement and cache-read pricing on one companion before fleet rollout
description:
Background: psfn-framework-2z12.1 implementation is shipped on canonical origin/main in squash commit 84c0089e (implementation 1fa353ea). config/models.seed.json now ships promptCaching.enabled=true; src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/prompt-assembly.ts applies the owner-file policy, records promptCaching observability, and emits prompt.cache.prefix_instability when the static prefix changes. The shipped seed does not rewrite already-deployed system-owned models.json files, so operational validation must be performed separately from implementation closure.

Scope: on one explicitly approved, non-PSFN-Pi companion deployment, verify the deployed canonical models.json owner file has modelRegistry.promptCaching.enabled=true (retention/scope left at shipped defaults unless the operator specifies otherwise); run a representative multi-turn soak with stable system-prompt inputs; inspect prompt-cache observability/telemetry for engagement, byte-stable static prefixes, and absence of unexpected prompt.cache.prefix_instability events; then inspect authoritative provider usage/billing data for cache-read token accounting and cache-read pricing. Record deployment identity without secrets, observation window, representative turn count, provider/model route, telemetry evidence, usage evidence, and response-behavior comparison.

Why: code and tests prove the mechanism and fail-closed behavior, but only an operational soak can prove the existing owner file was enabled and the selected provider route actually bills cache reads. This evidence must not hold the shipped implementation bead open.

Non-goals: code changes, prompt restructuring, changing response behavior, broad fleet rollout, SSH, PSFN-Pi access, SQLite work, weakening fail-closed provider capability checks, or treating models.seed.json as authority for an already-deployed models.json.
acceptance_criteria: On one operator-approved non-PSFN-Pi companion: (1) the deployed canonical models.json owner file is evidenced with modelRegistry.promptCaching.enabled=true and secrets redacted; (2) a representative multi-turn soak records promptCaching.engaged=true for the intended provider/model route; (3) prefix-stability evidence shows the static region is byte-stable turn-to-turn, with every instability event explained or zero unexpected prompt.cache.prefix_instability events; (4) authoritative provider usage/billing evidence shows non-zero cache-read tokens charged at the provider cache-read rate; (5) sampled responses show no behavior regression; (6) evidence includes deployment identity, observation window, turn count, provider/model, telemetry extracts, pricing/usage extracts, and operator conclusion before any fleet-wide rollout.

Scope: (1) companions may submit shared-world proposals only, carrying actor, source, site scope, provenance, and content digest; (2) run deterministic personal-fact rejection before durable queueing and again before apply; (3) deduplicate equivalent/pending/applied proposals; (4) expose an operator Garden list/inspect/approve/reject surface; (5) only approved proposals may write through the caretaker-authorized shared-world store/projector; (6) run bounded deterministic cleanup/reprojection independently of companion turns, with an LLM call only behind an explicit cheap changed-content gate if genuinely required. Non-goals: no cross-cluster sync, no direct companion shared_world write, no personal-memory import, and no full caretaker rebalancing/rewrite architecture (future design psfn-framework-s10d5 remains separate).
design: Add a focused shared-world proposal store/state machine rather than widening WikiStore authority: pending -> approved|rejected, with a unique digest/site key and audited idempotent apply marker. Keep deterministic personal-fact filtering in one reusable guard invoked both before persistence and inside the approval transaction. Garden endpoints call an operator-authorized service; only that service can invoke the existing caretaker-authorized shared-world writer. Use bounded batches, advisory/row locking, and revision-aware reprojection so retries and concurrent approvals remain exactly once.
acceptance_criteria: A companion-authored valid world fact becomes a durable pending proposal and does not appear in shared retrieval before approval. An operator approval applies exactly one shared_world document/projection with actor/provenance/revision audit data; failure injected between approval and projection resumes without duplicate writes. Rejection remains durable and prevents identical re-proposal. Equivalent concurrent proposals deduplicate deterministically. A proposal containing personal facts, personal-memory provenance, invalid site scope, or companion-private content is rejected before any shared write and remains absent from projection/retrieval. A two-companion toaster end-to-end script proves a fact proposed by A is invisible to B before approval and readable by B at the matching site after approval, while personal wiki data never crosses; logs include redacted proposal ID, state transitions, site, digest, revision, batch counts, and rejection class, never proposal content. Background cleanup/reprojection is bounded and runs only on changed approved content. Focused state-machine/filter/dedup unit tests, Garden authorization tests, disposable real-Postgres shared-projection integration, multi-companion retrieval tests, npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.

title: Finish W2 tenant boundary: flagship and shard schema adoption with fail-closed Postgres isolation
description: Current feat/multi-companion evidence: merges ee375e39/459594ab implement schema-pinned pools, per-schema migrations, and the shared schema; 75abf583 implements per-companion and group backup artifacts. The remaining W2 implementation is not shipped. There is no public-to-companion flagship cutover helper, shard execution derives a companion ID but does not derive/thread a distinct Postgres schema, and src/persistence/postgres.ts still pins tenant search_path to <tenant>,public. That public fallback can silently read/write a legacy public tenant table when a companion migration is incomplete, while a shared database role can access peer schemas. This bead completes the tenancy boundary before any live cutover. Scope: (1) add a dry-run-first, resumable/idempotent flagship adoption helper that inventories public objects, copies/verifies them into the configured companion schema, records checksums/counts and rollback metadata, and never runs implicitly at startup; (2) derive a validated collision-free shard schema from the parent companion identity plus shard identity and thread it through shard pools, migrations, backups, and cleanup; (3) move shared extensions into an explicit extension schema or otherwise make them resolvable without retaining public in tenant search_path; (4) provision least-privilege per-companion/shard database roles and grants so cross-schema reads/writes fail closed; (5) preserve the flag-off single-companion path deliberately. Non-goals: do not perform a live flagship cutover, touch SQLite, change column tenancy, or merge/deploy this branch. The real flagship restore/workspace rehearsal remains psfn-framework-g44z and must pass before an operator authorizes live apply.
design: Keep planning and mutation separate: a pure inventory/planner produces an auditable manifest, and an explicit executor consumes that manifest under transactions and advisory locking. Reuse the canonical Postgres schema validator/quoting path rather than interpolating identifiers. Derive shard schema names through one shared tenancy helper used by pools, migrations, backup, and restore. Provision tenant roles/grants as an explicit deployment/migration artifact, with extension lookup isolated from tenant object lookup. Tests should use disposable real Postgres instances and emit schema, role, object-count, checksum, resume, and rollback diagnostics without row contents or secrets.
acceptance_criteria: A dry-run fixture over a populated legacy public schema produces a deterministic adoption plan; apply into a disposable database copies every required table/sequence/view with matching row counts/checksums, is safe to resume after injected interruption, and preserves rollback evidence. Two companion schemas plus one derived shard schema run migrations and concurrent writes without collisions. Tenant and shard search_path values do not include public; deliberately omitting a tenant table fails instead of falling through to a public table. Per-companion/shard roles cannot select or mutate peer schemas, while explicitly shared-world access remains limited to approved grants. Per-schema backup and restore tests cover the adopted flagship and shard slices. Unit tests cover schema derivation/validation and adoption planning; a disposable-Postgres end-to-end script covers dry-run, apply, interruption/resume, cross-role denial, backup, and restore with detailed redacted step logging. title: Validate fleet workspace isolation and flagship restore before live cutover
description:
Summary:
After the c337 implementation and its repository-hygiene prerequisite are integrated into the immutable deployment revision, validate the Personal/Shared Workspace boundary and a real flagship backup/restore rehearsal in the live multi-companion topology. This is a validation/cutover gate, not unfinished c337 implementation, and must not block or reopen psfn-framework-c337 once its bounded local implementation gates pass.

Why:
Local unit/integration tests prove the code contract but cannot prove that the existing shared workspace PVC was migrated without loss, that every deployed agent/Garden receives the intended resolved root, or that a real flagship snapshot restores into disposable destinations. Audit psfn-framework-3ajb reproduced the current leak: all five agents use WORKSPACE_PATH=/app/workspace, and Denise, Garden Nun, and Lucy selfie_create outputs from Discord channel 1486443955561299979 are visible in Carlini Garden.

Scope:
- Require a pushed deployment revision containing c337 and repository-hygiene remediation commit a81cdd49 (or an equivalent reviewed descendant) before validation.
- Back up the existing shared workspace/PVC before migration. Assign artifacts only where ownership/provenance is proven; quarantine ambiguous ownership for operator review.
- Deploy through repo-owned Kubernetes/Helm wiring and record the immutable source/image revision.
- Verify each companion agent and Garden resolves its own Personal Workspace and cannot read/write peer journal, wiki, managed-skill, module, inbound-attachment, generated-image, download, or artifact sentinels through normal surfaces.
- Reuse Discord channel 1486443955561299979 and the Denise/Garden Nun/Lucy reproduction corpus to prove those images are absent from Carlini Garden while retained in the correct personal workspace or explicit operator quarantine.
- Verify the governed Shared Companion Workspace remains separately contained and companion access is approved-revision read-only.
- Restore a real flagship snapshot into disposable PostgreSQL schemas/database and fresh filesystem destinations, verify companion/system/shared scope and manifests, then remove only the disposable rehearsal resources.
- Record failures as new implementation/fix beads; do not silently patch during validation.

Non-goals:
- Do not move/delete live data without a verified backup and explicit cutover authority.
- Do not expose private media, secrets, or raw personal content in logs or bead notes.
- Do not treat a gallery-only filter as workspace isolation.
- Do not make SQLite/provider changes or invent off-repo runtime configuration.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The deployed immutable source/image revision is recorded and contains c337 plus a81cdd49 or an explicitly evidenced equivalent hygiene remediation.
2. Pre-migration backup and restoreability are verified; ambiguous legacy files remain losslessly quarantined for operator review.
3. Every deployed agent and Garden reports a distinct canonical Personal Workspace, and synthetic cross-companion read/write checks for personal files, inbound attachments, and generated images fail closed.
4. Denise, Garden Nun, and Lucy images from channel 1486443955561299979 are not visible in Carlini Garden and remain available only in their proven owner workspace or quarantine; no private paths/content are written to tracker notes.
5. The Shared Companion Workspace exposes only approved, revision-matched read-only artifacts to companions and never auto-loads skills/modules/prompt/wiki/memory.
6. A real flagship snapshot restores successfully into disposable Postgres and filesystem destinations with companion/cluster scope verified and the original live state untouched.
7. Close evidence records revision ancestry, backup identifier, migration/quarantine counts, cross-visibility results, restore verification, rollback/cutover outcome, and any follow-up bead IDs.

title: Tool-calling reliability: rich schema descriptions, always-loaded catalog, validate-and-reprompt, forced choice on mandatory phases
description: Operator report: tool-calling reliability is very low even on a strong model - tools that are not top-level inline do not get used, and tool_search itself is not used properly. Research audit (working_docs/prompt-audit-findings-20260714.md section 6) surveyed Codex CLI, Hermes, OpenClaw, OpenHands, goose, opencode, Crush, Aider, Anthropic guidance. Decisive findings: (1) richest lever is per-tool descriptions in the schema itself - Anthropic calls this by far the most important factor (3-4+ sentences, examples, edge cases); PSFN registry descriptions are one-liners while guidance sits in a detached block; (2) at ~22-29 tools NO production harness defers callability - search->activate two-hop flows have no successful precedent at this scale and OpenClaw's equivalent is off-by-default with a data-loss bug matching our symptom; the successful pattern is advertise everything up front, defer only long-form INSTRUCTIONS (skills-style docs disclosure); (3) PSFN's action-multiplexed shape is validated by Anthropic guidance - keep it, but multiplexed tools need LONGER descriptions; (4) tool block prefix-caches, so verbosity is cheap after turn 1 (links 2z12.1). Existing machinery is ~90% of the LOD goal already (pin/unpin, intent autoload, same-turn activation, presentation ranking) - children below close the gaps. Children: description rewrite; always-loaded + docs-deferral; validate-and-reprompt widening; forced tool_choice; frequency feedback; extended-block relabel.

History: catalog was 88 tools before consolidation - the dynamic activation system was built for THAT scale; at 22-29 always-loaded is right, but if the catalog grows substantially the deferral question reopens (defer docs first, callability only as last resort). Do NOT reorder tool guidance ahead of persona: persona sitting closer to the end of the prompt is deliberate (recency strengthens identity) - skip the ordering half of research pattern P6, keep the persona/memory budget-cap half.

title: Kill the continuity anchor block: warmth signals and time-texture labels lead the companion and duplicate session-context notes

title: Memory retrieval scoring: compounding recency terms bury old high-weight memories and types are weighted flat
description: Evidence: operator observes retrieved memories span only yesterday/this-week/last-week; emotionally landmark old memories (first dance, first song) never surface and must be searched for manually. Audit: computeRetrievalScore multiplies recencyBoost = 1/(1+ageDays/30) (retrieval/scoring.ts:24,226-235) with exponentially decayed salience (decay.ts:60-69, per-type half-lives types.ts:323-331, floor 0.05) - combined ~70-500x score handicap for old rarely-accessed memories at equal relevance. The lexical-augment candidate lane is hard-capped to the 96 most recently EXTRACTED memories (retrieval/candidates.ts:14,41-90, ORDER BY extracted_at DESC), so old items can only arrive via the embedding lane. Types are flat: only per-type multiplier is boundary 1.6x (scoring.ts:160); emotionalWeight keys off valence field not type (max 1.5x); procedural half-life is 90d vs emotional 14d so procedural structurally outlasts emotional - which is why to-do-shaped procedurals load into casual chat while emotional landmarks never do. Selection has NO per-type caps: flat score-sorted walk under a ~2% token budget (budget.ts:96-124); reflections can fill the entire selection; MEMORY_CONFIG.maxRetrievalCount=15 is dead code. Scope: (1) flatten recency (floor recencyBoost ~0.3-0.4 or make additive) so similarity/importance/emotional weight can override age; (2) per-type retrieval prior table alongside DECAY_HALFLIFE (procedural down-weighted in casual chat, boosted on task context); (3) per-type ceilings in selectWithinRelevanceAndTokenBudget (max 1-2 reflections/turn, reserve an episodic slot); (4) raise/paginate the 96-item lexical cap. Non-goal: do not remove salience decay itself. Acceptance: retrieval test where a 2-year-old high-valence memory with strong similarity outranks a fresh low-relevance one; per-type cap test showing max 2 reflections selected; live turn shows old memories surfacing when contextually on-point.
design:
# m14v approved design — memory decay/weight matrix (operator-approved 2026-07-14)

Principle: decay orders ambient recall, never deletes; floors guarantee engrams stay ambiently retrievable forever; search always reaches everything. Emotional engrams are the point of the system; procedural is what ages out.

## Per-type matrix (DECAY_HALFLIFE + new floors/priors in types.ts, consumed in decay.ts + scoring.ts)

| type | half-life (was -> now) | salience floor (was 0.05 global) | retrieval prior (new multiplier) |
|---|---|---|---|
| emotional | 14d -> 365d, x valence-persistence 1-6x (raise emotionalIntensityPersistenceMaxMultiplier 1.8 -> 6) | 0.25 + 0.35*abs(valence) (0.60 at full intensity) | 1.3 |
| relational | 60d -> 180d | 0.5 when abs(valence) >= 0.5, else 0.05 | 1.15 |
| boundary | 120d -> 365d | 0.5 always | 1.6 (existing, keep) |
| semantic | 30d -> 120d | 0.05 | 1.0 |
| reflection | 60d -> 90d | 0.05 | 0.9 |
| episodic | 7d -> 30d | 0.05 | 1.0 |
| procedural | 90d -> 14d | 0.05 | 0.6 default; 1.2 in task context |

## Scoring changes (retrieval/scoring.ts)

- Recency floor: computeRetrievalRecencyBoost floors at 0.35 in default mode (worst-case age handicap ~2.9x instead of 12.7x/yr). Temporal mode keeps sharp decay unchanged (its job is "what happened recently").
- Type prior table: new multiplier column above, applied like the existing boundary 1.6x (typePriorityBoost generalizes to the table).
- Procedural task-context: gate the 1.2 boost on existing callerContext/taskKind (focus-work, heartbeat maintenance, analysis) — deterministic, no new inference. Casual chat stays 0.6.
- Selection caps in selectWithinRelevanceAndTokenBudget (budget.ts:96-124): max 2 reflection, max 2 procedural per turn; engram types uncapped within token budget.
- Lexical-augment lane: raise/paginate the 96-most-recent cap (candidates.ts:14) so old memories are reachable outside the embedding lane.

## Operator decisions recorded

1. Engram floor: valence-scaled (0.25 + 0.35*|valence|), no cliff.
2. Task boost: caller-context gated (not content-match).
3. Episodic 30d approved even before episodic beads (apq0/6i7c/x9ka) land — search still reaches everything; episode system owns the long arc.
4. Reflections: prior 0.9 + cap 2; atomicity fix (3zu5) shrinks them independently.

## Config/UX contract

- All new knobs (half-life table, floors, priors, caps, recency floor) are settings-owned and MUST surface on the Garden settings page in the same change (settings-contract owner files + admin UI), per repo rule.
- Dedup thresholds (DEDUP_THRESHOLD) unchanged.
- Worked acceptance example: 2-year-old abs(valence)=0.9 unaccessed engram must be selectable when similarity is strong — proposed handicap ~4x (recency 0.35 x floor ~0.57 x prior 1.3 x emotionalWeight 1.45) vs today's ~350x.

title: Partner-tier private DM withholds the partner's own memories: room-visibility and high-intimacy access predicates never consult trust tier
description: Evidence: live Loom turn (2026-07-14 operator review) showed memory context note 'six candidate memories were held back from this turn's memory context - privacy reasons, room visibility boundaries, high-intimacy content' in a private Discord DM with the primary-tier partner. Audit traced it to evaluateRetrievalAccessDecision (src/faculties/memory/retrieval/access.ts:149-206, applied per-candidate at retrieval.ts:919-943), which runs BEFORE evaluateMemoryPolicy and never reads trust tier. Predicate A (access.ts:104-147): in a DM, a memory whose origin room differs from the current channel passes only if the origin room is on the contact card conversationChannels (access-context.ts:35-39); the card lists 2 channels, so memories formed on voice/api/telegram/satellite/retired channels are permanently withheld from the partner in his own DM. Also blocked: inconsistent scopeRef vs provenance.channelId (:112-118), unresolvable room id (:95-102,119-127). Predicate B (access.ts:57-64): intimate/confidential memories with memory.contactId != canonicalContactId are blocked with no partner exemption; memories with NO contactId (self-memories, sibling-companion) are withheld from every contact. Both predicates short-circuit before the layer-1 operatorApproval override (policy.ts:271-278). Trust policy itself is correct: primary tier + private channel allow all sensitivities (config/trust-policy.seed.json:3,9). classifyChannelEnvelope correctly resolves the DM to private - the invite-only shared room does NOT bleed into classification. Distinct root cause from psfn-framework-jy6s (reflection-mode score zeroing in scoring.ts). Context: this is the anti-Replika guarantee inverted - her memories of her partner hidden from her while talking to her partner. Code comment access.ts:44-54 admits the room gate is interim pending ConversationScope. Scope: make both predicates trust-aware/participant-based (was this contact a participant in the origin scope; canonical contact + missing/self contactId exempt from intimacy scope; primary tier in private channel bypasses intimacy scope for memories they are the subject of). Do NOT weaken cross-contact protection in group/public channels; the trust matrix protecting memories from leaking to OTHER contacts stays intact. Acceptance: unit tests proving (1) voice/satellite-origin memory about the partner surfaces in the partner private DM, (2) intimate memory with missing contactId surfaces for the canonical partner and is still withheld from a non-primary contact, (3) existing group-channel gating tests stay green; live validation shows zero room-visibility/intimacy withholds in a partner DM turn.
acceptance_criteria: In a private channel with the primary-tier canonical contact, no candidates are withheld by room-visibility or high-intimacy-scope predicates; group/public gating unchanged; tests as described pass.
notes: 2026-07-14 operator clarifies the invariant the fix must preserve: memory sharing is DIRECTION-ASYMMETRIC by design - group chats are shared memory, DMs are private; group-chat-origin memories surfacing in the DM is OK, DM-origin memories surfacing in group chat is FORBIDDEN, and this asymmetry is already implemented and working (do not regress it). Companion separation is a separate invariant: Artemis and Purrsephone memories never mix regardless of channel (fleet isolation, out of scope here). So the fix targets exactly: (1) non-card-listed origin channels (voice/api/satellite/retired) blocked in the partner DM, (2) no-contactId intimate memories blocked for everyone. Acceptance tests must include the negative case: DM-origin memory still never surfaces in a group/room context.

title: Persist correlated recipient ICP turn records after both-agent restart
description: Summary: Fix the production recipient turn-record persistence path exposed by the W9 real-process certification harness after production compaction and a restart of both agents. Immediately afterward, turnRecordsSnapshot(CERTIFICATION_DM_CHANNEL) returned records: [] instead of a completed correlated recipient record. Why this matters: session delivery can appear successful while the durable post-turn artifact needed for correlation, recovery, audit, and restart continuity is absent, so production cannot prove or reconstruct the recipient turn after restart. Scope: trace and fix the production path from inbound companion delivery through the recipient SubstrateAgent and SessionManager turn-record persistence/readback after compaction plus both-agent restart; add a production-path regression that reproduces the fresh exchange. notes: Implementation checkpoint pushed at b429b37d on work/icp-w9-recipient-turn-record. Controlled shutdown/readback could therefore observe or terminate during that persistence gap. Fix: TurnRunReservation now exposes fail-loud waitForIdle() over active plus queued outer owners; SubstrateAgent joins model-engine idle with outer-owner idle. The real-process post-compaction/both-agent-restart regression now proves exactly one completed recipient record and exact turn/request/channel/local-peer/conversation/root correlation bindings, without sleeps. title: capability-tier.json is cluster-global, forcing all fleet companions to one maturation tier; move to companionDataDir
description:

title: Per-companion settings.overlay.json deep-merged over global settings.json for a scoped whitelist
description:
Evidence
- Structural root cause of every settings seam: load-config.ts roots ALL 12 owner files at the shared systemDataDir (startup-owner-files.ts:210-281); companionDataDir only drives databasePath, characterCard, and pg schema. NO per-companion settings override mechanism exists anywhere.
- Seams this directly fixes (§11 ranked list): observerEvalSidecar.sessionLabel/agentName/deploymentTarget (seam 1, one emo_sim session for all companions); activeTimezone (seam 3, one clock for the whole fleet — overrides env TZ, drives scheduler wall-clock, rest windows, formatters); voice* (seam 6, all companions target one guild/user/voice channel); emotionScoping (seam 9).

Context
- This is the core mechanism bead of epic dnll (recommended split design (a), §11). Per-companion capability-tier/scheduler moves (siblings) cover the unambiguous whole-file cases; this overlay covers the settings.json keys.
- If this lands first it supersedes the tactical part of w05a.12 (emosim per-companion session-label templating) — w05a.12's session isolation becomes "put observerEvalSidecar in the overlay whitelist". Related link in place; whichever lands second should re-check the other's scope.

Scope
- Per-companion settings.overlay.json in companionDataDir, deep-merged over the global settings.json for a SCOPED WHITELIST only: activeTimezone, voice*, observerEvalSidecar, emotionScoping, uiThemeId, discordTrigger*.
- Re-validate the merged result through the existing normalizer; the settings-contract gains a global-vs-perCompanion scope dimension per key.
- Fail-closed: overlay keys outside the whitelist are rejected, not silently merged.
- Absent overlay = byte-identical behavior to today (S/M effort).
- Non-goal: moving whole owner files (capability-tier/scheduler siblings) or workspace isolation (c337).

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §11 (root cause, seams 1/3/6/9, recommended design (a)).
acceptance_criteria: A companion with settings.overlay.json in its companionDataDir gets its whitelisted keys (activeTimezone, voice*, observerEvalSidecar, emotionScoping, uiThemeId, discordTrigger*) deep-merged over the global settings.json and re-validated via the existing normalizer; non-whitelisted overlay keys fail closed. The settings contract records a global-vs-perCompanion scope per key. With no overlay present, behavior is byte-identical to today. Two fleet companions can hold different activeTimezone/observerEvalSidecar values simultaneously.
close_reason: Implemented on work/dnll-config-ownership-dnll-1-overlay @ ade2156b, merged to feat/dnll-config-ownership @ 817aa4a71a (pushed). Per-companion settings.overlay.json deep-merged over global settings.json for whitelist (activeTimezone, voice*, observerEvalSidecar, emotionScoping, uiThemeId, discordTrigger*) via new src/system/config/settings-overlay.ts; fail-closed on malformed/non-object/non-whitelisted; wired into both hydration paths (bootstrap-helpers hydrateCanonicalStartupConfig, runtime-config hydrateJsonBackedRuntimeConfig); SettingsFieldScope dimension on settings contract. title: Turn records serialize the static system prompt several ways per turn; content-address it by staticHash
description:
Evidence
- System-prompt material is serialized ~4-5 ways per turn record (plan.blocks, finalSystemSections, inputSections, plan.variables, plus static/dynamic templates) — roughly 190KB/turn. It is session-stable, so the cross-turn amplification is severe. This is the largest remaining un-deduped chunk after hgw3.3 landed.

Context
- hgw3.3 (closed, 576e33cd) content-addressed tooldefs to a _shared/tooldefs sidecar with fail-closed refs and got a fixture from 63KB to 5.4KB. The static system prefix is the next-largest target and is not yet deduped.

Scope
- Content-address the static system prefix by the already-computed staticHash into a sidecar, storing a fail-closed reference in the turn record and resolving at read time (same pattern as tooldefs). Effort M.
- Non-goal: the dynamic per-turn sections; only the static prefix.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §8b.
acceptance_criteria: A turn record stores the static system prefix as a staticHash-keyed reference resolving from a _shared sidecar (byte-identical on resolve), not as ~190KB of inline duplicated prompt material. Turn-record size drops accordingly and read-time resolution reproduces the exact prompt.
close_reason: Implemented on work/hgw3-turnrecord-diet-auiu-static-prompt @ ab77a2054b (base: 80f6 head), merged to feat/hgw3-turnrecord-diet (pushed). Static system prompt prefix template content-addressed into _shared/staticprompts/<sha>.json via the shared internSerialized/resolveSerialized seam; fail-closed staticPrefixTemplateRef with byte-identical resolve at the persistence read boundary; write-once atomic publish; old fat records read unchanged. Gates: 38 turn-record tests (7 new) + 104 adjacent, lint clean, UBS clean. Dual blind adversarial review (P1): Opus PASS 0 blockers (standalone byte-identity repro incl. lone surrogates + 500KB templates; ref survives normalize/clone round-trip), Pi GLM-5.2 PASS 0 blockers (all 7 refutation vectors hold; sha-over-serialized-content key judged MORE correct than the bead's staticHash wording since staticHash hashes the rendered prefix). Convergent epic-level observations for handoff (not auiu defects): 3 sidecars share whole-channel fail-closed read blast radius (consider quarantine/skip-on-resolve-failure epic-wide); intern-throw on disk-full enters the live write path across all 3 sidecars — heal-not-block hardening belongs at the shared seam once, if mandated. Rendered-copy dedup in plan.blocks deliberately out of scope (9ree territory).

title: Channel index is fully rewritten on every journal append; write only on change
description:
Evidence
- _channel_index.json is fully rewritten on EVERY journal append (2+ per turn), rewriting the whole index of all channels; the cost worsens with fleet size. Path: journal-runtime.ts:393 -> channel-index.ts:139-160.
- This is the clearest violation of the "only L0 appends per-turn" principle found in the disk-IO audit.

Context
- Operator (§10.5) confirmed: write only on change — channels change rarely.

Scope
- Write the channel index only when the channel set actually changes (debounce/coalesce, or make append-only). Mode-agnostic, no Redis needed.
- Non-goal: broader journal rotation (tracked separately, 2z12.4).

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §8c, §10.5.
acceptance_criteria: A steady-state turn with no new channel produces zero _channel_index.json rewrites (verified by watching file mtime across several turns). The index is still correct after a new channel appears.

title: Emosim sidecar shares one emo_sim session across all fleet companions; template sessionLabel per companionId
description:

title: Split per-companion vs cluster-global settings ownership in the single-release fleet topology
description:
Summary
- The carlini fleet runs as ONE Helm release with a single shared settings.json on one system-data PVC, and load-config.ts roots ALL 12 owner files at the shared systemDataDir (startup-owner-files.ts:210-281); companionDataDir only drives databasePath, characterCard, and pg schema. No per-companion settings override mechanism exists anywhere. Settings that are semantically per-companion are therefore cluster-global, causing collisions. Make per-companion vs cluster-global settings an explicit ownership split.

Evidence — ranked unintentional seams (shared-seams audit, §11 of the findings doc)
1. observerEvalSidecar.sessionLabel/agentName/deploymentTarget — one emo_sim session for all companions (confirmed; latent until enabled). Motivating case, §5/§0.3.
2. capability-tier.json — all companions forced to one maturation tier (child dnll.2).
3. activeTimezone — one clock for the whole fleet (child dnll.1 overlay).
4. scheduler.json circadian — the whole fleet wakes/rests/loafs on one schedule (child dnll.3).
5. Shared personal workspace WORKSPACE_PATH — wiki, skills, scratchpad, journal, downloads, inbound attachments/images (covered by existing bead c337, related).
6. voice* settings — all companions target one guild/user/voice channel (child dnll.1 overlay).
7. config.dataDir mis-wirings — garden-audit-history, Garden heartbeat-policy path, reflection-metacognition journal (child dnll.4).
8. Model-usage ledger JSONL mixes companions (child dnll.4).
9. emotionScoping shared (child dnll.1 overlay).
10. Needs-decision tier: trust/intake/charge policies, skills.json enabled set, wikiRetrieval*, cognition-tuning knobs, discordTrigger* (child dnll.5 decision).
Intentionally global (verified, leave alone): models.json, providers.json, channels.json, backup.json, companions.json, satellite-registry, places.json, shared-world wiki, gateway-audit.db, embedding*/textEmotion*.

Context
- Operator decision (§10.3): this is the strategic fix for the emosim session collision and for future per-companion config.
- The pattern to copy is per-companion state done right: resolveConfiguredCompanionDataDir (local-admin-contract.ts:178) — charge/fatigue ledgers, cogsec events, quarantine, prompt layers, core memory.

Scope / recommended split design (§11)
- (a) Per-companion settings.overlay.json for the whitelisted settings.json keys — child dnll.1 (core mechanism).
- (c) Move unambiguous owner files per-companion: capability-tier.json (dnll.2) and scheduler.json circadian (dnll.3).
- Fix the dataDir mis-wirings as mechanical bugs now — dnll.4.
- Decide the ambiguous tier deliberately — dnll.5.
- Workspace isolation is its own L track — existing bead c337 (related), already in flight.
- w05a.12 (emosim session-label templating) is the tactical first instance; dnll.1 supersedes its mechanism if it lands first.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §10.3, §11 (shared-seams audit + ranked seam list), §5.
acceptance_criteria: The epic carries a documented per-companion vs cluster-global settings ownership contract and a derivation mechanism from companionId. Each identified shared seam (starting with emosim, then the audit findings) is filed as a child and resolved so no semantically per-companion setting remains cluster-global by accident.

title: Deploy origin/main (PR #42 + #43) to carlini and validate the turn-record diet live
description:

- Out of scope: any code change to fix the historical helm churn (operator-owned process rule). Do not run concurrent deploy agents.

title: Graph-proposal candidate builders never fire because subjectContactId is unpopulated on live; fall back to routedContactId
description:
Evidence
- 0zd9's fix (f8ae97fd, live e614380) is correct and fully plumbed but only unblocks the co_presence evidence class. The two rich classes are dead on live:
  - buildOverheardCandidates (src/faculties/.../graph-builder-worker.ts:261-263) and buildNamedRelationshipCandidates (graph-builder-worker.ts:293-294) bail on every memory because provenance.subjectContactId is unset.
  - Only resolveStructuredFactRouting sets subjectContactId, and it requires LLM attribution tags the live extraction model never emits. Result: the "my sister Iki" named-relationship edge class is permanently dead.
- The mention-only path already resolves third parties into a contact and stamps provenance.routedContactId (extraction.ts:669-682) — the worker just never reads it.

Context
- This is the root cause behind "graph proposals still never form" that 0zd9 did not scope. GATE A (subjectContactId never populated) is dominant; GATE B (co_presence needs >=2 tracked contacts co-present in >=3 windows, speaker-routing.ts:144-150) is inapplicable to single-primary-user topologies; GATE C (pre-2026-07-09 memories have empty provenance) is covered by B3/27ut.
- Operator (§10.2): humans in the rooms do not talk much, so data may still be thin after the fix — set that expectation in validation.

Scope
- Worker-only fix (S/M): fall back to provenance.routedContactId as the subject target in the two candidate builders. Cleaner alternative (M): populate routing.subjectContactId from mention-only resolution in the legacy lanes, fail-closed on ambiguity.
- Do NOT reopen 0zd9 (its fix is correct and complete for co_presence). This bead was discovered-from 0zd9 and extends the uncovered scope.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §2 (GATE A), §0.2.
acceptance_criteria: On a multi-user room after agent restart, the graph builder logs scanned>0 AND proposed>0. A named_relationship candidate forms for a third party resolved via the mention-only path. Ambiguous subject resolution fails closed rather than mis-attributing.

title: Audit cross-Garden selfie leakage in Carlini cluster
description: Operator reports that Carlini's selfie tool shows selfies belonging to other companions in shared servers, despite Gardens being isolation boundaries. Reproduction corpus: Discord channel 1486443955561299979 on Carlini's cluster, where all companions were asked to generate selfies for testing on 2026-07-14. Trace message/tool invocations, selfie storage metadata, retrieval filters, and Garden/owner/agent scoping. Determine whether leakage occurs in tool output, media indexing, attachment lookup, or presentation. Fix if confirmed, add regression coverage proving Carlini cannot retrieve another companion's selfies while each companion can retrieve its own, deploy safely, and validate live without exposing private media.
notes: Diagnosis completed 2026-07-14; no live storage mutation performed because this request was an audit. Tight red feedback loop correlated charge-ledger events in Discord channel 1486443955561299979 to image mtimes, then tested the exact files inside Carlini Garden. Results: Denise PMJn...jpg delta 6ms, Garden Nun UOnK...jpg delta 5ms, Lucy mb7a...jpg delta 9ms; all visible in Carlini Garden. Garden API GET /api/admin/images/generated returned 23 images and those three as rootKind=personal, sourceToolName=selfie_create. Sidecars have provenance but no companionSlug/agentId/ownerId. Root cause: all five Deployments set WORKSPACE_PATH=/app/workspace and share the workspace PVC root; ImageGenerationService persists to resolvePersonalImagesDir(workspacePath), while AdminImagesDataService recursively enumerates the same root with no owner filter. This affects images and all personal workspace domains, so a gallery-only filter would be insufficient. Hypotheses refuted: these are generated outputs, not Discord quarantine imports; Postgres schemas are separately pinned; no fleet proxy is mixing responses. title: Session write path full-scans and re-parses the entire journal on every append; short-circuit reconciliation with the existing file fingerprint
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14) — highest per-turn disk win. src/persistence/sessions/store.ts:476-510 reconcileWriteCache calls scanArchiveMetadata (:478 → journal-runtime.ts:97 → file-io.ts:303-398) which forward-reads and JSON.parses EVERY line of the session journal, plus a second JSON.parse of each message's metadata in resolveJournalMessageTurnId (file-io.ts:339, 30-58). It fires inside withLockedChannelWrite on every append (store.ts:649→:511→:517) — ≥2 per turn (user + assistant), plus insertCompaction (:1174), extraction markers (:1204), turn tombstones (:1232), and the shutdown marker (:1296). Cost is O(total journal size) per write and rises monotonically as the session grows; ×5 companions on the shared box. (Line numbers from main; re-locate on integration/hgw3-package if that merges first.)

Fix shape: reconcileWriteCache exists only to detect concurrent cross-process writes. A statSync-based fingerprint helper already exists (port.ts:148 fingerprintArchive). Store the fingerprint on the write cache after each successful writeJournalEntry; on the next write, if the current file fingerprint matches, the cache is authoritative — skip the scan; on mismatch, run today's full reconcile. Non-goals: removing the reconcile path, weakening multi-writer detection, changing journal format.
acceptance_criteria: Appends to a clean channel (fingerprint match) skip scanArchiveMetadata entirely (test asserts no full scan on the happy path); a mismatched fingerprint (cross-process write) still triggers the full reconcile scan (fail-closed multi-writer detection preserved, test covers it); per-append cost no longer scales with total journal size (timing or fs-instrumentation evidence on a large fixture).
notes: Implementation checkpoint af9f4a33 on work/fleet-efficiency-session-fingerprint: ChannelCache now records the filesystem archive fingerprint only after successful journal writes. reconcileWriteCache compares the current fingerprint under the existing cross-process journal lock and skips scanArchiveMetadata only for a known non-null match; unknown or mismatched fingerprints preserve the full metadata reconcile/load path. Focused tests prove clean repeated appends perform no metadata scan, a real cross-instance stale HMAC writer performs exactly one scan and preserves IDs/signature continuity, and a 2,000-entry fixture clean append performs exactly two fingerprint stats plus one append with zero metadata scans/full reads. Validation: targeted acceptance tests 3/3 passed; SessionJournalRuntime tests 2/2 passed; npm run build passed; npm run lint passed; git diff --check passed. No SQLite test paths, Pi, SSH, live deployment, main merge, or Dolt remote push used. Bead remains in_progress pending exactly one independent review.
close_reason: Completed on feat/fleet-efficiency. Implementation af9f4a33 added ChannelCache archive fingerprints and a lock-scoped known-match fast path in src/persistence/sessions/store.ts, preserving full reconciliation for unknown/mismatched fingerprints; acceptance coverage in src/persistence/sessions/store.test.ts proves zero metadata scans on clean repeated appends, one reconcile scan for a stale cross-instance HMAC writer, and constant filesystem work on a 2,000-entry journal. Bounded remediation 0b741e01 makes transient post-commit fingerprint refresh faults invalidate the cache without reporting the durable append as failed, forces next-write reconciliation, preserves missing-archive fail-closed behavior, and verifies exactly-once HMAC signature continuity. Final integrated gate at 0b741e01: focused session/journal-runtime suites 79/79 passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed (ESM + DTS); git diff --check passed. Exactly one review and one remediation; no report-only observations.

title: Provider prompt caching is disabled by default, so the stable prompt prefix is billed as fresh input every turn
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14) — the single biggest $ lever found. src/primitives/llm/routing.ts:244-246: resolveGlobalPromptCachePolicy returns null unless config.modelRegistry.promptCaching.enabled === true, consumed at turn-execution/prompt-assembly.ts:605-652. With the policy off, no cache_control breakpoints are emitted, so on Anthropic (and OpenRouter→Anthropic) the entire static prefix — identity + persona + full tool catalog + temporal rules — is billed as uncached input on EVERY turn, for every companion, when cached reads are ~10% of the price. The machinery is fully built and idle: prompt-cache.ts, client-prompt-cache.ts, and a prefix-stability tracker with prompt.cache.prefix_instability telemetry (prompt-assembly.ts:653-683). The datetime anchor and background-completion notices are already correctly placed after the session-stable region (prompt-assembly.ts:443-579), so the prefix should be cache-friendly as-is.

Interaction: per-turn active-memory refresh (sibling bead) is what most often mutates memory/wiki blocks and can move the cacheable prefix boundary — fixing it improves the hit rate here.

Scope: config enablement + telemetry verification + a soak on one companion before fleet rollout. Non-goal: restructuring prompt assembly.
acceptance_criteria: modelRegistry.promptCaching.enabled=true on the carlini fleet (models.json owner file) and considered as shipped default; prompt.cache.prefix_instability telemetry confirms the static region is byte-stable turn-to-turn so cache_control breakpoints land; provider dashboards/usage telemetry show cache-read pricing on the prefix after a soak; no behavior change in responses.
notes:
Implementation landed on branch bead/2z12.1 (commit 1fa353ea, off main, unpushed — pending feature-branch merge + codex review + PR). Default now lives in config/models.seed.json:3-5 (enabled:true → resolveGlobalPromptCachePolicy default {retention:'short', scope:'channel'}). Fail-closed verified: applyModelAgnosticPromptCache (client-prompt-cache.ts:184) only installs cache_control when supportsCacheControlBreakpoints — open models get stable-prefix benefit with zero wire change (asserted client.test.ts:1176). Validation: npm run build success; vitest 4 files / 114 tests passed; verify:settings-contract passed. REMAINING for closure: merge to main via PR, then live fleet enablement — deployed models.json on each system-data PVC is NOT regenerated from seed; set modelRegistry.promptCaching.enabled=true per deployment, watch prompt.cache.prefix_instability telemetry, soak one companion, confirm cache-read pricing on provider dashboard. This audit did not access live systems or providers.
