title: Fleet efficiency: cut idle churn, per-turn disk/DB amplification, and redundant model spend across companions on shared clusters
description:
Companion epic to psfn-framework-t5z7 (Garden WAN performance). Source: four-lane Opus efficiency sweep, 2026-07-14, audited against main. Constraint for all children: no functional change, no weakening of fail-closed posture — "do more with less in constrained environments" (carlini: 5 companion deployments = 10 processes sharing one small k3s box and one Postgres).

Themes the children cover: (1) money — provider prompt caching is off, and retrieval work is recomputed per turn; (2) per-turn disk/DB amplification — the session write path full-rescans the journal on every append, and the Postgres projection issues no-op statements per message; (3) idle load — an audited no-op keepalive writes audit rows every 30s per deployment, and maintenance loops full-scan stores when nothing changed; (4) structural — session journals have no segment rotation so several paths remain O(all history); (5) a P3 grab-bag of small syscall/CPU wins.

Verified non-problems the sweep cleared (do not re-investigate): telegram long-polling is efficient; schedule.tick is cheap (no handlers); settings.json load is fingerprint-cached; no fsync anywhere is INTENTIONAL (durability rests on the HMAC chain — do not add fsync); memory store is DB-indexed with no per-turn re-embedding of stored content; turn-record whole-file reads are already fixed by hgw3.4 segment rotation on integration/hgw3-package — verify the admin path is covered once that branch merges.
close_reason: Epic completed. All child beads are closed; final remaining child 2z12.12 merged via PR #72 at b093158455 after mandatory gates and a CLEAN independent final review. Earlier children were already shipped/verified in their recorded commits and close evidence.

title: Transcript fetches ship up to 50 full turn snapshots because admin-ui never sends messagesOnly, OOMing the browser on long sessions
description:
Evidence: getSessionMessages (src/operator/garden/services/session-service.ts:670-743) attaches `turns` = up to DEFAULT_ADMIN_TURN_LIMIT=50 records, each the ENTIRE persisted turn snapshot via cloneTurnSnapshotRecord (src/operator/garden/services/session-turn-observability.ts:97-99) — full prompt context, provider wire messages, tool definitions. The server already supports ?messagesOnly=true (session-routes.ts:64, session-service.ts:697-725) to skip turns/roleEnvelopePreviews/compactionAuditViews, but the client never sends it: admin-ui/src/lib/api/endpoints/sessions.ts getSessionMessages has no messagesOnly param, and +page.svelte calls it on initial load (:146) AND every load-older page (:182-185), whose handler consumes only data.messages and data.messageOntologyViews. Observed live: transatlantic Garden session views against carlini are very slow and paging through a long session OOM'd Chrome (2026-07-14).

Fix shape: (1) send messagesOnly=true on pagination, and on initial load if turn detail moves to lazy fetch; (2) add a per-turn detail endpoint (or reuse existing turn lookup) fetched when the operator expands a turn; (3) consider client-side list virtualization or dropping far-scrolled pages so accumulated pages don't hold the DOM/memory.

Scope: Garden service + admin-ui only. Do NOT change turn-record persistence or the snapshot contract — hgw3.2 (in progress) owns read-time derivation and 1hr8 owns Loom payload bounding; coordinate, don't duplicate.
acceptance_criteria: Load-older network responses contain only messages/ontology views (no turns/roleEnvelopePreviews/compactionAuditViews); deep-scrolling a 1000+-message session against a remote cluster does not grow browser memory unboundedly; turn snapshot detail loads via a per-turn request only when the operator expands a turn; existing prompt-monitor/Loom behavior unchanged or explicitly migrated.
notes:
Implementation landed on branch bead/t5z7.1 (commit 352cb714, off main, unpushed — pending feature-branch merge + codex review + PR). Root-cause sharpened: the session browser NEVER rendered turn data (only prompt-monitor/Loom uses it) — the 50 snapshots were pure waste. Server: includeTurns option gating turns+roleEnvelopePreviews; new GET /api/admin/sessions/:channelId/turns/:turnId (compressed, bounded to recent-turn window, fail-closed 404). UI: initial load includeTurns:false (keeps compaction), load-older messagesOnly:true, per-turn detail on expand. Loom unchanged (default includeTurns=true). Validation: garden suite 63 files/451 tests passed; build success; svelte-check 0 errors/0 warnings; admin-ui build ok. DEVIATION: client list virtualization not added (bead listed as 'consider') — lean message text still accumulates on deep scroll; acute OOM driver (multi-MB snapshots) eliminated; strict bounded memory falls to t5z7.10 local-first work or a follow-up. FOLLOW-UP found: admin-ui chat/+page.svelte:329 also full getSessionMessages while reading only data.messages — same trim applies.
Codex-reviewed, findings fixed, shipped in PR #42 (perf/efficiency-wave-1 → main, https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/pull/42). Gate on the branch: build+lint clean, full suite 7715 passed / 1 pre-existing environmental failure (psfn-framework-engc). Ready to close on PR merge.

title: Garden transatlantic performance: bounded payloads, wire compression, cached/delta reads for multi-companion clusters
description:
Operating Garden against the carlini cluster (transatlantic WAN, 5 companions on one box) is painfully slow and has OOM'd Chrome. Root causes mapped 2026-07-14: transcript fetches ship up to 50 full turn snapshots the UI ignores, load-older pagination full-loads the whole channel JSONL server-side, most /api/admin JSON goes uncompressed with no conditional requests, and the sessions list joins every contact on every load.

Goal: Garden does more with less in constrained environments — bounded payloads (fetch only what the operator clicked), compression on the wire, ETag/304 for polling, server-side Redis read caching where it kills disk ops, and client-side caching with delta fetches. Zero functional change to what the operator can see.

Children carry the file:line evidence. Related existing work: psfn-framework-hgw3.2 (Loom read-time derivation, in progress), psfn-framework-1hr8 (Loom payload bounding), psfn-framework-efc2 (Garden UX cleanup wave 1).

title: Repair local Artemis Helm shakedown bootstrap for strict owner/auth contracts
description: Summary: the local production-shape Artemis smoke script at scripts/ops/setup-local-artemis-shakedown.sh is stale relative to current fail-closed runtime and Helm contracts. The value must be a role-bound proof derived from COMPANION_ID and GATEWAY_SESSION_HMAC_KEY via scripts/resolve-single-companion-auth.ts, not an independent random placeholder. Why: the official local production-shape gate cannot certify current code without undocumented manual mutation, and the default reset-data path is also poised to seed a topology-incompatible owner file. Scope: update the shakedown bootstrap so app Secret credentials satisfy current role-bound auth; seed or migrate newly required owner files without overwriting existing mutable owners; filter fleet-only companions.json unless multi-companion is explicitly enabled; add fixture-driven script/chart tests for clean and preserved PVC paths. acceptance_criteria: With provider credentials unset, the script succeeds on both a fresh local k3d namespace and a preserved PVC fixture that predates intake-policy.json; it derives a valid GATEWAY_SESSION_INTEGRITY_AUTH_TOKEN from the same HMAC keyring and companion ID used by gateway; it never installs companions.json in single-companion mode; it does not overwrite existing mutable owner files; psfn-agent, psfn-gateway, and psfn-garden reach Ready on the exact expected image; scripts/ops/validate-kube-rollout.sh passes with --skip-provider-routing; focused script/Helm tests, npm run lint, npm run verify:repository-hygiene, and npm run verify:backup-restore pass.

title: Expose relationship progression with family/partner HITL
description: Live Carlini reported that contact lookup exposes relationship values stranger, acquaintance, friend, family, and partner, but the model-facing contact tool only provides set_trust/propose_trust and no canonical relationship mutation. Relationship progression is also supposed to be considered by the daily relationship/trust check, but trust is the higher-priority HITL-gated axis and may be starving relationship progression. Implement the canonical relationship mutation and evaluator path: stranger to acquaintance is low-friction autonomous progression; acquaintance to friend remains autonomous but requires stronger evidence/threshold; transitions to family or partner require explicit HITL approval. Trust proposals remain separate and higher priority but must not suppress an otherwise eligible relationship proposal/change. Live turn records show contact calls that Garden tool-use audit did not display, so fix the canonical audit projection/display seam for contact calls as part of this work. Do not route relationships through trust proposals or bypass the canonical contact store. Preserve provenance/audit metadata and fail closed for malformed targets or missing approval infrastructure. Additional relationship classifications are a future schema decision and out of scope.
design: Keep trustLevel and relationshipType as separate axes. Reuse the canonical contact mutation/proposal and HITL approval infrastructure. Family and partner are approval-required relationship targets; acquaintance and friend are autonomous targets with target-specific progression evidence. Do not add new relationship enum values in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: The contact tool schema exposes an intention-revealing relationship mutation action; tests prove autonomous stranger/acquaintance/friend changes persist through the canonical contact store with friend using the stronger evidence policy; tests prove family and partner cannot persist without explicit HITL approval and do persist after approved flows; the daily relationship/trust evaluator considers relationship progression even when trust is unchanged, gated, or higher priority; contact reads, mutations, and approval proposals appear in Garden tool-use audit with action/result status but no private payload leakage; existing trust actions remain unchanged; targeted tests, lint, build/typecheck, and full tests pass.
notes:
Implemented canonical contact set_relationship/propose_relationship actions with evidence derived from stored history, stronger friend threshold, family/partner HITL, CAS+atomic audit in SQLite/Postgres, trust/relationship independence, and daily two-axis review. Garden now shows contact invocations with tool/action/status/channel/time and redacts contact failure details; private IDs/args/results are excluded. Verification: focused cross-cutting suite 303/303 plus final regression suite 146/146; Garden check 0 errors/warnings and production build green; core build/lint green; two independent final reviews clean.
Live deployment: PR #41 merged as c0385f2b. Garden adaptive-tools endpoint returns 200 with recentInvocations projection keys toolName/action/status/channelId/timestamp; zero recent calls was expected immediately after restart. Carlini plus Denise/Garden Nun/Julienne/Lucy are 1/1 on c0385f2b, all see GLM 5.2, Postgres vector and Redis PONG verified.
close_reason: Implemented and verified relationship progression, HITL gating, daily review, and private-safe Garden contact audit.

title: Prevent false image-attachment claims when no image tool ran
description: Live Carlini DM diagnosis on 2026-07-14: ChatGPTN produced repeated assistant replies containing *image attached* while turn records, image ledger, and outbound responses showed zero image tool calls and zero attachments. The active selfie_create/generate_image schemas and backend tool calling were healthy. Root cause: session context intentionally omits persisted tool observations but retains final assistant marker text, so successful image turns are replayed as ordinary assistant prose and repeated false markers contaminate the prompt. Implement two bounded safeguards: preserve safe structured provenance that an artifact-producing tool succeeded without replaying full/stale tool payloads, and fail closed or retry if current assistant text claims an image attachment without a current-turn image result/attachment. Do not expose image bytes, stale URLs, tool arguments, or private tool payloads in history.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test proves a prior successful selfie_create turn is represented in later model context with bounded tool-success/attachment provenance while full tool output remains excluded; a turn-level regression proves assistant text claiming an attached image cannot be delivered or persisted unchanged when no current-turn image tool result or attachment exists; real selfie_create/generate_image attachments still deliver normally; targeted tests, lint, build/typecheck, and full test suite pass.
notes:
Implemented bounded historical image-tool success provenance without payloads/URLs/arguments; current-turn attachment claim guard now rejects affirmative image/selfie/photo claims unless a structured attachment exists and replaces/persists an explicit correction. Tests cover real attachments, common grammar, historical/prompt-description non-claims, and private-data exclusion. Verification: focused image/session/runtime tests green; reduced-concurrency full suite 7,730 passed with sole stale expectation corrected and rerun green; core build, lint, and independent reviews clean.
Live deployment: merged by PR #41 to main c0385f2b and deployed remotely as Helm revision 35. Carlini and all four fleet agents are 1/1 on the exact image; tool wiring reports 23 tools and Ready; external/Garden health 200 with admin transport OK.
2026-07-14 post-deploy live regression: turn 019f6238-2177-77ed-bfcc-4396240de220 had selfie_create and generate_image in the provider-visible tool set, zero tool calls, and no image gateway activity. The guard correctly caught ChatGPTN's false attachment claim but persisted/sent MISSING_IMAGE_ATTACHMENT_CORRECTION verbatim as companion dialogue. Follow-up filed to keep fail-closed behavior while moving correction internal and adding bounded recovery.
close_reason: Implemented and verified bounded image provenance plus fail-closed attachment claims.

title: Ship current main (28b5e334 stamp fixes) to psfn-shard
description:

title: Session context capture intermittently misses the previous assistant reply, causing duplicate replies
description:
Evidence: turn 019f60eb (Discord 1313001762793197678, 2026-07-14 09:57:49 EDT) — observability.snapshot.promptContext.providerWireMessages ends: user '[Tue 07-14-26 09:37] i gave you headpats last night!' then user 'its ok my heart the cross channel sync stuff is still a bit weird'. Assistant entry 5256 (the reply between them) is missing from sessionContext.recentEntries (max id 5255) even though: it was recorded synchronously in-turn at 09:38:20 (turn-execution-runtime.ts:1067), it is present and HMAC-chained in the L0 journal, and recordUserMessage assigned id 5257 at 09:57:49 — meaning the write-path reconcile (store.ts reconcileWriteCache) saw disk maxId 5256 moments before the capture read missed it. Signature across the turn-record file: 5 of 49 turns since Jul 12 (21:23, 23:20 Jul 12; 00:21, 22:55 Jul 13; 09:57 Jul 14), each with recentEntries frozen at exactly the PREVIOUS turn's user entry (5081/5112/5115/5197/5255), gaps 2-60 min. Model then re-answers the older message; with bbacbaa2 stamps the merged consecutive user messages make it re-answer with the older stamp mimicked.

Context: read path suspects in src/persistence/sessions/store.ts — ensureChannelFullyLoaded returns a fullyLoaded cache with no file-staleness check (this is the path used whenever compaction summaries exist, via compaction-boundary-store getEntriesInRange); recentEntriesByLimit fingerprint cache; syncLightweightCacheFromIndexEntry fed by the shared _channel_index.json which any co-mounted process (gateway/garden) rewrites whole-file via saveChannelIndex. Journal itself is append-only and intact — this is purely a read-view coherence bug.

Scope: (1) root-cause with a repro test around the fullyLoaded/getEntriesInRange path under cross-turn timing and multi-process index writes; (2) in-turn DETECT-AND-HEAL guard in captureTurnSessionContext: the pipeline knows the just-recorded user entry id — if recentEntries does not reach the entry immediately preceding it, force a disk reconcile and recapture once, log loudly, then PROCEED REGARDLESS. Never block or drop the reply: operator decision 2026-07-14 — a duplicate reply is better than no reply. Non-goal: do not add Redis here (separate child bead).

Acceptance: repro test demonstrates the stale read and passes with the fix; guard emits a named telemetry/log event on heal; 7 days of live turn records show zero captures missing the previous turn's assistantSessionEntryId (scan script: compare each record's recentEntries ids against previous record's assistantMessage.sessionEntryId).
notes:
2026-07-14 root cause found + fixed on branch bead/hgw3.1-capture-staleness (377cb801, based on c77e1f45). ROOT CAUSE: store.ts:404 ensureChannelFullyLoaded returned in-memory fullyLoaded cache with NO archive staleness check (same hole in getRecent's fullyLoaded fast path :744) — the exact path the compaction-summaries route takes (compaction-boundary getRecent → getEntriesInRange → ensureChannelFullyLoaded). Cross-instance appends (agent/gateway/garden share the dir) leave a reader frozen. FIX: ChannelCache.archiveFingerprint (statSync dev/ino/size/mtime/ctime) stamped before loadChannel and refreshed on every journal write; fullyLoadedCacheIsCurrent gates both serve paths; new SessionStore.reloadChannelFromDisk. GUARD: pre-turn healStaleCapturedSessionWindow — raw window max entry id < just-recorded currentSessionEntryId → warn + session.context.stale_window_heal telemetry + forced reconcile + ONE recapture; never blocks (heal failure emits stale_window_heal_failed and proceeds). Repro test proves it: 5/6 fail with fix stashed, 6/6 pass with fix. 264 tests across touched suites pass; lint clean; tsc byte-identical to baseline. Orchestrator re-ran repro+guard: 12/12.
Residual (watch after ship): same-process mechanism of the live 5255 freeze unproven — monitor stale_window_heal telemetry on psfn-shard; metadata-only surfaces (count/getSessionActivity) can still serve stale counters from a frozen cache (possible follow-up bead).
close_reason: Shipped in 576e33cd (helm rev 53+, tag 0.1.0-kube-576e33cd, gate 11/11). Root cause: fullyLoaded cache serve paths without file-staleness checks (store.ts ensureChannelFullyLoaded + getRecent fast path). Fix: archive stat-fingerprint gates; heal guard emits session.context.stale_window_heal + one forced reconcile/recapture, never blocks. Repro test fails 5/6 with fix stashed, passes with fix. Live: rollout gate + two-turn smoke passed; monitoring plan = watch stale_window_heal telemetry; the 7-day zero-recurrence scan is post-hoc (reopen if it fires with a non-healing outcome).

title: Duplicate replies and turn-record bloat: session read coherence, turn-record diet, session tail architecture
description:
Work package from the 2026-07-14 duplicate-reply investigation on psfn-shard.

Evidence anchor: turn 019f60eb-6e4a-757a-b369-90786a093b31 (Discord, 09:57:49 EDT) — provider wire messages ended [user 'i gave you headpats last night!', user 'its ok my heart...']; assistant reply session entry 5256 (written synchronously 09:38:20, present and HMAC-intact in the L0 journal) was absent from the captured context, so the model regenerated its previous reply. Same signature in 5 of the last 49 Discord turn records back to Jul 12 — predates bbacbaa2, so this is not a temporal-work regression; the Jul 9 fix 3375fece addressed a different layer (prompt assembly), the store-read staleness was never fixed.

Secondary findings in the same sweep: turn records are ~631KB/turn with the same conversation stored 3x and tool schemas 2x (392MB _turn_records file ≈ only ~600-700 turns); readRecentTurnRecords parses the whole file (Garden sessions/:id times out); sessions have no Redis tail (in-process caches over JSONL only); leaked history stamps are persisted inside L0 content (entries 5240/5254/5258); no automatic L0 max-turns cap exists despite operator memory of one.

Children carry the individual fixes. Non-goal: no behavior change to what the companion says beyond eliminating the dropped-context duplicates.
notes:
2026-07-14 Codex second-party review of integration/hgw3-package (session 019f6179-8915-7f10-bb30-64d9738ce939): 12 confirmed findings — 2 Critical (Redis tail can resurrect CogSec-redacted content cross-process via async/process-local invalidation + redis-wins overlap; concurrent turn-record rotation can clobber a completed segment via renameSync), 5 High (unscoped tail keys across companions; unsigned tail rows override HMAC-verified journal rows; interior tail gap defeats the heal guard; start-gateway-agent.sh env -i strips PSFN_REDIS_*; tombstone fast path serves stale cross-process state), 5 Medium (reader/rotation race; count/activity metadata staleness; tombstone → unbounded full-history read; sidecar interning trusts corrupt existing file; malformed-line quarantine invisible to callers).
Fix wave launched on two branches off the integration branch: fix/hgw3-redis-tail-hardening (per-channel epoch INCR'd synchronously by every journal rewrite — rewrite fails loudly if INCR fails while enabled; id-contiguity check; companion-scoped key prefix; launcher allowlist; merge rule flipped to journal-wins-on-overlap / redis only fills ids newer than the journal window) and fix/hgw3-turnrecord-concurrency (cross-process lock + exclusive-create rotation; reader ENOENT retry + inode dedupe; bounded tombstone overscan; fingerprint-gated tombstone/count/activity state; sidecar hash validation on intern; quarantine telemetry).
Deliberately deferred: full HMAC signing of Redis tail rows (threat requires in-cluster Redis access; exposure shrunk to newer-than-journal gap-fill rows by the merge-rule flip) — revisit if the tail is ever enabled on shared/untrusted Redis.
close_reason: All children closed. Epic delivered across two packages: core session-coherence package shipped 2026-07-14 (PR #43 -> main 576e33cd: stale-window heal, slim records + tooldefs sidecar, rotation concurrency, Redis tail shipped-disabled per operator HOLD). Turn-record diet package (this wave, feat/hgw3-turnrecord-diet @ e71bafde17, pushed, PR pending): 80f6 true provider wire capture + wirebodies sidecar, auiu static-prompt-prefix content-addressing, 9ree recentEntries as L0 id-refs with redaction-aware reconstruction (sidecar pattern deliberately rejected to preserve redaction propagation), jsi9 memory candidates as id+score refs resolved at Garden boundary, hgw3.10 old-fat redaction gating + heal-drop telemetry (closes the epic's resurrection pathology for records of any vintage). Every bead through tiered adversarial review (P1 dual blind, P2 single Pi; all PASS; 1 cross-remediated blocker). 24o5 (cross-process archive mint) remains a separate open bead outside this epic. Epic-level handoff notes: wirebodies GC/retention + CogSec reach, 3-sidecar whole-channel fail-closed blast radius, heal-drop Garden ring surfacing.

title: Restore credentials: reject indirect libpq secrets and sanitize child environments
description: Summary: The c337 final review found that src/persistence/backups/postgres-connection.ts omits PostgreSQL credential-bearing parameters including scram_client_key and scram_server_key, and restore subprocesses inherit ambient libpq credential sources such as PGPASSWORD, PGPASSFILE, PGSERVICE, PGSERVICEFILE, and PGSSLKEY. Unsupported secrets can reach argv, durable restore journals, operation identifiers, logs, or authenticate a destructive restore outside the explicitly approved URL credential. Why: restore credentials and authorization must fail closed and never leak through process listings or durable state. Scope: maintain a complete supported credential classification; reject unsupported URI credential channels before connectionArg construction; build a sanitized child environment that removes ambient/service credential variables and disables default password/client-key discovery; set only the explicitly parsed URL password as PGPASSWORD; redact errors, journals, hashes, and logs. Files: src/persistence/backups/postgres-connection.ts and restore/marker/service call sites plus unit and integration tests. Non-goals: support every libpq authentication mechanism or add ambient credential fallback. Current implementation is backed up on origin/feat/fleet-workspace-isolation at c8e95be453ce644904004f6fc48307ab1db1879d.
acceptance_criteria: scram_client_key, scram_server_key, passfile, sslkey, service and other credential-bearing URI forms reject without raw or encoded secret disclosure. Restore child environments remove PGPASSWORD, PGPASSFILE, PGSERVICE, PGSERVICEFILE, PGSSLKEY and equivalent ambient sources before setting the one approved explicit password. Secrets never appear in argv, journals, operation IDs, logs, or wrapped errors. A supported-current-libpq keyword matrix and real PostgreSQL tests pass with npm run lint, build, and backup verification.
notes:
Implementation pushed in 76635cd9 and 677b4cdd. Validation: focused credential/backup/fleet/restore matrix 111 passed; real PostgreSQL fleet restore integration 3 passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; npm run verify:backup-restore passed; dependency-cycle subcheck passed. Full npm test: 7758 passed, 3 skipped, 2 inherited failures in untouched scheduler owner-file tests due missing minPartnerIdleMinutes fixture expectation. Repository hygiene remains blocked by inherited identity-literal and shared-type-guard findings in untouched files; public sanitize and dependency-cycle checks pass. Single-review remediation pushed at 4e555d92049e7726f9eecc1ba7c184b55a4a2c8e. redactPostgresCredential now preserves literal case while matching percent-escape hex case variants and independently covers form encoding. Added raw/URI/form mixed-case warning and wrapped-error regressions. Validation: focused connection/restore plus real PostgreSQL integration 77 passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; npm run verify:backup-restore passed. Full npm test: 7760 passed, 3 skipped, with the same 2 inherited scheduler fixture failures for minPartnerIdleMinutes in untouched config tests. Awaiting the same reviewers final regression check; bead remains in progress.
Correction to the preceding note: the exact remediation commit is 4e555d92c74e87ee53e3a8de2fb38a73bdc2655b.
close_reason: Completed and integrated on feat/fleet-workspace-isolation. Implementation 76635cd9 and 677b4cdd classified supported current libpq URI parameters, rejected unsupported credential-bearing and indirect-auth channels without disclosure, stripped ambient libpq/GSS credential sources from backup/restore child environments, passed only the explicitly approved URL password through PGPASSWORD, and kept credentials out of argv, journals, operation identifiers, logs, and wrapped errors. The single independent review found one IMPORTANT redaction gap: the redactor lowercased whole URI spellings and did not generate the form-encoded spelling, so mixed-case percent-escape variants and + space encodings could leak while unrelated lowercased literals could be over-redacted. Remediation 4e555d92 preserves literal password case, varies only percent-escape hex case, independently covers form encoding, and adds warning/wrapped-error regressions. Final reviewer regression PASS at 4e555d92: 77/77 focused connection/restore tests including 3 real-Postgres integrations; npm run lint, npm run build including DTS, and npm run verify:backup-restore with verified=true passed. Combined integration merge 28c7cba4 preserved both restore fixes: 127/127 connection/restore/transaction/service/fleet tests including 3 real-Postgres integrations passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build including DTS passed; npm run verify:backup-restore passed with verified=true; git diff --check passed. title: Restore rollback: retain operation ownership through destructive filesystem cleanup
description: Summary: The c337 final review found that src/persistence/backups/fleet-restore-transaction.ts:245-256 removes the durable PostgreSQL restore-operation marker before cleanupPublishedTrees and cleanupStagedTrees finish. A crash after marker removal leaves a rolling_back journal with absent ownership evidence; recovery at lines 283-311 may delete a destination tree that was recreated or repopulated after the marker disappeared. Why: destructive restore cleanup must remain bound to the exact restore operation until every PostgreSQL and filesystem mutation is complete. Scope: retain the exact prepared/committed marker through database rollback and all staged/published tree cleanup; remove it only after durable confirmation that every owned tree is gone; make absent or foreign marker recovery non-destructive; preserve journal evidence for safe operator recovery. Files: src/persistence/backups/fleet-restore-transaction.ts, fleet-restore-database-marker.ts, focused crash/recovery tests. Non-goals: redesign backup formats or relax restore collision policy. Current implementation is backed up on origin/feat/fleet-workspace-isolation at c8e95be453ce644904004f6fc48307ab1db1879d.
acceptance_criteria: A killed-process test publishes at least one destination tree, enters rolling_back, loses the response after marker removal, and proves restart with an absent or foreign marker performs zero filesystem or schema deletion. Exact owned markers permit bounded rollback. The ownership marker is removed only after PostgreSQL and owned filesystem cleanup are durably complete. Focused restore tests, real PostgreSQL integration, npm run lint, build, and backup verification pass.
notes: Implementation checkpoint 28dac42341031c50ec114008ffaf708513d23cae plus single review remediation 078f7bfefc4dfb171ba2bc1e3c5cca85d4fc1fb9 are pushed on work/fleet-restore-rollback-ownership. The remediation fixes the IMPORTANT staging-ownership finding only: a fresh restore now rejects any deterministic staging collision before database preflight, rechecks after preflight, atomically claims new staging directories, and cleans only directories claimed by the current invocation. Absent- and foreign-marker regressions reproduce a lost journal with staged sentinel content and prove the sentinel, missing-journal state, and destination remain unchanged. Final remediation validation: focused restore suite 4 files / 40 tests passed, including fleet-restore.integration.test.ts against real PostgreSQL (3 tests); npm run lint exit 0; npm run build exit 0 with ESM and DTS; npm run verify:backup-restore exit 0 with verified=true; git diff --check passed. Original SIGKILL marker-removal and recreated-tree regressions remain green. No credential-channel, SQLite, Pi, SSH, live, or unrelated changes. Bead remains in_progress pending the assigned reviewer final regression check; no new review was run.
close_reason: Completed and integrated on feat/fleet-workspace-isolation. Implementation 28dac423 retained the exact durable Postgres restore marker through database rollback and durable published/staged filesystem cleanup, made absent/foreign marker recovery non-destructive, preserved journal evidence, and added lost-response/SIGKILL regressions. The single independent review found one IMPORTANT gap: fresh staging deleted a pre-existing deterministic staging tree before authenticated ownership. Remediation 078f7bfe made unauthenticated staging collisions fail closed, rechecked after database preflight, atomically claimed new staging directories, and cleaned only paths claimed by the current invocation. Final reviewer regression check PASS at 078f7bfe: 33/33 focused restore tests including 3 real-Postgres tests and prior lost-response/SIGKILL paths; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed including DTS; npm run verify:backup-restore passed with verified=true; git diff --check passed. Branch commit 078f7bfe is integrated and pushed. Parent psfn-framework-c337 remains open because psfn-framework-5s70 is still in flight.

title: History timestamps leak into companion output (mimicry) — must never reach chat display or TTS
description:
Evidence: operator observed [Ddd MM-DD-YY HH:mm] stamps leaking into chat display after 2x37.1 (bbacbaa2); not yet observed in voice. Fix (two layers): (1) stamp only user and system history messages — assistant turns render unstamped so the model never sees its own speech prefixed; (2) outbound reply hygiene strips any leading stamp pattern before channel dispatch/TTS as fail-safe.

title: Fan temporal wakeup notes out to all recently-active chat channels, not just latest session
description:
Evidence: both wakeup lanes resolve a single target via resolveStartupSessionMetadata('reuse_latest_session') (src/core/scheduler/temporal-wakeup.ts:710, resolveWakeupSessionContext). If the latest session is e.g. the API channel, the new-day note never reaches discord/satellite where the partner talks next morning — confirmed operator symptom.
Fix: enumerate recently-active conversational channels (partner activity within a lookback window, default 72h; config knob under temporalWakeup) and run per-channel eligibility + injection. Per-channel anti-loop already works — morningNoteBySession/combinedNoteBySession maps are keyed by sessionId. Keep existing gates per channel: isInternalSessionId, public-channel privacy boundary, partner-idle guard. title: Full-suite Vitest exits 1 from late unhandled ENOENT on a *.jsonl.write-lock session path during subagent-cancellation teardown
description:
Evidence: two consecutive normal full-suite runs on feat/icp-autonomy at 72238bc8 completed all assertions (720 files / 8,342 passed / 3 skipped) but Vitest exited 1 both times with a late unhandled ENOENT referencing a missing session path matching *.jsonl.write-lock, arriving around the teardown of 'SubagentFaculty > cancels active bounded workers without crossing into shard semantics' (src/faculties/subagents/faculty.test.ts). That test passes 1/1 in isolation. The exact generated temp path and full stack were not preserved; see working_docs/w6-fresh-eyes-handoff.md (Unresolved full-suite teardown failure).

Context: this is a test-gate issue, not a confirmed W6 correctness defect — but until it is explained or a clean full-suite exit is obtained, feat/icp-autonomy cannot honestly claim a green latest full suite, which gates closing psfn-framework-s10mc.6.6. Relevant surfaces: src/faculties/subagents/faculty.test.ts (synchronous temp-root deletion), src/faculties/subagents/faculty.ts (cancel/run lifecycle), src/persistence/sessions/store.ts (journal write-lock create/remove). Plausible-but-unproven cause: late canceled-worker session work outliving test cleanup. Do not record that as diagnosis without a controlled reproduction.

Scope: diagnose with durable logging (preserve the failing path and stack), then either fix the race (test cleanup ordering or write-lock lifecycle) or prove it pre-exists the W6 range. Do not weaken fail-closed write-lock semantics to make the error disappear; do not blanket-serialize the suite as the fix.

Acceptance: a controlled reproduction (or proof of non-reproduction across >=3 serialized and >=3 normal full-suite runs) with captured stack; root cause stated with evidence; two consecutive normal full-suite runs exit 0.
close_reason: Root cause proven, fixed, validated. Captured unhandled-rejection stack: mkdirSync *.jsonl.write-lock -> withJournalWriteLock (store.ts:262) -> SessionStore.append -> recordAssistantMessage -> handleMessageForTurn. Cause: SubagentFaculty.message() dispatched follow-ups as fresh ordinary turns never tracked by the handle's completion; wait()/execute() resolved after the initial turn only, so a detached follow-up turn wrote its journal after test teardown deleted the temp session root. The bead's named cancel test was a bystander — the rejection merely landed in its window; the leak came from the follow-up delivery test. Fix a0b25eac (merged 1100b786 on feat/icp-autonomy): track outstanding follow-up/steer turns on the handle, drain before terminal, route failures to audit instead of the prior fire-and-forget swallow. Write-lock semantics untouched; suite not serialized. Evidence: 20x targeted loop 0 captures (was 1/run); two consecutive clean full-suite runs on the fix branch AND two more on the merged tree (722 files / 8,357 passed / 3 skipped, exit 0 each); lint and build green.

title: Accounting query engine: calendar/custom ranges, time buckets, multidimensional breakdowns, sorting, and export

design: One query grammar serves all operator consumers. Named windows resolve server-side from a stated timezone and return exact resolved boundaries. Graph points and table totals must reconcile. Prefer raw indexed queries first; introduce rollup tables only with benchmark evidence and a rebuildable derivation contract.

title: Operator accounting: reconcile behavioral charge units to monetary cost by lane, surface, and run lineage
description: Summary: Add the missing operator-only mapping between PSFN behavioral charge and real/estimated monetary cost. Charge units deliberately encode autonomy/resource stewardship rather than dollars, but charge events and model usage already share lane/surface/run/root lineage fields. Scope: join canonical model-usage events to charge runs/events using typed correlation; totals by lane, surface, run/root, companion, model, channel and time range; report charge units, provider cost, estimated/effective cost, dollars per charge unit, token mix and call count; attribution coverage and explicit charged-without-usage, usage-without-charge, ambiguous/many-to-many and non-LLM charge buckets; deterministic allocation rules when multiple model calls belong to one charge event/run; avoid assigning dollar cost to zero-call actions; reconcile shard/subagent lineage without mixing their policy scopes; operator API and query projections consumed by UI; companion prompt/runtime_charge_budget remains unit-only and monetary-free. Coordinate with the original charge ledger and psfn-framework-574y rather than introducing a parallel accounting table. Files: run-charge/charge-ledger/model-usage contracts and stores, charge ledger service, model usage service/query store, Garden types/routes/tests. Non-goals: making one charge unit equal a fixed USD amount, changing charge policy automatically from current prices, or exposing money to the companion.
design: Charge and dollars are two axes. Compute observed dollars per charge unit over a selected scope; never encode a universal exchange rate. Preserve unmatched buckets so coverage is measurable. Prefer run/root correlation for one-to-many calls, with event-level joins only where exact. Any allocation must state method and confidence/coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Operator queries show charge units and effective/provider/estimated dollars together by lane/surface/run/root/channel/companion/time; dollars-per-unit is computed only for attributable nonzero units and never presented as a fixed policy price; unmatched/ambiguous/non-LLM buckets and coverage percentages reconcile to both source ledgers; retries and nested shard/subagent lineages do not double count; companion prompts and decisions remain dollar-free; reconciliation/API/integration/build/lint tests pass.

title: Dashboard cost repair: replace in-memory month samples with durable live model-usage queries
description: Steps to Reproduce: Run an LLM call while the Garden operator process is not receiving the agent event bus directly or restart the operator after usage. Load the main dashboard and observe that in-memory cost windows are empty/stale despite rows in model_usage_events. Compare with /api/admin/model-usage. Summary: Fix the main Garden dashboard cost estimate that does not update reliably. Current AdminDashboardDataService accumulates agent.turn.usage in memory, prunes samples before the current UTC month, and computes Today/Week/Month locally. This resets on operator restart and can miss agent events across process/socket boundaries even though durable Postgres model_usage_events exists. Scope: make persisted canonical model usage the source for cost/token/call dashboard cards; remove or demote the independent usageSamples/usageTotals accounting path; query selected range via AdminModelUsage service/store; include cache read/write and provider/estimated/effective cost; define freshness timestamp/source and unavailable/stale states; reliable refresh after new usage via bounded polling, existing Garden event invalidation, or another shared mechanism without creating duplicate truth; handle concurrent requests and operator/agent restarts; maintain active-session context-pressure data separately where in-memory state is appropriate; no-store API caching; regression tests reproducing stale/non-updating dashboard. Files: dashboard-service.ts, overview routes/admin contracts/local composition, dashboard types/API/frontend, model usage service/store, tests. Non-goals: full graph UI or historical grouping beyond consuming the canonical query contract.
design: Durable usage is accounting truth. Live events may invalidate/refresh a cached projection but must not be the only source. Dashboard should fail visibly when model-usage storage is unavailable rather than display a plausible $0.00 as fresh truth. Keep transient TTFT/context-pressure telemetry clearly labeled separately.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard totals derive from persisted model usage, survive operator/agent restart, include usage recorded by separate processes, and update within a documented bounded interval after a new call; switching ranges cannot race stale responses; unavailable/stale storage is labeled rather than silently zeroed; cache read/write and effective/provider/estimated cost reconcile with /api/admin/model-usage for the same range; regression, route, frontend, restart/concurrency, build and lint tests pass.

title: Accounting attribution: persist and query companion, channel, origin, tool, lane, lineage, and workload dimensions
description: Summary: Complete typed attribution so every dollar/token/call can be grouped and filtered instead of landing in an ambiguous total. The table already stores channel_id, purpose, origin, service/process, turn/request/tool IDs, charge lane/surface/run lineage and provider/model, but ModelUsageQuery exposes only time, provider/model, tool, callKind and runId, and companion/shard/subagent/conversation dimensions are incomplete. Scope: define a normalized attribution envelope; propagate companionId, canonical session/channelId and channel type, call kind/type, purpose, origin type/stage, service/process, provider/model/slot, tool, charge lane/surface/run/root/parent, shardId, subagentId, ICP conversationId/root initiation, status, cost source and other bounded workload IDs; decide first-class indexed columns versus metadata based on query needs; add strict query filters and group-by dimensions; explicit unknown/unattributed buckets and coverage percentages; channel normalization without revealing message content; indexes for time-plus-dimension workloads; tenancy behavior in multi-companion schemas and fleet aggregation. Files: shared telemetry/runtime correlation contracts, all recorder call sites, model-usage Postgres schema/query store, Garden service/API types and tests. Non-goals: UI charts or guessing missing historical attribution.
design: Attribution is a typed envelope captured at call time; do not infer critical dimensions later from free-form purpose strings. Unknown is data and must remain visible. ChannelId is operator-sensitive but allowed on authenticated Garden surfaces; never persist prompt/message content in accounting. Design indexes from actual filter/group queries and avoid an unbounded label system.

title: Accounting capture: reconcile attempts, provider/estimated cost, and input/cache/output token economics
description: Summary: Make the existing model-usage event pipeline complete and arithmetically trustworthy before adding analytics. Current contracts already carry input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite tokens, providerCostUsd, estimatedCostUsd and costSource, and Postgres persists token counts plus total provider/estimated cost. Scope: direct chat/completion, streaming, tool continuations/retries, embeddings, image calls, summaries, extraction, reflection/sidecars, analysis workbench, subagents and shards; normalize provider-specific prompt/read/cache-read/cache-write/output usage; preserve raw provider usage/cost evidence in bounded metadata; add explicit monetary components for input, cache read, cache write and output when rates/provider data permit, with unknown rather than fabricated allocation when provider reports only a total; define requested vs routed provider/model; logicalCallId/attempt semantics, retry cost inclusion and dedupe; provider-reported versus locally estimated precedence; total-token semantics that do not double-count cache tokens; success/failure/partial-stream settlement; late/missing provider cost; currency; startup wiring so every path records to the same Postgres store; reconciliation fixtures. title: [S10 ICP] Certify autonomous ICP with two real agents, restart continuity, privacy, fatigue, charge, and cost stops
description: Summary: Build the production-shape acceptance harness and staged shakedown that proves ICP autonomy as one coherent system rather than a collection of mocks. Use one gateway, two real SubstrateAgent processes, separate companion data roots/Postgres schemas, shared schema, canonical owner files, and deterministic model fixtures plus an optional live-model smoke. Scope: candidate formation from at least free time and weighted thought; zero-LLM closed gates; availability/decline/defer; permit races/replay; target-channel first-message persistence before delivery; recipient normal turn; sufficient messages to force compaction; both-agent restart and summary continuity; independent extraction/trust with no schema crossover; private-room exit/rejoin privacy; fatigue progression, social charge, final reserve, and suppression; DM/room anti-evasion; lowered test dollar warning/hard stop aggregating both agents; delivery failure/retry; feature-off and single-companion parity; adversarial identity, block/DND, recursive trigger, malformed config, missing cost, and duplicate frame cases; structured logs. Run live or production-faithful rollout with emergency disable and rollback. Non-goals: cross-cluster Artie link or rich media.
design: Do not certify only the pure gateway LaneAgent harness: it does not prove SessionManager, summaries, extraction, restart, or cost propagation. title: [S10 ICP] Enforce canonical conversation-scoped USD warning and runaway breaker across both companions
description: Summary: After the canonical cost-accounting review psfn-framework-cam lands, implement an ICP conversation-scoped dollar warning and hard breaker using the canonical model-usage records rather than a parallel counter. Why: fatigue/charge should normally stop conversation, but a high dollar ceiling catches duplication, routing bugs, pathological model behavior, or policy misconfiguration; an illustrative USD 2 ceiling would be extremely long on current models, but exact defaults require verified pricing and evidence. Scope: propagate conversationId/rootInitiationId through both agents and all attributable direct/tool/summary/extraction/sidecar calls; define which background work counts; cross-process aggregate reservation and actual settlement; deterministic projected-cost preflight; warning band reserving the final eligible closeout response; hard suppression before an over-budget call; missing/late provider cost behavior; restart/concurrency/race reconciliation; typed events and Garden projections; owner-file settings; explicit scope separation from shards, subagents, human chat, and global daily/monthly model budgets. Non-goals: replacing canonical accounting, freezing illustrative prices, or allowing an importance claim to bypass the hard breaker.
design: The gateway/canonical usage store is the aggregation boundary. Use costSource-aware reservation and settlement from psfn-framework-cam. The breaker should almost never fire; any event is an investigation signal. Exact thresholds are mutable owner policy selected from verified model pricing. Shard goal correlations must never enter an ICP conversation scope.
acceptance_criteria: All attributable costs from both agents query under one conversationId without double counting; projected reservation and actual settlement reconcile across streaming, retries, cache, tools, summaries, extraction, failures, restart, and concurrency; warning leaves a configured final-response reserve and hard limit suppresses before a model call; missing cost fails according to explicit conservative policy; shard/subagent/human/global budget scopes are provably unaffected; exact thresholds are owner-configured and tested; Garden/audit events explain every warning/stop; targeted accounting tests, settings-contract, build, and lint pass.

title: [S10 ICP] Integrate soft conversational allowance, social charge, closeout reserve, and cross-channel anti-evasion
description: Summary: Extend the existing FatigueBudgetPort and charge system so autonomous ICP begins naturally, becomes progressively intentional, and stops at fatigue plus the configured one-to-two response closeout reserve. Why: the operator explicitly prefers charge/fatigue over small arbitrary message-count quotas, while still requiring a reliable end to loops. Scope: relationship/channel/intent-derived soft allowance targeting roughly 6-8 combined messages for an ordinary trusted conversation without hardcoding that count universally; shared conversation activity for observability; per-companion fatigue and choice; transition into a dedicated companion_social charge lane after the allowance; prompt-visible maturing/charge/wrap/final-closeout states; typed continuation evidence; marginal charge policy; existing deterministic recent-human/work-like overcharge triggers plus carefully reviewed ICP continuation evidence; final suppression when hard fatigue and reserve exhaust; decaying initiation pressure; relationship/root state that prevents DM/room hopping from resetting regulation; daily reset semantics reviewed against multi-episode conversations; Garden telemetry inputs. Extend charge-policy owner schema and tests. Non-goals: human attention fatigue, unlimited importance exemptions, dollar accounting, or shard budgets.
design: Do not build a second fatigue engine. Current per-local-companion fatigue remains authoritative for reply choice; shared conversation/root state adds aggregate context and anti-evasion. The final reserve is finite and visible to the model as the last closeout opportunity. Importance consumes reserve and is auditable; it never manufactures new reserve.
acceptance_criteria: Policy tests show normal relationship/channel/intent-sensitive allowance, progressive fatigue guidance, switch to the social charge lane, bounded continuation, final closeout reserve, and suppression after exhaustion; human turns remain free under existing rules; both companions retain independent fatigue choices; DM/room hopping and recursive new episodes cannot reset recent relationship pressure; decline/silence and elapsed time affect initiation pressure without arbitrary daily quotas; strict config/Garden metadata are produced; existing fatigue regressions, targeted new tests, settings-contract, build, and lint pass.

title: [S10 ICP] Connect free time, weighted thoughts, intentions, foreground choices, and co-location to one initiation-candidate path
description: Summary: Wire genuine companion motivation into the shared ICP candidate broker without adding unconditional LLM polling or parallel outreach implementations. Sources are free time, weighted thoughts, durable intentions/concerns, foreground realizations, and low-weight co-location observations. Why: autonomy requires opportunities to choose outreach, but every source must share the same deterministic policy, consent, and audit path. Scope: free-time action creates only a private candidate and never sends from internal:free-time; weighted-thought outreach resolves known same-cluster peer targets and preserves lifecycle/provenance; intention follow-ups create candidates only while their source is live; foreground choices enqueue after the active response reaches idle; co-location may reinforce/create a thought but cannot auto-greet or call an LLM; one candidate store, dedupe, TTL, decline dampening, deferral, cancellation, restart recovery, and root-chain propagation; deterministic gates precede the companion consent moment; consent can send, defer, or decline; accepted consent requests a permit and target-channel turn. Likely files: free-time.ts, weighted-thought-outreach.ts/lane, intention appraisal/action translation/outbox, post-turn action runtime, co-location wiring, startup composition, tests. Non-goals: automatic social quotas, repeated unanswered invitations, or source-specific transport.
design: Adapters create intent, not messages. Preserve the existing weighted-thought deterministic gate and free-time autonomy framing. A peer conversation cannot create a fresh candidate whose only independent cause is that same MI root; elapsed time or genuinely new provenance is required. Silence/decline should dampen rather than erase motivation.

title: Implement isolated personal and governed shared workspaces for fleet companions
description:
Implement the runtime contract documented by psfn-framework-3ury so a multi-companion installation can give each peer companion an isolated Personal Workspace while exposing a separately governed Shared Companion Workspace.

Why:
The current fleet supervisor isolates agent processes, companion-data directories, and Postgres schemas but forwards one inherited WORKSPACE_PATH to every agent. That makes journal, personal wiki, managed skills, modules, experiments, and other workspace files shared across peers. This violates the intended privacy/continuity boundary for companions with independent personal lives.

Scope:
- Define the canonical runtime layout for personal workspaces and one installation-owned shared workspace, preferably beneath the configured runtime root.
- Extend the fleet manifest/resolver or use a deterministic validated derivation so every CompanionFleetEntry gets one non-overlapping personal workspace path.
- Update supervisor spawn plans and per-agent environment construction to inject the resolved personal WORKSPACE_PATH, fail closed on missing/escaping/overlapping paths, and preserve single-companion behavior deliberately.
- Add an explicit, policy-gated Shared Companion Workspace surface. Shared material must have actor, provenance, revision, containment, and review semantics; default it read-only for companions.
- Keep Companion Library / Seed Bundle material versioned and separate from companion-authored files. Provisioning may seed a new Personal Workspace without overwriting personal work.
- Ensure shared files never auto-load as skills/modules or enter prompt/wiki/memory without CogSec screening and explicit policy.
- Extend backup/restore: personal workspaces belong in per-companion slices; shared workspace belongs in the cluster artifact.
- Add migrations, unit/integration tests, fleet launch validation, and documentation.

Non-goals:
- Do not merge peer personal data, memories, journals, identities, credentials, or runtime state into the shared workspace.
- Do not treat the existing site-scoped shared-world wiki as a general shared filesystem.
- Do not add an undocumented SHARED_WORKSPACE_PATH environment escape hatch.

Example target layout:
<runtime-root>/workspaces/personal/<companion-uuid>/ plus <runtime-root>/workspaces/shared/.

Current evidence:
- scripts/start-gateway-agent.sh forwards one inherited WORKSPACE_PATH to every fleet agent.
- companions.json has no personal workspace field.
- personal journal/wiki/skills resolve from WORKSPACE_PATH.
- docs/PSFN_PROJECT_CHARTER.md §6.27 and docs/multi-companion.md now describe the target contract.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Multi-companion launch resolves a unique, canonical, non-overlapping Personal Workspace for every companion and fails closed on invalid paths.
2. Each agent receives only its own WORKSPACE_PATH; personal journal, wiki, managed skills, modules, and artifacts cannot cross-read/write through the normal companion surfaces.
3. A separately contained Shared Companion Workspace exists with explicit policy, provenance, review, and safe default access; it cannot expose personal state or auto-load executable skills/modules.
4. New companion provisioning can apply a versioned Companion Library/Seed Bundle without silently overwriting personal files.
5. Fleet backup/restore captures each Personal Workspace in its companion slice and the Shared Companion Workspace in the cluster artifact.
6. Targeted tests, npm run verify:settings-contract where applicable, npm run verify:repository-hygiene, and npm run lint pass.

title: Run adversarial E2E certification and staged rollout for fleet SSO
description:
Summary: Integrate and certify the complete optional fleet-auth initiative against single- and multi-companion topologies using a deterministic local OAuth fixture plus Discord-shape contracts. Exercise one login across the fleet portal, multiple Gardens, and Companion UI with per-companion contact/role differences, Discord evidence, device pairing, self/co-subject JIT, privacy break-glass, logout, revocation, first-owner bootstrap, provider replacement/recovery, durable restore fencing, and feature-off parity. Adversarially test CSRF, provider SSRF, state/code replay, fixation, confused deputy, stale authorization, cross-companion leakage/IDOR, WebSocket bypass, audit forgery, and secret leakage. Stage behind explicit opt-in with rollback/operator setup docs.

Certification must prove gateway-only fleet-auth authority, strict separation of enabled trusted-host recovery from legacy token mode, safe first-owner bootstrap, current-plus-new provider authentication, exclusive opl1.15 non-subject disclosure, and monotonic durable-authority restore fencing. The canonical account-authority resurrection regression is: create backup; revoke/unlink provider/contact/role after backup; restore the old backup; attempt fresh OAuth; authorization remains denied until an exact trusted-host reapproval against current authority/contact state. The separate credential regression is: back up with passkey A; trusted-host revoke/replace A with B; restore the old backup; reapprove the exact account/binding/role; A remains denied for authentication, strong JIT, and opl1.15 privacy break-glass. B is accepted only from an exact non-restored credential-floor entry; missing/unavailable/mismatched verifier state requires a distinct expected-provider trusted-host plus live origin/RP/user-verification enrollment of a new generation.
design:
Do not require live Discord or production secrets in CI. Use deterministic fixtures for OAuth, user-verifying WebAuthn, trusted-host ceremonies, Ed25519 hops, Discord effective permissions, Hub assertions, and PostgreSQL backup/restore. The Discord evidence fixture matrix must distinguish: ordinary current ADMINISTRATOR with no hard veto may contribute to visibility/private-thread moderator evidence; ordinary member-specific channel deny denies; and current ADMINISTRATOR plus member-specific channel deny still denies under PSFN's hard-veto rule. A live smoke may be operator-run later. Preserve byte-identical single-companion feature-off behavior. Deployment uses exact-pinned dependencies/images and repository-owned configuration.

The restore harness must keep `TrustedHostAuthorityFloor` and authoritative `PasskeyAuthorityFloor` state outside the restored fleet_auth artifact. The passkey floor fixture retains current credential ID/fingerprint, public-key/RP/principal/provider binding, generation/status, counter/backup state, and replacement/revocation tombstones. Checkpoint post-backup account revoke/unlink and passkey A→revoke/replace with B, restore the older artifact, and assert all restored provider/link/tombstone/binding/role/passkey candidates are quarantined. Certification may promote an exact account candidate only after explicit trusted-host account reapproval; this never promotes a passkey. It must prove no automatic reconcile, fresh OAuth, session cookie, operator approval, account reapproval, or restored passkey row promotes credential authority. Current B may authenticate only by exact non-restored floor match; if that verifier is unavailable or inconsistent, only a separate expected-provider one-time trusted-host plus live origin/RP/user-verification enrollment creates a new generation, while A remains tombstoned.
acceptance_criteria:
Deterministic E2E proves allowed/denied paths across at least two companions and two principals, including per-companion bindings/roles, Discord evidence, authoritative Hub device identity, self/co-subject JIT, opl1.15 privacy break-glass, logout, and revocation. Discord evidence certification separately proves ordinary ADMINISTRATOR visibility/private-thread moderator evidence, ordinary member-specific channel denial, and the combined ADMINISTRATOR plus member-specific channel deny => deny; ADMINISTRATOR never grants PSFN role, trust, contact binding, memory, or other authority. No operator-side process can exchange OAuth, mint sessions, access fleet_auth, resolve private credentials, or sign gateway assertions. Feature-off token parity passes; enabled routine and recovery HTTP/WebSocket reject ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token. The independently revocable recovery credential alone cannot grant a role, reveal private data, or enroll a passkey; only the complete subject-bound matching-OAuth plus UV-WebAuthn trusted-host recovery ceremony may replace a passkey, and completion still does not authorize a privacy disclosure.

First-owner tests bind provider+companion+contact+owner grant and require matching OAuth, UV WebAuthn, explicit trusted-host confirmation, no-existing-owner recheck, atomic consume/audit; mismatch, replay, concurrency, pending-login self-elevation, passkey-only elevation, and post-owner reuse deny. Provider add/relink/replace authenticates current+new subjects; inability to authenticate current permits only trusted-host recovery, never approval-only relink. Routine memory/JIT is self/co-subject only; every non-subject owner/admin attempt denies unless the exact opl1.15 UV-WebAuthn privacy ceremony completes.

Backup→revoke/unlink→restore older snapshot→fresh OAuth denies. Restore/re-enable preserves the non-restored monotonic account and passkey floors, advances the account restore checkpoint and auth epoch before listen, invalidates ephemeral authority, quarantines all restored durable provider/link/tombstone/binding/role/passkey candidates, merges later account and credential revocations, and requires exact trusted-host account reapproval against current state before account promotion. That reapproval never promotes a passkey. A deterministic backup-with-A→trusted-host-revoke/replace-with-B→restore-old-snapshot→account/binding/role-reapproval fixture proves A is denied before and after reapproval for authentication, strong JIT, and opl1.15 privacy break-glass. B works only from an exact current non-restored floor entry; a missing, unavailable, or mismatched verifier denies until the distinct expected-provider trusted-host plus live origin/RP/user-verification enrollment creates a new generation, after which A remains denied. Tests cover stale generation, unavailable floor, concurrent promotion/login/enrollment, restored tombstone rollback, unchanged pepper, role use before reapproval, and restored credential use.

Ed25519 hop fixtures cover key rotation/revocation, operator-vs-agent audience, canonical query/resource/action/body binding, parent decisions, and atomic idempotent replay. Threat suites cover CSRF, provider SSRF, state/code replay, fixation, confused deputy, stale/private-thread Discord evidence and the ADMINISTRATOR-plus-member-deny hard veto, cross-companion IDOR/enumeration, WebSocket bypass, audit forgery, privacy projection staleness, and secret leakage. Secrets never appear in logs, URLs, browser storage, diagnostics, backups, or prompts. Lint, build, settings contract, repository hygiene, same-snapshot backup/restore, targeted suites, Companion UI, multi-companion E2E, and Helm checks pass; staged smoke/rollback are documented.

title: Enforce subject-scoped JIT access to sensitive memories per companion
description:
Summary: Extend Garden memory redaction/elevation from anonymous per-browser grants to authenticated principal-aware grants scoped to one companion and the correct memory subjects. Routine visibility and JIT grants exist only for a proven self/co-subject relationship under policy. Owner/admin/member role never authorizes a non-subject memory or profile. Every owner/admin non-subject disclosure is exclusively opl1.15 privacy break-glass with trusted ingress, an identified principal, user-verifying WebAuthn, exact action/resource/reason, short expiry, single-use confirmation, and audit. Intimate/confidential self/co-subject bodies remain redacted until their matching JIT grant. Multi-contact, third-party, companion-private/reflection, shared-room, ambiguous/unattributed, and derived artifacts fail closed and cannot leak through IDs, snippets, counts, exports, prompts, telemetry, embeddings, or bulk operations.

Authorization cannot trust a classification row only because it was current at creation. Bind every grant/use to current memory revision, classifier version, and evidence digest or re-evaluate transactionally. Subject-affecting create/update/repair/restore and contact lifecycle changes recompute/invalidate before visibility; stale/missing projection hides.
design: Build on AdminMemoryBodyGate and the shared SQL-aware subject-classification projection rather than a parallel viewer. Replace string-only browser keys with authorization context containing principal, session, companion, self/co-subject set, action, resource, assurance, purpose, versions, and expiry. Never equate memory contactId alone with subject classification. The routine viewer relation is exactly self/co_subject/other/none: self/co_subject may proceed under sensitivity/JIT policy; other, ambiguous, multi-subject/shared-room, companion-private, and none deny. Route every deliberate non-subject reveal only to opl1.15; a routine JIT grant can never encode or upgrade to non-subject authority.
acceptance_criteria:
Policy fixtures cover self, co-subject, other, owner/admin-other, multi-subject, shared-room, companion-private/internal, ambiguous/unattributed, and profile artifacts across roles/sessions. Routine access/JIT succeeds only for current proven self/co-subject scope. Owner/admin status, ordinary JIT, Discord approval, and trusted-host recovery never reveal non-subject memory/profile; every non-subject attempt either denies or enters only opl1.15 privacy break-glass with UV WebAuthn and exact audited target.

No body, ID existence, count, snippet, embedding, export, prompt preview, telemetry, or bulk/update result leaks without matching current authorization. Grants bind companion, principal, browser session, subject/action/resource, memory revision, classifier version, and evidence digest. Create/update/repair/restore/contact merge/delete recomputes or invalidates in the same transaction; failure/stale/missing state hides. Bulk mutation/export preauthorizes all targets atomically and one inaccessible/stale target denies without revealing which/count. Expiry, logout, authority/auth epoch, session/role/provider/contact revocation, and restore invalidate grants. Audit records actor/purpose/revision without content. Memory, disposable-Postgres transaction/race, Garden E2E, build, and mandatory lint pass.

title: Implement JIT step-up approvals with passkeys and bounded Discord challenges
description:
Summary: Implement PSFN-controlled fresh authorization for sensitive actions. Discord OAuth login and the mfa_enabled profile flag do not prove a fresh OTP, because Discord exposes no documented OAuth API for PSFN to invoke or validate the users current OTP. Use WebAuthn/passkeys as the strong primary step-up mechanism. Optionally support a short-lived, single-use approval challenge delivered to the already verified Discord identity as possession evidence for lower-assurance deployments, clearly labeled and policy-selectable. Bind approvals to principal, session, companion, requested capability, target subject/scope, nonce, origin, and expiry. Reauthentication or consent screens alone must not silently count as MFA.

Adversarial correction: privacy break-glass requires a user-verifying WebAuthn passkey and trusted ingress; the lower-assurance Discord possession challenge may never satisfy it. Initial enrollment and recovery use a repo-owned trusted-host CLI to bind a one-time nonce to the expected stable provider subject, then require matching OAuth and RP/origin-valid user-verifying WebAuthn registration; enabled-mode legacy ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token is never accepted. Passkey enrollment/recovery creates or replaces only a credential and grants no contact binding or role. The distinct first-owner bootstrap additionally pre-binds companion, intended contact, and initial owner grant and requires explicit trusted-host confirmation plus a no-active-owner atomic check. Passkey enrollment, compromise, revocation, replacement, and recovery atomically advance the trusted-host-owned non-restored `PasskeyAuthorityFloor` before a superseded credential can remain usable; recovery also revokes superseded sessions/grants/challenges, bumps the auth epoch, and audits. Every passkey row imported from restore is quarantined. Account/binding/role reapproval is a distinct ceremony and cannot promote a passkey. Replacement B remains current only by exact match to the non-restored floor; restored A stays denied, and missing/unavailable/inconsistent verifier state requires a separate expected-provider trusted-host plus live origin/RP/user-verification re-enrollment.
design: Integrate with existing confirmation/approval and audit primitives. Record assurance method and mfa_enabled only as metadata. Challenges must be replay-safe, rate-limited, cancellable, and invalidated by logout, contact unlink, role revocation, session rotation, passkey replacement, or credential-floor generation change. The trusted-host-owned non-restored `PasskeyAuthorityFloor` is the sole source for current credential identity, public-key/RP/principal/provider binding, generation/status, counter/backup signals, and replacement/revocation tombstones; any restored `fleet_auth.passkey_credentials` row is quarantined and non-authoritative. Trusted-host account/binding/role recovery, exact passkey enrollment/recovery, and opl1.15 privacy break-glass are separate, loudly audited ceremonies. Account reapproval cannot reconcile or promote a passkey, the recovery credential cannot satisfy privacy assurance, and a passkey enrollment alone cannot grant a binding/role. Current replacement B may satisfy assurance only by exact floor match. If current verifier state is missing, unavailable, or inconsistent, deny until a separate expected-provider one-time nonce plus matching OAuth and live origin/RP/user-verification registration creates a new generation; restored or tombstoned A can never be selected.
acceptance_criteria: Passkey registration/authentication validates RP ID, exact origin, user verification, challenge/session/principal binding, credential counters/backup state, attestation policy, revocation, races, and an exact current non-restored `PasskeyAuthorityFloor` credential/generation/status match. Initial enrollment requires a trusted-host one-time nonce pre-bound to the expected stable provider subject plus matching OAuth and UV WebAuthn; enabled ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token cannot enroll a credential. Enrollment/recovery grants no contact binding or role. First-owner bootstrap additionally binds exact companion, intended contact, and owner grant, requires explicit trusted-host confirmation and no active owner, and atomically consumes/audits; pending login, passkey-only elevation, replay, concurrency, and post-owner reuse deny. Recovery uses its distinct trusted-host ceremony, atomically records the new current credential generation and prior-credential tombstone in `PasskeyAuthorityFloor` before superseded authority can remain usable, revokes replaced passkeys/sessions/grants/challenges, bumps the global auth epoch, and is fully audited. Restore quarantines every imported passkey. Account/binding/role reapproval cannot promote one. Backup with A→revoke/replace with B→restore old backup→account/binding/role reapproval leaves A denied for authentication, strong JIT, and privacy assurance before and after reapproval. B remains current only from an exact non-restored floor entry; missing/unavailable/mismatched verifier state denies until a separate exact expected-provider trusted-host plus live origin/RP/user-verification enrollment creates a new generation. Privacy break-glass specifically requires a user-verifying passkey, trusted ingress, exact target/action/reason and single-use confirmation; Discord challenges, mfa_enabled and OAuth re-consent never satisfy privacy assurance. Optional Discord approval is labeled lower assurance, single-use, rate-limited, expiring and exact-action/target/session/companion bound for explicitly permitted non-privacy actions only. Logout, contact/provider unlink, role revocation, session rotation and key/passkey revocation invalidate challenges/grants. Phishing/replay/race/rate-limit tests, audit redaction, build and mandatory lint pass.

title: Add Discord human login to Companion UI while preserving device enrollment
description:
Summary: Let Companion UI obtain the fleet human session through Discord OAuth and attach the authenticated principal to Satellite Hub/PSFN sessions without asking the human to paste an enrollment token. Preserve a separately provisioned device identity for room/location claims: OAuth identifies the user, while device enrollment identifies the trusted Office/Bedroom/etc hardware endpoint. Support shared displays, explicit user switching/logout, anonymous/guest mode when configured, and reconnect behavior without leaking OAuth or device credentials into diagnostics. A logged-in user must not be able to claim a different room or device ID.

Adversarial correction: consume only a Satellite Hub asymmetric assertion with an explicitly configured issuer and public verifier trust ring. Raw browser hello claims remain untrusted. Bind the Hub assertion to the exact fleet-auth human-session attachment without merging human and device identities; define key rotation/revocation and audience/replay ownership across Hub, gateway, operator and Companion UI.
design: Replace routine token entry with one-time device pairing or repo-owned provisioning and an HttpOnly session. The Hub hello should carry authenticated server-derived claims, not browser-authoritative user/contact/place fields. Bind WebSocket upgrades to the SSO session and enrolled device, and namespace channels by the authoritative identities.
acceptance_criteria: OAuth login/logout works in the PWA while device enrollment remains separate. An enrolled Hub device assertion plus logged-in session yields distinct authoritative device/place and human principal/contact claims; switching/logout clears only the human attachment. PSFN validates configured Hub issuer, Ed25519 kid/public key, validity, audience, companion, enrollment version and jti; wrong/revoked/rotated keys, replay, stale enrollment and cross-companion assertions deny. Browser-provided device/place/contact/companion/channel values never become authoritative and forged claims deny. Shared-display and offline/reconnect flows fail safely; no OAuth/device credentials occur in browser persistence, query strings, snapshots, logs or diagnostics. Cross-repo deterministic fixtures from opl1.18, Companion UI unit/E2E, build and mandatory lint pass.
notes: 2026-07-16 security audit warning: Do not reuse or forward the legacy psfn-amica caller-authored X-PSFN-Author-ID/name/channel path when wiring human/device attachment. That path treats caller headers as authorship under a shared API key and conflicts with Charter authorship integrity for fleet sessions. The .9 ingress must derive human principal/contact only from the validated fleet session and device/place only from the verified Hub assertion plus server-owned enrollment state; all browser body/header identity claims deny.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: 2026-07-16 read-only audit confirmed enabled fleet mode is currently fail-closed, but four latent P0 integration hazards must be prevented: root-scoped Companion UI service worker/cache on the unified origin, Hub assertion replay not bound to exact human/session/socket attachment, tautological expected Hub binding derived from assertion/browser input, and reuse of legacy caller-authored satellite/X-PSFN-Author identity. Human actor and Hub device remain sibling contexts; device channel excludes human so switch/logout clears only actor, and human action grants intersect the physical capability ceiling. Decomposed into .9.1 subpath/PWA safety, .9.2 exact attachment ledger, .9.3 gateway WS/action broker, and .9.4 login/shared-display UX/E2E.

title: Promote the read-only fleet status page into an authenticated fleet portal
description: Summary: The current fleet-level implementation in src/boundary/gateway/fleet-status.ts is a loopback-only read-only HTML/JSON status page, not a fleet Garden. Build an authenticated fleet portal on the unified origin that lists only companions the principal may access, provides companion switching and deep links, shows connection/health posture, and supports fleet-safe logout/session management. Keep operational status read-only unless a later explicit fleet-management capability authorizes an action. Preserve the existing loopback health surface for operators or deliberately consolidate it behind the new implementation without weakening startup or network boundaries.
design: Reuse the gateway connection registry and fleet manifest. The portal is fleet-owned and must not read companion-private stores directly. It should aggregate bounded status and links, not become a god admin service. Include accessible loading, denied, partial-outage, and headless-companion states.
