acceptance_criteria: Authenticated users see only authorized companions and correct health/link state; unauthorized companion IDs and metadata are not enumerable; partial fleet outages do not break login/logout; headless companions render honestly; no fleet write action exists without a separately declared capability; current loopback/status JSON behavior is preserved or migrated with compatibility explicitly named in the live alpha boundary; UI, route, multi-companion E2E, build, and lint tests pass.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: 2026-07-16 read-only audit confirmed the current loopback fleet-status page is an operator surface with full manifest/ports/timestamps/reasons and must not be reused as portal data. New server-side batch projection is mandatory: authenticate session, read all current per-companion grants consistently, intersect manifest+connection snapshot, serialize only authorized coarse data, and reauthorize every stateless destination. Decomposed into .8.1 authorized projection, .8.2 authenticated portal/routes, .8.3 loopback compatibility hardening, and .8.4 production origin/E2E. No portal writes or client-side filtering; unknown and unauthorized targets remain indistinguishable.

title: Serve fleet-wide SSO through one trusted HTTPS origin
description:
Summary: Provide one stable HTTPS origin and routing model through which a single PSFN session can reach the fleet portal, each authorized companion Garden, and Companion UI. Avoid cross-port token copying and browser-readable bearer credentials. Route paths or subdomains must preserve companion identity and audience binding, prevent open redirects, and prevent one companion service from minting or interpreting another companion session. Existing direct per-Garden ports may remain local/internal operational endpoints but should not become the public SSO contract. Include reverse-proxy and Kubernetes/systemd deployment ownership under repository-controlled configuration.

Adversarial correction: the internal principal assertion is a concrete hop-specific Ed25519 request-capability protocol, not a generic typed assertion. Bind the canonical validated query/resource selector as well as method/path/body. Operator assertions cannot be forwarded to agents; downstream agent calls require a broker-authorized child assertion. Define public-key distribution/rotation/revocation and atomic idempotent replay consumption.
design:
Prefer a path-routed origin such as /fleet, /companions/{id}/garden, and /companion-ui, with validation by the gateway-owned fleet-auth broker at the boundary and a typed principal assertion over authenticated internal transport. Rotate the opaque session ID after OAuth callback and elevation. Use CSRF tokens for state changes and strict trusted-proxy handling.

Gateway signs with a private Ed25519 key resolved only in gateway mode; operator/agent receive a strict public verifier key ring.
Use aud=operator:<companionId> for ingress-to-operator. For an operator-to-agent call, the operator exchanges the parent decision over authenticated control-plane transport for aud=agent:<companionId>; the broker reauthorizes the exact child action/resource.
Canonical request targets include method, normalized path, duplicate-rejecting normalized query, compiled action/resource selector, body digest, audience, companion, request/decision/parent IDs, jti and lifetime.
Each audience consumes jti transactionally; an identical transport retry returns the recorded consume result, while changed or cross-audience reuse denies.
acceptance_criteria: One login reaches only authorized companions and unknown routes/actions/queries deny before forwarding. Ed25519 fixtures prove valid signatures and reject forged, unknown/revoked kid, wrong issuer, expired/not-yet-valid, wrong audience/companion, changed method/path/query/resource/action/body, and parent-decision mismatch. Operator assertions cannot authorize agent calls; broker-issued child assertions use a distinct agent audience and linked decision. Query canonicalization rejects duplicate/unknown/ambiguous selectors and prevents ID substitution on sensitive GET routes. Replay storage atomically accepts the first request, returns the same decision for a byte-identical retry, and denies any mutated/cross-audience reuse. Verifier-key rotation overlap and emergency revocation work without distributing private/HMAC material. Direct unauthenticated access, forged companion IDs, open redirects, host spoofing, callback confusion, cookie theft, fixation and cross-companion replay deny; WebSockets use no query secret. Repo-owned deployment, rollback, E2E, Helm/repository hygiene, build and mandatory lint pass.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: 2026-07-16 read-only implementation map confirmed enabled production remains bootstrap-only and Ed25519 assertion key config is currently unwired. Decomposed the release path into children .6.1 canonical route targets/catalogue, .6.2 Ed25519 hop capabilities, .6.3 atomic replay plus independently reauthorized child assertions, and .6.4 unified origin/deployment/E2E. Dependency order is .5.3+dut9.2+dut9.3 -> .6.1 -> .6.2 -> .6.3 -> .6.4; cycles check is empty. Direct Garden ingress, forwarded-host trust, operator-to-agent mTLS-without-user-capability, query ambiguity, and replay-result persistence are explicitly covered.

title: Migrate Garden from shared-token assumptions to principal-aware authorization
description:
Summary: Thread the authenticated fleet principal and per-companion authorization context through Garden HTTP, WebSocket, admin transport, service, and audit boundaries. Replace the current assumption that every valid admin token is one all-seeing operator with explicit per-route capabilities. In enabled fleet mode, legacy ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token is neither a routine credential nor a recovery/owner path; feature-off token behavior alone remains unchanged. Read-only health assets remain deliberately scoped; all private UI/API/WebSocket surfaces require authorization. Existing confirmation queues, contact approvals, settings changes, tool execution, memory operations, and cognitive-security actions need an explicit capability matrix. Never trust browser-supplied principal/contact/role headers.

Enabled-mode recovery is a separate trusted-host ceremony with an independently provisioned/revocable credential, exact scope, expiry, reason, atomic consume, and audit. It cannot reveal subject-private data, confer a role, or enroll privacy assurance. Per-companion Garden/operator code consumes only gateway-derived AuthContext and public-key assertions. Feature-off token mode remains byte-identical.
design: Extend src/operator/garden/server-auth.ts, server request routing, Admin domain services, transport contracts, and audit actor plumbing. The gateway-owned fleet-auth broker derives AuthContext; internal assertions must be audience-bound, short-lived, and authenticated. Avoid duplicating authorization checks in every page by enforcing centrally plus domain-level checks for high-risk actions.
acceptance_criteria: Every Garden route and WebSocket is classified and tested for owner/admin/member/guest/recovery access; unknown routes and missing/invalid contexts fail closed. With fleet auth enabled, bearer/cookie ADMIN_TOKEN and psfn_token cannot authenticate any routine HTTP/WebSocket route or confer owner; the old login endpoint is absent or refuses the token. Recovery requires trusted-host ingress plus an independently revocable credential and exact companion/action/resource/reason/expiry; it is single-purpose and audited. The credential alone cannot expose privacy data, confer a role, or register a passkey; passkey replacement requires the complete subject-bound matching-OAuth plus UV-WebAuthn trusted-host recovery ceremony from opl1.10. Feature-off mode preserves the existing configured token behavior byte-for-byte. A member cannot reach another contact body, settings, confirmations, contact approvals, tools or companion; admin actions keep explicit confirmations. Trusted AuthContext/ActorContext and linked decisions cross HTTP, WebSocket, transport and service boundaries; caller headers/JSON cannot override them. Targeted Garden tests, token-bypass tests, E2E, build and mandatory lint pass.
notes: 2026-07-16 Garden seam review: resolveMemorySubjectAccessContext is deliberately absent in production and therefore remains fail closed. When OPL1.7 wires it, resolve only from authenticated request-local principal context and add parallel-request isolation; never use a mutable singleton closure or map legacy admin/token status to a subject. Audit actor attribution must become request-bound ActorContext.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: 2026-07-16 read-only audit confirmed no currently reachable fleet-mode P0 because both Garden entrypoints abort before listen, but OPL1.7 is a P1 release blocker: all active HTTP/WS admission remains shared-token or process-mTLS, action vocabulary is too coarse, trusted request context does not reach services/audits, memory JIT is token/browser-session keyed, caller actor fields remain untrusted, and recovery has no exact one-use capability. Decomposed into .7.1 exhaustive route/action policy, .7.2 discriminated legacy/fleet HTTP/WS/hop admission, .7.3 request-bound subject-aware services/audit, and .7.4 exact recovery. Strong self-memory JIT remains deny until OPL1.10 and non-subject disclosure deny until OPL1.15; no mutable singleton AuthContext.

title: Bind Discord principals to contact cards and per-companion roles
description:
Summary: Connect a fleet Discord principal to existing verified contact channel identities independently for each companion, then authorize surfaces through explicit per-companion roles. Reuse contact identity verification/conflict machinery under src/core/contacts; never match usernames or create duplicate people. Provider subjects are fleet-global, while contact IDs and role grants are companion-local. A principal may be owner for one companion, member for another, and unbound for a third. First login always remains pending with no contact binding or role.

Implement the complete provider/contact/role lifecycle: first-owner bootstrap, ordinary first link after an owner exists, provider add/relink/replacement, provider/contact unlink, account recovery, principal merge, permanent subject tombstones, binding conflicts, contact merge/delete, companion removal, and atomic session/grant/version fencing. First-owner bootstrap is the only no-existing-owner path and binds a trusted-host nonce to expected stable provider subject, exact companion/contact, and initial owner grant; matching OAuth, user-verifying WebAuthn, explicit trusted-host confirmation, atomic consume/audit, and a no-active-owner recheck are mandatory. Ordinary provider change authenticates current and new subjects; current-subject unavailability forces the trusted-host recovery ceremony. Authority never follows username, approval alone, passkey enrollment alone, pending login, restored durable state, or a newly attached subject.
design:
Store per-companion binding and role lifecycle/version state in gateway-owned fleet_auth; contact cards remain in companion schemas and are accessed through the synchronous/durable lifecycle port. Discord room evidence may narrow entry but cannot manufacture a contact binding or role; companion trustLevel remains distinct from operator role.

First-owner bootstrap atomically creates/activates only the pre-bound contact binding and owner grant after all ceremony checks. Later grants use ordinary privileged policy. Provider replacement requires both provider authentications plus WebAuthn for privileged principals and explicit approval; if current authentication is unavailable, only trusted-host recovery may substitute and it must fence old authority first. Restore/re-enable imports durable subjects/bindings/roles as quarantined/suspended and no lifecycle lookup may activate them until trusted-host reapproval against current provider and companion/contact state.
acceptance_criteria:
Stable provider IDs resolve per companion only after an explicit valid binding. First login is pending/no-role, and passkey enrollment or approval cannot self-elevate. First-owner bootstrap binds expected provider+companion+contact+owner grant, requires matching OAuth, user-verifying WebAuthn, explicit trusted-host confirmation, atomic consume/audit, and no active owner; mismatch, replay, concurrent bootstrap, or reuse after owner creation denies. Later owner/admin grants use ordinary privileged capability policy.

Ordinary add/relink/replacement authenticates current and new provider subjects, requires WebAuthn for privileged principals, checks conflicts, and records approval; inability to authenticate current permits only audited trusted-host recovery, never approval-only relink. Historical provider subjects are permanently unique/tombstoned and cannot move principals. Provider/contact unlink, principal/contact merge/delete, companion removal, and role change atomically fence sessions/grants/evidence and suspend conflicts. Restored provider/link/binding/role candidates stay quarantined until exact trusted-host reapproval against the current authority floor and current companion/contact state. Unknown actions, unbound/conflicting identities, cross-companion ID collisions, stale generations, and spoofed headers deny. Audit records principal, provider, companion, contact, role, ceremony, versions, and decision without secrets. Transaction/race/restore tests, build, and mandatory lint pass.
notes:
2026-07-16 implementation audit: Complete .5 in two stages to break the semantic .5/.6/.10 cycle without duplicating WebAuthn policy. Stage 1 (.5-core) owns the per-companion authorization resolver plus binding/role/contact/provider lifecycle and fencing; it unblocks .6. Then .6 provides the unified origin and signed request authority; existing bead opl1.10 remains the sole strong-assurance/WebAuthn implementation. Stage 2 (.5-final) wires first-owner/relink/recovery flows through opl1.10 and completes required audit/race coverage before .5 closes. Current foundations are first-login pending/no-role, first-owner SQL, provider revocation, and restore reapproval; production resolver, ordinary lifecycle, completion routes, and contact lifecycle bridge remain missing.
2026-07-16 dual read-only feature-HEAD audit at b349ae17: no current P0 or reachable authorization bypass; enabled production is explicitly bootstrap-only and fail-closed. P1 release blockers are the absent per-companion authorization resolver, absent ordinary atomic provider/contact/role lifecycle, absent durable exact-contact bridge, unmodelled principal-merge/companion-removal semantics, unreachable first-owner/recovery/reapproval composition, and incomplete structured allow/deny audit. Verified foundations: first login pending/no-role, single-use epoch-bound OAuth state, exact first-owner SQL, permanent provider tombstones, single-provider broad revocation fencing, restore quarantine/reapproval, bounded gateway persistence, and enabled-mode rejection of legacy surfaces. Tracker graph repaired to represent .5-core (.5.1/.5.2/.5.3) -> .6 -> .10 -> new .5.4 final ceremonies, avoiding the prior semantic cycle while keeping the parent open until final composition.

title: Derive bounded Discord guild, role, and room-access evidence
description: Summary: Use consented Discord guild membership and current-guild-member role data as bounded evidence for which configured PSFN companion or room surfaces a principal may enter. Guild membership alone is not channel membership. A complete current bot-observed Discord effective-permission calculation is mandatory: combine the stable Discord user ID and current guild roles with the bot-observed guild, channel, overwrite, and thread inputs required by official Discord permission precedence. Only after that calculation proves visibility may PSFN-owned mappings from Discord guild/channel IDs to companion rooms narrow the result. Explicit configured role rules, a PSFN role, or any other PSFN authorization can never substitute for missing Discord evidence or widen the Discord result. A member-specific channel deny is a PSFN hard evidence veto even when Discord ADMINISTRATOR would bypass channel overwrites under Discord semantics; missing or unknown overwrite input, expired evidence, bot absence, removed membership, or other incomplete permission input also denies deterministically. For a private thread, lack of both explicit current thread membership and current MANAGE_THREADS denies. When no member-specific deny exists, current Discord ADMINISTRATOR may otherwise contribute to the computed Discord visibility result and private-thread moderator evidence, but it never grants PSFN role, trust, contact binding, memory access, or other PSFN authority. Keep evidence TTL-bound and refresh or revoke it when provider membership or observed permission inputs change. Never mutate contact trust, memory sensitivity, or admin roles merely because a user shares a guild.
design: Discord guilds scope lists guilds; guilds.members.read returns the current user member record and roles for a selected guild. Collect the complete current permission input set through the bot observation path, including guild base permissions, channel type and parent, everyone overwrite, aggregate role overwrites, member overwrite, and private-thread membership plus MANAGE_THREADS status where applicable. Compute Discord effective visibility in official everyone-to-roles-to-member order. Apply PSFN's stricter member-specific-deny hard veto before accepting any positive Discord result: a member-specific channel deny denies even for Discord ADMINISTRATOR. When no member-specific deny exists, current ADMINISTRATOR may otherwise contribute to Discord visibility and private-thread moderator evidence according to Discord semantics, but it is never translated into PSFN role, trust, contact binding, memory access, or other authority. Treat missing or unknown input, bot observation failure, removed membership, and expired evidence as denial rather than as a policy choice. Store provenance, the full input and configuration digest, the native Discord permission result, an explicit member-specific-deny veto bit, the final PSFN evidence result, fetched time, and expiry. Run the PSFN mapping decision only after a complete current positive calculation; configured guild, role, channel, or room rules may narrow that result but cannot substitute for evidence or widen it. Reuse channels.json routing identities where authoritative without turning provider data into config ownership. Positive cached evidence is usable only inside its bound TTL and exact input/config generation; outage or uncertainty after expiry denies.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover member and non-member cases, current role changes, the complete official everyone-to-role-to-member overwrite precedence, ordinary member-specific deny, implicit VIEW_CHANNEL denial, private channels, private-thread explicit membership, private-thread MANAGE_THREADS access, lack of both membership and MANAGE_THREADS, unknown or missing overwrite and thread inputs, stale or expired evidence, provider outage, bot absence, removed guild membership, ordinary Discord ADMINISTRATOR visibility/moderator evidence, the combined Discord ADMINISTRATOR plus member-specific channel deny => deny regression, and multi-companion mappings. Evidence stores the provider subject, guild/channel/thread IDs, complete bot-observed permission inputs, native Discord permission result, explicit member-specific-deny veto bit, final PSFN evidence result, mapping/config version and digest, provenance, fetched time, and expiry. Any member-specific channel deny, including when the principal has Discord ADMINISTRATOR, is a PSFN hard evidence veto and denies deterministically; incomplete or unknown input, expired evidence, absent bot observation, or a private thread with neither proven current membership nor proven current MANAGE_THREADS also denies. Configured role rules and all other PSFN authorization are evaluated only after a complete current positive Discord result and can only narrow it; they never substitute for evidence, override a denial, or widen visibility. When the member-specific-deny veto is absent, current Discord ADMINISTRATOR may otherwise contribute to proven Discord visibility and private-thread moderator evidence, but it never grants PSFN role, trust, contact binding, memory, or other authority. No broader OAuth scopes are requested unless configured; targeted tests, build, and mandatory lint pass.
notes:
2026-07-16 commit 2ecb15d6 one-pass evidence: npm ci completed and reported the already-tracked vulnerable dependency graph; targeted command ran exactly once. fleet-auth broker suite passed 7/7; discord evidence runtime suite failed 9/9 because providerMembership was placed in the unavailable-method signature and shifted every later argument to incomplete_observation. The implementation corrected that argument order after the run and intentionally did not rerun per operator instruction. npm run lint then passed exactly once. Final corrected runtime path and PostgreSQL integration coverage remain explicitly unproven until the single full integration-branch pass; do not close this Bead before that evidence and blind review.
2026-07-16 blind static review rejected 2ecb15d6 with one P1: production evidence refresh exists only in the active OAuth callback. No role/guild/channel/overwrite/thread change listener, TTL renewal, startup bot-readiness recovery, or session-bound reauth signal exists. Positive evidence can remain usable until expiry and bot_absent/expired evidence cannot recover without a new login. Tracked as psfn-framework-ycse. Permission precedence, member-deny veto, private-thread rules, strict parsing, cross-authority store bindings, and non-conversion to role/trust/contact/memory authority passed static review. Final runtime and PostgreSQL suites remain required.
2026-07-16 follow-up 3b348c56 for ycse: focused lifecycle/runtime/DB 13/13 and build passed once; lint exposed 5 unnecessary-condition assertions corrected afterward without rerun. Final two-commit blind re-review pending; integration pass must prove corrected lint plus the original runtime suite.
2026-07-16 closeout verified implementation complete: commits 2ecb15d6, 3b348c56, 63632fba, 36d8833c, aef5b3b2, c8507a61, 527071ba, 6dcbe137 integrated at d92e1357, plus exact cleanup 117feb83. Current permission/runtime/lifecycle/store/broker code read; all discovered children closed; focused evidence, integration lint/build, first full-branch attribution, and final independent PASS show no P0/P1 or Charter issue. bd close is structurally blocked only because declared blocker psfn-framework-opl1.3 remains open; do not force-close or misstate that dependency.

title: Implement gateway-owned Discord OAuth broker and server-side sessions
description:
Summary: Add an optional fleet-level Discord authorization-code login owned exclusively by the unified HTTPS gateway's fleet-auth broker, separate from per-companion Discord bot accounts. Per-companion operators only verify hop-specific public-key assertions and proxy domain work; they never exchange OAuth codes, mint/rotate fleet sessions, access fleet_auth, resolve OAuth/session/pepper/private-signing credentials, or hold private signing material. Validate state and exact redirect URI, exchange codes server-side, request the minimum configured scopes, resolve the stable Discord user ID, and create a rotating opaque PSFN session. OAuth access/refresh tokens never reach browser storage, operator/agent processes, companion prompts, logs, telemetry, snapshots, or URLs. Support logout, provider revocation, session version/revocation checks, idle/absolute expiry, and secure cookies. Enabled fleet mode has no legacy ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token login or recovery route; recovery is the separate trusted-host exact-scope ceremony. Non-goals: operator-side broker, implicit grant, username matching, self-bot behavior, or treating Discord authorization as PSFN role/trust/memory authority.

A successful first OAuth callback creates only a pending principal/provider subject with no binding or role. Passkey enrollment alone grants no binding or role. The first owner is activated only when the callback participates in the one-time opl1.1 trusted-host bootstrap pre-bound to expected provider subject, companion, contact, and owner grant and completes matching OAuth plus user-verifying WebAuthn. Ordinary add/relink/replacement authenticates both current and new provider subjects; inability to authenticate current forces trusted-host recovery, never approval-only relink.
design:
Use one fleet OAuth app and start with identify, adding guilds/guilds.members.read only for configured evidence. The gateway-owned broker binds callback state to the initiating pre-auth transaction and allowlisted return target, performs PKCE S256 exchange, and owns provider-token custody plus all session rotation/revocation. Discard provider tokens after identity/evidence refresh unless refresh custody is explicitly configured and encrypted.

Route trusted-host recovery and first-owner bootstrap through dedicated one-time transaction types that cannot be converted into ordinary sessions by a pending login. First-owner completion atomically rechecks no active owner, exact provider/contact/companion binding, nonce, WebAuthn UV, and trusted-host confirmation before activating binding/grant. Provider replacement requires both provider authentications in ordinary flow; only the distinct trusted-host recovery transaction may proceed without current-provider authentication.
acceptance_criteria:
Gateway-only login, callback, session refresh/rotation, logout, revocation, denial, expired code, replayed/mismatched state, callback-origin mismatch, provider outage, and malformed response tests pass; no operator-side path can exchange a code, mint a session, access fleet_auth, resolve private credentials, or sign an assertion. Cookies are opaque Secure HttpOnly __Host- cookies with narrow scope/SameSite; mutations require exact Origin plus session-bound CSRF; no provider token enters a browser, operator/agent, log, URL, diagnostic, prompt, or backup. Enabled mode rejects ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token on every routine and recovery HTTP/WebSocket path; feature-off parity remains owned by opl1.7/.12.

First login creates a pending no-role principal/subject. Pending login and passkey enrollment cannot create a binding/role. First-owner bootstrap succeeds only for the pre-bound provider+companion+contact+owner tuple after matching OAuth, user-verifying WebAuthn, explicit trusted-host confirmation, no-existing-owner recheck, and atomic nonce consume/audit; mismatch, replay, concurrent consume, or post-owner reuse denies. Ordinary add/relink/replace authenticates current and new provider subjects plus required WebAuthn/approval; when current is unavailable only trusted-host recovery may proceed. Tombstone conflicts suspend and every lifecycle transition atomically fences sessions/grants/evidence. Targeted lifecycle/race tests, build, and mandatory lint pass.

title: Specify fleet identity, authorization, tenancy, and threat-model contracts
description:
## Summary
Define the canonical contracts before implementation: a fleet human principal identified by provider plus stable provider subject; per-companion contact binding and role assignment; Discord guild/role/channel evidence; browser and device sessions; JIT elevation grants; audit actors; revocation; and fail-closed behavior. Trace current Garden shared-token authentication in src/operator/garden/server-auth.ts and server-routes.ts, per-browser memory grants in src/operator/garden/api-routes-memory.ts and services/memory-body-gate.ts, verified channel identities in src/core/contacts, multi-companion topology in docs/multi-companion.md, and Companion UI device hello credentials in companion-ui/src/lib/api/auth.ts. Explicitly distinguish authentication, authorization, contact trust, Discord room evidence, device/location identity, and memory subject scope.

## Rationale
The current pieces are individually sound but use different identities and authority assumptions: Garden has a shared all-seeing token, memory grants are keyed to a browser cookie, contacts already support verified channel identities, the fleet has schema-per-companion tenancy, and Companion UI authenticates devices. A shared contract is required before OAuth or RBAC code so a Discord login cannot accidentally become contact trust, room hardware identity, global administration, or blanket memory access.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Keep one admin token per companion: rejected as poor multi-companion UX and incapable of representing multiple humans or subject-scoped memory access. 2. Treat Discord guild membership or bot roles as the complete authorization model: rejected because provider evidence is stale/partial, channel visibility is nuanced, and PSFN must remain policy authority. 3. Replace device enrollment with OAuth: rejected because a human account does not prove a physical room endpoint. 4. Treat Discord mfa_enabled or OAuth re-consent as step-up: rejected because neither proves a fresh OTP to PSFN. 5. Build a separate identity stack per companion: rejected because it recreates multiple logins and creates cross-companion drift.

## Non-goals
Discord usernames as identity, guild membership as automatic admin or trust, OAuth login as proof of room hardware, and Discord MFA-enabled metadata as fresh step-up authentication.
design:
Canonical decision (2026-07-15): fleet authentication is a gateway-owned security domain implemented by the unified HTTPS gateway's dedicated fleet-auth broker. Discord authenticates a stable provider subject; PSFN remains authoritative for human principals, per-companion contact bindings and roles, companion tenancy, device/location identity, memory subjects, authorization, and revocation. Persist fleet auth in a dedicated `fleet_auth` Postgres schema. The existing `shared` schema remains shared-world data. Gateway fleet-auth broker replicas alone exchange OAuth codes, mint/rotate sessions, run `fleet_auth` DML or migrations, resolve OAuth/session-pepper/private-signing credentials, and hold assertion private keys. Companion agents and per-companion operators have zero `fleet_auth` access and are verifier/proxies only.

Authoritative contracts and owners:
- `FleetHumanPrincipal { principalId: UUID, status, authnVersion, authzVersion }`: one person independent of provider/companion; `fleet_auth.human_principals`.
- `ProviderSubject { provider, subjectId, principalId, status, metadata }`: unique active `(provider, subjectId)`; Discord snowflake serialized as string is identity, username/display name is metadata; `fleet_auth.provider_subjects`.
- `PrincipalContactBinding { principalId, companionId, contactId, state, verificationProvenance, version }`: state is pending/active/conflict/suspended/revoked; contact card remains in companion schema. A contact channel identity/trust row is relationship evidence, not fleet authority.
- `CompanionRoleGrant { principalId, companionId, role, lifecycle, version }`: one active owner/admin/member/guest base role per companion. Config may narrow the compiled action vocabulary, never invent/widen it; `fleet_auth.principal_role_grants`. Role is orthogonal to contact trust.
- `DiscordEvidenceSnapshot { providerSubject, guildId, roleIds, optional channelId, permissionInputs, discordPermissionResult, memberSpecificDenyVeto, psfnEvidenceResult, provenance, fetchedAt, expiresAt }`: bounded room-entry evidence only. Preserve the native Discord calculation separately from PSFN's stricter veto/final result; the snapshot never changes contact trust, PSFN role, or memory access; `fleet_auth.discord_evidence_snapshots`.
- `BrowserSession { recordId, tokenDigest, principalId, audience, assurance, auth/binding/policy versions, idle/absolute expiry, replacement/revocation }`: opaque raw token only in `__Host-psfn_session`; server digest in `fleet_auth.browser_sessions`.
- `PasskeyCredentialAuthority { credentialIdHash, publicKeyVerifier, rpId, principalId, expectedProviderSubject, generation, status, signCount, backupState, replacement/revocation }`: the current WebAuthn verifier and its lifecycle live in the trusted-host-owned monotonic `PasskeyAuthorityFloor` outside restorable `fleet_auth`; authenticator private material is never stored. Any `fleet_auth.passkey_credentials` row is a non-authoritative projection/import candidate.
- `DevicePrincipal` is Hub issuer + stable enrolled device ID/version/assurance; `LocationPrincipal` is an enrolled device-place binding. Satellite Hub owns both. Browser hello IDs are untrusted requests. OAuth cannot prove a device/place; logout and device de-enrollment are independent.
- `JitMemoryGrant { principalId, browserSessionId, companionId, subjectScope, action, resourceSelector, purpose, assurance/challenge, policy/binding versions, issuedAt, expiresAt, revokedAt }`: exact, short-lived, revocable; `fleet_auth.jit_authorization_grants`. Routine grants authorize only a proven self/co-subject relation. No fleet-wide intimacy unlock and no owner/admin non-subject grant.
- `BreakGlassActor` is a scoped auth mode, not a role: credential ID, identified human principal when privacy data is involved, session, assurance, reason, companion, exact action/resource. Trusted-host recovery uses its independently revocable credential only for an exact recovery action and cannot confer a role or reveal private data. Privacy break-glass is a separate opl1.15 path requiring trusted ingress plus an identified principal's user-verifying WebAuthn passkey.
- `AuthContext`: trusted-ingress request facts only (request/session/principal/auth method/assurance/audience/companion/binding/role/evidence references/versions/CSRF/expiry), never provider token or cookie secret.
- `ActorContext`: audit-safe discriminated human/break_glass/device/companion/system actor with stable IDs, assurance and correlation; never caller-supplied actor strings.

Memory subject is intrinsic and separate from viewer relation. Canonical classification is one of single_contact(contactId,evidence), multiple_contacts(contactIds,evidence), shared_room(roomId,contactIds), companion_private(reflection|internal|system|shard), unbound_person(labelHash?), unattributed, or ambiguous(candidateContactIds,reasons). Viewer relation is derived separately as self/co_subject/other/none. `provenance.subjectContactId` and episodic participant IDs are stronger evidence. Speaker/source contact/room participation alone does not prove subject. Missing, contradictory, stale, or classifier-version-mismatched evidence becomes ambiguous, never permissive. Store a versioned per-companion classification projection plus subject-contact rows for SQL-safe list/detail/search/count/export/bulk filtering; missing projection rows are hidden. New writes classify transactionally; rollout backfills before enforcement. `ContactProfileArtifact.contactId` is a canonical single-contact subject.

Deny-by-default authorization ceiling (owner-file policy may only narrow):
- Anonymous: callback/static/bounded health only; no fleet/companion/memory/admin data.
- Guest: authorized companion metadata and configured room entry only with fresh Discord evidence plus enrolled device; no Garden or memory bodies.
- Member: own contact/profile; low-sensitivity single-subject self memory; intimate/confidential self memory only with JIT; no other/multi-subject/ambiguous/companion-private bodies; no admin actions.
- Admin: bounded operational routes for that companion; own-subject memory as above; another subject remains denied; tool/settings actions require explicit compiled capability and existing confirmation.
- Owner: companion administration within the compiled capability ceiling; routine memory/profile visibility is still limited to proven self/co-subject data. Owner/admin status never authorizes non-subject content. Every non-subject disclosure is exclusively opl1.15 privacy break-glass; multi-subject/shared-room/ambiguous/unattributed/companion-private content remains denied outside that exact ceremony.
- Break-glass: recovery-only exact action/resource. Privacy override requires local/trusted ingress, registered passkey, reason, exact target, single-use confirm→decide, expiry and full audit.
- Memory mutation/export/bulk preauthorizes every target and applies atomically; one inaccessible target denies the whole request without revealing inaccessible count.
- Companion-private/reflection content is denied for routine administration. Holistic multi-subject/reflection policy remains opl1.16 future design.

Request boundary:
1. Unified HTTPS gateway authenticates a fleet session cookie or, only on the dedicated recovery endpoint from trusted-host ingress, the independent recovery credential; it resolves companion from the trusted manifest and derives AuthContext once. Legacy ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token is not accepted anywhere in enabled mode.
2. A central route descriptor maps normalized method/path to known action/resource/assurance; unknown route/action denies.
3. Strip inbound Authorization, Cookie, Forwarded, X-Forwarded-*, X-PSFN-*, actor/principal/role/contact/companion assertion headers before internal forwarding.
4. Authorize and write a central decision/audit ID, then sign a short-lived audience-bound internal assertion containing redacted context, exact companion, method, normalized path, body digest, request ID, jti, iat/exp and decision ID.
5. Operator/agent transports validate signature, kid, expiry, audience, companion, method/path/body binding and replay over the existing authenticated transport. Business JSON cannot override context.
6. Pass explicit `GardenRequestContext { auth, actor, authorizationDecisionId }` through routes/services. Link per-companion domain audit to the central decision. Denials before the companion remain centrally audited.
7. WebSocket upgrade validates exact Origin/cookie/audience/companion/route; context is immutable and version/revocation changes close the socket.

OAuth/session/CSRF:
- Server-side authorization-code exchange, exact registered redirect, high-entropy single-use state bound to pre-auth transaction + allowlisted relative return path, and PKCE S256. Production Discord endpoints are compiled constants; only tests inject alternates.
- Default scope `identify`; add `guilds`/`guilds.members.read` only when evidence mappings require them. Official sources: https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/oauth2, https://docs.discord.com/developers/resources/user, https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/permissions.
- `__Host-psfn_session`: Secure, HttpOnly, Path=/, no Domain, SameSite=Lax; raw token only in cookie. Separate short-lived pre-auth cookie cannot become session.
- Rotate after callback, passkey step-up, privilege change, or break-glass activation; transactionally revoke replaced session and its grants/challenges. Independent idle/absolute expiry.
- Every cookie-authenticated mutation, including logout, requires exact configured Origin and a session-bound custom-header CSRF token. SameSite is defense in depth.
- Provider access/refresh tokens never enter cookies, browser storage, operator/agent processes, logs, prompts, diagnostics or backups. Discard after identity/evidence collection unless refresh is explicitly enabled; retained tokens are gateway-only encrypted rows with key version. Discord `mfa_enabled` and OAuth re-consent are metadata, never step-up.

Discord evidence uses OAuth user membership/roles plus bot-observed channel state and the official overwrite precedence. Positive evidence expires at configured TTL. Provider outage after expiry, missing bot observation, removed membership, unknown overwrites, or unproven private thread visibility denies. PSFN adds one stricter evidence rule above Discord's native effective-permission result: any member-specific channel deny is a hard veto even when Discord ADMINISTRATOR would bypass channel overwrites. When no member-specific deny exists, current ADMINISTRATOR may otherwise contribute to proven Discord visibility and private-thread moderator evidence, but it never grants PSFN administration, role, trust, contact binding, memory access, or other authority.

Tenancy/lifecycle:
- Every binding, role, evidence, grant, decision, assertion and store API includes companionId; never look up a bare contactId fleet-wide. Route companion must be in the trusted fleet manifest. Fleet responses filter before construction so unauthorized companion existence is not emitted.
- Provider unlink increments authn version and revokes sessions/evidence/challenges/grants; username matching never relinks. Contact unlink/delete fences broker access first, then mutates companion state; failure stays suspended. Contact merge retargets only without binding conflict, otherwise suspends both. Role change increments version, invalidates caches/JIT and closes sockets. Logout revokes the human session/grants, not device enrollment. Device de-enrollment closes device sessions, not all human sessions. Shared-display switching revokes previous human attachment. Contact lifecycle requires a synchronous `FleetIdentityLifecyclePort` or durable outbox, not optional audit-string observation.

Configuration/persistence:
- Add strict system-owned `fleet-auth.json`, activated by one bootstrap topology flag (e.g. PSFN_FLEET_AUTH). Flag off+file absent constructs no broker/routes/schema/migrations and preserves byte-identical token mode. Flag on+missing file, flag off+present file, malformed flag, unknown/partial provider, duplicate mappings/roles, wildcard/non-HTTPS production origins, unknown actions, invalid TTL ordering, missing/inaccessible secret refs all fail before listen.
- Owner file contains schema version, canonical origin/callback, TTLs, narrowing role policy, guild/channel/companion mappings, modes and credential references; never secrets. Reuse CredentialReference/CredentialVaultPort for OAuth secret, token encryption, session pepper, assertion private signing key ring, and the independently revocable trusted-host recovery credential. Operator/agent config receives only the public verifier ring; privacy break-glass assurance comes from registered user-verifying passkeys, not a reusable token.
- `fleet_auth` tables: schema_migrations, human_principals, provider_subjects, principal_contact_bindings, principal_role_grants, discord_evidence_snapshots, oauth_transactions, optional encrypted provider_token_custody, browser_sessions, non-authoritative passkey_credentials projections/quarantine candidates, step_up_challenges, jit_authorization_grants, append-only authorization_audit_events. The authoritative passkey verifier registry and replacement/revocation ledger live in `PasskeyAuthorityFloor` outside the restorable artifact. Use a dedicated advisory lock/ledger and least-privilege broker role; companion roles have no access.
- Backup/restore explicitly includes `fleet-auth.json` and a separate `fleet_auth` cluster-schema artifact/manifest from the same snapshot; secrets, `TrustedHostAuthorityFloor`, and the authoritative `PasskeyAuthorityFloor` remain external and monotonic. A restored passkey row is never a verifier source. Rollback disables feature/config and returns to untouched token mode without down-migrating/dropping auth audit state.

Implementation seams: strict config beside src/system/config/companions-config.ts and startup-owner-files.ts; dedicated Postgres schema sibling to persistence/postgres/shared-schema.ts; backup cluster schema list in persistence/backups/service.ts and system-config-tree.ts; broker wired only in app/gateway/main.ts; contact lifecycle around core/contacts/contact-store-port.ts; gateway assertion/header stripping at operator Garden transport; AuthContext replaces boolean token checks at operator/garden/server-auth.ts and threads through routing/transport/service/audit; memory gate extends operator/garden/services/memory-body-gate.ts below every query/mutation surface; profile gate applies at faculties/memory/memory-store-port.ts; Satellite Hub owns authoritative device assertions.

Threat certification must cover OAuth state/code replay, PKCE, open redirect/Host spoof, provider SSRF, session fixation, CSRF, header/assertion forgery/replay/key rotation, cross-companion IDOR/enumeration, guild/role escalation, ADMINISTRATOR-plus-member-deny hard-veto, stale/outage/private-channel evidence, username replacement, contact unlink/merge/delete, device/human conflation, memory body/snippet/count/embedding/prompt/export/bulk leaks, multi-subject/ambiguous rows, simultaneous sessions, WebSocket bypass/revocation, audit forgery, break-glass misuse, secret leakage, malformed config, broker migration race, restore/rollback drift, feature-off byte parity, and Discord MFA metadata abuse.


Adversarial decision remediation (2026-07-15; one bounded pass):

Database and backup authority:
- fleet_auth has three distinct least-privilege credential classes: gateway fleet-auth broker runtime DML, gateway migration-owner DDL, and a dedicated repo-owned backup/restore coordinator. They are never derived from or passed through the companion POSTGRES_DATABASE_URL; companion agents and per-companion operators retain zero fleet_auth privileges.
- The existing leader-companion backup lane may continue companion/shared data work but cannot snapshot or restore fleet_auth. A gateway-owned or dedicated repo-owned backup coordinator obtains one PostgreSQL exported snapshot/consistent point for the fleet data family and the separate fleet_auth artifact, records both in one manifest, and is the only restore authority.

Internal request-capability protocol:
- Use asymmetric Ed25519 request assertions. The gateway-owned fleet-auth broker alone owns private signing keys; strict system config distributes only a versioned public verifier key ring (issuer, kid, validity window, status) to operator/agent verifiers. Rotation overlaps old/new verification keys for a bounded window; emergency revocation denies the key immediately. HMAC/shared signing secrets are forbidden outside the gateway broker.
- Assertions are hop-specific. Public ingress is exchanged for aud=operator:<companionId>. An operator needing an agent call obtains a separately authorized child assertion from the gateway over the authenticated control plane with aud=agent:<companionId> and a parent decision ID; it cannot forward or retarget the operator assertion.
- The signed request digest includes normalized method, canonical path, canonical validated query/resource selector, action, companion, audience, body digest, request ID, parent/decision ID, jti, iat, and exp. Query canonicalization is defined once and rejects duplicate/unknown/ambiguous selectors before signing.
- Each receiving audience consumes jti atomically. A byte-identical retry with the same request/digest may return the recorded consume result until expiry; reuse with any changed target, action, audience, query, or body denies and is audited.

Break-glass and feature modes:
- With fleet auth enabled, legacy ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token is absent from all routine HTTP/WebSocket authentication and from recovery. Recovery is only the repo-owned trusted-host ceremony using an independently provisioned and revocable recovery credential, exact companion/action/resource, reason, short expiry, atomic consume, and full audit. It cannot confer owner/admin/member authority, reveal subject-private data, or bootstrap privacy assurance.
- Feature-off token behavior remains byte-identical. Re-enabling retained auth state follows the durable-authority quarantine and monotonic-floor rules below before listen.
- All non-subject memory/profile disclosure, including an owner's or admin's, is exclusively opl1.15 privacy break-glass. It requires trusted ingress and a user-verifying WebAuthn passkey for an identified principal; recovery credentials, role status, and bounded Discord possession challenges are never sufficient.
- Initial passkey enrollment and recovery use a repo-owned trusted-host CLI ceremony that pre-binds a one-time nonce to the expected stable provider subject, plus a matching OAuth login and live user-verifying WebAuthn origin/RP validation. The ceremony atomically writes the new current credential generation and prior-credential tombstone to `PasskeyAuthorityFloor` before the prior credential can remain usable, revokes superseded sessions/grants/challenges, bumps the auth epoch, and records a full audit; failure over-fences. Credential enrollment/recovery alone creates or replaces only a passkey and creates no contact binding or role. Account, binding, or role reapproval is a distinct ceremony and cannot enroll, reconcile, or promote a passkey.
- First-owner bootstrap is a distinct one-time trusted-host ceremony. Before browser interaction, the trusted-host command binds a nonce to the expected stable provider subject, exact companionId, intended contactId, initial owner grant, expiry, and a no-active-owner precondition. Matching OAuth and user-verifying WebAuthn plus explicit trusted-host operator confirmation are required. In one transaction the gateway rechecks that no active owner exists and that provider/contact evidence matches, activates the contact binding and initial owner grant, consumes the nonce, bumps versions, and audits the decision. Any mismatch, replay, concurrent consume, or attempt after an owner exists denies. A pending first login and passkey enrollment can never self-elevate; later owner grants use ordinary privileged role policy.

Evidence and identity lifecycle:
- Discord configured guild/role/channel mappings may only narrow a fully computed current effective-permission result; they never override a member-specific channel deny, missing/unknown overwrite input, expired evidence, or a private thread lacking both current membership and current moderator evidence. The member-specific deny is a PSFN hard evidence veto even for a principal with Discord ADMINISTRATOR. With no such veto, current ADMINISTRATOR may otherwise contribute to proven Discord visibility and private-thread moderator evidence. Evidence binds the native Discord result, explicit veto bit, final PSFN evidence result, full permission/config input digest, and TTL.
- First provider login creates a pending principal/subject with no binding or role. Ordinary add/link/relink/replacement requires authentication of both the current provider subject and the new provider subject, current-principal reauthentication, user-verifying WebAuthn for privileged principals, conflict checks, and explicit approval. Approval never substitutes for either provider authentication. If the current subject cannot authenticate, only the trusted-host audited recovery ceremony may proceed; there is no approval-only relink. Stable provider subjects have permanent historical uniqueness/tombstones and cannot attach to a different principal after unlink except that exact recovery/merge ceremony. Principal merge/recovery atomically fences sessions, grants, bindings and roles; conflicts suspend rather than inherit authority.
- Subject classification is revision-bound. Every mutation, repair, restore, contact merge/delete, provenance/text/contact/provenance-reference/embedding change that can affect subject evidence recomputes or invalidates the projection in the same transaction. Failure hides the row. JIT grants bind memory revision plus classifier/evidence digest or re-evaluate on use.
- Durable account authority is bound to a monotonic `TrustedHostAuthorityFloor` generation and revocation/tombstone checkpoint maintained by the repo-owned trusted-host recovery authority outside the restorable `fleet_auth` snapshot. Passkey authority is independently bound to the integrated, non-restored monotonic `PasskeyAuthorityFloor`, which is the sole authoritative registry for current WebAuthn verifier metadata, credential generation/status, and revocation/replacement tombstones. Revoke, unlink, credential compromise, passkey revoke, and passkey replace operations advance the applicable floor before superseded authority can remain usable; failure over-fences rather than preserving access. Restore or disable-to-re-enable advances the account restore checkpoint and global auth epoch before listen without replacing current passkey entries. Every restored provider-subject/history/tombstone candidate, contact binding, role grant, and passkey row enters quarantined/suspended state; restored tombstones merge with and can never replace or roll back either current ledger. Sessions, JIT grants, challenges, and cached evidence are invalidated. Exact trusted-host account reapproval against the current provider subject and companion/contact state may promote only a quarantined binding/grant; it never promotes a passkey. Current replacement credential B remains current only from an exact credential ID/public-key/generation/status match in `PasskeyAuthorityFloor`, not from restored state. If current verifier state is missing, unavailable, or inconsistent, passkey authentication and strong assurance deny until a separate trusted-host expected-provider plus live origin/RP/user-verification registration creates a new credential generation. Backup with A→revoke/replace A with B→restore old backup→account/binding/role reapproval leaves A denied for authentication, JIT, and privacy break-glass before and after reapproval.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Shared validators define every principal/subject/binding/role/evidence/session/device/grant/AuthContext/ActorContext identifier; no authorization API accepts bare contact IDs, usernames, caller roles, or actor strings.
2. The decision records a gateway-owned fleet-auth broker as the sole OAuth/session/fleet_auth/private-secret authority; dedicated broker runtime, gateway migration, and backup credentials; per-companion operator/agent denial; serialized gateway-replica migrations; same-snapshot backup/restore authority; and no reuse of companion POSTGRES_DATABASE_URL.
3. fleet-auth.json ownership, secret references, strict flag/file matrix, unknown-key rejection, invalid-origin/TTL/action rejection, and feature-off no-construction/byte parity are specified.
4. Role/action/resource and memory-subject matrices are executable policy fixtures; unknown roles/actions/resources/subject classes deny.
5. Subject classification defines evidence precedence, ambiguity, revisioned projection/backfill, transactional create and subject-affecting mutation invalidation, and SQL filtering for list/detail/search/count/export/prompt/telemetry/bulk paths.
6. HTTP/WebSocket propagation defines trusted derivation, inbound-header stripping, Ed25519 public-key distribution/rotation/revocation, hop-specific audiences, canonical query/resource/action/body binding, atomic idempotent replay consumption, CSRF, explicit service context, and linked audit.
7. OAuth/session contract covers state, PKCE, exact redirect/canonical origin, cookie attributes, expiry, fixation rotation, token custody and Discord scopes/evidence TTL.
8. Device and human identities have different owners/sessions/revocation and a named Satellite Hub dependency with its own issuer/verifier trust anchor.
9. Provider lifecycle covers pending first login; current-plus-new-subject authentication for ordinary link/relink/replace; trusted-host recovery as the only path when the current subject is unavailable; no approval-only relink; permanent subject tombstones; provider/contact unlink/delete/merge; role change; companion removal; logout; evidence expiry; key/passkey rotation; and simultaneous sessions.
10. Enabled fleet mode rejects legacy ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token for routine Garden auth and recovery. Trusted-host recovery and opl1.15 privacy break-glass are distinct exact-scope, short-lived, audited modes; recovery uses its independently revocable credential and cannot grant roles/private data, while privacy requires trusted ingress plus an identified principal's user-verifying WebAuthn passkey.
11. Initial passkey enrollment/recovery is bound by a trusted-host one-time ceremony to the expected stable provider subject and live origin/RP/user-verification validation, atomically advances the non-restored `PasskeyAuthorityFloor`, revokes superseded credential/session/grant/challenge authority, and grants no binding/role by itself. Account/binding/role reapproval is distinct and cannot promote any passkey. First-owner bootstrap separately binds provider subject, companion, intended contact, and initial owner grant; requires matching OAuth, user-verifying WebAuthn, explicit trusted-host confirmation, atomic consume/audit, and no existing owner; mismatch, replay, concurrency, self-elevation, and post-owner reuse deny.
12. Discord effective-permission evidence follows official overwrite precedence plus PSFN's stricter member-specific-deny hard veto, proves private-thread membership/moderator status, binds the native Discord result, explicit veto bit, final PSFN result, full input/config digest, and TTL, and permits configured mappings only to narrow. The executable matrix includes ordinary ADMINISTRATOR visibility, ordinary member-specific denial, and ADMINISTRATOR plus member-specific channel deny => deny; ADMINISTRATOR may otherwise contribute to private-thread moderator evidence but never PSFN role, trust, contact binding, memory, or other authority.
13. JIT grants bind current memory revision and classifier/evidence digest; subject-affecting updates, repairs, restores and contact lifecycle changes cannot leave a stale visible projection.
14. Restore and disable-to-re-enable preserve the non-restored monotonic `TrustedHostAuthorityFloor` and `PasskeyAuthorityFloor`, advance the account restore checkpoint plus global auth epoch before listen, invalidate sessions/grants/challenges/evidence, quarantine every restored provider/link/tombstone/binding/role/passkey candidate, and merge rather than roll back current account or credential revocations. Account/binding/role promotion requires exact trusted-host reapproval against current companion/contact state and never promotes a passkey. Current replacement B is usable only from an exact non-restored credential-floor match; missing/unavailable/mismatched verifier state denies until a distinct trusted-host expected-provider plus live origin/RP/user-verification registration creates a new generation. Backup→revoke/unlink→old restore→fresh OAuth denies, and backup with A→revoke/replace with B→old restore→account/binding/role reapproval leaves A denied for authentication, JIT, and privacy break-glass.
15. Threat certification covers every scenario in the design, including gateway-only authority, first-owner bootstrap replay/concurrency, provider replacement without current-subject authentication, routine non-subject privacy access, feature-off parity, backup→revoke/unlink→restore→fresh-login resurrection, backup A→replace with B→restore→account reapproval with A still denied for strong JIT/privacy, unavailable or inconsistent passkey-floor state, and secret absence.
16. Child scopes/dependencies embody these decisions before implementation; .17 and .18 are blocked by this accepted decision.
17. Independent adversarial final review accepts the remediated decision; no code is required to close .1.

title: Add strict fleet auth configuration and shared principal persistence
description:
Summary: implement strict system-owned configuration and gateway-owned persistence for optional fleet authentication. The unified HTTPS gateway's fleet-auth broker is the only runtime DML client and the only resolver of OAuth client secret, token-encryption key, session pepper, assertion private-signing material, and trusted-host recovery credential references. Per-companion operators/agents are verifier/proxies with zero fleet_auth access. Mutable provider settings, canonical public origin/callback, permitted Discord evidence mappings, narrowing role policy, session/evidence/JIT TTLs, and modes belong in canonical fleet-auth.json with Garden exposure where appropriate. Persist principals, immutable provider history/tombstones, per-companion bindings/roles, evidence, sessions, revocation/version state, non-authoritative passkey projections/quarantine candidates, JIT grants, durable authority generations, and authorization audit in dedicated fleet_auth. Keep authoritative WebAuthn verifier records plus passkey generation/status and revocation/replacement history in the trusted-host-owned monotonic `PasskeyAuthorityFloor` outside restorable fleet_auth. Extend backup/restore manifests with fleet-auth.json and a separate same-snapshot fleet_auth artifact; secrets, `TrustedHostAuthorityFloor`, and `PasskeyAuthorityFloor` remain outside that restorable artifact. Non-goals: operator-side brokering, one-companion schema ownership, WORKSPACE_PATH, raw long-lived OAuth token storage when exchange suffices, inline JSON secrets, env fallback, companion-process schema provisioning, or enabled-mode legacy-token recovery.

Use three separate least-privilege credentials: gateway broker runtime DML, gateway migration-owner DDL, and a dedicated repo-owned backup/restore coordinator. None may flow through companion POSTGRES_DATABASE_URL. The monotonic `TrustedHostAuthorityFloor` records the current account-authority generation plus revocation/tombstone checkpoint outside restorable fleet_auth snapshots. The integrated `PasskeyAuthorityFloor` is the sole current credential verifier/revocation authority and retains credential identity, public-key/RP/principal/provider binding, generation/status, counter/backup signals, and replacement tombstones; authenticator private material is never stored. Restore/re-enable advances the account restore checkpoint and ephemeral auth epoch, quarantines every restored durable provider/link/tombstone/binding/role/passkey candidate, and merges current revocations rather than replacing them. Exact account/binding/role reapproval may promote only that account authority. Current replacement B remains usable only from an exact non-restored passkey-floor match; restored A remains denied, and unavailable or inconsistent current verifier state requires a separate exact trusted-host plus live WebAuthn re-enrollment.
design:
Follow opl1.1. Add strict config beside companions-config/startup-owner-files and a dedicated fleet_auth schema/migration ledger/advisory lock. Gateway fleet-auth broker replicas alone migrate and access it: runtime uses narrow DML, migration startup uses DDL owner, and the repo-owned backup coordinator uses backup/restore. Operator/agent verifier config receives only the Ed25519 public key ring; no per-companion process receives OAuth, encryption, pepper, recovery, private-signing, or database authority. Feature-off constructs no broker/schema/routes/migrations.

Coordinate companion/shared and fleet_auth artifacts through one exported snapshot/manifest, but never restore either trusted-host authority floor backward. Bind every durable provider subject/link/tombstone/contact binding/role grant to `TrustedHostAuthorityFloor.authority_generation`, and every session/grant/challenge/evidence row to `global_auth_epoch`. Treat `fleet_auth.passkey_credentials` as a non-authoritative projection/import candidate: gateway passkey verification and credential lifecycle consult only the non-restored `PasskeyAuthorityFloor`, whose current entries contain credential ID/fingerprint, public-key verifier, RP/principal/expected-provider binding, generation/status, sign counter/backup state, and replacement/revocation tombstones. Revocation/unlink advances the account floor; passkey enrollment, compromise, revocation, and replacement atomically advance the passkey floor before superseded authority can remain usable. Failure leaves authority fenced. On restore or re-enable, advance the account restore checkpoint and auth epoch before listeners, import durable rows and every passkey row as quarantined/suspended candidates, invalidate ephemeral rows, and merge restored tombstones without deleting later account or credential revocations. Promotion per exact provider/binding/grant requires the independently credentialed trusted-host account ceremony, current provider authentication as applicable, current companion/contact verification, conflict checks, version bump, and audit; it cannot promote a passkey. Replacement B remains current only from an exact passkey-floor match. If that current verifier is missing, unavailable, or inconsistent, all passkey assurance denies until a separate expected-provider one-time trusted-host ceremony plus live origin/RP/user-verification registration creates a new generation.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Feature-off flag+file-absent startup remains byte-identical and constructs/opens/migrates no fleet_auth component or route/cookie; every flag/file mismatch fails.
2. Enabled mode rejects missing/inaccessible gateway and trusted-host credential references, invalid/wildcard production origins, unknown keys/actions/roles, duplicate identities/mappings, impossible TTLs, invalid public verifier rings, and partial config before listen. Legacy ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token is not an enabled-mode credential.
3. Gateway fleet-auth broker replicas alone use the runtime DML credential and migration-owner DDL credential under a dedicated advisory lock; the repo-owned coordinator alone uses backup/restore. Per-companion operator/agent roles and POSTGRES_DATABASE_URL have zero fleet_auth access.
4. Strict tables/constraints cover principals, immutable provider-subject history/tombstones, pending/link lifecycle, per-companion bindings/roles, evidence, OAuth transactions, sessions, non-authoritative passkey projections/quarantine candidates, challenges, revision-bound JIT grants, durable authority_generation, global auth epoch, quarantined/suspended restore state, and append-only audit. A separate non-restored monotonic `PasskeyAuthorityFloor` owns current WebAuthn verifier metadata and credential generation/status/replacement/revocation history.
5. Owner-file read/write and Garden metadata expose no secrets. Only gateway mode resolves OAuth, encryption, pepper, Ed25519 private signing, and trusted-host recovery references; operator/agent verifiers receive only the public ring.
6. One repo-owned coordinator produces companion/shared and separate fleet_auth artifacts at one PostgreSQL consistent snapshot and records both in one manifest; the companion backup lane cannot read/restore fleet_auth, and restore never replaces or rolls back the non-restored monotonic `TrustedHostAuthorityFloor` or authoritative `PasskeyAuthorityFloor`.
7. Restore and disable-to-re-enable preserve both non-restored floors, advance the account restore checkpoint and auth epoch before listen, revoke ephemeral state, import every restored provider/link/tombstone/binding/role/passkey candidate quarantined, merge current account and credential revocations/tombstones monotonically, and audit. Exact trusted-host account/binding/role reapproval can promote only that account authority and never a passkey. No restored passkey authenticates, steps up, mints JIT, or satisfies opl1.15 privacy assurance.
8. Backup→revoke or unlink→restore the older artifact→fresh OAuth login denies, even with the same pepper. Backup with passkey A→trusted-host revoke/replace with B→restore old artifact→account/binding/role reapproval leaves A denied before and after reapproval for authentication, JIT, and privacy break-glass. Current B remains usable only from an exact current non-restored floor entry; if its verifier is missing, unavailable, or inconsistent, the system denies until a separate expected-provider one-time trusted-host plus live origin/RP/user-verification registration creates a new generation. Concurrent login/reapproval, stale-generation promotion, missing floor, unavailable trusted-host authority, and restored-role/passkey use all fail closed. Feature-disabled rollback retains audit/tombstone state without down migration.
9. Replica migration races, least-privilege denial, disposable-Postgres isolation, same-snapshot backup/restore, durable resurrection, feature-off parity, settings contract, repository hygiene, build, mandatory lint, and diff check pass.

title: Unified Discord identity, fleet SSO, and subject-scoped administration
description: Summary: Replace human-facing pasted tokens with an optional fleet-level Discord OAuth identity and authorization layer shared by Garden and Companion UI. One Discord login should resolve a stable PSFN human principal, link that principal to verified per-companion contact cards, and issue short-lived audience-scoped sessions across a multi-companion fleet. Guild membership and role evidence may inform configured room access, but Discord data must never directly grant PSFN trust or memory access. Routine memory visibility and JIT elevation are limited to a proven self/co-subject relationship; every owner/admin non-subject memory or profile disclosure is exclusively the opl1.15 privacy break-glass ceremony. Device enrollment remains distinct from human login so location and room hardware identity cannot be spoofed by an OAuth user. With fleet auth enabled, legacy ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token authentication is disabled for routine access and recovery; recovery is a distinct trusted-host ceremony using an independently revocable credential, exact scope, expiry, reason, and audit, and it never grants routine or privacy authority. Feature-off token behavior remains byte-identical. Current baseline: each companion can have its own Garden, while the only fleet-level page is the gateway read-only loopback fleet-status HTML/JSON surface in src/boundary/gateway/fleet-status.ts; it is not a unified authenticated Garden.
design:
Security boundaries: Discord authenticates a provider subject; PSFN owns authorization. The unified HTTPS gateway's fleet-auth broker is the sole OAuth code exchanger, session authority, fleet_auth DML client, security-secret resolver, and private assertion signer. Per-companion operators only verify gateway assertions and proxy authorized domain work; they never broker OAuth, mint fleet sessions, access fleet_auth, or resolve private credentials. Use a fleet-level OAuth application separate from per-companion bot identities and only stable Discord snowflake IDs for identity matching. Treat Discord mfa_enabled as risk metadata only. Strong JIT and privacy assurance use PSFN-controlled user-verifying WebAuthn; a bounded Discord possession challenge is permitted only for explicitly lower-assurance, non-privacy actions.

The first owner is created only by a trusted-host one-time bootstrap ceremony pre-bound to the expected stable provider subject, exact companion, intended contact binding, and initial owner grant. It requires matching OAuth, user-verifying WebAuthn, explicit trusted-host operator confirmation, atomic consume/audit, and proof that no active owner exists; passkey enrollment or a pending first login alone grants nothing. Ordinary provider replacement authenticates both current and new subjects; if the current subject is unavailable, only the audited trusted-host recovery ceremony may proceed.

Restore and re-enable use monotonic `TrustedHostAuthorityFloor` and `PasskeyAuthorityFloor` state owned by the repo-owned trusted-host recovery authority outside the restorable `fleet_auth` artifact. The passkey floor is the authoritative non-rollback registry for credential identity/fingerprint, public-key verifier and RP/principal/provider binding, generation/status, counter/backup signals, and revocation/replacement tombstones; authenticator private material is never stored. Restored provider/link/tombstone/binding/role data and every restored `passkey_credentials` row are quarantined, and current revocations merge rather than roll back. Account/binding/role reapproval may promote only that exact durable account authority and never promotes a passkey. A current non-restored credential such as replacement B remains usable only by exact match to the current passkey floor; missing, unavailable, or inconsistent current verifier state denies until a separate trusted-host expected-provider plus live origin/RP/user-verification WebAuthn re-enrollment creates a new generation. A revoked credential A can never become current through restore or account reapproval.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are implemented and integrated. One optional Discord login reaches authorized Garden and Companion UI surfaces across the fleet without pasted human tokens, while the gateway-owned fleet-auth broker remains the only OAuth/session/fleet_auth/private-secret authority and per-companion operators remain verifier/proxies. Per-companion roles and contact bindings fail closed; configured guild/role/channel evidence may only narrow access and never becomes trust authority. First-owner bootstrap binds the expected provider subject, companion, contact, and initial owner grant through a one-time trusted-host OAuth plus user-verifying WebAuthn ceremony; pending login and passkey enrollment alone cannot self-elevate. Provider replacement authenticates current and new subjects or uses only audited trusted-host recovery. Routine memory/JIT is self/co-subject only, and every non-subject owner/admin reveal uses opl1.15 privacy break-glass. Enabled mode rejects legacy ADMIN_TOKEN/psfn_token for routine access and recovery; feature-off token parity is preserved. Backup→revoke/unlink→old-snapshot restore→fresh login remains denied because restored durable account authority is quarantined behind a non-restored monotonic authority floor and explicit trusted-host reapproval. Independently, backup with passkey A→trusted-host revoke/replace with B→restore old snapshot→account/binding/role reapproval still denies A for authentication, strong JIT, and opl1.15 privacy assurance: every restored passkey is quarantined and passkey credentials plus revocation/replacement history are authoritative only in the non-restored monotonic `PasskeyAuthorityFloor`. Current B remains current only by exact floor match; an unavailable or mismatched current verifier fails closed until the distinct trusted-host expected-provider plus live origin/RP/user-verification re-enrollment ceremony creates a new current generation. Companion/device enrollment remains separately authenticated; security, integration, E2E, settings-contract, repository-hygiene, build, and lint gates pass.

title: Morning wake note has never fired on live: overnight idle-refresher notes and post-midnight chats trip the daily eligibility gates every day
description:
**Evidence (live, psfn-shard, image 0.1.0-kube-5d33c3bb, 2026-07-12):**
- Zero temporal_wakeup_morning entries in ANY session JSONL under /app/companion-data/state/sessions/ — the E7.1 morning wake note has never landed in production. Only temporal_wakeup_refresher notes exist.
- Agent log: zero 'Morning wake note injected' lines; registration shows `{"timingMode":"habit","source":"habit_fallback","effectiveLocalTime":"08:00","timeZone":"America/New_York","sampleDays":0,"fallbackReason":"no_recurring_sleep_gap"}`
- CADENCE TIMING IS CORRECT (correction from initial filing): daily-review fires 06:00 ET, weekly-review 07:00 ET Sun on live — ensureActiveTimezone() (agent main.ts module scope) writes process.env.TZ='America/New_York' before the scheduler starts, so the 'local' Date.setHours branch resolves ET. The wake task fires at 08:00 ET as intended.

**Root cause — eligibility gates deterministically suppress the note every day (temporal-wakeup.ts:388-398):**
1. `anti_loop_note_today` counts idle-REFRESHER notes (WAKEUP_NOTE_SOURCES includes both sources, temporal-wakeup.ts:69-72). The refresher fires after >=240min idle — i.e. nearly every night ~4-5h after the partner stops — so a refresher note timestamped after midnight ET exists on almost every morning, and the 08:00 morning wake self-cancels. Live example: refresher note 02:34 ET Jul 11 → morning wake suppressed Jul 11.
2. `partner_already_active_today` uses a calendar-date key: any partner message between midnight ET and 08:00 ET (regular occurrence, e.g. chat until 00:42 ET Jul 12) suppresses the note for the whole day. Live example: Jul 12.
Between the two, every day since the feature shipped has been covered — hence zero firings ever.
3. Observability: both skip paths log at debug only; production runs info, so the suppression was invisible.

**Latent hardening (same area, lower priority — fold in or split):**
- Scheduler.getCurrentSlotStart 'local' branch (scheduler.ts:64-119) uses process-local Date methods; correctness depends entirely on ensureActiveTimezone() having synced process.env.TZ before first tick and on V8 honoring runtime TZ change. Make it resolve via resolveActiveTimezone + Intl like rest-window.ts does, or assert the sync.
- Active timezone is env/code-default owned (active-timezone.ts:1, TZ env else 'America/New_York') — not settings-owned, no Garden surface; contrary to config-ownership doctrine.
- Habit estimator returns sampleDays 0 / no_recurring_sleep_gap despite months of history — check its scan surface.

**Scope:** rework morning eligibility so an overnight refresher note or a post-midnight chat does not suppress the new-day frame — sleep-gap semantics (partner idle >= minSleepGapHours AND last partner activity before today's wake slot), and exclude refresher-source notes from the morning anti-loop (or make the overnight refresher escalate to the full new-day note). Raise skip logging to info. Do NOT change note wording/sources or widen refresher behavior silently.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Unit: morning note injected when partner last spoke 00:42 local and wake fires 08:00 local; refresher note from 02:34 local does not suppress it; genuine morning-wake note from earlier the same day still suppresses (anti-loop preserved).
- Live: agent log shows 'Morning wake note injected' at ~08:00 ET and a temporal_wakeup_morning system entry appears in the active session JSONL; skips visible at info with reason.
