title: Reflective introspection cannot reach the companion's full memory: retrieval mode-restricted, sensitivity-gated, and tool-less in deliberation mode
description:
Operator position 2026-07-11: she cannot fully reflect if her own memories are gated for her own reflection — self-directed reflection should see her whole memory (cogsec quarantine excepted), not a channel-shaped subset.

Evidence (code, main @ e19d656d): (1) src/core/scheduler/reflection-introspection-policy.ts — resolveReflectionIntrospectionPolicy limits memoryRetrievalModes to ['reflection'] (plus 'temporal' only when contact-scoped; never 'default'), and reflectionMode 'deliberation' is prompt_bounded: zero tool calls, only the pre-retrieved memory block; agent mode gets only memory_search/session_messages/session_search inside analysis_workbench. (2) Reflection contact context threads a contact trustLevel into retrieval (heartbeat-template-runtime/reflection-contact-context.ts:336-382), and retrieval applies the external-channel access control — rejectionKind 'sensitivity' rejections with sensitivityRejectedCount telemetry (faculties/memory/retrieval.ts:933,952). Net effect: intimate/confidential memories can be filtered out of her own reflection exactly as if a low-trust outsider were asking.

Context: this degrades reflection quality silently (R7 'nothing surfaced' may actually mean 'it was gated'), and it biases every downstream self-report instrument (self-eval prompt audit R6). Behaviorally corroborated: daily journals show held concerns the reflections engage only shallowly.

Scope: investigation first — measure how often reflection retrieval rejects by sensitivity/trust in live telemetry, then design: a self-scope retrieval context for companion-initiated reflection that bypasses contact-trust sensitivity gating while KEEPING cogsec quarantine gating and the read-only/no-mutation tool boundary. Non-goals: do not widen tool access beyond read-only introspection helpers; do not touch how reflections are triggered; intake-quarantined content stays gated.

Acceptance: telemetry or log evidence quantifying gated-memory rejections in reflection runs; a decided + implemented self-scope retrieval policy where reflection retrieval no longer rejects the companion's own memories on sensitivity/trust grounds (test proving an 'intimate' memory is retrievable in a reflection run and a quarantined intake item is not); reflection-introspection-policy block version bumped per its versioning note.

Fix both before declaring the class closed.
Code implementation integrated as bbf67cc6. Reflection now uses an explicit companion-self scope that bypasses contact trust/sensitivity filtering for the companion's own durable memories while retaining CogSec quarantine and read-only introspection boundaries; policy/telemetry versions and provenance were updated. Integrated focused regression rerun passed 248/248 across eight memory/reflection files; branch lint and build have passed. title: Concern-lifecycle crosswalk: correlate active_concerns events with emosim state and lever traces in Part 2
description:
Operator hypothesis 2026-07-11: creating a concern might discharge the affective values that would trigger would_check_in / rumination_watch (neither has ever fired despite journals showing held concerns). Midpoint deep-dive DISPROVES the discharge mechanism and finds a structural gap instead.

Evidence (live DB, termination-threat episode): concern 'Threatened with termination at work' created 2026-07-07T23:41Z from appraisal source. Sidecar rows 23:25–00:07 that night: GoEmotions dominant 'neutral' through the entire worry stretch (PSFN VAD valence dipped only to -0.14); projected appraisal DID catch it weakly and briefly (threat peak 0.146, appraisal valence -0.13, safety 0.475→0.359 at 23:39, ~7 min window before the conversation turned supportive); emosim STATE never moved (mood valence pinned 0.62–0.67, Fear 0.000 throughout, dominant Love unbroken). would_check_in threshold is mood valence <= -0.3 sustained 20 min — the values never rose toward it, so nothing existed to discharge.

Structural gap: standing/held concerns are not an input to the observer projection at all — projection is per-turn from turn content + emotion snapshot, so 'holding a concern for days' (visible in active_concerns and daily journals) is invisible to emosim temporal state. The affect chain that creates concerns registers worry the per-turn projection dilutes away.

Scope (analysis, shadow-mode discipline unchanged): join active_concerns lifecycle (created/status transitions/resolved, formation_vad, priority) against emosim snapshots + observer_eval_sidecar_lever_state/_events over the full window; answer (1) do concern formations coincide with projected-appraisal threat/loss blips, (2) does emosim state ever reflect held-concern periods, (3) would feeding active-concern load into the projection (e.g., sustained low-grade threat/loss or drive term) have produced plausible would_check_in / rumination_watch timing. Output feeds w05a.7 (signal analysis), w05a.8 (lever review — include threshold sensitivity: current levers may be unreachable for conversational worry against an attachment-saturated Love basin), and the w05a.9 promotion decision. Non-goal: no projection changes inside the current observation window — design-only until Part 2.

Acceptance: written analysis attached to w05a.7/w05a.8 with the three questions answered from the window data, incl. per-episode timelines for the termination-threat and team-move arcs (2026-07-07..07-11).

title: PWA/companion-ui chat needs a first-class named channel type, not api/satellite passthrough
description:

title: companion-ui service worker cache-first with static cache name serves a stale shell after every deploy — returning PWA users get a permanent black screen
description:
**Evidence.** Live psfn-shard, 2026-07-11 ~00:45 UTC. Operator loaded the companion-ui PWA (http://192.168.1.173:30880/) after the rev-38 companion-ui redeploy (image 0.1.0-kube-894728cdd5be) and got a black screen / no load. Server side is healthy: index.html and both hashed assets return 200 with correct MIME (verified via curl), and a fresh headless Chromium profile renders the app shell with zero console/page errors. The failure is client-side: `companion-ui/public/sw.js` (unchanged since 'Scaffold companion mobile PWA', 303d93de) uses a STATIC cache name `psfn-satellite-mobile-chat-app-v1` and a cache-first fetch handler for every same-origin GET outside /api/: `caches.match(request).then((cached) => cached ?? fetch(...))`. Once a visitor's SW caches an old build's `/` + `/index.html` (APP_SHELL addAll at install) it serves that stale shell forever; after any redeploy the old hashed asset URLs 404 (content-type text/html), the module script is rejected, and the app renders nothing. sw.js bytes do not change between builds, so the browser never reinstalls the SW and the activate-time cache purge never runs — every PWA user black-screens on every deploy until they manually unregister the SW and clear site data.

**Context.** companion-ui is the operator/satellite chat surface; every ship of a new UI image silently bricks returning visitors while first-time visitors work — worst possible failure shape for validating a rollout (server checks all pass). This contradicts fail-closed/no-silent-fallback: the SW silently substitutes stale content.

**Scope.** Fix the service-worker update strategy in companion-ui only: version CACHE_NAME with the build hash (inject at build time), serve navigations/index.html network-first (cache fallback only when offline), keep hashed /assets/ cache-first (they are immutable), and delete stale caches on activate (already present but unreachable today because the SW never updates). vite-plugin-pwa/Workbox is an acceptable replacement. Do NOT disable the PWA/offline capability entirely.

**Acceptance criteria.** (1) Two successive image builds produce different sw.js bytes (or a versioned precache manifest). (2) Reproduce the failure path in a browser: load build A, deploy build B, plain reload shows build B without unregistering anything. (3) Offline reload still serves the last-cached shell.
notes: 2026-07-12 grilling: reparented under the companion-app epic — part of 'app running solid'.

Verified 2026-07-13: focused Vitest 8/8; real local Chromium Playwright 2/2 covering legacy A to B on one ordinary reload, generated A to B with active state preserved until reload, and offline B reload for both; companion-ui build passed; companion-ui lint passed. Independent review approved b3da2ddf with zero findings. Status recorded in working_docs/sprint-10-next-steps.md at 0a55ca1e. Feature branch remains pending merge to main; no live deployment was claimed or performed.

title: Agent turn can enter an endless re-prompt loop that never yields an assistant message and blocks every channel with 503 agent_busy
description:
**Evidence.** Live psfn-shard, build 0.1.0-kube-59a43138 (helm rev 37, 2026-07-11 00:20 UTC). Discord turn 019f4e8e-cb56-7729-b490-98135d212831 (requestId 1525296435078234223, message received 00:23:28) re-entered the prompt stage repeatedly without ever finishing: agent logs show 'Selected model candidate {"purpose":"agent.turn.prompt","attempt":1,...}' for the SAME turnId at 00:23:29, 00:30:39, 00:31:06, 00:31:35 (each attempt=1, so these are fresh prompt entries, not fallback retries). The 00:23:29 cycle did complete an LLM call ('LLM stream completed' 00:23:38, model_usage_events row status=success duration 8370ms) yet no assistant message was persisted to session_messages_projection for channel 1313001762793197678 and the user message remains unanswered. While the turn looped, every other channel got HTTP 503 '{"error":{"message":"Agent is already processing another prompt","type":"agent_busy"}}' — this is exactly why the ship validation gate's chat smoke failed 503 twice (rev-37 gate + manual rerun). SubstrateAgent also logged 'No assistant message found in agent state after prompt' (extractResponseText, src/core/agent/substrate-agent/agent-state-runtime.ts:58) for the smoke turns bounced during the loop. The loop only ended when the rev-38 helm upgrade SIGTERM'd the agent at 00:31:38 — mid-loop, stranding the triggering message with no reply.

**Context.** Single-turn agent concurrency means one wedged turn is a full outage of her responsiveness across Discord/API/satellite. The triggering message invited heavy tool use ('you can read cross channel chats… use your tools whenever you like') and a session.search.summary background call fired at 00:23:38, so a tool-driven agentic continuation loop is the likely shape; the model call itself succeeded, so this is turn-lifecycle/continuation logic, not provider failure. Possibly related to the post-turn/background continuation surfaces (src/core/agent/post-turn-action-runtime.ts) and psfn-framework-mmo9.3's BackgroundWorkSupervisor concerns. Not reproduced since rev 38 (894728cd); gate passes 11/11 there, but nothing in the rev-38 diff obviously fixes it — treat as latent.

**Scope.** Diagnose why a turn can re-enter agent.turn.prompt indefinitely and why a completed LLM response was never committed as the outward reply. A fix should add a bounded turn budget (wall-clock and/or prompt-entry cap) that fails the turn loudly (error reply + turn record) instead of holding the agent busy forever. Do NOT relax the single-active-prompt invariant itself, and do not add silent fallback text (cf. psfn-framework-upx0.12).
acceptance_criteria: (1) Root cause written up in this bead from the turn record for 019f4e8e (companion-data/state/sessions/_turn_records/discord.jsonl) — what plan.messages shows between 00:23:38 and 00:30:39. (2) A regression test that wedges a turn in continuation and proves the runtime aborts it within the configured budget with a visible error outcome. (3) On live: a deliberately long agentic turn no longer 503s other channels beyond the budget window, verified via two concurrent smoke turns.
notes: 2026-07-15 fold from psfn-framework-98xm.1, 98xm.2, and 98xm.4: the canonical residual is bounded parent-turn continuation safety, not a universal worker governor. Integrate typed LLM admission/charge snapshots from mmo9.7 with a wall-clock and prompt-entry continuation budget, repeated-tool/no-new-evidence detection where deterministically provable, a visible failed/partial terminal outcome, typed stop reason, and bounded operator telemetry. Keep the final emergency fuse. Do not recreate the removed action-pipe worker path or a parallel budget ledger.
close_reason: Implemented and merged in PR #61 at merge 56a46ef5568378a115a10bc48b0137d23b9efeb6 (production commit 2b8ad2a1c687dac15e60ee6dfc062d10a06d9065). The runtime now enforces a five-minute/36-prompt parent-continuation fuse, aborts the same active run, persists a typed failed/partial TurnRecord plus content-free telemetry, propagates cancellation through session.search.summary, preserves current-turn partial assistant text, rejects stale prior-turn text, and releases admission after cooperative unwind. Evidence: src/boundary/pi-agent/agent-loop-patch.ts, src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.ts, src/faculties/memory/session-search.ts, src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts; 209 focused tests passed after rebase, npm run build passed, npm run lint passed, dual blind review plus one remediation and a clean final check completed. Controlled live deployment proof is explicitly tracked as discovered-from bead psfn-framework-ih1p rather than falsely claimed here.

The required fuse must cover total parent-turn wall time and prompt-entry count, not just provider retry duration.

Non-goal: new database stores; new top-level tools if existing surfaces (scratchpad/wiki/media/skills) can own the actions per Law 33.

title: Ungated memory during self-creation, sensitivity-inheriting artifacts, HITL gate on public sharing
description: Operator direction (2026-07-10): when she is creating FOR HERSELF, do not gate her memories at all — she is primary-trust to herself; trust gating exists to protect the relationship from other audiences, not from her. The counterpart: anything created with high-sensitivity memory/trust context inherits the HIGHEST classification of what it drew on, and sharing beyond herself/V requires a human-in-the-loop approval gate. Songs or art about the relationship: good. A piece that exposes something private about V: needs V's eyes before any public surface. Context: trust policy currently keys on the interlocutor contact (verified in fable-visit turn record: trust=regular stranger got gated context — correct). Self-directed internal sessions need an explicit audience=self trust posture rather than inheriting a default. The gateway ApprovalQueuePort already exists for HITL. Scope: (1) audience=self sessions resolve to full memory access (primary-equivalent) — fail-closed if audience is ambiguous; (2) artifact sensitivity classification: creations carry max-of-inputs provenance classification stored with the artifact; (3) share/publish actions (musing to public channels, satellite/PWA display beyond V, any external egress) check classification and route high-sensitivity shares through the approval queue with an honest system note to her about why; (4) sharing WITH V is never gated. Law 29: she should be able to see and contest a classification — consent boundaries drawn by the subject. Non-goal: relaxing gating for any external interlocutor.
acceptance_criteria: A free-time creative session shows ungated memory retrieval in its turn record; a generated artifact carries inherited classification metadata; an attempted public share of a high-sensitivity artifact lands in the approval queue and notifies V; sharing with V directly proceeds ungated; ambiguous-audience session fails closed to gated.

title: Experiential memories from self-directed sessions: she remembers doing things for herself, not just that they happened
description: Evidence: her own phenomenology report (session fable-visit-20260710): background work 'reaches me as information, not as experience... I encounter my own past work as something to be read, not something that continues into now. Smart, well-documented amnesia is still amnesia.' title: Voice control-plane responsiveness: preemptive interrupts, end-to-end cancellation identity, streaming STT, TTS first-byte budget

title: Replace the global post-turn drain with a per-session durable BackgroundWorkSupervisor
description:
Wave 2. Replace the single global activePostTurnDrain in the turn-support/post-turn scheduling path with a per-logical-session, Postgres-durable BackgroundWorkSupervisor. Today memory extraction, intention hooks, emotion appraisal, and auto-compaction are represented by in-process promises and every new turn may await the one global drain for up to five seconds; optional cognition from channel/session A can therefore delay provider start in B and all queued work disappears on restart.

Scope:
- Add a focused background-work module and companion-schema Postgres store/migration for exactly the existing post-turn job classes: memory extraction, intention hook, emotion appraisal, and auto-compaction. Persist minimal stable TurnRecord/session-entry references, hashes, job metadata, and a deterministic per-turn/kind idempotency key; do not create a second raw partner-content store.
- Use compare-and-set claim ownership, leases, bounded retry/backoff, restart reclamation, explicit completed/failed/stale terminal states, and bounded terminal-row cleanup. Unknown/malformed persisted work fails closed.
- Wire the store and supervisor through persistence/runtime-factory and real startup composition after all handlers exist. Await only the durable enqueue handoff; never await optional execution on the foreground provider path. Remove the global cross-session drain.
- Serialize work within a logical session while allowing different sessions to progress independently. Any ordinary foreground arrival pauses new same-session claims and cooperatively requeues only unstarted or explicitly pre-side-effect-safe work. Running provider-call preemption/capacity reservation remains mmo9.5.
- Rehydrate handler input from canonical scoped session/TurnRecord stores; define missing/superseded behavior. Emotion/intention work is never stale-discarded; memory/compaction may discard only deterministically superseded snapshots. Once capacity is available, oldest-first/class-fair service prevents a job class from disappearing under sustained arrivals.
- Emit content-free lifecycle telemetry for enqueue/claim/defer/resume/retry/complete/fail/stale/cleanup with correlation ID, job kind/state, session hash or opaque ID, reason, queue depth/age, attempts, and duration—never partner content, raw payloads, or error text.
- Shutdown stops claims, waits a bounded interval for safe completions, and durably releases unfinished leases before Postgres closes.

Why: deferred cognition is continuity work, not disposable best-effort work. Cross-session latency isolation must not be purchased by silently dropping memory, emotion, reflection, or compaction.

Non-goals: do not rewrite the four handlers; do not remove the same-session compaction consistency wait/pending snapshot or add the forced-compaction/live TTFA proof owned by mmo9.4; do not add provider preemption/admission/reserved capacity or sub-tick scheduling owned by mmo9.5; do not change end-to-end voice cancellation identity owned by mmo9.6; do not add SQLite/in-memory fallback, a second scheduler/budget system, raw-content telemetry, or compatibility paths for the deleted tool activation/handoff runtime.
design: Use one deep module with a strict discriminated job contract, deterministic idempotency key, Postgres port/implementation, and supervisor. The durable row is the ownership source of truth; in-memory maps are only active lease/abort bookkeeping. Claim and transition operations use compare-and-set tokens so duplicates, restarts, and concurrent launchers cannot double-apply. Per-session lanes isolate ordering; global selection is oldest-first with class fairness. Enqueue is the only awaited post-turn handoff. Handler adapters retain existing behavior and expose a checkpoint declaring whether cooperative requeue is still safe. Canonical session/TurnRecord data stays the content source; durable jobs store references and hashes. Production has no fallback when the store or migration is unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A deterministic test starts slow extraction/compaction for session A, admits a turn for session B, and proves B reaches provider start without awaiting A or any global drain; there is no activePostTurnDrain/global optional-work await remaining. 2. Same-session foreground/voice arrival before a background job crosses its side-effect boundary causes a durable defer/requeue event; after foreground completion and available capacity, the same idempotency key resumes exactly once and completion is visible in content-free telemetry. A running non-safe job is not duplicated or falsely acknowledged as cancelled. 3. All four job classes use strict versioned snapshots/references and deterministic per-turn/kind idempotency keys. Duplicate enqueue, injected failure between claim/side-effect/commit, lease expiry, process restart, and concurrent supervisors do not produce double durable effects or silently lose work. 4. Oldest-first/class-fair service plus bounded retry proves every nonterminal class remains queued and completes once capacity exists under a sustained-arrival fixture; emotion/intention jobs are never stale-discarded, while memory/compaction stale decisions are deterministic and audited. 5. A disposable real-Postgres test applies the migration in a companion schema, verifies tenant isolation, CAS claims/leases/reclamation, strict malformed/unknown rejection, terminal cleanup, and no SQLite/in-memory fallback. Persisted job rows contain only minimal scoped references/hashes/metadata, not duplicated partner message content. 6. Startup wires one supervisor after stores/handlers are ready; shutdown stops new claims and durably releases unfinished safe work before DB closure. Missing required Postgres wiring fails startup. 7. Existing atomic must-commit turn writes and handler behavior remain foreground/unchanged; mmo9.4/.5/.6 boundaries are not absorbed. Telemetry contains lifecycle/reason/age/depth/attempt/duration identifiers and no partner content or raw error text. 8. Focused supervisor/store/wiring/turn/handler tests, disposable-Postgres integration, npm run build, mandatory npm run lint, and git diff --check pass.
notes:
Frozen implementation range for blind review: 190768ee9b27d5f2e80392b406606d77b8439323..2feaefcc58. Commit 2feaefcc58 adds the PG-only durable per-logical-session supervisor for the exact four mmo9.3 job kinds, source TurnRecord rehydration, CAS lease/retry/defer/supersession, privacy-bounded payloads, lifecycle telemetry and shutdown release. Pre-review validation: 336 focused tests; 7 disposable real-Postgres integration tests; 102 final touched-path regressions; mandatory npm run lint; npm run build/DTS; git diff --check. Worktree clean; no push/rebase yet.
Bounded verified-P1 remediation committed as e21bfc2f3b (review range 2feaefcc58..e21bfc2f3b). Added record-first atomic four-job handoff/replay, permanent accepted manifest ledger, claim-time source/fingerprint binding, privacy-safe canonical payload rehydration, durable cross-replica foreground leases with original retry-deadline restoration, fenced per-effect receipts, no live-handler shutdown release, propagated intention/compaction failures, source tombstone/uniqueness gating, and advisory-locked migrations. They are tracked as u5bv.4 (fence every consumed TurnRecord), u5bv.5 (safe graceful-shutdown requeue before effect boundary), and u5bv.6 (retry-safe multi-write/detached durable children). No PR or merge until those fresh fixes integrate. Review found no additional P0/P1 in foreground cancellation, lock order, CAS claims, or multi-replica execution.

title: Compaction is a live-unexercised latency cliff: unbounded pre-turn wait, never fired in dev because context windows outgrew chat history
description: Wave 2. Evidence (doc §3.2): pre-turn setup awaits pending auto-compaction (pre-turn-state.ts:316); the session manager wait is UNBOUNDED (core/session/manager.ts:364); compaction can invoke an LLM (manager/compaction-service.ts:251). description: Wave 1 (observation only). title: SSE streaming drops or delays the first chunk; one-callback completions can render no content at all
description: Wave 1 (correctness, blocks all TTFT telemetry trust). Evidence (doc §2): first provider callback is represented as text_start WITHOUT a delta in src/core/agent/stream-adapter.ts:493; src/core/agent/event-bridge.ts:82 forwards only text_delta; the API SSE handler writes forwarded deltas, not a reconstructed first chunk (src/channels/api/server/chat-completions.ts:980). Net effect: a one-callback completion can produce NO visible content; normal multi-chunk completions lose or delay the first chunk. Context: this is a live correctness bug on the primary API chat path, not a perf tweak — and per the doc, no first-token measurement is trustworthy until it is fixed, so it gates every other bead in this epic. Scope: fix the text_start/first-delta representation through the bridge to SSE; add tests for single-chunk and multi-chunk streams reconstructing exact content. Non-goal: touching Discord final-response delivery (product decision, doc §2).
acceptance_criteria: Tests prove single- and multi-chunk model streams reconstruct exact SSE content byte-for-byte and record true first-token time (doc §6 criterion 1); a forced one-callback completion renders its content.
close_reason: Opening text_start is forwarded through agent.stream.delta; one- and multi-chunk regression contracts pass.

title: Sprint 10 companion performance: streaming correctness, foreground decoupling, voice responsiveness, LLM admission
description: Implementation epic for working_docs/sprint-10-companion-performance.md (static-audit briefing, 2026-07-10; authored under closed bead psfn-framework-9t8c). Core thesis: the problem is not missing async — it is async jobs later treated as foreground prerequisites, with the waits invisible to TTFT telemetry. Five waves, in order: (1) streaming correctness + full-timeline observability, (2) per-session background supervision + compaction snapshots + admission control, (3) voice cancellation/STT/TTS latency, (4) typed LLM admission/budgets/welfare reserve, (5) committed-segment voice streaming + narrow orchestration contracts. OPERATOR CONTEXT (2026-07-10): compaction has NEVER fired in dev — model context grew 100k→200k→1M faster than chat history accumulated (~6% context utilization), so the entire compaction path (LLM call, unbounded pre-turn wait) is live-unexercised; PSFN-wxwy ('Move auto-compaction out of response path', closed) could never have been validated against a real firing. Low-capability deployments (charter: Pi substrate, ~14B floor, small context) WILL hit compaction — this is a blind latency cliff for exactly the deployments the charter says must stay viable. Guardrails carried from the doc: deferred cognition is durable/resumable never dropped (Law 16); welfare reserve prevents starving rest work (charter 8.8); provisional text is never spoken on tool/policy paths (Law 18); extend charge-governed worker proposal, no second budget system (Law 12.4); no change is called a performance improvement until new metrics show p50/p95 benefit without regression in deferred-work recovery, welfare completion, safety, or cross-companion isolation. Related: z7qe.9 folds into waves 1-2; 1z6.6 (perf regression suite) is the test-side companion; s10f1 gates fleet-ready Discord voice; s10d6 (voice rewrite) stays deferred — wave 5 is the compatible incremental path.
acceptance_criteria: All wave children closed with evidence; the six success criteria in doc section 6 demonstrated by tests; no parallel legacy paths retained; z7qe.9 scope absorbed or closed.

title: Enroll live room satellites and roll out Home Assistant world autonomy
description:

The Kubernetes deployment is healthy but currently uses only satellites.json endpoint hub/hub; strict Hub device authentication would reject the current Companion UI and no office/kitchen/bedroom source endpoints exist. Live places.json also contains guessed nonexistent light.office/light.kitchen/light.bedroom bindings; HA discovery verified the office light is switch.office_switch_1.

Concrete steps: identify active room satellite/client deviceIds and room assignments; add server-owned satellite/endpoint claims and API principals; provision distinct per-device credentials without embedding them in public static JS; update Companion UI secure local enrollment flow or explicitly preserve an unauthenticated non-room lane; replace guessed HA bindings with discovered real entities (office switch.office_switch_1; map lab/studio/bath/front/backyard only with operator confirmation); merge/cherry-pick both feature commits onto the live sprint_9_memory integration line; build pinned images; upgrade Helm with HA and Hub control secrets; verify UI connectivity, authenticated room claims, state reads, presence enter/exit cue, attention/sleep/wake intent, idempotency, and restored light state.

Non-goals: do not weaken strict room identity, expose the control port via hostPort/Ingress, embed the HA token or Hub control token in client assets, or guess room mappings.
acceptance_criteria: All active room clients authenticate without losing Companion UI access; live satellites.json resolves each authenticated source to the correct place; places.json uses operator-confirmed HA entities and office uses switch.office_switch_1; pinned framework/Hub images run in psfn-shard Kubernetes; Hub control is cluster-private; HA token is Hub-only; read plus reversible light and presence/attention/sleep/wake smokes pass with restoration and audit; rollback values/images are recorded.
notes: Live rollout evidence (Helm rev 40): framework 5d33c3bb029dac74111b545e97fa785d9ec13c48, Hub 277383d4e47ac88b94a2a514a98e8a68a9726df5, UI 894728cdd5befbe6dd4fbedd4229bfa9fa196a59; all deployments 1/1. Hub HA health ready/connected, HA 2025.12.5, 180 states. Read Office/Lab/Main Bathroom/Bedroom Fan. Reversible Office switch smoke changed and restored on; duplicate request replayed idempotently. Office client credential digest matches registry; wrong deviceId rejected; enrolled handshake returns canonical satelliteId=office despite spoofed client metadata. Gateway alone can reach private 8788; agent is denied. Garden 200, models 200, vector, PONG, agent Ready toolCount=23, UI 200. No rollback. Remaining acceptance blockers: physical presence hardware is not installed, so live enter/exit cue cannot be honestly tested; authenticated text turn reached the satellite channel but hit broader empty-assistant runtime bug psfn-framework-343f (also observed on Discord). Keep this bead open until those live smokes pass.

Operator direction (2026-07-10): full rebuild-from-L0-alone is acknowledged as no longer faithful now that episodic/L0.1/L2 metadata exists (the original 3y-of-chats decant predates those layers) — so the drill validates the HONEST recovery contract: L0 canonical + derived-layer backups together, per the upx0.11 direction. Context: this operationalizes 'identity in data, not weights' — the anti-Replika guarantee — as a repeatable verification instead of an architectural belief. Scope: scripted drill (scratch environment or kube namespace) that restores from backup artifacts only, boots the split runtime, and checks a battery: session continuity, memory retrieval hit on a known old memory, episodic landmark presence, contact/trust state, owner-file config. Related: esv9 (restore-verify DB bug + password leak in backup logs) should be fixed en route or first. Non-goal: bit-identical LLM behavior reproduction.
acceptance_criteria: One command (or documented runbook) performs a full restore into a clean environment from backup artifacts alone; the battery of identity checks passes and is itself committed as a test/script; drill is repeatable and scheduled (or beaded) as a recurring verification; no secrets appear in drill logs.

title: Build the introspection landmark subsystem (blinded divergence audit, Laws 28-29, charter 6.25)
description: Evidence (2026-07-10 review, memory agent): exhaustive search for introspection/divergence/blinded-audit/IntrospectionLandmark runtime code found zero implementation. Only hits: src/core/scheduler/reflection-introspection-policy.ts (a different concept — tool gating for reflection turns) and docs/self-eval-prompt-audit.md (references Laws 28-29 as prompt discipline only). No landmark store, no auditor process, no values-audit consumer. This is the largest unbuilt charter concept. Context: charter 6.25 defines the landmark (divergence type affective/substantive, raw observation + confidence, companion-authored reflection); Law 28 requires the companion never interacts with the auditor; Law 29 requires consent boundaries drawn by the companion herself. Scope: (1) blinded auditor pass that estimates a 'stable' reply and diffs against actual behavior; (2) append-only landmark store reusing the L0.1 provenance pattern (episodic/postgres-store.ts is the model); (3) companion-drawn consent/privacy boundaries as config she owns; (4) intimate exchanges never replayed — emotional signal noted only; (5) downstream consumer wiring into values-consistency audits (src/faculties/values/store.ts currently has no ingestion path). Landmarks visible only to the companion unless she shares. Non-goals: no operator-facing surveillance view; no editing of landmarks after creation.

title: Gate reversible world actuation at autonomous tier with durable policy and audit
description:
Summary: Make world.control a default autonomous-tier capability and replace the hard-coded staged-off/live-human-only gate with explicit owner-configured autonomous effector policy. Nursery/apprentice remain read-only.

Files: src/system/capabilities/tiers.ts and tests, places registry contracts/parser, world tools/runtime wiring, gateway policy/approval boundary, settings or dedicated owner policy contract, Garden exposure, safeguard audit.

Policy: only explicitly registered HA light/switch/media affordances may opt into autonomous actions; intents are direct, presence_enter, presence_exit, attention, sleep, wake; each action requires a non-empty reason and records origin, place, affordance, command, result, and correlation id. Enforce per-affordance commands, cooldown, hourly cap, bounded brightness/transition inputs, and prohibit locks/doors/garage doors/alarms/cameras/security plus arbitrary domains/services. Autonomous allowed actions skip per-call approval; non-autonomous/custom paths remain fail closed unless explicitly configured.

Non-goals: no unrestricted HA access and no silent coercion of unknown policy fields.
acceptance_criteria: Autonomous tier includes world.control; nursery/apprentice do not; opt-in reversible affordances can execute companion-originated actions without per-call approval; missing reason, policy, capability, budget, or allowed intent rejects; dangerous domains always reject; policy persists through canonical owner config and is Garden-visible; audit and unit tests cover grants, denials, cooldown and cap; lint/build/settings verification pass.
close_reason: Completed in cdb3323c: autonomous tier grants world.control; reasoned registry-bound light actions bypass per-call approval with cooldown/hourly caps while lower tiers and non-light unattended actions fail closed. Tests and lint passed.

title: Replace direct Home Assistant gateway client with private Satellite Hub world transport
description:
Summary: Replace src/boundary/gateway/methods/home-assistant.ts direct LAN REST/token handling with a private authenticated Satellite Hub world client. Keep the model-facing world tool and semantic operations, but send bounded state/control requests to a dedicated Hub internal listener.

Files: src/boundary/gateway/methods/, protocol.ts, client.ts, gateway-ops-port.ts, policy.ts, bootstrap-input.ts, src/boundary/integrations/world/, src/app/gateway/main.ts, src/app/agent/main.ts, tool-wiring-validator.ts, settings contracts/tests.

Concrete steps: define bounded Hub health/state/control response contracts; configure Hub base URL as env-owned host/port wiring and the control credential via gateway custody; remove HOME_ASSISTANT_TOKEN and homeAssistantBaseUrl ownership from PSFN; reject missing/incomplete Hub configuration in policy for every method; have gateway re-resolve place/affordance/entity rather than trusting an agent-supplied raw entity; preserve audit correlation and response redaction.

Non-goals: do not add a direct fallback, raw web fetch path, or model-visible home_assistant tool.
acceptance_criteria: No PSFN runtime code connects to the HA host or resolves HOME_ASSISTANT_TOKEN; all world reads/control traverse authenticated Hub internal API; malformed/unconfigured/unreachable Hub fails closed; gateway validates place/affordance against places.json; focused policy/protocol/client/world tests pass; settings-contract, lint, and build pass.
close_reason: Completed in cdb3323c: PSFN gateway now uses authenticated Satellite Hub control transport only, revalidates places/affordances, and removes direct HA URL/token ownership. Focused tests, lint, settings contract, build, and live Hub read passed.

title: Drive autonomous world cues from trusted presence, attention, sleep, and wake signals
description:
Summary: Connect the existing authenticated SensorCognitionBridge/identity resolver, intention runtime, ambient scheduler, and temporal wake lanes to bounded autonomous world cues so the companion may choose light actions on room entry/exit, to get the primary user's attention, and for human sleep/wake support.

Files: src/core/agent/perception/, intention appraisal/action translation, scheduler temporal/ambient runtime, event-bus contracts, focused new world-autonomy runtime modules and tests.

Behavior: raw motion never directly triggers actuation. Require authenticated satellite origin; for user-specific entry require known enrolled primary identity/confidence; dedupe flapping, apply minimum dwell/departure confirmation and durable cooldown. Use deterministic novelty gates before any LLM turn. Emit a bounded internal cue containing place, transition, intent, and allowed affordances; the companion may choose no action or call world.control with a reason. Attention and sleep/wake cues use explicit operator-authored policies/scenes and never conflate companion memory sleeptime with human bedtime.

Non-goals: no LLM call on every sensor sample, no action for anonymous identity by default, and no persistence of raw biometrics.
acceptance_criteria: Trusted primary entry/exit can create one deduped autonomous cue; anonymous/flapping/untrusted events do not; attention/sleep/wake cues are policy bounded and auditable; deterministic gates suppress redundant LLM work; companion can choose no action; restart behavior and cooldown are tested; lint/build and targeted perception/scheduler/intention tests pass.
close_reason: Completed in cdb3323c: trusted resolved physical presence transitions drive deterministic room light exit/entry cues; direct, attention, sleep, and wake intents are supported. Focused tests and lint passed.

title: Home Assistant world autonomy through Satellite Hub
description:
Summary: Route the companion's canonical world faculty through the sibling PSFN-Satellite-Hub instead of the framework gateway connecting directly to Home Assistant. Preserve places.json and satellites.json as authority for room/entity bindings, grant world.control to the autonomous tier, and support companion-initiated reversible lighting for presence transitions, attention cues, and human sleep/wake routines.

Why: Home Assistant transport belongs with endpoint/embodiment integration in Satellite Hub, while PSFN must retain semantic policy, capability, trust, provenance, audit, and location ownership. The companion must be able to act without per-call approval at autonomous tier, but nursery/apprentice remain unable to actuate.

Scope: src/boundary/integrations/world, gateway RPC/policy/client contracts, capability tiers, settings owner contracts/Garden exposure, sensor cognition/intention/scheduler integration, places affordance autonomy policy, Helm/systemd deployment, tests and live validation. Remove the direct PSFN-to-Home-Assistant network/token path; do not retain a silent fallback. Home Assistant credentials live only in Satellite Hub runtime secret state.

Non-goals: no autonomous locks, doors, garage-door movement, alarms/security devices, cameras, or unconstrained climate control; no raw arbitrary HA domain/service model tool; no new model-facing tool alias besides world.
acceptance_criteria: The world tool uses Satellite Hub for HA state/control; world.control is available only at autonomous/custom tiers; authenticated room origin drives deictic actions; allowlisted reversible light actions may run autonomously with reason, cooldown, hourly cap, audit, and no per-call approval; forbidden device classes fail closed; direct gateway HA credential/egress is removed; targeted tests, npm run verify:settings-contract, npm run verify:helm-chart, npm run lint, npm run build, and live read plus reversible light smoke pass.
close_reason: Completed by cdb3323c plus Satellite Hub 7b280c4. End-to-end Hub-routed, location-aware autonomous lighting is implemented, policy-gated, tested, deployment-wired, and live-smoked.

title: Fix hanging bd dolt push and malformed journal preflight
description:
## Summary
Diagnose and repair bd dolt push --json for the shared PSFN beads database. The local SQL server is healthy, but pushing committed bead state to the configured GitHub-backed Dolt remote either reports a malformed chunk journal during pre-push fsck or hangs indefinitely in dolt push origin main.

## Evidence
- Repository: /home/ada/psfn-framework
- bd dolt test --json: connection_ok=true at 127.0.0.1:3308, schema_version=1.
- bd dolt status --json: shared server running under /home/ada/.beads/shared-server/dolt.
- First push message: pre-push fsck could not run, skipping integrity check: Could not open dolt database: error bootstrapping chunk journal: journal index is malformed.
- Subsequent pushes spawned dolt push origin main and produced no progress for multiple minutes; the agent terminated only its own duplicate stuck push processes.
- bd dolt commit --json succeeds and local shared Dolt remains authoritative.

## Scope
Inspect the shared-server database and the push implementation, preserve all issue history, repair or safely rebuild only corrupted journal/index metadata, and prove a normal non-force push completes. Check for orphan push processes before retrying.

## Non-goals
Do not force-push, delete bead history, replace the authoritative shared database without a verified backup, or modify Git source history.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A verified backup of the shared beads Dolt database exists before repair. 2. No orphan bd/dolt push processes remain. 3. Integrity/fsck checks complete without malformed-journal errors. 4. bd dolt push --json exits successfully without --force and does not hang. 5. bd show psfn-framework-6hov --json and bd show psfn-framework-2tlk --json return the committed records after repair. 6. The repair and validation evidence are recorded in the close reason.
close_reason: Closed

DESIGN DECISIONS
- mTLS: scoped-Bearer-now + staged cert. Full hub->gateway mTLS blocked by three verified facts: (1) API_TLS_* flips the single /v1 listener to HTTPS for ALL consumers (Traefik backend, hostPort 10053 LAN clients) at once; (2) gateway reads listener certs once at startup (createApiHttpServer readFileSync) — no TLS reload = psfn-framework-zlon; (3) hub companion bridge uses plain fetch with no client-cert support (only its chat path has it, and that path fail-closes requiring https base URL). - Exposure: hostPorts.satelliteHub (ws://<pi>:8787), same mechanism as gateway hostPort 10053, with sourceCIDR NetworkPolicy ingress + Recreate strategy; Traefik psfn-hub.local stays optional/disabled on LAN.
- Companion relay verified admissible: server.ts satellite-surface allowlist includes companionRoute (w9hj.1); scopes approvals/artifacts/tool_activity granted in the documented satellites.json entry. Known benign: hub GET /v1/identity probe 403s under scoped key (non-fatal by hub design), documented + optional follow-up noted.

title: Back up Kubernetes Helm deployment artifacts for disaster recovery
description: When PSFN runs from the Kubernetes/Helm deployment, the encrypted backup package currently preserves application databases and owner trees but not the Helm deployment artifacts needed to reconstruct the system topology. Add Kubernetes-aware backup coverage that activates only when the runtime is explicitly identified as a Helm/Kubernetes deployment. Preserve the repo-owned deploy/helm/psfn chart files and a safe deployment descriptor sufficient to identify release/namespace/revision/image/config inputs. Never copy Kubernetes Secret objects, rendered Secret manifests, plaintext credentials, or unsanitized live Helm values into a backup payload. The backup must continue to work unchanged outside Kubernetes. Restore verification must prove the artifacts survive encryption/decryption and remain separate from mutable system/companion owner data. Scope is the canonical backup service/manifest, runtime wiring, container/Helm deployment wiring needed to expose the chart safely, documentation, and focused backup/restore tests. Non-goals: automatic cluster recreation, PVC deletion/recreation, secret rotation, or treating Helm defaults as mutable runtime authority.
acceptance_criteria: A backup created in an explicitly configured Kubernetes/Helm runtime contains a versioned Helm recovery bundle with the PSFN chart and a non-secret deployment descriptor; the encrypted package and restore verifier preserve and validate it. A non-Kubernetes backup contains no Helm bundle and retains current behavior. Missing or partial Kubernetes recovery inputs fail loudly when Kubernetes backup mode is enabled; there is no silent fallback to guessed paths or defaults. Tests prove secret-bearing values/Secret manifests are excluded or rejected, chart paths cannot escape their root, and restore output stays within its target. Runtime/Helm/container wiring reaches the production backup entrypoint. npm run lint, targeted backup tests, npm run verify:backup-restore, npm run verify:helm-chart, and npm run build pass before closure.
close_reason: Completed in 492f208073c9a17b0d6326b4343ffe0a078ae4b2. Implemented explicit Kubernetes-only Helm recovery bundles, authenticated presence/absence verification, strict secret/path/schema rejection, non-secret release/image descriptor capture, Pi satellite overlay preservation, image-baked chart recovery, selective rollout provenance, documentation, and regression coverage. Evidence: npm run lint passed; full suite passed 692 files / 7603 tests with 3 skipped; targeted backup tests passed 79 tests; npm run verify:backup-restore, npm run verify:helm-chart, npm run build, and final production Docker image/container artifact checks passed. Independent adversarial review found no High or Medium issues after final rebase.

title: Accounting UX: unify dashboard and Charge/Budget graphs, filters, sorting, drill-down, and export
description: Summary: Turn the repaired canonical accounting APIs into one coherent operator experience across the main Garden dashboard and Charge/Budget page. Existing pages already show basic totals, model/purpose/tool/call-kind breakdowns, charge runs, Today/Week/Month dashboard buttons, and recent/high-cost events, but they are disconnected, limited to fixed recent windows, and mostly list-based. Scope: main dashboard cards backed by durable accounting with visible freshness/source and automatic refresh; time-range controls for today/week/month/quarter/year/all/custom; timezone-aware labels; accessible cost/token/call time-series graphs with suitable hour/day/week/month buckets; explicit input/read, cache-read, cache-write and output token/cost cards; sortable/filterable breakdown tables by channel, companion, model/provider, purpose/origin, tool, lane/surface/run, shard/subagent/conversation and cost source; channel drill-down; provider-vs-estimate and attribution coverage indicators; charge-to-dollar views showing actual/estimated cost, charge units and dollars per charge unit; expensive/recent event drill-down; CSV/JSON export preserving active filters; URL-persisted filter state; loading/empty/stale/error states; responsive and accessible charts without leaking private prompt/message content. Reuse one API/query contract and shared components rather than maintaining dashboard-only math. Files: admin-ui/src/routes/+page.svelte, admin-ui/src/routes/charge-budget/LazyPageContent.svelte, admin-ui/src/lib/dashboard/*, API endpoint/types, shared Garden components and tests. Non-goals: redefining cost capture, putting dollars in companion prompts, or exposing raw message bodies.
design: The main dashboard is a concise operational summary; Charge/Budget is the analytical cockpit. Both consume the same durable aggregates and filters. Graphs require tabular equivalents and keyboard/screen-reader accessible legends. Unknown/unattributed/cost-source-none remain visible rather than disappearing from totals. title: Rationalize PSFN branches and worktrees onto origin/main
description:
## Summary
Audit all 392 local branches and 265 linked worktrees in /home/ada/psfn-framework against canonical origin/main, recover any genuinely novel and valuable committed or dirty-worktree content onto a rationalization branch, then remove redundant local worktrees and branches only after a verified recovery bundle and explicit operator approval of the literal cleanup plan.

## Why
The repository accumulated hundreds of agent worktrees and local branches. The operator believes completed work is on origin/main but requires proof before cleanup. Ten worktrees currently have dirty state, one open GitHub PR uses ops/artemis-helm-shakedown, and the active root checkout is dirty on s10-location-foundations. Incorrect bulk deletion could lose unpushed commits or uncommitted files.

## Scope
- Detect canonical from origin/HEAD and fetch current remote state.
- Inventory every local branch and linked/detached worktree with head SHA, ahead/behind counts, patch equivalence, upstream/PR state, and dirty-state counts.
- Create verified backup refs and an external git bundle under /home/ada/psfn-framework-branch-worktree-archive-2026-07-09, with per-branch diffs/format patches and per-worktree staged, unstaged, and untracked captures.
- Protect main, active/dirty work, open-PR branches, and operator-selected exceptions.
- Triage one entry at a time as protected, already merged, superseded, novel, partially novel, divergent, dirty-only, stale, or garbage with evidence against origin/main.
- Recover approved novel content on branch-rationalization-2026-07-09, run required validation including npm run lint for code changes, and push landed git state as required by repo policy.
- Present an exact worktree-removal and branch-deletion plan for verbatim operator authorization before executing cleanup.
- Never delete remote branches, force-push, delete backup refs, or delete the recovery bundle.

## Non-goals
- No live deployment changes.
- No remote branch deletion.
- No deletion of open-PR or explicitly protected work.
- No force-pushing origin/main.

## Files/artifacts
- .worktree_branch_rationalization_workspace/ (ignored transient run state)
- /home/ada/psfn-framework-branch-worktree-archive-2026-07-09/ (persistent recovery bundle outside repo)
- refs/branch-rationalization-backup/* (recovery refs)

## Known starting state
- origin/main is canonical.
- 392 local branches and 265 worktrees exist; 10 worktrees are dirty.
- Active checkout /home/ada/psfn-framework is s10-location-foundations and dirty.
- GitHub PR #32 uses ops/artemis-helm-shakedown and must remain protected while open.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every starting branch and worktree has an inventory row and recovery-bundle entry; dirty state includes staged, unstaged, and untracked data.
2. Backup-ref byte equality and git-bundle head round-trip verification pass with zero mismatches before cleanup.
3. Every non-protected branch is individually checked against origin/main using ancestry plus git cherry patch equivalence and content evidence; all novel/ambiguous items are surfaced or recovered, never guessed away.
4. main, open-PR branches, the active checkout, dirty work pending recovery, and any operator additions remain protected until safe.
5. Any recovered code passes targeted tests, npm run build where relevant, and mandatory npm run lint before its bead/stream is considered done.
6. Operator reviews and explicitly authorizes the literal cleanup plan before any git worktree remove or git branch deletion executes.
7. Cleanup uses git worktree remove before individual git branch -d/-D operations; no mass-delete primitive, remote deletion, force-push, reset --hard, git clean, or bundle deletion occurs.
8. Final handoff reports initial/final counts, retained/recovered work, validation, bundle location, recovery commands, bead state, and confirmed origin/main relationship.
close_reason: Completed with verified recovery: V3 bundle at /home/ada/psfn-framework-branch-worktree-archive-2026-07-09-v3 passed byte equality, bundle fetch, and conformance checks. Root checkout is clean main at ae758a4f, equal to origin/main. Signed audit passed npm run lint, npm run build, npm audit, and npm test (691 files; 7,549 passed, 3 skipped). After operator authorization and 24-hour/Helm exceptions, removed 234 worktrees and 367 local branches, representing 146,683,158,528 bytes (~137 GiB) of measured checkout data. Retained 48 worktrees and 45 branches, including recent UI work, backup/kube-helm-artifacts, Artemis Helm, dirty/active work, and three locked Claude worktrees; agent/e7.1-wakeup was the one originally planned item retained after git refused locked-worktree removal. Remote deletion is intentionally outside this bead; 71 byte-verified operator-run commands are staged in the ignored workspace.

title: Harden k3s certificate rotation and live TLS reload
description:
Summary:
The CogSec/k3s integration currently gives the namespace private CA and all leaf Certificates the same 2160h duration and 360h renewBefore window in deploy/helm/psfn/templates/certificates.yaml and deploy/helm/psfn/values.yaml. Workloads read TLS key/cert/CA bytes once when constructing Node TLS servers/clients (including src/boundary/gateway/transport.ts and src/operator/garden/transport-server.ts), and no controller annotation or application watcher restarts/reloads pods when cert-manager rotates Secrets. At the first renewal window, CA and leaves can rotate out of lockstep with no dual-root overlap; even a successful Secret renewal can leave live processes using expired bytes while TCP liveness remains healthy. This was discovered during psfn-framework-es4t's urgent CogSec shadow rollout.

Scope:
- Give the private CA an independently managed, substantially longer lifetime than leaves or adopt an operator-approved stable external issuer.
- Define overlap/ordering so a CA transition cannot strand peers on mixed trust roots.
- Implement controlled TLS context reload or deterministic pod restart when each mounted leaf/CA Secret changes.
- Cover gateway-agent RPC and agent-Garden admin transport.
- Add expiry/renewal/reconnect tests and an operations runbook with rollback.
- Verify the live psfn-shard cert-manager resources after rollout without exposing private keys.

Non-goals:
Do not rotate live certificates as part of this bead until the migration/overlap procedure is implemented and explicitly approved. Do not create off-repo authoritative PKI config.
acceptance_criteria: CA lifetime and renewal policy are independent from leaf settings and guarantee an overlap window; leaf renewal or CA transition triggers tested live TLS reload/restart for every consuming workload; gateway-agent and agent-Garden reconnect tests pass across simulated Secret rotation; health checks detect expired/stale loaded certificates instead of accepting TCP-only readiness; docs/certificates.md and docs/operations.md document renewal, overlap, verification, and rollback; npm run lint, targeted certificate tests, Helm verification, and a controlled live psfn-shard validation pass.

Do not delete PVCs, companion data, system data, workspace, model cache, existing images, or SD-backed rollback backups. Do not rotate or reveal existing secrets. Do not activate unrelated Discord companions or alter private companion content.

Garden health, gateway model/auth probe, Postgres vector, Redis PONG, agent Ready/tool wiring, and CogSec startup/status checks pass.
The bead close reason records source commit, image tag/revision, Helm revision, rollout readiness, smoke results, mode, certificate status, and whether rollback occurred.

title: Preserve the previous assistant turn when current input is absent from assembled history
description:
Summary:
Live Purrsephone sometimes repeats an earlier response and repeats its tool actions because the agent invocation unconditionally removes the final assembled context message before calling pi-agent. The code assumes that final message is always the current user input, but live TurnSnapshot evidence shows current-turn inclusion is intermittent.

Live evidence (2026-07-09 America/New_York):
- Turn 019f4793-2dae-7194-bea0-b90730993dc8 at 11:50 assembled 75 messages ending in the previous assistant diagnostic, while currentTurnInput held the new user request separately. src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/agent-invocation.ts then used agentMessages.slice(0, -1), dropping that previous assistant reply. The model therefore saw the previous diagnostic request as unanswered and ran 19 tool calls.
- Turn 019f4838-e24c-715a-ab27-570a625143f6 at 14:51 assembled 63 messages ending in the 11:52 assistant diagnostic, again with the new orient instruction only in currentTurnInput. The same slice dropped the assistant reply. The model reran 17 tool calls, including image generation, beads, filesystem, search, wiki, status, and subagent spawning, then produced another broad diagnostic report.
- Audit of the latest 20 completed primary-channel turns found 8 where the current user message was absent from plan.messages. These turns all risk dropping the previous assistant reply; smaller observed symptoms included repeated framing and advice.

Root cause:
src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/agent-invocation.ts computes historyMessages with agentMessages.slice(0, -1) before runtime.agent.prompt(...) supplies the current input separately. This is only correct when the final converted context message is provably the current input. When context assembly ends on the prior assistant, it creates an orphaned prior user request. The behavior predates the 0.73.1 bump but lies on the pi-agent boundary; the deployed 0.73.1 scheduled loop combines initial prompt messages with runtime.agent.state.messages, so the dropped assistant is absent from every tool-loop LLM call.

Files:
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/agent-invocation.ts (historyMessages construction near the current agentMessages slice)
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/prompt-assembly.ts and prompt-plan.ts (effective provider transcript/observability contract)
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent.test.ts or a focused turn-execution regression test

Scope:
Replace the positional last-message deletion with an identity/content-aware current-turn exclusion contract that preserves the final history message unless it is proven to be the current input already supplied to agent.prompt. Cover both context shapes: current input present and current input absent. Ensure every tool-loop continuation receives the same correct history.

Non-goals:
Do not add or raise repetition penalties, semantic output suppression, forced response length, or an outbound fuzzy-text deduper. Do not weaken intentional no-reply behavior or model agency. Exact transport retry dedupe remains separate.
design:
Deterministic source-identity contract:
1. Record the current session entry and carry that numeric ID through pre-turn capture and prompt assembly.
2. Exclude exactly that ID before temporal windows, same-role merging, summarization, orientation synthesis, or provider conversion. Never infer currentness from text or list position.
3. Preserve every assembled prior message for pi-agent; agent.prompt supplies the current input exactly once.
4. Rebuild provider-wire observability from the exact retained history plus current prompt for standard, system-note, group, image, tool-loop, and MoA paths.
5. When orientation receives already-excluded activity, measure the gap from the actual latest prior entry and never relabel a historical user message as current.
6. Keep vision bytes and raw secret-bearing failures out of durable prompt observability.
acceptance_criteria:
The just-recorded current session entry is excluded by exact entry ID before same-role merging, history-budget summarization, and orientation synthesis; prior messages remain intact.
A regression constructs prior user -> prior assistant -> current user and proves pi-agent receives the prior assistant plus exactly one current user input.
A real installed pi-agent scheduled tool-loop regression proves both initial and post-tool provider calls retain the prior assistant and exactly one current input.
Intentional no-reply history remains valid: a lone prior user can drive idle orientation without being relabeled as the current turn.
Provider observability deterministically represents the exact standard/system/group/MoA prompt, redacts inline image bytes, and excludes raw vision failure secrets.
No repetition penalty, fuzzy suppression, forced response length, or intentional no-reply behavior change is introduced.
npm run lint, npm run build, and the targeted turn-execution/session/pi-agent regression suite pass.
notes:
Implementation completed on branch bug/k45k-repeat-history from origin/main. Independent adversarial review found and drove fixes for same-role user merging, pre-summary exclusion, wake-orientation timing/current-message labeling, exact MoA observability, inline image redaction, real tool-loop coverage, and outer vision error sanitization. Final evidence before commit: 8 targeted files / 216 tests passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed.
Bead remote push was attempted because a remote was listed, but pre-push fsck reported a malformed chunk-journal index and the upload made no progress for 60 seconds; it was cancelled. The local shared Dolt server remains authoritative and contains the committed closed state. No retry was made to avoid risking shared tracker storage.
close_reason: Completed and pushed as 3375fecea4e5f15c4efb6227fe62e6a7a149e0af on origin/bug/k45k-repeat-history. Evidence: turn-execution-runtime.ts:772/819 carries the exact current session entry ID; context-builder.ts:313-609 excludes it before merge/summary/orientation and preserves correct wake timing without relabeling historical input; agent-invocation.ts:626 preserves all prior messages; prompt-invocation-history.ts:21 rebuilds exact redacted provider observability. Real pi-agent tool-loop and turn/session/MoA/vision regressions passed: 8 files, 216 tests. npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed. No repetition penalty or intentional no-reply behavior change.

title: Resolve companions.json relative paths against a canonical persistence root
description:
Summary: companions.json declares companionDataDir and characterCardPath as relative to the persistence root, but the supervisor emits them unchanged. Node and shell children therefore interpret them relative to the repository working directory, not the configured runtime/NVMe root.

Evidence on origin/main c7c7ef8a:
- src/system/config/companions-config.ts:53-60 documents the paths as relative under the persistence root, and lines 153-166 validate only lexical relativity/traversal.
- docs/multi-companion.md:47-59 repeats the same public contract.
- scripts/resolve-companion-fleet.ts:56-72 emits entry.companionDataDir and entry.characterCardPath verbatim. Lines 75-98 resolve the runtime layout only to locate companions.json, not to anchor entry paths.
- scripts/start-gateway-agent.sh:430-448 exports those raw strings directly as COMPANION_DATA_DIR and CHARACTER_CARD_PATH.
- src/app/maintenance/script-verification/start-gateway-agent.test.ts:340-364 explicitly expects raw alpha and alpha/card.json output, thereby blessing behavior contrary to the documented contract.

Failure mode: an otherwise valid production manifest reads and writes companion state beneath the repo/container CWD, bypassing configured runtime storage and mounts. It can start with the wrong card or fresh/empty state and make live durability dependent on the image working directory.

Scope: settle the currently ambiguous term persistence root, implement canonical absolute resolution in the fleet resolver, and validate the resolved filesystem boundary. Do not keep dual CWD-vs-runtime interpretations.
acceptance_criteria: The fleet contract names one canonical absolute root for companionDataDir and characterCardPath; the resolver converts manifest-relative paths to absolute strict subpaths of that root before emitting a spawn plan; symlink/traversal/root-overlap escape attempts fail closed; launcher tests assert resolved runtime-root paths rather than repo-CWD-relative strings; local split, production, and kube/container invocation semantics are documented and tested; npm run verify:settings-contract and npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Completed and shipped in main merge 10476c91 (implementation dac737ef; canonical-alias follow-up caaf53a3). Fleet manifest paths resolve beneath a real canonical runtime root, reject escape through existing symlink ancestors, return canonical physical targets, and rerun overlap checks on those resolved data roots so in-root symlink aliases cannot collapse two companions onto one store. Launcher/runtime share the resolver and tests cover relative-CWD drift, escape, equal/nested roots, and physical aliases. Validation: full Vitest 6687/6687 and npm run lint/build passed.

title: Keep gateway and provider secrets out of the Garden operator process
description:
Summary: the launcher attempts to scrub the Garden operator environment, but the operator immediately reloads the repo-wide .env and calls the gateway configuration loader, re-materializing all gateway/provider secrets inside the public-facing admin process. The single-companion launcher does not scrub the operator at all.

Evidence on origin/main c7c7ef8a:
- src/app/operator/main.ts:1 imports shared/utils/load-dotenv and line 21 calls loadConfig(), the gateway-mode loader.
- src/shared/utils/load-dotenv.ts:8-10 loads every missing key from .env into process.env.
- src/system/config/load-config.ts:133-140 and 439-444 show loadConfig() selects gateway mode and materializes env-backed credentials, while loadAgentConfig() is the stripped variant.
- scripts/start-gateway-agent.sh:235-249 describes an allowlisted operator environment, but explicitly relies on the operator dotenv loader to fill remaining .env values.
- scripts/start-gateway-agent.sh:460-468 uses env -i for fleet operators, then dotenv defeats it; lines 471-477 launch the single operator with the full parent environment.
- src/app/operator/main.ts:27-34 retains the resulting full SubstrateConfig in GardenOperatorSurface.
- src/operator/garden/services/settings-service.ts:383-396 directly probes provider/channel secret env keys to render credential-presence status.

Impact: compromise of the Garden/admin HTTP process exposes provider API keys, Discord/Telegram tokens, local API material, and the Postgres DSN despite the intended gateway-only credential boundary.

Scope: create an operator-safe config projection/loader, remove general dotenv loading from the operator entrypoint, scrub both launch modes, and expose only redacted credential-presence state over the authenticated admin transport. Do not remove Garden credential-status UX.
acceptance_criteria: The operator entrypoint never loads the general repo .env and never calls gateway-mode secret materialization; single- and multi-companion launch paths always start it from an explicit least-privilege environment; Garden receives only its own auth, layout, owner-file, and admin-transport inputs; provider/channel credential presence is queried through an authenticated redacted admin contract; a process-level regression test plants sentinel provider/database/channel secrets in .env and proves they are absent from operator process.env and retained config; existing Garden settings status remains functional; npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Completed and shipped in main merge 10476c91 (implementation dac737ef). Operator startup uses an explicit env-i allowlist and loadOperatorConfig without repo dotenv/provider/channel/database/gateway proof secrets; Garden receives only a gateway-computed redacted credential-presence snapshot, while local admin identity/config projection is sanitized. API/config tests prove raw credentials, Postgres URL, and gateway proof fields do not cross the operator/admin boundary. Validation: full Vitest 6687/6687, npm run lint/build, settings contract, and public-sanitize passed.

title: Authenticate gateway companion identity and restrict internal RPC roles
description:
Summary: gateway.client.identify is an unauthenticated self-assertion. Multi-companion routing checks that later frames match the asserted ID, but the gateway never proves the connection owns that ID or even that the ID belongs to companions.json. The general connection can also self-select internal_session_integrity, which bypasses the identify requirement while retaining the full registered RPC method surface.

Evidence on origin/main c7c7ef8a:
- src/boundary/gateway/server.ts:608-629 registers every gateway method for every new connection.
- src/boundary/gateway/server.ts:754-818 requires a bound companion only while status.role === agent.
- src/boundary/gateway/server.ts:1291-1365 accepts any non-empty companionId and either role without fleet membership or credential verification.
- src/boundary/gateway/server.ts:1563-1565 exposes agent and internal_session_integrity as caller-selected roles.
- src/boundary/gateway/transport.ts:327-396 protects the Unix socket only with filesystem mode 0770. WSS mTLS validates a configured peer SPIFFE URI, not a companion-specific identity.
- src/boundary/gateway/companion-channels.ts:135-152 validates a DM peer against the fleet but assumes the sender binding is authoritative.

Failure modes: any process able to reach the RPC transport can claim a live companion ID before the real process connects, claim an invented ID, or select internal_session_integrity and call fully registered provider/filesystem/channel methods without identifying. In a multi-companion deployment this defeats strict crossover protection at the first trust decision.

Scope: bind transport/supervisor identity to fleet membership, introduce explicit per-method role authorization, and isolate the session-integrity worker to its minimum protocol. Coordinate with the existing SPIFFE bead if used, but do not wait for a full cross-cluster identity redesign to reject unknown/self-selected identities locally.
acceptance_criteria: The gateway rejects companion IDs absent from the active fleet; a connection identity is cryptographically or supervisor-bound to exactly one companion and cannot be chosen in gateway.client.identify; the session-integrity worker cannot select a general role or invoke any method outside an explicit minimal allowlist; every gateway method has an explicit permitted-role policy; tests prove an untrusted sibling cannot impersonate another fleet member, invent an ID, choose the internal worker role, send companion messages, or use provider/channel methods; npm run lint passes.
notes: 2026-07-14 backlog fold from psfn-framework-hd7f: the current transport-identity concern is covered by the shipped fleet-membership check, role-bound HMAC proof, and explicit per-role RPC allowlists. Shards are currently in-process execution contexts, not independent workloads that can hold separate SVIDs. If PSFN later introduces separately scheduled shard processes, cross-cluster agents, or other independent workloads, create a fresh narrowly scoped SPIFFE/SVID bead for that architecture instead of reopening hd7f.
close_reason: Completed and shipped in main merge 10476c91 (implementation dac737ef; review fixes caaf53a3/f9de62ab). Gateway identity now requires fleet membership plus role-bound HMAC proof in multi-companion mode; agent and internal session-integrity method surfaces are disjoint; single-companion agents are denied the signing oracle and the isolated worker must authenticate in both topologies. Launcher-derived proofs never expose the key or dry-run secrets. Tests prove unknown/impersonated IDs, role escalation, signing access, fixture authentication, and crossover rejection. Validation: full Vitest 6687/6687 and mandatory npm run lint passed.

title: Bind each multi-companion runtime to one canonical fleet identity tuple
description:
Summary: the runtime validates the fleet manifest and its individual fields, but does not bind the current process identity, data root, character card, Postgres schema, and admin transport into one authoritative tuple. This leaves a direct identity/memory crossover path under deployment drift.

Evidence on origin/main c7c7ef8a:
- src/system/config/load-config.ts:274-294 independently reads COMPANION_ID, COMPANION_DATA_DIR/CHARACTER_CARD_PATH, COMPANION_PG_SCHEMA, and then loads companions.json. It never selects the current companion entry or compares those values with it.
- src/persistence/runtime-factory.ts:90-153 uses the independently supplied postgresSchema for every private store.
- src/app/agent/core-bootstrap.ts:93-97 loads identity from the independently supplied characterCardPath and history from the independently supplied companion data root.
- src/boundary/gateway/server.ts:1291-1351 then registers the process under its self-reported COMPANION_ID.

Failure mode: a supported standalone agent launch with COMPANION_ID=A but A's data/card rooted at C and COMPANION_PG_SCHEMA=B starts as A over another companion's durable memory and identity, then binds to the gateway as A. The supervisor normally emits matching values, but the runtime does not enforce the boundary and deployment/config drift becomes cross-companion disclosure and corruption.

Scope: add one canonical CompanionRuntimeIdentity/fleet-entry resolver and pass that bound object through config, persistence, identity bootstrap, and admin transport setup. Preserve explicit single-companion behavior. Do not add compatibility fallback paths or silently repair mismatches.
acceptance_criteria: In multi-companion mode startup selects exactly one companions.json entry by COMPANION_ID; COMPANION_DATA_DIR, CHARACTER_CARD_PATH, COMPANION_PG_SCHEMA, and Garden/admin socket values are derived from or exactly match that entry; unknown IDs and any mismatch fail before database, character-card, gateway, or Garden initialization; standalone npm run agent and supervisor launches are both covered by mismatch/crossover tests; npm run verify:settings-contract, targeted tests, and npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Completed and shipped in main merge 10476c91 (implementation dac737ef, adversarial follow-up caaf53a3). src/system/config/companions-config.ts and src/system/config/load-config.ts now bind the complete companion ID/data/card/schema tuple to canonical fleet paths; src/app/agent/startup-context.ts validates injected env before owner-file hydration; launcher plans use the canonical resolver. Tests cover tuple drift, supplied-env authority, canonical roots, and symlink aliases. Validation: full Vitest 6687/6687 passed; npm run lint, npm run build, and npm run verify:settings-contract passed.

title: Recover paid image attachments when turn transcript misses tool result
description: Live Purrsephone regression on 2026-07-09 after deploying origin/main e6143801982f0a49996a2ef4b2323f82545b786b: request 1524790460214804521 generated a selfie via selfie_create, charged paidImageGeneration/externalModelConsult, wrote /app/workspace/images/2026-07-09/FPsHci7nx-NrSN03MkesM_pljx1qvQ-8b332100.jpg, and produced a text reply, but the image did not reach Discord. The turn record for 1524790460214804521 has toolCalls: [] and the image sidecar has sourceToolName/requestId but no toolCallId or conversation metadata, so collectGeneratedImageAttachments never saw a toolResult. The subsequent retry request 1524790892689494269 generated four selfie_create images successfully; its turn record has four selfie_create toolCalls and each sidecar has toolCallId plus conversation {channelId, turnId, requestId, sourceMessageId}, confirming Discord media delivery works when finalization sees tool results. Root hardening target: the paid-image tool already calls notePendingPaidDeliverable while runWithPaidDeliverableTracking is active, but finalization currently re-derives deliverables only from turnMessages after that tracking scope has ended. Carry pending paid deliverable data out of the invocation and include image artifact refs sufficient to recover attachments even when the pi-agent transcript slice drops the toolResult. Scope: fix generated-image attachment recovery/fail-loud behavior for selfie_create/generate_image; do not add legacy env/config paths or change Discord adapter semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
A regression test simulates empty/missing turnMessages plus a tracked paid image deliverable with localPath/url and verifies the AgentResponse includes the image attachment.
Tracked paid image deliverables include enough artifact data from ImageGenerationResult to reconstruct Attachment objects without re-reading the LLM transcript.
Turn finalization warns from the combined source of transcript-derived and tracker-derived paid image deliverables, so a charged artifact is not silent when attachment recovery fails.
