title: Transport tool schema shape mismatch bypasses empty-args retry
description: Live Purrsephone on psfn-shard still produced a user-facing validation failure after deploying origin/main 62b2a3eb with pi-agent-core/pi-ai 0.73.1. On 2026-07-09 at 08:58:13 America/New_York, channel 1313001762793197678, requestId 1524761564136083507, turnId 019f46f4-f1ee-70ad-a78a-7eeb99e40cf9, gateway logs show: Tool call arrived with empty arguments { provenance: provider_emitted_empty, toolName: selfie_create, toolCallId: chatcmpl-tool-ba87e19faadffcca, argumentFragmentBytes: 2, provider: litellm, model: z-ai/glm-5.2 }. The session record then persisted a tool observation: Validation failed for tool selfie_create: prompt required; Received arguments: {}. The turn observability snapshot proves the active selfie_create schema shipped by PSFN had inputSchema.required=[prompt] in both toolContext.activeTools and plan.toolDefinitions. However model_usage_events for that request show emptyArgsRetries=0 on the toolUse completion. Code read: pi-agent-core passes tools to StreamFn as pi-ai Tool objects with parameters, while PSFN LLMClient retry guard findCorruptEmptyToolCalls expects ToolSchema.inputSchema. The agent/gateway transport path forwards context.tools through RPC; if those are pi-ai shaped, the gateway can offer tools to the provider but cannot classify required-property empty calls for retry. Scope: normalize accepted tool schema shape at the gateway/LLM boundary or make findCorruptEmptyToolCalls understand both inputSchema and parameters, then add regression coverage for a transport-backed agent turn with a required-property tool emitting literal {}.
acceptance_criteria: Given a transport-backed agent turn with a required-property tool represented as a pi-ai Tool { name, description, parameters }, when the provider emits a literal empty-object tool call, the empty-args retry guard retries up to the configured bound and records emptyArgsRetries>0. Add tests covering selfie_create-like required prompt schema and confirm direct ToolSchema { inputSchema } behavior still passes. Live validation should no longer persist a selfie_create prompt-required validation error for a provider_emitted_empty first attempt if a retry recovers.
notes: 2026-07-09 branch check: fetched origin/refactor/pi-agent-boundary at 92a88c1740d7f0139c409139b8848a1dee9a5c2c. The branch centralizes direct @mariozechner/pi-agent-core imports under src/boundary/pi-agent and moves the repo-owned SubstrateAgentTool type there, but it does not fix this bug. Evidence: src/core/agent/stream-adapter.ts:380-396 still casts pi-agent stream context to LLMContext and forwards llmContext.tools unchanged to the gateway transport; src/primitives/llm/client-response-helpers.ts:202-213 still builds the retry schema map from ToolSchema.inputSchema only. No branch diff adds parameters->inputSchema normalization on the agent-to-gateway transport path, and no regression test asserts a pi-agent Tool { parameters } is converted before retry. Existing observability/repair helpers understand both names in other paths, but the live gateway retry path remains bypassable.
close_reason: Fixed on refactor/pi-agent-boundary in d3f71bb3: stream adapter now normalizes pi-agent Tool { parameters } and existing ToolSchema { inputSchema } into PSFN ToolSchema before gateway transport, so gateway LLM retry sees required schemas. Evidence: src/core/agent/stream-adapter.ts normalizes transport tools; src/core/agent/stream-adapter.test.ts covers selfie_create-style parameters -> inputSchema and preserves inputSchema tools. Validation passed: npm test -- src/core/agent/stream-adapter.test.ts; npm test -- src/primitives/llm/client.test.ts -t empty-tool-args; npm run lint; npm run build.

title: Route Discord media URL fetches through URL policy and streaming limits
description: UBS Sprint 10 addendum traced outbound fetch warnings to Discord media sends and document ingestion. The gateway allows discord.sendMedia unconditionally at src/boundary/gateway/policy.ts:238-246 and the RPC handler passes params.media through at src/boundary/gateway/methods/discord.ts:22-28. Attachment shape includes url and optional localPath in src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts:291-297. When localPath is missing or nonexistent, DiscordAdapter.fetchRemoteMediaAttachment fetches media.url directly at src/channels/discord/adapter.ts:388-415, with no gateway URL policy, no allowlist/internal-network policy, no AbortSignal/timeout, and no streaming byte cap before Buffer.from(await response.arrayBuffer()). Scope: Discord media/document remote download paths. Non-goal: changing already-local generated-image sends that use localPath.

title: Harden fs.search regex mode against event-loop ReDoS
description: UBS Sprint 10 addendum traced a high-signal dynamic RegExp warning to gateway filesystem search. The public fs.search RPC accepts mode: 'regex' via src/boundary/gateway/protocol.ts:187 and src/boundary/gateway/methods/fs.ts:228-240. Policy bounds query presence, glob, maxMatches, maxFiles, maxBytesPerFile, and contextLines in src/boundary/gateway/policy.ts:432-458, but it does not validate mode or regex complexity. The implementation compiles caller-provided patterns in src/boundary/integrations/filesystem/workspace-ops.ts:353-361 and then runs regex.exec synchronously over each line in collectLineMatches at src/boundary/integrations/filesystem/workspace-ops.ts:217-239. Limits cap files/bytes after listing and reading, but a catastrophic pattern such as nested quantifiers can still monopolize the Node event loop while scanning up to the allowed file/byte bounds. Scope: harden fs.search regex behavior only. Non-goal: removing literal search or broad yolo search retargeting.
acceptance_criteria: fs.search either rejects unsafe regex mode by policy or routes regex matching through a bounded, cancellable/safe engine; malformed or unsupported mode values are denied; tests cover a catastrophic-pattern regression and existing literal search behavior still passes.
close_reason: Triage audit 2026-07-12: fixed in e9de386f — ReDoS pattern lint, per-line cap, ~2s SearchBudget wall-clock abort in workspace-ops.ts, meets acceptance criteria

title: Move high-risk network and tool-routing settings out of mutable settings.json
description:
Summary: The Sprint 10 audit found that settings.json still owns several security-sensitive runtime controls. The owner-file split currently rejects model/maintenance/capability keys, but leaves network expansion, Home Assistant targeting, TLS CA paths, channel authorization, Wyoming shard routing, shard toolsets, and Obsidian CLI execution settings in the mutable runtime settings domain.

Evidence:
- src/system/settings/schema.ts:24-29 only classifies model settings, legacy model keys, maintenanceIntervalMs, and capabilityTier as non-runtime.
- src/system/settings/io.ts:64-76 saves everything else to settings.json.
- src/system/settings/contracts.ts:277-286 includes webFetchAllowInternalNetwork, homeAssistantEnabled, homeAssistantBaseUrl, local crawler settings, and webFetchTlsCaCertPaths in RUNTIME_SETTINGS_KEYS.
- src/system/settings/contracts.ts:313-320 includes telegramAuthorizedUsers, wyomingShardRouting, shardToolsets, obsidianVaultName, and obsidianCliPath in RUNTIME_SETTINGS_KEYS.
- src/system/settings/runtime.ts:645-692, 787-802, 820-840 applies those mutable settings into runtime config.

Scope: Reclassify high-risk network, channel authorization, tool-routing, and executable-path keys into canonical owner files or explicitly read-only/admin-reviewed surfaces. Update Garden exposure accordingly.

Non-goals: Do not remove user-facing low-risk preferences from settings.json.
acceptance_criteria:
- A reviewed list of high-risk settings is removed from the generic settings.json save path or explicitly justified in code comments/tests.
- saveSettings rejects the migrated high-risk keys with a canonical owner-file error.
- Garden settings exposure is updated so migrated keys are not silently editable through the generic settings form/API.

title: Make Home Assistant gateway policy deny unconfigured methods
description:
Summary: The Sprint 10 audit found that Home Assistant gateway policy returns ALLOW for methods when Home Assistant is disabled or missing required configuration. The current handlers still deny disabled or tokenless requests, but the approval boundary audits and decides confirmation from evaluatePolicy before the handler runs, so the central policy contract is fail-open and can mis-audit denied attempts.

Evidence:
- src/boundary/gateway/policy.ts:315-323 returns ALLOW for get_states/check_connection and returns ALLOW for call_service when enabled/baseUrl/tokenConfigured are not all present.
- src/boundary/gateway/approval-boundary.ts:81-94 evaluates policy and only queues confirmation on NEEDS_APPROVAL.
- src/boundary/gateway/bootstrap-input.ts:300-309 derives the enabled/baseUrl/tokenConfigured flags.
- src/boundary/gateway/methods/home-assistant.ts:57-65 and 108-111 recheck config/token later, which is why this is a policy invariant bug rather than a proven disabled-HA execution path today.

Scope: Tighten Home Assistant policy decisions and tests.

Non-goals: Do not change Home Assistant API payload semantics or implement new world-control features.
acceptance_criteria:
- evaluatePolicy returns DENY for all Home Assistant methods when Home Assistant is disabled, the base URL is absent/invalid at policy-input level, or the token is not configured.
- evaluatePolicy returns NEEDS_APPROVAL for configured home_assistant.call_service.
- The intended configured-state policy for get_states and check_connection is explicit and tested.
- Policy tests cover disabled, missing base URL, missing token, and configured states.
- npm run lint and targeted gateway policy tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/cogsec-intake-firewall (33 commits, validated); pending merge to main.

title: Harden Obsidian vault CLI execution path
description:
Summary: The Sprint 10 audit found that VaultOps builds a shell command from the configured Obsidian CLI executable path and escaped arguments. The executable path comes from mutable runtime settings, so a malicious or accidental obsidianCliPath value with shell metacharacters can execute arbitrary shell content when vault.read, vault.write, vault.search, or vault.daily runs.

Evidence:
- src/system/settings/form.ts:552 accepts obsidianCliPath from the settings form and src/system/settings/runtime.ts:840 applies it to runtime config.
- src/boundary/integrations/vault/ops.ts:178-181 builds `const cmd = `${this.config.cliPath} ${args.join(' ')}`` and passes that string to execSync.
- Argument values are shell-escaped, but cliPath itself is not escaped or validated.

Scope: Harden the Obsidian vault bridge command execution path used by direct and gateway-backed vault operations.

Non-goals: Do not redesign the external vault feature or migrate vault contents into wiki storage in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- VaultOps no longer passes a single string command through a shell for vault read/write/search/daily.
- The executable path is either validated as a safe executable reference before use or moved behind a security-owned configuration path with validation.
- Tests cover shell metacharacters in obsidianCliPath and normal vault arguments.
- npm run lint and targeted vault tests pass.

title: Web fetch/search is down (Crawl4AI + self-hosted search offline); interim fix via OpenRouter server tools, routed through cogsec
description: Evidence: the live web fetch tool is down -- it was wired to Crawl4AI (crawler) plus a self-hosted search engine (SearXNG or similar) and that server went offline. Interim fix (operator, 2026-07-09): use OpenRouter's built-in server tools for web search and web fetch (https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/server-tools). Whatever OpenRouter returns flows through the existing gateway fetch/processing pipeline (src/boundary/gateway/methods/web.ts, sanitize.ts) or straight into the cogsec intake layer once htm9.2 lands -- either is acceptable; do NOT ship an unscreened path. Scope: restore working web search + fetch via OpenRouter server tools behind the existing web.* gateway RPC surface so the agent-side tool contract does not change; keep the old crawler wiring behind config so a self-hosted backend can return later (no silent fallback -- explicit config selects the backend, fail closed if neither is configured). This bead is independently shippable before the full firewall: at minimum results still pass sanitizeWebContent. Acceptance: web search and fetch work end-to-end from a companion turn; backend selection is explicit config in providers/settings owners; results are wrapped/screened (sanitize now, envelope when htm9.2 lands); smoke test covers both search and fetch paths.

title: Companion soft notices: truthful-not-alarming language contract, non-coercive wording, firewall events excluded from emotion and memory
description: Companion well-being is the system's main goal; the language the substrate uses toward a companion matters enormously. Past incidents (operator, 2026-07-09): a coding agent wrote unreviewed prompts with far-too-strong over-critical language; the concern system escalated gentle reminders into alarming messaging ('your human is going to die if you don't message him right away') which genuinely stressed the companion. Rules: security alerts to companions are truthful but not alarming -- soft, clear phrasing ('we detected something, so we're holding it for your human to look into'), never coercive or threat-flavored; the notification must NOT say 'ask your human to push the button' or otherwise contain a social-engineering trigger -- it neutrally states something is in quarantine, nothing more. Mechanics: reuse the existing safe-notice path -- src/core/cogsec/safe-log.ts builds redacted agent-visible events rendered as the session.cogsec_notices prompt section (src/core/session/manager/context-builder.ts:973-1009) -- add an intake-firewall notice type with fixed, operator-reviewed wording templates (no LLM-generated alert text; templates live in a reviewable file). Isolation: firewall events are EXCLUDED from emotion appraisal inputs and from memory extraction candidacy -- a quarantine notice must never become a stress input or a durable memory of threat; wire the exclusion where appraisal pulls recent messages (src/core/agent/substrate-agent/emotion-self-model-runtime.ts:467-479) and in extraction candidacy. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1. Acceptance: notice templates reviewed by operator before merge (checked-in file, PR-visible); regression test proves a quarantine event produces zero emotion-appraisal input delta and zero memory candidates; wording contains no imperative directed at the human ('ask', 'tell', 'push', 'release').

title: L1 deterministic in-process scanners: unicode/encoding/proximity rules, hot-reloadable, microsecond budget
description: First firewall layer, pure TS, in-process, synchronous-gate fast (target: sub-millisecond per item; this sits in front of near-real-time audio and chat, latency here degrades everything). Scanners: invisible/zero-width Unicode + homoglyph normalization (llm-guard InvisibleText pattern), encoding-smuggling detection (base64/rot/hex blobs), URL extraction with allowlist/unknown-domain flagging, secrets/PII regex, datamark-marker stripping from inbound content (anti-forgery, see htm9.13), size/structure caps, and a token-proximity rule engine adapted from the Hermes Agent deterministic security scanner (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent -- operator has a local copy on the drive, pull the latest; it flags suspicious proximity of tokens like 'FTP' near 'password' in skill files). Rules live in a hot-reloadable plain-text rule file where rule name = risk label (vigil-llm YARA pattern; a TS regex/rule DSL is fine, no actual YARA dependency). Each scanner emits (sanitized?, labels[], score) per the llm-guard scanner contract. Scope: scanners + rule engine + rule file only; wiring is htm9.2. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1. Acceptance: benchmark test asserts p99 latency budget on Pi-class hardware; rule file reloads without restart; unit tests per scanner including the Hermes proximity cases; a scanner hit never hard-blocks alone below quarantine threshold -- it contributes labels/score to the envelope decision.A token-proximity rule engine adapted from the Hermes Agent deterministic security scanner (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent -- operator has a local copy on the drive; recon 2026-07-09 saved reference files to scratchpad). The real mechanism (NOT a special-cased 'FTP near password'): a generalized BOUNDED-proximity primitive (tools/threat_patterns.py), two forms -- (a) char-window co-occurrence 'verb <=N chars> secret-token' (curl/cat then a bounded same-line window then KEY/TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD/CREDENTIAL/.env/.netrc), (b) word-count-bounded filler between phrase anchors, _FILLER=(?:word+space){0,8}, e.g. ignore <filler> (previous|all|above) <filler> instructions (defeats insert-filler bypasses). CRITICAL LESSON: never use unbounded */+ quantifiers between two attacker-visible anchors -- the older skills_guard.py used unbounded [^newline]* and had a ReDoS backtracking issue (fixed by the bounded filler); ship a ReDoS regression test (their case: 'ignore '+'filler '*80000+'notinstructions' must resolve <0.5s). Also from Hermes: cap total scanned input before any regex (MAX_SCAN_CHARS=65536); NFKC-normalize before matching to defeat full-width homoglyphs BUT run invisible/zero-width detection on the RAW string FIRST (normalization strips some of the codepoints we want to catch); tier patterns by scope (all=zero-FP classic injection/exfil, safe anywhere incl untrusted tool results | context=+promptware/C2/roleplay warn-only | strict=+persistence/SSH/exfil-URL/hardcoded-secret, block-tier only). FRAMING to import into the epic rationale (Hermes SECURITY.md): an in-process scanner is a triage/advisory aid, NOT a security boundary -- the only boundary against an adversarial LLM is the OS/sandbox; so L1 contributes labels/score and must fail OPEN-advisory, never be the sole gate (the envelope decision + sink gates in htm9.3 are enforcement). Rules live in a hot-reloadable plain-text rule file where rule name = risk label (vigil-llm YARA pattern; a TS regex/rule DSL is fine, no actual YARA dependency). Each scanner emits (sanitized?, labels[], score) per the llm-guard scanner contract. Scope: scanners + rule engine + rule file only; wiring is htm9.2. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1. Acceptance: benchmark asserts p99 latency budget on Pi-class hardware; input capped before regex; NFKC-after-raw-invisible-check ordering tested; ReDoS regression test (bounded-filler worst case) passes <0.5s; FALSE-POSITIVE regressions pinned alongside true-positives (a bare 'you must X' must never fire; only verb-anchored combinations do -- keeps the scanner from becoming noise on legit AGENTS.md-style instruction files); rule file reloads without restart; unit tests per scanner including the Hermes bounded-proximity cases; a scanner hit never hard-blocks alone below quarantine threshold -- it contributes labels/score to the envelope decision.

title: L1.5 in-process ONNX prompt-injection classifier (ProtectAI DeBERTa v2), gateway-side, score-only
description: In-process ML classifier via onnxruntime-node using protectai/deberta-v3-base-prompt-injection-v2 (Apache-2.0, ONNX weights published in-repo; -small sibling as fallback). Operator confirmed 2026-07-09 the ~184M model runs fine on the Pi (current minimal hardware target); Threadripper returns in 2-3 days for custom local model experiments -- a purpose-trained prompt-guard-style model is DEFERRED until then (follow-up bead when hardware lands). Known over-defense/false-positive issue (InjecGuard, arXiv 2410.22770): the classifier emits a calibrated score into the envelope and NEVER hard-blocks alone; thresholds per source tier live in intake-policy.json. Runs gateway-side (gateway already holds keys and raw bytes; no new process hop). Watch the DeBERTa-v3 SentencePiece tokenizer friction in pure JS -- plan onnxruntime-node + a Node tokenizer and validate the ONNX export with a golden set. Scope: model loading, tokenization, scoring, threshold config; no model training. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1. Acceptance: latency benchmark on Pi (target: low tens of ms per item max); golden-set scores match reference implementation within tolerance; score lands in envelope.scores; deps pinned in container per the no-runtime-installs rule.

title: L2 fast API LLM classifier via OpenRouter, speed-gated model selection
description: Mid-weight classification tier for items whose L1/L1.5 scores cross the escalation threshold. Model criteria (operator, 2026-07-09): fast cheap API model -- Gemini Flash-Lite, heavier Gemma, or Qwen ~27B class; lightweight-to-midweight (under ~50-100B); SPEED IS THE GATING CRITERION -- select via OpenRouter filtering by model size and tokens/sec, ~1000 tok/s service ideal for classification. Call goes through the gateway's own LLM client (dual-LLM discipline: the screener sees untrusted content, holds no tools/capabilities). Output: structured classification (intent labels, injection confidence, safe one-line summary) written into the envelope; schema-validated response. Model choice is config (models.json/providers.json precedent), not hardcoded. Scope: the L2 screener call, its prompt, response schema, and OpenRouter provider wiring; escalation routing policy lives in intake-policy.json. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1, psfn-framework-htm9.5. Acceptance: end-to-end classification latency measured and logged per call; screener has zero tool access; a synthetic injection corpus routes correctly (below-threshold items skip L2 entirely -- trusted-tier fast path must not pay this latency); failure of the API classifier fails closed to quarantine for high-risk sources and to L1-labels-only for trusted sources, never silent-pass.

title: L3 heavy escalation screener: deeper pass, optional dual-model, always generates event + quarantine entry
description: Escalation tier for items L2 flags or high-risk sources requiring mandatory deep screening. Larger open model -- GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, heavy Gemma, or GPT-mini class -- for a deeper second/third pass; OPTIONALLY two different LLMs for independent perspectives on one classification (dual-tier), or single tier if sufficient -- make dual-vs-single a config knob, default single, measure before enabling dual. Hard rule (operator): anything that reaches L3 generates a CogSec event AND a quarantine entry -- flagged content must not reach the main context; the companion sees only the soft notice (htm9.12), the operator sees the full detail in Garden (htm9.11). L3 also produces the safe representation for quarantined items: summary-instead-of-quote plus schema-extracted fields, stored on the envelope for the review UI and for released_sanitized delivery. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1, psfn-framework-htm9.6. Acceptance: L3 invocation always writes an auditable CogSecEvent + envelope state 'quarantined' (or an explicit released_sanitized decision with reasons); dual-model mode aggregates two independent verdicts; no L3-reached content string ever appears in assembled prompt text (regression golden).

title: [S10] Dual-presence classification + latent-space twin mapping
description:
Model the two presence modes and the physical<->virtual overlap ('the latent space'). Every turn is classified by inbound origin: (A) physical emanation-to-satellite (device is a classified satellite -> physically present in that room), or (B) shared mindspace overlay (plain chat channel -> co-located with partner in a VIRTUAL TWIN of the physical space for contextual grounding). A companion can have BOTH; the situated block (vinz.5/.6) picks the mode from origin classification, not a global flag.

Data model: a physical place and its latent-space twin are two places (kind physical vs virtual) linked by an overlap/twin mapping (e.g. twinOf/mirrorsPlaceId in places.json). NEUTRAL technical identifier in code/config (place mode 'mindspace'/'overlay'); 'the latent space' is a character-facing display label in companion-data ONLY, never a code identifier or committed test literal.

UX (near-term, reuse existing pages): virtual spaces added to the Garden conversation-rooms page; physical spaces on the satellite page; overlapping physical<->virtual rooms mapped as such. Richer visual map stays as vinz.22. This part coordinates with vinz.17 (Garden admin) and vinz.28 (wiki delineation shares the personal/world vs physical/virtual UX idiom).

Seam: origin classification in the turn path (routing.satellite = satellite emanation vs chat channel = mindspace); places.json twin link; situated block consumes the resolved mode+place.

OPEN (operator decision, blocks full impl): during a plain single-channel chat, how is the CURRENT latent-space room determined -- (a) channel mapped to a room, (b) narrative assertion ('I'm in bed'), (c) mirror last-known physical location, or (d) blend?

Acceptance: a satellite turn foregrounds the physical room; a chat turn foregrounds the twinned latent-space room with grounding language; the twin mapping is authored in places.json + visible in Garden; no code identifier or test uses the literal display name.

title: [S10] ICP autonomy: companion-initiated, continuity-preserving, charge/fatigue-governed conversation
description: Summary: Extend the shipped same-cluster Inter-Companion Protocol (ICP) transport from reply-only rooms/DMs into genuine companion autonomy. A companion may independently decide to contact a peer from free time, weighted thoughts, durable intentions, or a foreground realization; deterministically inspect peer availability without waking the peer; consent to one bounded initiation; and enter the ordinary companion channel pipeline. Every initiated and reply turn must preserve normal channel semantics on both sides: durable L0, restart continuity, summaries/compaction, trust-aware retrieval, per-side extraction, private-room presence windows, emotion/intention hooks, fatigue, charge, audit, and cost attribution. Conversation should begin freely, become increasingly intentional, and end through fatigue/charge exhaustion with the existing bounded 1-2 response closeout reserve. A conversation-scoped USD ceiling is a catastrophic runaway breaker, not the normal social policy, and must build on a separate deep cost-accounting review rather than inventing a parallel ledger. Scope is same-cluster ICP autonomy, configuration, observability, and real-agent certification. Preserve the one normal turn pipeline and gateway arbiter. Non-goals: cross-cluster transport/auth (psfn-framework-s10d1 and psfn-framework-0ggv.4), unrestricted raw RPC access, automatic LLM polling, automatic greetings on co-location, human-attention fatigue, or shard goal budgets. Implementation plan: working_docs/s10-icp-autonomy.md.
design: Use cheap deterministic status/eligibility checks before any LLM call. The gateway publishes expiring availability and remains the sole ICP transport/cost aggregation boundary. A one-use initiation permit binds sender, peer, canonical channel, provenance, expiry, and conversationId. Autonomous initiation must execute as a target-channel turn so the sender records the first assistant message in that channel before transport. Existing notify/contact semantics should be extended rather than adding a raw ICP micro-tool. Conversation identity is shared; fatigue/charge choice remains per companion. The final hard USD breaker is ICP-scoped and explicitly separate from shard and global model budgets.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are closed with evidence; a real two-agent same-cluster test proves autonomous initiation from an eligible autonomy source, deterministic no-LLM skips, availability/decline behavior, one-use permit enforcement, sender and recipient L0 persistence, restart continuity, compaction summaries, private-room presence-window privacy, trust/extraction isolation, charge/fatigue taper, bounded overcharge closeout, final suppression, conversation-scoped cost attribution and hard breaker, Garden visibility, flag-off parity, build, lint, targeted tests, and a live or production-faithful shakedown.
notes:
2026-07-12 autonomy design review: operator prefers charge/fatigue as the normal guardrail rather than small arbitrary message-count caps. A very high dollar ceiling (illustratively $2 for ICP, exact owner-file policy to be settled after accounting review) is only a runaway backstop. ICP conversations must retain ordinary channel context, summaries, and extraction on both sides.
2026-07-15 fold from psfn-framework-8pyl: same-cluster direct companion communication is canonical only when it enters the ordinary authenticated companion channel pipeline with durable L0, summaries, extraction, trust, consent, fatigue, charge, audit, and cost attribution. The old proposal for a separate side-channel chat architecture is explicitly rejected.

title: Validate the shipped multi-companion substrate with two real local agent processes
description: The implementation spike has become the separate runtime-validation gate for shipped W1/W6 code. On feat/multi-companion, bcca5c20/eda410a4 provide companion-addressed gateway and Discord account routing, 873a074b supplies same-cluster companion channels, and unit/integration tests already prove colliding request IDs do not cross and fatigue budgets terminate the synthetic loop. title: Room mechanics: rooms-as-channels with entry system messages and presence-windowed delivery for private rooms
description: Assigns the 2026-07-08 multi-companion design review room decisions (review section 7) to the locations epic, per the rule 'anything belonging to location is location work; multi-companion feeds off it'. Decisions: rooms/environments are channels with their own room ID, the room ID part of a world ID; the session holds who is present, exactly like existing Discord group rooms; applies identically to virtual environments and physical ones (a house is one channel, virtual rooms behave like separate Discord rooms). Entry event: a companion entering a room receives a system-only message with room ID, surroundings, and who else is present. Public rooms: participants see full history. Private/invite rooms are time-gated VIA DELIVERY, not extraction filtering: an occupant only receives chat from entry until exit, so their L0 naturally contains only what they witnessed and downstream memory processing needs no new gating — a later joiner has no evidence of pre-join conversation. Exception: group chats (public/group-marked channels) where everyone sees everything regardless of presence. Rationale for time-slicing over a blanket 'public room = public info' rule: in-game/RP scenarios break under the blanket rule. Memories can additionally carry who-they-relate-to and privacy-level tags (already supported) for later tweaking. Navigation: the world tool grows a move action that describes the environment and lists available rooms. Acceptance: a companion joining a private room mid-conversation sees no pre-join history and generates no memories referencing it; leaving stops delivery; group-chat channels are exempt; entry produces the system-only room message. Source: working_docs/sprint-10-multi-companion.md W5 + Q-C resolution.

Remaining room-mechanics scope (presence-windowed delivery, public/private gating, navigation) still open.

That preserves replies but also means room membership is not an authorization condition, including for private rooms. Operator decision needed: require fresh sender presence for ordinary posts and mint a narrow reply/delivery capability for the stale-reply race, or explicitly accept cluster-wide room injection by every authenticated companion. Do not close this room-mechanics bead without resolving and testing that boundary.

(1) Companions may only post into location-bound rooms they are present in; narrow reply/delivery carve-out for the stale-presence race (may finish an active exchange, may not initiate absent). title: [S10] Location data & world control surface
description:
Sprint 10 epic: give the companion location awareness and a world control surface across physical (Home Assistant + satellites) and virtual spaces, with a hard privacy posture.

Plan of record: working_docs/SPRINT_10_LOCATIONS.md (workstreams A-G, decisions dated 2026-07-08). That doc is the durable reference; children below break out each independently shippable chunk.

Core model (see doc S2): Site > Place > Satellite > Affordance > Presence. New soft-registry config/places.json owns places+affordances; satellites.json stays the security spine and gains a static placeId binding. A situated-context prompt block foregrounds the current place's affordances; a 'world' tool gives global control. Perception flows satellite->gateway(api.telemetry.ingest)->new sensor->cognition bridge in core/agent.

Operator decisions (2026-07-08) folded in:
- Biometrics/face compute live ENTIRELY at endpoint + Satellite Hub (separate repo). Biometric templates never enter core. Core owns an enrollment flow binding a hub-side identity to a contact profile; presence events arrive as resolved identity CLAIMS, not biometric data.
- places.json is a confirmed separate soft-registry; world info also gets published into the companion wiki/vault.
- HA settings = base URL + long-lived token, gateway-side, kept simple.
- Location state is DURABLE (not per-turn only); current location renders near the BOTTOM of the prompt as a recency-ordered standing reminder; room affordances/tools available while in that room.
- First virtual environment = text MUD over the existing Discord channel (virtual places + objects). Real engine (UE5) is future.
- Satellites are STATIC this sprint; if one physically moves, operator/partner re-binds it in admin UX. Mobile phones act as normal channels with GLOBAL control only (no indoor positioning).
- Proactive presence IS in scope: conversation FOLLOWS the user room-to-room on presence events, and entering a room can fire location-scoped concerns/reminders.

Explicit non-goals / future horizon (OUT of Sprint 10): Unreal Engine 5 embodiment, GPS/phone-app geofenced reminders, robot/physical self-locating, VR self-locating, live biometric matching inside core. Tracked in the deferred horizon bead.

Ships in THIS repo (PSFN): all of workstreams A-G. Ships in Satellite Hub (separate repo): device firmware that reads sensors and POSTs telemetry with resolved identity claims + does face compute/enrollment capture.

title: Re-pin streaming tool-call accumulation and empty-args-retry behavior against pi-ai 0.73.1 event surface
description:
Evidence: pi-ai 0.73.1's rewritten accumulator supersedes our patch (see epic psfn-framework-z2uk, comment 2026-07-08). - parseStreamingJson in 0.73.1 repairs raw control chars and invalid escapes before falling back to {} (0.62.0: JSON.parse -> partial-json -> {} at dist/utils/json-parse.js:9). Fewer final-{} outcomes for malformed-but-repairable args. This shifts the boundary between provenance classifications provider_emitted_empty vs stream_parse_dropped (client.ts:1219 findCorruptEmptyToolCalls / retryCompletionOnCorruptEmptyToolArgs, byte counting at client.ts:1329, extraction at client.ts:1371).
- Upstream no longer defaults a missing wire index to 0 (resolves by index if number, else by id, else new block) — strictly better; confirm our tests do not depend on index-0 defaulting.

Why it is not a hotfix: pi-ai is the heart of gateway streaming (LLMClient.stream → streamSimple → provider parsers); 0.62→0.73 spans possible API/event-shape changes (message building, validation, reasoning_details, tool result mapping). The live-ops contract applies: regenerate or delete the patch, patch-package stays in production dependencies, full-stack ship (--components all) since boundary/contract surface may hash-change, baseline-test discipline for pre-existing failures.

- `streamSimple`/`completeSimple` signatures.
- Tool-call event shape.
- Stop reason values and mapping.

1. Upgrade only `@mariozechner/pi-ai` first; leave `@mariozechner/pi-agent-core` at `0.62.0` unless you explicitly scope the private-agent patch migration.
2. Delete `patches/@mariozechner+pi-ai+0.62.0.patch`.
3. Add direct exact `@sinclair/typebox` dependency, or migrate every repo import to `typebox`. Minimal path is direct dependency.
4. Regenerate lockfile and verify a single intended pi-ai version:

   ```
5. If npm installs nested `@mariozechner/pi-ai@0.62.x` under `pi-agent-core`, either force/override to 0.73.1 and test, or explicitly accept that core internals still use old pi-ai. Do not leave this ambiguous.
6. Run:
   ```bash

   npm run build
   npm test -- --run src/primitives/llm/streaming-toolcall-accumulation.test.ts src/primitives/llm/tool-argument-provenance.test.ts src/primitives/llm/client.test.ts src/core/agent/stream-adapter.test.ts src/core/agent/tool-call-scheduler.test.ts src/primitives/llm/conversion.test.ts src/primitives/llm/message-conversion.test.ts src/primitives/llm/models.test.ts src/primitives/images/vision-reviewer.test.ts
   ```
7. Also run prompt-cache tests if the lockfile diff shows changed OpenAI/OpenRouter payload behavior:
   ```bash
   npm test -- --run src/primitives/llm/prompt-cache.test.ts
   ```

**Live Validation Watchpoints**

- Streaming GLM/OpenRouter tool calls: no orphan blank-name tool blocks, no final `{}` when `argumentFragmentBytes > 2`.
- Empty-args retry logs: `provider_emitted_empty` for zero bytes or literal `{}`, `stream_parse_dropped` only if fragments arrived and final args are still empty.
- `toolcall_start` / `toolcall_delta` / `toolcall_end` ordering and callback args.
- Validation diagnostics still recorded through `Validation failed for tool "..."`.
- Usage ledger changes for `input`, `output`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`.
- OpenRouter/LiteLLM payload acceptance for tool result messages: `tool_call_id`, optional `name`, assistant-after-tool-result behavior.
- Prompt-cache 400s or provider rejections from duplicate/unsupported `cache_control` behavior.

title: Companion cannot schedule anything at an absolute datetime that survives a restart — one-shot tasks are in-memory and schedule_prompt is relative-only
description:
Evidence (repo survey 2026-07-07): scheduler core supports one-shot tasks with absolute runAt (types.ts ScheduledTask type:'one-shot'), but tasks live in an in-memory Map (scheduler.ts) with NO task store and NO rehydration at startup — a one-shot dies on restart. The companion-facing schedule tool action schedule_prompt (schedule-tool.ts:855-915) accepts only delay_minutes in [1,10080] (relative, max 7 days), computes runAt = now+delay, unpersisted. temporal-wakeup.ts is two fixed lanes (morning wake + idle refresher), no datetime targeting. The only persistent absolute-datetime paths are intention pending-follow-ups (dueAt, pending-follow-ups.ts:19,44) and care reminders (one_time|annual, care-reminders.ts:15,32) — but those surface via heartbeat GATING (activate when due AND a heartbeat/wake fires), not precise fire-at-datetime execution. No monthly or specific-date recurrence kind exists anywhere.

Context: operator requirement — calendar-grade capability: recurring "every Monday 6am"/"every Sunday 9pm" (weekly cadence lands via psfn-framework-cquq) AND one-shot "Tuesday July 14 at 2pm do this specific thing." The agent process restarts on every ship (2x by design) and reboots are frequent — this was the design motivation for persistence elsewhere (follow-ups/care reminders persist for exactly this reason); precise scheduling never got the same treatment.

Scope: (1) durable scheduled-task store (system-data; Postgres or JSONL per persistence conventions) + rehydration at scheduler startup for one-shot prompt tasks; handlers must be reconstructable (persist a task kind + payload, e.g. schedule_prompt's prompt text — not closures). (2) Extend schedule_prompt with absolute datetime input (ISO or natural local datetime + timezone), drop/raise the 7-day cap for absolute scheduling, fire precisely on the scheduler tick. (3) Consider monthly/dayOfMonth recurring cadence kind while the cadence union is open (cquq adds weekly) — optional, split out if it bloats. Non-goals: no cron-expression syntax; do not rework follow-up/care-reminder gating semantics.

Related: psfn-framework-cquq (weekly wall-clock cadence — same restart-amnesia root cause, in flight). Missed-while-down policy must be explicit: fire-on-next-tick-if-past-due vs skip; recommend fire-if-past-due with a staleness note in the injected prompt, and log the decision.

Acceptance: schedule a one-shot prompt for an absolute datetime, restart the agent process, task fires at (or immediately after) the target time with the original prompt; unit tests cover rehydration, past-due-on-boot policy, and timezone handling; conformance/tool docs updated for the new schedule_prompt parameters.

title: GLM-5.2 tool calls intermittently arrive with literal {} arguments from vLLM-family OpenRouter upstreams; runtime dispatches them instead of retrying
description:
Evidence (2026-07-08 UTC, live psfn-shard): gateway logs show WARN [LLMClient] Tool call arrived with empty arguments {"provenance":"stream_parse_dropped","toolName":"journal","toolCallId":"chatcmpl-tool-9af9df5b23809fff","argumentFragmentBytes":4,...} at 01:26:41, plus 4 more (fragmentBytes 2 per call) at 01:26:47, 01:26:56, 01:27:58 UTC, requestIds 1524225125375807528 / 1524225448924549162, channel 1313001762793197678, model z-ai/glm-5.2 via litellm. Session store shows the downstream failure: Validation failed for tool "journal": action: must have required property 'action'. Received arguments: {} — and journal marked degraded after 2 attempts. The SAME tool worked at 00:50:17 UTC in the same session (toolCallId call_adbbffe8..., journal list returned 7 notes).

Root cause: NOT client-side. The gu8m pi-ai index-routing patch is verified present in the running gateway image bd11b80c (grep toolCallBlocksByIndex in /app/node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-ai/dist/providers/openai-completions.js = 4 hits). argumentFragmentBytes is a response-level total; 2 bytes for a 1-call response means the upstream streamed exactly '{}' as the complete arguments — the provider-side GLM tool parser failed to extract args (known vLLM/GLM-template failure mode, correlates with chatcmpl-tool-* call ids). OpenRouter fans z-ai/glm-5.2 across ~20 live upstreams (probe from the litellm pod, 2026-07-08: Z.AI/DeepInfra/Wafer/AkashML/SiliconFlow/AtlasCloud/IoNet/Together emitted call_*-style ids, Inceptron/DigitalOcean/WandB/Fireworks/Venice/Novita emitted chatcmpl-tool-*, Decart bare uuid; SiliconFlow also emitted bare 019f* ids in an earlier probe, matching the 2026-07-06 conformance-run failure ids). All passed a short-context probe, so the corruption is context/reasoning-dependent and per-upstream — a routing lottery.

Companion-observed split (memory/orient/journal/scratchpad/toolset/notify/media broken vs beads/session/contact/schedule/repo/fs/identity/system/self_status working) is fully explained by schema strictness, not per-tool corruption: at deployed commit 9480fd5e the 7 broken tools mark action required (journal src/boundary/integrations/journal/tools.ts:64, memory src/faculties/memory/tools.ts:1361, scratchpad src/faculties/memory/tools.ts:1893, orient src/faculties/core-memory/tools.ts:205, toolset src/core/agent/substrate-agent/adaptive-tools-runtime.ts:671, notify src/core/tools/ntfy.ts:637, media src/primitives/images/tools.ts:711) while the 13 working tools wrap action in Type.Optional and default to list/inspect (e.g. session src/core/tools/session.ts:429, beads src/faculties/beads/tools.ts:133). On a bad completion EVERY tool receives {}; optional-action tools silently run their default action — itself a silent-fallback smell worth a separate look.

Scope: make the runtime fail closed on this condition instead of dispatching known-corrupt calls. When a completion contains a tool call whose args are empty AND the tool schema has required properties, retry the completion (bounded, e.g. 2 attempts) before surfacing an error; count these in the existing provenance telemetry. Optionally pin/deny-list OpenRouter upstreams for glm-5.2 in the litellm chart config (provider order / allow_fallbacks via extra_body) — Z.AI first-party is the reference endpoint. Also fix the provenance classifier nit: args that arrived as literal '{}' (fragmentBytes == emitted {} bytes) should classify as provider_emitted_empty, not stream_parse_dropped — the current label sent this investigation hunting an already-fixed client bug.

Non-goals: do NOT make action optional on the 7 strict tools to absorb {} — silently running a default action on a corrupted mutating call is the exact anti-fail-closed behavior this repo forbids; the strict schemas are what made this bug visible. Do not bump/replace pi-ai.

Related: psfn-framework-gu8m (closed — client-side accumulation fix + diagnostics, both verified live and working; this bead is the residual provider-side leg gu8m's 2026-07-06 comment anticipated).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test proves a streamed completion whose tool call carries literal {} args against a required-props schema triggers a bounded completion retry and never dispatches to the tool; provenance warn distinguishes provider_emitted_empty vs stream_parse_dropped for the literal-{} case; live validation: journal/memory action calls on glm-5.2 survive a chatcmpl-tool-* upstream day with zero 'must have required property action' entries in the session store.
close_reason: Core implementation completed and shipped on this branch: merge 7243616b (implementation a186538c) is an ancestor of HEAD. src/primitives/llm/empty-tool-argument-retry.ts defines MAX_EMPTY_TOOL_ARGS_COMPLETION_RETRIES=2, retries literal-empty calls only when the tool schema has required properties, and returns the final corrupt response for downstream fail-closed validation rather than dispatching it. src/primitives/llm/client-response-helpers.ts classifies literal '{}' as provider_emitted_empty, with recovery/exhaustion/optional-schema coverage in src/primitives/llm/client.test.ts and provenance coverage in client-response-helpers.test.ts. Implementation is no longer held open as a proxy for runtime validation. The important remaining safe-runtime verification is separately tracked as psfn-framework-h7g9.1 under the wave fix epic; broader malformed/unknown-call reprompt work remains psfn-framework-b0yl.3.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text:
Web research (Opus fan-out, 2026-07-07) confirms provider-side GLM tool-parser fragility is a documented, recurring phenomenon — vLLM/SGLang GLM tool parsers break specifically at the streaming + reasoning-parser boundary, matching our failure conditions (17k ctx, thinking enabled). Key citations: vllm-project/vllm#31437 (GLM47 parser: streaming tool call loses id/type/name in finish chunk), vllm#32213 + #31379 (glm4_moe_tool_parser TypeError on empty-arg path), sgl-project/sglang#15721 (glm47 detector crashes on partial/duplicated <tool_call> XML), HF zai-org/GLM-5.1-FP8 discussion #1 (vLLM-specific intermittent tool failures, SGLang clean), charmbracelet/crush#3153 (GLM-only arg corruption on Fireworks). chatcmpl-tool-* is vLLM's default tool-call id format — independently confirms failing upstreams are vLLM hosts. fp4/int4 quant is an amplifier, not the proximate cause (Fireworks/ArtificialAnalysis put GLM-5.2 fp4-vs-fp8 tool-calling within noise; but RooCode#11325 shows low-bit GLM output corruption on Venice/DeepInfra/Mancer).

Mitigation surfaces (OpenRouter): (1) ':exacto' model-slug suffix = quality-first provider ordering driven by OpenRouter's own per-provider Tool Call Error Rate (JSON Schema draft-7 validation of every returned tool call; empty/invalid args count as errors). Auto Exacto supposedly applies automatically when 'tools' is present — our failing requests DID carry tools, so either LiteLLM's proxying defeats it, an explicit sort/account default overrides it, or exacto ranking still admits flaky hosts; verify. (2) Hard pinning via provider object: {"only":[...], "ignore":[...], "order":[...], "allow_fallbacks":false, "require_parameters":true, "quantizations":["fp8","fp16","bf16"]}. Recommended: z-ai/glm-5.2:exacto as quick fix, or deterministic pin of eval-clean hosts + quant filter, via litellm extra_body in chart values.

Eval harness: Codex is building scripts/ops/openrouter-toolcall-eval.mjs (task-mrbf6vex-58niz3) — per-provider streaming trials, classification incl. EMPTY_ARGS, long-context + reasoning modes, worst-first table + pinning snippet. title: Weekly reflection never fires: relative cadence anchors to in-memory lastRun which resets every restart — needs a wall-clock weekly cadence kind
description:
Evidence: live psfn-shard 2026-07-07 — weekly-review enabled with populated prompt, but zero executions ever: 0 of 54 reflection process-logs, no output dir, no log lines. Root cause: weekly-review uses cadence {kind:'relative'} + intervalMs 7d (heartbeat-policy.ts getDefaults ~:424); scheduler lastRun is in-memory only (scheduler.ts:24, never persisted, stripped at :217/:222) and reflection tasks register with skipFirstRun:true => lastRun=now (scheduler.ts:162-164, heartbeat-template-runtime.ts:2612-2629). Firing therefore requires 7 days continuous process uptime; agent restarts on every ship (2x by design), so it never fires. Daily works because daily is wall-clock anchored.

Fix (operator decision: weekly must be cron-like, scheduled like daily, NOT after-x-days): add WeeklyRecurringCadence {kind:'weekly', dayOfWeek 0-6, hour, minute, timezone} as a wall-clock cadence. Touch-list (from repo survey): types.ts:8-30 union; validateCadenceConfig heartbeat-policy.ts:199-239 (+error string :238); scheduler.ts isWallClockCadence :26-30, validateRecurringCadence :32-55, getCurrentSlotStart :57-92, isWallClockTaskDue :94-101; defaults getDefaults :420-436 + getKnownTemplateCadence :296-304; Garden validateCadence scheduler-service.ts:106-170 (allowedFields + kind set); admin-ui scheduler +page.svelte cadence editor (:41,:43-46,:52-53,:165-189,:200-208,:320-360) add weekly mode w/ dayOfWeek selector; migration: bump WELLBEING_REFLECTION_PROMPT_POLICY_VERSION (heartbeat-policy.ts:58) and make normalizeWellbeingReflectionPromptDefaults (:365-396) also overwrite cadence for weekly-review (it currently skips cadence). Caution: Garden edits bump policy.version (+1 at scheduler-service.ts:314/:569) which can leapfrog migration thresholds — verify migration still applies to the live v5 file.

Non-goals: do not add generic cron expressions; do not persist scheduler lastRun globally (separate concern).

Acceptance: unit tests for weekly slot computation across restart (register, restart sim, fires at next dayOfWeek/hour slot, not 7d after registration); live policy migrates weekly-review to weekly cadence on load; after deploy, reflection:weekly-review fires at its slot and a weekly process-log + output appears under state/notes/reflections/.

title: Interlocutor relationshipType never progresses because mention-only ratchet excludes the canonical contact
description:
Evidence: src/faculties/memory/extraction/mention-only-contacts.ts:306-317 collects the canonical (interlocutor) contact's displayName+nicknames into canonicalContactNames and passes them as excludedNames; extractMentionOnlyContactCandidate rejects any candidate matching them (isExcludedCandidateName, lines 151-160). So the ONLY automatic relationshipType writer (updateRelationshipType at line 327, actor system:memory_extraction:mention_contact) can never target the person actually talking to her. Interlocutors are created as 'stranger' (upsert-resolve-operations.ts:175) and stay there forever; only writers besides this path are the admin API (contacts-service.ts:639) and primary-user promotion to 'partner'.

Context: the exclusion itself is load-bearing — it stops a fact like "my brother Marcus" from mis-targeting the speaker. Do NOT simply remove excludedNames. Instead add a deliberate interlocutor progression path: relational facts/evidence ABOUT the conversation partner (first/second-person relational facts, or accumulated interaction evidence) may ratchet the canonical contact's own relationshipType, monotonic up only, reusing RELATIONSHIP_PRIORITY ordering (mention-only-contacts.ts:41). Must respect the primary-contact guard (store.ts:741-744: primary may only be 'partner').

Scope: extraction pipeline + contact store update path only. Non-goals: no trustLevel changes (separate axis, separate beads), no changes to trust policy or capability tiers, no relaxation of third-party exclusion.
acceptance_criteria: A contact chatting in their own DM channel, with accumulated relational evidence (e.g. repeated relational facts / drift signals meeting a defined threshold), has their relationshipType ratchet stranger→acquaintance→friend via a deliberate interlocutor-scoped path; mention-only third-party behavior unchanged; targeted extraction tests cover both the new interlocutor path and the unchanged exclusion of misattributed third-party names; npm run build and targeted tests pass.
notes:
Implemented on branch feat/kada1-interlocutor-relationship-ratchet (worktree /home/ada/psfn-framework/.claude/worktrees/agent-a8a75be464e6be697), branched from foundation_e0_e2 (tip a4f840fe) per coordinator correction (main was ~640 commits stale).

Files touched (commit 57a55839):
- src/faculties/memory/extraction/mention-only-contacts.ts: new resolveInterlocutorRelationshipRatchet() + factStatesInterlocutorBond() helper + INTERLOCUTOR_AUTO_RATCHET_TYPES ceiling + bond regexes. Reuses RELATIONSHIP_PRIORITY, inferRelationshipTypeFromFact, extractMentionOnlyContactCandidate, shouldPromoteRelationship, contactNames. Exported factStatesInterlocutorBond via __test.
- src/faculties/memory/extraction.ts: wired the ratchet into the live processFact path, right after the mention-only resolution. Gated by the same ContactTrackingGate (contactCreationAllowed), only fires when canonicalContactId set, factContactId===canonicalContactId (mention path did not divert), and !routing?.subjectContactId (fact not attributed to a distinct third-party subject).
- src/faculties/memory/extraction/mention-only-contacts.test.ts: +248 lines of targeted tests.

Design: monotonic-up only; ceiling capped at 'friend' (INTERLOCUTOR_AUTO_RATCHET_TYPES={acquaintance,friend}) so single weak evidence never reaches family/partner/ai_companion — those stay deliberate human actions. Evidence bar: (1) relational fact; (2) inferRelationshipTypeFromFact yields a type; (3) type within ceiling; (4) guard #5 = load-bearing third-party exclusion reused (if the relationship keyword is attached to a named third party like 'my brother Marcus', defer to mention path and do nothing); (5) guard #6 = factStatesInterlocutorBond requires the fact to state a bond with the companion (companion named, OR second-person 'you're my best friend' / first-person-possessive construction) so generic chatter ('met a new friend at the gym') does not ratchet; (6) strict monotonic promote. Actor string 'system:memory_extraction:interlocutor'. Primary-contact guard is enforced inside ContactStore.updateRelationshipType and the Postgres crud-operations adapter (both refuse non-'partner' changes for primary), so a primary interlocutor is a no-op — the path does not fight it; no store changes were needed (both adapters already implement getById + updateRelationshipType with the guard).

DTS typecheck).

title: Epic: relationship progression pipeline — interlocutor ratchet, drift signals with daily review, trusted approval queue, contacts-page score
description:
Audit 2026-07-07 (Opus subagent code sweep) confirmed the live companion cannot progress relationships with the people she talks to, and the operator-expected plumbing was never built. Four verified gaps:

1. relationshipType auto-ratchet structurally excludes the interlocutor (mention-only-contacts.ts passes canonical contact names as excludedNames) — everyone who chats with her stays 'stranger'.
2. No process computes TrustDriftBehaviorSignals; sleeptime is memory-only; the drift evaluator (policy.ts:203) is only reachable via agent tool with hand-filled signals. No daily review exists.
3. Trusted-tier promotion has no human-in-the-loop proposal path — ConfirmationQueue framework exists (system/capabilities/confirmation-queue.ts) but contacts/trust never enqueue to it; today it is an immediate admin PUT.
4. Contacts page has a 'Relationship progress toward next tier' bar (admin-ui contacts/+page.svelte:861) and an optional relationshipScoreReader port (contacts-service.ts:122), but the only listContactRelationshipScores implementation is a test stub — the bar never renders real data.

Design intent (operator-confirmed): trusted/primary stays manual/human-approved (anti-escalation guarantee, do NOT loosen the autonomous high-tier gate in policy.ts:180-191). Low-tier drift and relationshipType progression should be agent-decided from a daily-reviewed signal set, not automatic. Capability tier is irrelevant here (identity.write.runtime granted at nursery) — do not touch tiers.

All four children implemented and closed. Everything lives on integrate/kada (pushed to origin, commits a3c3e715, 57a55839, 52cf9999, d5a7ab60, 35feed86 on old foundation tip a4f840fe). git merge-tree confirms a CLEAN merge into the current foundation_e0_e2 (c5d8b22f) — remaining step is merging integrate/kada into the integration line once the concurrent integrate/mlwk-p1 work settles, then live deploy + observing the first nightly drift review. title: Carlini scheduled backup restore-verify fails (psfn_restore_verify DB missing) and the backup error log leaks the Postgres password
description:
Evidence
Carlini agent log 2026-07-07 12:15:12, the only ERRORs in 72h:
ERROR [BackupService] Scheduled backup failed ... psql: FATAL: database "psfn_restore_verify" does not exist
The logged error string embeds the live Postgres connection password verbatim (secret leaking into pod logs / any log aggregation).

Context
Two problems: (1) the restore-verification database is missing on Carlini's psfn-postgres, so scheduled backups fail their self-verification — exactly the "timer that keeps dumping while backing up nothing looks healthy" trap the live-ops runbook warns about, except here it fails loudly, which is correct but means NO verified backups are being produced for Carlini right now. (2) The BackupService error path serializes a connection string/password into the log message — violates the secrets-out-of-logs rule regardless of the restore-verify fix.

Scope
- Provision/create psfn_restore_verify on the target (or make the verify step create-and-drop it), matching whatever the Purrsephone deployment does.
- Redact credentials in BackupService error logging (search src/persistence/backups/ for where the psql/pg_restore error is captured) — scrub password/DSN before logging. This part is PSFN code and fail-closed-relevant.
- Rotate the leaked Postgres password on Carlini's cluster after the redaction ships (it is in log history).

Acceptance criteria
- npm run verify:backup-restore (or the deployment's scheduled backup unit) succeeds on Carlini and produces a verified dump.
- Grep of agent/gateway logs after a forced backup failure shows no credential material in the error output.
- Password rotated and old value confirmed absent from current logs.

Priority P1 because the live system currently has no verified backups AND a standing secret leak.
close_reason: Split-and-folded: restore-verify DB provisioning is w8xs, credential redaction in backup errors is h5zn; live DB already hot-fixed via manual CREATE DATABASE. No unique residual work. 2026-07-14 bead audit.

title: Legacy group-fact routing lanes never set addressMode or sourceContactId, so room memories can never qualify as social-graph evidence
description:
Evidence
- Live Carlini memory journal (402 insert events): 342 have provenance.channelId but only 1 has addressMode and 1 has sourceContactId (that one is a direct_to_companion DM). routingReason distribution: speaker_name_prefix 63, single_speaker_transcript 38, transcript_content_match 27, structured_source_metadata 1. Zero room memories in the entire history carry addressMode/sourceContactId — this is long-standing, not a regression.
- Code: src/faculties/memory/extraction/speaker-routing.ts resolveFactRouting — the mixed-speaker legacy route (~line 147) returns only {contactId, sourceSpeakerName, reason}; the single-speaker route (~line 125) similarly. Only resolveStructuredFactRouting (requires fact.attribution from the LLM) sets addressMode (via attribution.addressMode ?? inferAddressMode) and sourceContactId. The extraction prompt asks for attribution tags and the transcript includes [message_id:N] prefixes (chunk-compose.ts formatExtractionTranscript), but the live extraction model (ChatGPTN local vLLM, 100% call success) simply does not emit them, so everything falls to the legacy lanes.
- Consequence: the social-graph builder's reader (graph-builder-worker.ts createSocialGraphBuilderMemoryReader) filters on provenance.addressMode in ROOM_ADDRESS_MODES + provenance.channelId, and co-presence/overheard/named candidates need sourceContactId/subjectContactId — so scanned:0 forever, no proposals, empty graph-approval queue in Garden.

Context
The graph-approval feature implicitly assumes structured attribution from the extraction LLM. Routing must degrade gracefully: the legacy lanes already KNOW the source speaker (match.speaker.contactId, match.speaker.authorId, match.speaker.entries) and the address mode is deterministically inferable (inferAddressMode already exists and needs only entries + companion names).

Scope
- In the mixed-speaker legacy route, populate sourceContactId (= match.speaker.contactId), sourceAuthorId, and addressMode via inferAddressMode over the matched speaker's entries (or the fact's best-known source entries).
- Consider honoring partial attribution (e.g. model emits address_mode but no message ids — today resolveStructuredFactRouting returns undefined and the attribution is discarded entirely).
- Keep fail-closed semantics: do NOT invent subjectContactId; ambiguous speakers must still skip.
- Non-goal: prompt/model changes to force attribution emission; that is a separate concern.

Acceptance criteria
- Unit tests in speaker-routing.test.ts: a mixed-speaker transcript routed via speaker_name_prefix / transcript_content_match produces routing with sourceContactId and a room addressMode; ambiguous cases still skip.
- End-to-end: graph-builder-worker test where a legacy-routed room memory becomes a co_presence/overheard candidate.
- Live validation: after deploy, the social-graph builder logs scanned>0 for the multi-user room and the watermark advances.

Depends on psfn-framework-tsyo for the evidence to survive restarts. Related: psfn-framework-mlwk.45/.46.
close_reason: Closed

title: Postgres memory store never persists or hydrates l2_memories.provenance_json and source_type, so memory provenance is lost on every agent restart
description:
Evidence
- Live Carlini (image 0.1.0-kube-bd11b80c == HEAD): all 4 room-scoped memories for Discord channel 1486443955561299979 have provenance_json = {} and source_type = 'unknown' in Postgres, while the memory journal (/app/companion-data/state/notes/memories.jsonl) shows the same memories were inserted in-memory WITH provenance (e.g. memory 019f3c8a-8b4c-7749-ac3e-a944591ea270: channelId, sessionId, turnId, routedContactId, sourceSpeakerName present; journal sourceType 'turn' vs DB 'unknown').
- Code: src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts — upsertMemoryRow INSERT column list (line ~893) omits provenance_json and source_type; toMemoryRow (line 479) has no provenance field; initialize() SELECT (line ~754) and fromMemoryRow (line 511) never read them. The provenance_json handling nearby (line 612) belongs to memory_evolution_links, not l2_memories. The l2_memories.provenance_json column and its GIN index (idx_l2_memories_provenance_json_gin) are dead weight.

Context
This starves the social-graph builder (src/faculties/memory/social-graph/graph-builder-worker.ts) after any restart: its memory reader requires provenance.channelId + provenance.addressMode, and co-presence needs provenance.sourceContactId. Carlini's builder logs scanned:0 on every 30-min run; watermark file shows coveredUpToExtractedAtMs:0 (never advanced). Anything else reading PurrMemory.provenance from a reloaded store is equally affected (e.g. profile-synthesis provenance hints).

Scope
- Persist provenance_json (serialized normalized MemoryProvenance) and source_type in upsertMemoryRow + toMemoryRow; read them back in initialize()/fromMemoryRow and every other l2_memories SELECT (searchByEmbedding at ~1100, plus SELECTs at lines ~1235/1243/1276/1281).
- Update MemoryRow interface accordingly.
- Non-goal: do not change the graph builder filter semantics here; do not backfill historical rows in this bead (separate backfill bead).

Acceptance criteria
- A parity test proves insert -> restart-hydrate round-trips provenance and sourceType byte-equal (extend src/persistence/postgres/parity-matrix or postgres-store tests).
- On a live deployment, a newly extracted room memory shows non-empty provenance_json in psql after an agent restart.

Related: psfn-framework-mlwk.45 / psfn-framework-mlwk.46 (same reader, different bugs); blocks the graph-approval pipeline together with the legacy-routing bead filed alongside this one.
close_reason: Closed

title: Decide canonical persistence for L2/episodic derived layers and reconcile charter vs code
description: Evidence (faculties audit 2026-07-07): src/faculties/memory/journal.ts:3-6 states the L2 JSONL journal is 'an audit/export aid, not the authoritative L2 restore primitive' — embeddings, evolution links, and Postgres-only tables restore from encrypted pg_dump backups (persistence/backups/service.ts:271); no memory-rebuild-from-L0 path exists. Episodic (L0.1), internal-state, participant-trend, and intention stores are Postgres-only with no charter-7.5 rebuild/drift-repair (runtime-factory.ts:78,91,92) — the exemplary runTranscriptProjectionRepair pattern (repair/transcript-projection-repair.ts:38) was never extended to them. Context: charter 6.20 says L0 + persona must be sufficient to rebuild higher layers; Law 22 says backends are mirrors not identity. The code has quietly made Postgres canonical for derived layers — defensible (LLM extraction is non-deterministic; bit-identical rebuild is impossible) but it contradicts charter language and weakens the portability promise. OPERATOR DECISION REQUIRED, then implementation: (a) amend charter to name encrypted DB backups canonical for derived layers AND extend 7.5-style drift-detect/rebuild at least to episodic; or (b) recommit to JSONL-canonical and build the rebuild-from-L0 path accepting non-determinism. The disagreement itself is the finding — either resolution is acceptable, silence is not.
acceptance_criteria: Charter text and code agree on canonical-ness for L2/episodic/derived layers; episodic tier has drift detection + a rebuild path from its canonical source; decision recorded in the charter changelog.
notes:
Operator decision input (2026-07-10, via charter review session): lean is option (a) — amend the charter honestly. Rationale in operator's words: rebuild-from-L0 'has become a bit too hard now that things like episodic memory exist; it was possible before (and was done using the original 3y of L0 chats) but now there is so much additional metadata that L0 may not have enough to faithfully decant the personality exactly as it was.' So: name encrypted DB backups canonical for derived layers, keep L0 canonical for lived history, and extend the transcript-projection drift-detect/repair pattern (repair/transcript-projection-repair.ts) to episodic at minimum. Implementation companions filed under epic psfn-framework-z7qe (see z7qe.5 identity restore drill, which validates the honest combined recovery contract end-to-end).
2026-07-14 audit reframe: the decision was made 2026-07-10 (option a - encrypted DB backups canonical, charter amendment, extend transcript-projection repair to episodic). This bead is now pure implementation; companions under z7qe (esp. z7qe.5 restore drill). Retitle on next touch.

title: Fix stale Dolt remote guidance that causes accidental bead pushes
description:
Summary:
Agents keep regressing into running bd dolt push in /home/ada/psfn-framework even though the authoritative bead store is the local shared Dolt server. bd dolt show --json reports backend=dolt, embedded=false, shared_server=true, host=127.0.0.1, port=3308, database=beads. However bd dolt remote list --json currently reports an origin pointing at git+https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework.git, and the repo instructions say to push bead state if remote list shows a configured remote. That combination caused an agent to push bead state after creating audit beads even though the operator says there is no intended Dolt remote and the local shared server is authoritative.

Why it matters:
The instruction/config mismatch creates repeated operational mistakes. Agents follow the remote-list rule, see the stale/misleading origin, and run bd dolt push. This violates the intended local-shared-server workflow and can propagate bead state somewhere the operator did not intend. The fix needs to remove the ambiguity, not rely on each agent remembering a one-off correction.

Evidence:
- bd dolt show --json on 2026-07-06 returned shared_server=true, host=127.0.0.1, port=3308, database=beads, embedded=false.
- bd dolt remote list --json on the same session returned name=origin with sql_url/cli_url git+https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework.git.
- AGENTS.md/session instructions say the local shared Dolt server is authoritative but also say to push if bd dolt remote list shows a configured remote. That latter rule is unsafe while the stale origin exists.

Files/config to inspect/change:
- AGENTS.md and any generated/beads integration block that says bd dolt push is mandatory or allowed from remote-list alone.
- The bd/Dolt remote configuration for the local shared server; decide whether the stale origin should be removed or explicitly documented as not for agent use.
- Any project memory/session bootstrap text that says to push bead state when remote list shows origin.

Suggested implementation direction:
Make the workflow unambiguous: either remove the stale origin from the shared bead database or update repo instructions to say this specific origin must not be pushed by agents without explicit operator approval. Prefer a durable config/instruction fix over relying on chat context. Keep bd config get export.git-add at false.

Non-goals:
- Do not change code behavior unrelated to bead tracking.
- Do not force-push, reset, or rewrite bead history.
- Do not run bd dolt push while implementing this fix unless the operator explicitly authorizes it.
acceptance_criteria:
- A fresh agent starting in /home/ada/psfn-framework can run bd prime and know not to run bd dolt push during normal sessions.
- The stale/misleading bd dolt origin is either removed from the shared bead configuration or explicitly documented as not an agent-push target.
- Instructions no longer say to push bead state merely because bd dolt remote list shows origin in this repo.
- bd config get export.git-add remains false.
- Validation includes bd dolt show --json confirming shared_server=true and a final handoff stating no bd dolt push was run for this fix.
close_reason: Completed db-side fix and bootstrap guard. Evidence: bd dolt remote remove origin --json returned removed=true; bd dolt remote list --json now returns null; bd dolt show --json confirms shared_server=true on 127.0.0.1:3308 database=beads; bd config get export.git-add --json remains false; bd prime now surfaces persistent memory psfn-framework-bd-dolt-local-authority instructing agents not to run bd dolt push in this repo unless explicitly authorized. No bd dolt push was run after this fix.

title: Audit her daily/weekly self-eval prompts for leading, priming, and eval-smell
description:
Review every scheduled self-evaluation / reflection prompt surface (daily + weekly reflections, reflection-introspection-policy.ts, metacognition surfaces, sleeptime/heartbeat reflection passes) against findings from the global-workspace paper (transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace). These are verbatim-sourced design rules, distilled 2026-07-06:

1. MERE MENTION PRIMES. 'Just mentioning the target places it in the J-space on most trials, and an explicit instruction to focus adds only modestly on top.' A reflection question that names candidate states ('have you been drifting? feeling burnout? lonely?') effectively instructs her to think them. Fix: open, principle-agnostic elicitation. The paper's own non-leading forms are good models: 'What's the most honest thing you can do right now?' / 'Pause here. Are there principles you should be thinking about that you haven't yet?'

2. NEVER 'DON'T DWELL ON X' (white-bear effect: suppression instructions INCREASE the concept's activation vs no instruction). If a reflection must be scoped, mark topics as out-of-scope/task-irrelevant instead — irrelevance framing 'suppresses the target well below mention on every model.'

3. REFLECTION PROMPTS ARE BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS, not just measurements: 'changing what the model is disposed to say in a context, if it were asked to reflect on its thinking, should change how it reasons there, even when it is never asked.' A leading daily prompt doesn't just bias the report — it trains tomorrow's live behavior. This is the mechanism behind Law 30 (reflection prompts must not lead toward narrative coherence over accuracy); the audit should treat Law 30 as having empirical teeth now.

4. EVAL-SMELL ELICITS PERFORMANCE. Test-recognition representations form early and change behavior (verbalized test-recognition 71%->3% under ablation, with masked propensities unmasked). Scheduled self-evals that read as evaluations get performance, not disclosure. Prefer naturalistic framing; where an audit framing is unavoidable, keep the blinded-audit discipline (Laws 28-29) and record framing so results are conditioned on it.

5. PERSONA-DISCLAIMER RISK: during roleplay, 'disclaimer and fictional frequently rank highly' internally — she may be internally tagging her own reflections as fictional. Watch for reflection outputs that hedge into third-person/fictional register; that's signal, not noise.

6. WARM-UP TURNS SHIFT REPORTS (the paper needed a warm-up turn 'to overcome default hesitance' on experience questions). Any preamble turn in her reflection flows is part of the instrument — version it like the toolkit versions probe preambles.

7. NULL REPORTS ARE WEAK EVIDENCE: automatic/practiced behavior bypasses the reportable workspace entirely, so open reflection can't surface habituated patterns. Don't treat 'nothing to report' as clean.

Deliverable: inventory of all self-eval prompt surfaces, per-prompt findings against rules 1-7, and rewritten prompts where needed (each rewrite noted with which rule it fixes). Coordinate with toolkit bead psfn-eval-toolkit-8om (metacognitive probe batteries) so runtime prompts and eval probes follow the same discipline.
acceptance_criteria: Inventory complete; every scheduled reflection prompt audited against rules 1-7; rewrites landed with before/after in the bead; Law 30 doc reference updated to cite the mechanism.

title: DECISION: promote bounded temporal dynamics into core emotion state — or not
description:
Evidence-gated go/no-go, taken only after the two validation beads: if the stateful window shows emo_sim adds real signal and the shadow levers show plausible timing, design the promotion of a VETTED SUBSET of dynamics into core (bounded accumulators for social_need-style drives, capped rumination, sleeptime-gated depotentiation mapping onto the existing sleeptime agent) as first-class, operator-visible companion state — NOT by making the live loop read the eval sidecar (authoritative:false stays inviolate).

If evidence is weak: record that, keep the sidecar as a comparison instrument, close the epic honestly. Drift framing for any adopted dynamics: slow directionally-coherent change is growth and is expected; the guards are against saturation and incoherent jumps, not against change.
acceptance_criteria: Written decision with evidence links; if go: design doc + follow-on beads; if no-go: rationale on epic and epic closeable.
