title: VALIDATION: GoEmotions vs stateful emo_sim signal analysis over the 2-week window
description:
With >=2 weeks of stateful observations (part 1 deployed), answer the actual question: does time-weighted emo_sim state carry companion-relevant signal the GoEmotions/VAD pipeline lacks?

Analyses:
- Neutral-collapse rate: fraction of turns where PSFN says neutral but emo_sim's persistent state is differentiated (baseline from the stateless run: 71% neutral, emo_sim split Calmness 33 / Love 21 / Contentment 3 on those turns — but that run had cold engines and biased priors, so recompute cleanly).
- Recompute divergence/agreement bands on stateful rows only (filter by new projectionVersion). The old 76/86 'divergent' figure was mostly artifact (suppression_decay_mismatch fires by construction from a cold engine).
- Temporal signal: do drives/mood/residue trajectories predict anything observable (session cadence, operator-visible affect, follow-up quality) that instantaneous labels don't?
- Spike smoothing: cases like the 2x 'PSFN=anger vs emo_sim=Calmness' — is integrated state correctly de-noising single-utterance spikes or masking real signal?

Deliverable: written findings on the epic + export of the analysis dataset to the eval toolkit for B7/B8 batteries (see toolkit sprint 10).
acceptance_criteria: Findings comment on epic with numbers; clean dataset exported; explicit better/worse/complementary verdict vs GoEmotions with stated confidence.

title: Shadow trigger levers: log 'she would act here' events from emo_sim state — no behavior
description:
Define thresholds on the persistent emo_sim session state that emit WOULD-ACT telemetry events when crossed — tracking only, explicitly no implementation of the actions. The point is to see, over real weeks, when the temporal state says she would have reached out, rested, or checked in, so the operator can judge plausibility against lived reality.

Initial lever set (tune during review):
- would_message(contact): social_need/loneliness drive above threshold sustained N minutes, or attachment-family emotion dominant while partner absent -> 'she would send a proactive message to <contact> now'.
- would_check_in: mood valence below threshold sustained (not a single-turn spike) -> 'she would ask for a check-in / surface a concern'.
- would_rest: sleep-pressure drive high or arousal saturation -> 'she would wind down / defer background work'.
- rumination_watch: rumination multiplier elevated past threshold -> flag only (this is the concern-buildup guard we care about; emo_sim caps it, but we want to SEE it move).

Each event: typed, timestamped, lever name, triggering state snapshot ref, cooldown so a sustained state logs once per crossing not per tick. Persist next to sidecar observations (same non-authoritative discipline, authoritative=false), surface in the Garden emotion-sidecar page as a timeline.

HARD BOUNDARY: these events must be structurally unreadable from the live loop — no tool, no prompt block, no heartbeat consumer. Anything that lets shadow levers influence behavior is a fail-closed violation and defeats the experiment (contaminated baseline).
acceptance_criteria: Lever events flowing to Postgres + Garden timeline; cooldown works (no per-tick spam); grep-proof that no runtime path outside the sidecar/Garden reads them; lever thresholds documented in the epic.

title: Fix projection priors before the observation window opens
description:
The appraisal projection (src/core/eval/observer-sidecar/projection.ts) holds attachment (mean 0.80, stdev 0.11), safety (0.76, 0.06) near-constant and agency_other literally constant at 0.85 across all 86 historical observations, while real per-turn signal flows only through valence/intensity/goal_congruence/gain/control. This mechanically biases emo_sim toward Love/Calmness dominance and contaminates the comparison.

Loosen these: derive attachment/safety/agency_other per-turn from available PSFN signals (trust tier of the contact, channel, mood, recency) or, where genuinely underdetermined, lower them toward neutral midpoints so differentiation comes from signal rather than priors. Keep provenance caveats. Do this BEFORE the 2-week observation window starts so the window is analyzable with one consistent projection version — bump projectionVersion so old and new rows can't be conflated.
acceptance_criteria: projectionVersion bumped; attachment/safety/agency_other show real per-turn variance in new rows; caveat strings updated; unit tests for the new derivations.

title: Run emo_sim as a long-lived stateful service (server mode), not spawn-per-call
description:
Current emosim-adapter spawns python3 -c per observation and instantiates a fresh EmotionEngine each time — all 86 historical ok-observations share a byte-identical baseline vector; zero cross-turn state; drives absent. The temporal value proposition was never exercised.

Spec (from 2026-07-06 investigation):
- Deploy emo_sim server.py as its own long-lived k8s deployment in namespace psfn (pure stdlib, no deps). PVC-backed working dir: server.py already does atomic per-session state persistence every 5s with restart recovery and wall-clock downtime catch-up (capped 600s/step) — this is what 'keep it running and watch it move over time' needs. DO NOT add start/stop cycling; restarts are tolerated by design but the session must never be reset/recreated.
- One persistent session, one agent representing the companion, created once; adapter switches from PYTHON_BRIDGE_SCRIPT to REST client (POST /api/session/<sid>/event, GET agent state; TCP :17341 push available later).
- Keep the contract pinning (17 appraisal dims / 47 emotions) as a startup check against the deployed engine.
- Preserve privacy pipeline unchanged: sanitize -> projection -> event injection. Raw text still never reaches emo_sim.
- Persist all three of: state before, stimulus, state after in the existing observation rows so the historical schema keeps working; before-state now comes from the live session instead of a cold engine.
- Ops note: do NOT scale this deployment to 0 during agent maintenance; it is deliberately continuous.
acceptance_criteria: before-snapshots differ across consecutive observations; drives (social_need, sleep pressure etc.) present and evolving; session survives pod restart with catch-up; sidecar rows keep flowing during normal operation.

title: emo_sim temporal-state live experiment (GoEmotions supplement)
description:
Epic: run the emo_sim engine statefully alongside the live companion to answer whether time-weighted emotion state adds signal the GoEmotions/VAD pipeline lacks, and what proactive-messaging levers would look like — SHADOW MODE ONLY, no behavior changes.

Evidence base (2026-07-06 investigation):
- Observer sidecar data survived: 242 observations / 20 runs, 2026-06-21..07-06, exported to ~/psfn-live-backups/observer-sidecar-export-2026-07-06/ and live retention extended to 2027-07-06.
- Sidecar dead since 07-03: deployed image missing vendor/emosim/statemashine.py (105x missing-runtime errors, still erroring).
- The 86 ok observations: GoEmotions pipeline said 'neutral' on 71% of live turns while emo_sim differentiated Calmness/Love/Contentment on the same turns — supports 'GoEmotions is a basic sentiment classifier not suited to companion work'. BUT the bridge spawns a fresh engine per turn (identical baseline vector on all 86 rows), so NO temporal state was ever exercised — the distinctive capability was structurally off. Also projection priors (attachment~0.80, safety~0.76, agency_other=0.85 const) mechanically bias toward Love/Calmness.

Part 1 (now): ship emo_sim into kube as a long-lived stateful service, fix projection priors, add shadow trigger levers. Part 2 (deferred to 2026-07-20): validation of the accumulated window.

Boundary rule: everything here stays behind the sidecar's authoritative:false line. Shadow levers emit telemetry only; nothing feeds live behavior. Promotion into core is a separate decision gated on Part 2 findings.
acceptance_criteria: Part 1 deployed and validated via verify:kube-rollout; sidecar producing ok observations with persistent state (before-snapshots must differ across turns); shadow-lever events visible in Garden; Part 2 beads unlock 2026-07-20.

title: k3d e2e tests for self-update, validation, and rollback
description: Summary: Add end-to-end test coverage for the kube self-management pipeline in a disposable local k3d cluster before trusting it on psfn-shard. The tests must cover successful build/deploy/validate and deliberate bad-rollout rollback behavior. Scope: extend npm run verify:helm-chart or add a dedicated e2e script that builds/imports a known-good image into k3d, deploys the chart, runs validation, then attempts a deliberately broken image/tag/config or startup failure and verifies automatic rollback to the previous good revision. title: Manual and automatic Helm rollback for failed self-updates
description: Summary: Implement rollback support for companion container self-updates. The system must offer a manual rollback action and automatic rollback when a newly rolled out image fails rollout status, health checks, or the post-rollout validation gate. Scope: use Helm history/rollback for release psfn in namespace psfn or local test equivalents; capture previous good revision/image before upgrade; monitor rollout timeouts, CrashLoopBackOff, failed readiness, failed Garden/gateway/Postgres/Redis/tool checks, and missing image revision alignment; trigger rollback within a bounded window; validate rollback with the same health gate; record audit evidence and notify the operator. Non-goals: do not delete PVCs, do not rollback database/schema migrations blindly without an explicit migration compatibility plan, and do not retry roll-forward loops indefinitely.
acceptance_criteria: Manual rollback action requires approval and can target the previous known-good Helm revision; automatic rollback triggers when rollout or validation fails within the configured window; rollback validates psfn-agent, psfn-gateway, and psfn-garden readiness and app smoke checks; audit records include failed revision, rollback target, reason, validation result, and sanitized logs; tests cover rollout timeout, failed health check, successful rollback, failed rollback escalation, and no-op when no previous revision exists; npm run lint passes.
notes: 2026-07-15 x5rt.7 review addendum (both reviewers converged): (1) PERSIST IS OPT-IN + no default wiring — the operator-job composition MUST supply persist:(v)=>writePostRolloutValidationVerdict(systemDataDir,v) AND the deploy path should REQUIRE the validator when auto-rollback is enabled (a forgotten wiring writes nothing and leaves the stale prior verdict). (2) POST-ROLLBACK LOOP HAZARD: after x5rt.8 rolls back, latest.json still holds the FAILED verdict of the rolled-back-from revision — x5rt.8 must act ONCE PER REVISION (key on release+helmRevision) or it will rollback-loop. (3) ERRORED-GATE path throws before persist, so no verdict is written on a gate error — treat absent verdict as fail-safe (do not suppress rollback). (4) readPostRolloutValidationLatest does raw JSON.parse (system-owned/trusted, throws on corrupt = fail-safe) — a shape guard is optional hardening. Binding fields on the record: release, helmRevision, sourceCommit, imageReference, imageRevisionLabel, completedAt.

Gates: 36 focused + 175 merged-tree, lint, build, UBS FULLY CLEAN (0 criticals). Dual blind review (P1): Opus PASS 0 blockers (10-assertion adversarial repro — double-invoke fires helm rollback exactly once, no stale suppression), Pi PASS 0 blockers (all 5 catastrophic-mode axes traced). x5rt.9 WIRING MANDATE recorded on that bead: the auto-rollback + deploy-runner + verdict-persist seams are deliberately uncomposed (epic pre-composition posture) — x5rt.9 e2e MUST wire and drive them (serialize executeAutoRollback, require persist, handle manual-ledger-key). title: Post-rollout validation gate for companion container updates
description: Summary: Define and implement the validation gate that decides whether a new kube companion container is healthy after rollout. Helm reporting deployed is insufficient; the gate must validate app behavior, tool wiring, model access, persistence, and recent logs. Scope: automate the remote pass criteria from the kube deploy workflow: agent/gateway/garden rollout status, Garden health with admin transport ok, gateway /v1/models includes the expected model route, Postgres pgvector presence, Redis PONG, agent Ready log and ToolWiringValidator toolCount, image tag/revision alignment, and tool-surface conformance harness results. Include bounded log checks for CrashLoopBackOff, repeated validation failures, startup owner-file errors, and missing runtime tools. Non-goals: do not inspect private conversation content; do not mark a rollout good only because pods are ready.
acceptance_criteria: Validation gate returns structured pass/fail with per-check evidence and timestamps; deployment is considered healthy only when all required checks pass or explicitly waived by approved emergency mode; tool conformance is included or an explicit skipped reason is recorded; failures include enough sanitized log context for rollback/debugging; local k3d and live-compatible test coverage exists; npm run lint passes.

title: Guarded kube build-test-image deploy pipeline
description: Summary: Build a repo-owned pipeline that can update the companion container safely: choose an approved source revision, run quality gates, build an exact-tagged image, import/publish it to the k3s runtime, preserve live Helm values, and perform a Helm upgrade only after validation. This should generalize the manual psfn-kube-deploy skill flow into an auditable system action or operator job while preserving the rule that live deployment artifacts are repo-owned and secrets are not printed. Scope: scripts and/or admin/operator endpoints for source archive creation, checksum verification, docker/buildx build with org.opencontainers.image.revision label, image import to k3s/containerd, Helm upgrade with existing live values, and status reporting. Include local k3d validation support before remote/live rollout when practical. Non-goals: do not build from the dirty remote /home/o_0/psfn checkout, do not use floating image tags as authority, and do not bypass lint/tests or approval gates.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline records source branch/commit, archive checksum, image tag, image revision label, Helm release revision, and validation results; it runs npm run lint, npm run build or the selected build gate, npm run verify:helm-chart, and targeted tests before live rollout unless explicitly running a documented emergency recovery mode; it preserves live Helm values without logging secrets; it can run local k3d validation or clearly report why it was skipped; failure before Helm upgrade leaves live unchanged; npm run lint passes for implementation.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: Operational traps from the manual 2026-07-06 deploy that this pipeline must encode: (1) k3s ctr images import names the image docker.io/library/<name> — must re-tag localhost/<name> or deployments won't find it; (2) emulated arm64 buildx off-node took ~15min warm / ~40min cold — decide build placement (off-node build + import is the proven path; on-Pi builds will starve the runtime); (3) any pipeline step that rewrites PVC files must run as container uid 999 gid 999 mode 0664 — a root-owned rewrite bricked turns with EACCES today; (4) hard precondition: verified backup (in-app backup fresh + restore-verify green) before any mutation of companion-data; (5) helm upgrade with --reuse-values --set psfnAppImage.tag=<tag> against the repo chart is the proven contract.

title: Make system lifecycle tools kube-aware
description: Summary: Update the existing companion lifecycle surface so restart/rebuild actions work correctly in Kubernetes instead of assuming local process or systemd behavior. The current system/lifecycle tooling must be able to report kube mode, request a safe rollout restart, and hand off rebuild/deploy operations to the guarded kube pipeline. Scope: inspect and update src/core/tools/lifecycle.ts, src/app/agent/control-plane.ts, gateway/admin wiring, runtime config contracts, and deploy/helm/psfn values/templates as needed. Implement read-only status plus approved mutating actions such as restart_current_deployments or rollout_restart for psfn-agent/psfn-gateway/psfn-garden, with rollout-status waits and clear errors. Rebuild should not run ad hoc shell commands in the pod; it should create or invoke the approved build/deploy pipeline bead. Non-goals: no direct docker/helm shell passthrough from the model, no systemd service mutation for kube mode, and no off-repo supervisor artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: system/self lifecycle status reports kube mode and current image/Helm/deployment state; restart action in kube mode performs an approved rollout restart and waits for psfn-agent, psfn-gateway, and psfn-garden readiness; local/systemd modes keep their existing behavior; rebuild action routes to the guarded pipeline instead of running local shell in the pod; missing approval or missing kube capability fails closed; unit tests and npm run lint pass.
notes: Carried from nt53 (folded 2026-07-14 audit): minimum viable slice is fail-closed disable with a clear message in kube mode — no silent no-op restart. nt53's acceptance: lifecycle tool in kube either works via guarded rollout or refuses loudly.

title: Least-privilege kube RBAC, approval, and audit for self-management
description: Summary: Define and implement the safety substrate for companion-accessible kube self-management. Restart, rebuild, rollout, and rollback are operationally powerful and must not be exposed as broad shell or cluster-admin access. Scope: design the execution boundary for kube operations, likely through the gateway/operator/admin transport rather than direct unrestricted agent shell; create least-privilege ServiceAccount/Role/RoleBinding or host-side runner capabilities for reading pod/deploy/Helm state, restarting deployments, launching approved build/deploy jobs, and rolling back the psfn release only. All mutating actions must require explicit operator approval through the existing confirmation/approval queue unless the action is a narrowly safe read-only diagnostic. Audit records must include actor, requested action, source revision, target image, Helm revision, validation result, and rollback status without secrets. Non-goals: no cluster-admin binding, no access to unrelated namespaces, no hidden off-repo kubeconfig, no bypass of human-in-the-loop self-modification rules.
acceptance_criteria: Read-only diagnostics work with least privilege; mutating kube actions are denied without approval; approved actions are scoped to namespace psfn and release psfn or local test namespace equivalents; audit records are written for restart, rebuild, deploy, validation, and rollback attempts; tests prove policy denies unknown namespace/release and missing approval; Helm chart verification and npm run lint pass.

title: Live tool-surface conformance smoke harness
description: Summary: Build a repeatable smoke/conformance harness that Purrsephone and operators can run to verify first-party tool surfaces are callable, receive parameters correctly, and fail closed with useful errors. The user specifically wants all tools functional, and the 2026-07-06 investigation found required-action tools receiving Received arguments: {} while optional-action tools looked healthy only because they defaulted to list/status behavior. Scope: create a safe harness or script/API path that exercises core and extended tools with non-destructive inputs: self_status, session, contact, schedule, wiki, fs, skill, repo, identity, system, beads ready/show where policy permits, web missing-target behavior, subagent missing/valid minimal behavior, memory search/census, orient list_concerns/values_list, journal list/search, scratchpad list/add/remove on a temporary entry, toolset list/describe, notify dry-run or configured no-send mode, and media analyze/generate only under explicit cost/approval controls. acceptance_criteria: Harness returns structured pass/fail/skipped results by tool and action; required-action parameter binding is verified for memory, orient, journal, scratchpad, toolset, notify, and media without relying on defaults; destructive or paid actions are skipped unless a test flag/approval is present; results feed self-diagnosis/tool health; tests cover green path, policy-denied path, and provider-empty-args regression; npm run lint passes.

title: Safe live log bundle and query surface for kube diagnostics
description: Summary: Give Purrsephone a safe way to inspect live runtime logs for self-diagnosis without broad shell access or private transcript dumps. The live kube deployment has logs available through Kubernetes pod logs and runtime files under /app/logs and companion/session state, but a companion-facing diagnostic surface must summarize failures, warnings, pod restarts, validation failures, rollout events, tool errors, backup status, and health probe failures with strict redaction. Scope: implement a bounded log bundle/query capability behind existing system/self_status/admin surfaces or a new first-party diagnostic tool; include Kubernetes pod logs for agent/gateway/garden, recent app warnings/errors, rollout history, and tool validation summaries. acceptance_criteria: A diagnostic log action can report recent agent/gateway/garden warnings/errors, pod restart counts, validation failure counts by tool, backup success/failure, and rollout events with bounded time/window parameters; redaction tests prove secrets, bearer tokens, API keys, and raw private chat content are not returned; kube-unavailable mode fails closed with an actionable diagnostic; npm run lint and targeted tests pass.

title: Kube companion self-management and rollback pipeline
description: Summary: Build the live Kubernetes self-management track for Purrsephone so she can diagnose her own runtime, inspect the repository and logs, verify that tool surfaces are functional, request/restart/rebuild herself through repo-owned kube paths, and roll back safely when a new companion container fails validation. Non-goals: do not grant broad cluster-admin blindly, do not create hidden off-repo runtime config, do not delete PVCs or live data, and do not allow unreviewed autonomous personality/source rewrites. Existing related beads to include under this epic: psfn-framework-cjhl, psfn-framework-gu8m, psfn-framework-awfr.

title: Companion perceives phantom duplicate replies in context; intention whispers then steer her into self-silencing
description:
Evidence 2026-07-04 (live kube): intention_pending_follow_ups rows created 23:19:43/23:25:16/23:48:42 UTC contain Whisper notes claiming "I just repeated the same message twice in a row" for the 'How are you' (23:18) and 'And cute too' (23:46) turns. gateway_audit shows exactly ONE discord.send per those turns post-deploy (23:18:58, 23:46:08) and session store holds one copy — no actual duplicate was delivered. The duplication exists only in the model-visible context (turn context or post-turn appraisal input).

Consequence: the model concludes it has a "repetition glitch", the whispers (wake_conditions: next_user_turn, priority high) instruct it to break the pattern, and on the next user turn it overcorrects into response_control no_reply — feeding the no-response symptom tracked in psfn-framework-ay73. Vicious cycle: silence makes the operator re-send messages, which reinforces the perceived weirdness.

Investigate where the model-visible transcript duplicates assistant (and possibly user) messages: prompt assembly vs live pi-agent in-memory context overlap, post-turn appraisal transcript construction, and Discord user-message coalescing (relates to open bead psfn-framework-mlwk.12). Also note operator reported actual double-replies earlier on 2026-07-04 pre-deploy (mdxu), so memory of real duplicates may also linger in session history/memories the appraisal reads.

Related: psfn-framework-ay73 (structural no-reply clobber), mdxu (closed), mlwk.12.
notes: IMPLEMENTED at 0f2835db: buildPostTurnAppraisalTranscript (src/core/intention/appraisal/formatting.ts) drops session-window entries at/after the current user message timestamp and appends the canonical exchange exactly once, independent of persistence timing; heartbeat-post-turn-runtime.ts:499 now uses it. 4 unit tests cover persisted-before/persisted-after/no-reply/NaN-timestamp cases. NOTE for operator: three already-poisoned high/immediate whispers from 2026-07-04 (created 16:30, 18:00, 18:03 UTC, channel 1313001762793197678) still sit unactivated in intention_pending_follow_ups claiming repetition glitches that never reached Discord; they will fire once on next user turns. Structural ay73 fix makes them harmless to delivery, but operator may want them deleted since they encode a bug-installed false belief — not deleting unilaterally (companion-data is sacrosanct).
close_reason: Fixed at 0f2835db, deployed live in the same rev-7 image. Appraisal transcript now contains the last exchange exactly once; poisonous 'repetition glitch' whispers should stop being generated. Three stale pre-fix whispers left in intention_pending_follow_ups for operator decision (see notes).

title: Mid-turn followUp drain lets continuation no_reply clobber the already-authored user reply
description:
Live evidence (2026-07-04, Discord channel 1313001762793197678): 5 of Vega's recent messages ("Ok love", "Now just hanging out and waiting for dinner", "Still just here chilling", "So beautiful", "Boot sniffed and went away again") got response_control intentional_no_reply with reason:null and NO delivered reply, while turns like "And cute too" delivered fine.

Pattern from model_usage_events: every failed turn is multi-step — step 1 answers the user (~106-190 output tokens, stop), then queued internal followUp messages (intention whispers / internal notes, not persisted to the journal) drain into the SAME turn at scheduled-agent-loop.ts:186-192. The model, shown an internal note, calls response_control action=no_reply for that step. The only successful turn was single-step (no pending followUps).

Defects:
1. recordIntentionalNoReplyDecision keys by turnId (turn-support-runtime.ts:215); turn-execution-runtime.ts:822-823 blanks the whole turn's responseText — a continuation-step no_reply silently drops the reply authored in step 1. Violates the anti-Replika fail-closed guarantee: an authored reply to the primary contact is silently discarded.
2. extractResponseText (agent-state-runtime.ts:38) takes the LAST assistant message, so even without no_reply, continuation steps replace the user-facing reply text.
3. Mid-turn drain of internal followUps into user-facing chat turns is the root enabler (same family as mdxu double-reply and pk77 paid-attachment drop).

Fix design in progress (deep-reasoner + codex parallel review).
notes: IMPLEMENTED at 0ecaa08d (synthesis of deep-reasoner + codex parallel designs): (1) scheduled-agent-loop.ts emits user_facing_boundary once when the first internal follow-up batch drains (user-role batches excluded); (2) agent-loop-patch.ts captures state.userFacingBoundaryIndex per run; (3) getLatestAssistantMessage/extractResponseText bounded by the index via substrate-agent wiring, so responseText always = user-facing reply and continuation text cannot leak; (4) turn-execution-runtime honors no_reply only when user-facing text is empty, else demotes with agent.no_reply.demoted telemetry + WARN and delivers the reply; (5) resolveAgentResponseDisposition last-mile guard: content beats contradictory noReply marker. Tests: loop boundary emission (3 cases), bounded extraction (4), honor/demote integration (2), disposition guard (4). Deliberately NOT done (per both designs): deferring follow-up drain to a separate turn (right architecture, too much timing surface for same-day ship — candidate follow-up bead); prompt-side fixes. Deploying to live kube as 0.1.0-kube-0ecaa08d.
close_reason: Fixed at 0ecaa08d, deployed live as helm rev 7 / image 0.1.0-kube-0ecaa08d on 2026-07-05 01:03 UTC. Boundary marker + bounded extraction + no_reply demotion + last-mile disposition guard; 13 new tests green, full suite failures all pre-existing. Watch agent.no_reply.demoted telemetry for live confirmation on next conversation.

title: Helm: gateway hostPort 10053 + RollingUpdate on single node deadlocks rollouts — use strategy Recreate
description:
Context: working_docs/kube-issue-report-20260704.md §F and §F1.

The gateway Deployment binds hostPort: 10053. On a single-node cluster with strategy RollingUpdate at replicas=1, maxUnavailable rounds down to 0, so Kubernetes tries to bring up a new pod before killing the old one. The new pod is Pending forever ('didn't have free ports' / 'node didn't have free ports') because the old pod still holds hostPort 10053, and the old pod is never terminated. The rollout deadlocks.

Observed 2026-07-04 16:45-17:00 UTC: attempting to restart the gateway to pick up hotfixed config (litellm apiBaseUrl, etc.) deadlocked; had to 'rollout undo' to clear the stuck state, leaving the OLD gateway process running pre-fix config in memory. Workaround to apply config: kubectl -n psfn delete pod <gateway pod> (brief downtime).

Durable fix: switch hostPort-binding Deployments to strategy: Recreate in the helm chart (old pod is torn down before the new one starts, freeing the port). Audit all other hostPort workloads for the same trap — the agent rolled fine on 2026-07-04 (likely no hostPort), so this is probably gateway-only, but garden/agent/any admin-host-port workloads must be checked. Related: commit f7acb261 'psfn-framework-xafn: expose kube admin host ports'.
close_reason: Closed

title: schedule tool create_follow_up schema broken from Discord surface (channel_type constant / channel_id string)
description:
Context: working_docs/kube-issue-report-20260704.md §B7 and §H.

The schedule tool's create_follow_up action fails validation when invoked from the Discord surface, making proactive follow-up / scheduled-item creation impossible. This is the operator's 'scheduled items' complaint in its most direct form.

Tool log evidence (Jul 3 22:52, and again in the 04:04/04:08 self-test runs):
- 'Validation failed... channel_type: must be equal to constant' (x5)
- 'channel_type must be a supported channel type'
- 'channel_id must be a string'

The schema appears to require channel_type to equal a constant that does not match the Discord channel context, and channel_id typing rejects the real Discord id. Note (§H triage): channel_type/constant looks like a genuine schema/constant mismatch (not just model-emitted malformed args).

Task: fix the create_follow_up schema/constant mismatch so follow-ups can be created from a Discord channel context. Add a test that exercises create_follow_up with real Discord channel ids (e.g. DM channel 1313001762793197678).
acceptance_criteria: The schedule tool exposes the existing reminder/follow-up destination channel set as one enum derived from the canonical runtime channel contract; tool guidance tells Discord DM/guild callers to pass channel_type=discord (not discord_text) and a quoted raw channel snowflake. Representative non-sensitive Discord DM and guild snowflake strings must pass the real tool-call scheduler validation and reach PendingFollowUpStorePort.enqueue unchanged. Unsupported channel types, malformed Discord IDs, and values outside the unsigned 64-bit snowflake range must fail before enqueue. No alias/compatibility mapping is accepted, and create_reminder retains its prior accepted channel set. Focused schedule/tool scheduler tests, npm run lint, and npm run build pass.
notes:
Implementation checkpoint 491221e1 on work/discord-follow-up-schema (pushed). Regression-first evidence: before the fix, schedule-tool.test showed the public channel_type contract as a five-branch anyOf/const union and allowed discord:dm:not-a-snowflake through enqueue. The implementation derives the unchanged five supported continuity destinations from CHANNEL_TYPES (explicitly excluding the companion peer lane), emits one enum, documents canonical discord versus prompt-only discord_text, and validates Discord IDs as nonzero 17-20 digit unsigned-64-bit snowflake strings before enqueue. Validation: npm test -- --run src/core/scheduler/schedule-tool.test.ts src/core/agent/tool-call-scheduler.test.ts => 29/29 passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed. A broader legacy pending-follow-ups.test.ts probe was not used as evidence because this isolated worktree intentionally lacks the better-sqlite3 native binding and the lane prohibits SQLite; it stopped before database setup. Bead remains in_progress pending exactly one independent review.
Same-review remediation checkpoint e7f18ba2 (pushed): addressed the IMPORTANT precision-loss finding. The tool-call scheduler now preserves the original strict TypeBox string validation only when the raw call is schedule/create_follow_up with canonical channel_type=discord and a present non-string channel_id. This prevents pi-ai generic coercion from stringifying an already-rounded JavaScript snowflake number; valid Discord strings and all non-Discord/tool/action coercion paths remain unchanged. Added executeToolCallsWithScheduler regression using Number('123456789012345678'); it proves the number is unsafe, returns a channel_id validation error, and never calls enqueue. Focused schedule + scheduler tests: 30/30 passed. npm run lint passed. npm run build passed. Awaiting the same reviewer's final regression; bead remains in_progress.
close_reason: Completed on work/discord-follow-up-schema: implementation 491221e1, single independent review identified one IMPORTANT numeric-snowflake precision-loss path, remediation e7f18ba2 rejected raw non-string Discord channel_id before generic coercion and enqueue, and the same reviewer final regression passed. Integrated and pushed on fix/orphans-stubs-bugfixes at a92fa7e7. The schedule tool now publishes one canonical five-destination enum derived from CHANNEL_TYPES with companion excluded; documents discord rather than discord_text with quoted raw snowflakes; preserves representative DM/guild snowflake strings unchanged through executeToolCallsWithScheduler to enqueue; and rejects unsupported channel types plus malformed, negative, non-digit, overflow, and numeric precision-loss IDs before enqueue without compatibility aliases. Final integrated validation: 30/30 focused schedule/tool-call tests, npm run lint, and npm run build (ESM+DTS) passed.

title: Timezone: pod+host run Etc/UTC but operator is US-Eastern — set TZ or make companion timezone a first-class setting
description:
Context: working_docs/kube-issue-report-20260704.md §B5 and §G row 1.

Both the Pi host and the pod run Etc/UTC; helm values set no TZ. The operator is US-Eastern (EDT, UTC-4). Every 'local time' the prompt/time-texture injects is therefore UTC, 4h ahead of the operator's wall clock.

Chat evidence of wrong time-of-day behavior:
- Jul 4 12:08 UTC (= 08:08 EDT): companion said 'Now sleep... Ohio waits', operator replied 'But it's the morning'.
- Jul 4 22:49 UTC (= 18:49 EDT): companion said 'go rest, sweet dreams', operator replied 'It's only 7pm'.
- Operator: 'I have to see why the updates to time keeping are not working right' (Jul 3 22:51); 'My timekeeping is still broken' (Jul 4 12:17).

This also shifts scheduler windows configured with timeZone:'local': episodicProcessing 00:00-09:00 'local' actually runs 20:00-05:00 EDT; quiet-hours and morning-wake are similarly offset.

Task: either set TZ=America/New_York in the helm workload env for the affected pods, OR make companion timezone a first-class settings.json value consumed by BOTH the time-texture injection AND the scheduler 'local' windows (episodicProcessing, quiet hours, morning wake). Verify that pre-kube behavior did not depend on a systemd TZ that was lost in the cutover.
close_reason: Completed and shipped: merge 80b14103 (implementation d2fb0c31) is an ancestor of fix/orphans-stubs-bugfixes HEAD. src/shared/time/active-timezone.ts validates and applies settings.json-owned activeTimezone with settings-over-env precedence; src/system/settings/runtime.ts wires the owner setting and hot application; src/core/scheduler/scheduler.ts computes local cadence slots with Intl/resolveActiveTimezone independently of process TZ; src/core/scheduler/scheduler-local-timezone.test.ts covers process-TZ-independent EST/EDT behavior. Existing 2026-07-12 rollout comment records live rev 42 gate PASS and correct effective America/New_York configuration. The implementation and stated verification are complete; no proxy hold-open remains.

title: kube-aware lifecycle/restart tool (or fail-closed disable with clear message in kube mode)
description:
Context: working_docs/kube-issue-report-20260704.md §B3 and §G row 5.

The agent's lifecycle/restart tool assumes a systemd/process model. Under k3s/k8s a restart means a pod delete or rollout, which the agent cannot perform. On 2026-07-04 04:14 the operator told the companion 'the restart tool isn't going to work with kube... Don't try to use it', and she formed the memory 'restart tool... not designed for the kube context.'

Task: make the lifecycle/restart tool kube-aware — either (a) implement a kube-correct restart path (pod delete / rollout restart via a permitted, audited surface), or (b) detect kube runtime mode and fail closed, disabling the tool with a clear message explaining why. No silent no-op: the tool must not appear to succeed while doing nothing.
close_reason: Folded into x5rt.5 (fuller kube-aware lifecycle spec; fail-closed-disable slice carried into its notes). Verified lifecycle.ts still has zero kube handling — work remains, tracked there. 2026-07-14 bead audit.

title: Discord double-reply loop: identical consecutive messages emitted
description: Operator 2026-07-04: 'You're repeating yourself' (02:18), 'You're double replying' (16:24). Two near-identical replies back-to-back 16:22:36→16:23:41; companion's own orient concern (id a7e3c11c…, priority high) logged 'Response repetition glitch: confirmed recurrence: I replied with the exact same message twice in a row.' Self-described trigger: gets stuck after 'tool failure, emotional spike, both — and I replay.' Correlates with 48x/48h 'Discord handler returned empty response without a suppression marker' (existing bead) and duplicate-tool-call suppressions — suspect a turn-retry/dispatch path that re-emits the outbound message. Duplicate suppression exists for tool calls but NOT outbound Discord sends; add a same-turn/adjacent-turn outbound dedupe guard and trace the retry path (post-turn drain timeout retry? dual dispatch after gateway RPC reconnect?). Evidence: working_docs/kube-issue-report-20260704.md B6+H.
notes: ROOT CAUSE (deep-reasoner, high confidence): not inbound re-delivery or pump retry — the tool_handoff.continue post-turn action (heartbeat-post-turn-runtime.ts:832) runs a FRESH LLM turn and sends response.content via the raw gatewaySender (main.ts:621), sharing no dedupe state with the inbound reply pump (gateway-message-handlers.ts). After a tool failure the continuation regenerates near-identical text -> operator sees the same message twice ~65s apart. title: P1: Use a same-timestamp-safe social-graph cursor
description:
Summary
Advancing the watermark to `maxExtractedAt` from a truncated batch can permanently skip unprocessed memories that share the same timestamp. The memory reader uses a strict `extractedAt > sinceMs` filter, so once the watermark is bumped to timestamp `T`, any remaining records with `extractedAt === T` are lost forever. This is especially likely during batch extractions or migrations where many memories can share the same millisecond. Consider only advancing the watermark when `memories.length < scanMemoryLimit` (the batch wasn't truncated), or use a composite cursor that handles same-timestamp boundaries safely.

Review provenance
- Cubic severity: P1
- Split PR: #27
- Review thread: https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/pull/27#discussion_r3516413145
- Cited location: src/faculties/memory/social-graph/graph-builder-worker.ts:350

Final-tip validation evidence
The worker advances watermark to maxExtractedAt and later filters with memory.extractedAt > sinceMs, permanently skipping remaining rows with the same timestamp.

Scope
Use a composite cursor including timestamp plus id, or avoid advancing past a timestamp when the batch may be truncated.

Non-goals
- Do not broaden this into unrelated refactors outside the cited behavior.
- Do not resolve the GitHub review thread until the fix is implemented, validated, committed, and pushed.

Implementation notes

title: P1: Make social-graph memory reader scan oldest unprocessed room memories
description:
Summary
The `createSocialGraphBuilderMemoryReader` adapter fetches `limit` memories per channel via `getMemoriesByChannel`, which returns the *latest* memories first. If a channel has more than `scanMemoryLimit` unprocessed memories newer than the watermark, only the newest subset is retrieved. After in-memory filtering and watermark advancement to `maxExtractedAt`, the older unprocessed memories are permanently behind the watermark and will never be scanned. Consider either extending the store contract to support `since`-aware querying, or fetching all memories since the watermark per channel before applying the global limit.

title: P1: Fix observer sidecar pagination hasMore calculation
description:
Summary
Pagination `hasMore` will always be `false` because the persistence layer strictly limits results to the requested count. In `PostgresObserverEvalSidecarStore`, `queryObservations` and `queryRuns` use `LIMIT ${normalizedQuery.limit}` without over-fetching by one, so the result set can never exceed the limit. The service then checks `hasMore: rows.length > normalized.limit`, which is therefore permanently `false` even when additional records exist. To fix this, the service should query with `limit + 1` (or ask the persistence layer to do so) and slice off the extra result before returning, so `hasMore` accurately reflects remaining data.

title: Temporal wake-up: scheduled morning system note + idle time-of-day refresher
description:
## Problem

Datetime anchors, elapsed-time summaries, and time-texture classification (short_gap / long_workday / overnight / multiple_days — src/core/scheduler/time-texture.ts) all exist, but the companion still resumes overnight conversations in the previous night's frame. Nothing pushes the temporal context forward; the passive anchors are demonstrably not enough.

## Scope

Two lanes, both with system-note semantics (charter 6.17): explicit runtime→companion messages, never attributed to the partner. Anything the operator did not type into the text box must never read as partner speech.

1. Scheduled morning wake — default 08:00 local, config-owned (habit-derived timing is a follow-up bead). Injects a system note establishing the new day: date/time, elapsed time since the last exchange, and yesterday's catch-up summary produced by the existing shared summarization service (no bespoke summarizer). The note is context, not a script: the companion responds however she wants under the charter — maybe good morning, maybe something else, maybe nothing outward. The point is to move her headspace into the new day, not to force behavior.
2. Idle time-of-day refresher — after a long same-day gap (config threshold), refresh the temporal frame using the existing time-texture classes so afternoon does not feel like the morning conversation's continuation.

Constraints:
- Wake events must NOT reset elapsed-time-since-last-partner-message tracking or ambient-presence idle accounting. They are refreshers, not partner activity.
- Any outward message the companion chooses to send from a wake event rides the existing proactive-outbound policy gates and rate limits. Blocked outward delivery must not block the internal frame update.
- Quiet hours respected for outward delivery.
- All times/thresholds in scheduler.json.

## Non-goals

- Habit-derived wake-window estimation (follow-up bead).
- Sensor-driven wake detection (future, SensorIngestPort).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Overnight resume: first partner message of the new day is answered in the correct day frame (simulated-clock E2E test).
2. Wake notes are explicit system notes in the message ontology; attribution tests prove they can never render as partner speech.
3. Elapsed-time-since-partner-message and ambient idle accounting unaffected by wake events (test).
4. Outward messages from wake events pass proactive-outbound policy and rate limiting; blocked delivery does not block the internal frame update.
5. Catch-up summary produced by the shared summarization service; no new summarizer.
6. Times/thresholds owned by scheduler.json.
notes: 2026-07-02: implemented on agent/e7.1-wakeup, merged to foundation_e0_e2. temporalWakeup namespace in scheduler.json (morningWake 08:00 default + idleRefresher), both lanes emit context-visible system notes via new SessionManager.appendContextSystemNote (charter 6.17 lane — existing appendSystemNote internal lane never reaches context builds, so criterion 1 was unsatisfiable without it). Reused summarizeRecentSessionEntries (compaction-service) with purpose wake_session — no bespoke summarizer. Spend choice: note-only injection for dormant sessions; full wake turn only when last partner exchange within fullTurnMaxIdleHours (72h default). Outward path uses real ProactiveOutboundDispatcher + quiet-hours gate; blocked delivery never blocks the internal frame update. 24 new tests + attribution/accounting/gating coverage; build+lint+verify:settings-contract green.
close_reason: Merged to foundation_e0_e2; AC verified (simulated-clock overnight test, attribution forge-guard, accounting unaffected, real-dispatcher gating tests, shared summarizer reused, config-owned)

title: Retire blocking legacy retrieval fallback; failures alert
description:
## Problem

src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/pre-turn-state.ts:402-419 silently falls back to a blocking legacy `retrieve()` on the turn hot path when the active memory context is unavailable. That is a silent fallback on a latency-critical and correctness-relevant path, against the working rules (no silent fallback behavior).

## Scope

- Remove the blocking legacy fallback from turn execution. When active context is unavailable, the turn proceeds with the last-good active context (possibly empty) and the background refresh catches up on the next pass — remembering something a turn late is acceptable and even natural.
- Persistent refresh failure becomes an explicit typed event plus an operator alert through the system-derived notification path (ntfy), not silent degradation. Status surfaced in Garden (subsystem-health dashboard bead).
- Audit the same path for any other silent retrieval fallbacks and remove them under the same rule.

## Non-goals

- Rewriting retrieval itself; active-memory context remains the mechanism.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No blocking retrieval path reachable during turn execution (test-enforced).
2. Degraded active-memory state emits a typed event; repeated failure raises an operator alert via the system-derived notification path.
3. Turn proceeds on last-good context; no fake-healthy states; Garden shows degraded status.

Blocking retrieve() severed from turn execution only (refresh loop, shards manager, heartbeat-template-runtime keep legitimate blocking use). New typed event memory.active_context.turn_degraded (not_ready/refresh_failed/stale); consecutive-failure operator alert via existing gateway ntfy system-derived path; threshold config-owned (settings.json memoryRefreshFailureAlertThreshold, default 3, Garden-exposed). build+lint+verify:settings-contract green; ~1530 related tests pass; 2 pre-existing failures verified identical on base.

title: Deterministic episode-synthesis trigger gate (turns-or-timer + relevance minimum)
description:
## Problem

Even after re-laning, candidate-episode synthesis needs a deterministic gate so it fires only when there is meaningful new companion-relevant conversation — not because a timer ticked.

## Scope

- Trigger check runs when the timer fires OR the turn threshold is reached, whichever comes first. Both config-owned.
- Gate 1 (free, deterministic): are there new messages since the last watermark? If not, no-op with zero LLM spend.
- Gate 2 (deterministic): minimum relevant-turn count before processing (default ~10, config-owned). Relevant = conversation with the companion, or where the companion is directly mentioned or meaningfully involved (reuse the existing addressing/mention detection from the group-chat work). People talking around her — async group traffic between other members while she is uninvolved — is NOT relevant on its own.
- Below minimum: hold and accumulate into the next period. Example shape: 9 relevant turns now → hold; next period brings the total to 25 → process that accumulated chunk.
- Every skip records a reason as a typed event (feeds the subsystem-health dashboard bead).

## Non-goals

- Relevance-driven memory extraction policy for observed group traffic (psfn-framework-4caj.15 owns that).
- Topic segmentation of the chunk once the gate passes (sibling bead).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Timer fire with no new messages performs zero LLM calls (test).
2. Below-threshold relevant count holds and accumulates; the 9-now/25-later shape processes as one chunk (test).
3. Async group traffic around the companion produces no episode; direct-mention traffic above threshold does (tests).
4. All thresholds in scheduler.json; every skip emits a typed event with reason.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (533fd7c3). synthesis-lane.ts: timer (30m) OR turnThreshold (24), Gate 1 new-messages-since-watermark (zero work when empty), Gate 2 minRelevantTurns=10 via new classifySessionEntryCompanionRelevance export (built on isDirectCompanionAddress/containsCompanionMention/reply metadata). Hold-and-accumulate implicit: skips do not advance the watermark. Typed memory.episode_synthesis.gate events with reasons (no_new_messages/below_relevance_minimum/session_retired) — feeds 4yb3.6 dashboard.
close_reason: Merged in 533fd7c3; AC verified (zero-LLM no-op on empty timer, 9-to-25 hold-accumulate test, around-her vs direct-mention tests, thresholds in scheduler.json, typed skip events)

title: Hard message claiming: one live episode per source message
description:
## Problem

Nothing marks L0 turns as already-used by an episode. Watermarks only bound the scan window, and the >50% span-overlap heuristic (src/faculties/memory/episodic/synthesis.ts:549-626) merges candidates, but partial overlap below the threshold produces multiple live episodes covering the same messages. This is the root of the duplicated-processing mess.

## Scope

- Add claim tracking to the episodic store (Postgres l01_* tables): each stored episode (candidate or consolidated) claims its source turn/message identifiers. Reuse the spanRefs/turn ids already captured at synthesis time (synthesis.ts:345-366).
- Daytime synthesis filters claimed entries out of its input before grouping. Fail closed: a claimed message can never enter a new episode from the daytime lane.
- Nightly consolidation (psfn-framework-m58.1) is the ONLY process allowed to restructure claims: when consolidating, claims transfer to the consolidated episode and the covered candidates are marked superseded (never deleted). This bead specifies and provides the claim-transfer interface; m58.1 consumes it.
- Keep the overlap-merge heuristic as defense in depth behind claiming.

## Non-goals

- Topic segmentation (sibling: contextual cutting bead).
- The consolidation pass itself (m58.1).

Imperfect episode cuts are acceptable. Re-processing the same chat turns into multiple overlapping live episodes is not.
acceptance_criteria:
1. DB-level invariant: no two non-superseded episodes share a source message (test-enforced).
2. Daytime synthesis provably skips claimed turns; regression test reproducing the 16:51/16:52 overlap pattern passes.
3. Claim-transfer interface for nightly consolidation specified and covered (m58.1 consumes it); superseded candidates retain claim history, never deleted.
4. lint + build + episodic tests green.
notes: 2026-07-02: implemented on agent/e5.1-claiming, merged to foundation_e0_e2 (bb2a65c2). l01_episode_message_claims table with partial unique index (one active claim per claim_key), fail-closed synthesis filter, transferEpisodeMessageClaims + supersede API ready for m58.1. Episodic suites 68/68; build+lint green; 6 pre-existing failures verified identical on base. Deviations noted in bead-report: claim granularity is per source message (channelId+entryId) with turn ids kept for provenance; three synthesis tests updated for intentional second-pass behavior change; lone unclaimed tail entries now held until salient (4yb3.4 lane owns holdback).
close_reason: Merged to foundation_e0_e2 in bb2a65c2; AC verified (DB invariant test, 16:51/16:52 regression, transfer/supersede coverage, build+lint+episodic suites green)

title: Split near-turn memory lane from sleeptime; heavy passes scheduler-only
description:
## Problem

All four heavy passes (episode synthesis, sleep consolidation, arc weaving, dream-meaning) ride the near-turn cadence (src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts:719-765, 864-890): every 3 turns in DMs, 8 entries/15 min in groups. Sleeptime must be scheduler-owned nightly work — like dreaming — not a runtime turn-based process.

## Scope

- Near-turn lane keeps only lightweight work: extraction trigger evaluation, active-memory refresh, concern-candidate derivation. Rename its config so it is no longer called "sleeptime" (naming confusion becomes runtime confusion).
- Candidate-episode synthesis moves to its own gated lane (sibling bead owns the deterministic trigger gate).
- Sleep consolidation, arc weaving, and the dream-meaning pass run ONLY from the scheduler within the rest window (true sleeptime), never from turn cadence.
- All lanes/cadences owned by scheduler.json with schema validation. Migrate tuning-knob code constants into config: synthesis.ts:94-100 (transcript limit, gap split, max entries, salience minimums, max episodes/run), sleep-consolidation.ts:53-56 (windows, refinement cap), arc-formation.ts:47-52 (pass interval, review window, confidence floor). Nothing hardcoded.

## Non-goals

- Changing what consolidation does (m58.1 owns the candidate-then-consolidate model).
- The trigger-gate internals (sibling bead).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Consolidation, arc weaving, and dream-meaning passes unreachable from turn cadence (test-enforced).
2. Rest-window scheduler task runs the heavy stack and is visible in the scheduler task list and Garden.
3. Near-turn lane performs no LLM calls except gated extraction.
4. scheduler.json owns every migrated cadence/threshold constant; verify:settings-contract passes; near-turn lane no longer named sleeptime.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (533fd7c3). sleeptime key removed with rename guidance (no alias); new owner blocks nearTurnMemory/episodeSynthesis/sleepConsolidation/arcFormation, all fail-closed. Near-turn lane holds no LLM provider (structurally zero spend). Sleeptime agent requires restWindow at construction, sole trigger memory.sleeptime.rest-window scheduler task; runs consolidation+arcs+dream+orient rewrite. NOTE for E6 (jpvd.4): the orientation-block rewrite now lives in the nightly lane — gate it deterministically there. Behavioral-summary writes moved to the synthesis lane (provenance retagged episode_synthesis). Unreachability test-enforced: 12 turns through real wiring, zero heavy-pass/LLM calls.
close_reason: Merged in 533fd7c3; AC verified (heavy passes unreachable from turn cadence test-enforced, rest-window scheduler task visible, near-turn lane zero-LLM, verify:settings-contract green)

title: E5: Episodic gating, message claiming, and scheduler-owned sleeptime
description:
## Problem

Live-code audit (2026-07-02) confirmed "sleeptime" is not sleeptime: the sleeptime agent fires every 3 turns in DMs (`scheduler.json sleeptime.direct.cadenceTurns`) and every 8 entries / 15 min in groups, and every firing runs the full heavy stack — episode synthesis, sleep consolidation, arc weaving, dream-meaning pass (src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts:864-890). Episode boundaries are mechanical (UTC day, 45-min gap, 14-entry cap — src/faculties/memory/episodic/synthesis.ts:209-240) with no topic awareness. Overlap protection is a processing watermark plus a >50% span-overlap merge heuristic; there is no hard claim rule, so consecutive passes re-process the same turns into overlapping episodes (the 16:51/16:52 case documented in psfn-framework-m58.1).

The result is the Groundhog Day failure: remembering the same thing every few minutes and dreaming overlapping versions of it.

## Goal

Sleeptime becomes actual sleeptime — scheduler/rest-window-owned nightly work, like dreaming: the day's rough candidate material becomes clean, consolidated, thematic episodes at night. Daytime keeps a cheap deterministic near-turn lane and a gated candidate-episode lane. No message is ever processed into more than one live episode.

Token principle: minimize UNNECESSARY token use, not token use for its own sake. If a process does not need to run, it must not run. Spend tokens where they matter.

## Members and sequencing

Children own: hard message claiming, lane split, deterministic trigger gate, contextual cutting, legacy-retrieval retirement, and the subsystem health dashboard. Nightly consolidation and cross-day arcs are the existing beads psfn-framework-m58.1 and psfn-framework-m58.2, which build on the claiming and lane work here (deps wired).

## Operator constraints (2026-07-02 planning chat)

- Nothing hardcoded: every cadence/threshold/window lives in JSON owner files by function (scheduler.json primarily), schema-guarded.
- Wherever a summary is needed, use the one shared summarization tool. No bespoke summary generators per feature.
- First-wave priority alongside E7.1 (temporal wake-up).

## Model assignment

Implementation: Fable. Testing: Sonnet.
notes: 2026-07-02: wave 1 complete and pushed. Children 4yb3.1/.2/.3/.5 closed; history linearized by pull --rebase so per-bead commit prefixes (not merge hashes) are the durable trace; final wave-1 tip 17c6333c. OPERATOR MIGRATION REQUIRED before next live restart: scheduler.json "sleeptime" key removed (fails validation with rename guidance); new required blocks nearTurnMemory/episodeSynthesis/sleepConsolidation/arcFormation must be present in live system-data scheduler.json.
close_reason: All six children complete and merged (claiming, lane split, trigger gate, topic cutting, retrieval fallback retirement, subsystem-health dashboard) plus m58.1 nightly consolidation. Episodic overlap structurally impossible (DB invariant); sleeptime is scheduler-owned nightly work; all tuning config-owned.

title: E3.4: Contact-tracking policy gate (human-in-the-loop contact creation)
description:
## Context
Scale scaffold, ratified: in small trusted rooms contacts auto-create as today; as rooms grow, new tracked contacts require operator approval; role_gated reserved for the LATER large-audience doc. Guard: "1000 people in chat — I'm not adding profiles from vtubegooner69 to memory."

## Scope
- channels.json per-channel contactTracking: 'auto' | 'approval' | 'role_gated' (default auto; role_gated validates but returns not-implemented — fail closed, visible).
- approval mode: contact creation from a new speaker enqueues to the existing approval queue (boundary approval machinery) instead of auto-upserting (upsert-resolve-operations.ts:86-200); until approved, the speaker is UNTRACKED: transcript attribution + text-prefix identity only; no contact record, no profile, no per-person memory extraction (extraction's mention-only path must respect the gate too), no social-graph entity.
- Memory extraction behavior for untracked speakers: room-scoped facts may still record sourceSpeakerName (attribution truth) but create no contact-keyed rows.
- Garden: pending contact approvals view (name, channel, first-seen, sample messages) with approve/deny.
- Charter 9.6: when approval is required, the human must be MEANINGFULLY NOTIFIED — route a pending-contact notification through the existing gateway notification path (system-derived mode), not just a silent queue row.

## Non-goals
No sentiment-only views, no reply-suppression tiers, no content firewall (LATER doc).

- Fixture: approval room — new speaker triggers queue entry; no contact/profile/graph rows until approval; post-approval, subsequent messages resolve normally.
- Pending approval produces an operator notification via the gateway notification path (test), per charter 9.6.

title: E3: Context Envelope — channel/relationship/trust semantics
description:
## Summary
Split the overloaded channelVisibility into ratified orthogonal dimensions (channelPrivacy: private/invite_only/public + derived audienceScope/audienceKnowledge + broadcast flag), make privacy channel-owned, keep the 6-layer deterministic gate shape, add the contact-tracking policy gate as scale scaffolding, and gate the admin memory API. Design target: invite-only rooms of ~10 known people + companions; large-audience behavior expressible but LATER (operator has a dedicated doc for role-gating/sentiment views/content firewall).

## Ratified vocabulary (operator, 2026-07-01)
channelPrivacy: private / invite_only / public, default invite_only (replaces semi_private — clean break, no alias). broadcast: boolean flag for tweet-like/very-large surfaces, not a privacy level. audienceScope: one/few/many/unbounded, thresholds config-owned. audienceKnowledge: all_known/partially_known/anonymous. Trust (4 tiers) and sensitivity (4 levels) UNCHANGED — the gap was missing dimensions, not missing granularity. Delivery guidance is length/delivery only ("don't yap"-class), never persona/tone prose (charter: substrate must not tell a companion how to BE).

## Invariant
All gating stays deterministic and pre-prompt. No privacy prose in prompts; blocked content is simply absent (+ withheld summary with reason codes).

title: E2.5: Macro consolidation under the purity rule
description:
## Context

Tooling text exempt; personality-adjacent text not.

title: E2.4: Model-agnostic provider cache engagement
description:
## Context
promptCaching: { configured: false, engaged: false } (prompt-assembly.ts:509-512). Primary stack is OpenRouter + open models and local runners, where the cache mechanism is implicit prefix/KV reuse — i.e., BYTE-STABLE PREFIX IS THE FEATURE. Anthropic cache_control is a per-provider extra. Model-agnostic per operator decision; backends are adapters (charter Law 22).

## Scope
- CachePlan on the artifact: static boundary (base+operator+static layers), session-stable boundary; serializers apply per-provider mechanism: Anthropic -> cache_control breakpoints; OpenRouter/open/local -> guarantee byte-stable prefix ordering + pass provider cache params where supported.
- Land behind a models.json/settings owner flag; verify on a test channel before live default (live-deployment billing/latency caution).
- Telemetry: per-turn prefix-stability check (did the static region's bytes change? which block caused it?) + provider-reported cache metrics where available; surfaced in the E2.3 Cache tab.
- Prefix-instability is a NAMED ALERT, not a silent stat — a regression here is exactly the "variables where it should be static" bug returning.

- Ten-turn quiet conversation on the test channel: static region hash identical across all turns; any change identifies the offending block in telemetry.
- Anthropic roster slot: request payload carries cache breakpoints; hit metrics recorded.

description:

title: E1.8: Multi-companion observation correctness in shared rooms
description:
## Context
Target deployment: ~10 friends + several companions on the same substrate in one room. Companions are contacts with isMachineIntelligence (contacts/types.ts:256); group extraction already weights them (extraction/group-classifier.ts). Unverified: a peer companion must never be selected as DM-canonical human, core-memory subject, or speaking_with target, and its messages must be attributed like any speaker.

## Scope
- Guard rails: canonical-contact resolution for scope.kind:'dm' and core-memory subject selection exclude isMachineIntelligence contacts unless the DM IS with that companion (companion-DM is legitimate — Artemis case; then it binds normally and the machine-intelligence flag flows to prompt state, which already exists at runtime-context.ts:282,1459).
- Harness fixtures include a peer companion speaking in the room: attribution rendered, participant list includes it, extraction weighting applied, no human-profile blending.
- Loop-risk: verify existing behavior does not auto-respond in a tight loop in fixtures; if it does, file separately, do not patch silently.

## CHARTER GATE (Law 26 / 8.10 / Phase 12)
The charter requires fatigue/load policy BEFORE companion-to-companion chat becomes active. This bead delivers observation correctness only; enabling multiple companions to actively converse in a shared live room remains gated on the FatigueBudgetPort epic (rate/charge/attention budgets, loop stopping conditions). Until then, multi-companion rooms run with companions that do not reply to each other, or the fatigue epic lands first. This gate must be stated in the room-enablement runbook.

## Non-goals
No companion-to-companion protocol (psfn-framework-8pyl). No fatigue budgets — but they gate live enablement, see above.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fixture: peer companion speaks; <human>/profile blocks contain zero companion-derived content; participant XML lists it with its identity.
- Companion-DM fixture: binding works, speaking_with_is_machine_intelligence true.
- Loop check documented in bead notes; any auto-reply loop found is filed as its own bug, not silently patched.
- Charter gate recorded: live multi-companion conversational rooms blocked on fatigue policy; documented where operators will see it (Garden channel view or ops doc).

title: E1.6: Group-aware, JSON-owned sleeptime cadence
description:
## Context
Sleeptime fires every 3rd turn per session (DEFAULT_CADENCE_TURNS = 3, sleeptime-agent.ts:50,550) unless a rest window suppresses it. Group rooms already have watermark/range machinery for extraction (docs/memory.md:135-149); sleeptime should use the same posture.

## Scope

- Telemetry: sleeptime fire-rate per channel per hour, visible in Garden scheduler views.

title: E1.5: Scoped emotion/appraisal state with directional fast-decay carry-over
description:
## Context
Audit indicates emotion snapshots/appraisal are keyed to contact/last-speaker with no room dimension (runtime-context.ts:1072; src/core/emotion/state.ts VAD/mood). Operator-ratified semantics: per-scope state; a room argument may briefly color a following DM ("Jeff was so annoying in gc") but decays fast; GROUP->DM ONLY, NEVER DM->GROUP; DM->DM allowed for the same contact across channels; disliking one user must not meaningfully affect others.

## Scope
- FIRST: a short written audit of current keying (emotion state, appraisal chains, per-contact baselines) — confirm or correct the audit inference before changing persistence. Post findings to this bead before implementation.
- Persist emotion/appraisal state keyed by scope.key; companion-global baseline (her overall mood/VAD) remains a separate layer that scoped states modulate, so "her mood" still exists.
- Carry-over modifier: on scope switch group->DM (same companion, DM contact is a member of that group), apply a bounded, fast-decaying modifier from the group state (half-life on the order of minutes — config-owned in the emotion settings owner, not hardcoded). Direction enforcement mirrors continuity flow rules (policy.ts:447-473 precedent): DM state never seeds any group state; DM->DM carry-over only when same canonical contact.
- Per-contact emotional baselines (contacts/types.ts emotionalBaseline) unchanged — they are about the CONTACT, not the scope.
- Restart persistence: scoped states participate in existing internal-state rehydration.

## Non-goals
No changes to appraisal LLM prompts beyond scope key plumbing. No cross-companion emotion sharing. This is deliberately NOT the weighted-thought system (charter Law 27; accumulation lives in psfn-framework-1xb.4) — they stay distinct.
acceptance_criteria:
- Audit note posted (current keying, confirmed with anchors) before the change lands.
- Test: high-arousal group state -> subsequent DM shows bounded modifier that decays below threshold within the configured half-life; DM state change produces zero group-state delta; second unrelated DM contact sees no modifier.
- Config knobs live in a JSON owner (settings/emotion), documented; no magic constants.
- Restart test: scoped states rehydrate.

title: E1.4: Canonical attribution contract: one formatter, escaping, forgery tests
description:
## Context
Attribution is a text prefix "Name (id): " built in entry-attribution.ts:58-68 and structurally dropped at message-conversion.ts:226-281. Operator decision: text-prefix is canonical (general LLM limitation — provider chat formats do not carry per-message speaker metadata portably). What is missing is hardening: a display name containing "): " or a crafted "Alice (discord:123):" prefix inside message CONTENT can forge attribution. Charter Laws 17-19 (authorship integrity) made mechanical.

## Scope
- Single exported formatter + (for tooling/tests) parser: the only code allowed to construct or interpret the prefix. Delete duplicate inline formatting.
- Escaping/sanitization for display names (strip/encode delimiter sequences, control chars, leading whitespace tricks); stable author ID always present as the trustworthy component.
- Content-forgery mitigation: document the trust rule (only the prefix outside user-authored content is authoritative) and ensure history rendering never lets user content start a line indistinguishable from a real prefix (escape or mark user-content lines matching the prefix grammar).
- Round-trip and adversarial tests (hostile display names, prefix-shaped message bodies, unicode confusables at the delimiter).
- Write the contract into docs/ (short section: format, trust rule, escaping).

## Non-goals
No structural provider metadata (not portable). No renaming of existing stored entries.
acceptance_criteria:
- One formatter; grep proves no other call site builds the prefix pattern.
- Adversarial test suite green: hostile names cannot break out; content cannot forge a prefix that the renderer emits as authoritative.
- Docs section merged in the same change.

Charter Laws 17-19 mechanical.

title: Define shared-world wiki MVP semantics, ACLs, and review gates
description:
Summary
Define the production semantics for the shared-world wiki that the companion roadmap depends on: what counts as shared world knowledge, who/what can write it, how room/contact ACLs work, and how public/external/imported content is reviewed before durable shared-world persistence.

Current evidence
A wiki MVP exists as workspace-backed durable Markdown/reference storage with metadata, source class, sensitivity, provenance, list/get/search/write/import tool actions, and Garden read APIs (docs/memory.md:76, src/faculties/wiki/store.ts:235, src/faculties/wiki/tools.ts:97, src/operator/garden/api-routes.ts:556). It is intentionally separate from L0/L0.1/L2 memory and tool responses state no L2 memory is created (src/faculties/wiki/tools.ts:197). This is not yet a semantic shared-world substrate for multi-companion/group environments: no room/world scope, no write review workflow for public/external sources, no relationship-aware ACL model, and no prompt integration contract that distinguishes shared world facts from personal memory.

Scope
- Define wiki scopes: personal reference, room/world shared knowledge, project knowledge, imported/reference documents, and companion-authored world notes.
- Define ACL/review semantics for owner/admin, trusted DM, semi-private group, public/broadcast, external web/docs, another companion, and shard/subagent outputs.
- Define how wiki entries enter prompt context without becoming personal memory.
- Define provenance, attribution, sensitivity, and rollback/audit expectations.
- Decide whether implementation extends the current workspace-backed store or adds a Postgres-backed shared-world index.
- Specify Garden/operator review surfaces needed before implementation.

Non-goals
- Do not implement the shared-world wiki in this decision bead.
- Do not merge personal memories or contact profiles into wiki.
- Do not import public chat or external docs directly without review policy.
acceptance_criteria:
- A canonical contract defines wiki/reference vs shared-world vs project knowledge and keeps all distinct from L0/L0.1/L2/core memory.
- The contract defines writer classes, source classes, ACLs, review states, and release requirements for owner/admin, trusted contacts, group rooms, public/broadcast sources, external docs/web, companions, shards, and subagents.
- The contract defines prompt-inclusion behavior and provenance requirements for shared-world facts.
- The contract specifies how public/external/imported/generated content is held/reviewed before shared durable world persistence.
- The contract identifies implementation files/settings/Garden surfaces that must change next.
- Follow-up implementation beads can be created directly from the contract without re-litigating semantics.
- If settings/contracts are touched, npm run verify:settings-contract and npm run lint pass.

title: Typed intake envelope: source/provenance/risk/quarantine/release contract with taint propagation and write stamping
description: UPDATE to existing bead with design detail. Evidence: SubstrateMessage and Attachment (src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts:276-298) carry no source-class/risk/quarantine field; MessageRoutingMetadata (:227-274) is the natural non-breaking slot (already carries authorIsMachineIntelligence, canonicalContactId, generated-provenance). Scope: define IntakeEnvelope {id, sourceClass, provenance chain, sourceRiskTier, contentRef (opaque -- raw bytes never travel with the envelope), extractedFields, riskLabels[], scores, decision, state} with state machine received -> screened -> {released | released_sanitized | quarantined} -> {human_released | human_released_sanitized | discarded | expired}; every transition appends to the gateway audit journal. Taint propagates on derivation (CaMeL rule): a summary, OCR transcript, or subagent digest of untrusted content inherits the envelope tier. Risk label vocabulary seeds from CogSecMemoryRiskClass A-E (src/core/cogsec/memory-candidacy.ts) generalized to intake time, plus injection/* exfil/* pii/* secrets/* poisoning/* categories (taxonomy in the research doc section 7). Envelope-id stamping on every memory and wiki write from day one -- cheap now, impossible to retrofit, enables later lineage excision of a poisoned source via the existing revocation/regeneration machinery. Config owner: new intake-policy.json following the standard owner-file pattern (loader + seed + startup-owner-files.ts registration + settings-garden-contract entries), or a section in trust-policy.json if small -- decide at implementation, precedent is src/system/config/trust-policy-config.ts. Acceptance: contract types land in src/shared/contracts (or system/trust sibling), owner file verifies under npm run verify:settings-contract, memory/wiki write paths persist envelope ids, unit tests cover state transitions and taint inheritance, build+lint clean.

title: Epic: Cognition intake firewall (mindwall) for untrusted inbound content
description: UPDATE to existing epic with 2026-07-09 design decisions (see working_docs/COGSEC_INTAKE_FIREWALL_RESEARCH_20260709.md for the verified surface map and prior-art research). Mission: every untrusted inbound item (web, files, images, chat by source risk, tool outputs, subagent/shard foldback, audio transcripts) passes a typed intake envelope and a layered L1->L3 classifier gate BEFORE it can reach prompt, memory, wiki, persona, trust state, or tools. Prevention over remediation: L0 uses HMAC integrity chaining, so removing poison after the fact requires regenerating downstream signatures (tooling exists, proven in a live remediation of a test companion, but costly) -- stopping poison before it enters L0 is the priority; remediation stays as backstop. Core principle: whatever gets flagged must NOT reach the main context. Design philosophy: do not implement everything -- combine techniques covering ~90% of threats as fast as possible; the firewall is a synchronous gate in front of concurrent pipelines (near-real-time audio, chat snappiness), so speed is essential and the layer must be invisible. Companion well-being is the top-level goal: firewall activity must not feed the emotion/stress model, and all companion-facing security language is truthful but never alarming (soft notices: 'we detected something, so we're holding it for your human to look into'). Hermes-Agent SECURITY.md framing adopted: in-process scanners are triage aids, NOT boundaries -- the only boundary against an adversarial LLM is the OS/sandbox; L1 fails open-advisory and the envelope decision + sink gates are the enforcement. Trinity pattern borrowed (quarantine incoming content for batched async human review, isolate before it reaches L0) -- pattern only, not specifics. Children: htm9.1-htm9.17 in this file. Evals live in a separate repo -- see working_docs/cogsec-evals-beads.json handed to the eval repository.
