title: P1: Expose safe agent-visible CogSec event log
description:
## Summary
Expose safe CogSec event metadata to agents and diagnostics so they know why context is missing, without exposing what the poisoned content said or how it worked. This is separate from transcript search: agents should learn from a CogSec log/notice, not by seeing tombstone rows in search results.

## Why
After tombstoning and search exclusion, an agent may encounter continuity gaps. It should be allowed and encouraged to know that a CogSec intervention occurred, but only at a bland, non-infectious level. Returning ten tombstones in transcript search will confuse the companion and pollute task context. A dedicated safe log is cleaner.

## Current Code Anchors
- src/core/session/manager/context-builder.ts and prompt/session context assembly can include safe notices where relevant.
- src/core/tools/session-search.ts should avoid tombstone spam; CogSec visibility belongs elsewhere.
- src/operator/garden/routes/session-routes.ts and future CogSec routes can expose admin/operator metadata.
- src/core/turns/observability.ts and prompt monitor surfaces may display safe diagnostic metadata.

## Required Behavior
Provide a safe CogSec event/log view for companion runtime and developer diagnostics:
- Agent-visible event summary: case ID, high-level type/severity/status, affected source/session/range metadata if safe, and bland reason text.
- No payload, no bypass pattern, no sealed artifact dereference, no exploit details, no raw tombstone row dump.
- Prompt/runtime inclusion only when relevant: e.g. current session/range had context sealed or an agent explicitly asks why context is missing.
- Operator/admin views may show richer metadata and counts but still not raw sealed payload by default.
- CogSec log should explain that derived cognitive artifacts were revoked/regenerated from clean sources when applicable.

## Example Safe Notice
`CogSec case cogsec_123 sealed unsafe instruction-like content from this conversation span. Related cognitive artifacts were revoked or regenerated from clean sources. The sealed payload is unavailable to companion runtime.`

## Non-goals
- Do not expose sealed payload content or reproduction details.
- Do not use transcript search as the primary way agents learn about CogSec interventions.
- Do not make every CogSec event a permanent identity/persona memory.
acceptance_criteria:
- Agents/diagnostics can access safe CogSec event metadata explaining missing context without payload details.
- Prompt/session context includes CogSec notices only when relevant and never includes raw payload, exploit mechanics, or sealed refs that can be dereferenced by companion tools.
- Normal transcript search does not return tombstone rows as the CogSec awareness mechanism.
- Operator/admin surfaces can show safe counts/status/action metadata.
- Tests prove prompt snapshots, session search, and agent-visible logs omit poisoned payload text and attack mechanics.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.
close_reason: Implemented safe CogSec event log and prompt/session notices. Evidence: src/core/cogsec/safe-log.ts exposes agent/operator-safe event views that omit sealed refs/hashes and dirty text; src/core/session/manager/context-builder.ts accepts relevant CogSec events and renders session.cogsec_notices into the final system prompt plus prompt-section telemetry; src/core/identity/prompt-runtime.ts registers session.cogsec_notices as a reorderable runtime prompt block; scripts/cogsec-remediation-smoke.ts validates the live remediation flow builds a safe notice without dirty text or sealed refs. title: P1: Add CogSec remediation mode to Session Recovery UX
description:
## Summary
Extend the existing Garden Review & Safety Session Recovery page with a CogSec remediation mode. This mode should guide an operator through creating a CogSec event, selecting affected source channel/message range, previewing lineage impact, and applying the seal -> tombstone -> search-exclude -> revoke -> regenerate -> epoch-cut workflow.

## Why
The current /session-recovery page handles emergency fresh logical session resets. CogSec remediation is more dangerous and specific: it removes contaminated payload from companion L0 and revokes derived cognition. Operators need a deliberate UX that distinguishes normal recovery from CogSec redaction and shows enough impact preview to avoid accidental broad damage.

## Current Code Anchors
- admin-ui/src/routes/session-recovery/+page.svelte is the existing page.
- admin-ui/src/lib/nav.ts already places Session Recovery under Review & Safety.
- admin-ui/src/lib/api/endpoints/sessions.ts has session route APIs.
- src/operator/garden/routes/session-routes.ts and services/session-service.ts own current admin session route endpoints.
- New CogSec services/routes should follow existing Garden route/service/type patterns.

## Required Behavior
The UX should include a CogSec mode separate from ordinary fresh split/quarantine:
- Inputs: source channel, logical session/message IDs or range, case type, severity, reason, actor.
- Option to create an event draft and preview lineage impact.
- Preview counts/classes: L0 rows, projection rows, memories/embeddings, summaries, active cache, episodic/profile/persona-adjacent artifacts, lineage gaps.
- Apply action with strong confirmation and clear destructive wording: dirty companion L0 will be tombstoned, sealed archive retained outside companion reach.
- Progress/result panel for seal, tombstone, projection rebuild, revocation, regeneration queue, epoch cut.
- Safe CogSec event log visible on the page.

## Safety Rules
The page must not render raw poisoned payload, exploit mechanics, sealed artifact contents, or reproduction details. It may display IDs, ranges, counts, safe summaries, and opaque sealed refs/hashes where appropriate.

## Non-goals
- Do not make CogSec remediation a companion-facing tool.
- Do not bury CogSec only in generic sessions page.
- Do not add raw payload preview by default.
acceptance_criteria:
- /session-recovery has a distinct CogSec mode separate from ordinary fresh split/quarantine.
- Operators can enter source channel, affected message/session range, case type, severity, reason, and actor.
- UX can request and display a safe lineage/remediation preview with counts/classes and lineage gaps.
- UX can apply the remediation pipeline and show step results without displaying raw payload.
- UX clearly states that companion L0 rows will be tombstoned and sealed evidence stored outside companion reach.
- Frontend/API contract tests or type checks cover the new endpoint contracts where practical.
- npm run lint, npm run garden:build, and relevant targeted tests pass before closure.

title: P1: Regenerate clean summaries, memories, and indexes after CogSec redaction
description:
## Summary
Add a maintenance/operator job that regenerates clean cognitive state after CogSec redaction and revocation. It should rebuild from tombstoned companion L0 plus clean lineage, never from sealed payloads.

## Why
After L0 tombstoning and derived-artifact revocation, the companion may have continuity gaps. The correct repair is to recompute summaries, memories, embeddings, search projection, active memory packs, and profile/episodic state from clean sources. This should not run synchronously in the chat turn path.

## Current Code Anchors
- src/core/session/manager.ts and context builder own compaction summaries and context assembly.
- src/faculties/memory/extraction.ts and orchestrator can generate memories from session content.
- src/faculties/memory/startup-hydration.ts warms active memory context.
- src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts handles background memory/orientation cleanup.
- src/persistence/sessions/store.ts and transcript projection adapters rebuild search projection from L0.
- src/operator/garden/services/session-service.ts can be extended or a new CogSec service can own operator-triggered regeneration.

## Required Behavior
After a CogSec case is applied:
- Rebuild transcript projection/search indexes from tombstoned L0, with tombstones excluded from normal search.
- Recompute compaction/session summaries from clean/tombstoned source only.
- Regenerate memories where lineage says clean recovery is possible.
- Recompute embeddings only from clean regenerated memory text.
- Rebuild active-memory cache from clean source.
- Queue/regenerate episodic/profile/contact/persona-adjacent artifacts where supported.
- Advance/cut session epoch or route fresh lane as needed after regeneration.
- Record regeneration results in CogSec event metadata.

## Safety Rules
The regeneration job must not read sealed payload content. It must not include tombstone text as a substantive memory. It may include a safe CogSec event notice when needed to explain a continuity gap.

## Non-goals
- Do not block normal chat responses on regeneration.
- Do not silently restore revoked artifacts without clean source provenance.
- Do not run broad model summarization over sealed forensic artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
- A CogSec regeneration job can rebuild projections, summaries, memories, embeddings, active memory, and supported episodic/profile artifacts from clean/tombstoned sources only.
- Regenerated artifacts contain no sealed payload text, attack mechanics, or tombstone text treated as substantive memory.
- Revoked artifacts are not restored unless regenerated from clean provenance.
- Regeneration is operator/maintenance triggered or queued, not synchronous in the chat response path.
- CogSec event metadata records regeneration results and failures.
- Tests prove poisoned text cannot re-enter prompt context after regeneration and clean unrelated memories remain available.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.

Evidence: src/core/cogsec/regeneration.ts adds applyCogSecRegeneration, which rebuilds transcript/search projection, regenerates invalidated compaction summaries from clean non-tombstone SessionEntry inputs, delegates clean memory/embedding regeneration, rebuilds active memory context from clean source text, queues/regenerates supported external artifacts through explicit ports, and records only safe IDs/counts/failures on CogSec events. Evidence: src/persistence/sessions/store.ts adds applyCogSecCompactionRegenerations, replacing only CogSec-invalidated compaction summary rows and rejecting regenerated summary text that contains CogSec tombstone/invalidation markers. Evidence: scripts/cogsec-remediation-smoke.ts now exercises tombstone -> lineage preview -> revocation -> regeneration with real SessionStore, MemoryStore, MemoryRetriever, CogSecEventStore, and sealed archive. title: P1: Revoke lineage-derived cognitive artifacts for CogSec cases
description:
## Summary
Implement the CogSec revocation executor that takes a CogSec event plus lineage preview and removes affected derived artifacts from companion cognition. This should revoke/soft-delete/invalidate artifacts by provenance, not by loose string search.

## Why
L0 tombstoning removes the direct payload, but poison can survive as summaries, memories, embeddings, active-memory cache, episodic landmarks, profile summaries, or persona-adjacent state. Since lineage exists, the right strategy is to revoke derived artifacts and regenerate clean state instead of patching poisoned artifacts in place.

## Current Code Anchors
- psfn-framework-4tkt will provide CogSec lineage preview.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts supports memory soft-delete/delete versions and stores embeddings on l2_memories.
- src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts already excludes deleted/superseded and retired-session-quarantined memories.
- src/faculties/memory/active-context.ts caches active memory context by session/channel identity.
- src/faculties/memory/startup-hydration.ts and src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.ts hydrate/update active memory contexts.
- Episodic/profile artifacts expose provenance in existing Garden/memory services.

## Required Behavior
Given a CogSec event and lineage preview, perform revocation/invalidation for affected artifacts:
- Soft-delete or revoke L2 memories with deleteReason including CogSec case ID.
- Ensure embeddings for revoked memories are not returned by vector search.
- Invalidate active-memory cache entries tied to affected sessions/artifacts.
- Invalidate compaction/focus/session summaries that include tainted rows.
- Invalidate or mark for rebuild episodic landmarks/episodes and profile/contact/persona-adjacent derived artifacts tied to affected provenance.
- Record result counts and failed items back to CogSec event metadata.
- Leave unrelated clean artifacts untouched.

## Safety Rules
Revocation logs and events must not include payload text. They may include artifact IDs, counts, source refs, case IDs, and safe reason codes.

## Non-goals
- Do not hard-delete memory rows where soft-delete/versioning exists.
- Do not regenerate clean artifacts in this bead; queue or mark for regeneration only.
- Do not revoke all channel memories unless the CogSec event scope is the full session/epoch.
acceptance_criteria:
- CogSec revocation executor consumes a lineage preview and revokes/invalidates affected derived artifacts by structured provenance.
- Revoked L2 memories are no longer returned by semantic/vector, lexical, proactive, active-memory, or contact/profile retrieval paths.
- Affected embeddings, summaries, active-memory cache entries, episodic/profile/persona-adjacent artifacts are invalidated or marked for regeneration.
- Unrelated clean artifacts in the same channel remain available.
- CogSec event metadata records artifact counts, IDs where safe, and failures without payload text.
- Tests cover direct memory revocation, embedding exclusion, cache invalidation, summary invalidation, unrelated artifact preservation, and failure reporting.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.

title: P1: Exclude CogSec tombstones from normal transcript search and projections
description:
## Summary
Make CogSec tombstoned L0 rows non-searchable in normal companion-facing transcript search, grep, and projection paths. Agents should know via the safe CogSec event log that a span was sealed, but normal search should not return tombstone spam or case refs as if they were useful transcript matches.

## Why
After CogSec remediation, affected L0 rows will contain safe tombstones such as `[CogSec redaction: case_id]`. If transcript projection indexes those tombstones normally, searches for CogSec/case IDs/redaction text can return many tombstones and confuse the companion. Searching for the original payload must return zero. Searching normal conversation should not be polluted by tombstones. Operators still need diagnostics for redaction counts by case through CogSec/admin views.

## Current Code Anchors
- src/persistence/sessions/store.ts syncs transcript projection and implements searchByKeywords.
- src/persistence/sessions/transcript-projection-port.ts defines projection/search interfaces.
- src/persistence/sessions/transcript-projection.ts implements SQLite projection.
- src/persistence/sessions/postgres-adapters.ts implements Postgres projection/search.
- src/core/tools/session-search.ts exposes session_search and session_grep.
- src/core/session/search-runtime.ts filters and summarizes transcript hits.

## Required Behavior
- Rebuild transcript/search projections from tombstoned L0 after CogSec redaction.
- Exclude CogSec tombstone rows from normal session_search/session_grep/searchByKeywords results by default.
- Ensure tombstone text, case IDs, sealed refs, and original payload text are not indexed into normal companion search.
- Provide an operator-only diagnostic path that can report tombstone/redaction counts by CogSec case without payload text.
- Keep projection rebuild deterministic and compatible with both SQLite and Postgres projection adapters.

## Safety Rules
Companion-facing search should not reveal payload, attack mechanics, sealed refs, or long lists of tombstones. Agent awareness comes from the safe CogSec event log, not transcript-search hits.

## Non-goals
- Do not hide the existence of a CogSec event from authorized operator/agent diagnostics.
- Do not delete sealed forensic evidence.
- Do not change L0 message schema.
- Do not solve memory revocation in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- After L0 tombstoning, searching for the original payload returns zero normal companion-facing hits.
- Searching for CogSec tombstone text or case IDs does not return tombstone spam through normal session_search/session_grep/searchByKeywords.
- Operator-only diagnostics can report redacted/tombstoned row counts by case ID without payload text.
- Projection rebuild excludes tombstones consistently for SQLite and Postgres-backed projections.
- Tests cover session_search, session_grep, projection rebuild, payload search miss, tombstone search miss, and diagnostic counts.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.

title: P1: Add sealed forensic archive outside companion runtime reach
description:
## Summary
Add the sealed forensic archive used by CogSec remediation to preserve contaminated source rows outside companion reach. This archive is for operators/security tooling and future CogSec shield classifier/tool development. Companion runtime, prompt generation, memory extraction, summarization, embedding, and normal search must not be able to read the sealed payload.

## Why
CogSec remediation must remove dirty payload from companion-owned L0, but the project still needs forensic continuity: exact payloads, row metadata, hashes, and context needed to build detectors and regression tools. That evidence belongs in a security-only archive, not in normal L0 or the CogSec event table.

## Current Code Anchors
- src/persistence/layout.ts owns runtime storage paths and must define any new owner path.
- src/operator/garden/services/session-service.ts and future CogSec services need to write archive refs.
- Existing backup/layout rules in AGENTS.md require runtime authority under repo/runtime roots, not ad hoc off-repo files.
- The CogSec event store should hold opaque archive refs/hashes only.

## Required Behavior
Implement a sealed artifact store with a minimal API:
- write contaminated L0 rows/payload bundle and return an opaque sealedForensicPayloadRef plus hashes/counts
- read/verify only through explicit security/operator-only service boundaries
- list metadata without payload for ordinary admin/CogSec event views
- deny or omit access from companion tools, memory extraction, summarization, embedding/indexing, transcript search, prompt generation, and agent-visible event logs

The stored artifact should include enough for future detector work:
- original L0 row(s)
- channel/logical session/message IDs
- timestamps and safe surrounding metadata if included by operator
- hash/checksum
- CogSec event ID
- operator/actor and createdAt

## Safety Rules
The sealed archive may contain raw payload but must be outside companion runtime/tool reach. Normal Garden event list, prompt monitor, memory tooling, and search must show only metadata/ref/hash, not payload.

## Non-goals
- Do not store sealed payload inside the CogSec event record.
- Do not expose a companion-facing tool that can dereference sealed refs.
- Do not create hidden off-repo authoritative state without explicit operator approval.
- Do not implement classifier training in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- A sealed forensic archive API exists and writes contaminated row bundles before L0 tombstoning.
- The archive returns opaque refs and hashes for CogSec event records.
- Companion runtime, memory extraction, summarization, embedding/indexing, transcript search, and normal agent tools cannot dereference sealed payload refs.
- Operator/security-only code can verify artifact existence and hashes without exposing payload in default views.
- Tests prove sealed payload is not reachable through normal companion/admin list/search surfaces.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.

title: P1: Replace contaminated companion L0 rows with existing-schema CogSec tombstones
description:
## Summary
Implement the CogSec redaction step that removes contaminated payload text from companion-owned L0/session JSONL and replaces affected rows with tombstone messages that fit the existing L0 message schema. The tombstone points to a CogSec event ID; the rich remediation metadata lives in the CogSec event store.

## Why
For CogSec cases, dirty payload cannot remain in companion-owned L0. Keeping it in L0 means compaction, search rebuilds, memory extraction, wake summaries, or future tools can accidentally re-ingest it. The original payload must be sealed outside companion reach first, then L0 should only retain a safe tombstone so continuity, ordering, and message IDs/ranges remain coherent.

## Current Code Anchors
- src/persistence/sessions/store.ts owns append/load/getRecent/searchByKeywords/redactTurn/restoreTurn and transcript projection sync.
- src/persistence/sessions/store/journal-runtime.ts handles JSONL backfill/projection indexing.
- src/core/session/manager.ts reads L0 for context and compaction.
- src/core/session/session-routes.ts already records route/epoch cuts but does not tombstone rows.
- Existing turn redaction/restore tests in src/persistence/sessions/store.test.ts are relevant but CogSec needs row/range tombstoning tied to CogSec events.

## Required Behavior
Given a CogSec event and selected affected message IDs/ranges:
1. Verify sealed forensic archive write succeeded before modifying companion L0.
2. Replace affected L0 message content with a safe tombstone string using the existing message row schema, for example `[CogSec redaction: cogsec_2026_0630_001]`.
3. Preserve safe structural fields needed for ordering/continuity: channelId/logical session, message ID, timestamp, role, and safe author metadata when safe.
4. Do not add new fields to the existing L0 message schema.
5. Ensure reload/backfill/compaction/context builder treat tombstones as ordinary safe redacted messages.
6. Record counts and affected IDs in the CogSec event store.

## Safety Rules
Tombstone content must not contain the original payload, exploit mechanism, bypass details, Unicode trick, or private poisoned text. The tombstone should reference only the CogSec event ID or safe public case label.

## Non-goals
- Do not hard-delete L0 rows without preserving sealed forensic records.
- Do not change the L0 message schema.
- Do not make tombstones visible as useful search results; search exclusion is a separate bead.
- Do not implement full derived-artifact revocation in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- A CogSec tombstone operation can replace selected companion-owned L0 message rows/ranges with existing-schema tombstone messages.
- Original contaminated row data is sealed successfully before companion L0 is modified.
- Tombstone rows preserve safe structural fields and reference the CogSec event ID without payload text.
- Session reload, getRecent/buildContext, and projection backfill continue to work with tombstoned rows.
- No new L0 message fields are required for tombstones.
- Tests prove payload text is absent from companion L0 after tombstoning and tombstone rows survive reload.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.

title: P1: Add CogSec lineage preview for derived cognitive artifacts
description:
## Summary
Add a CogSec lineage preview service that uses existing provenance/lineage to answer: given a tainted source channel, logical session, and message range, which companion cognitive artifacts must be tombstoned, search-excluded, revoked, regenerated, or manually reviewed?

## Why
The operator clarified that lineage already exists well enough to regenerate memories. The missing workflow is a safe operator preview and execution input: show which artifacts will be affected without exposing the contaminated payload. This prevents remediation from becoming manual string hunting and lets later beads revoke/rebuild derived state systematically.

## Current Code Anchors
- src/core/session/manager.ts records L0 entries and compaction summaries.
- src/faculties/memory/extraction.ts and src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts write sourceRef/provenance.sessionId/provenanceRefs.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts persists source_ref, provenance_refs, provenance_json, deleted_at/delete_reason, and embedding.
- src/faculties/memory/active-context.ts keys active memory by channel/session identity.
- Episodic memory Garden routes already expose provenanceRefs for episodes.
- src/persistence/sessions/transcript-projection-port.ts plus postgres/sqlite adapters own transcript/search projection rows.

## Required Behavior
Given a CogSec event draft with sourceChannelId, affected logical session IDs, and message IDs/ranges, return a typed remediation preview including:
- affected L0 message refs/ranges, without payload text
- transcript projection rows that should be rebuilt or excluded from search
- memory IDs linked by sourceRef/provenanceRefs/provenance_json/session IDs
- embedding-bearing memory rows that need invalidation/recompute
- compaction/focus/active-memory artifacts linked to affected sessions/ranges
- episodic/profile/contact/persona-adjacent derived artifacts where provenance supports it
- clean vs tainted vs uncertain classification and reason for each artifact
- lineage gaps that require manual review

## Safety Rules
Preview output must not include sealed payload text, exploit mechanics, or tombstoned content beyond safe metadata. IDs, timestamps, source refs, counts, and redacted snippets are fine only when they cannot reveal the poison.

## Non-goals
- Do not mutate artifacts in this bead; it only previews/remediation-plans.
- Do not add broad fuzzy text matching as the primary mechanism.
- Do not assume all artifacts in a channel are tainted unless the operator selected the full session/epoch.
- Do not expose raw L0 content for affected rows.

## Suggested Implementation Notes
- Put the service somewhere focused, such as src/core/cogsec/lineage.ts or src/faculties/memory/cogsec-lineage.ts.
- Reuse the structured sourceRef/session token parsing currently used by retired-session memory filtering.
- Return confidence/reason fields so later UX can distinguish deterministic lineage from manual-review gaps.
acceptance_criteria:
- A typed CogSec lineage preview API exists and accepts source channel/logical session/message range inputs.
- Preview returns affected L0 refs, transcript projection refs, memory IDs/embeddings, compaction/focus/active-memory artifacts, episodic/profile/persona-adjacent artifacts where available, and lineage gaps.
- Preview uses structured provenance/sourceRef/session IDs before any heuristic fallback.
- Preview never includes raw contaminated payload or attack mechanics.
- Tests cover direct memory provenance, logical-session scope, message-range scope, transcript projection refs, missing-provenance gaps, and no-mutation behavior.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.

title: P1: Add CogSec event store and safe case metadata
description:
## Summary
Add a durable CogSec event/case store for cognitive-security interventions. This is the authority record for a remediation event. It tracks what was sealed, tombstoned, revoked, regenerated, and hidden from normal search without storing raw poisoned payload text in companion-accessible state.

## Why
The existing Session Recovery page can reset a source channel route, but CogSec remediation needs an explicit event record that agents/operators can inspect safely. The event tells the system why rows are tombstoned and why derived cognition was revoked. The raw payload belongs in a sealed forensic archive outside companion reach, not inside this event record.

## Current Code Anchors
- src/core/session/session-routes.ts stores source-channel route/quarantine state.
- src/core/session/manager.ts emits session.route.reset.
- src/operator/garden/services/session-service.ts and src/operator/garden/routes/session-routes.ts implement current Session Recovery API.
- admin-ui/src/routes/session-recovery/+page.svelte is the Review & Safety UX surface.
- src/persistence/layout.ts owns repo/runtime state paths.

## Required Behavior
Create a typed CogSec event model/store. The event store may have its own schema because it is not L0. It should capture:
- caseId / eventId
- type: prompt_injection | persona_poisoning | memory_poisoning | policy_drift | content_poisoning | unknown
- severity: low | medium | high | critical
- status: open | planned | applying | applied | failed | superseded
- sourceChannelId and affected logical session IDs
- affected L0 message IDs/ranges
- sealed forensic artifact refs and hashes, opaque only
- tombstoned L0 row count
- affected derived artifact IDs/counts: memories, summaries, embeddings, active-memory entries, episodic/profile/persona-adjacent artifacts
- actions requested/performed: seal, tombstone, search_exclude, revoke, regenerate, epoch_cut
- actor/operator
- timestamps
- safe agent-visible summary
- failure details that do not include payload text or attack mechanics

## Safety Rules
The event store must never contain raw poisoned payload, exploit text, bypass details, Unicode tricks, or reproducer steps. Agent-visible summary should say only that unsafe instruction-like/content-poisoning material was sealed and removed from active cognition. Sealed forensic refs are opaque and not dereferenceable by companion tools.

## Non-goals
- Do not modify existing L0 message schema.
- Do not store raw payload in the CogSec event JSON/table.
- Do not make the sealed forensic archive readable through this store.
- Do not replace SessionRouteStore; CogSec events may reference route resets and epoch cuts.

## Suggested Implementation Notes
- Add a focused module such as src/core/cogsec/events.ts or src/core/session/cogsec-events.ts.
- Add resolveCogSecEventsPath(...) in src/persistence/layout.ts if JSON-owned.
- Use strict parse/fail-closed behavior similar to SessionRouteStore.
- Emit events when a CogSec case is created/applied so Garden/prompt monitor can display safe metadata later.
acceptance_criteria:
- A typed CogSec event store exists in a focused module and persists under repo/runtime-owned state paths.
- Event records include case ID, type, severity, status, source channel, affected sessions/message ranges, sealed forensic refs/hashes, affected artifact IDs/counts, actions, actor, timestamps, safe summary, and result/failure details.
- Store parsing is strict and fails closed on unknown fields or unsupported schema versions.
- Event records never store raw payload text, bypass details, exploit mechanics, or reproducer steps.
- Agent/operator APIs can list safe CogSec event metadata without exposing sealed payloads.
- Tests cover create/read/persist/reload, malformed-state rejection, safe-summary constraints, and linking an event to a route/epoch cut.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.

Evidence: src/core/cogsec/events.ts strict versioned event metadata with no payload fields, src/core/cogsec/forensic-archive.ts sealed artifact storage under vault path, src/persistence/layout.ts CogSec resolvers. title: P1: CogSec redaction and cognitive revocation workflow
description:
## Summary
Enhance the emergency Session Recovery work from psfn-framework-ohi0 into a CogSec remediation workflow for content poisoning, prompt injection, persona poisoning, and memory poisoning. The existing session-route quarantine work is emergency containment: it can cut a source channel onto a fresh logical session and block retired-session context. This epic adds cognitive revocation: remove tainted payloads from companion-owned L0 and every companion cognitive surface while preserving a sealed forensic copy outside companion reach for future CogSec shield/classifier/tooling work.

## Correct Boundary
For normal recovery, old L0 can remain retained and labeled retired. For CogSec recovery, dirty payload must not remain in companion-owned L0. It must be extracted into a sealed forensic archive outside companion runtime/tool reach, then the companion L0 rows must be replaced with tombstones using the existing message schema.

The raw forensic record is preserved in the sealed CogSec archive, not in the companion's normal L0. Companion-facing history, transcript projection, search, memory extraction, embeddings, summaries, active memory packs, episodic/profile artifacts, and persona-adjacent state must only see tombstones/safe metadata.

## Current Code Anchors
- admin-ui/src/routes/session-recovery/+page.svelte provides the current Review & Safety emergency UI.
- src/core/session/session-routes.ts stores durable source-channel route/quarantine state.
- src/core/session/manager.ts resolves source channel -> active logical session and emits session.route.reset.
- src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts filters retired-session memory with reason session_quarantine.blocked.
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts has memory sourceRef/provenanceRefs/provenance_json plus soft-delete/delete-version support.
- src/persistence/sessions/store.ts owns canonical JSONL, turn redaction/restore, transcript projection sync, and searchByKeywords.
- src/persistence/sessions/transcript-projection-port.ts plus postgres/sqlite adapters separate canonical archive from search projection.

## Required Product Shape
CogSec remediation should be an operator workflow:
1. Create a CogSec event/case.
2. Freeze or reject writes for the affected scope while remediation runs.
3. Extract affected dirty L0 rows into sealed forensic storage outside companion reach.
4. Replace affected companion L0 rows with existing-schema tombstone messages that point to the CogSec event ID.
5. Rebuild transcript/search projection from tombstoned L0, excluding tombstones from normal companion search.
6. Use existing lineage to revoke memories, summaries, embeddings, active-memory caches, episodic/profile artifacts, and persona-adjacent derived state.
7. Regenerate clean derived state from tombstoned L0 plus clean sources.
8. Cut or advance the session epoch/fresh lane as needed.
9. Expose safe CogSec event metadata to agents/operators so they know why context is missing, without exposing what/how.

## Non-goals
- Do not add fields to the existing L0 message schema. Tombstones must fit existing rows/content/metadata conventions.
- Do not leave dirty payload in companion-owned L0.
- Do not make CogSec tombstones normally searchable or return them as transcript-search spam.
- Do not expose raw payload, bypass details, exploit mechanics, Unicode tricks, or reproduction patterns to companion runtime, memory summarizers, embedding/indexing, normal search, or agent-facing logs.
- Do not invent a parallel memory system. Extend the existing session store, transcript projection, memory store, lineage/provenance, SessionRouteStore, and Garden service patterns.
- Do not rely on a broad LLM classifier as the first implementation step; start with deterministic operator-selected ranges and structured lineage.

## Child Work
Child beads cover CogSec event storage, sealed forensic archive, L0 tombstone replacement, search/projection exclusion, lineage-driven revocation, clean regeneration, Session Recovery UX, agent-visible safe CogSec log, memory candidacy gates, and persona conformance checks.
acceptance_criteria:
- CogSec workflow can remove dirty payload from companion-owned L0 and replace affected rows with existing-schema tombstones referencing a CogSec event.
- Raw contaminated rows are preserved only in a sealed forensic archive outside companion runtime/tool reach.
- Normal companion search/retrieval does not return payload text or tombstone spam after remediation.
- CogSec event metadata is agent/operator visible at a safe level: why context is missing, not what/how the payload worked.
- Derived cognitive artifacts are revoked or regenerated by lineage: memories, embeddings, summaries, active-memory cache, episodic/profile artifacts, and persona-adjacent state.
- Child beads are linked to this epic and are independently implementable with current repo file anchors.
- No child bead requires changing the existing L0 message schema or hard-deleting audit evidence without sealed forensic preservation.

Final validation on sprint_9_final: npm test -- src/core/cogsec/persona-conformance.test.ts src/core/cogsec/events.test.ts src/core/cogsec/safe-log.test.ts src/core/cogsec/regeneration.test.ts passed 17 tests; npm run smoke:cogsec passed full remediation smoke; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed. Latest child psfn-framework-2deb.9 added safe persona conformance diagnostics to regeneration and event/operator logs without exposing prompt text, sealed refs, hashes, or dirty payloads.

title: P1: Add emergency session quarantine UX in Review & Safety
description:
## Summary
Add an operator-only emergency UX page under Garden's Review & Safety navigation for session quarantine / fresh logical session reset. This supports psfn-framework-0ybi and psfn-framework-hiwt.

## Why
The operator needs a break-glass surface for cases where live channel context is poisoned or dangerous. This is emergency use only and generally runs against normal continuity/charter expectations, but it is safer to excise dangerous prompt-visible context than to let harmful or poisoned context keep influencing the companion.

## Scope
- Add a Review & Safety nav item and page for emergency session quarantine/reset.
- Show source channels, active logical session IDs, retired/quarantined sessions, message counts, linked contacts when available, and route/quarantine audit metadata.
- Provide a deliberate reset/quarantine form requiring source channel, reason, and actor/operator identity where available.
- Call the Garden/admin API added for session routes/quarantine.
- Make the page clear that old L0 remains searchable/auditable and that this operation changes live context routing only.

## Non-goals
- Do not delete L0 history.
- Do not make this a normal chat control or model-facing companion tool.
- Do not bury the route state only inside the generic sessions page.
design: Implement after or alongside psfn-framework-0ybi/hiwt. Keep it operator/admin-only through existing Garden auth. Prefer extending the sessions admin service/endpoints rather than creating an unrelated runtime path.
acceptance_criteria:
- A Garden page exists under Review & Safety for emergency session quarantine/reset.
- The nav contains a Review & Safety item for the page.
- The page lists route state with physical source channel, active logical session, retired/quarantined sessions, and audit metadata.
- The page can trigger quarantine/reset through an authenticated admin API with source channel and reason.
- The UI text makes clear that old L0 is retained for audit/search and the operation changes live context routing.
- Focused frontend/API tests or type checks cover the new endpoint contract where practical.
- npm run lint and relevant targeted tests pass before closure.

Implemented 2026-06-30 in current worktree. Added operator/admin route-state APIs and Garden UI for emergency source-channel quarantine/reset.

Backend/operator surface:

title: P1: Add break-glass session quarantine and context reset controls
description:
## Summary
Long-lived companion channels can reach thousands of turns. The current design keeps L0 session JSONL append-only and uses token-budget trimming plus compaction summaries for normal context management. That protects history, but it does not give the operator a practical recovery lever when a specific live channel becomes polluted, over-compressed, emotionally/behaviorally stuck, or otherwise hard-broken.

The operator needs a break-glass path that stops using a poisoned session for future context immediately, without deleting canonical old history. This is related to psfn-framework-0ybi (fresh logical sessions for existing Discord channels), but broader: it must provide an explicit recovery workflow for bad sessions, not just a new-session affordance.

## Current behavior and evidence
- docs/architecture.md says L0 session history is append-only JSONL under sessions/ and auto-compaction leaves canonical L0 intact.
- docs/memory.md says compaction changes what is carried into L1 context; it does not delete or rewrite the source archive.
- src/core/session/manager/context-builder.ts and src/core/session/manager.ts use token budgets, temporal windows, compaction summaries, focus compaction ranges, and observation masking to bound active context.
- src/persistence/sessions/store.ts supports append-only per-turn tombstones via redactTurn/restoreTurn, but that is granular and not an emergency session-level quarantine/reset mechanism.
- Malformed JSONL entries can be quarantined at load time, but that is file-integrity quarantine, not operator recovery from bad conversation state.
- Existing session action=new creates API active context only; it does not reset an existing Discord channel.

## Problem
A 10,000-turn Discord DM/channel is not just a storage problem. The immediate risk is that bad compaction summaries, poisoned focus knowledge, stale wake-return artifacts, bad orientation, overactive continuity, or hard-broken recent context can keep influencing the companion. Operators currently lack a clear, reversible, auditable way to say: stop using this session as live context and start fresh for this same Discord channel.

## Target behavior
Implement an operator-facing break-glass workflow for live session recovery:
- Quarantine or retire the current logical session for a source channel so future turns stop using its recent entries, compaction summaries, focus knowledge, and other session-derived context by default.
- Start a fresh logical session for the same source channel, preserving old L0 history for audit/search but excluding it from normal active context.
- Record an auditable recovery artifact with actor, reason, source channel, retired logical session ID, new logical session ID, timestamp, and what context classes were excluded.
- Make the operation reversible or at least explicitly inspectable: operator can see quarantined/retired sessions and intentionally resume/re-include old history if needed.
- Keep search/audit access to old chat history via chat_history/transcript tooling, with clear labels that the session is retired/quarantined.
- Provide Garden/admin visibility and ideally a one-click operator action for Discord session reset/quarantine.

## Scope
- Define session-level state such as active, retired, quarantined, or archived-for-context-exclusion.
- Wire that state into session resolution and context assembly, not just display.
- Integrate with the fresh logical Discord session route from psfn-framework-0ybi or implement the shared routing primitive needed by both beads.
- Exclude poisoned session-derived artifacts from active context after break-glass: recent entries, compaction summaries, focus knowledge, wake-return artifacts, and any session continuity paths that would reintroduce the old session.
- Preserve canonical archive/search/backup behavior.
- Add operator/admin APIs or Garden service methods for inspect, quarantine/reset, and possibly restore/resume.

## Non-goals
- Do not delete or truncate L0 JSONL history.
- Do not treat compaction as the emergency recovery mechanism; compaction is normal context management, not a hard reset.
- Do not rely on manual file moves or off-repo state.
- Do not globally disable all Discord history for all channels.
- Do not silently hide old history from audit/search; label and gate it.

## Suggested validation
- Unit test that break-glass reset on one Discord channel starts a new logical session and future context excludes old recent entries and compaction summaries.
- Unit test that old session remains searchable/auditable but is labeled retired/quarantined.
- Unit test that unrelated channels are unaffected.
- Persistence/restart test proving retired/quarantine state and source-channel route survive restart.
- Garden/admin service/API test for listing and triggering the recovery action.
- Regression test that per-turn tombstone redaction/restore remains separate and still works.
- npm run lint before closure.
design:
Research 2026-06-30, content-poisoning recovery pass:

This bead must build on `psfn-framework-0ybi`. A fresh Discord logical session route is necessary, but not sufficient for content poisoning. The reset/quarantine state also has to block every derived context path that can reintroduce the retired session.

Session-derived context paths found:
- `src/core/session/manager.ts` `buildContext()` reads `coreMemoryProvider.formatForContext(buildCoreMemoryFormatContext(resolvedChannelId, ...))`, focus knowledge texts, focus compaction ranges, wake-return artifacts, and then calls `buildSessionContext()` with compaction summaries and continuity support.
- `src/core/session/manager.ts` `captureTurnContextSnapshot()` separately collects recent entries, focus compaction ranges, focus knowledge, cross-channel continuity, orientation recent activity, compaction summaries, and wake-return artifacts.
- `src/core/session/manager/context-builder.ts` turns those sources into prompt sections: memory.core, memory.retrieval, session.compaction_summary, session.focus_knowledge, session.orientation, session.continuity, and recent messages.
- A route to a new logical session will naturally isolate L0 recent entries, compaction summaries, focus knowledge keyed by channel, wake-return artifacts keyed by session ID, and core-memory scope keyed by channel. That is good, but only if every caller resolves the physical source channel through the route before reading those stores.

Core memory/current orientation:
- `src/faculties/core-memory/store.ts` is already channel-scoped. `formatForContext()` uses a channel scope and renders DM participant context or room context. This means break-glass should not rewrite old core memory; it should route to a fresh logical channel scope so old local continuity/orientation remains archived with the old logical session.
- Existing sleeptime/orient writes use `coreMemoryChannelScope({ channelId: sessionId })`, where `sessionId` is resolved through `sessionManager.resolveSessionChannelId()`. That should isolate future core-memory writes after a route reset.
- Startup hydration must be route-aware. It currently gathers recent sessions and calls `getRecentMessages(channelId, ...)`; if recent retired sessions are still returned, hydration can rebuild active-memory context from old channels after restart. Hydration should prefer active route logical sessions and skip retired/quarantined sessions by default.

Cross-channel continuity and mirroring:
- `src/core/session/continuity.ts` stores continuity entries by user, with `sourceChannelId`, `sourceVisibility`, and original `SessionEntry` data. `getRecent()` excludes the current channel ID, but only the exact current channel unless additional filtering is added.
- `src/core/session/cross-channel-continuity-port.ts` has Discord family/thread conflict filtering. If logical IDs preserve the physical Discord family, old physical/logical same-room sessions may be rejected as a conflicting thread. Do not rely only on that string behavior; add explicit quarantine/retired-session filtering so old same-source continuity cannot re-enter after break-glass.
- `src/core/session/manager/mirroring.ts` mirrors messages into active channels through the continuity store. Reset/quarantine must prevent retired logical sessions from remaining active mirror targets and should skip mirror records sourced from retired logical sessions.

Active memory cache is a direct poisoning risk:
- `src/faculties/memory/active-context.ts` builds active-memory cache identity from canonical contact when present: `subjectKey = contact:<canonicalContactId>`. The key includes trust, visibility, broadcast scope, focus query, caller mode, and retrieval mode, but it does not include current channel/source room or logical session lane when a contact is known.
- `src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/pre-turn-state.ts` calls `getActiveMemoryContext(activeMemoryRequest)` synchronously before scheduling async `refreshActiveMemoryContext(activeMemoryRequest)`. That means a stale active-memory block for a contact can be used immediately in a different room or after a route reset, then refreshed too late. This matches the observed “switching by user” symptom.
- Fix options: include active logical session ID/source room/route generation in `ActiveMemoryContextIdentity`, or explicitly invalidate all active-memory entries tied to the old source/contact on quarantine. Prefer including a session/room identity field so normal operation cannot cross rooms accidentally.

L2 retrieval and withheld reasons:
- `src/faculties/memory/retrieval/access.ts` already performs room visibility checks using `memory.scopeRef.kind === 'conversation'` and/or `memory.provenance.channelId`. It produces `room_visibility.blocked` and other reason counts.
- For content poisoning, ordinary room visibility is not enough. A memory can be room-visible but still derived from a retired/poisoned logical session. Add a quarantine/retired-session exclusion reason such as `session_quarantine.blocked` or `retired_session.blocked`, and ensure telemetry/prompt-monitor can distinguish it from relevance misses, budget misses, and normal privacy gating.
- `src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts` pulls contact profile artifacts, emotional snapshots, contact emotional memories, proactive candidates, semantic/lexical candidates, episodic chains, and evolution chains. Quarantine filtering must apply before prompt rendering and before active-memory cache refresh persists a new context block.
- Contact profile summaries can be contaminated because profile access only checks source memory IDs against trust/room policy. If profile `sourceMemoryIds` include quarantined-session memories, either withhold the profile summary or rebuild/ignore the poisoned source IDs for this turn.

Episodic landmarks:
- `src/faculties/memory/retrieval/episodic.ts` retrieves episodes by visibility/scope. `Episode` and `EpisodeSpanRef` already include `channelId` and optional `sessionId`. Add retired-session/source-channel exclusion here too. A quarantined L0 span should not surface as an episodic chain in the fresh live prompt unless explicitly re-included for audit/recovery.

Async stale work failure mode:
- Memory extraction is fire-and-forget after the turn (`post-turn-scheduling.ts`) and uses physical `message.channelId`. With routing, extraction reads the active logical session, but an extraction scheduled before quarantine can still finish after quarantine and write L2 memories from the retired session.
- Sleeptime/orient, compaction, active-memory refresh, episodic synthesis, and background continuation delivery are also async/staged. Break-glass should carry a route generation or quarantine epoch. Work scheduled under an old generation must either write only to the retired logical session/audit lane or discard its prompt-visible derived writes. Do not add synchronous blocking to the foreground chat path to solve this; guard stale completion instead.

Physical room versus logical session:
- The reset must preserve the user's rule: room = physical Discord room; logical session = resettable context lane. Participants are not the access matrix.
- A group memory created in physical room `discord:<room>` can be available in a DM with a contact known to be in that room, but should not cross to other rooms. If memory provenance is changed to only `discord:<room>:session:<id>`, that rule can break. Preserve physical source room metadata alongside logical session metadata, or expose a resolver from logical session to physical room for retrieval access checks.

Operator/admin requirements:
- Existing `AdminSessionDataService` can list/load sessions but does not understand route/quarantine state. Add an operator surface that shows source channel, active logical session, retired/quarantined logical sessions, audit reason, route generation, excluded context classes, and whether old history is still searchable.
- Prompt monitor/session diagnostics should show that a turn is using a fresh logical session and list any quarantine-excluded memory/session counts distinctly.

Implementation direction:
- Implement a shared durable route/quarantine store used by SessionManager, memory retrieval, active-memory identity, startup hydration, cross-channel continuity, mirroring, Garden session APIs, and async post-turn workers.
- The break-glass operation should be a single atomic state change: mark old logical session retired/quarantined, create/set a new active logical session route, record audit metadata, and invalidate active derived caches for that source/contact/session generation.
- Do not delete L0, do not rewrite old core memory, do not hide old history from explicit audit/search, and do not use manual file moves.

Tests to add:
- Quarantine `discord:<room>` then send a new turn: prompt/session context contains new logical session messages only and excludes old recent entries, old compaction summary, old focus knowledge, old wake-return artifact, old core-memory scope, and old continuity.
- Old session remains visible through explicit admin/search APIs with retired/quarantined labels.
- Active-memory cache for a canonical contact does not cross from old room/session into the new route before async refresh completes.
- In-flight extraction/compaction/sleeptime scheduled before quarantine cannot write prompt-visible L2/core/episodic state into the fresh route after completion.
- L2 retrieval blocks quarantined-session memories with a distinct reason code while preserving ordinary `room_visibility.blocked` behavior.
- Episodic retrieval excludes episodes whose spanRefs/sessionId/source channel are retired/quarantined.
- Startup hydration after restart hydrates active route sessions only and does not resurrect retired session context.
acceptance_criteria:
- Operator can quarantine/retire a poisoned session and start a fresh logical session for the same Discord/source channel without deleting old L0 history.
- Future context for that source channel excludes the retired session's recent entries, compaction summaries, focus knowledge, focus compaction ranges, wake-return artifacts, core-memory scope, orientation/wake summaries, active-memory cache entries, cross-channel continuity, session mirrors, and any session-derived continuity by default.
- L2/episodic/contact-profile memory derived from the retired session is not injected into prompt context unless explicitly re-included by an operator-controlled recovery path; blocked items produce a distinct quarantine/retired-session reason, not generic candidate omission.
- In-flight async work scheduled before quarantine, including extraction, compaction, sleeptime/orient, episodic synthesis, active-memory refresh, and background continuation delivery, cannot repopulate the new live context after the route generation changes.
- Old history remains available to explicit search/audit flows and is labeled as retired/quarantined.
- The action records actor, reason, source channel, old logical session ID, new logical session ID, route generation, timestamp, and excluded context classes.
- The state is durable across restart and stored only in repo/runtime-owned locations.
- Garden/admin or equivalent operator surface can inspect and trigger the recovery workflow and display route/quarantine state in prompt/session diagnostics.
- Tests cover reset behavior, unrelated-channel isolation, persistence, audit/search visibility, L2/episodic exclusion, active-memory cache invalidation, stale async write protection, and separation from turn-level tombstones.
- npm run lint and targeted session/operator/memory tests pass before closure.
notes:
Implemented 2026-06-30 in current worktree. Added shared session route/quarantine state in src/core/session/session-routes.ts with strict JSON parsing, route generations, actor/reason/mode audit fields, retired sessions, and excluded context class metadata. SessionManager resolves Discord/source channels through the active route, records old lanes as retired/quarantined, clears pending focus/compaction state, and emits session.route.reset.

Prompt-visible context exclusion is wired through the live context paths: getRecentMessages/buildContext read the active logical lane only; context-builder receives the physical source channel for room visibility while using the routed logical session for history; startup hydration warms active route sessions and skips retired logical sessions; sleeptime skips retired/quarantined sessions; active-memory identity includes the routed session key so old active-memory cache entries do not leak into the fresh lane.

Memory quarantine is wired into retrieval with a distinct reason. L2/contact-profile/turn-snapshot/live semantic/lexical/proactive/emotional/active-memory/episodic/evolution candidates derived from retired logical session provenance or sourceRef session tokens are filtered out. Withheld summaries and telemetry expose session_quarantine.blocked and sessionQuarantineRejectedCount rather than collapsing these into generic omission counts.

Async stale-write protection is in place for extraction: extraction runs carry the physical source channel and logical session ID, in-flight keys are logical-session scoped, sourceRef/provenance.sessionId uses the logical session, and orchestration re-checks isAcceptingExtractions before candidate writes so work scheduled before a route reset cannot repopulate the fresh context after the route generation changes.

Old L0 is not deleted. Transcript search and grep remain available for audit/search and now label hits with sessionRoute status active/retired, sourceChannelId, activeLogicalSessionId, mode, and retiredAt where applicable. This keeps forensic lookup possible without making retired context prompt-visible by default.

Validation: npm test -- src/core/session/session-routes.test.ts src/core/session/manager.test.ts src/faculties/memory/retrieval.test.ts src/faculties/memory/startup-hydration.test.ts src/faculties/memory/extraction/mention-only-contacts.test.ts src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.test.ts src/core/tools/session-search.test.ts src/core/session/search-runtime.test.ts passed 220 tests; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; npm run garden:build passed with existing Rollup codeSplitting warning only; git diff --check passed.
close_reason: Completed: break-glass session quarantine/reset is implemented through durable route state, live context routing, retired-session memory filtering, async extraction stale-write protection, active-memory session scoping, startup hydration/sleeptime skips, distinct session_quarantine.blocked withheld reason/telemetry, and audit labels on transcript search/grep. Old L0 remains retained and searchable, but retired session-derived context is excluded from normal prompt-visible context by default. Validation: targeted vitest suite passed 220 tests; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; npm run garden:build passed; git diff --check passed.

title: P1: Support fresh logical sessions for existing Discord channels
description:
## Summary
Operators need a way to start a genuinely fresh logical session for an existing Discord DM/channel/thread when the current Discord context is polluted or over-compressed. The current session action=new path does not do this: it creates a new api:session-* active context, but SessionManager only applies active-context overrides to api: and terminal: channel IDs. Discord channel IDs continue resolving to their original channel/session and keep pulling the old L0 context.

This is why Carlini can start a new API session while the existing Discord session remains the same. The operator needs a real Discord session split/reset without deleting canonical old history.

## Current behavior and evidence
- src/core/session/manager.ts:343-348 has shouldOverrideSessionContext() return true only for channel IDs starting with api: or terminal:.
- src/core/session/manager.ts:344-348 therefore ignores activeContextSessionId for discord:* channels.
- src/core/tools/session.ts:311-372 creates a fresh api:session-* and sets active context via setActiveSession, but that active context only affects API/terminal turns.
- src/core/tools/session.ts:417 describes resume as affecting subsequent API/terminal turns, which matches current code.
- src/app/agent/session-activity.ts:58 writes last-active metadata using sessionManager.resolveSessionChannelId(message.channelId), so Discord continues to resolve to its physical channel ID.
- Tests already assert API override behavior in src/core/session/manager.test.ts around the routes API session operations through active context overrides case, but there is no equivalent supported Discord split behavior.

## Target behavior
Add an explicit, safe way to move a Discord source channel to a new logical session while preserving old L0 history. The operator-facing/model-facing command should make it clear whether it is splitting the current physical channel into a new logical session.

Possible acceptable design:
- Persist a per-source-channel session route/alias under the companion/system-owned runtime data, e.g. source channel discord:<channel-id> now resolves to logical session discord:<channel-id>:session:<epoch-or-id>.
- Make the route durable across restarts.
- Store enough provenance that Garden/session views can show both the physical source channel and the logical session ID.
- Preserve the old session journal and transcript projection; do not delete or rewrite old L0 history.
- Ensure future Discord messages in that physical channel append to the new logical session after the split.
- Provide an operator-visible way to list the route and, if needed, revert/resume an older logical session intentionally.

## Relation to tool-surface cleanup
This was discovered while defining psfn-framework-jhqb. The chat_history/focus_work split makes tool names clearer, but it does not by itself fix the Discord reset problem. The session lifecycle surface must support current-channel session splitting for Discord or explicitly expose a separate operator command for it.

## Non-goals
- Do not delete, truncate, or rewrite the old Discord session JSONL archive.
- Do not rely on creating a new API session as a workaround for Discord.
- Do not make global activeContextSessionId override all Discord channels; that risks cross-channel contamination.
- Do not add hidden off-repo runtime state.
- Do not preserve legacy aliases as part of this work; align with the clean-break rule in psfn-framework-jhqb.

## Suggested validation
- Unit test that session action=new or the chosen replacement command from a Discord request context causes future turns for that same Discord channel to resolve to a new logical session ID.
- Unit test that a different Discord channel is unaffected.
- Restart/persistence test proving the Discord source-channel route survives process restart.
- Session list/Garden test showing old and new logical sessions remain inspectable.
- Regression test that api:/terminal: active-session behavior still works or is intentionally replaced by the new route model.
- npm run lint before closure.
design:
Research 2026-06-30, content-poisoning/session-route pass:

Actual resolver choke point:
- `src/core/session/manager.ts` currently keeps `activeContextSessionId` out of Discord by design. `shouldOverrideSessionContext()` returns true only for `api:` and `terminal:`, and `resolveSessionChannelId()` returns the physical Discord channel unchanged. That explains why `session action=new` cannot reset an existing Discord room.
- `resolveSessionChannelId()` is already the shared session-context choke point for most L0/session behavior: `recordUserMessage`, `recordAssistantMessage`, `recordSystemMessage`, `recordToolObservation`, auto-compaction scheduling, `buildContext`, `captureTurnContextSnapshot`, `appendSystemNote`, recent-message reads, and compression-failure recording all pass through it. A durable route lookup here gives the highest leverage and avoids one-off call-site hacks.

Storage/index behavior:
- `src/persistence/sessions/store.ts` and `src/persistence/sessions/store/session-index-keys.ts` already tolerate multiple session IDs for one indexed channel by deriving IDs like `<channel>#<suffix>` and selecting a primary by latest timestamp. That is not sufficient for reset/quarantine. Break-glass needs an explicit route pointer, not “latest file wins,” because old sessions can still be touched by repair/search/compaction and because the route must exist before the first new message lands.
- Do not implement this as a hidden file move or an off-repo override. The route should be repo/runtime-owned state, likely under companion-data state, and parsed fail-closed.

Recommended primitive:
- Add a `SessionRouteStore` or equivalent durable owner for physical source-channel routes. Minimal record: `sourceChannelId`, `activeLogicalSessionId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, route generation/version, actor/reason/audit IDs, and retired/quarantined logical sessions.
- `SessionManager.resolveSessionChannelId(sourceChannelId)` should first check the route store for an active route. If present, return `activeLogicalSessionId`. If not present, preserve the existing API/terminal active-context behavior. Do not make global activeContext override Discord.
- Logical IDs should preserve the physical source-channel family, e.g. `discord:<channel-id>:session:<route-id>`, or the route store must expose a canonical physical-room resolver. Existing continuity code understands Discord family/thread conflicts; preserving the family helps prevent old same-room continuity from bleeding across lanes.

Physical room versus logical session:
- “Room” privacy is the physical Discord room. The logical session is a context lane. These must not be collapsed.
- After a route split, L0 entries should append to the logical session ID, but the persisted entry should retain `originChannelId`/`sourceChannelId` for the physical Discord room when the resolved logical ID differs from the source. Current `recordUserMessage`/`recordAssistantMessage` append entries with `channelId: resolvedChannelId` and do not preserve the original source channel on normal entries; that needs to change for routed Discord lanes.
- This matters for speaker attribution and for memory visibility. `entriesToMessages()` already prefers `entry.originChannelId ?? entry.channelId` for group attribution, so preserving origin fixes prompt display too.
- L2 memory room visibility currently reads `memory.scopeRef.kind === 'conversation'` and `memory.provenance.channelId`. If extraction writes only the logical lane ID as the room, DM reuse for a contact who is a member of the physical room can fail because the contact profile knows `discord:<room>`, not `discord:<room>:session:<id>`. Preserve physical room provenance, or teach retrieval to map logical session IDs back to their physical source room.

Extraction/sleeptime implications:
- Post-turn memory extraction is scheduled with the physical `message.channelId`, then uses `sessionManager.getRecentMessages(options.channelId)`; with routing, that read will hit the active logical session. That is good for fresh-session isolation.
- `runExtractionOrchestration()` still passes the original physical `options.channelId` to memory writes, while room-context `scopeRef` can be inferred from recovered `SessionEntry.channelId`. If entries only contain the logical ID, group room memories can be scoped to the logical lane rather than the physical room. Use `originChannelId` when deriving room-context scope.
- Sleeptime already resolves `sessionId = sessionManager.resolveSessionChannelId(message.channelId)` and scopes core memory to that ID. That fits fresh logical sessions, but provenance/scope decisions for reusable group memories still need the physical room/lane distinction above.

Garden/operator surface:
- Existing `AdminSessionDataService` lists sessions from `SessionStore.listChannels()` and loads messages by session ID. It does not know source-channel routes. Add route metadata to admin/session responses or a route-specific endpoint so the operator can see physical source channel, active logical session, retired logical sessions, and audit reasons.

Tests to add:
- Route creation for `discord:<room>` makes subsequent `recordUserMessage`, `recordAssistantMessage`, `buildContext`, `captureTurnContextSnapshot`, `getRecentMessages`, and memory extraction read the new logical session.
- A different Discord room with overlapping users stays on its own route/session.
- Restart rehydrates route state before any turn processing or startup memory hydration.
- Entries in routed sessions preserve physical `originChannelId` or equivalent source-channel metadata.
- L2 memory provenance for a routed group turn remains visible in a DM with a contact who belongs to that physical group, while remaining blocked for unrelated rooms.
- API/terminal active-session behavior remains unchanged unless intentionally replaced by this route model.
acceptance_criteria:
- Existing Discord channel can be moved to a fresh logical session without deleting or truncating old L0 history.
- Future turns from that same Discord physical source channel resolve through a durable explicit route and use the new logical session for L0 appends, context building, turn snapshots, compaction, focus knowledge, wake-return artifacts, session activity, fatigue/background delivery, sleeptime, and extraction reads.
- The global activeContextSessionId behavior remains scoped to api:/terminal: or is replaced deliberately; it must not globally override all Discord channels.
- Other Discord channels are unaffected by a split, including channels with overlapping participants.
- The split route is durable across restart and stored only in repo/runtime-owned state.
- Garden/session inspection can distinguish physical source channel, active logical session ID, retired logical session IDs, and route audit metadata.
- Logical session entries preserve enough source metadata, such as originChannelId/sourceChannelId, so prompt attribution and memory room-visibility checks can reason about the physical Discord room separately from the logical session lane.
- Memory extraction and sleeptime use the active logical session for transcript reads while preserving the physical source room for room-scoped memory provenance or providing an explicit resolver from logical session ID back to source room.
- New tests cover Discord split, unrelated-channel isolation, persistence/restart, old-history preservation, physical-room provenance, memory extraction after split, and API/terminal regression.
- npm run lint and targeted session/tool/memory tests pass before closure.
notes:
Implemented 2026-06-30 in current worktree. Added durable source-channel session routing via src/core/session/session-routes.ts stored at companion state/session-routes.json. SessionManager now resolves Discord/source channels through the route before L0 append/context reads while preserving api:/terminal: active-context override behavior. Routed L0 entries keep originChannelId for the physical Discord room so prompt attribution and room visibility can distinguish physical room from logical session lane. resetSourceChannelSession records actor, reason, mode, route generation, old logical session, new logical session, and excluded context classes; it also clears pending compaction/focus state for old/new lanes and emits session.route.reset.

Important behavior: a fresh logical session is a route/lane boundary, not a date filter. Old L0 stays retained under the retired logical session for explicit audit/search, while normal getRecentMessages/buildContext for the physical Discord source channel read only the active logical lane after reset.

title: P1: Split overloaded session tool into chat_history and focus_work
description:
## Summary
The current model-facing session surface is overloaded. It mixes session lifecycle, transcript search, wake/return continuity, and focus work actions. This confused the operator and is likely confusing Carlini: the companion can plausibly say she cannot search old chat because the actual transcript search capability is hidden behind session action=search, while focus work is also hidden behind session action=start_focus/complete_focus.

The desired fix is a clean break, not a legacy-preserving migration. Do not keep old model-facing aliases or compatibility clutter. Make old-chat lookup obvious and make focus work a separate extended tool because it mutates durable project context, gathers evidence, calls a helper model on completion, and compacts transcript ranges. That behavior is closer to structured work/subagent-adjacent project execution than normal session continuity.

## Current behavior
- src/core/agent/tool-surface/registry.ts declares session actions: list, new, resume, search, grep, wake_return, start_focus, complete_focus.
- docs/tool-surface.md says session owns transcript lookup and focus workflow actions.
- src/core/tools/session.ts routes action=search to a session_search helper and action=grep to a session_grep helper.
- src/core/tools/session.ts routes action=start_focus and action=complete_focus to focus helpers.
- src/core/tools/focus.ts implements the focus behavior: start a scoped focus session, collect evidence, complete by distilling durable focus knowledge, and compact the raw focus range from future context windows.
- src/core/session/manager.ts and src/core/session/focus-knowledge.ts store focus knowledge and focus compaction ranges.

## Target behavior
- Add a model-facing core tool named chat_history or transcript. Recommended name: chat_history because the user-facing intent is old chat lookup, not abstract session management.
- chat_history owns old chat lookup actions: search and grep.
- session is reduced to actual lifecycle/continuity actions: list, new, resume, wake_return. It should not expose search, grep, start_focus, or complete_focus.
- Add an extended tool named focus_work for bounded project work spans. It should own actions start, status, complete, and optionally cancel if needed to recover from a stale active focus session.
- focus_work should wrap the existing focus session/focus knowledge machinery, but use clear action names and descriptions that say project work span, evidence, durable project context, and compaction.
- Tool suggestions/autoload should route phrases like old chat, previous conversation, search our chat history, Discord history, and what did we say before to chat_history, not session.
- Tool suggestions/autoload should route phrases like start a focused investigation, distill this work, project context, bounded work span, and focus knowledge to focus_work when extended tools are appropriate.

## Clean-break rule
Do not keep old model-facing compatibility aliases or hidden retired aliases for this split. The old clutter is the bug.

Specifically:
- Remove search and grep from the model-facing session action list.
- Remove start_focus and complete_focus from the model-facing session action list.
- Remove retired/hidden alias declarations that preserve session_search, session_grep, start_focus, complete_focus, focus_start, or focus_complete as model-facing concepts.
- Update docs and tests to the new surface instead of documenting legacy aliases.
- If internal helper function names temporarily remain during refactor, they must not appear in the model-facing registry, tool descriptions, tool suggestions, or docs.

## Non-goals
- Do not change canonical L0 JSONL session history storage.
- Do not remove the transcript projection/search backend.
- Do not remove focus knowledge storage or focus compaction behavior.
- Do not add legacy shims that keep the old model-facing names alive.
- Do not bundle unrelated tool failures, journal registry drift, or image tooling changes here.

## Suggested implementation notes
- Reuse existing createSessionSearchTool/createSessionGrepTool logic by moving or renaming it behind chat_history.
- Reuse existing createStartFocusTool/createCompleteFocusTool logic by moving or wrapping it behind focus_work actions start/complete.
- Add status for focus_work so the companion can inspect an active focus session without guessing.
- Consider cancel for focus_work if stale active focus sessions can block future work; if cancel is omitted, document the recovery path.
- Update src/core/agent/tool-surface/registry.ts, docs/tool-surface.md, src/core/agent/tool-suggestion.ts, adaptive tool tests, and session/focus tool tests.

## Validation
Run focused tests for tool registry, tool suggestion/autoload, session tool behavior, chat history search/grep behavior, and focus work behavior. Run npm run lint before closure.
acceptance_criteria:
- A core chat_history or transcript tool exists; accepted name is recorded in the close reason. It exposes search and grep for archived chat transcript lookup.
- session no longer exposes search, grep, start_focus, or complete_focus as model-facing actions.
- An extended focus_work tool exists for bounded project work spans and exposes start, complete, and status; cancel is either implemented or explicitly rejected with rationale.
- Model-facing registry, tool descriptions, docs, and suggestion/autoload logic do not preserve the old session_search, session_grep, start_focus, complete_focus, focus_start, or focus_complete aliases.
- Old-chat phrases route to chat_history/transcript in tests.
- Focus/project-work phrases route to focus_work only when extended tools are appropriate in tests.
- Existing transcript search and grep behavior still works through the new tool surface.
- Existing focus knowledge persistence and compaction behavior still works through focus_work.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.
