title: Normalize Postgres timestamp adapter boundaries
description:
## Summary
Normalize Postgres timestamp reads and writes so storage-owned timestamp encodings cannot leak into runtime code with the wrong JavaScript type. This is the broad follow-up to the live scratchpad Invalid time value failure: Postgres BIGINT columns can be returned as strings, but runtime code treated them as numbers.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Use a Postgres-backed scratchpad row whose created_at and updated_at values come from BIGINT columns.
2. Read the row through the current Postgres memory store path where the pg driver returns BIGINT fields as strings.
3. Call the scratchpad list/read formatter that formats entry.updatedAt with new Date(entry.updatedAt).toISOString().
4. Observe RangeError: Invalid time value for a numeric string such as '1782772439988', even though the numeric value 1782772439988 formats correctly.

## Scope
- Fix scratchpad Postgres mapping so created_at and updated_at from BIGINT columns are parsed to the accepted canonical runtime instant type before ScratchpadEntry values leave the store.
- Audit other Postgres BIGINT millisecond columns and adapters for the same row-field leak pattern, including gateway_audit.timestamp, session projection timestamps, model usage started/completed/recorded fields, observer eval timestamps, L2 memory timestamps, maintenance review timestamps, and processing watermarks.
- Audit TIMESTAMPTZ adapter boundaries for L0.1 episodic tables so Date/string values are either converted into the canonical runtime type or explicitly retained only behind well-named boundary types.
- Prefer the shared timestamp helpers from the sibling utility bead rather than open-coded parsing.
- Fail closed on malformed or out-of-range timestamps with errors that identify the table/field or adapter context.

## Non-goals
- Do not do a database schema migration solely for timestamp type unification.
- Do not change SQL TIMESTAMPTZ columns that are needed for SQL range/query behavior.
- Do not loosen timestamp validation by substituting Date.now() for bad stored values.

## Known files and examples
- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts: scratchpad row mapping around created_at and updated_at.
- src/faculties/memory/tools.ts: scratchpad list/read formats updatedAt with new Date(...).toISOString().
- src/persistence/postgres/migrations.ts: source of BIGINT and TIMESTAMPTZ column inventory.
- src/persistence/postgres/model-usage-store.ts: model usage time fields and bucket keys.
- src/persistence/postgres/session-projection-store.ts or equivalent projection adapter files if present.
acceptance_criteria:
- scratchpad list/read no longer throws Invalid time value when Postgres returns BIGINT millisecond timestamps as strings.
- Regression coverage constructs or mocks a Postgres row with string-valued BIGINT timestamps and verifies scratchpad output handles the timestamp correctly.
- Every touched Postgres adapter converts timestamp row values through the shared helpers or an explicitly documented equivalent.
- TIMESTAMPTZ adapter handling is explicit and tested for at least one representative path.
- No broad DB schema migration is introduced.
- npm run lint and targeted Postgres/scratchpad tests pass before closure.

title: Decide canonical timestamp boundary contract
description:
## Summary
Decide the repository-wide timestamp contract before implementation starts. The current code uses epoch milliseconds, Postgres BIGINT epoch milliseconds, ISO strings, TIMESTAMPTZ, JavaScript Date objects, bucket keys, compact backup timestamps, and prompt/display strings. That diversity is acceptable only if each representation has a clear boundary and naming rule.

## Decision
Pending. Recommended decision: use a finite epoch-millisecond number represented by a branded/shared type such as EpochMs as the canonical TypeScript instant representation at runtime/domain boundaries. Storage adapters should convert Postgres BIGINT strings, TIMESTAMPTZ/Date values, and ISO strings into that internal form on read, and convert back to the storage-owned format on write.

## Rationale
The scratchpad failure in psfn-framework-c4jy demonstrates that ambiguous timestamp boundaries create runtime crashes: Postgres BIGINT millisecond columns can arrive as strings, but downstream code may assume numbers and call new Date(value). A single internal instant representation plus explicit boundary conversion prevents that class of bug without forcing every database or filename format into one physical representation.

## Alternatives Considered
- Use ISO strings everywhere. Rejected as a likely poor fit for hot runtime arithmetic, event streams, existing JSONL/session telemetry, and millisecond duration calculations.
- Use JavaScript Date objects everywhere. Rejected because Date serializes poorly through JSON/API boundaries and still requires storage conversion.
- Use Postgres TIMESTAMPTZ everywhere. Rejected because not all timestamp data lives in Postgres, and high-volume telemetry/JSONL paths already use epoch milliseconds.
- Keep current mixed formats without a contract. Rejected because it already produced a live Invalid time value failure and spreads string-or-number ambiguity into tools/UI.

## Required policy details
- Which names are allowed for epoch millisecond numbers, for example timestampMs, createdAtMs, updatedAtMs, startedAtMs, completedAtMs.
- Which names are allowed for ISO strings, for example createdAtIso or updatedAtIso, and whether legacy createdAt string fields are permitted only in explicitly legacy/domain JSON stores.
- How to distinguish bucket keys such as YYYY-MM-DD and YYYY-MM, for example dayKey and monthKey suffixes.
- Where JavaScript Date objects are allowed, likely only transient channel/provider boundaries.
- Where Postgres TIMESTAMPTZ remains appropriate, likely SQL-queryable episodic history and span/range data.
- Whether tool/API outputs should prefer millisecond machine fields, ISO display fields, or both with explicit names.

## Non-goals
- Do not implement the migration in this decision bead.
- Do not require physical database columns to use one universal type.
- Do not bless ambiguous string-or-number timestamp fields for new code.

## Context
This decision was discovered from psfn-framework-c4jy after scratchpad list/read failed with Invalid time value because Postgres BIGINT timestamps were read as strings and later formatted as Date inputs.
acceptance_criteria:
- The bead is closed only after the accepted timestamp contract is recorded in the issue design/notes or a repo-owned contract document referenced by this bead.
- The decision states the canonical TypeScript instant type and the allowed storage/display exceptions.
- The decision defines naming conventions for epoch milliseconds, ISO strings, bucket keys, and display-only timestamps.
- The decision states whether new tool/API schemas expose AtMs, AtIso, or both.
- Follow-up implementation beads are updated if the final decision differs from the recommended EpochMs-centered contract.

title: P1: Standardize timestamp contracts across runtime boundaries
description:
## Summary
PSFN currently uses several timestamp representations across runtime state, Postgres, JSON stores, tools, UI contracts, prompt macros, bucket keys, and backup paths. The current scratchpad Invalid time value failure shows the operational cost: Postgres BIGINT epoch milliseconds can arrive in TypeScript as strings, then code treats them as numbers and calls new Date(value).

The goal is not to force every storage layer into one physical format. The goal is to define one canonical TypeScript instant representation at runtime boundaries, explicit conversion rules for each storage/display boundary, and naming conventions that make the format unambiguous.

## Observed timestamp formats
- Epoch milliseconds as TypeScript numbers in runtime events, JSONL sessions, telemetry, model usage, and turn records.
- Postgres BIGINT epoch milliseconds in scratchpad, gateway audit, model usage, observer eval, L2 memory, and session projection tables.
- ISO-8601 UTC strings in JSON/config/domain stores such as skills, wiki, values, identity, contacts, concerns, reflections, and internal state snapshots.
- Postgres TIMESTAMPTZ in L0.1 episodic memory tables and span/range-query data.
- JavaScript Date objects at in-memory channel/message boundaries.
- Date/month bucket keys such as YYYY-MM-DD and YYYY-MM for daily/monthly aggregation.
- Filename-safe compact timestamps for backup directories.
- Prompt/display-only formats such as unix seconds or humanized date strings.

## Scope
Create and land a repository timestamp contract that keeps one canonical internal instant type while preserving appropriate storage-specific encodings at boundaries. The contract should cover naming, conversion points, allowed formats, and tests/verification that prevent another string-valued BIGINT timestamp from leaking into runtime formatting.

## Non-goals
- Do not perform a broad database migration just to make all existing columns physically identical.
- Do not remove TIMESTAMPTZ from SQL tables that need SQL-native range/date queries.
- Do not remove date bucket keys or filename-safe backup timestamps; they are not general-purpose instants.
- Do not silently coerce malformed timestamps in security- or audit-sensitive paths. Fail closed with actionable errors.
- Do not bundle live deployment or Kubernetes rollout work into this epic.

## Suggested child work
- Decide and document the canonical timestamp boundary contract.
- Add shared timestamp parsing/formatting primitives.
- Normalize Postgres adapter read/write boundaries, especially BIGINT millisecond columns.
- Normalize tool/API/UI timestamp schema surfaces so ambiguous string-or-number fields are phased out.
- Add focused tests and a lightweight verifier for timestamp contract drift.
acceptance_criteria:
- A decision bead records the accepted canonical runtime timestamp representation, naming rules, and boundary conversion policy.
- Shared timestamp utilities exist and are used by touched adapters instead of ad hoc new Date(row.field) coercion.
- Postgres BIGINT millisecond timestamps are parsed to finite numbers or rejected at adapter boundaries.
- Tool/API/UI timestamp schemas avoid ambiguous instant fields for newly touched surfaces, using explicit suffixes such as AtMs, AtIso, or Key.
- Regression tests cover the scratchpad-style Postgres BIGINT string case and at least one TIMESTAMPTZ/ISO boundary conversion.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before implementation beads are closed.

title: P1: Fix live tool surface failures and schema drift
description:
## Summary
Live Carlini has multiple observed tool-failure symptoms, but the current-runtime evidence separates them into one real runtime bug, one current schema/metadata drift, one noisy malformed-call behavior, and several stale pre-deploy failures that should not be chased unless they recur on the current image.

Investigation context from 2026-06-30:
- Live deployment was on image `localhost/psfn-framework:0.1.0-kube-c09b1926` with image label `org.opencontainers.image.revision=c09b1926`.
- Agent, gateway, and Garden were ready.
- Agent startup log showed `ToolWiringValidator` passed with `toolCount=22`.
- Since the latest rollout around `2026-06-30T05:28Z`, persisted tool-observation errors were limited to scratchpad `Invalid time value` and journal malformed-argument calls. No current `Tool ... not found` errors were found after that rollout.

## Current failure 1: scratchpad list/read crashes with Invalid time value
Raw session evidence:
- Session file: `/app/companion-data/state/sessions/20260628_1486443955561299979_266127174426165249_933871.jsonl`
- Request `1521388575852335205`, line 1180, at `2026-06-30T05:35:45.568Z`
- Tool observation: `scratchpad` error, content `Error using scratchpad: Invalid time value`

Live DB evidence:
- `scratchpad_entries.created_at` and `scratchpad_entries.updated_at` are `BIGINT` columns.
- Live row example: `id=b487d0eb-b2a0-49d5-872d-69a216ea729b`, `created_at=1782772439988`, `updated_at=1782772439988`.
- Node behavior verified in the live container: `new Date(1782772439988).toISOString()` works, but `new Date('1782772439988').toISOString()` throws `RangeError: Invalid time value`.

Likely cause:
- The PostgreSQL driver returns `BIGINT` values as strings, but the scratchpad runtime types currently assume numbers.
- `src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts:866-875` loads `created_at` and `updated_at` directly into `ScratchpadEntry` values.
- `src/faculties/memory/tools.ts:172-185` formats entries with `new Date(entry.updatedAt).toISOString()`, which crashes when `updatedAt` is a numeric string.
- Related mapper: `src/faculties/memory/store/mappers.ts:231-237` maps scratchpad rows without validation/coercion in the SQLite path; check whether shared parsing is appropriate, but do not regress SQLite.

## Current failure 2: journal schema/registry drift
Raw session evidence:
- Request `1521392654217248808`, lines 1221-1225, at `2026-06-30T05:52:25Z`.
- Journal produced three malformed-call errors first:
  - `journal failed for action=write: path or title is required`
  - `journal failed for action=write: content is required`
  - `journal failed for action=write: content is required`
- The same turn then succeeded: `Journal note created: carlini-notes.md`.
- `/app/workspace/journal/carlini-notes.md` exists on live and was 555 bytes at inspection time.

Source evidence:
- Actual journal tool supports `list`, `read`, `write`, `append`, and `search` in `src/boundary/integrations/journal/tools.ts:8` and exposes those literals in its TypeBox schema at `src/boundary/integrations/journal/tools.ts:68-98`.
- The canonical first-party surface registry still says journal only has `actions: ['write']` at `src/core/agent/tool-surface/registry.ts:471-476`.
- Runtime catalog action descriptions prefer canonical registry actions over extracting action literals from the actual tool schema at `src/core/agent/tool-catalog.ts:102-105`, so registry drift can hide valid journal actions from `toolset describe` and related discovery surfaces.

## Current failure 3: noisy repeated malformed calls before success
Examples:
- Journal calls repeatedly omitted `path/title` or `content` before eventually succeeding.
- Orient request `1521371908128505856` had three bad `reorient` calls (`persona must be a string`, `human must be a string`) before a valid one succeeded in the same turn.

Relevant scheduler behavior:
- `src/core/agent/tool-call-scheduler.ts:170-185` halts remaining sequential calls only after an error in the current compatible batch.
- Similar malformed calls with different arguments are not treated as the same signature, so the model can burn several invalid variants in one assistant turn.
- `src/core/agent/tool-call-scheduler.ts:240-264` already degrades duplicate completed/in-flight or repeated same-signature failures, but it does not aggregate repeated missing-required-field errors for the same tool/action.

## Stale failures and non-current symptoms
Do not treat these as current runtime blockers unless they recur after image `c09b1926`:
- `selfie_create not found`, `media not found`, and `journal not found` were observed before the current deployment/image and are not present in post-rollout observations.
- Current logs after rollout show `ToolWiringValidator` passing and no recent `Tool ... not found` messages.
- Contact lookup failures from earlier turns were tied to pre-fix list/guidance behavior. Current source includes IDs in `contact action=list` output at `src/core/contacts/tools.ts:433-449`, and commits `2b9345d1` / `1e2a20a4` improved invalid-call guidance.
- Web failures were malformed calls with missing `target` plus one policy denial; not a wiring failure.
- Image URL leakage/multiple visible images was separately fixed by commit `c09b1926` and should not be mixed into this bead unless it recurs.

## Scope
Fix and verify the current live tool-surface issues:
1. Coerce/validate Postgres `BIGINT` timestamps for scratchpad entries before exposing them as `ScratchpadEntry.createdAt`/`updatedAt` numbers.
2. Add regression coverage for Postgres scratchpad rows where `created_at`/`updated_at` arrive as strings.
3. Update the journal canonical registry metadata to include all actual supported actions: `list`, `read`, `write`, `append`, `search`.
4. Add a registry-vs-tool-schema drift test or validator that catches mismatches between canonical surface `actions` and actual `parameters.properties.action` literals for first-party tools.
5. Improve malformed-call behavior enough that repeated missing-required-field variants for the same tool/action do not create long noisy tool-error sequences in a single turn. A minimal acceptable fix is a scheduler/tool-result steering guard that stops repeated same-tool/same-action missing-field errors and returns one actionable minimal-valid-JSON instruction.
6. Add or document a small live smoke path for non-mutating tool health after deploy: `toolset describe journal`, `journal list`, `scratchpad list`, `contact list`, and image tool availability/discovery check.

## Non-goals
- Do not rebuild or redeploy as part of this bead unless the implementer is explicitly asked to do deployment work.
- Do not chase pre-`c09b1926` `Tool ... not found` observations unless a new post-`c09b1926` occurrence is captured.
- Do not change image model defaults, image URL hiding, or generated-media attachment behavior here.
- Do not loosen tool validation by silently accepting missing required fields; fail closed but make the feedback more agent-usable.
- Do not create off-repo runtime config or hidden live overrides.

## Suggested validation
- Targeted unit tests for Postgres scratchpad timestamp coercion and scratchpad list formatting.
- Targeted unit tests for journal registry/schema action parity.
- Targeted scheduler/tool-call test for repeated malformed required-field calls in one turn.
- `npm run lint` is required before closing this bead.
- Run the smallest relevant test subset first, then broaden if shared scheduler/catalog behavior is touched.

- `scratchpad action=list` no longer throws `Invalid time value` when Postgres returns `created_at`/`updated_at` as strings for `BIGINT` columns.
- A regression test covers string-valued Postgres scratchpad timestamps and verifies formatted scratchpad output includes a valid ISO timestamp or otherwise handles the timestamp without throwing.
- `journal` canonical surface metadata lists `list`, `read`, `write`, `append`, and `search`, matching the actual journal tool schema.
- A test or validator fails if a canonical first-party tool registry action list drifts from the actual tool schema action literals for tools where both exist.
- Repeated same-turn malformed missing-required-field calls for the same tool/action are reduced to one actionable steering/error result instead of several near-duplicate tool errors.
- Tests for the changed areas pass, and `npm run lint` passes in the worktree before the bead is closed.
- Handoff or closure evidence names the commit(s), files changed, tests run, and whether any post-fix live smoke was run.

title: Stop image tool replies from leaking provider image URLs
description:
Summary
Live Carlini image generation replies are showing the generated image attachment plus the upstream FAL/provider image link in the text reply. Discord renders the text URL/embed, so the user can see multiple image previews and a FAL link instead of a clean single delivered image.

Root cause
src/primitives/images/tools.ts formatResult() strips localPath from ImageGenerationResult before returning tool text, but it still includes images[].url and file metadata in visible JSON. The post-turn generated-media path already extracts the structured imageResult/mediaResult from tool result details and sends response.attachments separately, so the URL in text is redundant and leaks provider/CDN implementation details into chat.

Scope
- Change image/media/selfie tool visible text so successful image generations do not include images[].url or localPath/provider CDN links.
- Keep structured details.mediaResult/details.imageResult intact so collectGeneratedImageAttachments can still deliver the generated image attachment.
- Preserve useful non-link status context such as image count, provider/model, fallback reason, and vision review.
- Add/update regression tests proving tool text does not contain generated image URLs while details still contain the original image result.

Non-goals
- Do not change FAL payloads, model defaults, or image generation provider behavior.
- Do not remove image gallery metadata or attachment URL storage from internal details/sidecars.
- Do not change Discord attachment upload mechanics unless required after the text leak is fixed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Successful media/image/selfie tool result text does not contain generated image URLs from images[].url.
- Successful media/image/selfie tool result details still include the full image result with URLs for attachment extraction.
- Existing generated-media attachment extraction tests continue to pass.
- Targeted image tool/generated-media tests and npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Completed in git commit c09b1926. Changed src/primitives/images/tools.ts formatResult() to emit URL-free generated-image summaries for tool-visible text while preserving full image URLs/request IDs in structured details for generated-media attachment extraction. Added regressions in src/primitives/images/tools.test.ts proving details retain URLs but visible text omits provider image URLs, local paths, and request IDs. title: Fix Discord image MIME mismatch blocking vision
description:
Summary
Live Carlini vision failed in Discord on 2026-06-30 even though LiteLLM/OpenRouter vision and the PSFN API image path both worked. Gateway logs for Discord message IDs 1521370331560804442 and 1521370546380734505 show image.png was declared by Discord as image/webp, but the filename and sniffed bytes were image/png. The Discord adapter treated that safe image-to-image disagreement as metadata quarantine risk, withheld the attachment, and the agent received only a text quarantine notice, so the turn stayed on ChatGPTN/chat instead of routing to the vision purpose.

Files
- src/channels/discord/file-quarantine.ts: appendDeclaredExtensionMismatchReasons, appendSniffMismatchReasons, hasDiscordAttachmentMetadataQuarantineRisk
- src/channels/discord/adapter.ts: extractAttachments skips metadata-risky images before vision
- src/channels/discord/file-ingest.test.ts and/or src/channels/discord/adapter.test.ts for regression coverage

Scope
Allow benign image-to-image MIME disagreements such as declared image/webp with .png name and PNG sniffed bytes to pass into normal image attachment/vision handling. Continue to quarantine scripts, archives, executables, macro docs, plugin/skill manifests, executable mode bits, and non-image payloads masquerading as images. Do not weaken document or code quarantine.

Non-goals
Do not change the vision model route or OpenRouter/LiteLLM config. Do not permit non-image sniffed bytes through as image attachments.

Evidence
Direct live smoke via LiteLLM openrouter/google/gemini-3.1-flash-lite with an inline red PNG returned Red. Direct PSFN gateway /v1/chat/completions with the same inline image returned a vision-grounded answer. Discord turn records show the userMessage contained [Attached file quarantined: image.png] and no image attachment.
acceptance_criteria:
- classifyDiscordAttachmentQuarantineRisk does not quarantine when declared, extension-expected, and sniffed content types are all image/* even if their exact image subtype differs.
- hasDiscordAttachmentMetadataQuarantineRisk does not cause the Discord adapter to skip a real image solely because Discord declared a different image/* type than the filename extension.
- Existing spoof/script/archive/macro quarantine tests still pass.
- Targeted Discord attachment tests and npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Completed in git commit b647aa59. src/channels/discord/file-quarantine.ts now treats mismatched safe raster image MIME subtypes as compatible, so image/webp vs .png/image/png no longer creates declared_extension_mismatch or mime_sniff_mismatch quarantine reasons. Regression tests added in src/channels/discord/file-ingest.test.ts for metadata-only and sniffed PNG image subtype disagreement, plus src/channels/discord/adapter.test.ts for the live Discord shape where image.png declared image/webp remains a visible image attachment instead of a quarantine-only prompt block. Validation passed: npm test -- --run src/channels/discord/file-ingest.test.ts src/channels/discord/adapter.test.ts; npm run lint; git diff --check.

title: P1: Add first-class owner-file migration framework
description:
Summary
The Carlini rollout failure on 2026-06-30 showed that persisted owner files can outlive prompt/runtime schema changes. A code deploy removed substrate_health.* system_language template keys, but /app/companion-data/state/prompt-layers.json still contained those keys, causing startup to fail before normal seeding could repair the file. Commit 7b950ba8 fixed that one prompt-layer case with a named pre-validation migration, but the project needs a reusable owner-file migration framework before wider multi-user deployments.

Why this matters
When many users/companions exist, manual live data repair or one-off compatibility shims will not scale. Startup must be able to load raw persisted owner files, apply explicit reviewed migrations, write backups/audit records, then run strict validation. Unknown/unmigrated schema drift should still fail closed with actionable diagnostics.

Scope
- Design and implement a reusable migration runner for JSON owner files used by system-data and companion-data.
- Migrations must run before strict validation when the file schema version or known retired fields require it.
- Each migration must have a stable id, description, owner file family, input predicate, output validation, and audit/backup behavior.
- Migration results should be logged and inspectable from operations/debug tooling.
- Migration must distinguish system-owned defaults from admin/user-owned custom data and preserve custom edits unless the migration explicitly documents deterministic removal/transform.
- Add tests using prompt-layers/system_language as the first concrete fixture, including the substrate_health.* retired-key case already fixed in 7b950ba8.

Non-goals
- Do not silently accept arbitrary unknown keys.
- Do not reintroduce retired prompt fields into model-facing context.
- Do not mutate live production files without backup/audit semantics.

2026-07-15 live rollout expansion
A second concrete failure at merged framework 5d1785dcb1 broadened this bead beyond prompt layers. Existing scheduler.json lacked the newly mandatory disabled icpAutonomy block; existing charge-policy.json lacked companion_social, companionSocialContinuation, icpCostBreaker, and fatigue.socialRegulation. Forward-only atomic additions let the target image validate, but rollback to the prior image then rejected icpCostBreaker until the exact newly added paths were removed while preserving custom operator quotas. The reusable framework must therefore serve system-data as well as companion-data, support target-image preflight, and make rollback restore exact pre-migration bytes before the old image starts. Generic recursive seed merging is explicitly unsafe because it cannot distinguish operator authority, removed fields, or backward compatibility.
design: Use a small versioned migration registry keyed by owner-file family and exact from/to schema fingerprint. Each migration declares a stable ID, source-shape preconditions, deterministic transforms, invariant/output validation, audit-safe changed paths and before/after digests, atomic file+directory fsync, and an exact-byte backup/rollback strategy. Deployment preflight validates a read-only candidate against the target image before mutation; unknown source shapes or operator-modified migration fields fail closed for review. Startup may apply only explicitly registered migrations named in the live alpha boundary; it never recursively merges arbitrary seed defaults or accepts unknown keys.
acceptance_criteria:
- A generic migration runner exists and is used by at least PromptLayerStore or an equivalent owner-file load path.\n- Migrations have stable IDs and are recorded in logs/audit/history with before/after evidence or checksums.\n- Known retired fields can be migrated before strict validation; arbitrary unknown fields still fail closed.\n- System-owned default data can be reset to current defaults; admin/user-owned custom data is preserved unless a migration explicitly transforms it.\n- Tests cover successful migration, failed unknown drift, idempotent rerun, and backup/audit output.
- Fixtures matching the pre-5d1785 live scheduler and charge-policy files migrate while preserving every existing value, including custom run-charge quotas; only declared paths change.
- A forced target rollout failure restores exact pre-migration bytes before prior pods restart, and both target and prior validators are exercised.
- Migration writes are atomic and fsynced; diagnostics contain stable migration/file/version IDs, digests, and changed paths but no owner values.
- Unknown, malformed, already-modified, or unregistered source shapes leave bytes unchanged and fail closed.
- Temporary alpha support is named in docs/specifications.md with validation and beta-removal criteria before production enablement.
notes: 2026-07-01: soft dependency of psfn-framework-76rn.2 (channel-owned privacy migration) — if this framework lands first, E3.2 uses it; otherwise E3.2 does a guarded one-off.

title: P1: Improve fallback history summary and compress repeated tool failures
description:
Summary
Replace fallback history-summary line dumping with a compact, speaker-aware summary format and compress repeated tool failures. This is separate from full LLM compaction; the immediate target is the deterministic fallback summary path that can dump random recent lines and repeated failures.

Current behavior
buildSessionHistorySummaryText emits [History summary] plus clipped speaker lines. Tool observations already have some masking/summarization support, but repeated failures can still appear as individual noisy lines in fallback history context.

Required behavior
- Preserve speaker names in summary output.
- Avoid dumping many raw lines when a short prose summary or grouped summary is enough.
- Compress repeated tool failures into one line such as: A tool failed 4 times while attempting X. Most recent failure: Y.
- Omit tool failures entirely when they do not affect current behavior and no useful summary can be produced.
- Keep summaries bounded by the existing token budget.

Files to inspect first
- src/core/session/manager-primitives.ts: buildSessionHistorySummaryText and helper functions.
- src/core/session/tool-observation.ts: formatToolObservationForContext.
- src/core/session/manager/context-builder.ts: fallback summary insertion.
- Existing compaction service for semantic/LLM summaries, but do not expand scope unnecessarily.

Non-goals
- Do not redesign full session compaction in this bead.
- Do not add a new LLM summarization call for every turn unless a separate design decision approves that cost.
design: Keep this deterministic and cheap for P1. True semantic summarization can remain in the existing compaction path.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fallback history summary preserves speaker names for multi-user chats.
- Repeated equivalent tool failures are compressed into a single bounded summary line.
- Raw repeated tool failure lines are not dumped individually into fallback history context.
- Summary remains within the configured token budget.
- Tests cover multi-speaker summary and repeated tool failure compression.
notes: This was in the original notes as P0-ish, but it is less privacy-critical than room gating and attribution.
close_reason: Completed in 701158a3 on the integration branch. Evidence: src/core/session/manager-primitives.ts now groups consecutive failed tool observations into one bounded failure summary while preserving speaker-aware summary lines; src/core/session/manager-primitives.test.ts covers multi-speaker summaries and repeated tool failure compression. Validation: src/core/session/manager-primitives.test.ts passed, context-builder test passed, targeted integrated suite passed (309 tests), npm run lint passed, npm run build passed.

title: Fix media generation charging so successful images are not hidden as failed tool calls
description: Audit evidence from Carlini live deployment on 2026-06-29: in Discord channel 1486443955561299979, turn 019f1364-812e-74bf-b064-d5231bf256c0 / request 1521133054708678848, the user asked Carlini to retry image generation after tier upgrade. The first media call failed with FAL no_media_generated for a marijuana seedling prompt. The second media call succeeded at the provider level: model_usage_events has success call_kind=image_create, purpose=media, provider=fal, model=fal-ai/nano-banana-2 at 2026-06-29T12:40:02.865Z with requestId 019f1364-d578-7bc2-9d3a-7191fc3b6a61, and /app/workspace/images/2026-06-29/Ov2ZeQpdawyQfDAt3SAU0_2g009nUm-8c72667b.png plus sidecar metadata were written. The tool result shown to the model was still an error: 'media generate failed: Charge quota exceeded for lane interactive while charging paidImageGeneration (27/24; rolling 24-hour budget).' Carlini then told the user the budget was tapped out, and Discord did not receive the generated attachment. Likely cause: paid image charge is applied after provider generation/artifact persistence, so charge failure can mask a successful provider result and prevent attachment collection. Scope: fix media/selfie charge accounting and result propagation for generated images. Non-goal: changing the charge budget policy amount or deploying to live in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test simulates paid image generation when the rolling interactive quota is exhausted and proves the provider is not called and no artifact is written; a second test covers a successful in-budget media generation and proves the returned AgentResponse includes image attachment details for Discord delivery. Existing successful generation paths still write gallery sidecars. npm run lint passes.
notes: Likely root cause of sibling stnk.3 (media/selfie tool generates image but output fails to reach chat stream). Pre-checking the interactive quota before calling the provider fixes both: over-budget rejects upfront instead of masking a successful generation, and in-budget results propagate attachments. title: Stop persisting admin token in localStorage and WebSocket URLs
description:
Summary: The admin UI stores the admin token in browser localStorage and appends it to WebSocket URLs even though the server login path already issues an HttpOnly SameSite cookie and WebSocket server auth accepts cookies. This increases token exposure to XSS and URL logging without providing useful WebSocket authentication.

Evidence and affected files:
- admin-ui/src/lib/stores/auth.svelte.ts:1 initializes token state from localStorage key psfn_token.
- admin-ui/src/lib/stores/auth.svelte.ts:50 writes the token to localStorage and also writes a non-HttpOnly document.cookie copy at line 56.
- admin-ui/src/lib/api/websocket.ts:91 builds the WebSocket URL and appends ?token=... at lines 94-96 when getToken() returns a value.
- src/operator/garden/operator-surface.ts:168-172 already sets psfn_token as an HttpOnly SameSite cookie after successful login.
- src/operator/garden/server-auth.ts authenticates WebSocket upgrades from bearer token headers or cookies, not from a query token, so the query parameter is redundant.

Why it matters: localStorage tokens are exposed to any successful script injection. Query-string tokens can leak through browser history, proxies, and logs. The safer cookie path already exists and should be the browser UI source of truth.

Scope: Remove persistent localStorage storage for the admin token. Rely on server-issued HttpOnly SameSite cookies for the browser UI session. Keep a narrowly scoped in-memory bearer-token path only if there is a real non-browser/API-token use case. Remove token query parameters from WebSocket URL construction.

Non-goals: Do not redesign Garden login, rotate token format, or add a new auth provider in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: The browser admin UI no longer stores psfn_token in localStorage; browser WebSocket URLs never include the token as a query parameter; existing HttpOnly SameSite cookie login/session behavior still authenticates API and WebSocket requests; tests cover auth store behavior and WebSocket URL construction; npm run lint passes.
close_reason:
Implemented admin browser token hardening. Evidence:
- admin-ui/src/lib/stores/auth.svelte.ts no longer initializes from localStorage, no longer writes psfn_token to localStorage, and no longer creates a script-visible psfn_token cookie during login. It keeps only a transient in-memory token path and relies on the server-issued HttpOnly SameSite cookie for normal browser sessions.
- admin-ui/src/lib/stores/auth-storage.ts removes legacy localStorage tokens and can expire old script-readable cookies only during explicit cleanup/logout.
- admin-ui/src/lib/api/websocket.ts no longer imports getToken and buildAdminWebSocketUrl returns same-origin ws/wss URLs without ?token= query parameters.
- admin-ui/src/lib/stores/auth-storage.test.ts covers legacy token cleanup without setItem and cookie expiry helper behavior.
- admin-ui/src/lib/api/websocket.test.ts covers ws/wss URL construction and asserts no token query is appended.
Validation passed: npx vitest run src/lib/api/websocket.test.ts src/lib/stores/auth-storage.test.ts --reporter=dot from admin-ui (5 tests); npm test -- --run src/operator/garden/server.test.ts src/operator/garden/operator-surface.test.ts --reporter=dot (38 tests, including login/logout and websocket auth paths); npm --prefix admin-ui run check; npm --prefix admin-ui run build; npm run lint.

title: Reject unauthenticated Garden admin on non-loopback hosts
description:
Summary: The public API server already fail-closes insecure local mode to loopback hosts, but the Garden/admin surfaces do not enforce the same boundary. If ADMIN_HOST is set to a non-loopback address and ADMIN_ALLOW_INSECURE=true is set, the Garden surface can start without ADMIN_TOKEN and listen on that address.

Evidence and affected files:
- src/operator/garden/operator-surface.ts:59 only rejects startup when both token is missing and allowInsecureWithoutToken is false. It then listens on this.config.host ?? '127.0.0.1' at line 84 with no loopback check.
- src/operator/garden/server.ts:54 has the same pattern in the legacy AdminServer, listening on this.host at line 79 and only warning at line 85 when auth is disabled.
- src/channels/api/server/auth.ts:24 demonstrates the desired policy for the OpenAI-compatible API server: missing API_KEY requires insecure mode, and line 35 also rejects non-loopback hosts when auth is missing.

Why it matters: Admin/Garden endpoints expose operator capabilities. Insecure/no-token mode should remain a local development convenience only and should fail closed if bound to 0.0.0.0, a LAN address, or any other non-loopback host.

Scope: Add a shared or local loopback-host guard for GardenOperatorSurface and AdminServer startup. Use the existing API auth guard behavior as the model. Include tests for no token + ADMIN_ALLOW_INSECURE=true + 0.0.0.0/non-loopback rejection and no token + loopback acceptance.

Non-goals: Do not redesign admin authentication, cookie handling, or deployment service files in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: GardenOperatorSurface and the legacy AdminServer refuse to start without an admin token when the configured host is non-loopback, even if ADMIN_ALLOW_INSECURE=true; loopback insecure dev mode still works intentionally; tests cover 0.0.0.0/non-loopback rejection and 127.0.0.1/localhost acceptance; npm run lint passes.
close_reason:
Implemented fail-closed Garden admin startup auth policy for insecure mode. Evidence:
- src/shared/net/hosts.ts now owns the shared isLoopbackHost predicate; src/channels/api/http-policy.ts reuses/re-exports it so the API behavior stays unchanged.
- src/operator/garden/auth-policy.ts adds validateAdminAuthStartupPolicy with the same required-token check plus a non-loopback rejection when ADMIN_ALLOW_INSECURE=true is used without ADMIN_TOKEN.
- src/operator/garden/operator-surface.ts and src/operator/garden/server.ts call the policy before binding/listening, so both split GardenOperatorSurface and legacy AdminServer refuse unauthenticated non-loopback startup.
- Tests in src/operator/garden/operator-surface.test.ts and src/operator/garden/server.test.ts cover 0.0.0.0 rejection plus explicit 127.0.0.1 and localhost acceptance.
Validation passed: npm test -- --run src/channels/api/http-policy.test.ts src/channels/api/server.test.ts --reporter=dot (101 tests); npm test -- --run src/operator/garden/server.test.ts src/operator/garden/operator-surface.test.ts --reporter=dot (38 tests); npm run lint; npm run build.

title: Autonomy tier gating audit: ungated benign tools, tier-lock internal/destructive, fix false-positive media-tool denial
description:
Operator ask (sprint-9-wrapup item 4): audit and correct the autonomy-tier gating so benign tools are not over-gated, destructive tools are not under-gated, and a false-positive error (companion believes she lacks permission for a benign tool like the media tool when she actually has access) is resolved.

## Current state (verified)

- Capability tier type: src/system/capabilities/tier-types.ts — CapabilityTier = 'nursery' | 'apprentice' | 'autonomous' | 'custom'. (Note: the operator prompt uses low/medium/highest wording; map to these actual tiers.)
- Gate: src/system/capabilities/gate.ts — gateToolWithCapabilities() at line 64 produces the 'Capability denied: tool X requires Y, but tier Z only grants W' error (line 54).
- Requirements / scope tokens: src/system/capabilities/requirements.ts — e.g. selfie_create() => 'external.web' (line 250). This is a scope token, NOT a tier; the gating decision chains scope->tier elsewhere.
- Supporting: src/system/capabilities/safeguards.ts, tiers.ts, compositional-policy.ts, runtime.ts.
- Tool surface: src/core/agent/tool-surface/registry.ts and tool-wiring-validator.ts wire per-tool gating.

## Scope

1. UNGATED (benign) tier — must be globally accessible regardless of tier. Strictly includes:
   - Journaling
   - Selfie creation
   - Image generation (Media tool)
   - Web search and Internal search
   Audit each against requirements.ts + gate.ts; any of these currently requiring a non-lowest tier is a misclassification to fix.
2. MEDIUM tier — read-only / internal-state tools (reading internal settings or states) gated to medium.
3. HIGHEST tier — ONLY self-modification tools or destructive/modifying tools gated to the highest tier. Confirm nothing destructive leaks into lower tiers and nothing benign is stranded at the top.
4. FALSE-POSITIVE ERROR FIX: the companion currently believes she lacks permission for a benign tool (e.g. media) when she actually has access. This is the operator's named symptom. Fix at the gating layer / requirements mapping — the tool must either not require the tier it's asking for, or the denial path must not fire when access is in fact granted. NOT a workaround that blanket-grants everything.

## Non-goals

- Do not redesign the capability-tier model. Work within nursery/apprentice/autonomous/custom.
- Do not change the compositional policy engine semantics; this is a classification + denial-path fix.
- No new tiers.

## Why

Over-gating benign tools (journaling, selfie, search) chokes everyday companion behavior and — combined with the false-positive — makes her believe she cannot do things she can. Under-gating destructive tools is a safety hole. Both directions need correcting in one pass so the tier contract matches its intent.

## Files (likely touched)

- src/system/capabilities/requirements.ts (tool -> scope/tier classification)
- src/system/capabilities/gate.ts (denial path that fires the false positive)
- src/system/capabilities/safeguards.ts, tiers.ts (as needed)
- src/core/agent/tool-surface/registry.ts, tool-wiring-validator.ts (per-tool gating wiring)

## Dependencies / links

title: Regression: media/selfie tool generates the image but output fails to reach the chat stream
description:
Operator ask (sprint-9-wrapup item 3): regression where the companion successfully accesses the media/selfie tool and GENERATES an image, but fails to push the generated asset into the chat stream. Tool execution works; output handling is failing.

## Current state (verified)

- src/primitives/images/tools.ts is the media/selfie tool:
  - buildToolContent() (~line 123) assembles content: text (formatResult) + image content blocks.
  - buildMediaResultDetails() (~line 339) wraps result into mediaResult.
  - Tool execute path returns `content: buildToolContent(result, ...)` and `details: buildMediaResultDetails(...)` (~lines 479-480 for generate, similar for edit ~511+).
  - chargePaidImageGeneration handles billing (line 350).
- So the TOOL produces a valid result + content payload. The break is DOWNSTREAM: between tool.execute returning and the message (text + image) landing in the chat stream the companion emits to.

## Scope

1. IDENTIFY THE PIPELINE BREAK: trace the tool result content from tool.execute return through the tool-call scheduler / tool-surface registry / message assembly into the chat stream emit. Pin the exact stage that drops or mis-serializes the image content.
2. ROOT-CAUSE FIX: fix at the shared point all tool outputs route through — not a per-tool or per-call patch. The bug is named on media/selfie, but if the output-handling break is in a shared path it will affect every tool that returns non-text content; fix it once.
3. TOOLING CONSOLIDATION CROSS-CHECK: the operator explicitly suspects this regressed from the recent tooling consolidation work (tool-surface registry / tool-wiring-validator / tool-call-scheduler area). Cross-check recent commits touching src/core/agent/tool-surface/, src/core/agent/tool-wiring-validator.ts, src/core/agent/tool-call-scheduler*.ts. Identify the commit that introduced the regression in the close notes.
4. Confirm the generated asset reference (localPath/url) survives serialization into the chat message and renders, not just that text reaches the stream.

## Non-goals

- Do not change the image generation pipeline itself (src/primitives/images/service.ts, generated-media.ts) unless the break is provably there. The tool generates fine; the symptom is output delivery.
- No new media tool variants.

## Why

A working tool whose output never reaches the user is worse than a broken tool — it looks successful to the companion (she thinks she sent the selfie) while silently failing to deliver. This directly breaks a flagship companion capability.

## Files (likely touched)

- src/primitives/images/tools.ts (verify content shape at execute return)
- src/core/agent/tool-surface/registry.ts
- src/core/agent/tool-call-scheduler.ts (and test)
- src/core/agent/tool-wiring-validator.ts
- the message-assembly / chat-stream emit path that consumes tool `content`/`details` (trace and pin)

## Dependencies / links

- Coordinate with psfn-framework-stnk child 4 (autonomy gating): if the companion is ALSO mis-believing she lacks permission for the media tool (false-positive denial), the two bugs can mask each other. Disentangle before claiming either fixed.

title: Add group-room memory conformance fixtures and regression tests
description:
Summary:
Build a group-room memory conformance test suite and fixtures that lock in the expected behavior.

Scope:
- Create representative fixtures for a 500-message group room with four humans, direct mentions, overheard facts, jokes, boundaries, preferences, relationships, and repeated chatter.
- Include a direct/1:1 fixture proving old behavior remains stable.
- Assert extraction yield, attribution, per-contact coverage, profile refresh, skip reasons, and no egress from observed triggers.
- Include privacy attack cases where a participant tries to obtain or rewrite another participant's memories.
acceptance_criteria:
- The suite proves a normal online group room window, configured at 50 messages in one fixture and 100 messages in another, produces useful memories when salient facts exist.
- The suite includes a larger backlog/backfill stress fixture to prove range processing and resume behavior without implying that live extraction batches 500 messages at once.
- The suite proves casual chatter and repeated low-signal messages do not become durable memories.
- The suite proves each accepted memory has correct source/subject/trigger attribution and privacy metadata.
- The suite proves observed-message extraction never sends a Discord response.
- The suite proves direct/1:1 extraction cadence, window size, and max-write defaults are unchanged.
- The suite proves non-default JSON config for windows, triggers, salience, and caps changes behavior without code changes.
- The suite includes regression coverage for ambiguous-speaker, write-cap, profile coverage, and cross-contact privacy failures.
notes: Test correction: use 50/100-message online fixtures plus separate larger backlog stress; assert knobs come from JSON config.
close_reason: Implemented group-room memory conformance fixtures and regression coverage. title: Make profile synthesis contact-coverage aware for group rooms
description:
Summary:
Refresh contact profiles for all qualifying group-room participants after group extraction.

Problem:
Current profile refresh follows accepted writes and fallback trigger contact behavior, which leaves only the most active/triggering contact with a synthesized profile in group rooms.

Scope:
- Group accepted writes by routed contact and subject contact.
- Identify contacts whose source memory count/quality now meets profile thresholds.
- Refresh profiles for each qualifying contact subject to cooldown and privacy policy.
- Make skip reasons visible for contacts who have activity but no profile yet.
acceptance_criteria:
- After group extraction, every contact with sufficient active source memories can receive or refresh a profile, not only the trigger contact.
- Profile synthesis uses memories attributed to the target contact and does not absorb facts belonging to other participants.
- Contacts with one memory or low-quality memories are skipped with explicit reason diagnostics.
- Cooldown behavior prevents profile refresh storms in active rooms.
- Tests cover multiple qualifying contacts, one qualifying/one non-qualifying contact, cross-attribution contamination, and cooldown skips.
close_reason: Implemented group-room profile coverage improvements: accepted writes now preserve sourceContactId and subjectContactId, profile refresh grouping considers routed contact plus subject contact instead of falling back to the trigger contact, room-scope-only writes remain excluded from contact profile refresh, profile synthesis returns structured refreshed/skipped results, and profile synthesis filters explicitly non-target source memories before threshold checks/prompt rendering to prevent cross-participant contamination. Added orchestration coverage for multiple routed group contacts and profile-synthesis coverage for insufficient source memories, cooldown skips, and non-target memory filtering. title: Add group-specific write caps and candidate ranking
description:
Summary:
Tune group-room write caps and ranking so high-volume rooms can produce enough memories without flooding L2.

Scope:
- Keep direct extraction max writes unchanged by default.
- Add group-specific caps: max writes per run, per contact, per chunk, per low-salience class, and per backlog catch-up run.
- Rank accepted candidates by importance, novelty, confidence, address mode, relationship relevance, emotional intensity, and per-contact coverage.
- Record skipped-by-cap counts and preserve enough backlog state to revisit high-value candidates when appropriate.
acceptance_criteria:
- Group write caps are configurable separately from `memoryExtractionMaxWrites` used by direct extraction.
- Config includes max writes per run, per chunk, per contact, per subject, per low-salience class, per backlog catch-up run, and per time window where applicable.
- A normal 50-100 message group fixture can write more than two total memories when enough salient facts exist, while respecting configured per-contact caps.
- Larger backlog/backfill fixtures prove caps scale by configured chunking/backfill policy rather than a hard-coded batch size.
- No single loud participant can consume all writes when other contacts have higher-priority qualifying facts.
- Low-salience facts remain tightly capped or skipped.
- `write_cap` telemetry reports skipped count, cap type, configured limit, and affected contacts/classes.
- Direct/1:1 tests prove the old default max-write behavior remains unchanged.
- Tests prove non-default cap config changes write selection without code changes.
- npm run verify:settings-contract passes if settings are added.
notes: Cap correction: group caps/ranking limits must be JSON-owned and velocity-aware; 500-message behavior belongs to backlog/backfill stress, not normal online extraction.

title: Implement structured source/subject attribution for group facts
description:
Summary:
Define and implement structured attribution for group-memory extraction outputs.

Problem:
Current mixed-speaker routing relies on the extracted fact text containing a clear speaker name or matching source content. Because the transcript already knows author IDs and names, group extraction should carry structured source evidence through the pipeline.

Scope:
- Extend the extraction prompt/schema or post-processing contract so each candidate fact references source message IDs and optional subject/target names.
- Resolve source speaker/contact from message IDs, not from LLM prose alone.
- Resolve subject/target contact when a fact is about someone other than the speaker.
- Classify address mode: direct_to_companion, mention_of_companion, reply_to_user, overheard_room_context, or system/api.
- Preserve trigger contact separately from source speaker and subject contact.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every group-extracted fact carries source message IDs or a source span sufficient to identify the speaker deterministically.
- Persisted memory provenance can distinguish trigger contact, source speaker/contact, subject/target contact, address mode, routing reason, and channel/message span.
- If the LLM emits a speaker name that conflicts with source message metadata, deterministic metadata wins or the fact is rejected with a specific reason.
- Facts about one participant mentioned by another are attributed without merging both people into one profile.
- No raw private transcript text is persisted solely for routing metadata.
- Tests cover source speaker, subject contact, direct mention, overheard context, reply chains if available, unresolved unknown speaker, and conflicting LLM attribution.
close_reason: Implemented structured group fact attribution: extraction prompt and transcript IDs now expose source IDs, parser accepts source message IDs/spans/source speaker/subject/address mode, routing resolves source and subject contacts from deterministic message metadata with conflict rejection, and memory provenance normalizes trigger/routed/source/subject/address/span fields without storing raw transcript text. title: Add group salience candidate selection
description:
Summary:
Add a group-specific candidate selection stage before fact extraction so high-volume rooms do not become memory spam.

Scope:

- Downrank casual chatter, memes without durable context, repeated jokes, acknowledgements, and low-information one-liners.

- Emit skip telemetry by reason.

- Candidate selection returns message IDs/spans plus salience reason codes, not just raw text snippets.
- Important events can be selected even if Carlini was not directly addressed.
- Chatter-heavy test fixtures produce low candidate counts without losing explicit preferences, boundaries, relationship claims, or companion mentions.
- Salience thresholds, reason weights, max candidate spans per chunk, neighboring-context size, and low-signal skip rules are JSON-configurable.
- Defaults may live only in settings/channel contracts; candidate selection logic consumes resolved config and does not hard-code channel policy numbers.
- Telemetry reports messages considered, candidate spans selected, and skip reasons.

title: Add observed group-room extraction scheduler
description:
Summary:
Schedule group-memory extraction from observed group-room traffic without causing replies.

Scope:
- Add an observed-message trigger path for channels classified as group/group-capable.
- Trigger on configurable message-count thresholds, time thresholds, direct mention/high-salience signals, and backlog lag.
- Use debounce/cooldown and one in-flight extraction per channel.
- Ensure observed extraction never enters the chat response path or emits Discord messages.
- Keep response-turn extraction available for direct conversations and direct mentions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Observed group-room messages can enqueue a memory extraction job without invoking the response model.
- Trigger reasons distinguish observed_count, observed_time, direct_mention, high_salience, backlog_lag, manual, and response_turn when applicable.
- Message-count thresholds, time thresholds, direct-mention behavior, salience trigger rules, cooldowns, debounce, backlog lag thresholds, and max in-flight behavior are JSON-configurable.
- Cooldowns prevent extraction storms in fast rooms while preserving backlog progress.
- Duplicate Discord notifications do not enqueue duplicate extraction jobs for the same source message/span.
- The trigger is disabled or conservative by default until settings/policy enable it per channel class or channel.
- Implementation code reads resolved config and does not hard-code operational trigger values outside the settings contract/defaults.
- Tests prove observed extraction does not send a reply, even when direct mention/high-salience extraction is scheduled, and prove non-default trigger config changes behavior.

notes: Trigger correction: count/time/backlog/cooldown thresholds must be JSON-owned and operator-tunable for channel velocity.

The scheduler resolves JSON-owned group-memory settings, classifies group/group-capable channels, plans bounded watermark ranges, triggers on configured observed count/time/direct mention/high salience/backlog lag, enforces in-flight/cooldown gates, and only advances the watermark after the extractor accepts processing. title: Add group-memory watermark and range reader
description:
Summary:
Add a group-memory watermark and bounded range reader so group extraction processes unprocessed spans rather than only the latest 10 conversational entries.

Problem:
Current response-turn extraction calls `getRecentMessages(channelId, 10)`, so high-volume group rooms drop most observed history between extraction turns. A separate group path needs durable progress tracking by channel/session and bounded chunking from the last processed message ID.

Scope:
- Store a group-memory high-water mark per channel/session and extraction policy version.
- Read message ranges from session storage/projection by message ID bounds.
- Chunk large ranges into bounded windows with small overlap for context continuity.
- Record processed spans, skipped spans, and failure/retry state.
- Keep direct extraction markers unchanged unless intentionally reused through a compatibility wrapper.
acceptance_criteria:
- Group extraction can select messages from `(lastGroupMemoryWatermark, currentHead]` without relying on `getRecentMessages(channelId, 10)`.
- Range reads preserve role, author ID, author name, timestamp, channel visibility, source message ID, and metadata needed for attribution.
- Chunking supports JSON-configurable max messages, max tokens, overlap, backlog catch-up limit, and retry behavior.
- Normal online chunk defaults are suitable for active channels, expected around 50-100 messages per processed batch unless operators tune them.
- Larger spans are split into multiple bounded chunks or deferred to backfill; the live scheduler never relies on an unconfigurable hundreds-of-messages batch.
- Watermark advancement happens only after a chunk/span is successfully processed or explicitly skipped with recorded reason.
- Failed spans are retryable and do not permanently mark unprocessed messages as processed.
- Direct/1:1 extraction marker behavior remains unchanged.
- Tests simulate configured 50-message and 100-message windows plus a larger backlog stress case, proving no messages are silently skipped due to tail sampling and configured limits are honored.
- npm run verify:settings-contract passes if settings are added.
notes: Window correction: normal online group windows should be configurable, not hard-coded; use 50-100ish defaults and split/backfill larger spans.
close_reason: Implemented group-memory watermark and bounded range planner with JSON watermark persistence, processed/skipped/failed span state, retry count tracking, configurable message/token chunking, overlap, max chunks per run, and deferred backlog metadata. Validation: npm test -- --run src/faculties/memory/extraction/group-ranges.test.ts src/faculties/memory/extraction/group-classifier.test.ts; npm run build; npm run lint.

title: Define direct/group/auto memory-mode contract
description:
Summary:
Define the canonical contract for direct, group, and auto memory modes before changing extraction behavior.

Context:
Group behavior should be determined primarily by channel topology and recent canonical participants, not only by all contacts ever seen in a channel. Operators also need a manual override for channels whose provider metadata or participant patterns are misleading.

Scope:
- Define `memoryMode: direct | group | auto` ownership in channel/settings config.
- Define provider topology rules: Discord DM/private 1:1 stays direct; Discord guild channel/thread is group-capable.
- Define recent participant rules for auto mode using distinct canonical human contacts in a rolling window.
- Exclude the companion, system users, API principals, and bots unless explicitly marked as AI companion/human-relevant.
- Define fallback behavior for group-capable channels with only one recent speaker.
- Document that group mode changes extraction windowing/attribution/caps, not reply behavior or privacy boundaries.
acceptance_criteria:
- The direct/group/auto memory-mode contract is documented in authoritative config/design surfaces, not only in code comments.
- Manual mode overrides auto detection and can force direct or group behavior per channel.
- Auto mode classifies Discord DMs as direct and Discord guild channels/threads as group-capable.
- Auto mode promotes to group behavior when recent distinct canonical human contacts in the rolling window is at least 2, with the rolling window size JSON-configurable.
- Historical `contact_channel_activity` can inform group-capable status but cannot by itself force every future extraction into high-volume group processing forever.
- The contract defines the JSON owner for every group-memory knob: mode, participant window, trigger thresholds, chunk sizes, overlap, cooldowns, backlog limits, salience thresholds, write caps, per-contact caps, profile refresh thresholds, telemetry visibility, and backfill limits.
- Defaults may exist only through the settings/channel contract and typed config loader; implementation code must consume resolved config and must not bury operational constants in extractor/scheduler logic.
- The contract explicitly states that group mode never causes observed messages to receive replies.
- Tests or contract checks cover DM, guild one-speaker, guild multi-speaker, bot/system/API-only, manual override, and non-default configured thresholds.
- npm run verify:settings-contract passes if settings are added.
notes: Config correction: direct/group/auto and every group-memory threshold/cap/window need canonical JSON ownership so Garden can expose them later.
close_reason: Implemented group memory direct/group/auto settings contract: settings.json groupMemory object, channels.json discord groupMemory overrides, Garden exposure, seed defaults, docs, and regression coverage. title: Implement group-room classifier and recent participant detector
description:
Summary:
Implement the channel classifier and recent participant detector used by `memoryMode:auto`.

title: Epic: Group-room memory extraction and attribution reliability
description:
Summary:
Build a group-room memory extraction path that preserves the current lightweight 1:1 behavior while making Discord-style multi-user rooms produce useful, attributable, privacy-safe memories and contact profiles.

Problem:
The current extractor is acceptable for 1:1 turns because it samples the recent conversational tail after a response turn and writes at most a small number of high-value facts. In group rooms this collapses: observed messages are recorded but do not trigger extraction, normal extraction samples only the latest 10 conversational entries, write caps remain tuned for direct chat, mixed-speaker facts are skipped unless the LLM text itself clearly names the source speaker, and profile refresh follows accepted writes rather than ensuring all qualifying room participants are covered. Carlini's live room showed 465 projected messages and 393 human messages across 4 speakers, but only 27 total memories / 18 active memories and one synthesized profile.

Design intent:
- Direct/1:1 behavior must remain stable and cheap.
- Group rooms use a separate memory mode with explicit classification, watermarks, bounded range processing, stronger attribution, conservative salience gates, per-contact write caps, and operator-visible diagnostics.
- Observed group traffic may trigger memory extraction, but must never trigger a chat reply.
- Group memory should remember important room events, preferences, relationships, boundary/safety facts, mentions of the companion, and meaningful social dynamics; it must not turn every casual message into L2 memory.
- The extraction contract must preserve who spoke, who the fact is about, whether the companion was directly addressed/mentioned/overhearing, and which message span produced the evidence.

Out of scope:
- Autonomous relationship or trust mutation. This epic provides better evidence for that later system.
- Remembering every message.
- Relaxing cross-contact memory/privacy boundaries.
- Replacing 1:1 extraction with the group pipeline.
acceptance_criteria:
- A group-room memory mode exists separately from direct/1:1 extraction and does not regress 1:1 extraction cadence, prompt size, or write caps.
- All group-memory operational knobs live in canonical JSON-owned config, not buried literals: mode, participant window, message/time trigger thresholds, chunk sizes, overlap, cooldowns, backlog limits, salience thresholds, write caps, per-contact caps, and backfill limits.
- JSON-owned defaults are wired through the settings/channel contract so a Garden config page can expose them later without changing code.
- Channel memory mode can be manual (`direct`, `group`, `auto`) and auto mode uses provider topology plus recent canonical participant count.
- Normal online group extraction processes configurable bounded windows sized for channel velocity, with expected defaults in the 50-100 message range unless operators tune them.
- Large historical spans are handled by bounded backfill/stress processing, not by forcing the live hot path to consume hundreds of messages in one batch.
- Group extraction processes message ranges since a group-memory watermark instead of only the latest 10 entries.
- Observed group-room messages can schedule extraction without sending a response or changing Discord egress behavior.
- Group extraction records structured attribution for source speaker/contact, subject/target contact when known, trigger contact when applicable, address mode, and message span.
- Group extraction uses stricter salience filtering and per-contact/per-run caps so high-volume rooms produce useful memories without spam.
- Mixed-speaker facts are routed from structured message metadata rather than requiring the LLM to include speaker names in prose.
- Contact profile synthesis refreshes every qualifying participant after group extraction, not only the response-turn trigger contact.
- Garden/operator diagnostics show observed count, processed count, watermark lag, candidate count, parsed facts, accepted writes, rejection reasons, write-cap skips, ambiguous attribution skips, and per-contact coverage.
- Tests include normal 50-100 message multi-user fixtures plus larger backlog/backfill stress fixtures proving important facts are remembered, chatter is skipped, attribution is correct, direct/1:1 behavior is unchanged, and configured values are honored.
- npm run verify:settings-contract passes if settings are added.
- npm run lint and targeted memory/Discord/settings tests pass before implementation beads close.
notes: User correction 2026-06-28: live group extraction should not imply hard-coded 500-message batches. Normal online windows should be configurable and likely around 50-100 messages depending channel velocity; all thresholds/caps/windows must be JSON-owned for later Garden configuration.
close_reason: Completed group-room memory extraction and attribution reliability epic. Landed separate group classification/range/watermark processing, JSON-owned config and channel overrides, observed group scheduling without Discord egress, group salience candidate selection, structured source/subject/scope routing, group write caps/ranking, contact-coverage profile refresh, Garden diagnostics, safe bounded backfill, conformance fixtures, and operations documentation. Normal online windows are JSON-configurable and covered at 50 and 100 messages; larger 500-message history is covered only through bounded/resumable backfill. Direct/1:1 extraction cadence and default max-write behavior are covered unchanged. Validation across child beads included npm test -- --run src/faculties/memory/extraction/group-conformance.test.ts src/faculties/memory/extraction/speaker-routing.test.ts src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.test.ts src/faculties/memory/extraction/group-ranges.test.ts src/faculties/memory/extraction/group-salience.test.ts src/faculties/memory/extraction/group-write-caps.test.ts src/faculties/memory/extraction/group-backfill.test.ts src/faculties/memory/extraction/group-observed-scheduler.test.ts src/app/agent/gateway-message-handlers.test.ts; Garden diagnostics/API tests; settings/channel contract tests; npm run verify:settings-contract; npm run build; npm run lint.

title: Debug Carlini k3s response prefix artifacts
description:
Summary: Carlini on the remote K3s deployment is returning visible template artifacts, including the literal prefix <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜># Carlini's Response, instead of a clean assistant response.

Scope:
- Inspect the remote Carlini/K3s deployment state, pods, services, logs, and active model/provider configuration without making ad hoc off-repo runtime changes.
- Trace the repo-owned LLM request/streaming/client path that could preserve prompt echo, BOS tokens, or response header template text.
- Identify whether the artifact is caused by model chat template configuration, completion-vs-chat endpoint usage, LiteLLM/provider settings, prompt construction, or stream/text post-processing.
- Implement any required fix in repo-owned code or deployment artifacts only, with targeted tests.

Observed example:
<｜begin▁of▁sentence｜># Carlini's Response

Acceptance:
- The source of the visible BOS/response-header artifact is identified from code/config/log evidence.
- Carlini responses no longer surface <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜> or # Carlini's Response to the user.
