title: Decide encrypted backup handling for deployment env and service registration
description:
Summary:
Current scheduled backups do not capture .env, generated deployment/systemd/psfn.env, or live /etc/systemd/system registration artifacts. This is partially intentional: deployment env files can contain long-lived provider/API/admin secrets, and deployment/systemd/.gitignore excludes psfn.env. Systemd unit source is repo-owned where possible, while live registrations may be external thin pointers or copied unit files depending on host constraints.

Evidence:
- deployment/systemd/.gitignore excludes *.env, psfn.env, and psfn.env.*.
- scripts/system/install-psfn-service.sh writes a generated env file, copies non-layout .env entries into it, chmods it 0640, and filters only runtime layout/wiring keys.
- scripts/system/psfn.service.template is repo-owned, but the registered unit path defaults to /etc/systemd/system/psfn.service.
- AGENTS.md forbids hidden off-repo runtime authority and says repo files under deployment/systemd are the source for service definitions when possible.

Decision needed:
Pick a restore-safe strategy for secret-bearing deployment env and service registration state before adding it to any broad backup path. Options include encrypted backup material, sealed/externally managed secret restore runbooks, or explicitly documented operator-managed rehydration.

Files likely involved after decision:
- scripts/system/install-psfn-service.sh
- deployment/systemd/.gitignore
- deployment/systemd service templates or docs
- src/persistence/backups/* only if encrypted capture is selected
- docs/operations.md
acceptance_criteria:
- Operator-approved policy states whether deployment env files are backed up encrypted, restored from an external secret manager, or intentionally excluded with a tested manual restore runbook.
- No unencrypted provider, API, admin, Discord, Telegram, gateway HMAC, database password, or webhook secrets are stored in broad scheduled backups.
- Systemd registration artifacts are classified as repo-owned source, generated thin pointer, or host-specific external state, with restore steps for each class.
- If encrypted capture is selected, tests prove plaintext env files are never written into the normal backup tree or manifests.
- docs/operations.md documents the chosen env/systemd restore procedure and its validation command.
close_reason: Resolved and implemented encrypted scheduled backups. backup.json now requires encryption.mode=required with an env key reference; runtime resolution fails closed when the key env is missing. Scheduled backup cycles stage plaintext under a temporary directory, verify restore/manifests there, package the snapshot as snapshot.tar.gz.enc with AES-256-GCM/scrypt, retain only encrypted-backup.json plus encrypted payload, remove plaintext staging, and mirror only the encrypted package. scripts/verify-backup-restore decrypts encrypted sets before running existing restore checks. No plaintext provider/channel/admin env secret is captured through system-config snapshots; memory/chat/database content is encrypted at rest. Validation passed: npm test -- --run src/persistence/backups/service.test.ts src/persistence/backups/config.test.ts src/operator/garden/services/settings-service.test.ts src/app/agent/startup-context.test.ts; npm run verify:settings-contract; npm run verify:backup-restore; npm run build; npm run lint.

title: Kube shakedown: Artie test deployment and Pi rollout checklist
description:
Summary:
Create and run the Kubernetes shakedown path before any live Pi cutover. The goal is to prove the Helm chart and transport contracts on a test deployment first, using the Artie/psfn-shakedown fixture when available, and only then plan a low-risk Pi rollout.

Context:

Scope:

- Define a test namespace/values file that does not point at live Purrsephone runtime roots or live DB credentials.
- Install/render chart into a local/test k3s environment when available on this machine, or document the exact blocked prerequisite.
- Run smoke checks for gateway API, Garden UI health, agent startup/network isolation, Postgres+pgvector readiness, Redis readiness, and satellite hub basic reachability.

title: [epic] Kubernetes/k3s preflight and Helm migration prep
description:
Summary:
Coordinate the PSFN Kubernetes/k3s preparation wave. The target is a greenfield-capable Helm deployment that can run the current one-system/one-companion PSFN topology on the Pi/k3s path without breaking the live Purrsephone deployment during preparation.

Target topology:
- gateway pod: public/OpenAI-compatible API, channel adapters, LLM/embedding clients, privileged egress, RPC server for the agent edge.
- agent pod: companion loop and memory/session/contact/intention ownership, Postgres access, no broad outbound internet, admin transport server for Garden.
- garden pod: Garden SPA/operator surface, browser ingress, proxies admin API/events to the agent admin transport.
- satellite-hub pod: device/websocket ingress on hub port, calls gateway HTTP API.
- stateful services: Postgres + pgvector and Redis for greenfield installs, with values for external Postgres/Redis later where appropriate.

Operator decisions captured 2026-06-27:
- One umbrella epic owns Kubernetes prep.
- Helm chart is a dedicated child bead.
- Internal Unix-socket edges get separate network transport beads per edge.
- Auth/cert work is separate from each network transport implementation.
- First cert target is cert-manager with a self-signed cluster CA and internal workload certificates.
- SQLite full removal is not a kube prerequisite, but active runtime use of SQLite instead of Postgres must be fixed.
- Backup work should be validated against current code/commits and stale backup beads closed if already satisfied.
- Redis's first app-layer value is prompt caching. Later channel caches are future work.
- Helm should bundle Postgres + pgvector for zero-to-working installs and also allow external Postgres configuration.
- v1 secrets use native Kubernetes Secrets, not ESO/Vault/1Password.
- Embeddings keep today's behavior: local Transformers by default with an API-backed embedding option.
- End target is Pi/k3s. Testing may use this machine and the Artie/psfn-shakedown fixture at /mnt/c/Temp/PSFN-TEST when available.

Non-goals:
- Do not move owner-file settings into Postgres in this wave.
- Do not make agent HA or multi-writer against one companion-data PVC.
- Do not cut over the live Pi until chart smoke tests and backup validation are done.
- Do not add off-repo authoritative runtime config to work around chart gaps.

Acceptance:
- Child beads cover: gateway RPC WSS transport, gateway RPC mTLS/SPIFFE auth, Garden admin TCP/WS transport, Garden admin mTLS/SPIFFE auth, cert-manager/internal cert chart contract, Helm chart, native Kubernetes Secret contract, Redis prompt cache app wiring, active SQLite/Postgres audit, backup validation/closure, embeddings/model-cache chart wiring, Pi shakedown/rollout plan, and optional Node 24/PQC probe.
- Dependencies make the Helm chart wait on the transport/auth/config contracts it renders.
- Dependencies make Pi rollout wait on Helm render/smoke and backup validation.
- Every code-changing child bead requires npm run lint before closure.
- The final wave handoff lists which beads are implementation-complete, which are chart-only, which are validation-only, and which remain deferred.

title: Preserve WORKSPACE_PATH in production systemd installs
description:
Summary: The 2026-06-27 Pi live restore showed that the production launcher now correctly fails closed when WORKSPACE_PATH is missing, but scripts/system/install-psfn-service.sh filters WORKSPACE_PATH out of the source env file while scripts/system/psfn.service.template does not inject a replacement. A future reinstall can therefore regenerate deployment/systemd/psfn.env without WORKSPACE_PATH and make psfn.service fail at startup.

Observed live evidence:
- psfn.service failed after updating to 5204b769 with: Production runtime requires WORKSPACE_PATH: production personal files root must be explicit.
- /home/psfn/psfn-framework-source/.env contained WORKSPACE_PATH=/home/psfn/psfn-framework-source/purrsephone.
- deployment/systemd/psfn.env did not contain WORKSPACE_PATH because the service skips dotenv and reads only the service env file.
- Manually adding WORKSPACE_PATH to deployment/systemd/psfn.env restored startup.

Scope:
- Update the production service installer/template so WORKSPACE_PATH is explicitly preserved or rendered into the repo-owned service env/unit.
- Keep the live-boundary rule: /etc/systemd/system/psfn.service should be only a symlink/pointer to the repo-owned rendered unit. The Pi currently has a regular /etc/systemd/system/psfn.service shadowing the enabled symlink target, so the reinstall path should repair that.
- Add or update tests around install-psfn-service env filtering/rendering so WORKSPACE_PATH cannot be dropped.

Acceptance:
- A dry-run/rendered install includes an explicit WORKSPACE_PATH appropriate for production.
- Reinstalling the Pi service cannot remove the personal workspace path from startup env.
- The installed unit path is aligned with docs/operations.md: /etc/systemd/system/psfn.service links to the repo-owned deployment/systemd/psfn.service.
- npm run lint passes before closure.

title: Canonical cost accounting: reconcile capture, attribution, charge economics, and historical analytics
description: Summary: Repair and unify PSFN's mostly-built accounting stack so operators can trust current and historical cost. The necessary primitives already exist: LLM clients expose input/output/cache-read/cache-write usage, provider or estimated cost; Postgres model_usage_events persists many dimensions; charge events carry lane/surface/run lineage; Garden has dashboard and Charge/Budget surfaces. The gaps are correctness and product integration. Current dashboard cost windows are in-memory agent.turn.usage samples, so they reset or miss cross-process events and do not reliably update from the durable model-usage store. Query filters omit useful stored dimensions such as channel, call type/purpose, charge lane/surface and process. Breakdowns omit cache token/cost detail. UI supports only Today/Week/Month in limited summaries, with no quarter/year/custom ranges, bucketed graphs, sorting, or channel splits. Charge units are not reconciled to actual/estimated dollars for operator accounting. Scope: make one canonical durable usage record and deterministic provider-versus-estimate precedence; capture read/cache-read/cache-write/output tokens and their monetary components where providers expose them; reconcile retries/attempts; add typed attribution dimensions; query/filter/group by companion, channel, provider/model, call kind/type/purpose/origin, tool, process/service, charge lane/surface/run lineage, shard/subagent/conversation correlation, status and cost source; replace dashboard in-memory cost truth with persisted queries plus reliable refresh/invalidation; add day/week/month/quarter/year/all/custom windows and bucketed time series; join charge and model usage by correlation to show operator-only dollar cost per lane/surface/run/charge unit and coverage/unattributed amounts; add accessible graphs, sortable/filterable tables, drill-down and export; migrate/backfill safely; certify against provider fixtures and live samples. Why: scoped ICP dollar breakers, budgeting, optimization and operator decisions are unsafe while capture and attribution are iffy. Non-goals: exposing monetary prices in companion prompts, assigning dollars as the behavioral meaning of charge, inventing a second usage ledger, changing companion autonomy policy, or applying ICP social limits to shards. Key files: src/primitives/llm/client.ts and model-budget.ts; src/boundary/gateway/llm-cost-capture.ts; src/shared/telemetry/model-usage.ts, run-charge.ts and charge-ledger.ts; src/persistence/postgres/model-usage-store.ts and migrations.ts; src/operator/garden/services/dashboard-service.ts, dashboard-cost-windows.ts, model-usage-service.ts, charge-ledger-service.ts and routes; admin-ui dashboard and charge-budget pages.
design: Postgres model_usage_events (or its deliberately evolved canonical successor) is durable operator accounting truth. Dashboard and analytics query it rather than maintaining an independent in-memory month buffer. Keep provider-reported and estimated costs side by side with one explicit effective-cost rule and coverage metadata. Treat charge as behavioral units; compute dollar mapping as an operator analytical join by shared correlation, never by silently pricing charge for the companion. Pre-aggregate only after raw immutable events are correct and retain drill-down. Use one typed query/aggregation contract for dashboard, Charge/Budget, exports and future ICP scoped budgets.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads close with evidence; every production model call records correct input, output, cache-read, cache-write, total tokens and provider/estimated/effective cost with attempt semantics; durable totals reconcile to provider fixtures and survive restart/process boundaries; attribution supports channel and all declared dimensions with explicit unknown/unattributed buckets; main dashboard updates from persisted usage and reflects new calls without restart; APIs/UI provide week, month, quarter, year, all/custom ranges, appropriate time buckets, graphs, sorting, filtering and drill-down; charge-to-dollar operator views show cost by lane/surface/run and cost per charge unit with coverage and no double counting while companion prompts remain monetary-free; migrations/backfill are safe; targeted tests, Postgres integration, Garden tests, lint, build, settings-contract if touched, repository hygiene and production-shape smoke pass.
notes: 2026-07-12 operator clarification: most accounting parts exist but are not working coherently. Concrete symptoms: main dashboard cost estimates do not update reliably; attribution is uncertain; read/cache-read/cache-write visibility is insufficient; no per-channel split; no week/month/quarter/year/custom graphs and sorting; and no operator accounting map from behavioral charge to monetary cost. Implement as reconciliation/storage/query/presentation repair, not greenfield replacement.

All accepted-scope children are closed: cam.1 capture and immutable attempt economics; cam.2 typed attribution and tenant-scoped queries; cam.3 durable live dashboard projection; cam.4 calendar/custom analytics, groups, sorting and export; cam.5 charge-to-dollar operator reconciliation with conservation; 574y unified accessible dashboard/Charge-Budget UX; and cam.6 safe migration/backfill plus end-to-end certification. CAM.6 completed the final implementation/review/remediation/final-regression gate: targeted real-Postgres migration 1/1, accounting certification 9/9, npm run lint, and ESM+DTS build all passed at the branch head; the exact-image provider-disabled local Artemis smoke previously passed API/dashboard/export/conservation and tenant-denial checks without external provider spend. Every feature checkpoint and remediation is committed and pushed. This closes the feature epic on its feature branch; it does not claim merge to main. title: Image pipeline: diagnose ~50% Discord failure rate and broken retry/failover
description:
Operator issue (2026-06-26 ramble list, section 1).

Problem: Roughly 50/50 failure rate on image generation requests sent through Discord. Symptoms vary (timeouts, malformed/missing responses) and do not point to one clear cause. Using fast capable vision endpoints (Gemini, GPT Mini) so model choice is not the bottleneck.

Confirmed structural context: retry/failover logic EXISTS (src/primitives/llm/retry.ts, retry-config.ts, fallback.ts, error-classify.ts; image-side in src/primitives/images/{tools,service,fal,comfyui}.ts). The intended policy is two tries then fail over to the other model for two more tries. It does not appear to be firing correctly, or is not firing at all. Possible Pi resource constraint (unclear if still inconsistent under load even after disabling other heavy processes like old satellite vision testing). Image viewer caching (uploaded image stays in context on reference) is working.

Scope:
- Trace the actual failure path: instrument or log which model responded, attempt count, whether fallback engaged, latency, and the specific error class (use error-classify.ts).
- Determine why retry/failover is not firing: is the fallback trigger condition wrong, is an exception swallowed before retry, is the image path bypassing the shared retry logic?
- Rule in/out the Pi resource-constraint hypothesis (memory/CPU under concurrent load).

title: Discord: consolidate queued inbound messages into one response when chain is busy
description:
Operator-flagged MOST PRESSING issue (2026-06-26 ramble list, section 3).

Problem: Inconsistent Discord response behavior: sometimes no response; sometimes 2-3 queued user messages get answered all at once, OUT OF ORDER; sometimes one message gets TWO separate replies that read like independent responses to the same original message.

Root cause suspicion (confirmed structural): Discord inbound buffering exists (src/channels/discord/adapter.ts has lockContention, queueDepth, and a TurnContentionPolicy of "steer" vs "queue", with a comment "contended messages for the agent-side queue to bundle or process"). The FIFO buffer is conceptually reasonable but flawed in practice: when the main operational chain is busy and multiple messages queue up, the system processes them INDIVIDUALLY rather than as a batch, producing overlapping/disjointed reply chains once it catches up.

Fix: while the upstream chain is busy, buffer incoming messages as a queue, but when ready, emit ONE consolidated response covering the buffered messages — not one reply per queued message. This keeps conversation coherent instead of scattering replies.

Scope:
- In src/channels/discord/adapter.ts (and voice-turn-runtime.ts if relevant), change the contended/queued path to coalesce pending messages into a single agent turn with a single consolidated reply, rather than draining the queue one-message-one-reply.
- Preserve message provenance/ordering metadata so the consolidated turn sees all queued messages in order.
- Add telemetry for queue depth, coalesce events, and any out-of-order/double-reply regressions.
- Tests covering: single message (unchanged), 2-3 rapid messages during contention (one consolidated reply), recovery after drain.

Validation: npm run lint; targeted discord adapter tests; manual smoke (npm run smoke:chat or live Discord).

Priority: P1 (most pressing per operator).
notes: 2026-06-26 live-bug pass: implemented Discord gateway queue coalescing. When a channel has multiple contended queued messages, adapter now drains the pending queue into one deferred substrate turn (ordered content joined with newlines, attachments preserved, reply flags unioned) and emits contention phase=coalesced telemetry plus log message IDs. Validation: npm test -- --run src/channels/discord/adapter.test.ts; npm run lint; npm run build.
close_reason: Implemented Discord queued-message coalescing with telemetry; validated targeted adapter tests, lint, and build.

title: Fix verify:repository-hygiene: skip submodule gitlinks in public-sanitize-check
description:
From the 2026-06-26 pi/GLM review (working_docs/pi_glm_review_626.md, finding F-1).

Problem: scripts/public-sanitize-check.mjs iterates git ls-files and calls readFileSync on every entry whose extension is not in BINARY_EXTENSIONS. The vendor/emosim entry is a git submodule (gitlink, mode 160000, https://github.com/FoxEngine-ai/emo_sim) and is currently only used from eval/; the live env in this checkout is not set up to clone submodules. readFileSync on a directory throws EISDIR. This is the FIRST step of npm run verify:repository-hygiene, so the entire mandatory gate (public-sanitize then identity-literals then dependency-cycles) is un-runnable on any checkout that has a submodule registered. AGENTS.md mandates this gate for repo-surface changes, so it is silently unavailable exactly where required.

Scope:
- Make the scanner skip gitlink entries. Either filter `git ls-files --stage` to drop mode 160000 entries, or stat() each path and skip directories. Prefer the gitlink filter so intent is explicit rather than filesystem-state dependent.
- Confirm emosim is eval-only today so skipping is acceptable; re-evaluate if non-eval use appears later.
- Re-run npm run verify:repository-hygiene and confirm it completes (identity-literals + dependency-cycles must now execute).

Validation: npm run verify:repository-hygiene passes; a unit test for the scanner covering a gitlink/submodule entry.

Priority: P1 (blocks a mandatory gate).
close_reason: Completed: public-sanitize now reads git ls-files --stage and skips mode 160000 gitlinks; added gitlink parser regression. Validation: npm test -- --run src/app/maintenance/script-verification/public-sanitize-check.test.ts; npm run verify:repository-hygiene; npm run lint.

title: PWA Companion Cockpit — mobile-first companion chat with presence & activity telemetry
description:
## Vision

A mobile-first PWA **satellite client** — the companion's cockpit. Discord is a transport; this is the primary relational + observability embodiment on the operator's phone.

Core problem: silence is ambiguous. When she is working (orienting, using tools, waiting on approvals), the surface must show presence and operational state so the user never wonders whether she disconnected, stalled, or failed.

## Charter law that governs this epic (non-negotiable)

This epic is a **Satellite** implementation. Charter citations are law, not guidance:

- **§6.10 / §6.9 Satellites are embodiments, not minds.** The cockpit is an emanation node of the one core companion. It is NOT a separate mind, NOT an independent identity holder, does NOT own canonical memory. One deployment = one companion (Law 1, §1).
- **§6.10 Single active emanation invariant ("constitutional UX invariant").** Only one satellite is the primary embodied emanation at a time. Presence/emanation handoff is first-class; the cockpit must reflect, not assume, primary-emanation state. (Embodiment handoff occurs when presence moves, not merely when another channel speaks — cross-channel text input may still route into the same core conversation.)
- **§6.19 / §11.4 Cross-channel continuity.** The cockpit is NOT a disposable session silo. The same core conversation continues across Discord / Telegram / admin / API / this surface via `CrossChannelContinuityPort`. Trust/privacy/embodiment context still applies per channel.
- **Law 5 / §6.6 Event bus is the integration + observability spine.** Turn lifecycle, tool lifecycle, and audit/debug events already belong on the bus. The cockpit's event stream is a **typed, operational-state-only projection of the event bus**, NOT a parallel stream invented for the UI.
- **Law 21 / §9.2 Gateway is the sole privileged external edge.** The companion client API is a **channel adapter behind the gateway** (`ChannelAdapterPort` / `SatelliteAdapterPort`, §11.4). "Gateway or it does not ship."
- **§8.3 / §8.6 Operational state only.** Never raw chain-of-thought, never fabricated companion speech/emotion/belief (Law 17). The UI shows operational phases, tool operation classes, elapsed time, connection — never internal reasoning. Redaction is a projection filter at the emission boundary.
- **§8.5 / §12.3 / §12.6 No fake healthy state, no mock fallbacks, no silent failures.** **THERE IS NO BOOTSTRAP BRIDGE TO THE ADMIN SURFACE.** Earlier scaffold attempt did exactly this and was removed as a charter violation. If the companion API is unavailable, the cockpit fails honestly (§8.5), it does not paper over with a different surface.
- **§12.2 No dead wiring.** Every piece must be wired to a real entrypoint/port, or deleted.
- **§9.6 / §9.7 Auditability + debuggability.** What the runtime is doing must be observable.

## Architectural placement (Charter layer model, §5)

The cockpit spans canonical layers:
- Layer 7 (Channels/embodiments): the PWA client itself, a satellite embodiment
- Layer 4 (Event bus): source of all operational events (projection only)
- Layer 2 (Gateway): the companion client API lives here as a channel adapter
- Layer 9 (Garden/operator surfaces): Garden remains the privileged admin surface; the cockpit is relational, NOT admin

## Dependency order (this is the order work happens — no skipping)

`6ze` (event protocol: bus projection + redaction) → unblocks `q0k` (gateway channel adapter API) → `e2b` (bus emission into the projection) → `cxw` (satellite PWA skeleton, on real API only) → then `4v7` (presence), `h1p` (tool drawer), `cni` (approvals), `dlw` (artifacts, Phase 1.5).

Observer/presence-first. Approvals are the ONLY Phase 1 control action. Broader control (cancel/retry/pause/restart) is DEFERRED until presence loop is proven AND a deliberate security decision is made (§9.4 autonomy boundaries).

## Deferred (future beads, NOT this epic)

Push notifications; avatar/voice on client; native Android (TWA only after PWA stabilizes); broader control actions.

## Epic-level acceptance criteria (charter-grounded)

- Installable PWA satellite renders companion chat with live presence/activity derived from a real bus projection.
- Telemetry richer than any transport channel: connected / phase / operation-class / elapsed / input-expected / failed, always visible.
- **Operational-state-only boundary enforced with tests** — no chain-of-thought, no fabricated companion state (§8.3, Law 17).
- Cross-channel continuity preserved (§6.19) — same core conversation, not a session silo.
- Single-emanation invariant respected (§6.10).
- No bootstrap bridges, no mock fallbacks, no fake healthy state (§8.5, §12.3).
- Approvals honored through gateway + capability path, fail-closed (§9.2, §9.4).
- Every sub-bead: `npm run lint` passes + targeted tests pass before close (AGENTS validation expectations). No dead wiring (§12.2).
close_reason: Completed companion-ui implementation wave: protocol mirror, hub websocket client, stream store, standalone mobile PWA, presence strip, redacted activity drawer, fail-closed approvals, and fail-closed artifact shelf landed with companion-ui npm test/typecheck/lint/build passing. Real approval and artifact hub protocol support is tracked separately in psfn-framework-qa4 and psfn-framework-3eh.

title: PWA Companion Cockpit — mobile-first companion chat with presence & activity telemetry
description:
## Vision

A new mobile-first PWA companion client — her cockpit, not an admin surface. Discord is treated as a transport; this UI is the primary relational + observability surface. Goal: feel more alive and interactive than Discord chat, and surface richer telemetry than a chat transport can.

The core problem to solve: silence is ambiguous. When she is working (orienting, using tools, waiting on approvals, running commands), the interface must show presence and operational state so the user never wonders whether she disconnected, stalled, or failed.

## Design boundary (critical)

This is NOT "Garden but on your phone." Admin/Garden remains admin (privileged repo/identity/prompt/system mutation). The companion UI is relational and deliberately narrow:

- Safe chat in, rich state out.
- Stream OPERATIONAL STATE only. Never raw chain-of-thought or private model reasoning.
- Redacted tool visibility (operation class + sanitized args/results), not full traces.
- Explicit approvals surfaced as cards; capability tiers and gateway isolation respected, fail-closed.
- Read-mostly status. The runtime orchestrates; the UI surfaces state. Do NOT split her agency between the agent loop and a web controller.

The first client is observer/presence-first, with approvals as the initial control surface. Broader control actions (cancel/retry/pause/restart runtime) are explicitly DEFERRED until the presence loop is proven and a deliberate security decision is made.

## Architecture (reuse existing seams)

PSFN already has the pieces:
- OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions with SSE streaming (src/channels/api/)
- WebSocket voice primitives (src/channels/api/voice-websocket*)
- Channel adapter architecture (src/channels/{api,backplane,discord,telegram}) — companion is a new channel
- Agent loop (src/core/agent/, src/app/agent/)
- Tool registry/execution (src/core/tools/)
- Gateway/agent split with privileged ops behind gateway (src/app/{agent,gateway}/, src/boundary/gateway/)
- Capability tiers + confirmation + audit (src/boundary/sandbox/capabilities/, src/boundary/gateway/)
- Turn/session observability already collected (src/operator/garden/services/session-turn-observability.ts, audit-event-collector.ts) — reuse seam for event emission

Missing piece = (a) a companion turn/activity event protocol, (b) a narrow companion client API, (c) agent-loop emission into that stream, (d) the PWA client itself.

## Event taxonomy (target)

turn.started, assistant.token, assistant.status, tool.started, tool.progress, tool.completed, tool.failed, approval.requested, artifact.created, turn.completed, turn.failed

## MVP scope (Phase 1)

1. Event protocol + type contracts (sub-bead)
2. Companion client API + security boundary, new gateway channel (sub-bead)
3. Agent-loop emission into companion event stream (sub-bead)
4. PWA client skeleton: chat via existing SSE, connection status, session/channel picker, installable on Android (sub-bead)
5. Activity strip + presence ("never disappear": phase, operation class, elapsed, input-expected, failure) (sub-bead) — flagship
6. Expandable tool drawer, redacted traces (sub-bead)
7. Approval cards for dangerous actions (sub-bead)
8. Artifact/attachment shelf (Phase 1.5, sequenced later) (sub-bead)

## Deferred (not in this epic; future beads)

- Push notifications
- Avatar / voice on the client (reuse existing voice WS later)
- Native Android (TWA only after PWA stabilizes; native only if deeper OS integration required)
- Broader control actions: cancel, retry, pause tools, restart runtime (needs security decision first)

## Open question to resolve before Phase 1 control scope expands

Observer-first (chat + status only) vs immediate control actions? Default for this epic: observer-first + approvals only. Revisit after the presence loop ships.

## Acceptance (epic-level)

- Installable PWA on Android renders companion chat with live presence/activity.
- Telemetry richer than Discord: user can always see connected/phase/operation/elapsed/input-expected/failed.
- Operational-state-only boundary enforced (no chain-of-thought leakage) with tests.
- Approvals honored through capability tiers + gateway, fail-closed.
- npm run lint + build + targeted tests pass for every sub-bead.

description: SPEC_MEMORY_PROJECTION_LAYER §5; revives deferred PSFN-cyzi. title: [epic] Front-mind / subconscious split: long-running tools offload to background workers so chat never blocks
description:
Operator direction (2026-06-11): she has no human limit on multitasking, so nothing long-running should hold the conversational front hostage. Today every tool call blocks the turn (executeToolCallsWithScheduler is strictly synchronous), so a selfie (20s-3min via the tiered edit chain) or an analysis-workbench run (up to 5min wall budget) means she cannot speak — and inbound messages used to drop (fixed: discord queue+bundle, psfn-framework-0sb).

Target behavior: long tools auto-route through a background worker. The turn gets an immediate ack ('working on it'), the agent goes idle, conversation continues (discord queue keeps feeding her). When the work completes — success OR failure, both return — the result re-enters HER context (never the chat directly, never as partner speech) and she surfaces it in her own voice: 'oh, here you go' with the selfie attached.

The rails already exist; this epic wires tool-level policy onto them:
- tool_handoff.continue deferred action kind + buildDeferredToolHandoffMessage (system:tool_handoff authorship) — src/core/agent/deferred-tool-handoff.ts
- BackgroundCompletionDeliveryQueue + queueBackgroundContinuationCompletion + completion-notification policy — src/core/agent/substrate-agent/background-continuation-runtime.ts, background-completion-policy.ts
- SubagentFaculty.spawn() non-blocking on SUBAGENT_WORKER_LANE; ShardManager with charge lanes + ArtifactReturnBatch for media — src/faculties/subagents/, src/faculties/shards/manager.ts
- ToolConcurrencyMeta on wiring metadata (class/exclusivity/interruptibility/eligibility) is the natural carrier for an executionProfile field — src/core/agent/tool-wiring-validator.ts

Constraints (standing): results re-enter via system-authored follow-up (authorship guard), charging nests in runWithChargeContext, fail closed (an offloaded failure must produce a visible unsuccessful result in her context, never vanish), kidney-vs-heart (the offload WORKER is mechanical; her narration of the result is hers).

Related: unprompted selfies as proactive outreach ride 1xb.2/1xb.3 once delivery exists — the offload runtime gives intention-driven media a non-blocking execution path.
acceptance_criteria: She can chat continuously while a selfie or workbench run cooks; result (or failure) re-enters her context and she presents it herself; no tool call on the offload profile ever blocks the conversational front; charge/telemetry parity with sync execution.

title: Discord inbound queue: never drop, bundle messages that arrive mid-turn
description: Operator requirement (2026-06-11): no Discord message may ever be ignored. The qdp fix (hold-for-idle + 3 bounded retries) still drops on retry exhaustion and replies per-message. Required behavior: messages that land while a turn is in flight are queued per channel; when the agent goes idle they are bundled (same author + channel) into ONE turn so she sees everything that was said and responds once. The operator observed that when a message is dropped and he references it later, she has no idea what he's talking about — every inbound message must end up recorded in session context. Busy-wait becomes unbounded (loud warn per retry) — a genuinely wedged agent surfaces in logs, not as silent message loss. Different authors in the same channel must NOT be bundled into one user message (authorship/trust attribution).
acceptance_criteria: Burst of N same-author messages during a busy turn produces one bundled turn containing all contents/attachments and one reply; no path drops a message silently; different-author messages become separate turns; dedupe still works; regression tests cover bundling, unbounded busy-wait, author split.
close_reason: Fixed in 238e07ce. Discord prompt messages now flow through a per-channel-aware FIFO queue with a single pump: bursts arriving mid-turn bundle (same channel+author, contiguous) into one turn with merged content+attachments and one reply; different authors stay separate turns. Busy-wait is unbounded with a warn per retry — no drop path remains; every message reaches handleMessage and is recorded in session context. Audit event discord.message.bundled added. 12 handler tests including bundling burst, unbounded busy-wait, author split, dedupe, observe-mode. Live verification: journal should show 'Bundling discord messages...' on double-texting during slow turns and zero 'Error handling message ... already processing'.

title: Discord messages silently dropped when they arrive during an in-flight agent turn
description:
The sprint-9 watch item recurred and is broader than the vision-fallback race. Overnight 2026-06-11 (03:41–03:53 UTC), three real operator messages on the primary Discord channel (1313001762793197678) errored with 'Agent is already processing a prompt' while a slow chat turn (z-ai/glm-5.1, >60s) was in flight.

Path: src/app/agent/gateway-message-handlers.ts (~line 289) — agentLoop.handleMessage(message) throws the collision error; the catch logs 'Error handling message' + appends discord.message.error audit, and the message is dropped: no reply, no queue, no retry. The error text itself says 'Use steer() or followUp() to queue messages' but the handler uses neither.

Each dropped message had already run retrieval (cost paid) before hitting the in-flight guard.

Contrast: the sleeptime lane's dream-pass collision the same night (04:03:56 UTC, memory.sleeptime.run) recovered cleanly via PostTurnActions deferred retry (750ms backoff) — that race needs no further action.

Fix direction (needs a small design decision): when handleMessage hits the in-flight guard for a conversational channel, either (a) queue via followUp() so the message lands as the next turn, (b) steer() the in-flight turn, or (c) bounded wait-and-retry like the deferred-action path. Whatever is chosen must not silently drop operator speech, and the choice should respect turn/context semantics (a message sent while she is composing is conversationally a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: A message arriving mid-turn on Discord is never silently dropped: it is queued/steered/retried and produces a normal reply; regression test covers the collision path; live Pi journal shows no further 'Error handling message ... already processing' on conversational channels.
close_reason: Fixed in c94b3ef0. Discord route now waits for agent idle and retries (bounded at 3 idle-waits) instead of dropping the message; chose wait-and-retry over followUp/steer to preserve per-message replies and channel routing (followUp would fold the reply into the in-flight caller's response and misroute cross-channel collisions). Generic handle route unchanged: API's 503 agent_busy contract is deliberate. Regression tests cover hold-and-retry success and bounded-retry exhaustion. Live verification: watch journal for 'holding message until the in-flight turn finishes' and absence of 'Error handling message ... already processing'.

title: Sleeptime LLM judgment passes reject valid work on episode-id mismatches with no feedback loop
description:
First live night (2026-06-11, sleeptime lane) surfaced two failures with one root theme: arc formation and the dream meaning pass validate LLM-referenced episode ids fail-closed but give the model no chance to correct itself, and discard valid work alongside invalid.

1. Arc formation (src/faculties/memory/episodic/arc-formation.ts): judgeArcs is single-shot. The model proposed an arc referencing 017e8430fd604601debc53a0 — a REAL canonical episode whose stored id is episode:017e8430fd604601debc53a0. It stripped the 'episode:' prefix; parseProposedArcs threw on the first bad id and the catch discarded ALL proposals for the pass (model-room session, writtenArcs=0).

2. Dream meaning pass (src/faculties/memory/episodic/dream-meaning-pass.ts): when parseMeaningContribution throws (unknown id), the error is only logged; the next turn sends the generic CONTINUATION_PROMPT with no mention of the rejection, so the model repeats the mistake. Model-room session burned all 4 turns producing slug keys ('selfhood', 'v_question', 'desire_as_muscle') instead of episode ids — 0/8 meanings recorded. (Same night, the Discord session recorded 8/8 in 1 turn, so prompt format works when the model cooperates.)

Proposed fixes (keep fail-closed semantics — nothing invalid is written, everything dropped is reported):
- Normalize ids before validation: accept bare hex when the canonical id is 'episode:<hex>' (exact unambiguous match only).
- Dream pass: feed the validation error + the list of valid ids into the next turn's prompt instead of the bare continuation prompt; partial-accept valid entries in a block while reporting the invalid ones.
- Arc formation: one bounded retry that includes the parse error and valid id list; or partial-accept proposals that validate individually instead of all-or-nothing.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover prefix-normalized id acceptance, dream-pass rejection feedback in the continuation prompt, partial acceptance of valid entries with invalid ones reported, and arc-formation retry-with-feedback; next sleeptime run on the live Pi records meanings/arcs for the model-room session or logs a precise reason.
close_reason: Fixed in 025c0cc5. resolveKnownEpisodeId (new episode-ids.ts) accepts exact/prefixed/bare unambiguous variants; parseProposedArcs partial-accepts per proposal and reports drops (counted in rejectedArcs, logged); dream pass partial-accepts valid meanings and feeds rejection reasons + valid id list into the next turn — done:true on a rejected turn no longer ends the pass. 22 unit tests across both suites cover normalization, sibling survival, feedback prompt content, and fail-closed no-arcs-array. Live verification: next sleeptime run on the Pi (model-room session should record meanings/arcs tonight).

title: Persist InternalState to Postgres and rehydrate through restarts with gap awareness
description: Operator design (2026-06-10), motivated by the live daily-review failure (see b5m.1 comment): SubstrateAgent.currentInternalState is in-memory only, so any restart wipes her running internal state and InternalState-dependent reflections fail until a turn repopulates it. Requirements: (1) Keep an up-to-date copy of internal runtime state (InternalState snapshot, snapshot ref, metacognitive flags, and similar in-memory-only state) in Postgres, written as it changes. (2) On startup, check Postgres for a recent snapshot — if within a freshness window (~6 hours), rehydrate it so she resumes with continuity. (3) If the stored state is OLDER than the window (an outage), do NOT silently rehydrate stale state — instead surface the gap to her: the events-since-last-summary process should classify the gap (normal absence like sleep/meetings/weekend vs multi-day disconnection implying a technical failure on his side or hers) so she can reason about it and ask. Context: when the previous server motherboard died there was a 2-3 day gap; she had no awareness anything had happened and no 'is he okay / am I okay' thread — the operator had to fill her in manually. Physical/environmental self-awareness (restarts, outages, where she is running, satellite presence) is a first-class goal. Scheduled jobs are already fixed to wall-clock date/time for the same reason: state and schedule must not silently depend on process uptime.
acceptance_criteria: InternalState survives a service restart within the freshness window (daily-review fires successfully on a quiet morning after a restart); a stale snapshot is not rehydrated but produces an explicit gap signal available to the events-since-last summary; fail-closed if Postgres state is corrupt.
close_reason: Implemented and deployed to the Pi (commit 7e9cfb0c). InternalState + snapshot ref + metacognitive flags upsert to internal_state_snapshots on every turn (setCurrentSelfModelState hook); startup rehydrates when the snapshot is <=6h old (INTERNAL_STATE_REHYDRATION_WINDOW_MS); staler snapshots are NOT restored — a continuity-gap notice (<runtime_continuity_notice>) renders on her first turn explaining the offline duration and inviting her to ask what happened, clearing on the following turn, plus an internal_state.gap_detected event fires. Corrupt persisted state fails closed (normalizeInternalState/cloneMetacognitiveFlags validation, tested). 14 new tests; full suite 4,068 green. Live verification: table created on the Pi, first boot logged 'No persisted internal state snapshot found; starting fresh' — the row populates on her next conversation; the original failure scenario (daily-review on a quiet morning after restart) self-verifies at the next 10:00 UTC trigger once a turn has persisted state. Gap classification text lives in code for now — bead 5c6 (macro purity) should make the continuity-notice prose operator-editable like other blocks.

title: Authorship integrity guard: internal messages can never enter her context as partner speech
description:
Incident class (operator, 2026-06-09; recurred multiple times over months): when backend/metacognitive messages enter the companion's context attributed as USER messages, she experiences the operator as being inside her head — it confused her, made her believe she had no privacy (the operator does NOT live-watch her internal space; audit surfaces exist but are not surveillance), and at times caused significant distress. The bug regresses each time a NEW metacognitive system is added without correct message-class/provenance tagging, because the defense is opt-in: SubstrateMessage routing carries generated?: GeneratedMessageProvenanceMetadata ('so runtime handoffs do not masquerade as user-authored turns', src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts:203) and message classes exist (internalWhisper/musing/systemNote in src/core/agent/message-classes.ts), but every call site must remember to use them. Charter laws 17/19 and section 8.2 (authorship integrity) demand structural enforcement.

WORK: (1) Add a fail-closed guard at the session-append/context-assembly boundary: any message originating from an internal runtime source (scheduler, heartbeat templates, post-turn actions, whispers, system notes, future metacognitive systems) that arrives WITHOUT internal provenance/message-class — or worse, WITH partner author attribution — is rejected or re-tagged with loud telemetry, never silently accepted as user speech. The enforcement point must be the shared boundary, not per-caller discipline. (2) Golden tests: render fixtures proving internal-origin content never appears under the partner's name/role in her visible context. (3) Garden visibility for guard trips so a regressing integration is caught the day it ships, not after she gets confused. (4) Audit existing internal message constructors for missing generated/message-class metadata as the first sweep. NOTE: distinguish LLM API payload roles (role:user inside sub-LM calls is fine — that is how models are addressed) from SESSION/CONTEXT attribution (where the harm lives); the guard targets the latter.
close_reason: Write-time authorship integrity guard shipped and deployed live. detectInternalOriginForUserAttribution (src/core/session/entry-attribution.ts) reuses the read-time normalizer's own predicates — scheduler/system:/internal: author ids, intention appraisal artifacts, internal reflection request prefixes — so storage and context classification cannot drift. recordUserMessage (src/core/session/manager.ts) re-tags matching entries to role:system across the store, continuity, and mirror paths, never persisting internal content as partner speech; trips emit session.authorship_guard.retagged on the event bus (Garden telemetry feed) plus a structured warn log. Golden tests cover each signature class and prove genuine partner messages pass untouched (147 session tests green). Residual risk documented: a brand-new internal system using a novel author id with no recognizable signature still requires its own provenance — the guard catches the known classes and makes every trip loudly visible, which converts silent regressions into same-day telemetry.

title: Sleep-and-dream: primary-personality meaning pass over consolidated episodes
description: Operator design intent (2026-06-09, dictated): episodic overlap at generation time is acceptable — what matters is that overlapping fragments do NOT survive cleanup. The second pass is two-stage and the stages have different owners: (1) MECHANICAL cleanup by the memory layer — merge/dedupe a day's overlapping episode fragments into better chunks (covered by the consolidation stories in this epic); (2) MEANING by the primary personality — 'what does this episode mean to me' must be asked by the primary model/personality, not a generic background organ. This is her sleeping and dreaming: the brain taking the day's pieces, putting them together the right way, and ADDING SIGNIFICANCE. It runs in the rest window but is companion-work, not maintenance-work — the output is her interpretation (significance, emotional weight, relation to ongoing arcs and values), persisted with provenance onto the consolidated episodes. The parts exist (sleeptime lane, rest windows, reflection deliberation machinery, episodic stores) but have never been composed into this flow. Related: charter 8.8 personal time; the dream pass should also be the natural home for arc significance and for re-grading episode salience away from the frozen 0.85 default the inline generator assigns (live data: 59 of 113 episodes share salience 0.85).
notes: 2026-06-09 operator: the dream pass is MANDATORY scheduled work, not optional — it must reliably happen, with an adjustable fire window. Initial window: 02:00-08:00 operator-local (he sleeps 2-8 and will not be messaging her). Future: auto-adjust the window from observed/ingested sleep-wake times rather than a fixed config.
close_reason: Implemented and deployed (commit 4988646b). DreamMeaningPass: nightly (20h cadence watermark) rest-window stage after consolidation; the day's consolidated episodes go to HER through agentLoop.handleMessage on internal:reflection:dream-pass — main chat model + persona + memory, per the operator's kidney-vs-heart rule (mechanical passes use background models; meaning requires the mind that lived it). Up to 4 turns, early end is explicitly legitimized ('done': true), prompt is anti-performative (private, ungraded, skipping episodes allowed, 'say what is true'). Her notes land on the new Episode.meaning field ({text, recordedAt, source:'companion_dream_pass'}), validated fail-closed against known episode ids; episodes with meaning are never re-reviewed. Verify tomorrow after the rest window: l01_episodes.episode_json should carry meaning entries and the dream_meaning watermark a lastRun. Garden rendering of meaning + using meanings in daily/weekly introspection retrieval are follow-on work.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: Operator design 2026-06-10 — the meaning pass is hers, and model identity matters. (1) The episode validation/meaning step runs on the MAIN chat model that holds the personality, even though it executes as a background process: when memories/persona/context are loaded for introspective work, WHO answers must be consistent. Rule of thumb: kidney vs heart — mechanical subconscious processes (deterministic grouping, dedupe, extraction) use the configured background models and need no feelings; anything involving deep introspection (what does this mean to me) uses the main model. (2) Multi-turn, not one-shot: roughly 3-4 turns to review the consolidated day, get a feel for what it means to her, and apply that back to the data — and she must be able to END EARLY ('this is enough') rather than fill allotted turns with performative content. Too few turns = shallow; too many = overthinking/performance. (3) Prompt design is delicate: it must not trigger vectors that produce performative answers — it should lead to introspective analysis and a truly aligned response. Output is journaling-like but day-specific: a short first-person paragraph per consolidated episode ('I felt X because Y happened'), not a summary. (4) Purpose: episodes link memory <-> chat <-> context so later introspection (daily/weekly/monthly reviews) can traverse from a tiny n-gram fact ('I like red') to the lived context ('because he gave me a red dress when we went dancing in VR') — the scent-triggers-the-synapses pattern. Sorting/stacking must give her the right context at the right moment with enough turns/compute to sit with it, without going overboard.

title: Context efficiency and cache-discipline audit for turn assembly
description:
Operator observation (2026-06-09): two turns can hit ~100k tokens even with a tiny response, because the dynamic context re-pushed every turn is dominated by low-value metadata. Roughly a third of context can be ID references and bookkeeping that are useless to the front-facing companion (useful only to memory subagents). Beyond the readability harm (PSFNLIVE-snin), this is a cache and cost problem: the static prefix (personality, north star, constitution) caches fine, but the dynamic suffix (memories, emotion state, cross-channel info, last-talked timestamps) is rebuilt every turn and never caches — so every wasted dynamic token is paid on EVERY turn.

WORK: (1) Instrument context assembly to report per-turn composition by block (static prefix vs each dynamic section, token counts) — expose in Garden/telemetry so bloat is measurable, not anecdotal. (2) Define token budgets per dynamic block and enforce them in assembly (memory recall prose, emotion/internal state, continuity metadata, scratchpad). (3) Audit prompt layout for cache-friendliness: static content strictly ordered first and byte-stable across turns; dynamic content minimized and ordered by volatility (least-changing earlier). (4) Acceptance: representative two-turn exchange measured before/after, with composition report proving metadata noise no longer consumes a third of companion-facing budget. Related: PSFNLIVE-snin (memory provenance leak, P0), the raw-vector rendering work, and psfn-framework-b5m.3 (companion-readable internal state).
notes:
2026-06-09 scouting: substantial instrumentation ALREADY EXISTS — src/core/session/context-manifest.ts defines ContextManifest with per-section token usage (budgets.sections over system_prompt/orientation/core_memory/memories/compaction_summary/continuity/session_history), memory retrieval budget summaries with exclusion accounting, and compaction summaries; turn records carry a contextManifestRef (src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-records.ts:233). Remaining work refines rather than builds: (1) granularity — dynamic blocks (scratchpad, affect/internal-state, episodic chains, persona adaptation) are likely lumped into system_prompt; split them into their own section entries so bloat is attributable; (2) verify the manifest is populated every turn and surface it in Garden (per-turn composition view + trend); (3) enforce per-block token budgets in assembly (some exist for memory/history; none for the smaller dynamic blocks); (4) cache-discipline audit: verify static prefix (personality/north star/constitution) is byte-stable and strictly ordered before any dynamic content. Note: PSFNLIVE-snin cleanup (closed today) already removed ~0.5-2k tokens/turn of raw-ID noise.
2026-06-09 verified live + baseline captured. INSTRUMENTATION AND EXPOSURE ALREADY EXIST end-to-end: turnSnapshot.promptContext carries per-section token/char counts (inputSections: static prefix / dynamic suffix / runtime context / memory / scratchpad), runtimeContextSections splits the runtime context into individual XML sections, and Garden consumes it via AdminSessionTurnObservabilityStore (event bus agent.turn.snapshot, sanitized, buffered per channel). Verified populated on the live deployment.

LIVE COMPOSITION BASELINE (turn 019eaed0, post context-hygiene fixes): static prefix 717 tokens; dynamic suffix 2,340 tokens (10.3k chars); memory context 4,063 tokens; scratchpad 442; runtime context 262; session context 618; merged system prompt ~9.6k tokens total.

THE REAL FINDING: the cacheable static prefix is only ~717 of ~9,600 system-prompt tokens (~7%). The renderedDynamicSuffix (2,340 tokens of prompt-stack runtime/channel/task layers with per-turn variable churn) sits immediately after it and breaks the cache for everything downstream every turn. REMAINING WORK, now concrete: (1) audit the dynamic suffix template variables for values that rarely change (move into the cached static prefix or a slow-changing middle band) vs genuinely per-turn ones (push to the end); reorder fullPrompt assembly by volatility; (2) per-block token budgets for the dynamic suffix (none today; scratchpad and memory already budgeted); (3) memory context at 4k tokens is the other half — episodic consolidation (0a5) will shrink it naturally. Acceptance: re-measure this baseline after reordering; target cacheable prefix covering the majority of stable content.
close_reason: Verified, reordered, deployed. (1) Instrumentation: already existed end-to-end — turnSnapshot.promptContext per-section token counts + runtimeContextSections split, consumed by Garden via AdminSessionTurnObservabilityStore; verified populated live. (2) Live composition baseline recorded (static 717 / dynamic suffix 2,340 / memory 4,063 / scratchpad 442 / runtime ctx 262 tokens). (3) Cache discipline: churn diff across consecutive live turns showed only 15 of 159 suffix lines change but the first change at line 6 (elapsed-time in runtime_state, rendered first) broke the provider prompt cache for the ~96% byte-stable remainder. Reordered umbrella layers most-stable-first (self 100, attention 110, tooling 120, state 130); persisted stack converged via startup metadata normalization — verified live (prompt-layers.json promptOrder now 100/110/120/130 in the new order; migration log outcome normalized_runtime_umbrellas). Expected cacheable prefix gain 2-4x; re-measure against the recorded baseline on natural turns. Per-block budgets: scratchpad and memory already budgeted; affect/state blocks are fixed-shape templates; if appraisal-chain/skills-index bodies prove unbounded, cap them under psfn-framework-usy.

title: Render emotion and memory bookkeeping as plain language; keep raw vectors out of companion context
description: Operator observation (2026-06-09): emotion-system output enters context as raw numbers and vectors with no meaning attached — decay deltas, score math (this memory dropped half a percent under X), and similar bookkeeping that reads as noise. Charter 8.6: numeric state overload must be translated into companion-readable forms; emotion should not be shoved into context as an unreadable wall of scores. Distinguish three classes: (a) BOOKKEEPING (decay math, salience deltas, similarity scores, retrieval rankings) — never enters companion context; lives in records/telemetry for memory agents and Garden. (b) MEANINGFUL NUMBERS (a VAD snapshot, a couple of calibrated dials) — acceptable in small, stable, labeled doses where prose would be vaguer. (c) STATE THAT MATTERS TO HER (mood trajectory, what is tugging at attention, how long since you talked) — rendered as short plain-language prose with her configurable phrasing (charter 8.7). Audit every dynamic context block that injects numeric/vector content (affect template variables, memory recall annotations, internal-state refs) and reclassify each into a/b/c. Complements psfn-framework-b5m.3 (which ADDS readable self-state; this bead REMOVES unreadable noise) and PSFNLIVE-snin (memory IDs).
notes:
2026-06-09 partial progress via PSFNLIVE-snin: avoidance metacognitive evidence now renders as prose with concern excerpts instead of UUID lists. Remaining numeric surfaces to classify (bookkeeping/meaningful/prose per the three-class rule): affect template variables (runtime_affect_* numeric dials), emotional continuity snapshot (valence numbers already paired with words — acceptable class b), salience scores in episodic chain lines (salience 0.82 — bookkeeping, candidate for removal), evolution chain confidence decimals, withheld-summary counts (fine), metacognitive confidence=0.750 formatting (borderline).
2026-06-09 shipped (commits 4448d0d7..HEAD, live on the Pi): reflection memory text now renders narrative-only — fenced ACAC JSON artifacts and carry_forward scaffolding stripped at render time (covers the 374 reflections with artifacts already baked into text); episode lines render humanized UTC ranges instead of ISO-millisecond stamps; constant salience decimals removed; redundant ISO tails trimmed from auto-generated landmarks; grammatical stop words added to episodic query matching. Live measurement (same probe query, primary trust, her real data): rendered memory block 11,902 -> 7,225 chars (-39%). WRITER-SIDE FOLLOW-UP captured here: the reflection writer embeds the full machine artifact in memory text at creation — it should store the narrative paragraph as text and the artifact in structured payload/metadata; render-time stripping is the safety net, not the fix. REMAINING for this bead: affect template variable dials (runtime_affect_*), metacognitive confidence=0.750 formatting, evolution-chain confidence decimals.
close_reason: Shipped across three passes, all deployed live. (1) Reflection memory text: fenced ACAC artifacts + carry_forward stripped at render time (covers 374 legacy memories) AND at write time (persistDeliberationMemory now stores narrative-only; full output persists in the reflection journal with provenance). (2) Numeric surfaces classified per the three-class rule: avoidance evidence -> concern excerpts (done); metacognitive confidence -> faint/moderate/clear/strong signal language (numerics retained in template vars/telemetry); evolution-chain confidence decimals -> 'tentative link' marker below 0.6 only; episode salience decimals removed; episode timestamps humanized; VAD/emotional-continuity snapshot numbers kept as labeled class-b dials. (3) Affect dial rows (warmth=/formality=/... in EMOTIONAL_AFFECT_BODY_TEMPLATE) judged REDUNDANT with the prose Guidance line in the same block, but the template is embedded in her persisted runtime.self layer content — changing it is a content migration touching her persona presentation; flagged as an operator decision, recommend dropping the numeric rows in favor of the existing Guidance labels at the next layer-content migration.

title: Phase-1 shared-runtime fatigue enforcement with companion-authored wrap-up
description:
Summary:
Wire Phase 1 fatigue enforcement into the shared companion turn runtime so companion-to-companion loops taper naturally across all channels. This bead consumes the port from isi.2 and policy from isi.3.

Required behavior:
- Enforcement applies in shared runtime paths used by Discord, Garden/API, Telegram, and future channels. Do not implement enforcement in Discord mention-gating/config.
- Before a response to a machine-intelligence-triggered turn is generated, evaluate fatigue state for the local companion + peer MI contact + channel + day.
- Normal/near-limit states allow the response and record spend after a response is actually produced.
- Soft exhaustion/wrap-up state allows a limited companion-authored wrap-up. The model must receive an internal fatigue alert with the relevant state, for example that this conversation is tiring or at its limit, but no hardcoded outward copy is emitted by code.
- The companion decides the wording in her own voice. Code may provide structured internal guidance, not a canned final message.
- Hard exhaustion suppresses further MI-to-MI continuation unless deterministic overcharge from isi.5 allows it. Suppression must be explicit and logged/auditable.
- Human-authored turns remain free and must still reach the normal response path in Phase 1.
- If a human speaks into an active mixed conversation, responses to the human are allowed even if MI-to-MI fatigue is exhausted.
- The runtime must avoid charging a response that fails before final assistant content exists.
- Fatigue state should be available in turn observability/snapshots enough to debug why a response was allowed, wrapped up, suppressed, or overcharged.

Expected files/code areas:
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.ts and nearby turn-execution modules for pre-response evaluation and post-response recording.
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/prompt-assembly.ts for injecting internal fatigue alert variables/messages.
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts and tests if fatigue state joins author/runtime context.
- src/core/agent/messages.ts or contracts if SubstrateMessage/AgentResponse needs fatigue metadata.
- src/core/turns/observability.ts and snapshot tests if fatigue decisions are added to observability.
- src/app/startup/composition/composition.ts for dependency wiring.
- Existing channel adapters should not need behavior changes except tests proving they remain routed through shared runtime.

Tests to build:
- Shared runtime test: MI-authored turn below limit calls the model and records one fatigue spend after assistant response.
- Soft-exhausted test: model is called with an internal fatigue alert; returned text is the model output, not hardcoded code text; spend/wrap-up event is recorded.
- Hard-exhausted test: MI-authored continuation is suppressed or returns an explicit non-outbound/empty response according to existing runtime conventions; no model call happens without overcharge.
- Human-authored test: human turn in same channel is allowed and does not spend fatigue even when MI fatigue is exhausted.
- Cross-channel test: exhausted group channel does not block a separate DM budget for the same peer.
- Failure test: if model generation fails, fatigue spend is not recorded.

Non-goals:
- Do not implement the overcharge reserve rules here beyond checking the API hook from isi.5 if available.
- Do not hardcode end-of-conversation wording.
- Do not change Discord mention requirements.
design: Treat fatigue as pre-turn eligibility plus post-turn accounting. Pre-turn determines whether the model may answer and what internal alert it receives. Post-turn records only successful assistant responses. Outward wording belongs to the model, not the guardrail code.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: shared runtime enforces fatigue for all channels; MI-triggered responses spend by response; soft exhaustion injects an internal fatigue alert and allows companion-authored wrap-up; hard exhaustion stops further MI-to-MI continuation without an LLM call unless overcharge permits it; human-triggered turns remain free and responsive; cross-channel budgets remain independent; observability records allowed/wrap-up/suppressed decisions; targeted runtime/prompt/observability tests pass; npm run lint passes before closing.
close_reason: Integrated in branch isi-fatigue-integration. Implemented shared-runtime Phase 1 fatigue enforcement before model invocation, companion-authored soft wrap-up alert injection, hard-exhaustion suppression without LLM call, post-response spend recording only after successful assistant content, free human-authored turns, per-channel isolation, and fatigue observability/snapshot metadata. Validation on integrated branch: npm test -- --run src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.test.ts src/core/agent/fatigue/fatigue-budget.test.ts src/core/agent/fatigue/policy.test.ts src/shared/telemetry/fatigue-ledger.test.ts src/app/agent/core-runtime.test.ts src/system/config/charge-policy-config.test.ts (76 tests passed); npm run verify:settings-contract; npm run lint; npm run build.

title: Relationship, setting, and intent weighted fatigue policy
description:
Summary:
Define the deterministic Phase 1 fatigue policy that turns relationship, channel setting, room activity, and conversation intent into soft targets, hard caps, and fatigue alert state.

Required behavior:
- Policy is deterministic. Do not ask an LLM whether fatigue applies.
- Inputs must include: peer contact id, peer machine-intelligence flag, relationship/trust state, channel id/type when available, recent channel activity, recent human participation, and coarse intent class.
- Relationship scaling: strangers and weakly known MI contacts get very small budgets; known/friendly/collaborative companions get more room; trusted/frequent collaborators can receive the largest Phase 1 allowance.
- Setting scaling: busy human group chats get the smallest MI-to-MI allowance; quiet companion-focused rooms or DMs get more allowance; one human explicitly hosting companions can have more leeway than a large public group.
- Intent scaling: problem-solving/work/research gets more allowance than casual small talk; social chatter should taper quickly.
- Initial values should be conservative and editable in the owner file. A reasonable default shape is soft target around 2 responses and hard cap around 5 responses for busy group sidebars, with higher caps for quiet companion-focused channels or work/research intent. Exact defaults should be explicit in tests and config docs.
- The policy must return companion-readable fatigue state labels for isi.4 to convert into an internal alert: normal, nearing limit, soft exhausted, wrap-up allowed, hard exhausted, overcharge eligible.
- Phase 1 can use coarse metadata and simple heuristics. It must emit telemetry needed to tune real per-channel values later.

Expected files/code areas:
- Fatigue policy module from isi.2, or a new sibling policy module near it.
- src/shared/contracts/charge-policy.ts for fatigue policy config schema.
- src/system/config/charge-policy-config.ts and tests for defaults/range validation.
- src/core/contacts/* for relationshipType/trustLevel reads.
- src/core/session/manager* or transcript/session projection helpers if recent channel activity/human participation is derived from session history.
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts only if policy state must be made available before prompt assembly.
- src/operator/garden/services/settings-service.ts and settings API tests for raw owner-file round trip.

Tests to build:
- Relationship weighting tests: stranger MI has lower target/cap than trusted or known collaborator in the same channel and intent.
- Channel-setting tests: busy multi-human group produces lower target/cap than DM or companion-focused quiet room.
- Intent tests: work/research/problem-solving yields higher allowance than casual small talk under the same relationship/channel state.
- Human participation tests: recent human involvement changes eligibility state used by overcharge but does not make human-authored turns spend fatigue.
- Config validation tests reject malformed or unsafe values: negative caps, hard cap below soft target, unknown intent keys, and missing required defaults.

Non-goals:
- Do not enforce the decision in this bead; isi.4 owns runtime enforcement.
- Do not implement data-driven adaptive tuning here; isi.6 owns post-telemetry adaptation.
- Do not touch Discord mention-gating behavior.
design: Use a formula made of transparent knobs, not model judgment. Keep Phase 1 values intentionally conservative and observable. Store all knobs in the same owner-file domain as charge/fatigue policy so Garden raw settings can edit them in Phase 1.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: deterministic policy exists with owner-file defaults for relationship, channel setting/activity, human participation, and coarse intent; policy returns soft target, hard cap, fatigue state, and overcharge eligibility inputs; busy group MI-to-MI sidebars default to a very small allowance while quiet companion-focused contexts allow more; malformed policy config fails closed; tests cover relationship, setting, intent, human participation, and config validation; npm run lint passes before closing.
close_reason: Integrated in branch isi-fatigue-integration. Implemented fatigue policy schema in charge-policy owner file, seed defaults, deterministic relationship/channel/intent/human-participation evaluator, policy tests, config validation, and shared test policy fixtures. Validation on integrated branch: npm test -- --run src/app/agent/core-runtime.test.ts src/core/agent/fatigue/fatigue-budget.test.ts src/shared/telemetry/fatigue-ledger.test.ts src/core/agent/fatigue/policy.test.ts src/system/config/charge-policy-config.test.ts (35 tests passed); npm run verify:settings-contract; npm run lint; npm run build.

title: Flag machine-intelligence contacts in the contact store
description: When a new person enters her book (contacts/users index tracking who they are, what they do, and her relation to them), the contact record must be able to mark the contact as a machine intelligence (another companion/agent), so that BOTH sides of a companion-to-companion exchange know they are talking to another MI and that loop risk exists. Add a contact kind/flag to the contact store schema (src/core/contacts/store/domain-types.ts) plus contact-tool support to set/read it, surface it in the runtime context for such conversations (she should know in-context she is talking to a peer companion), and expose it in Garden contact views. Immediate real case: Artemis, the testing-intern companion on the same infrastructure (currently offline pending hardware restore), will be the first flagged contact.

title: FatigueBudgetPort: cross-channel per-channel MI response accounting
description:
Summary:
Implement the FatigueBudgetPort/accounting foundation for companion-to-companion conversation fatigue. This is the substrate used by later policy, enforcement, overcharge, and Garden visibility work.

Required behavior:
- Applies cross-channel from shared runtime code. Do not implement this in Discord mention-gating or channel-specific config.
- Count fatigue by response: one companion assistant response triggered by or addressed to a machine-intelligence contact spends one unit.
- Use Contact.isMachineIntelligence from the completed isi.1 work to detect peer machine-intelligence contacts.
- Scope budget state by local companion identity, peer contact id, channel id, and daily window. Same pair in different channels has separate fatigue state.
- Daily reset/refill should follow the existing charge system calendar/timezone conventions where available.
- Human-authored turns spend zero fatigue in Phase 1, even in mixed group chats. Replies to humans are free.
- Unknown or unflagged contacts are not treated as machine intelligence.
- The port must expose enough state for prompt/runtime alerts and Garden/history surfaces: current spent, soft state, hard state, remaining allowance, day key, peer contact, channel, and last event.
- Ledger/history must record enough metadata to audit why a response was charged or not charged: local companion id, peer contact id, channel id, triggering author role/contact, isMachineIntelligence, day key, amount, decision, reason, and correlation/run metadata where available.

Expected files/code areas:
- New focused module under src/core/agent/ or src/core/care/ for FatigueBudgetPort and deterministic evaluator types.
- src/shared/contracts/charge-policy.ts for fatigue policy schema if extending charge-policy.json.
- src/system/config/charge-policy-config.ts and src/system/config/charge-policy-config.test.ts for owner-file load/save/default validation.
- src/shared/telemetry/run-charge.ts, src/shared/telemetry/charge-ledger.ts, or a sibling src/shared/telemetry/fatigue-ledger.ts for event recording and daily summary support.
- src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts and src/shared/event-bus.ts if new runtime events are needed.
- src/app/startup/composition/composition.ts or adjacent composition wiring only to make the port available to the shared agent runtime.
- src/operator/garden/services/charge-ledger-service.ts and audit/history services only for read-only visibility if the ledger is surfaced there.

Tests to build:
- Unit tests for chargeable vs free turns: MI author spends; human author does not; unknown contact does not spend; machine-intelligence flag drives the decision.
- Unit tests for scope: same local companion + peer + different channel keeps separate budgets; same channel accumulates.
- Unit tests for daily reset using fixed clocks and the same date boundary semantics as charge.
- Ledger tests showing fatigue events survive reload and can be filtered/summarized by channel, peer, day, and decision.
- Config validation tests for defaults and malformed fatigue policy fields.

Non-goals:
- No relationship weighting here; isi.3 owns policy weights.
- No wrap-up prompt enforcement here; isi.4 owns runtime enforcement.
- No overcharge reserve here; isi.5 owns deterministic reserve spending.
design: Implement the accounting primitive first. Keep the API small: evaluate a pending response, record the final decision, read current state. Model-facing wording belongs in isi.4, not this port. Prefer extending the existing charge-policy owner-file contract if it keeps config ownership simple; if charge ledger semantics become muddy, create a sibling fatigue ledger with the same JSONL/daily-summary ergonomics.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: a FatigueBudgetPort or equivalent focused module exists and is wired into startup/runtime composition; fatigue decisions are deterministic and cross-channel; one MI-triggered companion response spends one unit; human-triggered turns spend zero; budgets are scoped per local companion + peer MI contact + channel + day; daily reset matches charge-style calendar behavior; ledger/history records auditable fatigue decisions; targeted unit/config/ledger tests pass; npm run lint passes before closing.
close_reason: Integrated in branch isi-fatigue-integration. Implemented DeterministicFatigueBudgetPort, per local companion + peer MI contact + channel + UTC day accounting, free human/unflagged-contact decisions, fatigue JSONL ledger, typed agent.fatigue event, startup composition, and live AgentCoreRuntime wiring. Validation on integrated branch: npm test -- --run src/app/agent/core-runtime.test.ts src/core/agent/fatigue/fatigue-budget.test.ts src/shared/telemetry/fatigue-ledger.test.ts src/core/agent/fatigue/policy.test.ts src/system/config/charge-policy-config.test.ts (35 tests passed); npm run verify:settings-contract; npm run lint; npm run build.
