Implementation steps:
1. Add stage timing instrumentation for trust resolve, retrieval, context build, compaction, and first token emit.
2. Add queue-depth/wait-time telemetry around per-channel processing locks.
3. Refactor processing flow to avoid unnecessary serialization where safe (or release lock once stream begins).
4. Ensure non-blocking async work (post-turn extraction/maintenance) does not delay visible token start.
5. Add regression tests/bench assertions for improved TTFT under rapid message bursts.

Example:
Before -> second message in same channel waits full first turn before any token can stream.
After -> queue behavior is explicit and first-token latency is reduced/measured under load.
close_reason: Added TTFT stage instrumentation and Discord queue telemetry with tests

title: Reduce low-value memory writes and add memory pipeline telemetry
description:
Summary:
Reduce extraction spam and low-value memory writes (e.g., repetitive greeting observations) while instrumenting retrieval/extraction/compaction cadence and LLM request counts.

Why:
Current extraction path can write nearly every extracted fact without strong value gates, creating memory bloat and poor signal-to-noise. We also need hard telemetry for how often retrieval/summarization run and how many prompts each turn triggers.

Files to modify:
- src/memory/extraction.ts
- src/memory/writer.ts
- src/memory/retrieval.ts
- src/session/manager.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/types.ts
- .env.example
- src/memory/extraction.test.ts
- src/memory/writer.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Add configurable acceptance gates for extracted facts (importance/confidence/novelty thresholds).
2. Tighten extraction prompt to request only durable/high-salience facts and reject chatter patterns.
3. Add dedup/novelty checks before writes for repeated interaction meta-facts.
4. Emit structured telemetry counters: retrieval calls per turn, extraction triggers, compaction summaries, and per-turn LLM request count.
5. Expose tuning knobs for extraction interval/threshold and minimum write score.
6. Add tests proving low-value facts are rejected and high-value profile facts are retained.

Example:
Before -> "user greeted assistant multiple times" gets persisted repeatedly.
After -> greeting churn is filtered; only meaningful profile/relationship facts persist.
close_reason: Added extraction quality gates, low-value filtering, and retrieval/extraction telemetry with tests

title: Protect durable relationship memories from aggressive salience decay
description:
Summary:
Stop critical long-term memories (anniversary, first dance, partner profile facts) from fading like short-lived conversational trivia.

Why:
Decay maintenance currently runs every 60s and applies generic type-level decay, which can erode core relationship context too quickly when extraction noise is high.

- src/memory/writer.ts
- src/memory/store.ts
- src/types.ts
- .env.example
- src/memory/decay.test.ts
- src/memory/writer.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Add durable-memory semantics (e.g., `tags: ['core_profile']` or `retentionClass: durable`).
2. Apply salience floors or slower/disabled decay for durable relationship/profile memories.
3. Add configurable decay profiles so ephemeral memories still fade quickly while durable memories persist.
4. Add writer pathways (manual tool or extraction rule) that can mark memories as durable when appropriate.
5. Add tests proving one-week inactivity does not erase durable memories while ephemeral memories still decay.

Example:
Before -> anniversary fact decays below retrieval usefulness after inactivity.
After -> anniversary fact remains retrievable with high confidence; transient greetings continue to decay.
close_reason: Implemented durable memory retention semantics with decay/profile safeguards and tests

title: Voice Frame Protocol + Processor Contracts
description:
Summary:
Define PSFN voice frame taxonomy and processor contracts that standardize streaming audio/text/control flow inside the voice runtime.

Why:

2. Define processor interface(s) for directional frame processing and lifecycle start/stop/cancel.
3. Define queue priority rules for control vs data frames.
4. Add unit tests that validate ordering and interruptibility invariants.

Example:
Before -> voice pipeline passes raw values and side effects directly between Discord, STT, and TTS logic.
After -> each stage consumes and emits typed voice frames with explicit contract boundaries.

title: Voice Reliability/Security Guardrails + Rollout Controls
description:
Summary:
Add reliability and security guardrails for voice vNext: per-stage timeout/retry budgets, provider fallback policy, and rollout controls.

Streaming and multi-connector expansion increases failure modes and attack surface; guardrails must be explicit and testable.

2. Implement connector fallback policy and circuit-breaker-like behavior.
3. Add config flags for staged rollout (shadow mode, canary percentage, hard fallback).
4. Validate with resilience tests and failure-injection scenarios.

Example:
Before -> provider call failures bubble as runtime errors with minimal policy handling.
After -> voice runtime applies bounded retries/fallback and controlled degradation while preserving safety constraints.
close_reason: Implemented voice reliability/security guardrail policy modules with retry/timeouts/fallback helpers

title: Voice Orchestrator + Composable Pipeline Runtime
description:
Summary:
Implement a reusable VoiceOrchestrator and composable VoicePipeline runtime that wires processors, lifecycle, and cancellation boundaries.

4. Add tests for lifecycle transitions and cancellation edge cases.

After -> Discord runtime delegates stream handling to VoiceOrchestrator through a stable runtime API.

title: Streaming STT Connectors (Deepgram First)

4. Add retry/timeout behavior and error mapping tests.

Before -> capture entire utterance and transcribe once.
After -> STT emits partial transcript frames during speech and final frame at turn close.

title: Streaming TTS Connectors (ElevenLabs First)
description:

4. Add timeout/retry and playback completion tests.

After -> begin playback from initial chunks while remaining audio continues streaming.

title: Turn Lifecycle + Barge-In Controller

After -> explicit turn controller drives interruption and progression with tested state transitions.

title: Real-Time Voice Platform vNext (Streaming + Multi-Transport)

title: Gateway hardening: fetch TLS diagnostics + module registry path policy

title: API: prevent stranded in-flight turns (timeout/disconnect handling)
description:
Summary: API chat completions can leave the agent in a long-running in-flight state after client timeout, causing subsequent requests to fail with `Agent is already processing a prompt` and return 500s. Add request lifecycle controls so timeout/disconnect does not strand the channel.

Files to modify:
- src/channels/api/server.ts
- src/channels/api/server.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Add per-channel in-flight tracking and serialization in ApiServer for `/v1/chat/completions` so concurrent same-session calls do not race the underlying agent.
2. Add request timeout handling for non-streaming requests (configurable via env, with sensible default) and detect client disconnect (`req.aborted` / `res.close`) to stop waiting.
3. Propagate cancellation signal where supported; otherwise ensure API returns deterministic timeout/busy errors and clears server-side bookkeeping safely.
4. Return explicit 429/503-style busy response instead of generic 500 for channel-busy contention.
5. Add regression tests for: timeout path, disconnect path, in-flight contention behavior, and successful recovery after timeout.

Example:
Before: Request A times out at client, request B on same `X-Session-ID` -> 500 internal error (`already processing`).
After: Request A yields timeout/busy response and bookkeeping cleanup; request B either queues/returns busy deterministically and succeeds once channel is free.
close_reason: Implemented API per-session in-flight gate, timeout/disconnect lifecycle handling, explicit busy/timeout responses, and regression tests.

title: Think loop routes through extraction purpose instead of reasoning model slot

title: Runtime settings do not propagate to model roster or active Agent model
description:
Summary:

Why this is a bug:
- applySettings() updates config.primaryModel / config.extractionModel but does not synchronize config.modelRoster slots (chat, background).
- SubstrateAgent resolves and sets the model once, then keeps modelResolved=true; later settings changes do not force agent.setModel(...) with updated values.
- Result: UI/settings claim model changes are live, but runtime can continue using the old model.

- src/settings.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/channels/admin/handlers.ts
- src/settings.test.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Make applySettings() keep modelRoster.chat and modelRoster.background aligned with primary/extraction settings (model, provider, maxTokens).
2. Add a safe runtime hook on SubstrateAgent to refresh model resolution after settings updates (or detect config drift before each turn and re-set model).
3. Ensure admin settings update path invokes the refresh hook after saving/applying settings.
4. Add tests proving model/provider/token changes in settings are reflected in actual resolved model IDs for subsequent turns.

Example:
Before: set primary model to moonshotai/kimi-k2.5 in admin -> responses still use old z-ai/glm-5.
After: next turn resolves and uses moonshotai/kimi-k2.5 immediately.

title: LLM auto-retry with exponential backoff
description:
PSFN has zero retry logic for LLM calls. If a call fails (rate limit, timeout, server error from LiteLLM→OpenRouter), the error propagates directly to the Discord adapter and the user sees an error. This is a significant resilience gap.

Mom/pi-coding-agent's AgentSession has auto-retry with exponential backoff: configurable maxRetries (default 3) + baseDelayMs * 2^(attempt-1). Retries are abortable via AbortController. Emits auto_retry_start/end events for UI status.

title: RLM evidence/provenance tracking in ThinkResult
description:
PSFN's ThinkResult returns only aggregate stats (iterations, token counts, duration). There's no record of what the think tool actually searched, found, or concluded at each step. This makes it impossible to cite sources, debug reasoning, or generate reflection memories about how conclusions were reached.

Aleph (github.com/Hmbown/aleph) tracks an evidence trail — every search, sub-LM call, and code execution records a citation with source, snippet, and timestamp.
design:
## Pattern (from Aleph `aleph/mcp/session.py:78-130`)

```python
@dataclass
class _Evidence:
    source: str  # "search", "peek", "exec", "manual", "sub_query"
    line_range: tuple[int, int] | None
    pattern: str | None
    snippet: str
    note: str | None = None
    timestamp: datetime
```

Session also tracks convergence: `confidence_history: list[float]`, `information_gain: list[int]`.

## PSFN Design

### New types in `src/repl/types.ts`

```typescript
export interface ThinkEvidence {
  source: 'memory_search' | 'memory_get' | 'session_messages' | 'llm_query' | 'code';
  query?: string;         // search query or llm prompt (truncated)
  snippet: string;        // what was found (truncated to ~200 chars)
  resultCount?: number;   // how many results returned
  timestamp: number;
}

export interface ThinkStep {
  iteration: number;
  code: string;            // code the LLM wrote (truncated)
  output: string;          // execution output (truncated)
  error: string | null;
  evidenceCollected: ThinkEvidence[];
  tokensUsed: number;      // this iteration's token count
}
```

### Changes

1. `src/repl/types.ts` — Add `ThinkEvidence`, `ThinkStep`. Extend `ThinkResult` with:
   ```typescript
   steps: ThinkStep[];
   evidence: ThinkEvidence[];  // flattened from all steps
   ```

2. `src/repl/sandbox.ts` — Add evidence collection hooks to injected functions:
   - `memory_search`: record query, result count, top result snippet
   - `memory_get_by_id`: record id, text snippet
   - `session_messages`: record channelId, message count
   - `llm_query`: record prompt (first 100 chars), response (first 200 chars)
   
   Evidence array lives on sandbox instance, collected per-execution:
   ```typescript
   private currentEvidence: ThinkEvidence[] = [];
   
   // In memory_search:
   this.currentEvidence.push({
     source: 'memory_search',
     query,
     snippet: results[0]?.text.slice(0, 200) ?? '',
     resultCount: results.length,
     timestamp: Date.now(),
   });
   ```
   
   Add `collectEvidence(): ThinkEvidence[]` method that drains and returns.

3. `src/repl/loop.ts` — After each sandbox.execute():
   - Collect evidence via `sandbox.collectEvidence()`
   - Build `ThinkStep` with code, output, error, evidence, tokens
   - Push to `steps[]` array
   - At end: flatten all step evidence into top-level `evidence[]`

4. `src/repl/tools.ts` — Include evidence summary in tool output:
   ```
   [Think: 5 iters, 8420 tokens, 1200ms, 12 evidence items]
   ```

### Use cases
- Purrsephone can cite: "Based on 3 memories I found about X..."
- Admin GUI can show reasoning chains in Active Branches
- Reflection memories can reference what evidence informed a conclusion
acceptance_criteria:
- ThinkEvidence and ThinkStep types defined
- memory_search, memory_get_by_id, session_messages, llm_query all record evidence
- ThinkResult includes steps[] and evidence[] arrays
- Think tool output header shows evidence count
- Evidence snippets truncated to prevent bloat
close_reason: Verified end-to-end: ThinkEvidence + ThinkStep types, evidence hooks in memory_search/memory_get_by_id/session_messages/llm_query, step assembly in loop, evidence count in tool header, snippet truncation. All 5 source types covered with tests. 875 tests passing.

title: Gateway split: voice turns need awaited agent response for TTS
description:
Voice runtime currently depends on `DiscordAdapter.onMessage()` returning the agent response synchronously so it can run TTS playback.

In gateway/agent split mode (`gateway-main.ts` + `agent-main.ts`), the gateway Discord handler forwards message notifications to agent via `gateway.notifyAll('discord.message', ...)` and returns a placeholder response immediately. This means voice transcript turns can produce empty responses at the adapter layer and skip TTS.

Why it matters:
- Single-process mode voice works with direct handler response.
- Split mode is the intended secure deployment model (keys host-side), so voice needs a request/response path there too.

Proposed fix directions:
1. Add a request-response RPC path for Discord turns (gateway asks one connected agent for response payload and waits with timeout), OR
2. Add dedicated voice reply RPC (`discord.voice.reply`) from agent to gateway carrying text/audio-ready payload tied to voice session, OR
3. Route voice turn through an explicit gateway event channel with correlation IDs and awaited reply.

Any solution must preserve existing text behavior and avoid double-send.
acceptance_criteria:
- In gateway+agent split mode, a voice transcript turn receives agent response and plays TTS
- No placeholder/empty response path in voice flow
- Text channel behavior remains unchanged
- Added integration test covering gateway+agent voice response correlation
close_reason: Implemented bidirectional JSON-RPC: JSONRPCServerAndClient per connection, discord.handleMessage reverse RPC, voice handler in adapter, gateway-main wiring, agent-main handler. 797 tests passing.

title: Fix DM metadata propagation across continuity + retrieval
description:
Validation bug: Discord DM metadata (`isDirectMessage`) is only used during append-time stamping in SessionManager, but not in all downstream trust/visibility decisions.

Observed gaps:
- `UserContinuityStore.getRecent()` recomputes sharing compatibility from raw channel IDs via `channelsShareContinuity(origin, currentChannelId)`.
- `channelsShareContinuity()` classifies both channels without DM metadata.
- `MemoryRetriever.retrieve()` classifies visibility from raw `channelId` only.

Impact:
- Numeric Discord DM channels still behave like `semi_private` in continuity sharing and retrieval filtering.
- Primary-tier DM behavior is degraded (e.g., private↔private continuity and intimate/confidential retrieval ceilings).

title: Core self-modification: git-backed guarded tools
description:
Controlled self-modification workflow using git-native change management and explicit review gates.

Direction update:
- Primary deployment target is private GitHub repo or local/private GitLab.
- Self-modification changes should be proposed as branch + PR/MR artifacts, not silent direct writes to main.

Toolchain scope:
1. `repo_status` — status/branch/dirty summary
2. `repo_diff` — staged/unstaged diff summary
3. `repo_apply_patch` — constrained patch apply (allowlisted paths)
4. `repo_commit` — signed-off commit with structured message template
5. `repo_create_branch` — feature branch creation
6. `repo_open_pr` / `repo_open_mr` — open review artifact in remote forge (GitHub/GitLab)
7. `self_rebuild` — run rebuild workflow
8. `self_restart` — supervisor restart with pre/post notifications

Governance model:
- Default path is PR/MR-first for auditable change history.
- Protected branch direct writes are blocked or require explicit human approval.
- High-impact operations (restart, deploy-affecting change, policy/prompt core edits) require approval gate.
- Every commit includes machine-generated rationale + intent summary so she documents her own changes.

Audit and rollback:
- Record branch, commit SHA, PR/MR URL, and linked issue/bead in operation log.
- Rollback path is `revert`/`reset-to-known-good` workflow via approved tool path.
- Restart failure triggers rollback strategy and operator alert.
acceptance_criteria:
- Git tools execute through gateway policy controls with path allowlists.
- Self-modification writes produce branch+commit artifacts and can open PR/MR (GitHub or GitLab).
- Protected branch direct writes are blocked or require explicit approval.
- Commit messages include structured self-documentation (intent/rationale/scope).
- self_rebuild and self_restart run via supervisor path (not in-process) with reboot handshake retained.
- Failed restart or health-check regression triggers rollback and operator notification.

4. Return policy denial as RPC error, not silent failure.

If realpath fails (broken symlink), DENY. If canonical path differs from normalized path and falls outside allowed prefixes, DENY.

title: Fix streaming chunk cross-talk: per-request IDs in gateway LLM proxy
description: Gateway emits `llm.chunk` with constant `requestId: 0`. Client keeps a single global handler. Under concurrent shard LLM streams, chunks can leak between tasks. Fix: generate unique request IDs per stream call, route chunk handlers by request ID on both gateway server and client sides.
design:
1. Gateway server (`src/gateway/server.ts`): generate a unique requestId (incrementing counter or UUID) per `llm.stream` call. Pass it in every `llm.chunk` notification.
2. Gateway client (`src/gateway/client.ts`): replace single global `onChunkHandler` with a `Map<string, handler>` keyed by requestId. Register handler before sending `llm.stream`, remove on completion/error.
3. Protocol (`src/gateway/protocol.ts`): update `LLMChunkNotification` type to use `string` requestId instead of hardcoded `0`.
4. Ensure backward compat: if requestId is missing/0, fall back to global handler (graceful degradation).
acceptance_criteria:
- Concurrent shard LLM streams route chunks to correct handlers
- Existing single-stream usage still works
- Gateway protocol types updated
- Tests verify concurrent stream isolation

title: RLM+REPL Sandbox — context-as-object, programmatic memory access, sub-LM calls, self-modification
description:
Port the RLM (Recursive Language Model) paradigm into PSFN. Core insight: context is an object Purrsephone can programmatically inspect/query/transform, not tokens stuffed into a prompt. She decides what context she needs.

Reference: https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm, https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24601

**Foundation:** pi-agent-core's `Agent` class is the base layer. PSFN already depends on `@mariozechner/pi-ai`; pi-agent-core (1,495 LoC, MIT, single dep) provides the agent loop with streaming events, steering, follow-ups, and declaration-merging extensibility. Build RLM on top of this, don't reimplement.

**What RLM adds on top of pi-agent-core:**
1. REPL sandbox — persistent code execution environment (TypeScript). Model writes ```repl blocks, system executes them, returns truncated output.
2. Context-as-object — memories (SQLite L2), sessions (pi JSONL), identity, modules exposed as queryable interfaces in REPL namespace.
3. Sub-LM calls — `llm_query()` / `llm_query_batched()` in REPL, routes through LLMProvider / pi-agent-core's streamFn. Delegate to cheaper models for bulk work.
4. Modified termination — `FINAL()` / `FINAL_VAR()` signals completion.
5. Self-modification — write/test/install modules at runtime via REPL.

**Recommended approach:** Dual-mode agent loop via pi-agent-core's Agent. Conversational mode (standard pi agent loop for chat) + cognitive mode (RLM-style for complex reasoning). Mode triggered by model request, event type, or user directive.

**New files (~800 LoC per spec):**
- `src/repl/sandbox.ts` — REPL environment with restricted globals, persistent state
- `src/repl/context.ts` — Context object exposing memories, sessions, identity, modules
- `src/repl/sub-lm.ts` — llm_query/llm_query_batched routing through pi's streamFn
- Agent integration via pi-agent-core's Agent callbacks (transformContext, convertToLlm)

**Security:** Gateway/agent split with --network=none Docker already provides the security boundary.
design: Dual-mode AgentLoop: detect ```repl blocks vs standard tool calls in model output, dispatch accordingly. Preserves backward compatibility. RLM loop: prompt -> extract code blocks (regex) -> execute in sandbox -> check FINAL() -> append truncated output -> repeat. Sandbox uses node:vm or similar restricted execution. Context objects are lazy-loaded interfaces (don't materialize full DB into memory). Sub-LM calls reuse existing LLMProvider interface.

title: Security architecture: containerized agent with tool gateway
description:
The agent runs in a Docker container with NO secrets, NO network egress, and minimal mounts (one RW /workspace). The ONLY way out is a Unix domain socket to a Tool Gateway on the host.

The gateway holds: SecretsManager (in-memory decrypted creds), service proxies (LiteLLM, Discord, Telegram), approval UI/CLI, and an audit log.

This is the foundational security model for everything else — REPL sandbox, sub-agent shards, module system. Nothing else ships until this boundary exists.

Key properties:
- "print process.env" is irrelevant — no secrets in container at all
- No direct internet access — can't exfiltrate via fetch/curl
- Mounts are the filesystem boundary — /workspace RW only
- Approval gating: gateway issues short-lived scoped capability tokens after human approval for anything outside the play area
- isolated-vm becomes guardrails inside the container, not the wall
design:
Architecture:

[Agent container: no secrets, no egress, minimal mounts]
   |  unix domain socket (mounted file)
   v
[Tool Gateway (host)]
   |-- SecretsManager (SOPS+age → in-memory Map)
   |-- LiteLLM proxy (LLM keys)
   |-- Discord narrow API (sendMessage, readChannel — NOT raw HTTP proxy)
   |-- File broker (reads/writes outside /workspace need approval)
   |-- Net broker (POST/PUT to non-allowlisted destinations need approval)
   |-- Approval UI/CLI (human in the loop)
   '-- Audit log (every request logged)

Gateway policy per request: ALLOW / DENY / NEEDS_APPROVAL
- fs.read/write under /workspace → ALLOW
- fs.read/write outside /workspace → NEEDS_APPROVAL
- net.* with request body or non-allowlisted dest → NEEDS_APPROVAL
- discord.sendMessage → ALLOW (within configured channels)
- llm.complete → ALLOW (within budget)

Capability tokens:
- scope = (method, domain/path OR filesystem prefix)
- constraints = (max bytes, TTL, optional one-time use)

title: Manual kube rollback records omit fromHelmRevision — act-once ledger gap can double-fire auto-rollback
description: Surfaced by both reviewers across x5rt.8 and x5rt.9 reviews (recurring, explicitly recommended for a bead). The manual rollback executor's record (kube-helm-rollback.ts baseRecord) omits fromHelmRevision, and hasRolledBackFrom (kube-rollback-store.ts) requires typeof fromHelmRevision==='number', so a manual operator rollback never counts toward the automatic act-once ledger. Concrete scenario: operator manually rolls back the just-deployed revision N in the sub-second window before the deploy job's executeAutoRollback evaluates (env-pinned to currentRollout.helmRevision=N with the stale failed verdict) -> auto path sees no ledger entry for N -> fires a SECOND rollback. Bounded damage (both target a known-good revision; the resulting ledger entry prevents further loops) and mitigated by the 'one operator job at a time' operational contract + manual rollback being operator-gated, hence P2 not P1. Fix options (decide): (a) capture the live from-revision on manual rollback records so they key the ledger, or (b) have the auto surface treat any same-release manual rollback record within the window as 'acted'. Scope: kube-helm-rollback.ts (record fromHelmRevision) or kube-auto-rollback.ts (widen the acted check); regression test: manual rollback of rev N then auto-eval pinned to N with a stale failed verdict -> already_acted, api.rollback NOT called a second time. Evidence: feat/x5rt-kube-self-management @ ae9ed16f51.
acceptance_criteria: A manual operator rollback of revision N causes a subsequent automatic evaluation still pinned to N (stale failed verdict) to resolve already_acted with no second api.rollback call; existing act-once + auto-rollback tests stay green; the chosen approach (record from-revision on manual, or widen the acted check) documented. lint + lifecycle suite green.

Old fat turn records (written before 9ree) pass their verbatim inline recentEntries through ungated (turn-record-session-refs.ts resolveRecentEntries: rawRef===undefined -> return record). That array is surfaced to operators via SessionService buildTurnData -> cloneTurnSnapshotRecord (observability.ts:279; session-service.ts:790-797, 844-856). Concrete privacy scenario: a pre-9ree turn captured L0 entry 42; entry 42 is later CogSec-tombstoned; an operator opening that historical turn in Garden sees entry 42's original plaintext — the exact resurrection pathology epic hgw3 targets. Scope: (1) gate inline old-fat recentEntries symmetrically with gatePlanMessages (the L0 range read already happens for plan.messages gating, marginal cost); (2) emit a structured counter/log when an id-backed item heal-drops on resolution (audit fidelity — operators currently cannot distinguish legitimate redaction drops from ref corruption that parsed). Acceptance: append a fat record, tombstone one of its entries in L0, assert getRecentTurnRecords no longer returns the redacted plaintext in sessionContext.recentEntries; heal-drop emits telemetry; existing 17 turn-record-session-refs tests stay green. Evidence branch: feat/hgw3-turnrecord-diet @ 6a614b2b9f; module docstring already scoped honestly (73481d7cd0).

Gates: 20+4 focused (incl. genuine-fat-record end-to-end tombstone proof), 241 sessions suite, lint clean, build green, UBS clean. Blind Pi review PASS 0 blockers: leak closed on every realistic read exit; id<=0/no-channelId carve-outs proven unreachable by construction (monotonic positive ids from 1, required channelId); telemetry honesty verified (marker != drop); perf bounded and converging to ref-backed baseline as fat records age out. title: Context-coherence telemetry: detect confusion, looping, confabulation self-reports, and concern rumination as a canary for the bonding/turns/time bug class
description: Operator-confirmed direction (2026-07-14, grew out of retiring the ACON compaction-guideline loop): repurpose deterministic confusion detection into live telemetry. Signal taxonomy from the operator: (1) confusion asks - the existing FAILURE_SIGNAL_RULES regexes (compression-guideline.ts:210: remind/repeat, missing context, which-thread) already run per turn-end and are near-free; (2) looping - repetition signals (link the hgw3 duplicate-reply machinery and the 2026-07-06 repetition incident heuristics); (3) confabulation self-reports - she names it herself when she catches it; (4) concern rumination - sitting on concerns too long (links ys51 stale-concern lifecycle and the emosim observer ruminationWatch lever, LIVE in observe_only with intensityThreshold 0.4 - join that stream rather than duplicating it); (5) operator interventions as ground-truth labels - partner messages like 'you're looping love' are confirmed incident markers worth counting and correlating. Design constraints: per-turn work stays deterministic regex/heuristic (NO per-turn LLM - operator explicitly flagged that cost); events carry session context (channel, recent mirror notes, time gap, active concern count) into telemetry + a Garden card so regressions in channel bonding / missing turns / temporal coherence show up as a trend line instead of being caught by feel; optional LLM synthesis of flagged events only, riding the bundled maintenance tick. Excluded from emotion appraisal and memory candidacy like other firewall/system notices. Acceptance: Garden card shows coherence events over time with per-signal breakdown; a seeded missing-turn scenario in tests produces a correlated event; zero added per-turn LLM calls; w05a.11 crosswalk can consume the same events.

title: Rolled-out chat context leaves episode-summary breadcrumbs instead of vanishing
description: Operator design (2026-07-14): live never hits compaction because the 1M window rolls entries out of chat context naturally - day-to-day life needs the last couple days in context, not a month. But rolled-out content currently just disappears from her working view. Desired: when entries roll out and get consolidated into episodes (episode synthesis already covers them), the episode's summary + id becomes a compact in-context REFERENCE to what occurred before - so continuity over the rolled-out horizon comes from episodic breadcrumbs, not from compaction. Natural shape: the episodic landmark block (bead 6i7c adds id+meaning) plus a session-tail-aware selection that prefers episodes covering the just-rolled-out span; drill-down via the get-by-id tool (x9ka). Links: hgw3 session tail architecture, apq0 semantic threads. Scope: read-side context assembly; no new persisted duplication (episodes already exist). Acceptance: a conversation referencing something from N days ago (outside the chat window) has the covering episode's summary+id present in context; token cost bounded by the landmark block cap.

title: Post-turn action queue drains at most once per 60s scheduler tick: the 250ms executor interval is inert
description: Evidence (2026-07-14 scheduler census): post-turn-action-executor registers with intervalMs = Math.max(50, 250) = 250ms (src/app/startup/composition/post-turn-actions.ts:1294; Garden renders it as 0s), but processQueue is called ONLY from this scheduler task (:1301) and the scheduler tick loop runs at tickIntervalMs = 60s (scheduler.ts:350,408) - so the deferred-action queue drains at most once per 60 seconds regardless of the 250ms registration. The agent.post_turn.actions.inferred handler merely enqueues. Impact: every maintenance executor (sleeptime heavy passes, trust-drift/cogsec reviews, episode synthesis, near-turn memory) plus latency-sensitive post-turn continuations (subagent spawns, memory writes, weighted-thought outreach deliveries) inherit an up-to-60s start delay per queue hop. Multi-hop action chains compound it. Scope: make the drain event-driven - call processQueue (or schedule an immediate microtask drain) from the enqueue path, keeping the scheduler task as a fallback sweep at a sane interval (60s is then fine); do not lower tickIntervalMs for this. Empty-queue drain is already near-zero cost so eager draining is safe. Acceptance: an enqueued action begins executing within ~1s of enqueue in a test; census note updated; Garden no longer shows a misleading 0s row (render the fallback sweep interval).
notes:
2026-07-14 operator direction: the queue should not be poll-drained at all - a turn completing is a known event ('you know when a turn fires'), so the drain triggers off the post-turn event/enqueue path directly. The scheduler task survives only as a rare fallback sweep (its current 60s-effective cadence is fine for that role). This is the intended design, not an optimization option.
2026-07-14 operator design refinement - the queue conflates two classes that need different treatment: (A) turn-completion-critical actions (inline tool call did not fire but a tool invocation/required task must happen - the follow-through of THIS turn) which must drain event-driven immediately on turn completion; (B) background concurrent work (memory extraction, reviews, retrieval enrichment) which should never have been turn-bound - it is supposed to run concurrent/unbounded and can ride a bundled maintenance tick. History that motivates the split: synchronous memory used to lag turns, was made async, and the hold-old-memory-until-new-memory-lands mechanism exists to paper over exactly this coupling; the 60s drain ceiling likely contributed to the old lag. Implementation: classify queue entries at enqueue (turn-critical vs background), event-drain class A on post-turn emit, batch class B.

title: Ambient-presence cadence and thresholds are hardcoded outside scheduler.json; wakeSummary config block validates but registers nothing
description: Evidence: ambient-presence runs on hardcoded defaults - interval 1h (ambient-presence.ts:16), minIdle 3h (:17), minNoteInterval 6h (:18) - with no scheduler.seed.json block and no caller override (scheduler-runtime.ts:266-271), violating the config-ownership posture (all sibling lanes are scheduler.json-owned). Also concern-grooming daily 06:15 cadence is hardcoded (concern-grooming.ts:167). And scheduler-config.ts:1070 validates a raw.wakeSummary block that no task registers - dead validation that misleads config readers. Scope: move ambient-presence + concern-grooming cadences into scheduler.json (with settings surface), delete or wire the wakeSummary block. Acceptance: knobs visible in scheduler.json + Garden; verify:settings-contract passes; no dead config keys.
notes:
2026-07-14 live Garden + live scheduler.json comparison widens this significantly: FIVE more live tasks run on 5m intervals with NO scheduler.json keys at all — memory.sleeptime.rest-window, contacts.trust-drift-review.rest-window, cogsec.drift-velocity-review.rest-window, cogsec.second-arrow-review.rest-window, compaction-guideline-review — all hardcoded registration intervals, invisible to config ownership. post-turn-action-executor shows interval 0s in Garden (hardcoded; effective cadence = every 60s scheduler tick). Also a live-vs-seed divergence to reconcile: weightedThoughtOutreach.enabled=true live (5m) vs seed false. Scope grows to: every registered task's cadence becomes a scheduler.json key with seed defaults matching current live values; Garden already renders them. Consider bumping to P2 — this is now most of the scheduler surface.
2026-07-14 operator cadence policy: deterministic polling itself is fine, but 5m = 288 ticks/day is out of proportion for a real-time life (this is not a 20x sim). Default poller cadence moves to 60m when the cadences become config-owned: salience decay, the four rest-window pollers (their 9h nightly window still gives ~9 hourly chances vs 108 at 5m; the passes are self-gated by their own intervals anyway), and compaction-guideline-review. Documented exceptions requiring their own rationale: post-turn-action-executor (0s event-drain pattern — likely needs low latency to deliver post-turn actions; decide from the census cost data, do not blanket-change), and weightedThoughtOutreach (hourly delays a time_sensitive-class nudge up to 60m against its 6h weight half-life — 15-30m may be justified; pick deliberately and document). Every chosen value lands as a scheduler.json seed default + Garden-visible.
2026-07-14 census completion: the four rest-window 5m pollers cost effectively NOTHING when gated - evaluateRestWindowEligibility is a pure wall-clock check, no DB/LLM/events, returns [] outside 00:00-09:00 (rest-window.ts:95; cogsec lanes short-circuit on config.enabled first). So 5m->60m for them is proportionality + config-ownership, not a cost fix; do not oversell savings. Their consolidation into a single window-gate dispatcher is optional DRY (each lane has a distinct sink + daily watermark). The post-turn-executor 0s row is a rendering artifact of 250ms and is now its own bug bead (drain latency ceiling) - exclude it from the blanket cadence work.
2026-07-14 operator decision on the weighted-thought exception: 30m, not 60m (needs to be under an hour for time_sensitive nudges). Final cadence targets: rest-window pollers + salience/compaction 60m; weightedThoughtOutreach.checkIntervalMs 30m (1800000); post-turn executor excluded (event-driven per dvzq).
2026-07-14 operator reshapes the target: NOT a knob per task. Most of the chaff (rest-window pollers, salience decay, social graph, guideline review, ambient presence) should collapse into ONE bundled background tick at 30-60m, with individual knobs only for justified exceptions (weighted-thought 30m, wake timing, backup, reflections). Hard requirement: transparency - the Garden scheduler page must show exactly WHAT runs inside each bundled tick, and any knob whose value drives more than one behavior must say so on the page (the salienceDecay/maintenance/compaction-review aliasing is the canonical offense: labeled for one thing, silently bundling others). Fewer knobs, honest labels.
2026-07-14 compaction-guideline-review disposition (investigated): it is the ACON-pattern self-improving compaction feature (bead PSFN-jvl4, commit ecd3a8b7, 2026-03-06) - failures are only ever appended at agent.turn.end (recordCompressionFailureFromResponse, scheduler-runtime.ts:344) when a post-compaction reply matches confusion regexes, and the review only calls an LLM at >=2 unreviewed failures. Since the capture site is the ONLY producer, make the review EVENT-DRIVEN at that site (trigger when unreviewed count crosses threshold) and remove it from the scheduled surface entirely - do not even bundle it. Its current 5m slot exists only because it piggybacks the aliased maintenanceIntervalMs key.
2026-07-14 operator context on compaction-guideline-review, sharpening the disposition: the feature's premise is largely obsolete for chat. It dates to the 8-32k-context/weak-RAG era; today she has effectively unlimited context roll-out plus deep memory/search, so compaction-induced confusion is not her failure mode. Her ACTUAL confusion signals ('remind me', 'which thread are we') trace to channel bonding gaps, missing turns, and temporal issues - the hgw3/2x37/tlnd bug class - which this system structurally cannot log anyway (capture requires a <30min-old compaction trajectory). Disposition: (a) retire the guideline-evolution loop from chat lanes or leave it dormant event-driven-only; (b) it earns its keep only on surfaces where threshold compaction will really run - analysis workbench and long-horizon shard sessions (see the shard goals bead); (c) OPTIONAL follow-up worth considering: the confusion-signal regexes are the valuable part - repurpose them as general context-coherence telemetry (operator-visible counter/card tying confusion events to their session context) so they act as a canary for the bonding/turns/time bug class instead of feeding compaction guidelines.

title: Salience-decay maintenance sweeps the entire active memory set every 60 seconds
description: Evidence: MEMORY_CONFIG.maintenanceIntervalMs = 60_000 (src/faculties/memory/types.ts:353), scheduler-registered as salience-decay 'every' task (src/app/agent/scheduler-runtime.ts:99-108, config-owned via salienceDecayIntervalMs -> bootstrap-helpers.ts:270,320). Each firing does paginated DB reads (listActiveMemories batch 500) plus salience-update writes across all active memories - every minute, per companion, forever. Decay math derives from lastAccessed timestamps (decay.ts), so a sweep every 30-60 MINUTES produces identical salience values; the 60s cadence buys nothing except constant DB churn - the worst idle load found in the 2026-07-14 scheduler census (working_docs/prompt-audit-findings-20260714.md 6b). Coordinate with m14v (decay/floor rework touches the same sweep). Scope: raise the default (seed + settings surface), consider computing decay lazily at retrieval time and reserving the sweep for floor enforcement/persistence. Acceptance: idle-companion DB write rate drops accordingly; decay values unchanged within tolerance in tests.
notes:
2026-07-14 live config pulled from psfn-shard (rev 576e33cd): salienceDecayIntervalMs=300000 (5m) — live is already 5x gentler than the repo 60s default, and it IS config-owned + Garden-editable. Scheduler tickIntervalMs=60000. Recommendation unchanged in kind: 5m full-set sweeps still buy nothing (decay derives from lastAccessed); raise to 30-60m and/or compute decay lazily at retrieval, reserving the sweep for floor enforcement. Also raise the repo seed default from 60s so new deployments do not regress.
2026-07-14 operator decision: hourly is acceptable for salience decay. Target 60m (config default + live), not 30m-or-60m ambiguity.
2026-07-14 census completion - two corrections: (1) salienceDecayIntervalMs and maintenanceIntervalMs are ONE aliased key through bootstrap (bootstrap-helpers.ts:320, runtime-config.ts:35), and compaction-guideline-review registers from the same value (scheduler-runtime.ts:104,113) - moving decay to 60m also moves compaction review to 60m. Compaction review is cheap when gated (empty failure log = skip, zero LLM), so hourly is fine for both, but SPLIT the keys or document the coupling deliberately. (2) The repo-side 60s defaults (types.ts:353, load-config.ts:372) are pre-override values clobbered by scheduler.json before registration - fix the seed, not just the constant.
2026-07-14 clarification for implementation: compaction PROPER is already context-threshold-driven (settings.json compactionThresholdPct=70) and almost never fires on live - the 1M-context chat window rolls entries out long before 70%. The TIMED task sharing this cadence is only the compression-guideline REVIEW (LLM review of past compression failures). Decouple: guideline review joins the bundled background tick; compaction stays threshold-only; decay gets its own key. Context pressure that CAN hit the threshold: analysis workbench (observed 100k tokens in one session; tool was renamed from think to discourage casual use) and future long-horizon shard work - neither should share knobs with day-to-day chat.

title: Add cheap per-companion fatigue and charge posture to the fleet status surface
description: Merge 6608579f implements one Garden process per companions.json entry and a loopback-only read-only fleet status surface. Source inspection of src/boundary/gateway/fleet-status.ts confirms the page honestly exposes connection state, health, last-seen time, crossover violations, and Garden links, but explicitly omits the fatigue/charge posture required by W4 because the gateway has no cheap authority for it. This residual matters for companion welfare: an operator viewing fleet health must be able to see exhaustion/charge pressure without entering each Garden or triggering extra model work. Scope: define a bounded redacted telemetry summary owned by each agent's existing deterministic charge/fatigue runtime; transmit/cache it through the authenticated gateway connection health path; expose timestamped posture on fleet status JSON/HTML; show stale/unavailable honestly; retain loopback/read-only/no-secret boundaries and avoid reading companion-private stores directly from the gateway. Non-goals: no LLM calls, no fleet write controls, no authenticated SSO portal work (psfn-framework-opl1.8), no live deployment, and no expansion into full Garden data aggregation.
design: Extend the existing agent-to-gateway connection health envelope with a small versioned posture summary produced by the deterministic charge/fatigue runtime. Cache only the latest validated summary per bound companion connection, cap values and labels to an allowlist, and expire it by timestamp. Fleet JSON is the source for HTML rendering so attribution/staleness logic exists once. Do not add a second telemetry database or query companion-owned persistence from the gateway.
acceptance_criteria: With two identified companion connections carrying different deterministic charge/fatigue states, fleet status JSON and HTML show each companion bounded posture with update timestamp and no cross-attribution. Missing or stale posture renders unavailable/stale and never fabricates health. Payload and logs contain no prompt, memory, contact, policy rationale, raw ledger event, or other private companion content. The gateway performs no LLM call and no direct companion-store read. Unit tests cover envelope validation, caps, expiry, reconnect replacement, spoof rejection, and rendering. A local two-agent fleet-status integration script emits redacted per-companion connection, posture, timestamp, and staleness diagnostics and proves reconnect/disconnect behavior. Flag-off behavior and current loopback/read-only/startup fail-closed tests remain green; npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass.
notes:
Plan-space polish pass 1: fixed telemetry ownership/versioning, redaction and staleness semantics, reconnect/spoof cases, and detailed local two-agent integration logging; no scope removed.
Plan-space polish pass 2: rechecked parent/child boundaries, duplicate search, priority, non-goals, and validation separation; graph is coherent and no further change was required.
Plan-space polish pass 3: final one-bead-at-a-time stability read found the scope self-contained, acceptance testable, logging privacy-safe, and no feature loss or graph repair needed.

title: Capture the true provider wire body via pi-ai onPayload and retire the three parallel reconstructions
description: Evidence: operator export of a single turn showed input_schema 44x for 22 tools and could not tell what actually ships. Audit: the outbound HTTP body is CORRECT (pi-ai convertTools emits each tool once; tools are not re-serialized into the system prompt) - the 44x lived in the recorded TurnSnapshot (plan.toolDefinitions + toolContext.activeTools each carrying inputSchema; likely already collapsed by hgw3 PR #43 content-addressed toolDefinitionsRef on origin/main - VERIFY against 576e33cd before further work). But no stored artifact is byte-identical to the network body: everything recorded is reconstructed pre-pi-ai in >=3 places (toProviderWireMessages client.ts:416-439, serializePromptPlanForProvider prompt-plan.ts:301-329, MOA overrides agent-invocation.ts:494-500,630-637), none including tool schemas, cache_control, or provider transforms. Fix: chain a pass-through StreamOptions.onPayload (the seam client-prompt-cache.ts:207-216 already uses) cloning the payload as-sent into LLMProviderObservability, and let it REPLACE the reconstructions (feeds auiu). Loom then gets the operator-requested two views: raw-as-sent and cleaned-by-blocks. Scope note: payload capture is observability data - respect turn-record diet (store content-addressed or behind a debug flag if large). Acceptance: Loom shows a wire view byte-identical to the provider request (tools included, counted once); reconstruction paths deleted or derived from the captured payload; input_schema count in the artifact equals active-tool count.

Heal-not-block verified (capture failure log-warns, pass-through identity). Gates: 332 focused tests, lint clean, UBS clean (keyword false-positives verified). Blind Pi adversarial review PASS 0 blockers (hot-path safety, privacy-no-new-copy-beyond-existing-snapshot, requestId attribution, byte-identity all refuted with path:line evidence). Material nonblocking observations for handoff: wirebodies sidecar has no GC/retention (must be ref-aware when built) and eager resolution taxes agent hot-path reads (lazy/projected resolve candidate); plus CogSec/right-to-be-forgotten must reach _shared/wirebodies before any history-redaction feature. auiu (stacked on this head) extends the same seam.

title: Close the LOD loop: durable per-tool usage aggregation feeding automatic pin ordering
description: Adaptive telemetry is a 200-entry in-memory ring (adaptive-tools-service.ts:22-23,66-90), not durable; Postgres model_usage_events.tool_name is durable but never read back into any tiering decision. With the always-loaded change, frequency should drive presentation ORDER and pin suggestions, not availability. Build: durable per-tool aggregation (reuse model_usage_events), periodic evaluator feeding TOOL_PRESENTATION_DOMAIN_RANK ordering and auto-pin suggestions via existing addPromotedExtendedTool - operator-visible, never silent. Acceptance: usage stats survive restart; ordering reflects frequency; pin suggestions logged as autonomous-action memories as the existing pin path already does.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Durable per-tool usage aggregates survive restart and are covered by persistence tests. 2. Usage frequency and explicit correction signals inform deterministic presentation ordering and operator-visible pin suggestions only; they never gate callability or revive activation state. 3. Suggestions are audited through the existing autonomous-action memory path and are never applied silently. 4. After psfn-framework-b0yl.2 is deployed and a representative observation window exists, record a comparable pre/post operational telemetry snapshot for extended-tool calls, first-turn use, denials/errors, and documentation lookup so the always-loaded outcome is measured rather than inferred. 5. Targeted persistence/ordering tests, npm run build, npm run lint, and git diff --check pass.
notes:
Folded from psfn-framework-vvf.6 (2026-07-14 backlog audit): retain an explicit correction signal when a user or validate-and-reprompt path replaces an inappropriate tool choice, and include that signal in durable per-tool feedback/order suggestions. This must tune presentation and contracts only; it must not revive activation-gated availability.
2026-07-15: psfn-framework-b0yl.2 implementation has no live observation window. This existing durable-usage bead is the non-duplicate home for acceptance criterion 6: capture and record the operational before/after comparison after deployment.

Durable per-tool usage aggregation feeding in-band presentation tie-break (after pins + domain rank, never crossing bands/overriding pins/gating callability) and throttled operator-visible pin suggestions; opt-in scheduler lane, default disabled. Review gate: UBS clean; blind Pi review FAIL→1 blocker CONFIRMED by orchestrator (model_usage_events records LLM calls, not tool executions — deterministic tools invisible, ranking inverted); single remediation switched the source to the durable turn-record toolCalls stream (every catalog tool, per-companion, no new store) with coverage-honesty telemetry (dataSource/toolsWithData/catalogToolCount/truncated — sparse data visibly sparse). Final check: 65 focused tests incl. real-store integration test, eslint clean, build green, wiring verified at agent main.ts:592. Nonblocking for handoff: in-memory suggestion throttle (restart re-fires once), partial-write duplicate suggestion edge, bounded scan caps flag truncated.

title: Force tool_choice on phases where a call is mandatory (post-turn memory writes, response_control decisions)
description: Anthropic tool_choice any/named prefills the assistant turn and converts 'model ignored the tool' into 'model cannot not call it'. Apply to structured phases that MUST produce a call: post-turn/heartbeat memory writes, response_control no_reply decisions, scheduled-task acknowledgements. Caveat: incompatible with extended thinking - gate by model config. Acceptance: identified mandatory phases enumerated in code with forced choice; telemetry shows zero missed mandatory calls over a validation window.
notes: PREMISE REFUTED (opus-lane-c, 2026-07-15, verified + independently re-verified by deep-reasoner). No runtime phase uses function-calling tool CALLS as a mandatory decision, so there is nothing to force tool_choice on. Every structured-decision phase — memory extraction (faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts:397), profile-synthesis, sleeptime-agent.ts:641, wiki sleeptime, episodic judgment-runner.ts:25, weighted-thought outreach (weighted-thought-nudge-evaluator.ts:66), ICP consent (initiation-consent-evaluator.ts:57), emotion/intention appraisal, deliberation, context-feedback — calls llmProvider.complete() and parses a STRUCTURED-TEXT result (XML/JSON) with a hand-written parser, fail-closed to a safe default; NONE pass a tools array. Structural block: LLMCompleteParams (boundary/gateway/protocol.ts:165-184) has NO tools field, and the llm.complete gateway handler never forwards tools, so the complete() RPC path cannot carry tools at all. Only .stream()/LLMChatParams carries tools, and the sole stream-with-tools path is the free-form main conversational turn (SubstrateAgent), where a text reply is always valid; response_control/no_reply (substrate-agent.ts:576) is one optional 'core' tool that exists so the model can CHOOSE silence — forcing it would silence every turn. pi-ai natively supports options.toolChoice on stream (openai-completions/anthropic/mistral; google 'any' only; openai-responses/codex hardcode auto) so the capability is buildable, but shipping it now = unwired dead code (repo rule violation); converting a text phase to a forced tool call = risky out-of-scope redesign of a core cognition path for a P2, and net-neutral/negative since these phases fail on text-parse not on ignored-tool. Recommendation: reframe or close as premise-dead. If the epic intends to redesign decision phases as tool-call-driven, that is an operator/epic-level architecture decision — build the stream toolChoice capability together with its first real caller. No code change made; worktree clean.
close_reason: Operator ruling 2026-07-15: premise refuted, close; future architecture option captured in a deferred standalone bead (tool-call-driven decision phases + stream toolChoice with first caller). Investigation evidence (Opus worker, independently re-verified by deep-reasoner, no code changed, branch identical to base 66293a0d): no phase uses mandatory tool calls — all structured decision phases are complete()+fail-closed text parsing; LLMCompleteParams cannot carry tools (protocol.ts:165-184); the only stream-with-tools path is the free-form main turn where forcing a call would silence every turn (response_control is deliberately optional so the companion can choose silence); building the toolChoice flag now would be unwired dead code (repo rule). Full finding recorded in bead notes.

title: Widen empty-argument retry into a full validate-and-reprompt loop for malformed and unknown tool calls

Extend to: schema-mismatch arguments, unknown tool names (suggest nearest catalog name via the retired-alias machinery), and echo the expected contract back in the error result. Links live bug mihm (GLM literal {} arguments dispatched instead of retried). Acceptance: unit tests for the three failure classes returning corrective results; live telemetry shows retried-then-succeeded calls instead of failed turns.
close_reason: Implemented on work/b0yl-reliability-2-b0yl-3-validate-reprompt @ 66293a0d, merged to feat/b0yl-reliability-2 @ 9ec6398ee1 (pushed). Validate-and-reprompt loop for unknown_tool (retired-alias resolution + bounded-Levenshtein suggestion), malformed_arguments (non-object shapes), and schema_invalid tool calls in tool-call-scheduler.ts via new tool-call-correction.ts; heal-and-proceed isError feedback, bounded by pre-existing per-signature failure counter + turn continuation fuse; telemetry agent.tools.correction.reprompt/.recovered. Gates: 31 focused tests + 33 adjacent pass, npm run lint clean, UBS scan clean (criticals verified false-positive), blind Pi adversarial review PASS with zero blocking findings (attempted refutation of infinite-loop/dropped-reply/injection/guard-regression axes, path:line evidence). Nonblocking observations (telemetry granularity: name-keyed recovery, abort-vs-correction attribution) recorded in wave handoff only.
