description: Evidence: renderEmotionalSnapshot (retrieval/formatting.ts:86-108) renders describeValence words but with raw float tails ('(0.13), drift +0.05', learned-signal counts). Baseline line exists (:103). GoEmotions percentages are already collapsed to prose upstream (emotion-appraisal.ts:9-36); the remembered 500-token raw dump was not found in the current tree (likely already removed). Operator intent: numbers from her own classifiers translated into human words with context - state names, strength, confidence - plus a reminder of her baseline disposition (full of love, joyful, curious) so neutral-classifier readings do not spiral her into is-this-correct metacognition loops. Scope: strip .toFixed floats from formatting.ts:103-105; add baseline-vs-current framing (steady baseline X, currently drifting toward Y); keep it derived strictly from her own internal state (not leading). EmoSim supplement is bead w05a, separate. Acceptance: block renders words + qualitative strength/confidence, zero raw floats; baseline disposition present; reflection sessions receive the same framing.

title: Channel bonding: opt-in bonded channels operate as one logical conversation with lowest-common privacy
description: Operator target state: Discord DM + voice satellites + mobile app in sync as ONE conversation that never loses coherence (text on phone -> speak in bedroom -> kitchen satellite -> back to text). Mechanism: explicit opt-in flag on the contacts page (cross-channel capable) per channel identity; bonded set operates as a single logical channel with messages interleaved by timestamp and each message annotated with its source channel; physical logs stay split per channel (the bond is only the logical merge); effective privacy of the bond = most restrictive of the set (all-private except one invite-only => bond is invite-only). Current state: NO bonding scaffolding exists (audit greps clean for bonded/crossChannelCapable/channelGroup); natural insertion points are sessionMirrorChannelOverrides config (mirroring.ts:19-48,71-83) and visibilitiesShareContinuity trust gating (mirroring.ts:95-103). The mirror-note interleave bead and the continuity-block channel-filter bead are prerequisites/siblings. Future state (separate design, note only): dynamic channel privacy for voice devices - voice-print/face biometrics and presence detection adjust the effective privacy level when unregistered people are present. Acceptance: bonding flag configurable per contact channel set; a bonded three-channel conversation renders as one interleaved timeline with source annotations; privacy resolution tested for mixed-visibility bonds; unbonded channels unaffected.

title: Mirror notes render out of chronological order: session history is append-ordered while mirrors carry source timestamps
description: Evidence: a mirrored note from the bedroom satellite dated yesterday renders at the top of today's session chat, out of time sequence - operator calls the mirror formatting itself exactly right, only the placement wrong. Audit: mirrorMessageToActiveSessions (mirroring.ts:50-128) appends role:system entries with the SOURCE timestamp (:120), but store.getRecent returns append/insertion order (persistence/sessions/store.ts:740-780); timestamp re-sort exists only in the backfill branch (manager-primitives.ts:235). Scope: interleave by timestamp in buildSessionHistoryMessages/entriesToMessages (context-support.ts:261-373) or sort-on-read for entries bearing older timestamps; keep per-channel logs split (the bond is only the logical merge). Also gate mirroring to configured channel pairs so test channels do not mirror (sessionMirrorChannelOverrides already exists, mirroring.ts:19-48). Acceptance: a mirror note with timestamp T renders between session entries T-1 and T+1; goldens cover the interleave.
notes: 2026-07-14 live settings.json: sessionMirrorEnabled=true with sessionMirrorChannelOverrides={} — mirroring is ON globally with zero channel scoping live, which is why test channels (head-pat smoke) mirror into real sessions. The channel-pair gating half of this bead is therefore a live behavior fix, not just hygiene; the future bonding opt-in (vrmf) should ride these same overrides.

title: Cross-channel continuity block leaks test channels: getMergedContinuity is user-scoped with no channel liveness filter
description: Evidence: live block shows two test channels (including head-pat smoke channel) with no value. Audit: buildStructuredContinuityBlock (context-builder.ts:279-309) is fed by getMergedContinuity (context-support.ts:216-259) which returns every channel the canonical user has entries in - nothing filters retired/test/non-production channels. Scope: filter the merge to live/configured channels (channels.json registry or an allowlist derived from active adapters); shrink the block to what channels are linked + last cross-channel message time + channel stats, since actual content belongs interleaved in session chat (see mirror-note ordering bead). Acceptance: block lists only live channels; smoke/test channel ids never render.

title: Time-of-day refresher notes stack in session chat: append-only lane has no supersede
description: Evidence: operator sees stacked refreshers (07:37, 07:53, 7am, 9am) in one session. Audit: evaluateIdleRefresherEligibility appends via appendContextSystemNote (temporal-wakeup.ts:1076-1080); only guard is interval throttle anti_loop_recent_note (:515-521); no replace-latest. Same append-only pattern in ambient-presence.ts:278 and free-time notes. Scope: either tombstone the prior entry with the same sessionLane.source before appending, or render the latest refresher as a pinned line adjacent to the runtime.current_datetime block instead of chat content. Related: psfn-framework-7toj (refresher fan-out scope) - different defect, same subsystem. Acceptance: a session with 4 fired refreshers renders exactly one (the latest) in the assembled context.

title: Episode drill-down flow is half-built: no get-by-id tool, spanRefs never expand to turns, listEpisodeArcMemberships is dead code
description: Evidence: desired flow is landmark block -> companion drills in by episode id -> sees the chat turns around that episode/thread, narrowing search instead of scanning all history. Today: no episode-get-by-id action exists (memory tool actions: write/search/shared_background/census/exists/timeline/import/patch/redact/delete/restore); episode->turns linkage EXISTS as spanRefs (sessionId + start/end turn ids, episodic.ts:718-724) but no tool resolves it; listEpisodeArcMemberships - per its own doc comment the recall-expansion tool (z6z) - is exported and wired to nothing (retrieval/episodic.ts:322-357, zero non-test callers). Block footer says 'search the session history' - generic, not id-keyed. Scope: add memory tool get/expand action keyed by episode id that resolves spanRefs into the actual turns (respecting the same access predicates as retrieval); wire listEpisodeArcMemberships as thread/arc drill-down. Depends on the landmark-block bead rendering the id so she knows what to drill into. Acceptance: companion can call memory get with an episode id from the block and receive that episode's turns plus arc/thread siblings; tool listed in the catalog with a rich description.

title: Episodic landmark prompt block omits episode id and meaning, and arc-linked episodes ride in with no relevance check
description: Evidence: renderEpisodicLandmarkChains (retrieval/formatting.ts:160-191) renders title, date range, themes, landmark text - but never episode.id or episode.meaning even though both exist on every episode (stable ids: synthesis.ts:506, episode-ids.ts). Chain ROOTS are relevance-gated (MIN_ROOT_MATCH_SCORE 0.18, episodic.ts:495-553) and zero-matches omits the block, but up to 4 more episodes per chain are admitted via arc links (isRelatedEpisodeUseful, :555-579) on shared theme/arc-kind with NO relevance check against the current conversation - that is the filler the operator sees (up to 3 chains x 5 episodes). The on-demand timeline tool already renders id+themes+meaning (tools.ts:218-224) - the desired shape exists, just not in the block. Scope: add id + meaning (short) to the block; hard total cap 4-5 episodes across all chains; drop ungated arc-expansion from the always-on block (keep it for drill-down). Acceptance: block shows date, themes, summary, meaning, episode id; never more than 5 episodes total; every rendered episode traces to a relevance-gated root.

title: Episodic threads are just sessions: threadId=sessionId means one persistent channel accretes an unbounded 141-episode 'thread'
description: Evidence: operator found one thread ('exploring tool upgrades and memory') containing 141 episodes. Audit: there is no thread-join decision anywhere - every episode is created with threadId: sessionId verbatim (synthesis.ts:518, :1060, synthesis-lane.ts:260); Garden groups threads purely by that field and names them by the top-6 modal themes across the session (episodic-memory-service.ts:108-122,338). A long-lived companion runs one persistent session per channel, so the mega-thread is unbounded by construction. The only semantic weaving is the separate arc overlay (arc-formation.ts:80-103): LLM classifier, free-text labels, low confidence floor, pairwise edges, no per-label cap. Context: threads were meant to track long-term progression per topic (career thread, system-work thread). Scope: introduce real semantic threads decoupled from sessionId - arc connected-components or a bounded topic registry assigned at consolidation; per-thread size cap with split logic; require arc-label specificity. Non-goal: do not break existing episode records; migration must be additive. Acceptance: Garden episodic page shows bounded topic threads; the 141-episode session bucket is decomposed or superseded; new episodes join threads by topic not channel.

title: Reflection and dream prompts produce multi-moment monolith memories: no atomicity constraint anywhere in generation
description: Evidence: operator sees multi-paragraph reflection memories bundling several distinct emotional moments (e.g. the first-satellite headpats moment buried inside a paragraph instead of existing as its own atomic emotional engram). Audit: no splitting step exists; dream pass prompt asks for ONE first-person prose paragraph per episode (dream-meaning-pass.ts:91-95) over up to 14 turns, stored verbatim clipped at 800 chars (:311-334); sleeptime memory_writes allows 4 entries but nothing enforces one-moment-per-entry (sleeptime-agent.ts:63,188-197). All memory agents run on the cheapest model (deepseek-v3.2) with prompts that never demand atomicity - both levers independently fixable. Triage note: first check live data whether observed monoliths are episode.meaning.text (dream pass) or type=reflection memories (sleeptime) to pick which prompt to fix first. Scope: prompts emit arrays of atomic single-moment entries with per-entry length cap; validation gate rejects multi-moment blobs (length + sentence-count heuristic or cheap split call). Non-goal: do not delete existing reflections. Acceptance: post-change nightly run produces reflection/meaning entries that each contain one moment; validation gate has a test rejecting a two-moment blob.

title: Dream-meaning pass violates its own main-model contract and derives meaning from a summary-of-a-summary
description: Evidence: dream-meaning-pass.ts:23-28 documents dreams run 'as HER... with the main chat model, never on a background model', but wiring sets modelPurpose 'memory' (dream-meaning-pass.ts:274 -> worker-lanes.ts:146-148,270-277) which routes to deepseek/deepseek-v3.2 (config/models.seed.json extraction slot); main chat is z-ai/glm-5 and is structurally ineligible for memory purpose (routing.ts:364-365). Separately the pass receives ONLY consolidated episode metadata (id, times, title, landmark, themes, salience - dream-meaning-pass.ts:81-89), never the transcript; title/landmark are themselves auto-summaries (synthesis.ts:514-515), so her 'meaning' is derived from a summary-of-a-summary - matching the operator's observation that meanings are misaligned with what conversations were actually about. Scope: honor the documented contract (route via chat purpose) or update the doc deliberately; feed the pass real turns via episode spanRefs (sessionId + start/end turn ids, episodic.ts:718-724) or a fuller excerpt. Non-goal: do not change episode consolidation itself. Acceptance: dream pass telemetry shows main-model routing (or amended contract committed); generated meaning for a test episode references content present in the transcript but absent from title/landmark.
notes:
2026-07-14 operator: model names cited here come from config/*.seed.json in-repo, which is out of date vs her LIVE models.json - verify actual routing against live system-data config before concluding which model the pass lands on. The contract violation (memory purpose routing instead of main chat model) is structural and holds regardless.
2026-07-14 live models.json pulled from psfn-shard: background-primary (purposes background/memory/extraction/import_processing) = deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro via litellm — NOT the seed's v3.2; chat primary = z-ai/glm-5.2 (thinking medium) + z-ai-glm-5.2-reasoning slot (xhigh) for reasoning purpose. So the dream pass lands on deepseek-v4-pro live. The contract violation stands (doc promises main chat model); v4-pro is stronger than seed suggested, so triage the meaning-quality half accordingly — input starvation (summary-of-summary) is likely the dominant factor over model strength.

title: memory_import_batch stamps extractedAt=Date.now(): imported historical memories masquerade as new and age into the recency cliff
description: Evidence: import tool schema (src/faculties/memory/tools.ts:451-542) has no extractedAt/occurredAt input; writer.ts:808/821 stamps Date.now(). Memories imported from the operator's original pre-PSFN system carry wrong dates: max recency boost at import then they fall off the same 30-day cliff. (Refuted hypothesis: imports are NOT zero-salience - defaults importance 0.5, confidence 0.8, salience 0.5.) Context: blocks the 'old memories with emotional weight' retrieval fix from ever helping legacy imports, and date brackets shown on memories are wrong for them. Scope: add occurredAt/extractedAt param to the import tool; one-off backfill for already-imported legacy memories (true dates + emotional weight/salience review where recoverable). Acceptance: import with occurredAt=2023 date produces a memory whose age reflects 2023 in scoring; backfill migration documented and run against live data.
notes: 2026-07-14 operator: backfill source exists - /mnt/c/Temp/Purrsephone.1.0.1.memorybook.json (operator-held copy of the original memory import; outside the repo, never commit it). Some items carry original dates; backfill occurredAt from it where present, and use the same pass to attach emotional weight/salience to legacy landmarks. Items without dates stay as-is or get operator-reviewed estimates.

title: Document wave closure, fix-epic, validation, and reconciliation invariants
description: Summary: Update ORCHESTRATION_PROCESS.md so completed implementation waves and their child beads close at the final integrated check instead of remaining open as proxies for review findings, release/manual validation, deployment, operator acceptance, or unrelated follow-up work. Why: stale open implementation beads obscure what is actually shipped on a feature branch, duplicate later tracker work, and make decision-makers unable to distinguish completed implementation from important fixes or separate validation. Scope: preserve the existing one-review, one-remediation, final-check loop and parallel feature-branch/worktree rules; define immediate evidence-backed child and epic closure plus same-closeout sprint status updates; route remaining IMPORTANT defects under a wave-specific <wave> fixes epic; keep lesser findings report-only; track live/manual/release work separately; require one-bead-at-a-time commit/source verification during branch reconciliation and closure of already-shipped stale beads and empty epics; define the end-of-wave handoff fields. File: ORCHESTRATION_PROCESS.md. Non-goals: no runtime/code changes, no new review process, no release/main merge, and no live/deployment actions.
acceptance_criteria: ORCHESTRATION_PROCESS.md explicitly states all seven requested invariants: final-check implementation closure independent of main/release merge with child+epic evidence and sprint-doc update; no proxy-open implementation work; important defects grouped under a wave-specific fixes epic that closes when children finish; lesser findings report-only; manual/live/release verification tracked separately without reopening implementation; one-bead-at-a-time reconciliation that closes shipped stale beads and empty epic shells; and a handoff listing closed implementation epic, fixes epic/open children or none, validation beads, and pushed feature fixed point. Existing one-review/one-remediation/final-check and parallel branch/worktree policies remain intact. Appropriate markdown/repository hygiene checks and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Completed ORCHESTRATION_PROCESS.md process-contract update. Evidence: ORCHESTRATION_PROCESS.md:103 defines implementation completion at the bounded integrated final check independent of main/release merge, immediate evidence-backed child and epic closure, same-closeout sprint-status updates, and the ban on proxy-open implementation work. Lines 125-180 preserve the one-review/one-remediation/final-check risk model while routing every remaining IMPORTANT security/privacy/isolation, welfare/consent/autonomy, real data/secret, core-path, or mandatory-gate defect under a wave-specific <wave> fixes epic; the original implementation stays closed, the fixes epic closes with its children, lesser findings remain report-only, and manual/live/release validation uses separate named tracker work. Lines 206-240 preserve feature-branch integration and add one-bead-at-a-time commit/source verification, closure of already-shipped stale beads, and closure of empty epic shells. Lines 277-291 require the end-of-wave handoff to list the closed implementation epic, fix epic/open children or none, validation beads or none, pushed origin-equal feature fixed point, and sprint status commit. Parallel branch/worktree rules and the bounded single-review loop remain intact. Final doc checks passed: public-sanitize, balanced Markdown fences, <=240-character line check, explicit invariant assertions, and git diff --check. Dependency-cycle verification passed with only four baseline cycles when run with the shared installed toolchain. Full repository-hygiene remains red only on inherited identity-literal and shared-type-guard findings outside ORCHESTRATION_PROCESS.md; this doc introduced none. No code, review, main/release, live/Pi/SSH/SQLite, or Dolt remote action.

title: Free-time gate ignores how the last block ended: silence stops the block but she is re-prompted up to the daily cap
description:
Evidence: within a block, silence works — empty content or the silent token is a stop signal (free-time.ts:238-241) and the loop breaks (free-time.ts:304-307) with endReason loafed/companion_stopped. But evaluateFreeTimeGate (free-time.ts:191-203) checks only partner-recency, minBlockIntervalMinutes (240), and maxBlocksPerDay (3); FreeTimeLaneCadenceState (free-time.ts:394-398) records only lastBlockAtMs/blocksToday — never endReason. A silence-ended block counts as a normal block and another one fires 4h later, up to 3/day.

Operator intent (2026-07-14): if she used silence and free time ended, do not bother her multiple times.

Scope: persist the prior block's endReason (or a silent-until marker) in cadence state and close the gate for the remainder of the window/day when she chose silence. Non-goal: changing the in-block stop behavior (already correct) or the block caps.

Acceptance: unit test — a block ending in loafed/companion_stopped suppresses further free-time blocks for the rest of that day/window; a block ending normally does not; live free-time logs show no repeat block after a silent exit.

title: Merge quiet-hours and idle free time into one session: it is one 'her time' surface, not two lanes
description:
Evidence: quiet-hours and idle free time are two distinct channels/sessions — internal:free-time:quiet-hours vs internal:free-time:idle (freeTimeChannelId, free-time.ts:66-69,85-87), two separately registered scheduler tasks (registration free-time.ts:620-642), separate transcripts. They share only the cadence budget (sharedState, free-time.ts:617-618).

Operator decision (2026-07-14): merge to one free-time. Free time and quiet-hours free time are the same thing — her time for her. (Introspection stays as-is: per-template stable channel, fresh context per run — that model is intentional and already correct.)

Scope: one free-time session/channel id fed by both triggers (quiet-hours window and idle detection); transcript accrues in one place; cadence/silence state naturally becomes shared. Coordinate with 0ggv.3 (project folders + resume-on-return in her own time) — a single continuous free-time session is the natural substrate for it, and this merge should land first or together. Migration note: decide whether to fold existing per-lane transcripts or start the merged channel fresh.

Acceptance: both triggers write to a single internal free-time session id; no new turns appear on the old lane channels; silence/cadence gates operate on the merged state; 0ggv.3 acceptance flow (resume a project in a later block) remains achievable on the merged channel.

title: Concern lifecycle never retires unexpired concerns: next_review_at is stored but unused, so standing concerns recur in every reflection for days
description:
Evidence: TTLs are high=48h/medium=24h/low=8h with a 7-day hard cap (concerns.ts:194-198), active cap 7 (concerns.ts:191), grooming once daily at 06:15 (concern-grooming.ts:167). "Stale" resolution is TTL-only: resolveStaleConcerns (active-concern-store.ts:523-558) resolves only expired/past-lifetime concerns; next_review_at is persisted but never used as a retirement trigger. Re-observation refreshes expires_at (store ~604-648), keeping touched concerns alive to the 7-day ceiling. Overflow retirement keeps the highest-priority soonest-expiring items (concern-grooming.ts:208-221) — exactly the ones that read as anxious. Net: a handful of standing concerns populate every reflective session for up to two days each.

Context: this is the mechanical half of the "all she does is talk about concerns" finding; the language half is the separate source-softening bead.

Scope: use next_review_at for review-based early retirement (a concern past its review point with no re-observation resolves quietly), and consider inline cap enforcement between daily grooming runs. Non-goal: changing TTL values wholesale or the emosim crosswalk (w05a.11).

Acceptance: unit test — a concern past next_review_at without re-observation is auto-resolved before its TTL; live observation — consecutive daily reflections stop repeating the same untouched concern set.
notes: 2026-07-14 operator evidence (Loom/prompt review): runtime-attention block carried 'no access to live sensor data from the hub' as an open thread AFTER the fix shipped and she demonstrably controlled the lights - she has to deliberately close threads and never does, then ruminates over already-resolved items during introspection/free time. Operator: the candidate-CREATION process needs a mirror CLEANUP process - closure is often visible from chat/tool usage (the successful hub tool call here). Also wants language tiering: default label 'open threads', escalating to concern-weight language only for items with real weight (safety, partner wellbeing), not 'check up on something I am programming' (naming overlaps psfn-framework-189d). Consider bumping priority: this feeds the introspection rumination loop the operator keeps hitting.

title: Test sessions need a 'testing' naming convention plus a cleanup path so finished test channels stop generating artifacts
description:
Evidence: channels exist only as session rows (no channels.json, no registry); channel type is inferred from sessionId prefix (src/core/session/session-id.ts:17-33). There is NO cleanup/purge/disable mechanism anywhere in src/core/session/ or src/persistence/sessions/ — sessions persist "in stores/backups until purged" (manager-primitives.ts:276 comment), where purge means manual data surgery. Result: one person accumulates a dozen unused test sessions attributed to them, which keep attracting temporal refresher notes and other artifacts that are never read.

Operator decision (2026-07-14): name test sessions with a 'testing' marker, and make it policy to clear test sessions when testing is done.

Scope: (1) a recognizable testing marker in the session/channel id or metadata; (2) exclusion of testing-marked sessions from autonomous fan-outs (temporal refresher, wake notes) and from artifact generation where sensible; (3) a purge command or Garden action that removes a named session's rows safely (fail-closed: explicit id, no wildcards); (4) a short policy note in docs/operations.md. Pairs with the refresher-targeting bead.

Acceptance: create a testing-marked session, exercise it, purge it — rows gone from the session store, refresher never targeted it; policy documented.

title: Time-of-day refresher fans out to any session with 72h activity plus the latest session unconditionally; scope it to actively-used live channels
description:
Evidence: enumerateWakeupChannels (src/core/scheduler/temporal-wakeup.ts:726-740) targets every session row with a user turn in the last 72h (SessionManager.listRecentlyActiveChannels, src/core/session/manager.ts:398-421, materializes ALL store sessions per 15-min tick) and then unconditionally appends the single most-recent session even past the lookback (temporal-wakeup.ts:736-738). Eligibility gates (internal-prefix, public-privacy, 120-min idle, anti-loop) cannot distinguish leftover test channels from real partner channels. Live symptom: [Time-of-day refresher] notes landing on unused/test channels.

Operator decision (2026-07-14): only a handful of live, actively-used channels per companion need date/time refreshers — active group chats, active DMs, active satellites/app. Nothing else.

Scope: (1) restrict fan-out to actively-used channels of those live types; (2) drop or partner-scope the unconditional-latest append; (3) exclude sessions marked as testing (see the testing-session naming/cleanup bead, which this pairs with). Related: 2x37.9 (enumeration cost — bound the store scan while here), kz0i (morning-wake gate bug, same lane).

Acceptance: over a 24h live observation, refresher notes appear only on channels with recent partner activity of the allowed types; dormant/test channels receive none; per-tick session enumeration no longer materializes the full store.

title: Carlini agent pods have no /app/companion/skills mount so the skills catalog loads empty
description:
Evidence: carlini live logs 2026-07-14 (image 0.1.0-kube-c0385f2b), per 6h: `WARN [SkillsLoader] Skills root missing; no skills can load from it: /app/companion/skills` — main 7x, julienne 3x, denise 1x, lucy 1x, garden-nun 0x. The directory does not exist in the pods, so the skills tool family has an empty catalog for affected companions.

Context: likely a missing volume mount or seed step in the carlini Helm chart, not a code bug. Previously noted as log noise in fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md par-8d.6; now confirmed as a functional gap (skills tools return nothing).

Scope: Helm/volume/seed fix on the carlini release. Non-goal: changing SkillsLoader code or the fail-closed warn (correct behavior).

Acceptance: after rollout, agent pod logs show a nonzero skills load count and no "Skills root missing" WARN; the skills tool lists entries on at least the main companion.

title: Four per-companion state files are mis-rooted at config.dataDir instead of companionDataDir
description:
Evidence — four confirmed sites where per-companion state is written under config.dataDir (shared systemDataDir) instead of companionDataDir (§11 seams 7 and 8):
1. garden-audit-history.jsonl — local-admin-contract.ts:197.
2. Garden heartbeat-policy.json path — scheduler-service.ts:290, while the layout signature at layout.ts:740 intends companionDataDir. This COMPOUNDS bead b9kb (Garden scheduler service already reads/writes heartbeat-policy.json at the wrong root) and should land with b9kb + psfn-framework-nljc (fingerprint-cache fix) so all three converge on one resolver.
3. Reflection-metacognition journal.
4. Model-usage ledger JSONL — model-budget.ts:338 — spend accounting mixes companions (the Postgres per-schema store mitigates, the JSONL does not).

Context
- §11 calls these "independent S-effort bugs" — mechanical mis-wirings, distinct from the mechanism work (overlay) and file moves (capability-tier/scheduler). The correct pattern already exists: resolveConfiguredCompanionDataDir (local-admin-contract.ts:178), used by charge/fatigue ledgers, cogsec events, quarantine, prompt layers, core memory.
- Batched as one bead because each fix is the same mechanical substitution; cite each site in the fix.

Scope
- Re-root all four sites onto resolveConfiguredCompanionDataDir. Decide per site whether existing shared-file contents need a one-time split/migration or can be left frozen (document the choice).
- Coordinate site 2 with b9kb and nljc (related links) — one resolver, one landing.
- Non-goal: any new config mechanism.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §11 (seams 7, 8).
acceptance_criteria: All four sites (garden-audit-history.jsonl, Garden heartbeat-policy path, reflection-metacognition journal, model-usage ledger JSONL) resolve through resolveConfiguredCompanionDataDir and write per-companion files; on a multi-companion fleet no two companions share these files. The heartbeat-policy fix lands coherently with b9kb/nljc on one resolver. Each site's handling of pre-existing shared file contents is documented.
close_reason: Implemented on work/dnll-config-ownership-dnll-4-dataDir @ 162955542b, merged to feat/dnll-config-ownership (pushed). Re-rooted three Garden per-companion state files from config.dataDir to companionDataDir: garden-audit-history.jsonl (local-admin-contract.ts:224) and heartbeat-policy.json + reflection-metacognition journal (AdminSchedulerService ctor, local-admin-contract.ts:264; param renamed to encode the invariant). 4th bead site (model-usage JSONL ledger) verified already-resolved: Postgres-only model_usage_events with per-companion attribution, no JSONL writer exists. Data continuity: old shared files left frozen, no dual-read shim (honest fail-closed; documented in docs/multi-companion.md). Gates: 19 focused + 68 broader tests, lint clean, UBS clean, regression-first test proving the split-root fix. Blind Pi review PASS 0 blockers: silent-heartbeat-reset thesis REFUTED (runtime pre-creates the file every boot; pre-fix Garden edits were already dead per b9kb split-brain — strict improvement), split-brain convergence verified across all readers, fleet threading per-process correct, ctor rename safe. Nonblocking for handoff: single-companion split-root deployments see old audit history frozen/invisible at systemDataDir until a one-time copy (data intact; optional startup WARN or copy suggested).

title: Apply the memory-subsystem last-result fallback pattern to post-turn loops to clear drain races
description:
Evidence
- Post-turn drain timeout (5s) is regularly exceeded under rapid turns, leaving memory_extraction / emotion_appraisal / auto_compaction unfinished (§8d.4). This is the subject of mmo9.3 (per-session durable BackgroundWorkSupervisor).

Context
- Operator decision (§10.4): the per-turn background LLM fan-out is ACCEPTED as necessary; the work is clearing the RACE CONDITIONS. Apply the memory-subsystem pattern across post-turn loops: if a concurrent task does not come back in time, proceed with the last turn's result rather than blocking or dropping.

Scope
- Apply the "if concurrent work does not return in time, use last turn's result" pattern to the post-turn loops (extraction/appraisal/compaction drains) so a slow concurrent task never blocks the turn or corrupts state.
- Relates to mmo9.3 (BackgroundWorkSupervisor) and mmo9.5 (admission control) — coordinate, do not duplicate.
- Non-goal: reducing the fan-out itself (accepted as necessary).

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §8d.4, §10.4.
acceptance_criteria: Under rapid turns, a post-turn drain that exceeds its window proceeds with the last turn's result instead of blocking the next turn or dropping work, with no state corruption. Verified by driving rapid turns and observing no post-turn block and no lost/duplicated background result.
close_reason: Folded into mmo9.3 — lp7g self-describes as its subject; the durable per-session BackgroundWorkSupervisor structurally solves the 5s drain race lp7g patches. 2026-07-14 bead audit.

title: Bound the session hot-cache to recent sessions per companion with hydrate-on-demand for older
description:
Evidence
- Live carlini agents show high RSS (~1.1Gi each). §8d assessment: this is probably cache, and cache-over-disk-IO is the right trade — but it must be bounded.

Context
- Operator decision (§10.6): keep only functional state hot (e.g. the last ~1k sessions per companion) with search/hydrate-on-demand for older sessions. Thousands of sessions x roughly half a dozen companions must not all live in memory. Memories are lower-risk (they grow slower than chat turns).

Scope
- Bound the session hot-cache to a configured recent window per companion (default around last ~1k sessions), hydrating/searching older sessions on demand.
- Non-goal: memory-store caching (lower risk); the Redis session tail (hgw3.5) is the related architecture — relate, do not duplicate.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §10.6, §8d.
acceptance_criteria: The session hot-cache holds at most the configured recent window per companion (around last ~1k sessions); older sessions are hydrated/searched on demand and evicted from the hot set. Agent RSS no longer grows unbounded with total session count. Correctness of older-session reads is preserved via on-demand hydration.

title: Make the cogsec override an audited break-glass path only, with no subject-consent approval system
description:
Evidence
- Strong reuse candidate for the override flow: the cogsec quarantine confirm->decide two-step with full audit (intake-quarantine-routes.ts), plus opl1.10 passkey step-up binding.
- §3 originally floated three options (subject-consent-required, owner-break-glass, dual-control) as an open design question.

Context
- Operator decision (§10.7 iii): the cogsec override is an AUDITED BREAK-GLASS ONLY. There is NO subject-consent request/approval system — too much work. It is for emergencies to fix things, not casual access, with a full audit trail.

Scope
- Implement the subject-scoped memory/profile override (PRIV1/PRIV2) as an audited break-glass action, reusing the cogsec quarantine confirm->decide two-step and opl1.10 passkey step-up. Every use writes a full audit record.
- Non-goal: any subject-consent request/approval workflow (explicitly rejected). No casual-access path.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §3, §10.7 (iii). Parent epic: opl1; relates to opl1.10 and opl1.11.


Adversarial correction: privacy override is not generic opl1.10 step-up. It requires the user-verifying WebAuthn branch specifically, plus trusted ingress, an identified principal, exact companion/action/resource, reason, short expiry and single-use confirm-to-decide. Lower-assurance Discord possession, owner role and legacy token recovery cannot authorize it. Initial passkey enrollment/recovery follows the trusted-host subject-bound ceremony.
acceptance_criteria: A non-subject memory/profile is never revealed by routine owner/admin/member authorization. Privacy break-glass requires local/trusted ingress, an identified principal, a user-verifying WebAuthn passkey, exact companion/action/resource selector, stated reason, bounded expiry and single-use confirm-to-decide. Discord possession challenge, mfa_enabled, OAuth consent, owner role, legacy token, and the trusted-host recovery credential alone cannot satisfy privacy break-glass or enroll a passkey; only the full subject-bound recovery ceremony may replace a passkey, and a separate exact opl1.15 UV-WebAuthn ceremony is still required for disclosure. Every attempt and decision records who/what/when/why/assurance/target/parent decision without private content and is visible in the audit trail. Concurrency/replay/target substitution/expired-session tests deny; no subject-consent workflow is added. Garden E2E, build and mandatory lint pass.

title: Hide the derived contact profile/bio from admins who are not the subject
description:
Evidence
- The derived user profile/bio is the freeform ContactProfileArtifact (memory-store-port.ts:27-34) produced by extraction.
- Same principal gap as PRIV1: "admin" is currently one shared token (server-auth.ts:10-14); subject-scoping requires the opl1 principal layer.

Context
- Operator decision (§10.7 ii): the derived user profile/bio is hidden unless the admin/user is logged in as the subject. Lands after Discord SSO (opl1, in flight).

Scope
- Gate the derived contact profile/bio so routine access is visible only to its proven subject, reusing the same principal/subject-classification layer as PRIV1. Owner/admin status provides no exception; any non-subject disclosure is exclusively opl1.15 privacy break-glass.
- Non-goal: the memory-body gate itself (PRIV1); this covers the profile artifact specifically.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §3, §10.7 (ii). Parent epic: opl1; relates to opl1.11.


Adversarial correction: remove the bare owner exception. A ContactProfileArtifact is routine-visible only to its proven subject. Any owner/admin non-subject reveal is exclusively opl1.15 privacy break-glass with trusted ingress, a user-verifying passkey, exact target/action/reason, short expiry and audit.
acceptance_criteria: The derived ContactProfileArtifact for subject Y is returned during routine Garden use only to the authenticated proven subject Y; owner/admin role alone never bypasses the gate. Any non-subject reveal is exclusively opl1.15 privacy break-glass with trusted ingress and user-verifying WebAuthn. Card, detail, search, count, export, prompt and bulk surfaces filter before construction; ambiguous/stale/missing subject classification hides. Focused policy/query/E2E tests, build and mandatory lint pass.

title: Hide all contact-associated (named) memories from non-subject admins by piggybacking the intimate-memory gate
description:
Evidence
- Visibility today is gated ONLY by sensitivity: memory-body-gate.ts:115-118 hides just intimate/confidential, never by contact/subject. "Admin" is a single shared token (server-auth.ts:10-14) with no principals/roles (AdminAuditActor = 'operator' | 'companion').
- Memory contactId is optional/nullable and often the conversation partner, not the subject; subjectContactId and episodic participantContactIds are separate. opl1.11 already warns against equating contactId with subject classification.

Context
- Operator decision (§10.7 i): hide ALL contact-associated (named) memories from any logged-in admin who is not the subject, REGARDLESS of sensitivity level, because procedural/reflection content can allude to intimate-level material. Memories are already attributed to who they relate to.
- Explicit instruction: PIGGYBACK on the existing intimate/high-intimacy gate mechanism (AdminMemoryBodyGate) — do NOT build a parallel system.
- Lands after Discord SSO (opl1, in flight). A subject-classification layer with a fail-closed ambiguous branch is prerequisite work (opl1.11).

Scope
- Extend the existing AdminMemoryBodyGate so a named (contact-associated) memory is hidden from any admin who is not the subject, at every sensitivity level, once principals exist (post-SSO).
- Leak paths beyond the body view (search snippets, counts, exports, bulk ops) must honor the same gate — opl1.11 acceptance already enumerates them.
- Non-goal: a new authz system; reuse the existing gate. Blocked behind opl1.3/.5/.7 principals.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §3, §10.7 (i). Parent epic: opl1; relates to opl1.11.


Adversarial correction: remove the bare owner exception. A non-subject principal, including an owner, never sees named memory through routine role authorization. The only override is opl1.15 privacy break-glass with trusted ingress, a user-verifying passkey, exact target/action/reason, short expiry and audit.
acceptance_criteria: A principal X sees a named memory for subject Y during routine Garden use only when X is the authorized subject/co-subject under the executable policy; owner/admin status alone never bypasses this at any sensitivity. Any non-subject reveal uses only opl1.15 privacy break-glass with trusted ingress and user-verifying WebAuthn. The shared SQL-aware gate filters IDs, bodies, snippets, counts, embeddings, exports, prompts and bulk/update paths before construction; ambiguous/stale/missing subject classification hides. Focused policy/query/E2E tests, build and mandatory lint pass.

title: ChatGPTN returns a provider template artifact that becomes an empty_response and wastes an LLM attempt
description:
Evidence
- ChatGPTN returns the provider template artifact <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>, which becomes an empty_response and triggers the deepseek fallback on scheduled lanes — wasting one LLM attempt and round-trip per affected turn.

Context
- Observed live on carlini scheduled lanes. It is a routing/template misconfiguration for that model, not a model-quality issue.

Scope
- Fix the routing/template config for the ChatGPTN model so it does not emit the template artifact / empty_response. Effort S.
- Non-goal: the fallback mechanism itself (it is working as designed); only stop the wasted first attempt.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §8d.3.
acceptance_criteria: ChatGPTN produces normal completions on scheduled lanes with no <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜> template artifact and no empty_response->deepseek fallback, eliminating the wasted LLM attempt per affected turn.
notes: Duplicate-candidate of psfn-framework-2nu6 (same ChatGPTN root cause; 2nu6 now carries quantified live evidence from 2026-07-14 triage: ~9.6% of turns, 88s worst-case fallback latency). Consider merging into 2nu6.
close_reason: Folded into 2nu6 (same ChatGPTN template-artifact -> empty_response bug; both beads flagged each other as merge candidates; 2nu6 carries quantified live evidence ~9.6% of turns). 2026-07-14 bead audit.

title: Agent gateway-connect retry budget is shorter than gateway readiness, crashlooping every fleet rollout
description:
Evidence
- On every fleet rollout, all agents die on gateway RPC ECONNREFUSED. The retry budget (10 retries / ~9s) is shorter than gateway readiness, and the fatal path exits 1 — bypassing the intended exit-75 reexec.

Context
- This is the rollout crashloop race observed live on carlini. It is a reliability bug, not just noise: agents crashloop until the gateway happens to be ready.

Scope
- Fix with a longer/jittered gateway-connect retry budget OR readiness gating, and correct the fatal path so it takes the exit-75 reexec instead of exit-1. Effort S/M.
- Non-goal: the "I'm back" duplicate notifications those restarts produce (dq9c/B11).

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §8d.2.
acceptance_criteria: A fleet rollout no longer crashloops agents on gateway ECONNREFUSED: the retry budget outlasts gateway readiness (or readiness-gates the connect), and when the agent does exit it takes the exit-75 reexec path, not exit-1. Verified by a rollout showing agents connecting on first/early retry with no crashloop.

title: Reclaim the ~241MB orphaned frozen turn-record tree at fleet/carlini/state/sessions on carlini
description:
Evidence
- A ~241MB orphaned frozen turn-record tree sits at fleet/carlini/state/sessions/ on the companion-data PVC — inode-distinct from and frozen since the Jul-9 layout migration; the live twin is at the top-level state/. This is ~40% of the PVC reclaimable together with rotation.

Context
- Operator (§10.1): the frozen fleet/carlini record tree likely dates to the cogsec incident; cleanup is still valid.
- SAFETY: this is on a live PVC near backups. NEVER use rm -rf near backups. Verify inodes and mtime confirm the tree is the frozen orphan (not the live twin) before any removal, and use verified targeted removal. Also verify the non-primary companion trees for the same orphan pattern.

Scope
- One-time verified cleanup of the confirmed orphaned tree only. Verify inodes/mtime first; use targeted removal, not rm -rf.
- Non-goal: turn-record rotation itself (2z12.4 theme) — but reclaimed space compounds with it.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §8d.1, §10.1.
acceptance_criteria: The orphaned tree is confirmed by inode + mtime to be the frozen pre-migration twin (not the live state/ tree) before any deletion. After verified targeted removal (no rm -rf), ~241MB is reclaimed on companion-data and the live session tree is intact and serving turns. Non-primary companion trees are checked for the same orphan.

comments.author: axAilotl
comments.text: LIVE CHECK 2026-07-15 (read-only, NO deletion). Orphan STILL PRESENT. du -sh /app/runtime-root/fleet/carlini/fleet/carlini/state/sessions = 242M (nested double fleet/carlini path — the frozen pre-migration twin). Live twin at /app/runtime-root/fleet/carlini/state/sessions = 305M (mtime Jul 15 00:02, actively serving). Both confirmed via find -path '*fleet/carlini/state/sessions'. Deletion remains a separate operator-approved task. Leave OPEN.

title: Turn records keep recentEntries and rendered plan.messages twice; store L0 id-ranges plus deltas
description:
Evidence
- recentEntries (raw) + plan.messages (rendered) are still persisted twice per turn record. This was explicitly deferred by hgw3.3 because it needs redaction-interaction design (hgw3.3 close note: "recentEntries-by-ref deferred by design — needs redaction-interaction design").

Context
- Storing both the raw L0 entries and the rendered messages doubles the conversation payload per turn. The deferral was about how redaction interacts with by-reference storage, not about whether the dedup is wanted.

Scope
- Store recentEntries as L0 entry-id ranges plus divergence deltas (rendered vs raw), designed so redaction still works correctly. Effort M.
- Non-goal: reopening hgw3.3; this is the follow-up it deferred.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §8b.
acceptance_criteria: Turn records reference recentEntries as L0 id-ranges plus divergence deltas rather than a full second copy of the conversation, and redaction of an L0 entry still correctly suppresses it in the rendered view. Turn-record size drops for conversational turns.
close_reason: Implemented on work/hgw3-turnrecord-diet-9ree-entry-ranges @ 6e099a3c8c (+docstring scoping 73481d7cd0), merged to feat/hgw3-turnrecord-diet (pushed). recentEntries replaced by L0 id refs (recentEntriesRef; divergence deltas only for entries with no positive journal id — provably never CogSec-redactable), reconstructed at the SessionStore read boundary via HMAC-verified getEntriesInRange so redaction/tombstones propagate; plan.messages redaction-gated at read via provenance.sourceEntryIds for ALL records incl. old fat ones; sidecar convention parity with documented heal-vs-fail deviation (absent L0 entry heals, structural corruption fails closed). Content-addressed sidecar deliberately REJECTED for this data (would resurrect redacted text). Gates: 17 focused + 475 sessions/garden + 516 broader tests, lint clean, UBS clean. Blind Pi review PASS 0 blockers with proof of the safety claims (positive-id invariant, all 5 read exits resolved, discriminator survives clone cycles, no cross-channel leak, archive chain spanned). Follow-up filed under hgw3 fixes: old fat records still pass inline recentEntries ungated (pre-existing exposure this bead shrinks; Garden can surface redacted plaintext from pre-9ree turns) + heal-drop telemetry. Handoff notes: per-page range-read batching perf opportunity; empty-provenance messages pass ungated (inherent to provenance-keyed gating); continuityEntries left inline by scope decision.

title: Turn records copy retrieved memory text verbatim; store memory ids and resolve at Loom read time
description:
Evidence
- Retrieved memory content is copied verbatim into every turn record (snapshot.memory.*Candidates) — embeddings are stripped but the text is not.

Context
- Part of the post-hgw3 turn-record diet. The memory text already lives in the memory store; duplicating it per turn is redundant.

Scope
- Store memory ids + scores in the turn record and resolve the content at Loom read time. Effort M.
- Non-goal: changing retrieval/ranking; only how candidates are persisted in the turn record.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §8b.
acceptance_criteria: Turn records store memory candidates as ids + scores rather than inline verbatim text. Loom read-time resolution reproduces the same candidate text/order. Turn-record size drops for turns with retrieved memories.
close_reason: Implemented on work/hgw3-turnrecord-diet-jsi9-memory-refs @ 4b9ca70fc6, merged to feat/hgw3-turnrecord-diet (pushed). Four snapshot.memory candidate arrays slimmed to candidatesRef (memory ids + retrieval-time similarity) at appendTurnRecord; resolution against the LIVE memory store only at the Garden boundary (AdminSessionDataService, now async, batch getById + sanitizeObservedMemory); absent/soft-deleted memories heal-drop, never resurrect; structural corruption fails closed; old fat records pass through; hot path adds zero memory-store round-trips (no hot-path consumer reads snapshot.memory — verified twice). Gates: 7 focused + 554 broad tests, lint clean, UBS clean. Blind Pi review PASS 0 blockers, all five axes source-traced: redact-delete drops via deletedAt, redact-abstracted never surfaces from the old id, patch serves current text by design, embeddings stripped on every resolve exit, live telemetry stream provably bypasses the slim, async contract handled at every caller. Nonblocking for handoff: episodicChains text left inline (out of scope, mirrors continuityEntries); pre-existing /autonomy GARDEN_CLIENT_ROUTES gap (one-line fix, unrelated).

title: heartbeat-policy.json bypasses the fingerprint cache and is read raw per request; route through loadRequiredJsonCached
description:
Evidence
- heartbeat-policy.json bypasses the fingerprint cache: it is read with raw readFileSync per Garden request and per heartbeat trigger (heartbeat-policy.ts:504-506), unlike mainstream owner configs which are mtime-fingerprint-cached via loadRequiredJsonCached.

Context
- b9kb is a confirmed regression: the Garden scheduler service reads/writes heartbeat-policy.json at the WRONG root (top-level vs state/), so reflection-template edits never reach the runtime (broken since 2026-03-29, d7a8ad71). The caching fix and the wrong-root fix touch the same file and should land together.

Scope
- Route heartbeat-policy.json through loadRequiredJsonCached and invalidate on save. Fix alongside b9kb's wrong-root path bug. Effort S.
- Non-goal: none beyond aligning both fixes on the same resolver.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §8c.
acceptance_criteria: heartbeat-policy.json is loaded through loadRequiredJsonCached (mtime-fingerprinted) rather than raw readFileSync, with cache invalidation on save. Fixed together with b9kb so Garden and runtime resolve the same path; a Garden edit to a reflection template reaches the runtime.

title: Skills telemetry does a full read-rewrite of the aggregate file per invocation; keep in RAM and debounce
description:
Evidence
- Skills telemetry does a full read + rewrite of the aggregate file on every skill invocation (skills/telemetry.ts:204-265).

Context
- Part of the disk-IO reduction pass. Per-invocation whole-file rewrites are avoidable state churn.

Scope
- Keep the aggregate in RAM and debounce the flush to disk. Mode-agnostic, no Redis. Effort S/M.
- Non-goal: changing what telemetry is recorded.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §8c.
acceptance_criteria: Multiple skill invocations in quick succession produce a single debounced flush rather than one full-file rewrite each (verified by file mtime/write count). Recorded telemetry values are unchanged after flush.

title: Owner-file edits on disk require a reboot; watch owner files and drive the existing refreshModels hook
description:
Evidence
- Garden-driven models.json edits already hot-swap in the running agent: save -> applySettings mutates shared config in place -> refreshModels hook re-resolves models + invalidates the prompt-prefix cache (settings-service.ts:136-158, substrate-agent.ts:598-620). LLMClient builds model objects per call from live config — no client cache to rebuild.
- The reboot requirement comes from a gap: DIRECT disk edits are invisible — there is no watcher on owner files; loads are one-shot at startup.
- Precedent for surfacing "on-disk edited, live process stale" as a divergence state exists (charge-policy, settings-service.ts:830-849).

Context
- Operator wants model changes without a reboot. The refresh path already exists; only the on-disk-edit trigger is missing.
- Caveat: LLMClient constructor-caches the LiteLLM base-URL/key from providers.json, so provider endpoint changes still need a rebuild (separate concern, M). The gateway container is never signaled (separate process; narrow impact — its injection model comes from env, not models.json) — cross-process signal is M-L if wanted.
- Related: the lifecycle/restart tool is not kube-correct (nt53); making config reboot-free reduces how often that broken path is needed.

Scope
- Add an mtime watch/poll on owner files -> loadModels -> the existing refresh hook (M). Extend the divergence-state precedent to anything unwatched.
- Non-goal: the providers.json base-url rebuild and the cross-process gateway signal (note them, do not build here).

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §6.
acceptance_criteria: Editing models.json directly on disk (no Garden save) causes the running agent to reload and re-resolve models within a bounded window, without a process restart, via the existing refreshModels hook. A divergence-state indicator is available for any owner file edited on disk but not yet reloaded.

title: Wiki backend scope model shipped but Garden UI has no Personal/World tabs
description:
Evidence
- The premise is stale at the backend. A full personal-vs-shared_world:<siteId> scope dimension already shipped (commits b75b855d, a0705063): scope field + write guards (faculties/wiki/scope.ts, store.ts — companion store fail-closed rejects shared-world writes); Postgres wiki_document_chunks.scope + shared_wiki_chunks with CHECK constraint; retrieval allowedScopes + shared-projection union; admin API /api/admin/wiki/scopes and /api/admin/wiki/shared-world/:siteId (mounted).
- The only gap is the Garden frontend: admin-ui/src/routes/wiki/+page.svelte is a flat single-scope list; no client functions exist for the scope endpoints; nav has one Wiki entry.
- Bulk import (vinz.27) and places->wiki publication (vinz.4) are functionally implemented too.

Context
- Operator (§10.9) confirmed the backend already shipped ("another case of me forgetting I did shit") — same pattern as hgw3 (merged but undeployed).
- Bead hygiene: vinz.28 / vinz.27 / vinz.4 are all still OPEN with stale premises. This bead's scope INCLUDES re-triaging them against shipped code: close vinz.27 and vinz.4 (already implemented, verify against b75b855d/a0705063 first), and re-scope vinz.28 to frontend-only (which this bead supersedes). Related beads are linked.

Scope
- Frontend-only (S-M): scope-aware client fns + Personal/World tabs, per-card scope badge, optional nav split.
- Also in scope: the vinz.28/.27/.4 re-triage above.
- Non-goal: the caretaker propose/approve/dedup layer (s10mc.5) remains future work (L), unrelated to the tab ask.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §4, §10.9.
acceptance_criteria: The Garden wiki page presents Personal and World (shared_world:<siteId>) tabs backed by the shipped /api/admin/wiki/scopes and shared-world endpoints, with a per-card scope badge. Separately: vinz.27 and vinz.4 are verified against b75b855d/a0705063 and closed if confirmed shipped; vinz.28 is re-scoped to frontend-only or closed as superseded by this bead.

title: Same-cluster fleet companions mint as stranger/public; default relationshipType to acquaintance for fleet peers
description:
Evidence
- Auto-minted contacts get stranger/public (a deliberate fail-closed floor, upsert-resolve-operations.ts:280-288). Garden-created contacts already default acquaintance.
- The sibling set IS defined (fleetCompanionIds from companions.json; the gateway validates DM peers against it, companion-channels.ts:33-38) but is NEVER consulted at contact mint.
- Sibling companions today: isMachineIntelligence=true but still stranger/public.

Context
- Operator wants same-cluster companions to recognize each other above stranger. Decision (§1c, §10): bump relationshipType ONLY; the trust floor stays public (fail-closed charter) unless deliberately decided otherwise.
- bead 0ggv.4 (Purrsephone<->Artie) is the cross-cluster case and is orthogonal to this intra-cluster fleet default.

Scope
- Plumb fleet membership into resolveChannelIdentity and default relationshipType: 'acquaintance' for companion-lane fleet peers at mint.
- Non-goal: do NOT raise the trust floor above public. Do not touch the cross-cluster 0ggv.4 case.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §1c.
acceptance_criteria: A newly auto-minted contact for a same-cluster fleet peer (validated against fleetCompanionIds) mints with relationshipType 'acquaintance', while its trust floor remains 'public'. Non-fleet strangers still mint stranger/public.

title: Garden admin contact card cannot show or edit the Human/Companion (isMachineIntelligence) marker
description:
Evidence
- Contact.isMachineIntelligence is first-class and auto-detected: Discord author.bot (discord/adapter.ts:860); the inter-companion gateway lane stamps it true by construction (gateway/server.ts:651-663). It is provenance-guarded and shown on the AGENT-facing card (tools.ts:546).
- The Garden ADMIN card shows nothing: the admin Contact type omits the field entirely and the service payload cannot set it.

Context
- Operator wants Garden to visually distinguish humans from companions. The data already exists; this is mostly UI plumbing to surface and edit it via the existing setMachineIntelligence port.
- Design wrinkle: relationshipType: 'ai_companion' duplicates the boolean. The boolean is load-bearing (fatigue policy). Recommend boolean-canonical, with the enum value derived/deprecated — not fixed in this bead but noted so the badge does not entrench the duplication.

Scope
- Add isMachineIntelligence to the admin Contact type + a Human/Companion badge on the card + payload/validation wiring to the existing setMachineIntelligence port. Effort M (mostly UI plumbing).
- Non-goal: resolving the relationshipType/boolean duplication.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §1b.
acceptance_criteria: The Garden admin contact card shows a Human/Companion badge reflecting isMachineIntelligence, and an operator can toggle it, persisting through the existing setMachineIntelligence port with provenance. Auto-detected values (Discord bots, inter-companion lane peers) display correctly without an operator edit.

title: Contact model has no gender, pronoun, or age fields; add them with inferred-vs-specified provenance
description:
Evidence
- Zero hits for gender/pronoun/age/birth-year fields across src/ and admin-ui/. Contact model: src/core/contacts/types.ts:266-283; SQLite schema src/core/contacts/store/schema.ts:64-78; Postgres migration src/persistence/postgres/migrations.ts:543-559.
- A reusable inferred-vs-specified provenance pattern already exists: the is_machine_intelligence marker (observed-machine-intelligence.ts:55-69) distinguishes system:channel_observation:* actors (inferred, never clobbers operator edits) from operator actors, with per-field audit rows (contact_mutation_audit) and an audited-fields whitelist (types.ts:141-154). New demographic fields should register there.
- Extraction today produces only a freeform ContactProfileArtifact (memory-store-port.ts:27-34) — no structured attribute slot.
- Garden service payload whitelists silently drop unknown fields (contacts-service.ts:379-385, 635-639).

Context
- Operator wants structured gender/pronouns/age on contacts. The MI-marker pattern gives inferred-vs-specified and per-field audit for free if the new fields register there.

Scope
- MVP first: operator-specified via Garden form (S once fields exist). Inference pipeline is L, separate follow-up.
- Full change (M): types + both schemas + hydration/upsert + Garden service payload whitelists + contact card UI.
- Non-goal: do not build the inference pipeline in this bead; register the fields with the provenance pattern so inference can be added later.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §1a.
acceptance_criteria: Gender/pronouns/age fields exist on the contact type, both schemas (SQLite + Postgres migration), and the Garden service payload whitelist (no longer dropped). An operator can set them from the Garden contact card and the value persists with operator provenance in contact_mutation_audit. Fields are registered so an inferred write cannot clobber an operator-specified value.

title: Extend the room-memory provenance backfill (27ut) to derive subjectContactId
description:
Evidence
- GATE C: pre-2026-07-09 memories have empty provenance and are filtered out of graph-proposal scanning.

title: Idle maintenance loops do full-store work when nothing changed: salience decay rescans all active memories and guideline review re-reads files every cycle
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14), two loops on the same maintenanceIntervalMs cadence (default 300s via schedulerConfig.salienceDecayIntervalMs, load-config.ts:60; MEMORY_CONFIG fallback 60s, memory/types.ts:353), registered at src/app/agent/scheduler-runtime.ts:99-108 and :109-132:

(1) SalienceDecay (faculties/memory/decay.ts:26, run() :48-84) pages listActiveMemories({limit:500}) over ALL active memories, recomputes exp() decay per row, and bulkUpdateSalience — every cycle regardless of any reads/writes since the last run. 5 agents × a full scan + bulk write every 1-5 min on the shared box, at idle, growing with the memory corpus. Decay is deterministic in dt, so options: compute lazily at read time; or precompute each memory's next threshold-crossing time and only touch rows due to cross the 0.01 delta (:72); or at minimum widen the idle cadence (half-lives are long).

(2) Compaction-guideline review (core/session/compression-guideline.ts:568-580) does guidelineStore.load() (existsSync+readFileSync, :319/:327) and failureLogStore.listSince() (:427/:428) every cycle BEFORE deciding to skip. Fix: mtime/size guard or an in-memory "last failure appended" watermark — skip both reads when unchanged.

Non-goals: changing decay math, half-lives, or guideline semantics.
acceptance_criteria: An idle deployment's maintenance cycles perform no memory-table scan and no guideline/failure-log file reads when nothing changed since the last cycle (DB/fs instrumentation over an idle window); decay values observed at read time are unchanged versus today's eager behavior (test tolerance on the exp curve); guideline review still triggers on new failure-log entries.

title: Inline image bytes cross the agent-gateway boundary twice per vision turn (intake screen, then main LLM call); retain once at the gateway
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14). For inline base64 images (Telegram photos, pasted images, voice-attached — up to 8MB decoded ≈ 11MB base64), the same bytes cross the agent-gateway boundary twice per vision turn: once for intake.screen_image (boundary/gateway/methods/intake-image.ts:27,55,109) and again inside the main-turn LLM call (the gateway holds provider secrets, methods/llm.ts). Each crossing pays a full JSON.stringify/JSON.parse (transport.ts:205,278). URL images are cheap (URL crosses, not bytes); this is specifically the inline path. That's 2x multi-MB serialize/copy/transit per vision turn per companion — steady-state CPU on the shared box.

Fix shape: on intake.screen_image, the gateway retains the decoded image keyed by originRef (already a param) for the immediately-following turn LLM call, or returns a screening handle the agent passes back — bytes cross once. Retention must be bounded (TTL + size cap) and a cache miss must fail closed to resending, not to a missing image.

Related: psfn-framework-j8gv (single vision pass) reduces VLM calls; this reduces transport copies — independent wins on the same path. Note for wss (cross-host) gateway deployments only: the backplane has no compression (transport.ts:205,278); enabling perMessageDeflate there is a possible follow-up, but do NOT enable it for same-box unix-socket pairs (CPU for no bandwidth gain).
acceptance_criteria: An inline base64 image crosses the agent-gateway transport once per turn (transport-level instrumentation or test on serialized payload sizes); the main-turn LLM call resolves the image from the gateway-side retention (originRef key or returned handle) with a bounded TTL/size and fail-closed miss behavior (falls back to resending bytes, never silently drops the image); screening and LLM behavior unchanged.

title: Per-turn retrieval re-runs the full pipeline on unchanged inputs and embeds the identical query twice (memory + wiki); short-circuit and share the embedding
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14), two compounding wastes on the per-turn hot path:

(1) Unconditional full refresh: refreshActiveMemoryContext is scheduled every non-vision turn (turn-execution/pre-turn-state.ts:531-555) and re-runs the whole pipeline (memory/retrieval.ts:373-418): query embed at :757, full vector scan + scoring, and — when compositionalPolicy is enabled for the channel — an LLM rerank call per turn (:1021-1027). The active-context identity key deliberately excludes contextText (memory/active-context.ts:116-125), so nothing short-circuits on unchanged input; coalescing only guards concurrent refreshes on the same key (:337-353). Fix: short-circuit when hash(contextText) and the store's corpus version pointer are unchanged since the last completed refresh — return the existing snapshot.

(2) Double embedding: the same memoryRetrievalContextText is passed to memory retrieval (pre-turn-state.ts:479/:482) and wiki retrieval (:661); memory embeds it at retrieval.ts:757, wiki independently at faculties/wiki/retrieval.ts:298. HttpEmbeddingProvider.embed (memory/embedding.ts:113-127) has no memoization and no embedding cache exists anywhere. Fix: compute the query embedding once in pre-turn state and hand it to both consumers, and/or a small content-hash LRU in the embedding provider.

Interaction: this is the main destabilizer of the cacheable prompt prefix — fixing it improves the prompt-cache hit rate from the sibling prompt-caching bead. Non-goals: changing scoring, ranking, or what memories surface.
acceptance_criteria: A turn whose retrieval context text and memory-corpus version are unchanged since the last completed refresh serves the existing snapshot without a new embed, vector scan, or compositional rerank call (test); one query embedding is computed per turn and shared by memory and wiki retrieval (call-count test on the embedding provider); retrieval results for changed inputs are byte-identical to today; compositional rerank still fires when inputs actually change.
notes: Single-review remediation shipped in 96c5ef34. Cache identity now includes normalized disclosure, room/contact visibility, scope, retired-session, channel-label revision, and trust-policy revision state; unsafe access fingerprinting disables reuse. Postgres retrieval generation remains monotonic across rollback and stable reads wait for transactions. Regressions cover consent grant-to-withdraw, contact-room visibility withdrawal, and concurrent rollback. title: Postgres transcript projection issues a no-op drift DELETE per message and preloads every message ID into resident memory at boot
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14), two fixes in one file (src/persistence/sessions/postgres-adapters.ts):

(1) Write amplification: every upsertSessionEntry enqueues the projection upsert PLUS an unconditional DELETE FROM session_projection_drift WHERE channel_id=$1 (:271-280, same pattern at :293-311 and :252-261). ~2 messages/turn → ~4 statements/turn, half of them no-op deletes — drift rows almost never exist and driftByChannel already tracks their presence in memory. Fix: only enqueue the DELETE when driftByChannel.has(channelId), or fold upsert+delete into one CTE.

(2) Boot memory: preloadMessageIds (:116-132) runs SELECT channel_id, message_id FROM session_messages_projection across ALL channels and stores a Map<channelId, Set<number>> on the projection for process life (:201, :424) — O(total messages) boot scan plus tens of MB resident at 100k+ messages, ×5 companions, growing forever. Fix: lazy per-channel hydration on first touch, or keep only the per-channel counts/max-id the drift reconciliation actually needs.

Non-goals: changing the projection schema or drift semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Messages on channels with no tracked drift enqueue exactly one projection statement (no unconditional DELETE; test asserts statement count); drift rows are still cleared when drift exists for the channel; boot no longer SELECTs all message IDs across all channels — hydration is lazy per channel or reduced to per-channel counts/max-id — with projection/drift reconciliation behavior unchanged under the existing test suite.
notes: Implementation checkpoint 0dd8e7c6 on work/fleet-efficiency-postgres-projection. Replaced the O(total projected messages) boot preload with one aggregate row per channel (COUNT plus MAX message_id), preserving exact boot reconciliation counts without retaining message-ID sets. Clean-channel upserts/tombstone deletes/replacements now clear session_projection_drift only when driftByChannel tracked the channel; explicit clearProjectionDrift remains explicit. Projection counts use bounded channel metadata and reconcile ambiguous inserts/deletes from PostgreSQL statement results. Regression coverage asserts no all-message-ID boot SELECT, exact aggregate boot count, one projection statement for a clean-channel message, persisted drift clearing when tracked, and existing repair/reconciliation behavior. Local PostgreSQL integration unavailable because pg_isready at 127.0.0.1:5432 reported no response; no external/live infrastructure attempted. PostgreSQL production code only; no SQLite implementation touched. Branch pushed and origin-equal at 0dd8e7c6. Awaiting exactly one independent review; do not close or merge yet.

title: Gateway keepalive fires an audited no-op RPC every 30s, writing audit rows and forcing rotation at full idle
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14) — top idle-load win. src/boundary/gateway/client.ts:1024,1044 (DEFAULT_GATEWAY_KEEPALIVE_INTERVAL_MS=30_000 at :148) fires a discord.typing RPC across the backplane every 30s forever, even fully idle. The handler is a no-op (methods/discord.ts:37) but it is registered through runtime.audited (methods/register.ts:14), so each beat runs the full audit wrapper (server.ts:326): canary-egress inspect → INSERT into the gateway audit store + enforceRotation (audit.ts:102,110) → UPDATE on completion (:115). Across 5 deployments that's an INSERT+UPDATE pair (+rotation scan) every ~6s on the shared box at 100% idle, and the no-op entries pollute real audit history into premature rotation. (Gateway audit store is the better-sqlite3 store in audit.ts — legacy SQLite, still live.)

Fix shape: keep the socket warm with a transport-level ping (ws ping frame / unix-socket noop) instead of an audited JSON-RPC method, or register the keepalive on a non-audited path. Non-goal: removing auditing from any real method or changing audit rotation policy.
acceptance_criteria: An idle deployment generates zero gateway_audit writes from keepalive over an observation window (verify by row count / audit log diff); the agent-gateway socket still detects disconnection within the same window as today (keepalive function preserved via transport-level ping or non-audited method); audit history no longer accumulates discord.typing ALLOW entries.
notes:
2026-07-14 reconciliation: premise correction — production gateway audit is Postgres-only, not SQLite. Commit 6ce9549f made src/boundary/gateway/privileged-core.ts:92-99 fail unless persistenceBackend=postgres and constructs createPostgresGatewayAuditStore; SQLite audit code is a retired adapter/testing surface. The performance problem itself was present on feat/fleet-efficiency d9ba500c: src/boundary/gateway/client.ts sent discord.typing every 30s and src/boundary/gateway/server.ts audited it through the Postgres store.

2026-07-15 implementation checkpoint for exactly one independent review: pushed commit 4d8807e1 on origin/work/fleet-efficiency-audit-keepalive. GatewayClient now uses GatewayRpcConnection.sendHeartbeat instead of discord.typing. Unix connections exchange connection-scoped non-JSON-RPC PING/PONG control lines; WSS uses native ping/pong frames. A missing/failed acknowledgement causes the client to close the connection, preserving detection. GatewayServer refreshes only the emitting connection health clock from the transport heartbeat, with no audit call. Real discord.typing remains registered through registerAuditedDescriptors and is regression-tested as ALLOW-audited. Validation: 178 proportional gateway client/server/multi-companion/companion-channel/transport/audit/Postgres-audit tests passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed (ESM+DTS); git diff --check passed. Bead intentionally remains in_progress pending the single independent review and orchestrator integration.

title: Garden runs like a local-first webapp: IndexedDB-backed client store with delta sync so navigation renders from local data and only changes cross the WAN
description:
Operator direction (2026-07-14): "gardenux needs to run like a webapp and have cache and use indexdb so we just delta updates."

Architecture: an IndexedDB store in admin-ui (per companion deployment origin) holding session transcripts (append-mostly — new messages have monotonic ids, a natural delta cursor via maxId/nextBeforeId), session/channel lists, queue states, telemetry snapshots. On navigation: render from IndexedDB immediately, then revalidate with a delta request (If-None-Match from psfn-framework-t5z7.3, or since-cursor params) and patch in place. Websocket events (psfn-framework-t5z7.7) update the local store directly, making polls redundant while connected.

Sequencing: depends on server-side cursors/ETags (t5z7.3) and pairs with slim payloads (t5z7.1, t5z7.4) — cache slim data, not today's bloated payloads. psfn-framework-t5z7.5 now covers the server-side Redis half only; this bead owns the client half.

Non-goals: offline mutation queueing (admin actions stay online-only), service-worker app-shell caching (t5z7.6's immutable assets get most of that win), caching any credential material.
acceptance_criteria: Revisiting a previously viewed Garden page renders immediately from IndexedDB and issues only a delta/conditional request (verified in devtools: no full-payload refetch for unchanged data); session transcripts, lists, and queue pages persist their last-known state across page reloads; deltas keyed by server cursors (ETag/updatedAt/maxId) with a full-refetch fallback when the cursor is stale; stale-while-revalidate UX (render cached, update in place); admin data in IndexedDB stays on the operator's machine only — no new server surface.
notes: Implementation committed as a6f27e12 on agent/t5z7-10-indexeddb-20260716. Added an origin-scoped IndexedDB resource store plus a schema-versioned LocalFirstResource boundary with runtime validation, explicit ETag conditionals, SWR callbacks, max-message cursor merge, and forced unconditioned replacement on stale transcript cursors. Wired persisted session indexes/lean newest transcript pages, confirmations/contact approvals/graph proposals/intake quarantine queues, and normalized telemetry websocket snapshots. No server routes, service worker, offline mutation queue, credentials/tokens, settings, dependency versions, or package files changed. Adversarial review found and fixed the canonical confirmation resolutionAuthority validator defect tracked/closed as psfn-framework-3yzf. Validation: focused admin Vitest selection 10 files/48 tests passed; event-envelope node:test 4 tests passed; existing Garden server ETag/session/telemetry contract selection 5 files/47 tests passed; admin npm run check passed with 0 errors and 0 warnings; admin npm run build passed; full root npm run lint passed; full root npm run build passed; git diff --check passed.
