title: Audit history reads and parses the whole JSONL file per request and ships raw source blobs the timeline never renders
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14). src/operator/garden/services/audit-history-service.ts:78-85 does readFileSync of the ENTIRE audit JSONL + JSON.parse per line, merges gateway+charge sources, sorts everything, and slices one page — on every request to /api/admin/audit/history (overview-routes.ts:372), i.e. every filter change and pagination click on the telemetry/audit page. Unlike the approvals stores there is no in-process cache, and the file grows unbounded with history. Additionally, list entries carry the full raw source record (...(raw ? { raw } : {}), returned verbatim at overview-routes.ts:411-424) while the timeline renders only narrative/decision/timestamp — a 50-row page inflates far beyond what the UI uses.

Fix shape: memoize parsed entries keyed by file mtime/size (safe: the service is the sole writer and can invalidate on its own append), or bounded tail-read; drop raw from list payloads and add a per-entry detail endpoint. Compression from psfn-framework-t5z7.3 helps but dropping the field helps more.
acceptance_criteria: Repeat /api/admin/audit/history requests with an unchanged file serve from an mtime-keyed memo (no full re-read; verify via fs instrumentation or timing on a large file); list responses omit the raw field; a per-entry detail request returns raw on demand; timeline UI behavior unchanged.
notes: Single independent-review remediation complete and pushed at 582f3160 on work/garden-wan-audit-history. Replaced unkeyed predictable hashes with companion-bound HMAC-SHA256 opaque IDs using the canonical GATEWAY_SESSION_HMAC keyring/credential-vault boundary; Garden startup fails closed without a usable active key, and no new env/config secret surface was added. Sanitized gateway entry errors to error=present and gateway reader failures to a fixed safe status; raw error/params remain available only from authenticated no-store detail. List and detail now read the same bounded unfiltered 2,000-row source window before local filtering, preventing filtered queries from producing unresolvable IDs. Added missing-key, key/scope separation, sequential-ID offline-derivation, raw-error privacy, sanitized source failure, and filtered older-row regressions. title: Admin-ui pollers keep refetching full payloads on hidden tabs; pause on visibility loss and push queue changes over the existing garden websocket
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14). No visibilitychange/document.hidden handling exists anywhere in admin-ui/src. Network polls that run forever on background tabs: confirmations/+page.svelte:126 (15s), contact-approvals/+page.svelte:72 (15s), graph-proposals/+page.svelte:75 (15s), cognitive-security/approvals/+page.svelte:198 (15s), cognitive-security/drift/+page.svelte:128 (30s), scheduler/+page.svelte:560 (30s, refetches full getFullData tasks+reflections), chat/+page.svelte:502 (30s health). Up to ~4 full refetches/min per forgotten tab, over transatlantic WAN, per open page. (shards/+page.svelte:109 and telemetry LazyPageContent.svelte:410 1s ticks are local-only relative-time recomputes with no network — leave them.)

The queue endpoints these pages poll re-serialize and re-send the entire (usually empty) queue every tick and send Cache-Control: no-store (routes/shared.ts:3), forbidding 304s; their stores are memoized in-process so poll cost is pure network. A garden event-bus ReconnectingWebSocket already exists (admin-ui/src/lib/api/websocket.ts) and is used by prompt-monitor (+page.svelte:186) — pushing queue-change events over it is low-effort reuse.

Fix shape: (1) shared visibility-aware interval helper (clear on hidden, immediate refetch+resume on visible) adopted by all polling pages; (2) queue pages subscribe to the websocket for change signals, falling back to the poll when the socket is down. Pairs with the ETag/304 half of psfn-framework-t5z7.3.
acceptance_criteria: A backgrounded/hidden Garden tab generates zero poll traffic (verified in devtools network log) and resumes with an immediate refetch on visibility; queue-style pages (confirmations, contact approvals, graph proposals, cogsec approvals) receive updates via the existing garden websocket or conditional requests instead of full 15s refetches; no page loses freshness when visible.

title: Static Garden assets ship uncompressed with no immutable caching and no ETag, so the full bundle and HTML shell re-download over the WAN
description:
Opus sweep finding (2026-07-14). src/operator/garden/server-transport.ts:75-100 serves static files via readFile+res.end with no Content-Encoding — SvelteKit bundles (commonly 200KB-1MB uncompressed) transfer full-size on first paint. Constants at :18-19: GARDEN_HTML_CACHE_CONTROL='public, max-age=0, must-revalidate' and GARDEN_ASSET_CACHE_CONTROL='public, max-age=86400'. Three compounding issues: (1) no compression at all on statics; (2) content-hashed /_app/immutable/* assets are safe for a year of immutable caching but revalidate daily; (3) no ETag/Last-Modified anywhere, so the HTML shell fully re-downloads on every navigation and every asset revalidation is a full re-download instead of a 304.

Scope: server-transport.ts static path only. Non-goal: changing the SvelteKit build or admin API caching (psfn-framework-t5z7.3 owns API ETags).
acceptance_criteria: JS/CSS assets serve brotli/gzip (precompressed .br/.gz or on-the-fly); /_app/immutable/* served with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable; HTML shell and non-immutable assets carry an ETag and return 304 on If-None-Match; verified with curl over two consecutive page loads (second load transfers only the API calls).
notes:
Implementation landed on branch bead/t5z7.6 (commit 005ee243, off main, unpushed — pending feature-branch merge + codex review + PR). server-transport.ts static path now: prefers precompressed .br/.gz siblings (admin-ui svelte.config.js precompress:true enabled via adapter-static), on-the-fly brotli/gzip fallback above 1KB memoized by path+mtime+size+encoding (bounded 512 entries); immutable max-age=31536000 for /_app/immutable/*; ETag (size-mtime, encoding-qualified) + bodyless 304 on If-None-Match, incl. SPA fallback. Serve methods now take (path, req, res) — routing interface + both handleRequest closures updated. Did NOT touch backplane primitives or /api/admin JSON (t5z7.3 scope). Validation: targeted 15/15, full garden dir 63 files/450 tests passed, npm run build success, eslint clean on all 7 touched files.
Codex-reviewed, findings fixed, shipped in PR #42 (perf/efficiency-wave-1 → main, https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/pull/42). Gate on the branch: build+lint clean, full suite 7715 passed / 1 pre-existing environmental failure (psfn-framework-engc). Ready to close on PR merge.

Codex review remediation 999bc573 made static ETags weak with full mtime precision and capped on-the-fly Brotli quality. GitHub PR #42 merged to main as 84c0089e on 2026-07-14; current origin/main 576e33cd contains that squash, and the seven t5z7.6 files on origin/main are byte-identical to reviewed commit 999bc573. Actual shipped source in src/operator/garden/server-transport.ts selects precompressed .br/.gz siblings before bounded memoized on-the-fly Brotli/gzip, applies public,max-age=31536000,immutable to /_app/immutable/*, emits encoding-qualified weak ETags, honors If-None-Match with bodyless 304, and sends SPA fallback index.html through the same validator path. admin-ui/svelte.config.js enables adapter-static precompress:true. src/operator/garden/server-request-routing.ts keeps /api and /api/* outside the Garden SPA/static path; neither 005ee243 nor 999bc573 touched API route files. Fresh verification ran against existing detached canonical origin/main worktree 576e33cd: exact server-transport and server-request-routing suites passed 2 files / 15 tests; mandatory npm run lint passed; root npm run build passed ESM+DTS; npm --prefix admin-ui run build passed and emitted 95 .br plus 95 .gz files; t5z7.6 diff check passed. Direct curl proof over the built shipped transport returned SPA /memory 200 with max-age=0, weak ETag then bodyless 304, and an immutable hashed JS asset 200 with max-age=31536000, immutable, Content-Encoding: br, encoding-qualified weak ETag then bodyless 304. No implementation, second review, remediation, main/release write, SQLite, live/Pi/SSH/provider, or Dolt remote action.

title: ICP SEE/SAW concept: one companion runs the vision pipe for a shared-room image and syncs the extraction to siblings as provenance-tagged turn context
description:
CONCEPT BEAD — ICP is not in main yet; a worktree of future ICP work exists and this must merge with/into it. Do not implement against main as-is.

Problem: in shared rooms (group Discord etc.) every companion independently runs the full vision pipeline on the same image. On carlini's 5-companion fleet that's 5x duplicated VLM work per image (10 calls today, 5 after psfn-framework-j8gv). The extraction is persona-free by design (fixed neutral prompts in vision-screener.ts:191 and vision-reviewer.ts:199-203), so nothing companion-specific is lost by sharing it.

Operator's design sketch (2026-07-14):
- One companion declares it will SEE the image — usually the one being replied to.
- It runs its normal vision pipe, then shares what it SAW over ICP.
- Siblings load the synced extraction as chat turn context exactly as if their own vision pipe had run, with provenance tagged as "icp synced image info".
- ICP sync of shared world info / vision results carries no cost and no fatigue charge — it's substrate synchronization, not social interaction.

Security shape (fail-closed): share the EXTRACTION, not the VERDICT. The synced payload is untrusted image-derived data and stays inside the taint-tracked intake envelope model; each receiving companion applies its own intake policy/screening verdict to the shared extraction locally (policies and tiers can differ per companion). Key the payload by image content sha256 (already computed at vision-screener.ts:456) plus screener model/prompt version so upgrades invalidate cleanly.

Related: existing shared-data groundwork via the wiki; psfn-framework-s10mc.6 (ICP autonomy epic); psfn-framework-j8gv (single-pass vision, makes the shared extraction the one canonical artifact).
acceptance_criteria: Design doc/bead updates settle: SEE claim protocol (who sees — default the companion being replied to — and how contention/absence is resolved), SAW payload schema (neutral OCR + description + content hash + screener model/prompt version), provenance labeling ('icp synced image info') in turn context and persistence, and the rule that verdicts are NOT shared — each companion applies its own intake policy to the synced extraction locally with taint preserved; synced context is exempt from cost/fatigue/charge accounting; implementation lands only after the ICP worktree merges to main.

title: Inbound chat images get two VLM passes (intake screen + dedicated review); collapse to one and reserve the review loop for generated-image validation
description:
Evidence (mapped 2026-07-14): every inbound image fires two eager VLM calls at turn build in buildTurnUserContent (src/core/agent/substrate-agent/vision-attachments.ts:209): (1) intake safety screen via intake.screen_image RPC -> screenImageWithVisionModel (src/boundary/gateway/intake/vision-screener.ts:331), which already produces OCR + a neutral description + injection flags; (2) dedicated describe pass via ImageVisionReviewer.analyze (src/primitives/images/vision-reviewer.ts:178) for URL images (vision-attachments.ts:541). No dedup within a message — identical images each get their own screen+review calls (Promise.all at vision-attachments.ts:439/550). On the 5-companion carlini fleet a single group-chat image costs 10 VLM calls.

Operator decision: the dedicated review/validation loop exists mostly for the selfie tool / image generation — seeing the output and comparing it to the prompt that created it. A meme in chat doesn't need two visual passes. For inbound chat images, run the intake screen only and reuse its neutral description as the model-visible description text (vision-attachments.ts:259-295) and the persisted attachment block (:619). Keep the reviewer path for generated-image validation.

Scope: vision-attachments orchestration + plumbing the screener description into the turn-content/persistence path. Non-goals: weakening or skipping intake screening (the security pass stays mandatory), changing inline base64 handling (those already go to the main model as raw image blocks), or touching the media analyze tool's per-turn reuse (src/primitives/images/request-context.ts).

This is also the prerequisite that makes cross-companion sharing cheap: one neutral extraction per image (see the ICP SEE/SAW concept bead).
acceptance_criteria: A meme/image arriving in chat triggers exactly one VLM call per unique image (the intake screen), whose neutral description feeds the model-visible turn text and persisted description; identical attachments within one message are deduped before fan-out; the ImageVisionReviewer validation loop still runs for selfie/image-generation outputs (compare output to generating prompt); intake screening security behavior unchanged; existing vision-attachment tests updated and passing.

title: Redis-backed server-side read caching for repeated Garden admin reads
description:
Operator direction (2026-07-14): reduce repeated disk-heavy Garden admin reads on shared multi-companion clusters without changing the canonical persistence contract. This bead is SERVER-SIDE ONLY. psfn-framework-t5z7.10 exclusively owns IndexedDB, client caching, delta-sync UI, stale-while-revalidate rendering, and all other browser-local behavior; do not implement or duplicate any client work here.

Implement at measured high-value seams: recent session/activity summaries, the hot transcript first page, and slim session-list payloads only where repeat reads currently re-scan JSONL or re-query Postgres. Extend the existing optional Redis/session-tail patterns in src/persistence/sessions/session-tail-cache-port.ts, src/persistence/sessions/redis-session-tail-cache.ts, src/persistence/sessions/store.ts, and the Garden session service/wiring rather than inventing a parallel cache stack. Keep modules focused and split new cache policy/serialization into owned modules instead of expanding god files.

Correctness contract: canonical JSONL/Postgres remains authoritative and behavior is identical with Redis disabled. On runtime Redis cache failure, surface the failure through the existing cache error/telemetry contract and fall back to the canonical read so Garden remains available; never silently return stale or partial cache data. Cache keys must include strict deployment/companion namespace scoping so companions sharing Redis cannot see one another's data. Writes must invalidate or refresh relevant cached reads before subsequent reads can return.

Security and non-goals: never cache mutation responses, CogSec/intake decisions, secrets, credentials, raw sealed data, or private data across companion scopes. Do not add owner settings unless the existing Redis wiring is insufficient. No IndexedDB/admin-ui client cache or delta UX (owned by t5z7.10), no SQLite, and no live deployment changes.
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation-backed tests prove a repeated unchanged hot transcript first-page/session-summary/list read avoids a second JSONL/Postgres read; Redis-disabled tests prove canonical file/Postgres parity; write-path tests prove invalidation/freshness before the next read; two companion/deployment namespaces sharing one cache backend cannot read or collide with each other's cached data; injected runtime cache failures are surfaced through the existing error/telemetry contract and fall back to correct canonical reads; mutations, CogSec/intake decisions, secrets, and sealed/private cross-companion data are never cached; focused tests, npm run lint, npm run build, and git diff --check pass. No client/IndexedDB/delta behavior is changed.
notes:
Implementation fixed point pushed 2026-07-14 on branch work/garden-wan-server-cache at commit 2ff153c0. Scope stayed server-side only: no admin UI, IndexedDB, delta UX, settings, SQLite, deployment, or live-system changes. Profiling found Garden recent-session/activity/list reads already use slim channel-index metadata, so adding a second Redis structure there would add invalidation risk without avoiding JSONL/Postgres work. The measured heavy seam selected was the hot transcript newest/first page. SessionService now asks the existing deployment/companion-scoped shared session-tail cache for that page, with an expected-min local journal checkpoint to reject behind tails without blocking on asynchronous write-through; cursor/older pages and every miss use the canonical reader. Existing Redis runtime-failure warnings and canonical fallback remain authoritative. Existing cache key scope, epoch fencing, and two-scope collision tests cover isolation; no mutations, CogSec/intake decisions, secrets, sealed data, or new data categories were cached.

TDD evidence: initial dedicated public-seam tests failed because the route still called the synchronous canonical reader and the async admin-read method did not exist. A second red test held tail write-through pending and proved an implementation that awaited the global write chain blocked the admin read; the local journal checkpoint/fallback made it nonblocking and fresh. Final targeted command: npm test -- --run src/operator/garden/services/session-service.server-cache.test.ts src/operator/garden/routes/session-routes.test.ts src/persistence/sessions/store.session-tail.test.ts src/persistence/sessions/redis-session-tail-cache.test.ts => 4 files, 49 passed. npm run lint => exit 0. npm run build => ESM and DTS success, exit 0. git diff --check => pass. Bead remains in_progress at this committed+pushed fixed point for exactly one independent review; implementation worker did not self-review or close it.
SOLE REMEDIATION fixed point pushed 2026-07-14 on work/garden-wan-server-cache at 77d2d825 (full 77d2d825d45d57cd68308a2c7f1e78d3fb304eb7). Addressed exactly the one independent review two IMPORTANT findings. (1) Garden now reads and HMAC-verifies the current bounded canonical journal window before accepting Redis data, then reuses the established journal-wins merge rule: overlapping IDs always use authenticated journal content/channel, and unauthenticated tail rows can only gap-fill IDs newer than journal coverage. title: Sessions list loads all contacts and per-channel joins on every page visit; slim the list payload and fetch per-channel detail only on click
description:
Evidence: listSessions (src/operator/garden/services/session-service.ts:462-491) returns all channels + per-channel recent activity AND calls contactStore.listAll() plus a linked-contact resolve per channel — an uncompressed O(channels x contacts) payload shipped on every sessions-page visit, before the operator has clicked anything. listSessionRoutes (:495) calls listSessions() AGAIN on top of the route table. Operator expectation (2026-07-14): "going to the sessions page shouldn't download every session, only what I clicked on."

Fix shape: (1) list endpoint returns lightweight rows; contact linkage resolves per selected channel (new or existing detail call); (2) drop the duplicated listSessions() inside listSessionRoutes; (3) client-side cache of the list with delta revalidation (updatedAt/etag cursor) so navigation back to the page is near-free; pairs with the ETag work in psfn-framework-t5z7.3.

Scope: session-service.ts list paths + admin-ui sessions page/api client. Non-goal: changing contact storage or trust modeling.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the sessions page issues one list request returning lightweight per-channel rows (id, name, activity summary, counts) with size bounded regardless of contact count; contact/link detail loads only for the selected channel; a repeat visit within a session serves from client cache and revalidates with a delta/conditional request instead of a full refetch.
notes: Implementation complete on work/garden-wan-sessions-list and pending the single independent review. Server/API slice 118890bd: AdminSessionDataService listSessions now returns only sessionId, channelId, messageCount, optional lastActivityAt/displayLabel and never calls contactStore.listAll or performs per-channel joins; listSessionRoutes builds the same lightweight rows directly instead of recursively calling listSessions. A focused GET /api/admin/sessions/:sessionId/detail resolves the selected session contact only after selection and exposes only the previously visible linkedContactId/displayName, never contact notes, trust, relationship, channel privacy, or other private fields. Client/UI slice af553dc0: the sessions page uses an in-memory Garden-session list cache, paints cached rows immediately on repeat SPA navigation, then issues exactly one apiGet no-cache revalidation compatible with the shared ETag/304 contract from t5z7.3. Selection concurrently loads bounded messages and focused detail; detail state is separate from list revalidation so linked display detail is preserved. Evidence: service plus API-route tests 27/27; admin endpoint/client/page-loader tests 17/17; Garden production build passed; root ESM+DTS build passed on the final tree; mandatory npm run lint passed; worktree and origin/main branch-range diff checks passed. npm run check also ran and reported only two untouched pre-existing prompt-monitor diagnostics in admin-ui/src/lib/events/prompt-monitor.ts and prompt-monitor.test.ts; the requested Garden build is green. title: All /api/admin JSON except the transcript endpoint is uncompressed and nothing supports conditional requests; compress everywhere and add ETag/304 to polled endpoints
description:
Evidence: sendCompressedJson (src/channels/backplane/http/primitives.ts:218, >=1KB threshold, Vary: Accept-Encoding) is used by exactly ONE route — the transcript endpoint (src/operator/garden/routes/session-routes.ts:380). listSessions, session-routes, search, and cogsec endpoints all use plain sendJson (primitives.ts:180, uncompressed). No Cache-Control/ETag/conditional handling exists on any /api/admin JSON response (server-transport.ts:18-19,80 covers only the static SvelteKit shell/assets). Several admin-ui pages poll on setInterval (subsystem-health, session-recovery, cognitive-security drift/approvals, scheduler, shards, confirmations, graph-proposals, chat, contact-approvals, telemetry) and re-download byte-identical payloads every tick — pure WAN waste against carlini.

Fix shape: (1) route all admin JSON through the compressed sender (or fold compression into a single response helper); (2) add ETag (payload hash) + If-None-Match => 304 in that helper and have polled endpoints/clients use it; (3) while in primitives.ts, check the synchronous brotli quality setting — sync high-quality brotli on multi-MB payloads would block the event loop; cap quality or make it async.

Scope: src/channels/backplane/http/primitives.ts, garden route files, polling clients in admin-ui as needed. Non-goal: caching mutation responses or anything under intake/cogsec apply paths.
acceptance_criteria: Every /api/admin JSON response >=1KB is served brotli/gzip when Accept-Encoding allows (spot-check listSessions, session-routes, search, cogsec events, telemetry); polled endpoints return 304 with matching If-None-Match and polling pages send it; compression settings verified event-loop-friendly (bounded brotli quality or async) on multi-MB payloads; no behavior change for clients without Accept-Encoding.
notes:
Opus sweep evidence (2026-07-14): sendJson used at 561 call sites across 28 non-test route files — dashboard, audit history, charge ledger, model usage, memory lists, telemetry, settings schema, contacts, wiki, scheduler, graph proposals — all uncompressed; sendCompressedJson's only user is session-routes.ts. Handlers already have req in scope, so the highest-leverage fix is swapping the shared JSON responder the route table uses rather than editing 28 files. Also confirmed: the polled queue endpoints (confirmations api-routes.ts:915, contact-approvals, graph-proposals-service.ts:127, cogsec approvals) send Cache-Control: no-store (routes/shared.ts:3) which actively forbids a 304 path — that header needs to change for the ETag half of this bead. Their backing stores are memoized in-process (e.g. pending-contact-approvals.ts:118-146), so poll cost is pure network; do NOT add store-level caching there. Alternative to ETag for queues: push over the existing garden ReconnectingWebSocket (admin-ui/src/lib/api/websocket.ts, already used by prompt-monitor:186).
Implementation landed on branch bead/t5z7.3 (commits 0afb4281 + 878fcccd, off main, unpushed — pending feature-branch merge + codex review + PR). Seam: WeakMap<ServerResponse,IncomingMessage> in primitives.ts, bound at the two admin dispatch sites (server-routes.ts dispatchAdminRoute, transport-server.ts dispatchAdminApiRoute) — all ~561 sendJson sites across 28 files get compression+conditional handling with zero call-site edits; unbound callers (api server, cert-manager, fleet-status) keep the exact legacy path. Brotli quality capped 11→4 (event loop). Weak ETag on GET 200 unless no-store; 304 on If-None-Match; mutations never get ETags. New ADMIN_POLLED_QUEUE_JSON_HEADERS (no-cache) applied surgically to the four polled queues only (confirmations, contact-approvals, graph-proposals, cogsec quarantine list) after a broad flip broke 8 unrelated endpoints' no-store assertions — reverted to surgical. apiGet cache mode no-store→no-cache so the browser revalidates. Validation: build success; vitest garden+backplane 66 files/476 tests passed; 9 new primitives tests incl. round-trip decode + 304 + legacy-path; eslint clean. Not run: admin-ui svelte-check (one typed literal).
Codex-reviewed, findings fixed, shipped in PR #42 (perf/efficiency-wave-1 → main, https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/pull/42). Gate on the branch: build+lint clean, full suite 7715 passed / 1 pre-existing environmental failure (psfn-framework-engc). Ready to close on PR merge.

Verified actual source: src/operator/garden/server-routes.ts:33-46 and transport-server.ts:39-52 bind inbound requests at both admin dispatch seams; src/channels/backplane/http/primitives.ts:193-206 keeps unbound non-admin callers on the legacy path while request-bound admin JSON uses the negotiated responder; primitives.ts:211-218 sets the 1KB threshold and synchronous brotli quality 4; primitives.ts:256-321 provides gzip/brotli, weak ETag/304, no ETags for mutation/no-store responses, and the review remediation defaulting authenticated cacheable GETs to private,no-cache; routes/shared.ts:3-13 plus the confirmations/contact-approvals/graph-proposals/quarantine routes scope no-cache revalidation to the four polled queues; admin-ui/src/lib/api/client.ts:69-80 uses browser no-cache revalidation. Focused canonical validation passed 84/84 tests across primitives, admin request routing/transport, API routes, quarantine routes, and the Garden API client. npm run lint passed; ESM+DTS build passed; Garden production build passed; git diff --check clean. No behavior change for clients without Accept-Encoding is covered by primitives.test.ts.

title: Load-older pagination full-loads the entire channel JSONL server-side; add bounded backward reads before a message id
description:
Evidence: when beforeId is set (scroll-up in Garden sessions page), AdminSessionDataService.getSessionMessages calls sessionStore.getEntriesInRange(sessionId, 0, beforeId-1) (src/operator/garden/services/session-service.ts:680). getEntriesInRange (src/persistence/sessions/store.ts:983) calls ensureChannelFullyLoaded (store.ts:432) which journalRuntime.loadChannel()s the ENTIRE channel JSONL into memory, then slices the last `limit` entries. Every older page costs a full-channel parse that scales with total channel length, not page size — heavy disk ops on the shared carlini box where 5 companions live.

Fix shape: extend the hgw3.4 bounded tail-read machinery (readRecentEntriesFromTail, store.ts:559 / segment rotation) to support "read N entries ending before id X" so backward pagination walks segments from the tail without a full load. Optionally serve the first page of hot sessions from the hgw3.5 Redis tail (currently wired to capture only, store.ts:663), but the file path must remain correct without Redis (Redis is optional; fail-closed).

Scope: src/persistence/sessions/store.ts + journal runtime read path. Non-goals: changing the pagination API shape (limit/beforeId/nextBeforeId), changing what entries are returned, or making Redis required.
acceptance_criteria: Requesting an older page on a large session performs IO bounded by page size (test asserts ensureChannelFullyLoaded/loadChannel is not invoked on the beforeId path); pagination results are byte-identical to the current implementation for the same cursor; getCompactionSummaries either bounded too or explicitly documented as full-load.
notes:
Implementation checkpoint awaiting independent review. Reader commit 2b0bc87b adds shared hgw3-compatible numbered JSONL segment discovery/backward byte scanning, readJournalEntriesBefore with bytes/read-calls/files instrumentation, SessionJournalRuntime HMAC verification with canonical replay on bounded-chain failure, and SessionStore.getEntriesBefore with tombstone full-replay fallback. Garden commit 689f7cfc replaces getEntriesInRange full-load pagination with a limit+1 bounded read while preserving nextBeforeId/hasMoreOlder; messagesOnly skips compaction projection. getCompactionSummaries remains intentionally documented as canonical full-archive replay pending a writer/index contract. Evidence: 107 focused reader tests passed; 102 focused Garden/store/port tests passed; final targeted Garden+port 23 tests passed; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed. Branch work/garden-wan-bounded-pagination is pushed and clean. Do not close until independent review.
Single bounded remediation complete after the one independent review; bead intentionally remains in_progress for orchestrator integration/final check. Commit 4b22e676 fixes every mandatory finding: HMAC-authenticated seek rows prevent unverified ids from excluding data; byte-offset binary seek bounds deep unsegmented cursor IO; verified segment-boundary binary search avoids linearly opening newer siblings; sibling-writer channel-index fingerprint refresh plus active tombstone IDs prevents stale secret disclosure without ordinary-page full replay; sealed siblings are canonical for replay, metadata, tail reads, fingerprints, quarantine/integrity fallback, and rewrite collapse; numbered siblings are excluded from session discovery; lint finding removed. Exact regressions cover tampered first row id (signed ids 1-8, row 1 id 999, before 7/limit 2 returns canonical ids 5-6), 1,000-row deep cursor IO, 100-segment traversal, sibling-writer tombstone privacy/no full replay, tampered sealed-segment canonical fallback, and full logical-archive authority. Validation: 137 focused tests passed across journal port/utils, journal runtime, SessionStore/stale-window, and Garden session service; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed ESM+DTS; git diff --check passed. Branch pushed; local and origin/work/garden-wan-bounded-pagination both 4b22e6768914db9b83ffcef2b87f6feed95f68d0.

Exactly one independent review identified mandatory HMAC skip-authority, deep-cursor/segment IO, sibling-writer tombstone privacy, segmented canonical authority, and lint gaps; exactly one remediation commit 4b22e676 resolved them. Final fixed-point evidence on the integrated feature branch: HEAD and origin/feat/garden-wan-performance were identical at 4b22e676 before validation; six exact regressions passed (unauthenticated first-row id, deep unsegmented cursor, 100 sealed segments, sibling-writer tombstone privacy, tampered sealed-segment canonical replay, and logical segmented archive authority); proportional journal/session/Garden slice passed 137/137; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed ESM and DTS; git diff --check passed. Public pagination API and optional Redis behavior remain unchanged. Parent psfn-framework-t5z7 intentionally remains open because .5/.9/.10 remain live.

title: SessionStore constructed before a channel's first append in another process can mint a duplicate archive file with overlapping ids
description:
Evidence: surfaced 2026-07-14 while writing the hgw3.5 Redis-tail parity test (two SessionStore instances over one sessions dir): an instance constructed BEFORE another process performs a channel's first-ever append does not see the new archive via its channel index, and its own first write for that channel mints a SECOND archive file for the same channel with ids overlapping the first. Pre-existing on main — not introduced by the hgw3 branches.

Context: multi-process deployments (agent/gateway/garden) all construct SessionStore over the shared sessions dir at startup; a channel first spoken to after startup is exposed. Related seams: resolveExistingSession / ensureChannelForWrite / primeChannelIndexFromDisk in src/persistence/sessions/store.ts + store/channel-index.ts (whole-file index rewrites). The hgw3.1 archive-fingerprint fix does not cover this (no archive exists yet to fingerprint at construct time).

Scope: on first write for an unknown channel, re-check the shared index/disk for an archive created since construction before minting a new file. Non-goal: general index redesign.

Acceptance: regression test — store A constructed, store B appends first entry for channel X (new file), store A then appends to X → exactly one archive file exists, ids strictly increasing, both entries present; fails on current main.
notes: Related read-side flavor confirmed during the hgw3 concurrency fix (2026-07-14): a store constructed before a channel exists never re-primes its channel index outside listSessionsByRecentActivity, so a sibling process's brand-new channel stays invisible to count/getRecent/getRecentTurnRecords until re-prime. Same root cause family (index priming at construct time); fix both here.

title: Remove regressed local record guards and restore shared-type-guard gate
description: Summary: npm run verify:shared-type-guards fails on the current feat/cost-accounting-derived branch after the earlier psfn-framework-qfa work was closed. The exact regressions are scripts/lib/supply-chain-check.ts:76 function isRecord, src/core/cogsec/intake/scanners/rule-engine.ts:111 function isRecordValue, and src/shared/contracts/intake-envelope.ts:390 function isRecordValue. Why: duplicated structural guards can diverge and violate the repository contract to use src/shared/utils/types.ts as the single owner. Preserve current validation behavior with focused tests. Non-goals: do not alter CAM accounting/certification behavior or perform unrelated type-guard refactors.

description: Summary: npm run verify:identity-literals fails on the current feat/cost-accounting-derived branch because config/identity-literal-scan-allowlist.json no longer accounts for the live source surface. title: Persisted leaked history stamps in L0 journal content need a rewrite + HMAC re-sign cleanup pass
description:
Evidence: Discord journal entries 5240, 5254, 5258 (and mirrored voice content, e.g. entry 5243's mirror note truncating at '[Tue') begin with leaked '[Ddd MM-DD-YY HH:mm]' stamps persisted INSIDE entry content by the 2x37.1 mimicry leak; on re-render they now double-stamp ('[Tue 07-14-26 09:37] [Tue 07-14-26 09:36] Wait...'). The outbound strip guard (28b5e334, merged 2026-07-14) prevents NEW leaks once deployed but does not clean history.

Context/ordering: BLOCKED until 28b5e334 is live on psfn-shard, else new leaks reappear after cleanup. Session journals are HMAC-chained: any content rewrite requires the full integrity-repair flow — run runSessionIntegrityRepair from a dev checkout against a copy of state/sessions (production image cannot run it; key is gateway-only GATEWAY_SESSION_HMAC_KEY), verify 0 failures and byte-identical content minus _hmac and the stripped stamps, install atomically with rebuilt _channel_index.json, restart the gateway. Backup trio first; agent scaled to 0. Cf. the 2026-07-07 self-inflicted unverified_history incident (psfn-framework-tswt/-68ou/-g59z).

Scope: strip leading stamp patterns from assistant-entry content (reuse stripLeadingHistoryStamps) across affected channels' journals; also fix stamped copies mirrored into other channels' system entries where the stamp came from the leak. Non-goal: touching any other content; no schema changes.

Acceptance: post-repair scan finds zero assistant entries matching the leading-stamp pattern; session integrity verify reports 0 signature failures on all rewritten files; two-turn live smoke shows no unverified_history wrapper.
close_reason: Operator decision 2026-07-14: skip. Only a handful of entries carry persisted leaked stamps (Discord 5240/5254/5258 + a mirrored voice fragment); the outbound strip shipped in 28b5e334 prevents new ones, and the residual context noise is too small to justify HMAC re-sign journal surgery. Reopen only if stamped history visibly affects her behavior.

title: Optional Redis-backed hot session tail so context builds stop depending on per-process file caches
description:
Context: session reads today are per-process in-memory caches (ChannelCache / recentEntriesByLimit / fullyLoaded entries) over the shared JSONL journals; agent, gateway, and garden each hold independent views of the same files, coordinated only by file-stat fingerprints and a whole-file-rewritten _channel_index.json. That coherence gap is the habitat of the duplicate-reply bug (sibling bug bead). A Redis hot tail (write-through on every session append; context capture reads the tail from Redis, falling back to file read on miss) gives all processes one consistent recent view and decouples L0 context assembly from file I/O. psfn-redis already runs in the chart and src/shared/cache/redis-cache.ts exists as the generic appCache — nothing session-shaped uses it yet.

Scope: adapter behind a port with config-owned enablement per deployment (owner-file field, fail-closed validation); JSONL journals remain the source of truth and the HMAC chain is untouched — Redis holds a bounded recent window only. Deployments without Redis keep exactly today's behavior. Non-goal: moving session persistence itself to Redis.

Acceptance: parity test — with the tail enabled, captureTurnSessionContext returns identical entries to the file path across a scripted multi-writer sequence including the recorded staleness scenario (append assistant, delay, append user, capture); enablement via owner file validated by verify:settings-contract; live validation gate passes with the feature on.
notes:
2026-07-14 landed on branch bead/hgw3.5-redis-session-tail (4d5c177b, based on hgw3.1's 377cb801). Write-through inside SessionStore (covers append, tombstones, CogSec rewrites=invalidate, reloadChannelFromDisk=poison); reads via per-capture decorator (session-tail-read-store.ts) with journal+tail merge by entry id, Redis wins, compaction proxy stacks on top. ZSET per channel psfn:session-tail:<sessionId>, score=entry id (idempotent out-of-order multi-process appends), _hmac stripped and rejected on read, ZREMRANGEBYRANK trim. Config: settings.json sessionTailCache {enabled:false, maxEntriesPerChannel:512(16-8192)}, owner-file validated; enabled+unreachable Redis fails startup; runtime failure degrades loudly (rate-limited warn 30s) to journal. Behind-tail = miss + repopulate; integrates with (never bypasses) the hgw3.1 heal guard. 30 new tests + all required suites green incl. parity on the recorded staleness scenario; verify:settings-contract, lint, build pass; zero new tsc errors. Orchestrator re-ran: 12/12 + settings contract pass.
Residuals recorded: cross-process poison propagation (pub/sub) out of scope; replaceTail doesn't hold journal lock (next behind-check repairs); CogSec invalidate fire-and-forget microsecond window. Default disabled — chart/values enablement is an ops step at ship time.
2026-07-14 review round 3 (Codex, resumed thread): TOCTOU double-read FIXED; async caller audit FIXED. Three residuals ACCEPTED for ship because the tail is DEFAULT-DISABLED (dormant code) and each has a bounding backstop — treat as pre-enablement checklist before sessionTailCache.enabled is ever set true anywhere: (1) enqueue-time epoch GET resolves after ensureConnected, so the sync journal lock can release before epoch capture (store.ts:589, redis-session-tail-cache.ts:109) — bounded by journal-wins-on-overlap for ids within the journal window; tighten by capturing epoch under an async-aware lock or a pre-issued pipelined GET. (2) post-rewrite INCR failure leaves the durable rewrite without a shared epoch advance (store.ts:632,653,1156) — first (pre-rewrite) bump already fenced old rows; local poison + loud throw; residual is repopulations-from-pre-rewrite-reads under the new epoch. (3) cross-process-write-lock restoration window: mismatched live lock renamed away before identity verify can let a third process acquire then be replaced (cross-process-write-lock.ts:68,79,113) — rotation is independently protected by exclusive linkSync claims; refine with verify-before-rename + non-clobbering rename-back.
Code shipped in 576e33cd but the feature is DEFAULT-DISABLED live — bead stays open for the enablement step: work through the pre-enablement checklist (three documented residuals), add chart/values sessionTailCache enablement + PSFN_REDIS_* env, then re-run the rollout gate with the feature ON to meet the remaining acceptance criterion.

title: Turn records persist the same data 2-3x per turn and duplicate static content across turns
description:
Evidence (turn 019f60eb, 631KB total): conversation content stored 3x — sessionContext.recentEntries 130KB (raw entries), plan.messages 64KB (same entries rendered), providerWireMessages 83KB (same messages serialized again; ~80/134 entry contents verbatim in all three). plan.toolDefinitions == toolContext.activeTools byte-identical (58KB x2 = 116KB/turn); across 49 turns only 5 distinct tool-definition sets (~5.7MB written for ~290KB unique). System prompt material ~4 ways: plan.blocks 51KB, finalSystemSections 53KB, inputSections 35KB, plan.variables 40KB, templates 15KB. Result: _turn_records/1313001762793197678.jsonl is 392MB at only ~600-700 turns.

Scope, in order: (1) drop intra-record dupes — activeTools becomes a ref into plan.toolDefinitions; stop persisting providerWireMessages (derive at read; keep a hash for integrity); (2) content-address cross-turn statics — tool-definition sets and static prompt blocks stored once by hash in a sidecar, records store the hash; (3) store recentEntries as L0 entry-id ranges + exclusions instead of copies, keeping inline only render-divergent deltas (stamps, merges, untrusted wrappers) — note refs must tolerate later journal redaction/repair. BLOCKED BY the read-side derivation bead (Garden must render slim records first). Non-goal: rotation/tail reads (separate bead); no loss of forensic fidelity — a slim record + journal + sidecar must reconstruct today's full view.

Acceptance: typical chat turn record <= ~100KB; reconstruction test proves a slim record derives views byte-equivalent to a fat record for the same turn; live validation gate still passes turn-record checks.
notes:
2026-07-14 landed on branch bead/hgw3.3-turnrecord-slimming (e5e88a26, based on hgw3.2's 56e325ca). Persist-time stripDerivableTurnSnapshotDuplicates in cloneTurnObservabilityForRecord (live agent.turn.snapshot events stay fat): providerWireMessages dropped ONLY when byte-equal to the shared derivation (deriveProviderWireMessagesForTurnSnapshot in prompt-invocation-history.ts — Garden Loom now calls the SAME function, no drift possible; group/system-speaker/MoA/vision turns auto-fail the compare and keep the copy). activeTools dropped when byte-identical to plan.toolDefinitions. Content-addressed tooldefs sidecar (_turn_records/_shared/tooldefs/<sha256>.json, write-once atomic, plan.toolDefinitionsRef; dangling/mismatched/ambiguous refs are loud errors + Garden requireResolvedPlanToolDefinitions guard). Contracts: providerWireMessages and activeTools now optional, absence-preserving everywhere. recentEntries-by-ref deferred as specced; finalSystemSections still persisted. Measured: realistic DM fixture 63,081B fat → 5,392B slim (8.5%). 769 tests green across substrate-agent/garden/persistence/core-turns; lint clean; zero new tsc errors. Orchestrator re-ran 23 tests across the three key files: pass.
Integration notes: expected small merge conflict with hgw3.4 in createFilesystemTurnRecordStorePort (imports + append/read tail); sidecar GC should fold into rotation design (orphaned tooldefs harmless but permanent); any NEW raw-JSONL reader must resolve toolDefinitionsRef (attribution-repair passes refs through untouched, correct).
close_reason: Shipped in 576e33cd. Persist-time strip (byte-compare vs shared derivation — write/read cannot drift), activeTools deduped, tooldefs content-addressed to _shared/tooldefs sidecar with fail-closed refs. Fixture: 63KB→5.4KB (8.5%). Live-verified post-ship: smoke turn record has no providerWireMessages, no activeTools dupe, toolDefinitionsRef=b8698f96... resolving from the sidecar; record 119KB vs ~631KB before. recentEntries-by-ref deferred by design (needs redaction-interaction design).

title: Garden/Loom derives wire and prompt views from canonical turn-record fields at read time
description:
Evidence: per-turn record measured 631KB (turn 019f60eb); providerObservability.providerWireMessages (83KB) is deterministically derivable from plan.messages + promptContext.currentTurnInput (rebuildProviderWireMessagesForPrompt already implements the conversion); toolContext.activeTools is byte-identical to plan.toolDefinitions (58KB each); promptContext.finalSystemSections largely re-renders plan.blocks.

Context: Garden session views (session-service buildTurnData, session-turn-observability buildPromptLoomData, admin-ui loom) currently read the embedded copies. Before the write side can stop persisting duplicates (sibling slimming bead), every display surface must derive those views from the canonical fields, and must handle BOTH old fat records and new slim records (years of history already on disk).

Scope: read-side only — no change to what is written. Non-goal: changing loom UX.

Acceptance: with providerWireMessages/activeTools/finalSystemSections absent from a record, Garden loom and turn views render byte-equivalent output to today (fixture test comparing derived views against an old fat record's embedded copies); old records still render.
notes:
2026-07-14 landed on branch bead/hgw3.2-loom-read-derivation (56e325ca, based on e76f7d87). Garden consumers now derive providerWireMessages (via runtime's own rebuildProviderWireMessagesForPrompt + contextMessagesToPiMessages — byte-exact for DM text turns), activeTools (from plan.toolDefinitions, byte-identical), finalSystemSections (lossy plan-block projection, commented as such). Embedded copies preferred verbatim when present. 6/6 new fixture tests + existing suites pass; lint clean; zero new tsc errors. Orchestrator re-ran: 6/6.
Handoff constraints for hgw3.3 (write-side): (1) cloneProviderObservability (src/core/turns/snapshot.ts:242) does unguarded .providerWireMessages.map and the contract field is required — must become optional with absence PRESERVED (not coerced to []); (2) derived wire diverges for group-attribution, system-speaker, and MoA turns (currentTurnInput is raw, not formatCurrentTurnUserContentForPrompt output) — slim records must keep enough to stay faithful for those shapes; (3) finalSystemSections is a semantic decomposition, NOT losslessly derivable from plan.blocks — keep persisting it. The two clean wins are providerWireMessages (~83KB) and activeTools (~58KB).

Garden derives wire messages (runtime's own derivation fn), activeTools (plan.toolDefinitions), finalSystemSections (lossy projection, documented) when embedded copies absent; fat records render verbatim. 6 fixture tests + suites green; live Garden serving turn views on slim records post-ship.

title: Make world tool schema advertise exact registry IDs
description:
## Summary
Live Home Assistant control is healthy, but the companion repeatedly makes a failing first world(action=control/perceive) call because the tool schema teaches or permits guessed identifiers. Persisted production evidence on psfn-shard (2026-07-13 ET): bedroom control first used placeId=place.bedroom and failed, then world(action=list) exposed placeId=bedroom / affordanceId=bedroom_lights and the retry succeeded; office control first used affordanceId=office_light and failed, then listed and retried office_lights successfully. Hub HA health was ready against HA 2026.7.2 with light.main_bedroom present, and the successful retries returned HA context IDs, so this is not a transport/entity failure.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Load a places.json whose exact IDs are placeId=bedroom and affordanceId=bedroom_lights.
2. Ask the companion to turn the bedroom light off without first listing the registry.
3. Observe the model use the schema example pattern place.bedroom; the tool rejects it.
4. Observe the model call world(action=list), discover the exact IDs, retry, and successfully reach Home Assistant. The same pattern occurs with guessed office_light versus exact office_lights.

## Code Evidence
src/boundary/integrations/world/tools.ts createWorldTool describes placeId with the example place.living-room even though the live registry uses unprefixed IDs such as bedroom and office, while affordanceId is unconstrained free text.

## Scope
Make the world tool parameter surface registry-aware at construction time or otherwise advertise a bounded list of exact loaded placeId and affordanceId values; remove misleading synthetic examples; guide the model to list before acting when a requested name is ambiguous; retain strict fail-closed lookup for unknown IDs; add focused schema/tool tests covering unprefixed place IDs and plural affordance IDs.

## Non-goals
Do not add alias/normalization compatibility for guessed IDs, change Home Assistant entity mappings, weaken gateway registry validation, or alter approval/autonomy policy.
acceptance_criteria: The constructed world tool schema or description exposes exact loaded place and affordance IDs (including bedroom and bedroom_lights in a fixture) and contains no misleading place.* example; a representative control request can select the exact ID without a failed discovery call; unknown guessed IDs such as place.bedroom and office_light still fail closed; focused world tool/schema tests, npm run build, and npm run lint pass.

title: Queue-ingress hardening: assign FIFO position before author resolution and add dedicated unit tests for the new turn concurrency primitives
description:
Evidence: W6 review of 72238bc8 (working_docs/w6-review-1-record.md). (1) FIFO position for idle ingress is assigned inside TurnQueueIngressCoordinator.runFreshOrdinary, after trySteerActiveRun awaits resolveAuthorContext (src/core/agent/substrate-agent.ts ~906-923), so ordering is call-order, not arrival-order; two un-awaited concurrent idle inputs whose author lookups race can invert, and an earlier idle steer can join a later fresh turn's run as ordinary active-run steering. Benign today because callers serialize per channel (e.g. Discord's per-channel processing lock). (2) turn-run-reservation.ts and turn-queue-ingress.ts have no dedicated .test.ts; coverage is integration-only via substrate-agent.test.ts despite subtle semantics (reader-behind-writer fairness, release-on-throw, descendant seal after callback settle, deferred-exclusive ingress).

Context: hardening carried out of the W6 (psfn-framework-s10mc.6.6) review; explicitly not a correctness defect at the current fixed point.

Scope: assign the FIFO slot before any await in the idle-ingress path (or document call-order semantics at the seam), and add direct unit/interleaving tests for TurnRunReservation and TurnQueueIngressCoordinator. Do not introduce a global cross-channel arrival-order guarantee; do not change candidate exclusivity semantics.

Acceptance: new unit tests cover writer fairness, release on throw/cancel, descendant seal post-settle, deferred-exclusive ingress identity, FIFO chain release-on-throw, and pending-flush bookkeeping; lint/build/focused suites green.
notes: Review #2 added two Low observations to this hardening scope: (O1) fresh-ordinary agent.prompt TOCTOU — between a fresh-ordinary run's agent.prompt and its agent_start event (which sets activePiQueueOwner), a concurrent handleMessage can hit pi-agent-core's 'Agent is already processing' throw; self-healing (both finally releases fire, no lock leak) and loud, no deterministic interleaving found. (O2) the 'multiple idle follow-up and steer inputs as fresh ordinary FIFO turns' test spies on Agent.prototype.prompt and never fires agent_start, so activePiQueueOwner coalescing is untested — drive real agent events in the new unit tests.
close_reason: Done in 8d56ec5b on feat/icp-autonomy. (1) runFreshOrdinary replaced with reserveFreshOrdinarySlot(): FIFO position claimed synchronously at ingress arrival before resolveAuthorContext, so arrival order (= reservation grant order) determines fresh-turn order; dispose() in finally means author-resolution failure cannot strand a slot; candidate exclusivity unchanged. (2) Dedicated unit tests added: turn-run-reservation.test.ts (5 — writer fairness/no-starvation, release on throw, release on AbortError, descendant seal after settle, deferred-exclusive ingress identity) and turn-queue-ingress.test.ts (8 — enqueued-flag no-dup, reference-identity splice, spread-clone no-false-match, O2 real agent_start/agent_end coalescing via canQueueIntoActiveOrdinaryRun, O1 FIFO release-on-throw self-heal for 'Agent is already processing', dispose release, arrival-order across concurrent slots). Validated: 246 focused tests, lint, build; merged tree passed two consecutive full suites (8,357 passed, exit 0).

title: Idle intention whispers deferred during a candidate turn are flushed only by public handleMessage, so coordinator-created fresh turns can delay them unboundedly
description:
Evidence: three independent W6 reviews of 72238bc8 (see working_docs/w6-review-1-record.md) converged on the same mechanism. An idle internal intention follow-up that cannot join an active run is retained by TurnQueueIngressCoordinator.deferInternalFollowUp (src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-queue-ingress.ts:50-60). The only flush call site, enqueuePendingInternalFollowUpsForOrdinaryRun, is invoked from public handleMessage (src/core/agent/substrate-agent.ts ~1203). Fresh ordinary turns created by the coordinator itself (idle steer/followUp via runFreshOrdinary -> handleMessageUnderReservation) bypass the flush, so under a sequence consisting only of such turns the whisper is never delivered. No loss or duplication: the message stays in memory and delivers on the next real handleMessage; realistic effect is bounded delay of a self-note.

Context: found during the W6 (psfn-framework-s10mc.6.6) queue-isolation review; graded Low/Medium, deliberately NOT a review-resetting finding. The deferral itself is intentional and improves candidate isolation versus the old always-enqueue-to-raw path.

Scope: flush pending internal follow-ups when coordinator-created fresh ordinary turns start (not only in public handleMessage), preserving the invariant that pendings never enqueue into a candidate turn. Do not revert to raw-queue enqueue; do not change candidate fail-closed refusal semantics.

Acceptance: a test proving (a) a whisper deferred during a candidate turn is delivered by the next fresh ordinary steer/followUp turn without a real inbound message, (b) whispers are never silently dropped, and (c) a pending whisper only ever refuses or waits out a candidate turn, never enters its prompt/tool scope. Focused substrate-agent suite stays green.
notes: Related: psfn-framework-8l9c (moving queued whisper/follow-up drain out of live user turns) touches the same flush seam; coordinate so the fresh-ordinary flush lands wherever the drain ends up.
close_reason: Fixed in 986a55d3 on feat/icp-autonomy: TurnQueueIngressCoordinator fresh-ordinary slot run now calls enqueuePendingInternalFollowUpsForOrdinaryRun after the FIFO predecessor settles, so coordinator-created fresh turns (idle steer/followUp) flush deferred whispers — no longer handleMessage-only. Invariants preserved: enqueued-flag no-dup, by-reference message_start splice, candidates bypass the coordinator so a pending whisper still only refuses or waits out a candidate turn. Acceptance tests added in substrate-agent.test.ts: whisper deferred during a candidate delivers on the next fresh ordinary steer turn without a real inbound message, exactly once, never dropped; never enters candidate prompt/tool scope. Validated: 246 focused tests, lint, build; merged tree passed two consecutive full suites (8,357 passed, exit 0).

title: [S10 ICP] Extend canonical contact/notify/availability tools for permit-governed companion outreach

title: Add soft-guidance and circuit-breaker principle to the charter
description: Update docs/PSFN_PROJECT_CHARTER.md, the sole canonical PSFN charter, with a normative principle for companion autonomy and operational pacing. The charter must state that weighted, contextual, and reversible guidance is preferred over arbitrary hard behavioral limits: concern, fatigue, charge/budget pressure, rest, tool cost, and loop risk should normally taper activity, recommend a lower-cost path, defer work, or invite a natural stopping point. It must explicitly distinguish acceptable contextual guidance such as 'be concise' from an imposed fixed response shape such as 'always reply in exactly two sentences' (unless a user-requested protocol or machine-readable format requires it). Preserve immediate hard fail-closed boundaries for CogSec, consent, authorization, secrets, containment, and other safety invariants. Define operational circuit breakers as rare, proportionate fallbacks for imminent resource harm or demonstrated failure of softer controls; require visibility/auditability and clear recovery/reset behavior. Keep scope to the charter only; do not modify runtime policy or implementation in this task.
acceptance_criteria: docs/PSFN_PROJECT_CHARTER.md contains a clear soft-guidance-first principle; it separates autonomy/resource pacing from non-negotiable safety boundaries; it prohibits arbitrary fixed personality/reply-shape constraints while allowing requested protocol formats; and it defines high-threshold, auditable, recoverable circuit breakers as exceptional operational fallbacks.

title: Habit wake estimator scans only the latest-active session tail, never the partner's cross-channel history — always falls back (sampleDays 0)
description:
**Evidence (live + code, 2026-07-12):** registration log shows `{"timingMode":"habit","source":"habit_fallback","sampleDays":0,"fallbackReason":"no_recurring_sleep_gap"}` despite months of partner history. Root cause (traced during kz0i): resolveMorningWakeSnapshot → resolveStartupSessionMetadata('reuse_latest_session') → store.getLatestSessionByTimestamp() picks the single most-recently-active channel system-wide (manager.ts:1439); getRecentSessionEntries(sessionId, 2000) returns only that one channel's retained tail (store.ts:740). If the last-active channel is an api:/PWA or low-traffic room — or even the right channel post-compaction — the role-user timestamps carry no recurring overnight→morning gaps in the 03–12 band, so estimateWakeWindow correctly returns no_recurring_sleep_gap. The estimator math is fine; the input surface is wrong.

**Scope:** feed the estimator a cross-channel partner-timestamp projection: role-user timestamps for the partner across their channels over habit.extendedWindowDays (SessionManager/SessionStore or a Postgres projection query — session_messages_projection already has author+timestamp). Recompute at the Garden admin route too (it re-resolves the snapshot live). Non-goal: changing estimator thresholds or wake-band defaults.

**Acceptance:** unit test where partner timestamps span two channels and months; snapshot returns source 'habit' with a plausible window; live registration log shows sampleDays >= minSampleDays and source habit (not habit_fallback) after a few days of normal use.

**Depends on:** psfn-framework-kz0i (gate rework shipped first; fixed-time fallback is the interim per operator). Related future: psfn-framework-twhd (sensor-driven wake).

title: Active timezone is env/code-default owned, not settings-owned — no Garden surface, contrary to config-ownership doctrine
description:
**Evidence:** resolveActiveTimezone() = process.env.TZ || 'America/New_York' (src/shared/time/active-timezone.ts:1,56-58); ensureActiveTimezone() syncs process.env.TZ at boot in all three entrypoints. No settings.json key, no Garden/admin endpoint. It currently happens to match the partner timezone (America/New_York) only because the code default does.

Additionally the core Scheduler 'local' cadence branch (scheduler.ts:64-119, getCurrentSlotStart) uses process-local Date methods and is only correct because ensureActiveTimezone ran before the first tick and V8 honors the runtime TZ change — verified firing correctly on live (daily-review 06:00 ET, weekly-review 07:00 ET Sun), but the coupling is fragile and inconsistent with rest-window.ts:32-49 which resolves via Intl + resolveActiveTimezone.

**Scope:** make active timezone a settings.json-owned value (owner-file contract + Garden exposure) with env TZ as bootstrap only, per CLAUDE.md config doctrine; refactor getCurrentSlotStart 'local' branch to resolve via the active timezone with Intl instead of process-local Date methods. Related-but-separate: UTC calendar day keys in fatigue-budget.ts:105 (daily fatigue budget rolls at 20:00 ET), analysis-workbench loop.ts:135 (daily cost governor), memory retrieval scoring.ts:273 recency bucketing — decide per-site whether UTC keying is acceptable or should follow active tz.

**Acceptance:** timezone editable via Garden and persisted in settings.json; scheduler unit test proves 'local' daily cadence fires at configured wall-clock in the settings timezone with process TZ forced to UTC and no ensureActiveTimezone call.
close_reason: Duplicate of psfn-framework-i698; content merged there as 2026-07-12 comment

title: Contact.timezone is stored and shown in prompts but no outbound gate consumes it; quiet hours are one global window
description:
**Evidence:** Contact.timezone exists (src/core/contacts/types.ts:274, Postgres-persisted, Garden-writable with IANA validation in contacts-service.ts:76-105) and renders into the contact card (runtime-context.ts:754,1010) — but grep of intention/ and scheduler/ shows no gate ever reads it. evaluateProactiveOutboundTimeGate (src/core/intention/proactive-time-gate.ts:109-128) evaluates a single global window (scheduler.json episodicProcessing rest window, live 00:00-09:00, timeZone 'local' → resolveActiveTimezone). The contact tool (contacts/tools.ts:34-66) has no timezone action, so the companion can neither read nor set it programmatically.

**Context:** Intent is "don't message people who are sleeping" — especially in multi-user rooms where recipients span timezones. Today all outbound suppression assumes everyone lives in the admin timezone.

**Scope:** (1) per-recipient quiet-hours evaluation using Contact.timezone with fallback to the global window; (2) recipient resolution in weighted-thought-outreach and proactive-outbound before delivery; (3) policy for mixed rooms (defer if any/all recipients in quiet hours — decide and document); (4) optionally expose timezone read (at least) on the contact tool. Non-goal: per-contact sleep-window schedules beyond timezone-shifted global window (separate feature if wanted).

**Acceptance:** unit tests where a proactive send to a contact with timezone Europe/Berlin is blocked at 03:00 Berlin while 21:00 ET, and allowed at 10:00 Berlin; multi-user room case exercises the documented policy.

title: Generate cute sprite sheets via the hub fal.ai pipeline and swap the CSS face for sprite rendering
description:
Evidence: the sprite is CSS spans (companion-sprite.tsx:22-30); a full sprite-sheet toolchain already exists in the hub repo — SpriteSheetManifest with kind 'expression'|'viseme' (src/ts/device-studio/sprites.ts:59-78) and fal.ai generation via sprite-cli.ts/fal-provider.ts (default model fal-ai/nano-banana).

Scope: (1) freeze the expression-id list from sprite v2 (~16) and generate each in TWO crops — full body (avatar view) and head-only (mini sprite) — plus the 7 tool-activity animation loops and the touch-reaction frames (headpat-happy, hug-squeeze, kiss-blush); (2) pack sheets with the existing pipeline, ship under companion-ui/public/ with a manifest keyed by expression id; (3) renderer swap in companion-ui behind the same three-layer state model — CSS face remains the fallback when the manifest fails to load (fail-visible, not blank); (4) character design consistency pass with the operator before bulk generation (one reference sheet approved first).

Non-goals: no viseme sprite set yet (amplitude lipsync only needs 2-3 mouth frames); no runtime fal.ai calls from the PWA — generation is offline/CLI.
acceptance_criteria: All expression/tool/touch ids resolve to frames in the shipped manifest (vitest enumerates); bundle size delta documented and < 1.5MB with lazy-loaded avatar-view sheets; manual: mini sprite and avatar view render sprite art with the same state transitions the CSS face had; operator signs off on the character sheet.

title: Phone GPS reaches PSFN as place semantics only: device.location -> hub geofencing -> placeId and context notes
description:
Evidence: PSFN deliberately has no lat/long type — location is placeId/siteId/label in SituatedLocation (src/core/self-model/state.ts:67) resolved from routing.satellite.placeId with 6h staleness handling (src/core/self-model/situated-location.ts). The S10 location epic psfn-framework-vinz owns the places/world surface; this bead adds only the mobile-device feed into it. No geolocation API usage exists in companion-ui.

Scope: (1) companion-ui: navigator.geolocation.watchPosition while foregrounded (browser PWAs get no background GPS — accepted v1 limitation), significant-change filter (~100m + min interval), new 'device.location' client->hub message {lat, lon, accuracyM, timestamp}, permission UX in the settings drawer; (2) hub (~/PSFN-Satellite-Hub): RAW COORDINATES TERMINATE AT THE HUB — geofence against configured zones (home first; HA zones later), bind/unbind the phone satellite's placeId on zone entry/exit, emit zone-transition stimuli ('left home' as observe, 'arrived home' as respond) via the PSFN stimuli endpoint, and pass a coarse label ('out, near <zone>') via per-turn contextNotes in PsfnChannelContext (embodied-session.ts:45-69) when unzoned; (3) zone config lives hub-side, not in the PWA.

Privacy invariant (hard requirement): no raw coordinates in any PSFN prompt, message content, log line, or relay payload — labels only, sanitized. Non-goals: no background tracking, no PSFN core schema changes, no HA zone sync yet.
acceptance_criteria: Hub tests: coordinate->zone binding and transition debounce; grep-level check that lat/lon fields never appear in stimuli/contextNotes payloads; manual: walking out of the home zone with the app open yields her awareness of departure without a forced reply; typecheck/lint/build green in both packages.

title: companion-ui implements the hub browser audio contract: composer Voice Chat and hands-free avatar mode
description:
Evidence: mic modes exist but are fail-closed by design — companion-ui README: 'Browser audio capture and TTS transport are shown fail-closed until the hub/client voice path is implemented.' The hub already streams audio to satellites: session.ready advertises audioFormat pcm_s16le_16000_mono_in / mp3_44100_out (hub server.ts:296), mp3 frames bracketed by audio-init/audio-end text signals (server.ts:795-815); the Node pi-client proves the contract.

Scope: (1) capture: getUserMedia -> AudioWorklet downsample to 16k mono PCM -> base64 'audio' client frames; (2) playback: buffer mp3 frames between audio-init/audio-end, decode via Web Audio, expose an amplitude signal the sprite uses for v1 lipsync (mouth open/close); (3) wire into BOTH composer Voice Chat mode and the avatar view (hands-free: mic open while view active, wake lock held, interrupt on user speech per existing 'interrupt' message); (4) update hello capabilities to include audio input/output so the hub actually streams; (5) iOS Safari quirks handled explicitly (user-gesture AudioContext unlock, permission persistence).

Non-goals: no viseme-based lipsync (amplitude only, v1); no Wyoming/legacy path; no server-side changes expected — hub contract already exists.
acceptance_criteria: Manual on phone (primary): full duplex voice turn in avatar view — speak, see 'listening', hear her reply with mouth movement; interrupt works mid-reply. vitest covers frame bracketing/reassembly; test/typecheck/lint/build pass.

title: companion-ui adds a full-screen avatar view with hit regions and a touch gesture vocabulary
description:
Evidence: companion-ui has no tabs/views — one thread surface plus two overlay drawers (README 'Current UI Surfaces'); the large-sprite interaction surface does not exist.

Scope: (1) simple view switcher (thread | avatar) — no router; (2) avatar view renders the large sprite (full-body expression ids from sprite v2) with hit regions (head, cheek, body) and gesture classification (tap / double-tap / long-press / drag; port thresholds from the hub Device Studio display-preview.ts:559-578 — double-tap 340ms, long-press 550ms); (3) region x gesture map: head tap/drag = headpat/petting, body long-press = hug, cheek double-tap = kiss, each with instant local reaction animation and the coalesced touch.interaction upstream path from the prior bead; (4) the view keeps the tiny connection indicator and drawers reachable; thread state is preserved when switching.

Non-goals: voice controls in this view land with the voice bead; no sprite art dependency (CSS face acceptable).
acceptance_criteria: companion-ui test/typecheck/lint/build pass; vitest covers region+gesture -> stimulus kind mapping; manual on phone: hug and kiss gestures each produce a distinct local reaction and a single upstream event; switching views mid-stream does not drop the live assistant draft.

title: Hub and companion-ui deliver coalesced touch interactions; mini sprite head becomes pettable
description:
Repos: ~/PSFN-Satellite-Hub + companion-ui. Evidence: the sprite is already a <button> (companion-sprite.tsx:16) with no onPress behavior; no ClientToHubMessage exists for touch (protocol.ts:1-13 union).

Scope: (1) hub: new ClientToHubMessage 'touch.interaction' {kind, region, count, durationMs} + handleMessage case (server.ts:312-414) + CompanionBridge POST to the PSFN stimuli endpoint (mirror submitApprovalDecision:100-136), gated on a control capability (e.g. 'touch'); (2) companion-ui: mini-sprite tap = headpat with INSTANT local reaction (blush/closed-happy-eyes/hearts animation — no round-trip wait) plus upstream send; (3) burst coalescing client-side: a petting session aggregates into one event with count+duration after ~2-3s of quiet, never N messages for N taps; (4) mirror the new message into companion-ui protocol files.

Non-goals: no avatar view yet (next bead); no haptics.
acceptance_criteria: Hub test: touch.interaction from a capable client POSTs one stimulus to a mock PSFN endpoint; UI vitest: 12 rapid taps within the window emit exactly one coalesced event with count=12; manual on phone: tapping the mini sprite produces an immediate local reaction and a companion reply referencing the headpat.
notes: Implementation shipped across framework main commits 16c5c1b9/af831212 and Satellite Hub main dcf1e92. Companion UI tests proved 12 rapid taps coalesce into one count=12 event; Hub tests proved touch capability gating and typed relay; build/lint passed. Live Helm rev 50 serves UI image localhost/psfn-companion-ui:0.1.0-kube-af8312129a62 and the deployed bundle contains headpat/touch.interaction markers. Hub/Core direct live stimulus and authoritative cooldown smokes passed. Remaining acceptance item before closure: operator taps the mini sprite from the enrolled phone/PWA and observes immediate local reaction plus companion response.
close_reason: Closed
