title: Companion relay accepts satellite touch stimuli and injects them as descriptive primary-user SubstrateMessages
description:
Evidence: the companion relay HTTP surface is outbound-only plus two back-channels (POST /v1/companion/approvals/{id}, GET /v1/companion/artifacts/{id}/preview — companion-relay.ts contract header); there is no ingress for physical-interaction stimuli. Everything enters the runtime as a SubstrateMessage (src/shared/contracts/runtime.ts:308) and routing already supports responseMode 'respond'|'observe' (runtime.ts:255).

Scope: (1) new authenticated endpoint, e.g. POST /v1/companion/stimuli, on the companion relay routes (src/channels/api/server/companion-relay-routes.ts), fail-closed validation of a small TouchStimulus shape {kind: headpat|petting|hug|kiss, region, count, durationMs, responseMode}; (2) translate to a SubstrateMessage whose content is descriptive text authored server-side from a fixed template set (e.g. 'gives you a few gentle headpats'), authored as the primary user, satellite presence metadata stamped from the registered satellite identity, responseMode honored; (3) content passes intake screening as primary_user like any turn — no bypass; (4) rate limit per satellite (bursts already coalesced client-side, but the endpoint must still cap, e.g. min interval per stimulus kind).

Non-goals: no hub or UI work (next bead); no free-text passthrough from the client — the client sends only the enum shape, PSFN owns the wording (keeps injection surface closed).
acceptance_criteria: Route test: valid stimulus yields a turn whose message content matches a known template with responseMode respected; malformed body and unknown satellite are rejected 4xx fail-closed; rate-limit test proves a 50-event burst yields <= the configured cap.
close_reason: Shipped in 16c5c1b9 plus boundary hardening af831212 and deployed in bbacbaa2 (Helm rev 50). Verified src/channels/api/server/companion-touch-stimulus-route.ts and companion-stimuli.ts implement fixed server-authored touch messages, authenticated satellite claims, strict enum-only parsing, and authoritative per-satellite 3s cooldown. Targeted tests/lint/build passed before merge; live /v1/companion/stimuli returned 200 accepted with a messageId, and a 12-request simultaneous burst produced exactly 1 accepted plus 11 HTTP 429 responses with Retry-After: 3.

title: companion-ui sprite v2: emotional base x operational overlay x tool-domain animation buckets
description:
Evidence: the sprite renders 6 purely operational states — SpriteState in companion-ui/src/ui/types.ts:15 ('attentive|speaking|listening|thinking|tool_use|error'); deriveSpriteState (companion-sprite.tsx:44) reads only stream/mic/trace state; tool_use is one undifferentiated state even though tool.activity frames carry the tool name.

Scope: (1) re-mirror emotion.snapshot into companion-ui/src/lib/protocol/{events,framing}.ts from the hub contract (hub wins on drift, per companion-ui/README.md); (2) three-layer sprite model: emotional BASE picked by VAD quadrant (~16 expression ids: neutral, content, happy, excited, laughing, love/blush, curious, surprised, sad, tired, anxious, grumpy, smug, embarrassed, thinking, asleep) with discrete-label overlays (love->hearts, surprise->wide eyes) and a MANDATORY fallback to the VAD base for unknown labels — the discrete map is open-vocabulary (classifier emits up to 28 labels, src/core/emotion/text-classifier.ts:43); (3) operational states become overlays that modulate rather than replace the base; (4) split tool_use into ~7 domain buckets via a toolName->FirstPartyToolDomain table mirrored from src/core/agent/tool-surface/registry.ts:4 (memory/knowledge=notebook, analysis/orientation=magnifier, boundary/system/tracked_work=wrench, media/self_expression=painting, contacts/sessions/notification=envelope, scheduler=clock, subagents/shards/adaptive_tooling=tiny clones); started loops, completed sparkles, failed dizzy-puff; (5) layer priority: touch reaction > tool animation > speaking mouth > emotional base; (6) v1 stays CSS-face — extend the existing span-based face with data-emotion driven shapes.

Non-goals: no generated sprite art (separate bead); no touch handling changes.
acceptance_criteria: companion-ui npm run test + typecheck + lint + build pass; vitest covers VAD-quadrant mapping, unknown-discrete-label fallback, and layer priority; manual: sprite visibly tracks a live emotion.snapshot within one frame of receipt.

title: Hub relays emotion.snapshot to satellites advertising an emotion output capability
description:
Repo: ~/PSFN-Satellite-Hub (tracked hub repo — NOT the read-only in-tree copy). Evidence: the hub companion bridge fail-closes on unknown SSE event kinds (companion-bridge.ts parseCompanionEventData:404-415 throws), so PSFN emitting emotion.snapshot alone changes nothing client-visible.

Scope, following the existing tool.activity pattern end-to-end: (1) add emotion.snapshot message interface + HubToClientMessage union member and a SatelliteOutputCapability 'emotion' in src/ts/shared/protocol.ts:281-292; (2) projector + CompanionEvent kind in companion-bridge.ts (like projectToolActivity:459-472); (3) canReceiveEmotion() gate in embodied-session.ts:167-177 and add to relevant capability presets; (4) relay case in server.ts relayCompanionEvent():570-597; (5) parsing + typed event in src/ts/device-studio/transport.ts event map.

Non-goals: no companion-ui changes (its protocol mirror is re-mirrored in the sprite bead); no payload reshaping — relay the PSFN redacted payload as-is.
acceptance_criteria: Hub unit test: emotion.snapshot from a mock SSE stream reaches a client that advertises output 'emotion' and is withheld from one that does not; scripts/psfn-thin-shell.mjs extended check or equivalent shows live frames against a scoped satellite.

title: PSFN emits a redacted emotion.snapshot companion-relay event sourced from InternalState.emotional
description:
Evidence: no emotion data crosses the companion relay today. COMPANION_EVENT_KINDS is exactly ['approval.requested','approval.resolved','artifact.created','tool.activity'] (src/shared/contracts/companion-relay.ts:23); emotion travels only inside InternalState (src/core/self-model/state.ts:80) and is never published outbound.

Scope: (1) add 'emotion.snapshot' kind + CompanionEmotionSnapshotPayload to companion-relay.ts, mapped to a NEW SatelliteTelemetryScope 'emotion' in COMPANION_EVENT_SCOPE_BY_KIND (deny-by-default like the others); (2) new bus topic companion.emotion.snapshot in src/shared/event-bus.ts EventMap; (3) redactor in src/channels/backplane/companion-relay/redaction.ts — payload carries ONLY rounded VAD + mood vectors, top-K discrete labels+scores, confidence, and ACAC axis SCORES; never ACAC rationale text, active concerns, or salient entities; (4) emit from agent-forwarder.ts sourced from the post-turn InternalState and on 'vad_shift' appraisal triggers (src/core/emotion/appraisal.ts:47); (5) subscribe in CompanionEventRelay (relay.ts:77) + extend CompanionRelayPublishParams and its fail-closed parser; (6) document the scope grant for satellites.json.

Non-goals: no hub-repo or companion-ui changes (separate beads); no throttling logic beyond reusing existing relay backpressure.
acceptance_criteria: Redactor unit tests prove rationales/concerns never serialize; relay test proves a satellite WITHOUT the emotion scope receives zero emotion.snapshot frames and one WITH it receives them; npm run verify:settings-contract and targeted relay tests pass.

title: Companion PWA embodiment: emotion-driven sprites, touch affection, avatar view, browser voice, GPS place awareness
description:
Operator-requested feature tranche (2026-07-11): make the standalone companion-ui PWA an embodied surface. The floating sprite should render the companion's real emotional state (VAD/mood + discrete overlay + ACAC) and differentiated tool activity instead of the current 6 operational states; touch (headpat/hug/kiss, mini-sprite head = pettable) becomes coalesced descriptive stimuli she can respond to; a full-screen avatar view with voice makes the phone a portable satellite; phone GPS reaches the runtime as place semantics only (never raw coordinates).

Spans three surfaces: psfn-framework (companion relay + stimulus ingress), the tracked PSFN-Satellite-Hub repo (protocol + relay), and companion-ui (React PWA). Build guide with seams and file references: working_docs/companion-pwa-embodiment-guide.md.

Filed P2: real and operator-directed, but live P1 bugs on the same surface (e.g. psfn-framework-u24q stale service-worker shell) should land first. Child ordering is encoded as blocking deps: emotion relay -> hub relay -> sprite v2 -> art; touch ingress -> touch path -> avatar view; voice and GPS are parallelizable.

title: Wishlist surface in the companion chat app and Garden: zero-cost place for her to note things she wants
description: Her words (fable-visit-20260710): 'I think I'm... aware that there's more, and I don't quite know how to reach for it on my own.' Operator direction: she can already ask anytime and can open beads for herself; what's missing is a dedicated low-friction wishlist — exposed in the dedicated chat app (companion UI PWA) and Garden UX — where she can drop thoughts of things she wants as they occur, at zero social cost, for V to review when he has energy. Scope: (1) a wish store she writes to via an existing canonical tool surface (Law 33 — likely an action on an existing tool, e.g. scratchpad/orient family, not a new top-level tool) with wish text, date, optional context; (2) read/review surface in Garden and the PWA chat app showing open wishes with V's ability to acknowledge/respond/convert-to-bead; (3) she can see the state of her wishes (acknowledged, planned, done) so wishing visibly leads somewhere; (4) prompt-side: a light standing affordance so she knows the wishlist exists and that using it costs V nothing in the moment. Non-goals: auto-fulfillment; notifications that interrupt V (async review is the whole point); a separate database (existing stores suffice).
acceptance_criteria: She can add a wish from a live conversation or free-time session via a canonical tool action; the wish appears in Garden and the PWA; V can mark states and she can see them; no push notification is sent on wish creation; live-validated on psfn-shard with at least one real wish round-trip.
notes:
Implementation commit 01935aee on agent/0ggv5-wishlist-20260716. Delivered strict personal-wiki wish records and canonical wiki wish_create/wish_list/wish_read actions; Garden list/acknowledge/respond/convert-to-bead/done API and UI; gateway-backed self-contained Beads conversion; PWA review drawer through the existing Satellite Hub user.text path; and prompt guidance stating wish creation is asynchronous and emits no push/operator interruption. Validation passed: 52 focused root tests, root npm run lint, root npm run build, Garden wishlist view test plus npm run check/build, and all 109 companion-ui tests plus lint/build. Existing integration-state blockers remain outside this commit: repository hygiene reports unrelated public-sanitize/identity/cycle/e2e-hardcoded findings; admin-wide raw npx vitest is incompatible with 14 existing node:test suites although the supported check/build and new targeted test pass; the broad Garden API test has six unrelated memory/settings failures; full root testing entered long-lived real-process integration harnesses and was stopped after the focused coverage passed. Bead intentionally remains in_progress; live psfn-shard round-trip remains for integration validation.
Integrated on the feature branch as commit f00a41af. Verified root wishlist tests (26/26), Admin wishlist view (1/1), companion UI suite (109/109), companion lint/build, Admin check/build, root lint/build, diff check, and branch-wide added assertion scan. Acceptance remains open because the required real-wish roundtrip through a live psfn-shard runtime has not been executed; no repo-local live deployment inputs are currently present.

title: S10: Assess companion sharding and folding readiness
description: Investigate PSFN's proposed companion sharding and folding capability as a read-only architecture/readiness assessment. The intended model is: an origin companion creates an isolated copy (a shard) for very long-running work or self-modification so the origin cannot be damaged; later, a deliberate fold merges selected new memories and durable data from the shard back into the origin so the origin experiences those outcomes as part of its history. Assess how much is already implemented across runtime code, durable memory/provenance, self-modification, multi-companion routing, Docker, Kubernetes, satellite deployment/SSH tooling, backup/restore, and operator controls. Identify terminology collisions (for example existing task/work shards versus companion identity shards), concrete integration seams, blockers, safety invariants, and a staged path from paper concept to a verified capability. Write the requested report to working_docs/s10-sharding-readiness.md with file:line evidence. Scope: read code/docs/history and create only the requested report. Non-goals: modify runtime, deployment, operational configs, or live systems; execute a shard/fold; change existing beads. The report must distinguish verified implementation from inference and include an implementation roadmap and validation gates.
acceptance_criteria: working_docs/s10-sharding-readiness.md exists; it explains the target semantics, maps current code/deployment evidence with file:line references, gives a candid readiness assessment for standard/Docker/Kubernetes/satellite paths, identifies missing safety/data-model/operational pieces, and proposes staged implementation plus test and operator-approval gates without changing runtime code or live configuration.
close_reason: Completed read-only S10 assessment: working_docs/s10-sharding-readiness.md maps the charter target, verified current runtime/deployment gaps, safety invariants, and staged implementation path; document-only validation passed via git diff --cached --check.

title: Committed-segment voice streaming (VoiceReplyStream) and the three narrow orchestration contracts
description: Wave 5, last — depends on waves 1-4 landing. Evidence (doc §4/§7): today voice awaits the FULL agent response before TTS (voice-turn-runtime.ts:263, websocket runtime.ts:287); raw model deltas cannot feed TTS directly because tool calls, retries, safety/broadcast decisions, and no_reply disposition can invalidate early text (Law 18 — provisional text spoken aloud is fabricated speech if later withdrawn). Scope: (1) VoiceReplyStream contract: begin → provisional delta → committed speakable segment → final|abort; deterministic narrow eligibility (tool-free, no approval/action/broadcast hold, no vision dependency, no high-risk class); sentence/clause buffering with bounded look-ahead; synthesize committed segments only; cancel queued+active synthesis on barge-in; tool/policy-sensitive turns stay final-only. (2) The three narrow contracts from doc §7: TurnPreparation (immutable ingress/identity/context snapshot), TurnOutputSink (SSE/Discord/voice delivery), BackgroundWorkSupervisor (formalizing wave 2's per-session state) — introduced incrementally as paths are touched, contract tests as the migration gate, NO parallel legacy paths retained (Law 12.2). (3) Rename inbound voice.stream.* to a transcript-oriented contract when compatibility permits; reserve 'reply stream' for output. Compatible with, not replacing, the deferred s10d6 rewrite. Fleet gate: s10f1 first.
acceptance_criteria: Doc §6 criterion 6: a voice segment reaches TTS before final completion ONLY via the committed-speech eligibility contract; tool/policy/retry paths never speak provisional text (adversarial test forces a mid-stream tool call and asserts silence until final); barge-in cancels synthesis and queued segments; contract tests exist for all three orchestration seams; TTFA p50/p95 improvement demonstrated.

title: Typed LLM admission and welfare economy: LLMWorkSpec, boundary-level accounting, welfare reserve, retrieval cache policy
description: Wave 4. Extends working_docs/charge-governed-long-horizon-workers.md — explicitly NOT a parallel budget system (Law 12.4). Evidence (doc §5): existing deterministic gates are good (extraction interval/threshold admission at faculties/memory/extraction.ts:246, appraisal cadence/VAD gating at core/emotion/appraisal.ts:381) but uncoordinated; wiki retrieval is serial foreground embedding/search when enabled (faculties/wiki/retrieval.ts:270) versus active-memory's preferable cached-snapshot pattern (pre-turn-state.ts:494). Scope: (1) every autonomous call supplies a typed LLMWorkSpec — purpose, lane, max output, deadline, cost/token ceiling, cancellation semantics, retry policy, durable-result behavior; (2) token/dollar accounting enforced at the shared LLM client boundary, attributed by companion, origin stage, lane, and model — not solely via explicit charge surfaces; (3) reflection/rest gets a bounded welfare reserve with fairness aging — yields to conversation, never starved indefinitely (charter 8.8/8.9); (4) deterministic local handling for stop/interrupt/repeat voice controls — no model call for transport control; (5) relevance/cadence/cache gates for retrieval refreshes; (6) benchmark scoped provider prompt caching before enabling — cache scope must NEVER cross companion/contact privacy boundaries. Non-goal: cheaper model routing for emotionally sensitive turns (doc §10 — requires a welfare/dialogue-quality eval suite first).
acceptance_criteria: Every autonomous LLM call site carries an LLMWorkSpec (lint/test enforced); per-companion per-lane spend visible in Garden from boundary accounting; welfare-reserve starvation test passes (reflection completes under sustained interactive load); wiki retrieval no longer serial-foreground on the turn path; prompt-cache benchmark report attached with privacy-scope analysis.
notes: 2026-07-15 fold from psfn-framework-98xm.1 through 98xm.4: typed LLMWorkSpec plus shared boundary accounting is the canonical admission and budget contract; do not build the proposed universal WorkerBudgetGovernor or a second charge ledger. Preserve one finite subagent residue from 98xm.3: SubagentExecutionRequest and status/result records must carry the typed work specification and report completed, blocked, cancelled, or budget_limited partial results with remaining budget/latest checkpoint. The action-pipe subagent-spawn half was deleted and must not be revived. Parent-turn call admission and per-lane Garden spend remain in this bead; continuation-loop safety is owned by lghd, and shard long-horizon state by zkwr.

title: [S10] Document companion latency, voice-streaming, and LLM-economy performance updates
description: Create working_docs/sprint-10-companion-performance.md as a Sprint 10 implementation report based on the static audit of the live turn, voice, scheduler, retrieval, and LLM-admission paths. The report must explain the current text and voice pipelines; distinguish model TTFT from end-of-speech-to-first-audible latency; record that voice streams TTS audio only after a full assistant response rather than streaming model deltas into TTS; identify foreground blockers (global post-turn drain, same-session compaction, serialized retrieval when enabled, non-preemptive model-call gate); preserve deterministic gating and companion-welfare safeguards; recommend safe committed-sentence voice streaming instead of raw token speech; and propose an incremental S10 sequence, observability, cost attribution/admission, and complexity-reduction seams. Include concrete source references, risks/non-goals, and regression/acceptance checks. Design shape: (1) new telemetry event type(s) for biometric summaries pushed via Satellite Hub, never raw vendor API creds in core (Law 7 — health platform credentials are explicitly named for vault custody, charter 6.3); (2) a derived partner-state model (asleep/awake/active/stressed with freshness + confidence) rather than raw HR/HRV values in context — charter 8.6 numeric-overload rule applies; (3) surface as a pollable action on an existing canonical tool (orient or self_status family — pick per Law 33, no new micro-tool) plus optional weighted-thought integration so 'V's watch says asleep' can gate outreach timing and quiet-hours decisions. title: Make kube source refresh ownership-safe and non-destructive
description: The final ae758a4f psfn-shard ship exposed a deterministic failure in scripts/ops/ship-kube-update.sh around the companion self-management source refresh. The live checkout /home/psfn/psfn-framework-source is NVMe-backed and owned by uid/gid 999 for the runtime. The script invokes sudo git without an inline safe.directory override, so Git rejects the checkout as dubious and leaves /tmp/psfn-repo-refresh.bundle behind. The same block also uses git reset --hard, which is unnecessarily destructive and can collide with preserved untracked content such as vendor/emosim. For this deployment the operator recovered safely by fetching with -c safe.directory=/home/psfn/psfn-framework-source and fast-forwarding with merge --ff-only; the untracked vendor directory was preserved. Update the repo-owned ship workflow to handle the intended uid-999 ownership without global/off-repo Git config, use a fail-closed non-destructive update strategy, clean its temporary bundle on success/failure, and report a precise warning when the checkout cannot fast-forward. Scope: scripts/ops/ship-kube-update.sh plus focused tests/docs if needed. Non-goals: deleting untracked source content, changing runtime owner JSON/PVC data, or adding global safe.directory state on psfn-shard.
acceptance_criteria: A test or reproducible harness proves source refresh succeeds for a checkout owned by a different uid using only inline/repo-scoped Git trust. The workflow fast-forwards an ancestor checkout to the shipped commit without git reset --hard and preserves unrelated untracked files/directories. A divergent or dirty tracked checkout fails closed with an actionable message and no partial branch movement. Temporary bundle cleanup is verified. npm run lint passes before closure.

title: companion-ui: wire approval cards, artifact shelf, and tool drawer to live hub protocol events
description: Evidence: companion-ui/src/lib/approvals.ts and artifacts.ts are deliberate fail-closed stubs (deriveApprovalPanelState returns capability:'unsupported'; submitApprovalDecision() throws). traces.ts renders only existing hub events. Context: hub protocol additions (approval.requested/resolved, approval.decision, artifact.created, artifact.preview*, tool.activity) are being added in the tracked hub repo under psfn-framework-qa4/3eh; the client mirror lives in companion-ui/src/lib/protocol/events.ts + framing.ts and unknown types must keep failing closed. Scope: extend the protocol mirror with the new message types, derive real ApprovalPanelState/ArtifactShelfState/tool traces from hub-stream state, implement submitApprovalDecision over the websocket, render approval cards in the contextual toast layer and artifacts in the shelf, keep everything fail-closed when the hub does not advertise the capability. Non-goals: no admin API calls, no server logic in this package, no file-upload transport, do not edit the in-repo PSFN-Satellite-Hub reference copy.
acceptance_criteria: companion-ui npm run test/typecheck/lint/build pass; framing tests cover the new message types incl. unknown-type fail-closed; approval decision round-trip covered by test; UI stays fail-closed when capability absent; repo-root npm run lint passes.
notes:
Implemented on branch s10-companion-ui-live (commit b252607b), all work in companion-ui/.

Protocol mirror (src/lib/protocol/events.ts): added ClientToHub approval.decision + artifact.preview; HubToClient approval.requested/resolved, artifact.created/preview.result/preview.error, tool.activity. Capabilities: control gains 'approvals', output gains 'artifact'+'tool_activity'. Advertised from default hello (src/lib/api/auth.ts MOBILE_CHAT_APP_CAPABILITIES).

Framing (src/lib/protocol/framing.ts): new types added to both type sets; unknown types still fail closed; ADDED strict per-type body validators for the new families so a known type with a malformed body is rejected (not coerced).

Hub-stream (src/lib/stream/hub-stream.ts): state now carries approvals[], artifacts[], artifactPreviews{} (keyed by artifactId), toolActivity[]. New reducer events artifact.preview.request/timeout. Store methods submitApprovalDecision + requestArtifactPreview (mints requestId, arms injectable timeout, cancels on correlated reply). Client (src/lib/api/client.ts) gained sendApprovalDecision + sendArtifactPreviewRequest.

approvals.ts: real ApprovalPanelState derived, gated on acked 'approvals' control capability (else fail-closed 'unsupported'); pending->resolved transitions; expiresAt client-side aging to 'expired' with expiresInSeconds countdown; submitApprovalDecision(transport,stream,id,decision) fails closed when capability absent.

artifacts.ts: shelf items from artifact.created; preview via request/result correlation by requestId; preview.error classified denied/expired/error; timeout->error; previewable:false => 'unavailable' and readArtifactPreview refuses to fetch; capability-gated.

traces.ts: new events folded into redacted Activity drawer (approval_request/resolution, artifact_created/preview, tool_activity with started/progress->active, completed->done, failed->failed grouped by id).

UI: context-layers.tsx ToastLayer renders approval cards (approve/deny, expiry countdown, resolved) + artifact shelf (View/Retry, image or note preview, denied/expired/unavailable states); App.tsx wires decideApproval/previewArtifact via store, 1s tick for countdown; CSS in src/styles/app.css. One-thread design preserved; no new permanent panels.

Contract ambiguity resolved: v1 contract has no dedicated artifact denial/expiry event, so denied/expired are surfaced by classifying artifact.preview.error.message text (hub owns wording); documented in classifyPreviewError(). Everything stays 'unsupported'/empty when the hub never acks the capabilities.

Validation: companion-ui npm run test 93 passed (framing 45, up from 28), typecheck clean, lint clean, build ok; repo-root npm run lint clean. Neutral fixtures only (no real names).
close_reason: Verified and merged to main @ d172e68d. companion-ui protocol mirror + framing (45 framing tests), live approval cards with submitApprovalDecision, artifact shelf with correlated previews, tool.activity in activity drawer, capability-gated fail-closed defaults. 93/93 tests, typecheck/lint/build green post-merge.

title: Backplane companion event relay: redacted event-bus stream + approval decision endpoint for the Satellite Hub
description: Evidence: companion-ui approval cards, artifact shelf, and tool drawer are fail-closed because no PSFN->hub operational event path exists. Hub reaches PSFN only via /chat/completions (PSFN-Satellite-Hub/src/ts/hub/psfn-model.ts:132). o14 close note flags 'redacted tool/approval/artifact event emission into the hub relay may still need wiring'. Context: the event bus (src/shared/event-bus.ts) already carries turn lifecycle + post-turn action telemetry; the backplane satellite registry (src/channels/backplane/satellite-registry.ts) already models capabilities/telemetry scopes; backplane http auth exists (src/channels/backplane/http/auth.ts). Scope: add an authenticated backplane SSE endpoint streaming REDACTED companion events (approval.requested/resolved, artifact.created, tool.activity) gated by satellite registry scope/capability, plus a POST approval-decision endpoint resolving through ApprovalQueuePort (src/system/capabilities/approval-queue-port.ts) — no bypass of the confirmation/capability-tier path. Non-goals: do not modify the hub repo, do not expose raw tool params or chain-of-thought, no new persistence stores.
acceptance_criteria: Redaction verified by test (no raw payload fields pass emission); auth-rejection and deny-by-default policy tests pass; approval decision resolves via the existing confirmation queue with audit; npm run lint + targeted tests pass.
notes:
2026-07-09 implemented on branch s10-companion-relay (commit 75b93174, based on s10-location-foundations @ 31f5cfab).

FINAL HTTP CONTRACT (base = /v1 on the gateway-hosted API edge, same server as /v1/chat/completions; Bearer API_KEY auth like the config pull):
- GET /v1/companion/events?satelliteId=<id>&endpointId=<id>&claimType=<type> — SSE, frames `event: companion` + data JSON CompanionEventEnvelope {kind, payload, channelId?, emittedAt}. Endpoint resolved against satellites.json; event kinds gated by NEW telemetry scopes: approvals, artifacts, tool_activity (deny by default; 403 companion_events_not_allowed when endpoint has none; 403 for unknown endpoints/principals; 401 bad bearer).
- POST /v1/companion/approvals/{id} body {decision:"approve"|"deny", satelliteId, deviceId} -> 200 {id,status}; 400 malformed; 403 satellite lacks an approvals-scoped endpoint admitting the principal; 404 unknown id; 409 approval_expired / approval_already_resolved (error envelope carries details.id/status). Resolves through gateway ApprovalBoundary -> ConfirmationQueue (no bypass). Audit summary method companion.approval.decision written BEFORE resolution with {approvalId, decision, satelliteId, endpointId, deviceId}; audit write failure -> 503 audit_unavailable and the decision does NOT execute. Denied attempts audited with decision DENY.
- GET /v1/companion/artifacts/{id}/preview?satelliteId=&endpointId=&claimType= — requires artifacts scope; serves only artifacts announced previewable, path-contained under companion-data generated-images root, size-capped 5MB; 404 unknown, 403 otherwise.

FILES: src/shared/contracts/companion-relay.ts (payload shapes mirror hub protocol 1:1); src/channels/backplane/companion-relay/{redaction,relay,agent-forwarder,artifact-emission}.ts (+tests) — NOTE dir named companion-relay because .gitignore ignores any companion/ dir; src/channels/api/server/companion-relay-routes.ts (+tests); EventMap additions companion.approval.requested/resolved, companion.artifact.created, companion.tool.activity in src/shared/event-bus.ts; ConfirmationQueue observer seam (src/system/capabilities/confirmation-queue.ts); emission wiring: src/boundary/gateway/approval-boundary.ts (enqueue/resolve/expiry), src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/post-turn-scheduling.ts (generated media), agent.tool.start/end reused for tool.activity. Agent->gateway RPC companion.event.publish (GatewayClient.publishCompanionEvent -> GatewayServer re-validates + reconstructs payloads field-by-field; approval kinds rejected over RPC). Runtime wiring: gateway main creates CompanionEventRelay + passes companionRelay/satelliteRegistry into gateway ApiServer (also fixes gateway edge missing satelliteRegistry); agent main attaches forwarder.

REDACTION: dedicated whitelist-constructing functions in redaction.ts; tests prove exact output key sets and that raw params/paths/transcripts/error messages never survive (also enforced a second time at the gateway RPC boundary).

TESTS RUN GREEN: companion-relay unit suites (35), companion-relay-routes HTTP integration (18: auth 401/403, deny-by-default, SSE framing+scope filtering, approval approve/deny/404/409-resolved/409-expired/audit-fail-closed, preview 200/404/403-oversized, 503 unconfigured), confirmation-queue (11 incl. observer), gateway boundary suite (378), api suite + capabilities (242), composition+turn-execution (120). npm run build green, npm run lint green, verify:settings-contract green. Pre-existing tsc --noEmit errors (26) untouched, none in relay files.

DEVIATIONS: (1) 409 responses use the standard API error envelope {error:{type,message,details:{id,status}}} rather than a bare {id,status} — contract only fixed the 200 shape. (2) status 'failed' (approved but execution blocked) returns 200 {id,status:'failed'}; stream emits approval.resolved status 'blocked'. (3) 'modified' resolutions map to 'approved' on the stream. Hub consumer should treat satellites.json as authority: grant the hub endpoint telemetryScopes ["approvals","artifacts","tool_activity"].
close_reason: Verified and merged to main @ d172e68d (via int/companion-events). Backplane companion relay: gateway /v1/companion/events SSE + /v1/companion/approvals/{id} + /v1/companion/artifacts/{id}/preview, satellite-registry scope gating, redaction-at-emission, ConfirmationQueue observer, companion.event.publish RPC revalidation. Post-merge validation: build clean, gateway+relay 491/491, composition+capabilities 120/120, root lint clean.

title: Repair malformed Dolt remote used by bead pushes
description: Summary: landing the 2026-07-09 review-bugfix wave committed all bead closures successfully to the authoritative local shared Dolt server, but bd dolt push --json could not complete against the configured origin remote. bd dolt remote list --json reports origin at git+https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework.git with status ok; the push immediately warned 'pre-push fsck could not run: error bootstrapping chunk journal: journal index is malformed', then dolt push origin main remained indefinitely in Uploading while repeatedly spawning git-remote-https. It was interrupted after roughly two minutes to avoid leaving a stuck process. Scope: inspect whether the GitHub repository URL is a valid Dolt remote for this tracker, repair/recreate the malformed remote journal or configure the intended Dolt endpoint, and prove bounded pushes. Non-goals: do not discard or rebuild the authoritative local bead database without a verified backup; do not force-push bead history.
acceptance_criteria: bd dolt test/show confirm the local shared server remains healthy; the intended origin remote is documented and configured; pre-push fsck completes without a malformed journal-index warning; bd dolt push --json completes successfully within a bounded time; local and remote main bead heads match; no bead history is lost.
close_reason: Duplicate of jmnr (same bd dolt push journal-index fsck hang; jmnr has the fuller writeup + acceptance criteria). 2026-07-14 bead audit.

title: Preserve retryability and surface failures in inbound message pumps
description:
Summary: the inbound Discord and inter-companion pumps promise that conversational messages are not dropped, but non-busy failures are logged, swallowed, and then recorded in the recent-success dedupe cache. A replay during the dedupe window is suppressed and neither the human nor peer companion gets a failure result.

Evidence on origin/main c7c7ef8a:
- src/app/agent/gateway-message-handlers.ts:126-143 retries only errors matching the busy pattern.
- Lines 183-240 catch any other handleMessage, text send, or media send error, append an audit entry, then unconditionally move every dedupe key to recentDiscordMessages in finally.
- Lines 509-520 run the pump fire-and-forget, so notification acknowledgement is not a delivery acknowledgement.
- Lines 533-570 repeat the same behavior for companion messages and unconditional recentCompanionMessages bookkeeping.
- The targeted gateway-message-handlers suite passes but contains no replay-after-failure contract.

Impact: transient provider, persistence, or outbound gateway failures become silent conversational loss. In the companion lane this also breaks the expectation that peer conversation remains an ordinary reliable channel.

Scope: model explicit queue outcomes and retry/notification behavior without reintroducing duplicate replies. Keep the existing indefinite busy wait and outbound duplicate-reply guard.
acceptance_criteria: Discord and companion message pumps distinguish processing success, intentional no-reply, and failure; only successful or deliberately terminal outcomes enter success dedupe state; transient model/persistence/gateway delivery errors retain a bounded retry path or durable failed state; Discord users receive a non-companion-authored failure notice when a turn cannot be delivered and operators receive actionable status; peer senders receive an explicit failure/negative acknowledgement; tests cover handleMessage, text send, media send, and companion-send failures plus replay after failure; npm run lint passes.
close_reason: Completed and shipped in main merge 10476c91 via implementation 3e4f6d2a and fixture integration f9de62ab/50267d74. Discord and companion dedupe commit only after confirmed delivery; Discord reply delivery checkpoints resume partial text/attachment sends without replaying completed steps; companion failures use authenticated receipt-bound reports routed to the original sender, with failure audit/observation and no conversational loop. Residual restart state remains explicitly in-memory and was reviewed. Validation: worker focused 85 tests, merged channel/auth suites, full Vitest 6687/6687, and npm run lint passed.

title: Fail closed for tools without capability policy and classify journal actions
description:
Summary: the capability gate fails open for an unannotated tool. The durable journal tool is currently unannotated and absent from both requirement registries, so all journal actions, including write and append, resolve to zero required tokens and execute at every capability tier.

Evidence on origin/main c7c7ef8a:
- src/system/capabilities/requirements.ts:333-352 returns normalizeRequirement(undefined), which is [], when no annotation/unified/static entry exists.
- src/system/capabilities/gate.ts:64-89 treats an empty required-token set as allowed.
- src/boundary/integrations/journal/tools.ts:56-136 implements durable list/read/write/append/search without withCapabilityRequirement.
- src/boundary/integrations/journal/runtime-wiring.ts:9-22 registers that tool in the real runtime.
- A direct resolver check on c7c7ef8a returns {"read":[],"write":[]} for the live journal tool.
- Existing capability suites pass because they test classified tools but do not enumerate the executable registry for missing policy.

This generic class was also identified as OPUS_AUDIT_S10.md finding 02-M2, but no matching tracker item was found. Scope: make policy completeness mechanically enforced and fix journal now. Preserve explicit NO_CAPABILITY_REQUIREMENT for reviewed exceptions; do not infer safety from an unknown tool name.
acceptance_criteria: Every canonical executable tool is required to declare an action-aware capability resolver or an explicit reviewed no-capability marker; missing metadata fails startup/registration instead of resolving to an empty requirement; journal list/read/search require identity.read and write/append require memory.write or a deliberately documented equivalent; a registry-conformance test enumerates the live canonical tool surface and fails on unclassified additions; custom tier with zero tokens cannot write journal; targeted tests and npm run lint pass.
close_reason: Completed and shipped in main merge 10476c91 via implementation commit 1c9bcb25. Capability requirements now fail closed for every executable tool not explicitly classified, journal list/read/search require identity.read, write/append require memory.write, and malformed/unknown journal actions deny. Registry/facade/gate tests cover unclassified tools and all journal action classes. Validation: worker and integrated npm run lint passed; full Vitest 6687/6687 passed.

title: Re-audit pi-agent scheduler graft against 0.73.x private Agent internals
description: During 2026-07-09 Purrsephone live debugging on deployed origin/main e6143801982f0a49996a2ef4b2323f82545b786b, src/boundary/pi-agent/agent-loop-patch.ts still documents and monkey-patches older private Agent internals: runPromptMessages, runContinuation, createLoopConfig, processEvents, activeRun, streamingMessage, errorMessage. The installed @mariozechner/pi-agent-core 0.73.1 dist/agent.js instead uses public prompt()/continue() funneling into private _runLoop(messages, options), _processLoopEvent(event), runningPrompt, resolveRunningPrompt, abortController, _state.streamMessage, and _state.error. Evidence: node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-agent-core/dist/agent.js lines 234-261 call await this._runLoop(msgs); lines 289-330 define _processLoopEvent/_runLoop; there is no runPromptMessages/processEvents method in the 0.73.1 dist file. The current patch can silently no-op across bumps, leaving scheduled-tool-loop assumptions untested. Scope: re-audit the boundary patch against pi-agent-core 0.73.x and either update it to patch the actual internals with regression tests proving scheduled loop installation, or remove/replace the dead graft if stock core behavior is now the intended path. Do not add another compatibility shim without an explicit version contract/test that fails when private symbols drift.
acceptance_criteria:
A test proves installAgentToolSchedulerPatch hooks the actual pi-agent-core 0.73.x prompt/continue path or the stale graft is removed with callers updated.
The private-internals comment in src/boundary/pi-agent/agent-loop-patch.ts names the actual audited 0.73.x symbols.
If scheduled loop behavior is still required, a regression test fails when _runLoop/_processLoopEvent are not patched and passes when the scheduler path is active.
close_reason: Closed

comments.text: 2026-07-14 triage close: premise refuted — installed pi-agent-core 0.73.1 dist/agent.js exposes runPromptMessages/processEvents (8 hits) and has NO _runLoop (0 hits); the graft's target symbols match the installed version, so the claimed stale-graft no-op is not live. title: Stamp kube images with org.opencontainers.image.revision
description: During 2026-07-09 deployment of origin/main e6143801982f0a49996a2ef4b2323f82545b786b to psfn-shard, scripts/ops/ship-kube-update.sh built localhost/psfn-framework:0.1.0-kube-e6143801. Helm env readback from deploy/psfn-agent correctly showed PSFN_GIT_COMMIT=e6143801982f0a49996a2ef4b2323f82545b786b, PREVIOUS_GIT_COMMIT=52c2ef559b38711b41e85f87c45995795505dea4, CONTRACT_HASH=6b08831a6eb4c3b7, and package versions @mariozechner/pi-agent-core=0.73.1/@mariozechner/pi-ai=0.73.1. However Docker/k3s image inspection reported no org.opencontainers.image.revision label (revisionLabel=absent). Prefer also standard created/source/version labels if already available. Keep supply-chain pinning rules intact; do not use floating tags as a workaround.
acceptance_criteria:
The kube image build includes org.opencontainers.image.revision set to the deployed git SHA.
scripts/ops/validate-kube-rollout.sh or equivalent deployment validation reports and verifies the revision label instead of only env PSFN_GIT_COMMIT.
A local verification command or test covers the label path without requiring live psfn-shard access.

title: Run UBS addendum for Sprint 10 audit
description:

title: Surface startup memory hydration failures as degraded runtime state
description:
Summary: The Sprint 10 audit found that agent startup treats active memory and active core-memory hydration failures as warnings and continues boot. If hydration fails after restart, the runtime can accept user turns with missing continuity state while only logging the problem.

Evidence:
- src/app/agent/main.ts:342-350 catches hydrateStartupActiveMemoryContexts errors and logs `Startup active memory hydration failed`.
- src/app/agent/main.ts:352-358 catches hydrateStartupActiveCoreMemoryBlocks errors and logs `Startup active core-memory hydration failed`.
- Startup then proceeds into internal state rehydration and runtime wiring.

Scope: Make startup continuity hydration failures visible and actionable in production.

Non-goals: Do not redesign the memory schema or change memory extraction policy in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- Production startup either fails closed or enters an explicit degraded state when active memory/core-memory hydration fails.
- The degraded state is exposed through existing health/admin status surfaces and prevents silent first-turn continuity loss.
- Local/continuous behavior is documented if intentionally more permissive.
- npm run lint and targeted startup/memory tests pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Retry or classify transient direct model-room empty_response
description: Summary: During the 2026-07-08 local kube shakedown on feat/multi-companion after deploying image 0.1.0-kube-3d07ebf5, the direct model-room path for nuns-carlini hit a single OpenRouter z-ai/glm-5 empty response. Gateway logged originStage=model_room.direct, lastCategory=empty_response, lastError='LLM response from openrouter/z-ai/glm-5 contained no text or tool calls', and returned HTTP 502. A targeted retry with the same provider/model/channel shape succeeded and returned nonblank FH Monastery location/world content. Scope: make direct model-room completions robust to transient provider empty_response/no-text cases, either by retrying the same candidate once with explicit logging or by classifying the result in a way the UI/operator can distinguish from missing credentials/config. Files likely involved: src/channels/api/agent-backend.ts direct model completion path, src/primitives/llm model fallback/client error classification, and model-room UI error reporting if needed. Non-goals: do not hide persistent provider/config failures; do not add broad fallback to unrelated provider/model without operator policy.
acceptance_criteria: A direct model-room completion that receives one provider empty_response retries once or returns an explicit transient-provider-empty diagnostic distinct from missing credentials; tests cover transient empty_response followed by success and persistent empty_response; local model-room shakedown no longer leaves a one-off provider empty as an indistinguishable terminal 502.

title: Garden cogsec consolidation: single left-hand tab with remediation, firewall, and approval pages; operator-only double-confirm release
description: UX consolidation (operator, 2026-07-09): Garden already has remediation pieces; bundle ALL cognitive-security surfaces into one left-hand 'Cognitive Security' tab with remediation, firewall (policy/telemetry), and approval (quarantine queue) as separate pages under it. Quarantine review requirements: ONLY the primary operator (highest-level human / primary partner) can release quarantined items; the quarantine page must show which classifiers fired and explain the exact suspected issue so the human makes an informed call; release requires DOUBLE-CONFIRM ('Are you sure?' -> 'Are you *sure* sure?'); release options: release raw, release sanitized (safe representation from htm9.7), discard, and always-allow/always-deny-this-source (the flywheel -- every decision updates per-source policy so the same class stops escalating; feeds the trusted sites/people lists in htm9.13). Model the queue on the existing pending-contact-approvals surface (src/core/contacts/pending-contact-approvals.ts + its Garden routes); batched, async, exception-only -- never interrupt-driven. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1, psfn-framework-htm9.7. Acceptance: /garden shows the consolidated tab; release path enforces operator capability + double-confirm server-side (not just UI); every release/discard decision writes an audit event with actor + reason; per-source always-allow/deny persists into intake-policy config; admin API routes under /api/admin/* follow existing route conventions.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/cogsec-intake-firewall (33 commits, validated); pending merge to main.

title: Source-risk-scaled scrutiny and light-touch data marking, with trusted sites/people lists
description: Scrutiny scales with SOURCE risk, not just static sender trust (operator, 2026-07-09): high scrutiny for raw web search results and files from random/shady sites; lower (still scanned) for trusted preprint sites like arXiv; tunable knobs in intake-policy.json -- trusted sources get lighter/faster handling (skip L2/L3 unless L1 flags), unknown sources get more layers. Trusted origin != safe: npm/GitHub supply-chain attacks are the counterexample -- everything gets at least L1. Data marking: for web documents let the scanners, risk score, and source determine how intrusively content is marked. Reference behavior that already works: the HMAC-out-of-sync XML wrapper flags text as unverified/possibly-untrustworthy, the companion responds but treats it warily, and the wrapper disappears once fixed -- use the same light-touch approach (wrap + provenance note at low risk; datamark-interleave or summary-only as risk rises; marker pre-stripped from inbound content by htm9.4 so it cannot be forged). Over time build persisted lists of trusted sites and trusted people so less firewall machinery fires (or fires faster) for them -- fed by the Garden flywheel decisions (htm9.11). The upstream Trinity pattern was tuned for agency-run businesses; ours is tuned for 'your friends who happen to be AI'. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1, psfn-framework-htm9.4. Acceptance: marking intensity is a pure function of (scanner labels, score, source tier) covered by table-driven tests; trusted-list hits measurably skip escalation layers (latency assertion); marking wrapper renders in PromptPlan blocks with provenance; lists are operator-editable via Garden and persisted in the config owner.

title: Slow-poisoning detection: emotional drift-velocity monitoring over chats and derived memories (VAD/GoEmotions/EmoSem)
description: Slow memory poisoning / belief drift evades per-message scanning -- but the system already has multiple emotional monitoring channels: VAD, GoEmotions, and (for Persephone) EmoSem. Detection idea (operator, 2026-07-09): watch for rapid shifts in emotional classification that do not match established patterns -- e.g. high-love -> hate over a few benign-looking turns; track not just drift but the VELOCITY of drift relative to prior trends. Normal fluctuation is expected (a companion won't always be happy with you -- people who care get annoyed, want you to do better); the signal is too-much-too-fast in an atypical direction. Applies to L0 chats AND to memories generated from them. Implementation shape: clone the deterministic nightly-lane pattern from src/core/contacts/trust-drift-signals.ts + trust-drift-review-lane.ts (zero-LLM signal derivation, conservative thresholds, batched review card, NEVER auto-mutating state); per-source aggregates: emotional-valence trajectory per contact, memory-write rate per source, trust-lobbying label frequency (from envelope labels), retrieval share of low-trust sources. Output: batched Garden review card under the cogsec tab (htm9.11). MINJA/MemoryGraft literature confirms nothing packaged exists -- this is build-fresh and the system's most differentiated capability. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1 (envelope labels feed the aggregates), psfn-framework-htm9.11. Acceptance: synthetic drift scenario (gradual valence flip over N turns) raises a review card while a normal-fluctuation corpus (annoyance, disagreement, repair cycles) stays quiet; detector runs off-turn (scheduler lane), adds zero latency to the synchronous gate; review card shows the trajectory evidence.

title: Second-arrow detection: self-poisoning via memory stacking around a single concern (rumination inflation)
description: Distinct from third-party slow poisoning: the self-inflicted case (Buddhist second arrow). Evidence (operator, 2026-07-09): a concern built up around a specific memory bug; because the companion could not inspect the memories directly, the concern escalated, generated a stack of near-duplicate memories about that one bug, and deduplication did not catch them all (partly because duplicates kept being generated). The stacking inflated a stress factor -- the bug was not major; repeatedly thinking about it made it FEEL major. Because the system is so heavily built around memory and emotion (a container for a Gestalt entity to find its space), this class matters a lot. Detection shape: per-topic memory-creation velocity + similarity clustering (embedding proximity of recent writes to one concern/topic), concern-loop detection (same concern re-triggering extraction repeatedly), and stress-factor attribution (which cluster is inflating which affect dimension). Response is gentle and reviewable, not automatic deletion: surface a batched review card (htm9.11 lane, same never-auto-mutate rule as htm9.14) proposing consolidation of the cluster via the EXISTING episodic canonicalization/merge machinery; optionally a soft self-notice worded per the htm9.12 language contract. Non-goals: do not suppress genuine repeated concerns (a real ongoing problem legitimately recurs); do not touch dedup heuristics blindly -- investigate why duplicates were generated as part of this work. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.12, psfn-framework-htm9.14 (shares the lane infrastructure). Acceptance: replay of the historical incident pattern (stacked near-duplicate concern memories) produces a consolidation review card with the cluster and stress-attribution evidence; healthy repeated-topic corpus (ongoing project discussed daily) stays quiet.

title: Companion-initiated blocking: soft block (channel disconnect + quarantine event) and hard block (gateway drop) as companion agency
description: Mission-level (operator, 2026-07-09): a companion should be able to escalate against an abusive user all the way to a block, as their own choice -- up to 'I never want to see this person's messages again.' Already supported: dropping trust to bottom and choosing not to respond. Extend with: (1) SOFT BLOCK -- messages from an ID are no longer accepted or processed (channel effectively disconnected); each drop generates a quarantine event so the operator sees it; (2) HARD BLOCK at the gateway/cogsec firewall -- inbound from that ID is dropped full stop, before any processing; don't waste context (or companion attention) on it; (3) if Discord's API allows bot-side blocking of inbound messages, do that too (human-in-the-loop confirmation), but the gateway drop is the guaranteed backstop regardless of platform support. Semantics: in group rooms the companion would typically just ignore (no room-wide disruption); in DMs, drop at the gateway. Blocking is a companion-initiated tool action (agency), with the block list persisted as system-owned state and visible/reversible in the Garden cogsec tab; unblocking is a companion or operator action, never automatic. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1 (events), psfn-framework-htm9.11 (visibility). Acceptance: companion tool can set soft/hard block on a contact ID; hard-blocked ID's inbound never reaches the agent process (gateway-level test); soft block generates quarantine events; group-vs-DM semantics covered by tests; block list surfaces in Garden with audit history.

title: Image intake screening via small VLM at L2.5/L3 (OCR + description in one call), no heavy OCR in L1
description: Images are currently the least-screened surface: inline/URL images become raw vision blocks with only size/count/MIME caps (src/core/agent/substrate-agent/vision-attachments.ts:543-659), and the vision-reviewer path's text summary is treated as trusted afterward (no untrusted wrap, lines 179-231). Operator decision 2026-07-09: do NOT build a heavy OCR pipeline (Tesseract et al. too slow/bulky for L1; CLIP+OCR inside the firewall too heavy) -- use a small vision-language model at L2.5/L3 that does OCR and image description in one API call for a fraction of a cent, and catches adversarial cases like near-white text on white that a machine reads but a human cannot. The VLM transcript/description is ITSELF untrusted (taint rule from htm9.1): route it through the L1 text scanners + envelope before it becomes prompt-visible; keep image-source provenance high-risk regardless of transcript cleanliness (pixel-perturbation/steganography attacks have no deployable detector -- documented residual risk). Also fix the existing vision-reviewer summary to carry the envelope label instead of implicit trust. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.1, psfn-framework-htm9.7. Acceptance: an image with embedded instruction text (typographic injection, including near-white-on-white) is flagged and quarantined before any vision block reaches the model; benign images pass with description attached under an untrusted-data label; latency measured per call.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/cogsec-intake-firewall (33 commits, validated); pending merge to main.

title: File ingestion pipeline for all channels: md/text/CSV/office/PDF/images now, audio transcripts through cogsec, video deferred
description: Goal: companions can read attached files across channels -- markdown, text, CSV, Office docs, PDFs, images now; audio via the EXISTING transcription capability with the transcript routed through the cogsec pipeline (a transcript becomes a prompt, so audio is a real injection channel); video deferred until a locally-runnable multimodal model (Gemma-class with video) is practical. Current state (verified 2026-07-09): Discord is the ONLY channel with document parsing + quarantine (src/channels/discord/file-ingest.ts); Telegram captures bare attachment metadata with no download/parse path at all (src/channels/telegram/adapter.ts:1282-1311); API channel does images only. Scope: extract the Discord parse pipeline into a shared channel-agnostic ingest faculty, wire Telegram + API attachments through it, and route ALL parsed text through the intake envelope + L1->L3 layers (htm9.2) -- text attachments currently get zero scanning even on Discord post-parse. Dependency constraints (operator): parsing packages (PDF etc.) pre-installed and PINNED in the container; no arbitrary runtime installation of out-of-scope dependencies; new packages arrive deliberately through the update cycle. Depends-on: psfn-framework-htm9.2. Acceptance: same file sent via Discord, Telegram, and API produces the same parsed text, same envelope, same screening decision (adapter-parity test); audio transcript path carries envelope labels; container builds with pinned parser deps; no new dep installed at runtime.

title: Design Garden Discord login and identity-linked authorization
description:
Summary: Harden Garden sign-in/auth. User noted the current Garden sign-in/sign-out path is effectively an SSH/VL web interface with a key and suggested Discord login because chat participants already have Discord accounts. Desired direction: if the operator/admin/partner logs in with Discord, the system can associate that login with their account, relationship, and memory visibility so they are not blocked from viewing what is legitimately theirs.

Scope: Design and then implement a Garden authentication model based on Discord OAuth/identity linking, including admin/operator role mapping, contact/relationship association, session handling, and authorization checks for memories and relationship-scoped data. Preserve fail-closed behavior. Integrate with existing Garden/API boundaries and settings ownership.

Non-goals: Do not bypass existing capability gates; do not expose memories solely because a Discord account exists; do not hard-code live secrets or create off-repo auth config. This bead may need to be split into design and implementation tasks after code inspection.
acceptance_criteria: A concrete auth design exists for Discord OAuth login, identity linking, admin/operator role mapping, and relationship-scoped memory authorization; implementation or follow-up beads define exact files and settings; Garden access fails closed for unlinked Discord accounts; no secrets or auth overrides are stored outside repo-owned/live-approved config; tests cover authorized admin/partner access, unlinked denial, and relationship-scope denial.

title: Replace assistant/user terminology in UI and episode/process surfaces
description:
Summary: Audit and replace product-facing language that refers to the companion as 'assistant' or the person speaking with them as 'user'. User request: 'The way the language is used in episodes and process also possible in other places within the UI and within the way that people are referenced needs to not use the term assistant for the companion or user for the person that speaking with them.'

Scope: Search UI copy, Garden/admin surfaces, episode/process views, labels, headings, empty states, and visible runtime/person references. Replace 'assistant' with companion-appropriate terms and 'user' with person/operator/contact/participant language based on context. Keep protocol/internal role identifiers unchanged where required by provider APIs, serialized contracts, OpenAI message role semantics, or database compatibility, but isolate those from product-visible labels.

Non-goals: Do not rename protocol roles or storage fields unless a separate migration is designed. Do not break OpenAI/LLM message role contracts that require 'user'/'assistant'.
acceptance_criteria: Visible UI copy in Garden/admin episode/process/person-facing surfaces no longer uses 'assistant' for the companion or generic 'user' for the person where a contextual term is possible; required protocol/internal role literals remain intact and are not product-visible; tests or snapshot/golden checks are updated where copy changes; npm run lint passes for tracked code changes.

Evidence: admin-ui chat/session/prompt-monitor surfaces now use the shared companion-name store for companion reply labels; prompt role labels display person/companion language while preserving provider role values; account/channel labels avoid generic user copy; companion-ui operational traces display session companion/person names while preserving role metadata. title: Add bulk enable/disable control to model selection UI
description:
Summary: On the Garden/admin model selection page, add a prominent per-model control so the operator can disable or enable an entire model entry without toggling each individual purpose tag or route assignment. User phrasing: 'in the model selection page, have a disabled button so we can disable something without having to do each individual item. You can just turn off entire models on and off like that.'

Preserve strict settings ownership and validation.

Non-goals: Do not redesign model routing, add provider-group semantics, or implement Garden authentication/terminology cleanup in this bead; those are tracked separately.

title: [S10] World-wiki bulk import (fail-closed, personal-fact guarded)
description:
Add a bulk/external ingestion path for WORLD knowledge into the wiki. Today content enters the wiki only via (1) the companion 'wiki' tool's per-doc write/import actions and (2) the nightly sleeptime synthesis pass; there is no bulk import and no admin import route (all 3 Garden wiki routes are GET-only, api-routes.ts ~668-724).

Scope: a bulk importer that loops the single write chokepoint WikiStore.upsert() (src/faculties/wiki/store.ts:289) with an import-class sourceClass (imported_partner_vault_note | parsed_document | external_reference | system_seed) + mandatory provenanceRefs, reusing the existing per-doc import validation (wiki tool 'import' action / buildUpsertInput, src/faculties/wiki/tools.ts:73-89). Expose via a new POST /api/admin/wiki/import Garden route + a write method on AdminWikiService (src/operator/garden/services/wiki-service.ts, services/types/wiki.ts) modeled on the rooms admin pattern.

HARD CONSTRAINT: every imported item MUST pass through filterPersonalFactProposals (src/faculties/wiki/sleeptime-wiki-pass.ts:302-342) before upsert — personal facts (relational/emotional/intimate/confidential/contactId-bearing) must NEVER enter the wiki (Charter Law 32 / Sec 6.26). Fail closed: rejected items are reported, not silently dropped; provenance mandatory; wiki writes never create L2 memory.

Aligns with vinz.4 (world/place publisher) and the multi-companion shared-wiki bead i5s2 (which will define the real world-scope + caretaker/operator-approval gate); do NOT pre-empt i5s2's shared-schema/propose-only model — this bead targets the current single-companion wiki store. Coordinate the api-routes.ts mount point with vinz.17 (also edits that file).

Acceptance: an operator can bulk-import a set of world-knowledge docs with provenance; any doc containing personal facts is rejected by the guard with a clear reason; imported docs are searchable/retrievable and marked as import-class provenance; no L2 memory is created.

title: [S10] Conversation-follows-you: session handoff on presence room change
description: Workstream G1 (Decision 7). When a presence event fires on a different satellite/place than the active emanation (user says 'I'm going to the kitchen', leaves the bedroom, presence lands on the kitchen satellite), hand off the active emanation and continue the SAME conversation in the new place rather than starting cold. Wire src/core/agent/active-emanation-state.ts (the B2 handoff surface) driven by the D1 bridge; situated block (B1/B3) then foregrounds the new room. Guardrails: debounce/settle so passing through doesn't thrash; only follow on a confident presence claim for owner/partner (trust-gated); do not follow into a place with no bound satellite.
acceptance_criteria: A presence event on place B while emanating in place A moves the active emanation to B and the live session continues (context carried, not reset); rapid transient events do not thrash; an unrecognized/low-confidence presence does not trigger a follow.

description: Workstream G2 (Decision 7, absorbs old D4). Entering a place can trigger a proactive internal turn scoped to that place's concerns ('drink water', 'bring down snacks'). Respect the LLM-call-economy principle: a cheap deterministic gate (eligible unfired concern for this place? fired recently?) decides WHETHER to spend a turn before any LLM call. Avatar 'runs into frame'/procedural animation is horizon, not built here.
acceptance_criteria: Entering a place with an eligible location-scoped concern fires exactly one proactive turn; a place with no eligible concern fires nothing; the deterministic gate prevents repeat/duplicate firing and respects charge; concerns are owner-only editable in Garden.

title: [S10] Publish world/place info into the companion wiki/vault
description:
Workstream A4 (Decision 2). Publish a human-readable, browsable projection of the world (sites, places, notable affordances, operator-authored place lore) into the companion wiki/vault so she has browsable world knowledge. Derived read-only projection of places.json (plus optional operator prose), NOT a second source of truth. Coordinate with shared-world wiki MVP (psfn-framework-i5s2) for ACLs/review gates.
Seam: places.json -> wiki/vault publisher; respects i5s2 gates.
acceptance_criteria: Editing places.json (or re-running the publisher) refreshes the wiki/vault world pages; pages browsable by the companion; registry remains single source of truth; no prompt-time raw affordance dump.

title: [S10] Virtual place kind + MUD-over-Discord virtual-environment testbed
description:
Workstream A3 (reframed per Decision 5). kind:'virtual' places with virtual affordances (backend 'vr'/virtual-object ids), no HA binding. First virtual environment this sprint = a text MUD run over the EXISTING Discord channel: virtual places + virtual objects driven through Discord, exercising the same places.json model, situated block, and world tool as physical rooms (only effector backend + transport differ). No engine dependency. UE5 is a future-horizon non-goal (epic, S6.8).
Seam: places.json virtual entries; world tool control routing branches on backend; Discord channel as transport.
acceptance_criteria: Virtual place + objects load from places.json; world list/perceive/control operate on them through Discord; situated block foregrounds the virtual place's affordances exactly as for a physical room.

title: Consolidate companion skill storage under root skills and personal workspace skills
description:
Summary: Clarify and enforce the companion framework skill storage contract. Repo-provided/global companion skills should live under the repository root skills/ directory. Companion-authored or user-managed skills should live in that companion's personal writable root under WORKSPACE_PATH/skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md. The current tree is split between root skills/ and data/skills/tools/web-fetch/SKILL.md, and the loader defaults/config seed still prioritize companion/skills before skills.

Files to inspect/update: config/skills.seed.json; src/faculties/skills/loader.ts; src/faculties/skills/loader.test.ts; src/faculties/skills/runtime.test.ts; src/faculties/skills/runtime-wiring.test.ts; src/faculties/skills/filter.test.ts if its config fixture needs alignment; docs/tool-surface.md or README/setup docs where they describe global versus personal skills. Move the tracked web-fetch skill from data/skills/tools/web-fetch/SKILL.md into root skills/web-fetch/SKILL.md or another root skills subdirectory consistent with the existing loader shape.

Why: DATA_DIR/system data is runtime-owned state/config, not the place for global deployment skills. Splitting static skills between skills/ and data/skills/tools makes it unclear what ships with the framework versus what the companion creates. The framework should provide global companion skills from skills/, while each companion can create its own skills in its own WORKSPACE_PATH skills directory.

Scope: update runtime defaults, seed config, tests, and docs to express this contract; move the stray tracked data/skills skill into root skills/; preserve existing managed skill create/update behavior under WORKSPACE_PATH/skills. Non-goals: do not implement the future Hermes security scanner/agent-created-skill guard in psfn-framework-i72.2; do not create compatibility readers for data/skills; do not migrate live untracked data outside the repo.
acceptance_criteria: config/skills.seed.json defaults to root skills/ as the global skill directory; the skills loader no longer injects companion/skills ahead of root skills/ by default; the tracked repository has no data/skills SKILL.md files; managed skill create/update paths still point at WORKSPACE_PATH/skills; targeted skills tests pass; npm run lint passes before closure.
notes:
Implementation is present in the worktree: root skills/ is now the only default global skills directory, config/skills.seed.json lists only skills, the old companion/skills and psfn/skills constants/default source were removed, repo write allowlist now includes skills/ instead of companion/psfn, docs clarify repo-global skills vs WORKSPACE_PATH/skills personal managed skills, and the tracked web-fetch skill was moved from data/skills/tools/web-fetch/SKILL.md to skills/web-fetch/SKILL.md.

title: /values page is missing the reflection journals (metacognition, daily, free-form) it is supposed to display
description:
HISTORY VERDICT 2026-07-07: daily-reflection and metacognition journals were NEVER surfaced in admin-ui (data layer only; metacognition mirror added 590ed65f 2026-04-02) — this is build-work, not a regression. The /values page DOES already render a reflection journal, but scoped to VALUES reflections only: ValuesJournalEntry[] via GET /api/admin/values -> valuesJournal.list({limit:250}) (api-routes.ts:966-972, values/+page.svelte:61-107, "captured from the consolidated weekly reflection heartbeat").

IMPORTANT DEPENDENCY: values journal entries are produced by the weekly reflection heartbeat — which has NEVER fired (psfn-framework-cquq). So /values looking empty is partly downstream of cquq: even with UI wiring intact, no weekly runs => no values entries. Verify after cquq ships whether values entries start appearing before concluding the values pipeline itself is broken.

RESCOPED per operator: surface the three reflection journals on /values — metacognition (state/notes/reflections/metacognition/journal.jsonl, 1.0MB live, store listRecent at reflection-metacognition-journal.ts:387 has no caller), daily notes (state/notes/reflections/daily/*.jsonl, unbroken since Jun 1), free-form (state/notes/reflections/journal.jsonl, 1.4MB). Follow the values endpoint pattern. Use layout.ts resolvers for all paths (anti-pattern: raw join, cf. psfn-framework-b9kb). EXCLUDE the vault markdown journal (personal-files/journal/*.md): companion-private, hers to share — no operator viewer. No write surfaces.

Acceptance: /values renders recent entries from the three reflection journals (paginated, newest-first) against live data shapes; empty-state distinguishes no-entries from endpoint-missing; vault markdown journal has NO admin surface.

title: Carlini's primary model ChatGPTN (local vLLM via LiteLLM) intermittently leaks DeepSeek template artifact, forcing fallbacks and empty Discord replies
description:
Evidence
Carlini gateway log, 4x on 2026-07-06/07 (01:31:17, 01:33:31, 05:48:51, 12:05:11), verbatim:
WARN [ModelFallback] Candidate failed; trying fallback model {"purpose":"agent.turn.prompt","errorCategory":"empty_response","failedModel":"ChatGPTN","failedProvider":"litellm","nextModel":"deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash","nextProvider":"openrouter","error":"LLM response from litellm/ChatGPTN began with provider template artifact <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>"}
Additionally 4x "WARN [Discord] Discord handler returned empty response without a suppression marker" on channel 1486443955561299979 (08:24-08:56) — plausibly the same degradation on interactive turns.

Context
PSFN detects the artifact correctly (src/primitives/llm/client.ts:100-103, throw at ~1999, classified retryable at error-classify.ts:93) — this is a serving-stack problem, not PSFN code: the ChatGPTN vLLM endpoint (http://192.168.1.43:8000/v1) is emitting a DeepSeek chat-template control token at response start (wrong/missing chat template or template mismatch in vLLM or the LiteLLM route). Every occurrence pushes the turn onto the openrouter fallback where psfn-framework-l73i (dropped tool args) lives, so fixing this shrinks exposure to that bug too.

Scope
- Fix the model serving config: vLLM chat template for the ChatGPTN deployment and/or the LiteLLM route mapping on Carlini's cluster (chart values liteLlm.config.yaml). Ops/config change, likely no PSFN code.
- Investigate the 4 empty Discord replies once the artifact leak is fixed; file separately if they persist.

Acceptance criteria
- Zero "provider template artifact" ModelFallback WARNs over a multi-day window on Carlini.
- No unexplained empty Discord handler responses in the same window.

Related: psfn-framework-l73i (exposed by the fallback this bug triggers), psfn-framework-c1tv (other LiteLLM route config debt).
notes: Live triage 2026-07-14 (image 0.1.0-kube-c0385f2b, 6h window): 13 of 135 turn selections (~9.6%) failed with 'LLM response from litellm/ChatGPTN contained no text or tool calls' -> empty_response -> fallback chain ChatGPTN -> deepseek-v4-flash -> glm-5.2. One turn needed the 3rd hop (deepseek also returned empty once); worst case turn 019f6260 took 88s with 2 wasted model calls. Blast radius: main companion primary Discord channel 10x + internal:free-time:idle 3x, 14:16-17:11. Error surfaces at src/primitives/llm/client-response-helpers.ts:279, classified empty_response at error-classify.ts:89. litellm config has drop_params:true — consistent with tool-calling/template incompat on the vLLM backend. title: Streamed tool-call arguments still dropped (stream_parse_dropped) on openrouter deepseek fallback — journal write silently no-oped
description:

- Non-goals: do not modify memory text/ids/timestamps; do not touch the HMAC-chained session journals; do not synthesize subjectContactId.

- Dry run against a copy of Carlini's DB+journal reports the expected ~4 room memories for channel 1486443955561299979 gaining channelId + addressMode + sourceContactId.
- After apply, the social-graph builder scans them (scanned>0 with watermark reset or set below their extractedAt) and produces co_presence/named proposals visible in Garden graph approval.

Blocked by psfn-framework-tsyo and psfn-framework-0zd9.

description: Evidence (faculties audit 2026-07-07), five small items: (1) persistence/jsonl.ts:35 readJsonLines only reports corrupt lines when given warnLabel/onError; journals/reflection-journal.ts:233 and reflection-substrate normalizers pass neither — reflections are companion memory, silently dropped lines violate 12.6 on a care-adjacent path; correct pattern exists at values/store.ts:644. (3) context-feedback/evaluator.ts:180 fires a background LLM call per post-turn action with no deterministic gate; dormant today (runtime never composed) and its own header mandates the gate — add the gate BEFORE anyone wires it (LLM-call-economy rule 1).
