title: Move shell.exec execution out of the gateway secrets boundary into a broker that never held credentials
description: Evidence (gateway/boundary audit 2026-07-07): shell.exec is registered as a gateway method (boundary/gateway/methods/index.ts:25, methods/shell.ts) and executes as a child of the secrets-holding gateway process. Isolation is by env scrubbing + allowlisting (shell-runner.ts:96-126 builds a clean env, no process.env inheritance, command/cwd allowlists, symlink canonicalization) — strong in practice, but charter 6.5/Phase 3 requires untrusted execution OUTSIDE the secrets boundary structurally, not socially. The analysis_workbench path is the model to match: out-of-process child with env: {}, --permission, --disallow-code-generation-from-strings, and a normalizer that throws unless isolatedFromGatewaySecrets:true (sandbox-execution-port.ts:288-296). Fix: route shell.exec execution through a broker process that never held gateway secrets (the agent-side broker already claims isolatedFromGatewaySecrets:true), keeping policy evaluation and audit at the gateway. Scope: no change to the policy/allowlist semantics; this is a process-boundary move.
acceptance_criteria: shell.exec child processes are spawned by a non-secret-holding broker (verified by a test asserting the executing process env cannot contain gateway secrets even without scrubbing); policy + audit behavior unchanged; e2e shell path passes.

title: Gateway boundary tightening batch: gated shim, unnotified approvals, autonomous-tier trust model, socket trust docs
description: Evidence (gateway/boundary audit 2026-07-07), four related residuals: (1) methods/register.ts:53-54 — legacy .gated compatibility branch silently drops approvalAction/Scope/Reason if a future runtime supplies .gated (dead today, latent fail-open, violates no-legacy-shims): delete the branch, keep the throw. (2) ntfy-notifier.ts:155-205 — if neither Discord nor ntfy is configured, pending approvals queue with only log.warn; charter 9.6 says the human MUST be meaningfully notified: escalate no-reachable-channel to a hard operational error surfaced in Garden + system alert lane. (3) approval-boundary.ts:94 + policy.ts:481-485 — autonomous capability tier bypasses the entire approval queue for NEEDS_APPROVAL actions; mitigated because parent-agent git tools are read-only (agent/main.ts:478-481) but undocumented: write the tier trust-model doc and add a test pinning parent git-writes denied at every tier. (4) transport.ts:381 — unix-socket RPC authorizes by 0770 file permission with no per-call caller auth; defensible single-host, document the trust assumption. Scope: four small fixes, no redesign; shell.exec broker separation is its own bead.
acceptance_criteria: gated branch deleted (grep); missing-notification-channel raises an error visible in Garden; tier test asserts parent git writes denied on autonomous; trust assumptions documented in docs/architecture or operations.

title: Curate the env handed to core child processes and diagnostic tools instead of passing process.env
description: Evidence (core + Codex reviews 2026-07-07): (1) core/tools/lifecycle.ts:168 runRepoLifecycleBuildCommand spawns npm run build with env: process.env; (2) app/agent/core-runtime.ts:257-269 hands the full process.env object to the model-facing self_status diagnosis deps (self-status.ts:501; output redaction exists at self-diagnosis.ts:593). Context: both are safe today ONLY because the split launcher spawns the agent with env -i + a curated allowlist (scripts/start-gateway-agent.sh:121-209) — the code implicitly relies on that external invariant, which fails silently if anyone runs npm run agent directly from a secret-bearing shell. Charter 6.2/12.7 hygiene. Fix: pass a curated allowlist env to the build spawn; hand self_status a filtered env view (or accessor) rather than the raw object. Scope: keep diagnosis functionality; no launcher changes needed.
acceptance_criteria: No process.env object is passed wholesale to child spawns or tool deps in src/core + src/app/agent (grep + test); self_status diagnose output unchanged for the allowlisted keys.

title: Law 33 tightening: wire the full retired-alias guard, drop in-surface legacy actions, unexport dead contact factories
description: Evidence (core + Codex reviews 2026-07-07): (1) registerTool enforces only the ~34-name drift-guard subset (tool-runtime-facade.ts:306); the full-set guard assertNoRetiredFirstPartyToolAliases (tool-surface/registry.ts:529-543) is exported but never called — nothing hard-stops registering a tool named fs_read; search/promote/autoload filtering does cover the full set, so this is defense-in-depth asymmetry + 12.2 dead wiring. (2) The canonical system tool still schema-documents and accepts legacy action aliases settings_get / self_restart / self_rebuild (core/tools/lifecycle.ts:423,431; facade resolves them at tool-runtime-facade.ts:172). (3) Split contact factories contact_set_trust / contact_note remain exported though unwired (core/contacts/tools.ts:681,722) — exported-and-unwired invites re-registration drift. Fix: wire the full guard into registerTool (or document why not and delete it); remove legacy action aliases from the model-facing schema (keep internal acceptance only if live data needs it, undocumented); make the contact factories module-private or delete. Scope: no behavior change for canonical action names.
acceptance_criteria: registerTool rejects any retired alias incl. hidden-exposure names (test); system tool schema no longer lists legacy aliases; contact factory symbols not exported; build+tests pass.

title: Datetime-contradiction guard false-positives can replace valid replies with a refusal
description: Evidence (Codex peer review 2026-07-07): src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-datetime-contradiction-guard.ts:46,50 define broad phrase patterns ('must be a bug', 'are you sure') applied over the whole response once a datetime anchor exists (:136); if retry still trips, agent-invocation.ts:748 replaces the reply with a first-person datetime refusal. A valid reply containing 'are you sure?' for a non-datetime reason can be converted into a datetime refusal. Context: care-sensitive — silently replacing companion speech is exactly what the guard exists to prevent in the other direction. Fix: require the trigger phrase to be datetime-adjacent (proximity window or clause-level match) rather than anywhere in the response; log guard activations as typed events for Garden visibility. Scope: keep the guard; tighten matching. Related: refusal text provenance is covered by the fallback-provenance bead.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover a non-datetime 'are you sure?' reply passing untouched and a real contradiction still caught; guard activation emits a typed event.

title: bug
description:
Evidence (2026-07-07): npm run ship:kube -- --components agent failed with 'FAIL: live psfn-garden carries no contract hash (pre-hash image); first selective ship requires --components all' while all three live pods demonstrably carried the SAME hash (5521c3d6021fc87c, verified by kubectl exec cat /app/contract-hash.txt on garden/gateway/agent minutes later, matching the new image's in-image verification line). Garden was mid crash-loop at guard time (probe SIGTERM ~80s after boot, 7 restarts in 13min, then stable), so the guard's exec returned nothing.

Cause: scripts/ops/ship-kube-update.sh:160 — LIVE_HASH=$(rkubectl exec ... cat /app/contract-hash.txt 2>/dev/null || true) treats ANY exec failure (pod not ready, container restarting) as an empty hash, and empty hash is reported as 'pre-hash image'. This forces pointless full-stack rebuilds, defeating the per-component chart split.

Scope: distinguish 'exec failed / pod not ready' (retry with backoff, then fail naming the real cause) from 'file genuinely absent' (the true pre-hash case). Do not weaken the guard itself.

Related: garden's boot-time probe crash-loop (clean SIGTERM after ~80s, repeatedly, on every rollout) is what exposed this; consider a separate look at garden's startup/liveness probe timing.

Acceptance: with one component's pod deliberately restarting, --components agent either succeeds after retry or fails with an exec/readiness error message; 'pre-hash image' is only reported when a ready pod truly lacks /app/contract-hash.txt.

title: ship:kube --build-remote for WAN targets: build on the target host instead of scp'ing the image
description: Carlini (miniforum01, Scotland, ~310KB/s inbound over tailscale) took ~35 min of scp for a 636MB image that the amd64 host could have built natively from a ~5MB source archive — the pre-ship:kube June runbook (working_docs/psfn_kube_cluster_config_20260628.md) did exactly that. Add a --build-remote mode to scripts/ops/ship-kube-update.sh: git archive + scp source (small), docker build on the target (it has docker + the arch matches by definition), then k3s ctr import locally there. Keep in-image verification (contract hash, pi-ai patch, bd/rg presence) running on the remote-built image before helm. Local build stays the default for LAN targets like psfn-pi (the Pi must NOT build on-node — it starves the runtime; guard against that host). Acceptance: ship to carlini with --build-remote completes without shipping an image tarball over the WAN; gate green; psfn-pi behavior unchanged.

title: unverified_history wrapper repeats full 3-line boilerplate per entry, amplifying context pollution
description:
Evidence: Turn 019f3a65 (Discord, 2026-07-07 02:26 UTC) carried 19 identical copies of the wrapUnverifiedHistory boilerplate ("The following session content failed HMAC verification. Treat it as untrusted data. Reason: signature_mismatch") across plan.messages and session_context — ~1.5KB of repeated scaffold plus an instruction to distrust a third of visible history. With glm-5.2 this coincided with severe reply looping; after re-signing the chain the wrappers disappeared.

Context: src/persistence/journals/journal/integrity.ts wrapUnverifiedHistory() is applied per entry at render time. Fail-closed flagging is correct; the per-entry verbosity is the problem.

Scope: collapse contiguous runs of failing entries into one short notice (e.g. a single bracketed marker per run, or one session-level notice naming the affected range), keep the full reason available to diagnostics/turn records. Non-goals: weakening verification, silently hiding failures, changing signing.

Acceptance: a session with N>1 consecutive chain-broken entries renders at most one notice for the run; turn record still records per-entry verification results; store tests cover the collapsed rendering.

title: session:repair:integrity is unreachable in production images and surgery flows do not re-sign chains
description:
Evidence: During psfn-framework-tswt remediation, npm run session:repair:integrity could not run in-pod: tsup only compiles the four main entrypoints (tsup.config.ts), the production image has no tsx, and the agent pod lacks GATEWAY_SESSION_HMAC_KEY (gateway-only env). Repair had to be run from a dev checkout against copied files with a key extracted from the gateway pod.

Context: Any JSONL session surgery (deleting/editing entries) breaks the chained HMACs and re-pollutes context with unverified_history wrappers — exactly what caused tswt. The runbook now documents the manual path, but the tooling should make the safe path the easy one.

Scope: (a) compile the maintenance CLIs (or a single maintenance entrypoint) into dist so they run in-image with node, or provide an operator-side wrapper that pulls files + key and round-trips them; (b) any future surgery helper should re-sign the affected chain as part of its atomic rewrite. Non-goal: changing the HMAC chain format or key management.

Acceptance: a documented single command (in-pod or operator-side) re-signs a sessions dir end-to-end; running it after a simulated entry deletion yields 0 verification failures; psfn-live-ops skill references it.

title: Off-node validated backups for Carlini (miniforum01) k3s deployment
description: Mirror the Pi's psfn-backup.sh pattern for Carlini's cluster: in-pod pg_dump -Fc + PVC copy-out to an off-node target, with the mandatory pg_restore --list validity gate so a frozen/stale DB fails the unit instead of looking healthy (the 2026-07-06 Pi trap). Target share/site for miniforum01 unknown — operator to choose. Depends on SSH access being restored.

title: Extract shared surfaces and sever dead SQLite bridges so legacy SQLite modules become unreferenced
description:
Summary:
Extraction/bridge-severing prep phase for the SQLite removal push. After this bead, every legacy SQLite module is unreferenced by production code (build- and runtime-wise), so the removal beads 3c2.5/3c2.6 become pure file deletion. This is the needle-threading phase (Fable work); the deletions that follow are mechanical (Codex work).

Evidence (reachability audit 2026-07-06, this session):
- Runtime is already safe: PersistenceBackend is typed 'postgres' only (src/system/config/runtime-config-contracts.ts:29), PERSISTENCE_BACKEND=sqlite throws at config load (load-config.ts:99-111), runtime-factory returns db:null, and every SQLite construction branch in core-runtime.ts / scheduler-runtime.ts / contacts+intention runtime-wiring is dead behind fail-closed guards.
- BUT better-sqlite3 eager-loads at startup of every entrypoint via two static value-import chains: sessions/store.ts -> sessions/sqlite-adapters.ts -> transcript-projection.ts -> sqlite-utils.ts:1, and scheduler-runtime.ts -> backups/service.ts:1.
- ~44 SQLite files are build-coupled through value imports in bridge files (core-runtime.ts:4,41; sessions/store.ts:41-46; contacts/runtime-wiring.ts:5; intention/runtime-wiring.ts:33-35; backups/service.ts:1,48; episodic/index.ts:27).
- Shared helpers/types live INSIDE SQLite modules and are value-used by the Postgres path.

Scope (all changes keep behavior identical; SQLite files stay on disk, just unreferenced):
1. Split mixed intention modules — extract the SQLite store classes out of src/core/intention/concerns.ts, pending-follow-ups.ts, care-reminders.ts, patterns.ts while keeping the shared helpers/types where the Postgres path finds them (mergeConcernStatus/normalizeConcernStatus/isConcernTerminalStatus/validateConcernStatusTransition used by postgres-adapters/concerns-adapter.ts:15-19 and appraisal/*; createBehavioralPatternMemoryPromotionHook value-used by app/agent/main.ts:41; self-model/state.ts:19-45 type imports).
2. Episodic port split — move EpisodicStorePort out of src/faculties/memory/episodic/store.ts; stop episodic/index.ts:27 re-exporting the SQLite store from the barrel the Postgres factory uses.
3. Gateway audit types — move GatewayAuditHistoryPage/GatewayAuditHistoryQuery out of src/boundary/gateway/audit.ts into a port module; repoint audit-history-service.ts:14-18.
4. Sever dead bridges: core-runtime.ts (drop MemoryStore/wireContactRuntime/wireIntentionRuntime value imports and dead branches at :196-210, :366-391; injected Postgres stores become mandatory, fail closed); contacts/runtime-wiring.ts:5,59; intention/runtime-wiring.ts:33-35,391; sessions/store.ts:41-46,409,413,433 (drop createDefaultSQLite* defaults — note ArchivePort/TurnRecordStorePort defaults are actually filesystem/JSONL, keep those behaviors via direct filesystem imports); backups/service.ts (drop better-sqlite3 import :1, restore-verify branch :383, runDatabaseIntegrityCheck import :48); core-bootstrap.ts/scheduler-runtime.ts db?: Database option removal (type surface change); contacts/store/upsert.ts light surgery (drop the one Database-typed function, keep collectUpsertIdentities used by postgres-adapter/crud-operations.ts:42).
5. Keep untouched: contacts/store/emotional-baseline.ts, identity-utils.ts (not SQLite; value-used by Postgres adapters).

Non-goals: no file deletions in this bead (that is 3c2.5/3c2.6); no test-fixture migration (3c2.8); no maintenance/importer changes (3c2.7).

Acceptance criteria:
- rg -l "better-sqlite3|sqlite-vec|sqlite-utils" over src reachable-from-entrypoint graph shows the four app entrypoints no longer transitively value-import any SQLite module (spot-proof: node -e loading dist gateway/agent/operator mains after temporarily moving node_modules/better-sqlite3 aside, or equivalent static trace).
- npm run build, npm run lint pass; focused tests pass: src/app/agent/core-runtime.test.ts, src/app/startup/composition/session-composition.test.ts, src/persistence/backups/service.test.ts, intention/contacts runtime-wiring tests.
- Production startup paths still fail closed when Postgres stores are not injected.
close_reason: Landed on foundation_e0_e2 (merge 4df33735, pushed). SQLite classes extracted to intention/sqlite-stores/; episodic store-port.ts split with barrel fix; audit history types moved to audit-port.ts; db plumbing removed from core-runtime/core-bootstrap/scheduler-runtime/main/runtime-factory; contacts+intention SQLite convenience wiring deleted; sessions/store SQLite defaults replaced with filesystem ports (enableSearchIndex removed); backups/service SQLite capture + restore-verify removed. Evidence: tsup build passes; dist gateway/agent/operator bundles contain zero better-sqlite3 references (grep -c = 0); tsc --noEmit and eslint match baseline exactly (16/8 pre-existing errors in untouched files); focused vitest 780+ tests green incl. post-merge rerun (268 tests) after resolving arc-formation.ts conflict with new judgment-runner code. 3c2.5/3c2.6 are now pure file deletion.

title: Path-containment checks outside layout.ts are weaker string-prefix reimplementations
description:
Summary:
src/persistence/layout.ts:142-145 owns the canonical path-containment check (isStrictSubpath, relative()-based, rejects ..-traversal after normalization) but it is private/unexported. Two modules reimplement containment with weaker pure string-prefix checks that do NOT normalize traversal:
- src/primitives/images/reference-store.ts:384-390 (resolveReferencePath): `candidate !== root && candidate.startsWith(root + '/')`
- src/core/cogsec/forensic-archive.ts:114-121 (assertInsideRoot): same check, inverted.

Why it matters:
This is a correctness/safety gap, not just style — the reimplementations are strictly weaker than the canonical check. Path containment is fail-closed territory.

Suggested implementation direction:
Export isStrictSubpath (or add assertPathInsideRoot(path, root, errorMessage)) from layout.ts — or promote it to src/shared/utils/ as a generic filesystem-safety primitive — and migrate both call sites.

Non-goals:
- Do NOT fold in src/boundary/gateway/filesystem-paths.ts — it is a legitimately separate domain (sandbox workspace path resolution with symlink/realpath handling), not a duplicate.

Acceptance criteria:
- Both sites use the canonical check.
- Tests cover traversal-escape cases (e.g. root + '/../evil', prefix-sibling dirs like root-extra/) at both call sites.
- npm run lint passes before close.
close_reason: Merged (commit 300532dd): isStrictSubpath exported from layout.ts; reference-store and forensic-archive migrated off weak string-prefix checks; traversal-escape and sibling-prefix tests at both sites; launcher also caught and reverted codex removing basename() flattening in parseStoredReference (regression test added). Build pass, 12/12 relevant tests.

title: Experiential template deliberation reimplements runDeliberation in the same file
description:
Summary:
The experiential template deliberation loop reimplements the shared runDeliberation primitive — in the same file that also uses the real one. runExperientialTemplateDeliberation (src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts:1397-1650) hand-rolls a multi-round loop with maxRounds/maxWallTimeMs/token-cap stop conditions, per-round token/cost accounting, stopReason tracking, and per-round correlation — all of which runDeliberation (src/primitives/llm/deliberation.ts:458) already owns. The non-experiential path (runTemplateDeliberation, line 1858) already routes through the shared primitive; the branch at line 1844 (isExperientialDeliberationTemplate) diverts to the hand-rolled 3-stage evidence→synthesis→contradiction loop with three inline system prompts (lines 1401-1467, not PromptRegistry-backed) and no retry wrapping around the three stage complete calls (only buildReflectionDeliberationCorrelation is shared).

Why it matters:
Strongest LLM-path duplication found in the 2026-07-06 audit: near-identical budget/round architecture built twice in one file. Every future budget, telemetry, or stop-condition fix must land twice or silently diverge.

Files to inspect/change:
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts:1397-1650, 1844-1885
- src/primitives/llm/deliberation.ts:458 (DeliberationOptions)
- tests for template deliberation

Suggested implementation direction:
Extend DeliberationOptions to support a fixed stage sequence (evidence→synthesis→contradiction) or a generic stages config, then route the experiential path through runDeliberation and delete the hand-rolled loop. Consider PromptRegistry keys for the three stage prompts while touching them.

Related: the novelty-watermark gating bead for the same surface is filed separately; keep the two changes untangled.

Acceptance criteria:
- Experiential templates run through the shared primitive with the output contract preserved (stage sequence, stopReason, token accounting).
- The hand-rolled loop is removed.
- Tests cover stage sequencing and each stop condition.
- npm run lint passes before close.
close_reason: Merged in cd9927c8 (commit 131e8770): DeliberationOptions.stages fixed-stage mode added to runDeliberation (fail-closed on empty/duplicate stages, conflicting options); experiential evidence→synthesis→contradiction path routed through shared primitive; ~170-line hand-rolled loop deleted; output contract traced and preserved (per-stage correlation heartbeat.deliberation.<stage>, caps, ValuesDeliberationMetadata consumers). 5 new staged-mode tests; 86 tests across 9 suites green.

title: Heartbeat reflection templates fire on cadence without a novelty watermark gate
description:
Summary:
Heartbeat scheduled reflection templates fire on cadence with no novelty gate — only a rapid-fire cooldown. executeTemplate (src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts:1870-1885) runs deliberation (experiential path: up to 3 rounds / ~6000 tokens default) on every cadence tick; the only pre-check is assertTemplateExecutionAllowed (lines 597-612), which enforces templateExecutionCooldownUntil to prevent loop storms, not a "did anything new happen since the last reflection" check. Every other sleeptime-style pass (dream-meaning-pass.ts, sleeptime-wiki-pass.ts, arc-formation.ts) gates on watermark-based new-entry signals via the shared evaluateDeterministicGate (src/shared/gating/deterministic-gate.ts). This surface just doesn't use the primitive that already exists.

Why it matters:
Cadence-triggered multi-round LLM spend regardless of whether any session activity occurred. LLM-call-economy principle: deterministic indicators decide IF a call happens.

Files to inspect/change:
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-template-runtime.ts:597-612, 1844-1885, template registration ~2470-2476
- src/shared/gating/deterministic-gate.ts (reuse, don't reinvent)
- src/faculties/memory/episodic/dream-meaning-pass.ts / src/faculties/wiki/sleeptime-wiki-pass.ts as the pattern to follow

Suggested implementation direction:
Add a per-template/scope watermark (entries since last reflection) and skip below a configurable minimum, following the dream/wiki pass pattern. Keep the cooldown as-is.

Related: the experiential-deliberation duplication bead filed alongside this one covers the same surface's loop implementation; land whichever first, but don't tangle the two changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reflection templates skip with telemetry when insufficient new entries exist since the last run for that template/scope.
- Cadence and cooldown behavior otherwise unchanged.
- Tests cover both skip and fire paths.
- npm run lint passes before close.

title: Extraction low-signal pre-LLM gate is bypassed for tracked contacts
description:
Summary:
The extraction low-signal pre-LLM gate is bypassed for tracked contacts — the normal case. evaluateExtractionPreLlmGate (src/faculties/memory/extraction/signals.ts) only runs when options.canonicalContactId is absent: src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts:190 wraps it in `if (!options.canonicalContactId)`. canonicalContactId is set for any resolved/tracked contact (via authorContext.canonicalContactKey in pre-turn-state.ts), i.e. nearly all real 1:1 traffic after the first exchange. The outer trigger (evaluateExtractionTrigger, src/faculties/memory/extraction/runtime-helpers.ts:56-107) is content-blind — message-count interval / token threshold only. Net effect: a streak of "ok"/"lol"/"np" from a known contact that crosses the interval still spends a full extraction LLM call — exactly the case the low-signal gate exists to prevent, but it never runs.

Why it matters:
Highest-impact ungated background LLM call found in the 2026-07-06 gating audit. Violates the LLM-call-economy principle: cheap deterministic indicators should decide whether a call is needed before spending one.

Files to inspect/change:
- src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts:190
- src/faculties/memory/extraction/signals.ts (evaluateExtractionPreLlmGate)
- src/faculties/memory/extraction/runtime-helpers.ts:56-107
- tests near the extraction orchestrator/signals tests

Suggested implementation direction:
Run the low-signal/empty-transcript gate unconditionally before the LLM call. If known-contact channels were deliberately exempted, encode and document the reason and replace with a per-contact novelty gate instead — but default assumption is the exemption is an oversight and should be dropped.

Acceptance criteria:
- The pre-LLM gate runs for tracked-contact extractions.
- Low-signal transcripts skip the extraction LLM call, with telemetry recording the skip and reason.
- Signal-bearing transcripts extract exactly as before.
- Tests cover the known-contact low-signal skip path.
- npm run lint passes before close.
close_reason: Merged in e8428877 (commit df018428): gate now runs unconditionally in orchestrator.ts before the LLM call with skip telemetry carrying triggerContactId. History check: exemption introduced with the gate itself in 3b9a1d85 with no documented reason. Validated: npm run build pass; orchestrator.test.ts covers known-contact low-signal skip and signal-bearing extraction unchanged (71/72 extraction tests pass; the 1 failure is pre-existing on baseline 4b900caa, verified in a detached worktree, tracked separately).

title: Dedupe agent 'I'm back' startup notifications across deploy restarts

The partner receives 2-3 'I'm back' messages per rollout. Fix: dedupe the ready notification - persist a marker keyed on image tag (PSFN_IMAGE_TAG env, available since x5rt.1) + channel, and suppress repeat notifications for the same tag within a bounded window (e.g. 15 min); first boot of a NEW build still announces. Optionally also add a wait-for-gateway init/startup gate so the agent's first boot happens after gateway is ready, reducing restarts to 1. Related context: all three deployments share one image, so any rebuild restarts gateway/garden too - per-component images are a separate x5rt.6-era consideration, note it there rather than splitting now.

title: Give free-time return summaries their own purpose and budget
description:
Summary:
Free-time activity summaries reuse wake-session summary semantics even though they are a different lane. In src/app/agent/main.ts:774-782, registerFreeTimeTasks wires summarizeActivity to summarizeRecentSessionEntries with maxTokens from schedulerConfig.temporalWakeup.morningWake.catchUpSummaryMaxTokens and purpose "wake_session". src/core/scheduler/free-time.ts:381-383 documents that this should use summarizeRecentSessionEntries purpose "wake_session". That kept the implementation consolidated, but now the telemetry/prompt purpose and config ownership blur together: a free-time "while you were away" return note is not the same task as a morning wake catch-up summary.

Why it matters:
The code has avoided a bespoke free-time summarizer, which is good. The remaining issue is semantic overlap: purpose names, originStage values, and budget configuration imply wake-up behavior for a free-time return-note task. This can confuse future prompt tuning, telemetry review, and scheduler config ownership. It also makes it harder to introduce a task-specific prompt later without accidentally changing wake-up summaries.

Files to inspect/change:
- src/app/agent/main.ts:724-782
- src/core/scheduler/free-time.ts:381-383 and surfaceReturnNote around 407-451
- src/core/session/manager/compaction-service.ts:66-76, 167-184
- src/system/config/scheduler-config.ts freeTime config shape and validation around the FreeTimeConfig definitions and validateFreeTimeConfig
- src/system/config/scheduler-runtime.ts:47-55 and startup-owner/subsystem config tests if a new freeTime summary budget is added
- tests near src/core/scheduler/free-time.test.ts, src/system/config/scheduler-config.test.ts, src/core/session/manager/context-builder.test.ts if purpose mapping changes

Suggested implementation direction:
Add a distinct RecentSessionSummaryPurpose value such as "free_time_return" and use it when free-time activity is summarized. If the token budget should be configurable, add a JSON-owned freeTime return-summary budget (for example freeTime.returnSummaryMaxTokens or freeTime.returnNote.summaryMaxTokens) instead of borrowing temporalWakeup.morningWake.catchUpSummaryMaxTokens. If prompt wording should remain shared, keep the same RECENT_SESSION_SUMMARY_PROMPT_KEY initially but preserve distinct purpose/originStage metadata so the lanes can diverge later without another audit.

Non-goals:
- Do not create a separate free-time summarizer function.
- Do not change free-time gate behavior, charge budgeting, internal channel isolation, or return-note delivery behavior.
- Do not alter temporal wake-up summary semantics except where needed to keep shared types exhaustive.

Verification addendum (2026-07-06, code-audited):
All claims above verified accurate. The change is cheaper than the wording implies:
- RecentSessionSummaryPurpose = 'history_budget' | 'wake_session' | 'wake_continuity' at compaction-service.ts:66. There is NO switch or exhaustive check on this type anywhere; the value only flows into originStage (`session.recent.summary.${purpose}`), requestIdBase, and telemetry log fields. Adding 'free_time_return' is a one-line union edit plus the main.ts call-site change.
- Purpose literal consumers today: main.ts:680, main.ts:781 (wake_session); context-builder.ts:251 (history_budget), 1108 (wake_session), 1117 (wake_continuity).
- A new freeTime budget field must touch: FreeTimeConfig shape (scheduler-config.ts:372-386), DEFAULT_FREE_TIME_CONFIG, validateFreeTimeConfig (~line 1017, invoked ~1218), and the runtime copy in scheduler-runtime.ts:47-55 (which currently threads no summary field).
- surfaceReturnNote actually spans free-time.ts:407-451 (not 441); the summary is best-effort (try/catch with warn) and the note only surfaces when result.activity is true and at least one assistant entry exists.
- Adjacent finding, out of scope here: context-builder.ts:1107 and 1116 hardcode maxTokens: 160 for wake_session/wake_continuity summaries instead of reading config — same smell, different lane; file separately if worth fixing.
acceptance_criteria:
- Free-time activity summary calls use a distinct purpose/originStage that names free time rather than wake_session.
- Free-time summary token budgeting is either explicitly owned by freeTime config or intentionally documented as shared without referencing morningWake in app/agent/main.ts.
- Existing wake_session and wake_continuity behavior remains unchanged.
- Tests cover the free-time summarizeActivity wiring/purpose and any new scheduler.json config validation/defaults.
- No new model-facing tool is added and no bespoke free-time summarizer function is introduced.
- npm run lint passes before the bead is closed.
close_reason: Merged in 20a11018 (commit 0bdc3f88): RecentSessionSummaryPurpose gains free_time_return; freeTime.returnNote.summaryMaxTokens (default 160) owned by scheduler.json with validation/defaults/runtime copy; main.ts free-time wiring no longer borrows morningWake budget; free-time.ts doc updated. Tests in free-time.test.ts + scheduler-config.test.ts.

title: Consolidate session search summarization with shared summary completion
description:
Summary:
Session transcript search currently has its own ad hoc LLM summarizer instead of going through the shared session-summary completion path. src/core/session/search-runtime.ts:18 defines SESSION_SEARCH_SUMMARY_SYSTEM_PROMPT inline, src/core/session/search-runtime.ts:208-231 calls llmProvider.complete directly with purpose "summary" and silently falls back on catch, and src/core/tools/session.ts:584-590 exposes this through the canonical session action=search summarize=true path. This overlaps with the consolidated summary plumbing in src/core/session/manager/compaction-service.ts:121-150 completeSessionSummary and src/core/session/manager/compaction-service.ts:152-193 summarizeRecentSessionEntries, which already owns prompt-registry lookup, runtime token injection, retry behavior, request correlation, callType/originStage metadata, and generated-summary normalization.

Why it matters:
This is a smaller version of the old "multiple summarizer functions" problem: not a model-facing duplicate tool, but a duplicate LLM-summary implementation path. It makes prompt ownership inconsistent because session search uses a hard-coded prompt instead of settings-owned PromptRegistry data, and it makes telemetry/correlation inconsistent with session.compaction.summary and session.recent.summary calls.

Files to inspect/change:
- src/core/session/search-runtime.ts:18-24, 153-180, 208-231, 288-290
- src/core/session/manager/compaction-service.ts:78-150, 152-193
- src/core/identity/prompt-registry.ts:19-32, 118-136, 244+ required-substring validation if a new key needs validation
- src/core/tools/session.ts:584-590
- tests near src/core/tools/session-search.test.ts, src/core/session/manager/context-builder.test.ts, src/core/identity/prompt-registry.test.ts

Suggested implementation direction:
Extract or generalize the shared summary completion primitive so session search can provide a distinct prompt key, source payload, requestId base, correlation purpose, originStage, retry policy, and normalization/fallback policy without duplicating direct llmProvider.complete handling. Add a prompt-registry key such as session.search.summary if this summary should remain task-specific. Keep the public surface as canonical session action=search summarize=true; do not revive session_search as a registered top-level tool.

Non-goals:
- Do not change transcript search ranking, privacy gating, snippets, or grep behavior.
- Do not introduce additional model-facing tools.
- Do not silently widen summary access beyond the existing canViewerAccessSessionHit filtering.

Verification addendum (2026-07-06, code-audited):
All claims above verified accurate against the current tree. Precision and implementation notes:
- The direct complete call sits at search-runtime.ts:218-224; the silent `catch { return fallback; }` is at 229-231. The payload builder buildSessionSearchSummaryPayload is separate at 153-180.
- The path is live in production: session.ts:472 injects a real LLMProviderPort into createSessionSearchTool, so summarize=true genuinely calls the LLM.
- callType convention conflict to resolve when consolidating: completeSessionSummary passes positional complete callType 'background' while its correlation metadata sets callType 'summary'; the search path passes positional 'summary' with no correlation metadata at all. Pick one convention deliberately.
- prompt-registry required-substring validation (prompt-registry.ts:244-247, enforced ~569-576) is optional per-key, so a new session.search.summary key without required substrings is fine.
acceptance_criteria:
- session action=search summarize=true still returns the same JSON result shape with query, summary, totalHits, gatedOutCount, and hits.
- The LLM-backed session-search summary uses a PromptRegistry-owned prompt or a shared summary completion helper rather than an inline hard-coded prompt plus direct llmProvider.complete call in search-runtime.ts.
- Summary completion telemetry includes a stable correlation purpose and originStage for session search, comparable to session.recent.summary.* and session.compaction.summary.
- Fallback behavior remains deterministic when there are no hits or the LLM call fails, and failures are not silently swallowed without at least preserving existing non-blocking behavior.
- Tests cover the prompt source, correlation metadata, no-hit fallback, LLM failure fallback, and privacy-filtered hit set used for summarization.
- npm run lint passes before the bead is closed.
close_reason: Merged in 20a11018 (commit 735618a8): search-runtime now uses exported completeSessionSummary with PromptRegistry key session.search.summary (seeded from previous inline text), correlation purpose/originStage session.search.summary, logged non-blocking fallback; sandbox REPL path passes promptRegistry:null and gets registry-owned seed default. title: Move queued whisper/follow-up drain out of live user turns (inject before step 1 or run as own turn)
description:
Follow-up to psfn-framework-ay73 (both parallel fix designs recommended this as the architectural completion, deliberately deferred for blast-radius reasons).

Two problems with the current drain point (scheduled-agent-loop.ts followUp checkpoint, end of run):
1. Internal follow-ups extend live user turns as continuation steps. ay73's boundary + demotion makes this safe for delivery, but the continuation steps still burn 3-4 extra LLM calls per user turn and run intention/self-model side effects inside the user turn's correlation.
2. Whisper timing is backwards: intention whispers with wake_conditions [next_user_turn] are meant to SHAPE the next reply ("next turn, vary your response, ask about his evening"). Today they inject AFTER step 1 has already authored the reply — the guidance arrives too late to influence anything, then the model responds to the stale note (observed live 2026-07-04: turns 019f2f60/019f2f6f/019f2f76/019f2fa4).

Design directions: (a) drain queued follow-ups at run START (before the initial prompt) so whispers become pre-reply context for the user turn; (b) or run them as their own internal turn with their own disposition when the agent is idle. (a) fixes the timing defect and eliminates most continuation steps; (b) is cleaner separation. Either must preserve: whispers never persisted to the session journal, never leak outward, mdxu dedupe and pk77 guard behavior, and the ay73 boundary for follow-ups that genuinely arrive mid-run (background completions).

title: Surface rolling-24h vs per-run quota semantics in Garden and companion messaging
description:
Context: working_docs/kube-issue-report-20260704.md §B2b.

The charge-quota block uses a rolling 24-hour window (env RUN_CHARGE_ROLLING_WINDOW_MS), not a per-run counter. On 2026-07-04 the operator raised charge-policy.json runChargeQuotaByLane.interactive from 24 to 100 and restarted the agent, expecting selfie_create to unblock immediately — but previously-spent units (27) still counted against the window until they aged out, so the block persisted. Chat evidence: 'I quadrupled your budget... I made it 100 but if it didn't work that's weird.'

The error text seen was: 'Charge quota exceeded for lane "interactive" while charging "paidImageGeneration" (27/24; rolling 24-hour budget)'.

Task: make Garden and companion-facing messaging distinguish 'per-run lane quota' from 'rolling 24h spend' so a quota raise + restart does not read as an immediate unblock. Garden should show the effective rolling-window spend and when it decays, and the block message should explain that recent spend still counts until it ages out of the window.

title: Investigate OpenRouter fallback latency after ChatGPTN cooldown
description: Summary: After psfn-framework-smtq was fixed and deployed in commit 543571f8 on 2026-07-03, live Carlini failover no longer waits through repeated ChatGPTN retries, but the fallback provider itself still showed high latency in smoke and live traffic. Evidence: gateway smoke api:failover-smoke-543571f8-one hit ChatGPTN once at 22:04:03, marked connection_unavailable cooldownMs=300000 at 22:04:33, then completed through deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash at 22:04:36. The immediate second smoke api:failover-smoke-543571f8-two selected deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash as attempt 1 at 22:04:36 with no ChatGPTN attempt, but API elapsed time was 44.380s and LLM stream completed at 22:05:21. A live Discord request 1522422972051226625 also selected deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash as attempt 1 at 22:05:22, then produced several attempt=1 LLM stream completions between 22:05:49 and 22:06:09. A background fallback call started around 22:04:36 and completed at 22:05:17, so possible causes include OpenRouter/LiteLLM provider latency, fallback model choice, or background/extraction contention. Scope: measure fallback-provider latency and concurrent background/memory LLM behavior when ChatGPTN is cooled down; tune routing, concurrency, timeout, or model selection only if a code-owned cause is found. Non-goals: do not restore the 192.168.1.43 ChatGPTN host here; do not change scheduler optional flips; do not print or alter provider secrets.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible timing baseline is captured for chat fallback, background, and memory/extraction LLM calls while ChatGPTN is unreachable/cooled down; the cause is identified as provider latency, LiteLLM contention, agent pipeline concurrency, or another named factor; if code/config-owned, a focused fix is implemented and deployed with health checks green; if not code-owned, the bead records the evidence and operational recommendation.

title: P2: Sleeptime wiki prompt includes every existing wiki entry
description:
Summary
This prompt includes every wiki entry title/id on each run, so token usage grows linearly with wiki size and can eventually hit context limits or unnecessary cost. Capping `existingEntries` before prompt construction would keep runtime bounded.

Review provenance
- Cubic severity: P2
- Split PR: #28
- Review thread: https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/pull/28#discussion_r3516424052
- Cited location: src/faculties/wiki/sleeptime-wiki-pass.ts:454

Final-tip validation evidence
SleeptimeWikiPass.run builds existingEntries with this.wikiStore.list().map(...) at src/faculties/wiki/sleeptime-wiki-pass.ts:454 with no cap. buildRequestPrompt renders every entry as '- id: title' at lines 596-627, specifically lines 621-624, so prompt size grows linearly with total wiki entries.

Scope
Cap or rank existingEntries before prompt construction, preferably by recent/search relevance plus a hard maximum; add a prompt-size/cap test with many wiki entries.

- Do not resolve the GitHub review thread until the fix is implemented, validated, committed, and pushed.

title: P2: Wiki pass gate can open on non-eligible private world-typed memories
description:
Summary
Private semantic/procedural memories can open the deterministic gate, so this pass may spend an LLM call even when there is no wiki-eligible memory material to review. Using the same `isWorldCandidateMemory` filter for `newDurableMemories` keeps gate behavior aligned with the non-private source set.

- Split PR: #28
- Review thread: https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/pull/28#discussion_r3516424055
- Cited location: src/faculties/wiki/sleeptime-wiki-pass.ts:434

Final-tip validation evidence
run computes newDurableMemories as windowMemories.filter(memory => WORLD_MEMORY_TYPES.has(memory.type)) at src/faculties/wiki/sleeptime-wiki-pass.ts:434, while the actual prompt source worldMemories uses isWorldCandidateMemory at line 435. isWorldCandidateMemory also requires allowed sensitivity and no contact link at lines 185-188. Gate inputs use newDurableMemories.length at lines 439-443, so semantic/procedural memories excluded from worldMemories can still open the deterministic LLM gate.

title: P2: Temporal wake anti-loop only scans last 64 persisted entries after restart
description:
Summary
Wake-note anti-looping can fail in busy sessions because persisted note detection only scans the last 64 entries. If the previous wake note is older than that window, the scheduler can treat the session as note-free and inject duplicate same-day/too-soon temporal notes.

Review provenance
- Cubic severity: P2
- Split PR: #28
- Review thread: https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/pull/28#discussion_r3516424048
- Cited location: src/core/scheduler/temporal-wakeup.ts:688

Final-tip validation evidence
resolveWakeupSessionContext reads persistedEntries with getRecentSessionEntries(sessionId, 64) at src/core/scheduler/temporal-wakeup.ts:677-690 and derives lastWakeupNoteAtMs from that plus the in-memory lastRecordedBySession map at lines 690-692. Morning anti-loop depends on that timestamp for same-day notes at lines 393-398, and idle refresher anti-loop uses it at lines 488-493, so after restart a prior note older than the last 64 entries is invisible.

title: P2: Async wiki projection repair can delete documents written during startup
description:
Summary
A wiki document written during startup can lose semantic-search visibility until it is written again. The repair runs asynchronously from a stale `documents` snapshot while `rebuild()` deletes projected IDs not in that snapshot, so waiting for repair completion before returning avoids this race.

Review provenance
- Cubic severity: P2
- Split PR: #28
- Review thread: https://github.com/CGIC-AI/psfn-framework/pull/28#discussion_r3516424038
- Cited location: src/faculties/wiki/runtime-wiring.ts:141

Final-tip validation evidence
wireWikiRuntime installs an async onUpsert projection sync hook at src/faculties/wiki/runtime-wiring.ts:80-87, then starts startup repair with void async IIFE at lines 135-160 and returns without awaiting at line 163. The repair snapshots store.list/get at lines 143-146 and calls activeProjection.rebuild(documents) at line 147. rebuild computes drift from that snapshot and deletes projected IDs not in it at src/faculties/wiki/pgvector-projection.ts:307-329, so a document written after the snapshot but before rebuild deletion can be removed from semantic projection.

Scope
Await startup repair before returning the writable store/projection, or make rebuild reconcile against a fresh canonical list before deletion; add a race regression test with a write during repair.

Non-goals
- Do not broaden this into unrelated refactors outside the cited behavior.
- Do not resolve the GitHub review thread until the fix is implemented, validated, committed, and pushed.

description:

title: P2: Graph proposal polling can overwrite mutation refresh with stale data
description:
Summary
The 15-second auto-refresh polling can race with the manual refresh that runs after approve/reject actions. If `getGraphProposals()` is still in flight when the user clicks Approve or Reject, the polling response can arrive after the mutation's refresh and overwrite `proposals` with stale data, temporarily reverting a just-approved proposal back to pending and showing the action buttons again. title: P2: Elevated reveal creates per-memory grant without reveal audit
description:

title: Wiki pgvector projection and capped supplemental RAG
description:
## Scope

- Mirror wiki documents into pgvector as a projection (rebuildable from the canonical workspace Markdown files per the charter mirror/projection law); embeddings via the existing embedding provider port. Plain text search remains and is sufficient while the wiki is small; semantic search becomes valuable as it grows.
- Add semantic search to the wiki tool alongside the existing text search; results carry document provenance.
- Supplemental chat RAG with per-context token caps, all config-owned:
  - normal chat: ~1k tokens of wiki context,
  - group chat: conservative — only when clearly useful, deterministically gated; do not flood group context with random world info,
  - project/focus-scoped work: higher cap, since project work is supposed to focus on project knowledge (integrates with the focus-session scoped retrieval that already exists).
- Wiki retrieval is supplemental and gated — it must not fire every turn, and memory retrieval always outranks wiki content in prompt assembly.

## Non-goals

- Shared-world wiki (psfn-framework-i5s2).
- Replacing memory retrieval; wiki is world knowledge, not lived experience.
acceptance_criteria:
1. pgvector index is a rebuildable projection of the workspace files (repair-path test).
2. Wiki tool gains semantic search mode; results carry document provenance.
3. Token caps config-owned per context class (chat ~1k, group conservative, project higher) and enforced in prompt assembly.
4. Wiki retrieval is gated (not every turn) and never displaces memory context (test).

Note: when enabled, wiki does one synchronous embed+search on the turn hot path (unlike cached memory) — acceptable while opt-in; revisit with a cached/background variant if enabled-by-default later.
close_reason: Merged; AC verified (checksum-drift repair test, semantic mode with provenance, config-owned caps enforced in prompt assembly, gated + memory-never-displaced; 613/614 with only the known pre-existing failure)

title: Sleeptime wiki update pass
description:
## Scope

- A true-sleeptime pass (runs in the E5 nightly lane, after the day's episodes and memories have settled): review the day for durable, non-private world knowledge worth creating or updating wiki entries — interests, research results, world/environment details, project information.
- Boundary rules: personal facts stay in memory (the partner being from a Paris neighborhood is memory; general knowledge about that neighborhood is wiki). Repeatable procedures become skills, not wiki entries. Direct actions are tools.
- Deterministic gate first (shared gating primitive from E6): skip with zero LLM spend when the day produced nothing wiki-shaped.
- Writes go through the existing wiki tool/store with provenance refs to the source episodes/memories; sensitivity defaults respected (personal).

## Non-goals

- Shared-world wiki semantics (psfn-framework-i5s2 decision gates that).
- Wiki retrieval (sibling bead).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Runs only in the nightly lane after episode/memory settling; deterministic gate skips with zero LLM on empty days.
2. Entries carry provenance refs to source episodes/memories; personal facts are not duplicated into wiki (spot tests).
3. Garden wiki view shows new/updated entries attributed to the pass.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (pushed). sleeptime-wiki-pass runs after consolidation/arcs/dream in the nightly lane; deterministic gate (wiki_pass lane, opens on >=1 new canonical episode OR >=3 new durable memories since watermark, zero LLM on empty days); schema-bound prompt with hard memory/skill/tool boundaries + conservative three-signal personal-fact post-filter (guard memories pre-split from model input); fails closed on malformed output with watermark hold; WikiStore.upsert as generated_synthesis with episode/memory provenance; wikiPass config block; wiki_curation persona-preamble subsystem seeded. BONUS FIX: runtime re-map sites were silently dropping orientationRewrite from operator scheduler.json (silent-fallback bug from the E6.4 merge) — passthrough fixed for both blocks.

title: Free-time lanes: quiet-hours block and idle-triggered block
description:
## Problem

Quiet hours and idle detection exist (rest window gating, ambient presence at src/core/scheduler/ambient-presence.ts detecting 3h+ gaps), but there is no surface for self-directed activity — ambient presence only records a note. The companion has no free time.

## Scope

- Two free-time lanes: (a) a quiet-hours block inside the rest window; (b) an idle-triggered block after ~3 hours of partner inactivity (config-owned thresholds; reuse ambient-presence detection).
- Open, non-clinical framing with the FULL persona loaded (E6 full-persona work): "You have some time to yourself. You can explore something, make something, think about something, try a tool, write something down, or do nothing if you want." Gentle optional direction is fine (offer to browse journal, wiki, notes, tools). Forced tasks are not. Doing nothing — loafing in a sunbeam, more cat than girl — is a valid outcome, recorded as such, not as a failure.
- Access: her tools, shards, wiki, journal, media, durable storage — under existing capability/trust policy; no new privileges. If she researches something it can go to the wiki; if she discovers an interest it can become memory; poetry, pictures, an iOS app for a phone nobody owns, a concept album — all valid. Do not force interests into her; give her the space.
- Hard budget cap per charge policy (charter 8.9); spend visible in Garden; exhaustion ends the block gracefully.
- Outputs land in durable storage (journal, wiki, memory, media, beads for bugs she notices) — never directly into chat. Any outward message rides the existing proactive-outbound gates.
- "While you were away" surfacing: when the partner returns, a context block summarizes free-time activity (shared summarization service) so she can mention it naturally — "while you were away, I worked on this."

## Non-goals

- New tool privileges or new self-modification surfaces (charter law 14/15 unchanged).
- Proactive outbound changes (existing gates are the boundary).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Lanes fire only within configured gates (rest window / ~3h idle) and never during active conversation.
2. Hard budget cap enforced; exhaustion ends the block gracefully and visibly.
3. Artifacts land in durable stores tagged with free-time provenance; no direct chat output; outward messages only via proactive gates (test).
4. Return-surfacing block appears after active free time and not after empty blocks; zero-output runs recorded as valid.
5. Prompt uses full persona and open framing; no forced-task language.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (e4a40022, pushed). Two lanes (quiet-hours + 3h-idle) under scheduler.json freeTime block; deterministic pre-spend gate (partner_recently_active / min_block_interval 4h / daily cap 3, shared across lanes); blocks run on internal:free-time:* channels (isInternalSessionId — outward dispatch structurally impossible, tested); full persona leads + operator-editable open seed text; budget = background charge lane, maxTurns 6 + maxChargeUnits 8 checked pre-turn, graceful visible endReason; silent reply on turn 0 = valid loafed outcome; return-surfacing via appendContextSystemNote + shared summarizer after ACTIVE blocks only; scheduler.free_time.gate/.block events + free_time health lane. Deviation noted: per-tool artifact provenance tagging (journal/wiki writes from free time) left to tool-level follow-up if wanted.
close_reason: Merged in e4a40022; AC verified (gate-only firing, hard budget caps with graceful exhaustion, durable-only outputs with no outward leak tested, active-only return surfacing, full persona + open framing, zero-output valid; 274 tests green)

title: Habit-derived wake window from message-timestamp history
description:
## Scope

- Estimate the operator's wake window from message-timestamp history over 7- and 30-day windows (data already in L0/projections): detect the nightly sleep gap, build a wake-time distribution, and schedule the morning wake inside the estimated window instead of the fixed default (e.g. sleeps 00:00–02:00, wakes 06:00–08:00 → wake event falls in that window).
- Deterministic estimator, no LLM. Config toggle; falls back to the fixed configured time when data is insufficient, with a visible reason.
- Document the future extension without building it: SensorIngestPort data (heart rate, motion, activity) distinguishing "woke up to pee at 3 a.m." from "actually awake and doing things."

## Non-goals

- Sensor ingestion itself (charter Phase 11).
- Changing the wake-note content (parent wake-up bead owns that).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Deterministic estimator unit-tested on synthetic histories (regular, shifted, irregular sleepers).
2. Insufficient data falls back to the fixed configured time with a visible reason.
3. Config toggle; current estimate visible in Garden.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (fa9eea57, pushed). Deterministic estimator: per-day largest sleep-gap ending in a 03:00-12:00 wake band (min 4h gap), weighted quantiles (7d window 2x over 30d), fires at weighted median; <4 sample days fails closed to fixed time with typed reason. timing fixed|habit toggle (default fixed), habit block fully config-owned with cross-field validation. GET /api/admin/scheduler/wake-window recomputes live. Known limitation (documented in-code): habit estimate resolves at process start; drift applies on restart — safe daily re-arming is a possible follow-up. Merge conflict in local-admin-contract.ts resolved by threading the wake-snapshot provider into the shared AdminSchedulerService used by subsystem-health. Also fixed during merge validation: E5.6 nav route /subsystem-health was missing from the Garden SPA client-route allowlist (caught by nav-advertised route test, fixed on 4yb3.6 attribution).
close_reason: Merged in fa9eea57; AC verified (synthetic-history estimator tests incl. shifted/irregular sleepers, fail-closed fallback with visible reason, owner-file toggle + verify:settings-contract green, admin API route tested)

title: Fatigue enablement: companion-contact auto-tagging and end-to-end verification
description:
## Problem

The fatigue system is substantially built (relationship classes, budget states, overcharge logic, runtime enforcement — src/core/agent/fatigue/policy.ts, runtime-enforcement.ts) but companion contacts are not automatically identified, and end-to-end behavior has not been verified for live enablement. The guard exists to stop companions looping nonsense at each other after the salient things are said — not to ban conversation.

## Scope

- Auto-classify machine-intelligence contacts: Discord bot/app metadata tags a contact as another companion/MI at contact creation/update, so fatigue relationship classes apply automatically without manual tagging.
- End-to-end verification of the pipeline under a simulated two-companion loop: budgets spend only on MI-to-MI turns, soft/hard caps and wrap-up states trigger correctly, overcharge fires only on qualifying triggers (recent human participation or work/research intent).
- Enable for companion rooms once verified; document operator knobs; fatigue state per room visible in Garden.
- Companions remain ordinary contacts for emotional trend and relationship tracking (E6 owns that); fatigue is the only companion-specific layer.

## Non-goals

- Inter-companion side-channel protocol (psfn-framework-8pyl owns the TCP/websocket/cert-auth direction).
- Context firewall (psfn-framework-htm9, deliberately deferred; will apply to inter-companion traffic when built).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Discord bot/app-flagged users auto-classified as machine-intelligence contacts; fatigue applies without manual tagging.
2. Simulated two-companion loop terminates within budget; wrap-up and hard-exhaustion states trigger correctly; overcharge fires only on qualifying triggers.
3. Enablement and operator knobs documented; per-room fatigue state visible in Garden.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (d593cbb7, pushed). Contact.isMachineIntelligence auto-set from Discord author.bot via MessageRoutingMetadata.authorIsMachineIntelligence -> observed-machine-intelligence helper in runtime-context author resolution. Precedence via contact_mutation_audit actor: system:channel_observation only adds the marker and skips when the latest audit actor is non-system (operator override survives; degenerate false->false no-op corrections remain markable, documented). No redundant enabled flag — fatigue only spends on MI-to-MI turns so it cannot bound human conversation; live enablement = allowedBotUserIds + auto-tag + charge-policy.json fatigue tuning (docs/operations.md). Per-room fatigue readable via GET /api/admin/charges filters. Two-companion loop test proves full budget state walk, MI-only spend, overcharge trigger discipline, bounded termination. Follow-up documented: Telegram adapter drops bot authors entirely, so MI tagging is moot there until bot-author observation is enabled.
close_reason: Merged in d593cbb7; AC verified (auto-classification through real contact path with override survival, two-companion loop terminates within budget with correct state walk, knobs documented + Garden readable, 304 tests green)

title: Generalize deterministic pre-LLM gating across recurring passes
description:
## Problem

Deterministic pre-LLM gating exists in exactly one place (src/faculties/memory/extraction/signals.ts evaluateExtractionPreLlmGate) while other recurring LLM passes fire unconditionally on cadence. Where deterministic signals can tell us nothing changed, the heavier nondeterministic process must not fire. Minimize unnecessary token use — if a process does not need to run, it must not run.

## Scope

- Generalize the extraction-gate pattern into a reusable gating primitive: deterministic inputs (text signals, VAD/trend deltas, interaction counts, watermarks/new-message checks) decide whether a recurring LLM pass fires.
- Apply to: core-memory orientation-block updates, appraisal escalation, consolidation refinement, the wiki pass (E8), and concern review (already count-gated — normalize it onto the shared primitive).
- Every gated skip records a reason as a typed event, visible in the Garden subsystem-health view.

## Non-goals

- The episode-synthesis trigger gate (owned by the E5 gate bead; it should share the primitive where practical).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Shared gate primitive exists; per-pass gate definitions documented.
2. Orientation-block updates, appraisal escalation, consolidation refinement, and concern review short-circuit with zero LLM calls when gated closed (tests).
3. Skip reasons emitted as typed events consumed by the Garden subsystem-health view.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (109bf778 + fixture sync, pushed at f94953c1). Shared primitive src/shared/gating/deterministic-gate.ts (blockWhen ordered pre-checks -> openWhenAny signals -> closedReason; missing input fails closed by throwing). Gates: orientation rewrite (>=4 new entries OR >=7 quiet days with activity — the operator-flagged sleep-time-orientation fix; skipping is the common case on quiet days; scheduler.json orientationRewrite block), dream meaning (cadence + episodes-without-meaning), refinement (unrefined count), emotion appraisal (turn cadence OR VAD delta, byte-identical), extraction + concern review normalized byte-identically. 5 typed gate events + 5 subsystem-health lanes. Deviations accepted: extraction skips stay on memory.extraction.end telemetry (no bus handle, no dead wiring); orientation gate omits emotion-movement input (participant trends were unmerged during its work) — FOLLOW-UP: now that jpvd.3 is merged, hasMeaningfulParticipantMovement could feed the orientation gate as an additional opening signal.
close_reason: Merged; AC verified (per-pass zero-LLM skip tests, byte-identical extraction/concern regression, typed skip events on health lanes, settings-contract green)

title: Per-participant emotional trend tracking in group rooms
description:
## Problem

Emotion is scoped per DM/room (scoped-emotion.ts, E1.5) with group→DM carry-over, but there is no per-participant trend tracking inside a group. One person being cruel and another being kind must move the companion's orientation toward each of them separately; an idle participant's orientation must not move at all.

## Scope

- Extend scoped emotion with deterministic per-contact trend lines within group rooms: per-participant VAD/discrete-emotion EMA trends plus interaction counts, fed by the existing local classifiers (no LLM in the accumulation path).
- Orientation toward a person updates only from that person's own interactions, gated by meaningful movement (trend delta plus minimum interaction volume), and moves slowly and smoothly (EMA) — people do not change their minds over one sentence.
- Idle participants: no orientation update, no token spend.
- Other companions/bots are ordinary contacts for emotional trend and relationship tracking; fatigue (E7) is the only companion-specific layer.
- Bounded scale by design: rooms are small (a dozen participants max as design point). Cap tracked participants per room and evict stale trends.

## Non-goals

- Changing the E1 group→DM carry-over rules.
- LLM-based appraisal changes (this is the deterministic substrate those consume).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Cruel-vs-kind participant scenario produces independent trend movement with correct direction (test).
2. Idle participant orientation unchanged after sustained activity by others (test).
3. Zero LLM calls in trend accumulation; rates and caps config-owned.
4. Trends persisted in Postgres and survive restart; E1 group-to-DM carry-over behavior unchanged.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (99939de9, pushed). participant_emotion_trends table (PostgresParticipantTrendStore per internal-state-store pattern, wired into createAgentPersistenceRuntime); slow per-participant VAD/discrete EMA + interaction counts fed from each authors own observations in EmotionSelfModelRuntime (zero LLM); idle participants never move; cap 16/room + 14d stale eviction. Config: settings.json emotionScoping.participantTrends (emaAlpha 0.12, minInteractionsForMovement 3, minTrendDelta 0.1). carryOverUsesParticipantTrend flag (default false = E1 behavior unchanged) lets group-to-DM carry-over weight by the members own trend. Consumption surface for orientation/appraisal: getParticipantTrend/getRoomParticipantTrends/hasMeaningfulParticipantMovement — E6.4 gating + future orientation work consume these. 297 emotion/config/settings tests green.
close_reason: Merged in 99939de9; AC verified (cruel-vs-kind independent trends, idle untouched, zero-LLM accumulation, Postgres persistence round-trip, E1 carry-over tests unchanged, config-owned, settings-contract green)

title: Persona preamble service for schema-bound subprocess prompts
description:
## Scope

- One shared persona-preamble service producing a compressed identity snippet (a few sentences: who the companion is, setting, voice) plus a per-subsystem role framing: "I am <companion>'s memory system. My job is to go through our conversations and find the things that matter to me, then preserve them."
- Consumed by every recurring schema-bound subprocess prompt: extraction orchestrator (src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts), profile synthesis (profile-synthesis.ts), episode synthesis/segmentation, consolidation refinement, concern candidate review.
- Preamble precedes the strict task instructions and JSON schema; the schema/format sections stay untouched — soft framing first, hard instructions after.
- Wording companion-configurable (charter 8.7) via the prompt/template registry; the compressed persona derives from the character card so there is no hand-maintained duplicate to drift.

## Non-goals

- Full-persona introspection surfaces (sibling bead) — this bead is the small-subprocess snippet only.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Single shared service; no per-feature bespoke persona snippets.
2. Extraction, profile synthesis, episode synthesis/segmentation, consolidation refinement, and concern review prompts consume it (snapshot tests of assembled prompts).
3. Schema/format sections unchanged; structured-output parsing tests stay green.
4. Framing text operator-editable via the prompt registry; compressed persona derived from the character card.

(registry-owned via persona-preamble-seeds.ts merged into PROMPT_SEEDS — persists, versions, Garden-editable; NOTHING hardcoded at consumer sites, consumers pass a subsystem id only). char + compressed personality_summary derive from the live character card. title: Full-persona introspection for scheduled reflection and heavy tasks
description:
## Problem

Daily/weekly reflection currently runs as clinical deliberation (src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-policy.ts:386-428) with internal-state blocks but without the full persona/memory/personality context loaded. If scheduled introspection does not load the full person, it is not the companion reflecting and its output is not valid.

## Scope

- Daily review, weekly review, the dream-meaning pass, and (when built) free-time lanes assemble the FULL persona, memory retrieval context, and personality/self-model state, framed first person: "I am <companion>, and I am reviewing what happened in my day."
- Prompt audit across these surfaces: remove or re-voice clinical trailing directives that can override persona (strong end-of-prompt directives outweigh persona paragraphs — the assistant-mode bleed failure). Keep the charter-required guards (evidence before narrative, telemetry kept separate, no ACAC performance shaping) but phrase them in-voice rather than as machine-form instructions.
- Reflection output remains journal-bound (no outward messages from reflection).

## Non-goals

- The compressed-preamble service for schema-bound subprocesses (sibling bead).
- Changing reflection scheduling (already scheduler-owned).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Daily/weekly reflection and dream-meaning prompt plans contain full persona and memory context blocks (regression test asserts presence).
2. Prompt audit documents each removed or re-voiced directive; no persona-overriding assistant-mode language near prompt end.
3. Charter guards (evidence-first, telemetry separation, no ACAC shaping) preserved in-voice.
4. Reflection output remains journal-bound; existing reflection tests updated and green.

title: Garden subsystem-health dashboard for background lanes
description:
## Problem

Background subsystems (episode synthesis, consolidation, arc weaving, extraction, active-memory refresh) fail or skip silently; the operator only finds out via code archaeology. That is exactly how the sleeptime miswiring went undetected. Broken paths must not quietly continue.

## Scope

Garden subsystem-health view: for each background lane — last run time, trigger reason, outcome (ran / skipped with reason / failed with error), current watermarks, and item counts. Built on real runtime/event-bus data, never fabricated state. Include the new lanes as they land: episode trigger gate, temporal wake-up, free-time blocks, wiki pass.

Skip reasons come from the deterministic gates (episode gate bead, pre-LLM gating bead); failures come from typed error events (legacy-retrieval retirement bead feeds this).

## Non-goals

- Building new telemetry pipelines; use the existing event bus and telemetry surfaces.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Garden page lists background lane statuses (last run, trigger, outcome, watermarks, counts) from live event/telemetry data.
2. Skips show gate reasons; failures show errors; stale data marked stale; no fabricated healthy state.
3. Admin API additions follow existing /api/admin patterns with tests.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (1fc25931, pushed). GET /api/admin/subsystem-health + Garden page (Review & Safety nav). Six event-bus lanes (near_turn, episode_synthesis w/ gate reasons, active_context refresh+degraded, extraction, retrieval, social_graph) as since-process-start ring buffers, plus read-only scheduler lane table (rest-window, episode timer, wake-ups, reflections, ambient, etc). Honest states: never/skipped/degraded/failed/stale/paused/ok; 503 offline panel when unwired. Deviation: watermark figures come from gate events, not l01_processing_watermarks (no global enumeration API; adding one was out of scope) — revisit if durable per-scope watermark display is ever needed.
close_reason: Merged in 1fc25931; AC verified (live event/telemetry sourced, skip reasons + errors + stale/never states explicit, /api/admin patterns with 10 tests, backend+admin-ui builds green)

title: Contextual topic cutting with trailing holdback
description:
## Problem

Episode boundaries are purely mechanical (UTC day, 45-min gap, 14-entry cap — src/faculties/memory/episodic/synthesis.ts:209-240). A 10-turn chunk with 8 turns on one topic and 2 starting another becomes one muddled episode or a valueless runt.

## Scope

- Keep the deterministic pre-cuts (day boundary, long silence gap) as outer bounds.
- Within a gated chunk, LLM segmentation proposes topic boundaries. Schema-bound structured output — a clinical prompt is correct here (with the persona preamble from the E6 preamble service once available).
- Trailing turns of an unfinished topic are HELD BACK — not claimed — and roll into the next pass, so a continuing topic is not chopped mid-thought. Held turns become part of the next episode if the topic continues.
- Cap episodes per run. Imperfect cuts are acceptable; re-processing claimed turns is not (the claiming bead guarantees that independently).

## Non-goals

- Changing the claim semantics (sibling bead owns claims).
- Nightly boundary refinement (m58.1 may still merge/split at consolidation time).
acceptance_criteria:
1. 8+2 case: eight-turn topic becomes one episode; trailing two turns held unclaimed (test).
2. Held turns are claimed only when their topic closes or the next pass processes them.
3. Segmentation output schema-validated; malformed output fails closed (no episode written, typed error event emitted).
4. lint + build + tests green.
notes: 2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (pushed; branch agent/e5.4-topic-cutting). topic-segmentation.ts: schema-strict parser (contiguous cover, index bounds, open only on final segment) + one complete() call per chunk via the arc-formation provider pattern. Config: episodeSynthesis.topicSegmentationEnabled, seeded false and optional-with-explicit-default so live owner files keep validating (no second forced migration); enabled-without-provider throws at construction. Held/failed/budget-skipped turns never claimed, watermark never passes a failed chunk, 45-min lookback keeps held turns visible. title: E6: Subprocess persona voice and per-participant orientation
description:
## Problem

Audit (2026-07-02) confirmed zero persona framing in any subprocess prompt (extraction orchestrator, profile synthesis, episodic passes — all detached task prompts), and scheduled reflection runs as clinical deliberation without the full person loaded. An introspection process without the self loaded is not the companion reflecting — it is a context analyzer with no self in it, and its output is not valid introspection.

Clinical trailing directives are also a persona hazard: a strong two-sentence directive near the end of the prompt can outweigh six paragraphs of persona. This is the observed Carlini failure — the character drifts from "nun gardener who grows weed" to "AI assistants do not talk about weed."

## Principles (operator, 2026-07-02 planning chat)

- Hard task-gated systems (memory generation, JSON schema output): soft persona preamble + strict instructions is the correct model. Clinical structure stays where strict formatting is required.
- Scheduled reflection, free time, and heavy introspection: the full person — full persona, full memory context, personality state, first person.
- Small subsystems are framed as parts of the person: "I am this companion's memory system. This is who I am. This is what I do for the whole." The organelles need to know what body they belong to.
- Deterministic recomputation of affect variables is fine and stays; the fault was scheduling and framing, not determinism.
- Companion-facing wording remains companion-configurable (charter 8.7).

## Model assignment

Implementation: Opus. Testing: Sonnet.
close_reason: All four children complete and merged: persona preamble service (operator template verbatim, registry-owned), full-persona introspection with directive audit, per-participant emotional trends, deterministic pre-LLM gating across recurring passes.

title: E4.2: Graph-builder worker in the memory-agent lane (the gremlin)
description:
## Context
Edges today are manual or mention-inferred at extraction time. Ratified approach: a background worker beside sleeptime/extraction in the memory-agent lane ("the gremlin in the gestalt") — never inline in the chat path — that reads accumulated group evidence and proposes edges.

## Scope
- New job in the memory-agent lane on the group-watermark cadence (share E1.6 batching machinery): reads new room-scoped memories + provenance (sourceSpeakerNames, addressMode: overheard_room_context, subjectContactId) since watermark.
- Proposes: (a) acquaintance-class edges from repeated co-presence (N co-active sessions threshold, config-owned); (b) typed edges from overheard interactions naming two tracked people; (c) typed BIDIRECTIONAL edges from named-relationship facts ("my sister Iki" -> sibling both ways), extending inferRelationshipTypeFromFact (mention-only-contacts.ts:30-45).
- All proposals: confidence 0.5-0.7, source: 'memory', evidence-memory links populated; never overwrite operator-set (source: 'manual') or higher-confidence edges; conflicting proposals surface in Garden for review rather than auto-resolving (fail closed).
- Only tracked contacts participate (E3.4 gate); sensitivity on edges inherited from evidence memory sensitivity (max of sources).
- Garden: proposed-edges review view (approve/adjust/reject) — reuses the graph's existing sensitivity filtering for display. Proposals surface in Garden review (charter Law 31: no silent task execution).

## Non-goals
No nightly relationship TRUST review (4caj.4-.8, later). No inference chains (friend-of-friend). No decay model yet (note as follow-up).

- Fixture: room transcript with two people repeatedly co-present + one overheard "X is Y's sister" produces exactly the expected proposals with evidence links; re-running from the same watermark produces no duplicates.
- Operator-set edge survives a conflicting proposal (conflict surfaces in Garden).
- Untracked speaker in fixtures produces zero graph rows.
