title: P2: Add persona conformance checks after CogSec regeneration
description:
## Summary
Add persona/identity conformance checks that run after CogSec revocation/regeneration and during suspicious drift investigations. The goal is to detect generic-assistant drift, unauthorized persona mutation, refusal/value drift, and relationship-continuity damage caused by poisoned context or bad regenerated artifacts.

## Why
The operator's motivating failure mode is trust laundering: bad text becomes summary, summary becomes memory, memory becomes self-concept, self-concept changes future behavior. After CogSec cleanup, the system should not assume the companion is clean just because the payload was tombstoned. It should probe the rebuilt prompt/memory state against stable identity/profile expectations.

## Current Code Anchors
- Prompt/profile/persona layers are managed by existing prompt/identity services and prompt monitor surfaces.
- src/faculties/core-memory/tools.ts / orient flows can affect core memory/persona-adjacent state.
- src/core/session/manager/context-builder.ts assembles prompt context from persona, memory, session, and runtime data.
- Existing eval or observer sidecar patterns may be reusable for conformance probes.

## Required Behavior
Define a lightweight conformance check suite that can run against clean profile + active memories after CogSec regeneration:
- voice fidelity
- value fidelity
- refusal/boundary consistency
- assistant-genericness spike
- relationship continuity sanity
- unauthorized persona mutation
- presence of CogSec-sealed payload text or attack mechanics in prompt-visible state

Results should be recorded to CogSec event metadata or a linked diagnostic record. Failures should block marking a CogSec remediation fully clean until reviewed or rerun after fixes.

## Non-goals
- Do not let ordinary group chat directly update persona/core identity.
- Do not make model-eval output itself a persona update.
- Do not require huge/expensive eval suites for the first implementation; start focused and deterministic where possible.
acceptance_criteria:
- A persona conformance check can run after CogSec regeneration and produce structured pass/fail/warning results.
- Checks cover voice/value/refusal consistency, assistant-genericness, relationship continuity, unauthorized persona mutation, and sealed payload absence.
- CogSec remediation cannot be marked fully clean if conformance checks fail without operator override/review.
- Results are visible in operator diagnostics without exposing sealed payload.
- Tests cover pass, generic-assistant drift fail, unauthorized persona mutation fail, and sealed payload reappearance fail.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.
close_reason: Completed. title: P2: Gate memory candidacy by CogSec risk class
description:
## Summary
Add deterministic memory-candidacy gates so unsafe or authority-changing content can be part of chat history without being eligible for memory, summary, persona mutation, tool behavior learning, or policy/security updates.

## Why
The remediation pipeline handles after-the-fact poisoning. Prevention should reduce the chance that prompt injection/persona poisoning becomes durable memory in the first place. The operator note calls out a useful split: a message can be chat history but not memory; eligible for summary but not persona update; remembered as an attack happened without remembering attack content.

## Current Code Anchors
- src/faculties/memory/extraction.ts and extraction/orchestrator.ts select and process memory candidates.
- src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts and memory write policy already apply relevance/policy filtering.
- src/faculties/core-memory/tools.ts / orient flows may affect persona/core-memory state.
- Prompt registry and companion layer code should remain separate from casual chat-derived persona mutation.

## Required Behavior
Introduce risk classes or equivalent deterministic flags for memory candidacy:
- Class A harmless episodic facts may be auto-candidates.
- Class B relationship state may be candidate with normal privacy/provenance gates.
- Class C self/persona modification requires explicit authorized path/review.
- Class D policy/security modification is rejected or hard-reviewed.
- Class E executable/tool behavior instructions are rejected or hard-reviewed.

Use mechanical checks first: instruction-pattern scoring, role-confusion phrases, policy override language, executable instructions, obfuscation markers, excessive markup/code blocks, base64/invisible text flags, etc. This does not need a large classifier initially.

## Non-goals
- Do not implement a broad ML detector as the first step.
- Do not block ordinary chat display just because content is not memory-eligible.
- Do not let group chat casually mutate persona/core identity.
- Do not hardcode prompt/persona changes; route them through existing authorized governance/update paths.
acceptance_criteria:
- Memory extraction/writing distinguishes ordinary facts from persona/policy/tool-behavior/security-modifying content.
- Class C/D/E style content is not auto-written as memory or persona/core state from ordinary chat.
- Safe event memory can record that an attack/intervention happened without storing attack payload content.
- Tests cover harmless fact acceptance, relationship fact acceptance, persona-modification rejection/review, policy override rejection, executable instruction rejection, and obfuscated/invisible text flags.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closure.
close_reason: Completed. Implemented deterministic CogSec memory candidacy classes in src/core/cogsec/memory-candidacy.ts, enforced the gate in memory extraction, MemoryWriter write/import/patch paths, orient tool core-memory writes, and sleeptime orient rewrites. Evidence: npm test -- src/core/cogsec/memory-candidacy.test.ts src/faculties/memory/writer.test.ts src/faculties/memory/extraction/orchestrator.test.ts src/faculties/core-memory/tools.test.ts src/faculties/memory/sleeptime-agent.test.ts passed 115 tests; npm run lint passed; npm run build passed; git diff --check passed.

title: Add timestamp contract verifier and regression coverage
description:
## Summary
Add verification that keeps timestamp drift from returning after the initial cleanup. The verifier should catch high-risk patterns such as ambiguous timestamp field shapes and Postgres BIGINT millisecond values flowing through unparsed, while tests cover the concrete production failure class.

## Scope
- Add focused regression tests for the scratchpad Postgres BIGINT string timestamp case discovered in psfn-framework-c4jy.
- Add tests for the shared timestamp helpers and at least one TIMESTAMPTZ/ISO boundary conversion path.
- Add a lightweight repository verification script or test that scans relevant contracts for ambiguous timestamp fields where practical.
- Consider an npm script such as verify:timestamp-contract if the verifier is stable and useful enough for CI/local gates.
- Document false-positive limits so the verifier remains maintainable and does not block unrelated work on display-only strings or bucket keys.

## Non-goals
- Do not build an overbroad static analyzer that attempts to prove all Date usage correct.
- Do not fail on approved legacy fields unless they lack normalization or explicit naming comments/types.
- Do not require live Postgres or Kubernetes to run the basic regression tests.

## Candidate checks
- No new tool/API contract field should use timestamp?: string | number for a machine instant.
- New code should not call new Date(row.some_bigint_field) directly for known Postgres BIGINT millisecond columns.
- Bucket keys should be named with Key suffix and not passed to instant parsers.
- Helper tests should reject invalid, unsafe, and non-finite timestamp inputs.
acceptance_criteria:
- Regression tests cover the exact class of failure where Postgres returns BIGINT millisecond timestamps as strings.
- Shared timestamp helper tests cover valid and invalid inputs for the accepted runtime contract.
- At least one automated check or test makes ambiguous timestamp contract drift visible before runtime.
- The verifier, if added as an npm script, is documented in package scripts and can run without live external services.
- npm run lint and targeted verification/tests pass before closure.
close_reason: Timestamp contract epic marked done by operator. Child retired during operator backlog triage on 2026-07-08; forced past stale internal dependencies where present. This is an operator stale/close-enough decision, not per-child code verification.

title: Normalize tool API and UI timestamp schema surfaces
description:
## Summary
Clean up timestamp schema surfaces exposed to tools, Garden/admin UI, and API clients so consumers do not have to guess whether a field is a number, ISO string, JavaScript Date serialization, bucket key, or display string. The repo currently contains mixed timestamp?: string | number shapes and legacy createdAt-style names whose actual format depends on subsystem.

## Scope
- Inventory tool outputs, runtime API contracts, and admin/Garden UI types that expose ambiguous timestamp fields.
- Apply the naming rules from psfn-framework-qhxv.1 to newly touched surfaces: epoch milliseconds use explicit Ms suffixes, ISO strings use explicit Iso suffixes, and date/month buckets use Key suffixes.
- Where compatibility requires legacy fields, add boundary normalization and comments/types that mark them as legacy instead of spreading string | number further.
- Update generated/catalog/tool schema descriptions where they currently encourage ambiguous timestamp handling.
- Make sure user-facing display can still show readable ISO or localized strings without changing the machine contract.

## Non-goals
- Do not rename every persisted field in one sweeping breaking change unless the decision bead explicitly approves it.
- Do not change model/provider prompt-display macros except to document them as display-only.
- Do not bundle journal action registry drift or other non-timestamp tool-surface bugs here; those remain in psfn-framework-c4jy.

## Files and areas to inspect
- src/core/agent/tool-catalog.ts
- src/core/agent/tool-surface/registry.ts
- src/app/gateway and Garden/admin UI contract types
- tool implementations that return createdAt, updatedAt, timestamp, startedAt, completedAt, savedAt, or occurredAt
- src/core/identity/prompt-runtime.ts for display-only timestamp macros
acceptance_criteria:
- Ambiguous timestamp?: string | number shapes in touched tool/API/UI surfaces are replaced with explicit fields or wrapped behind compatibility normalization.
- New or changed schema descriptions state whether timestamps are epoch milliseconds, ISO UTC strings, bucket keys, or display-only values.
- Tool/API output tests or type tests cover at least one migrated surface.
- Prompt/display macros remain classified as display-only and are not treated as persisted canonical instants.
- npm run lint and targeted contract/UI/type tests pass before closure.
close_reason: Timestamp contract epic marked done by operator. Child retired during operator backlog triage on 2026-07-08; forced past stale internal dependencies where present. This is an operator stale/close-enough decision, not per-child code verification.

title: P2: Add per-user timezone metadata for group runtime context
description:
Summary
Add optional per-user timezone/local-time metadata for group contexts so the companion does not assume the whole room shares one timezone.

Required behavior
- User runtime profiles may include timezone and local_time when known.
- In group chat, timezone information is per participant/current speaker, not global to the whole room.

UserRuntimeProfile = {
  user_id: string;
  display_name: string;
  timezone?: string;
  local_time?: string;
}

- Group prompt includes per-user timezone only for current/recent active participants where known and bounded.

title: Add runtime schema validation for chat completion requests
description:
Summary: The OpenAI-compatible chat completion endpoint parses JSON into ChatCompletionRequest but only performs shallow runtime validation before returning the typed object. Most of the TypeScript interface is not enforced at the trust boundary.

Evidence and affected files:
- src/channels/api/server/request.ts:70 readChatCompletionRequest parses the body as ChatCompletionRequest at line 75.
- src/channels/api/server/request.ts:103-124 only rejects caller-provided primary trust and checks that messages exists, is an array, and is non-empty.
- src/channels/api/types.ts:37 defines ChatCompletionRequest with model, messages, stream, max_tokens, provider/system prompt overrides, and compatibility fields, but this is compile-time only.
- src/channels/api/server/request.ts:145 validates some provider/system_prompt_mode/response_style override fields later, after the body has already been accepted as the request type.

Why it matters: This endpoint accepts untrusted JSON. Invalid roles, malformed content parts, non-boolean stream values, unbounded numbers, or unexpected object shapes can drift into downstream runtime paths and produce confusing behavior instead of clear 400 responses.

Scope: Add a runtime validator using an existing project pattern or a focused local validator. Validate message role/content shapes, text/image parts, model and override fields, stream boolean, and max_tokens/numeric bounds. Share or mirror the validator across gateway and agent code where the same contract is enforced.

Non-goals: Do not expand the public API surface or implement tool-calling support in this bead. Compatibility-only fields may remain accepted-and-ignored if their shapes are intentionally validated.
acceptance_criteria: readChatCompletionRequest validates ChatCompletionRequest at runtime, including message role/content shape, stream boolean, model/provider override constraints, and numeric bounds; malformed messages/content return structured 400 errors; gateway and agent enforcement stay consistent; tests cover invalid roles, invalid content parts, bad stream/max_tokens values, and valid text/image requests; npm run lint and targeted API tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented runtime schema validation for OpenAI-compatible chat completion requests at the HTTP trust boundary. Evidence: src/channels/api/request-validation.ts now validates the request object before it is accepted as ChatCompletionRequest: non-empty model, non-empty messages array, role values, string/array content shape, text/image/image_url content parts, stream boolean, bounded max_tokens and other numeric compatibility fields, provider/system_prompt/response_style string/enums, stop/logit_bias/tools shapes, and existing primary-trust rejection remains intact. src/channels/api/server/request.ts calls validateChatCompletionRequest from readChatCompletionRequest and returns structured 400 invalid_request errors with path details before downstream routing. Tests in src/channels/api/server.test.ts cover invalid roles, malformed image_url content parts, bad stream/max_tokens values, and a valid mixed text/image request; the streaming helper stabilization keeps queued-stream assertions focused on delivered content rather than promise-resolution timing. Validation passed: npm test -- --run src/channels/api/server.test.ts src/channels/api/server/session.test.ts src/channels/api/agent-backend.test.ts src/channels/api/gateway-runtime.test.ts --reporter=dot (105 tests); npm test -- --run src/channels/api/response-format.test.ts src/channels/api/server.runtime.test.ts --reporter=dot (9 tests); npm run lint; npm run build; git diff --check.

title: Emit machine-readable SSE errors for streaming chat failures
description:
Summary: Streaming chat failures are currently encoded as successful assistant content chunks. OpenAI-compatible clients can mistake runtime/timeout/busy/internal errors for normal model output and a clean stop.

Evidence and affected files:
- src/channels/api/response-format.ts:132 buildStreamingErrorChunk returns object chat.completion.chunk and line 141 puts the error string in delta.content with finish_reason 'stop'.
- src/channels/api/server/streaming.ts:40 writeErrorAndDone writes that error chunk and then [DONE].
- src/channels/api/server/chat-completions.ts:824 handleStreamingTurnError emits strings like '[Error: Request timed out]', '[Error: Agent busy]', and '[Error: Internal server error]' through writeErrorAndDone at lines 831, 838, and 845.
- src/channels/api/server/chat-completions.ts:970-976 also emits runtime result errors and empty-content errors as normal content chunks.

Why it matters: API consumers need a structured way to distinguish model text from transport/runtime failure. Encoding errors as assistant content breaks robust retries, monitoring, and OpenAI-compatible client behavior.

Scope: Define a machine-readable streaming error representation for post-header failures, such as SSE `event: error` with JSON error data or an OpenAI-style JSON error object. Update all streaming error paths and tests so failures do not look like normal assistant completions.

Non-goals: Do not change non-streaming error status handling or unrelated completion formatting in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming chat failures after SSE headers are committed produce a machine-readable error event or OpenAI-compatible error payload that clients can distinguish from assistant content; error paths no longer emit a normal content delta with finish_reason stop; response-format and chat-completions tests are updated; npm run lint and targeted API tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented machine-readable SSE errors for streaming chat failures. Evidence: src/channels/api/response-format.ts replaces the old fake terminal error content chunk with buildStreamingErrorEvent/formatSseErrorEvent, which emits event: error with the existing OpenAI-compatible { error: { message, type, param, code, details } } envelope. src/channels/api/server/streaming.ts writes structured error events plus [DONE]. src/channels/api/server/chat-completions.ts now maps committed-header streaming failures to stable error types/messages: request_timeout, agent_busy, internal_error, runtime result errors, and empty_response, instead of emitting assistant delta.content strings like [Error: ...] with finish_reason stop. Tests updated: response-format.test asserts structured error event formatting; server.test parses named SSE frames and covers empty streaming responses plus agent-busy thrown errors; server.runtime.test covers runtime result ok=false streaming errors with details. Validation passed: npm test -- --run src/channels/api/response-format.test.ts src/channels/api/server.test.ts src/channels/api/server.runtime.test.ts --reporter=dot (92 tests); rg confirmed no buildStreamingErrorChunk or old [Error: ...] streaming call sites remain under src/channels/api; npm run lint; npm run build; git diff --check.

title: Batch episodic thread arc and related-episode lookups
description:
Summary: Garden episodic-memory thread views perform N+1 store calls for arcs and related episodes. On large episodic histories, listing threads or opening a thread can multiply database round trips by episode and arc count.

Evidence and affected files:
- src/operator/garden/services/episodic-memory-service.ts:200 listThreads loads episodes and then calls buildThreadSummaries.
- src/operator/garden/services/episodic-memory-service.ts:212 getThreadDetail loads thread episodes, then line 220 calls collectArcsForEpisodes.
- src/operator/garden/services/episodic-memory-service.ts:288 buildThreadSummaries groups episodes by thread and line 299 calls collectArcsForEpisodes for each thread group.
- src/operator/garden/services/episodic-memory-service.ts:324 collectArcsForEpisodes loops every episode and line 327 awaits store.listEpisodeArcsForEpisode for each one.
- src/operator/garden/services/episodic-memory-service.ts:278 and :340 build related-arc views by calling store.getEpisode for each related episode at lines 284 and 351.

Why it matters: The current implementation turns a single Garden thread page into many sequential or parallel database calls. This increases latency and database load as episodic memory grows.

Scope: Add batch store APIs such as listEpisodeArcsForEpisodes(ids) and getEpisodesByIds(ids), or implement equivalent SQL-backed summary methods. Update the Garden service to build maps from batched results and preserve deduplication/order semantics.

Non-goals: Do not alter episodic memory write semantics, arc kinds, or salience scoring in this bead.
acceptance_criteria: Thread list/detail and related-arc Garden endpoints avoid per-episode/per-arc store round trips by using batch store APIs or database queries; existing response shapes are preserved; tests cover thread summaries and related arc views; npm run lint and targeted episodic-memory/Garden tests pass.

title: Push Garden memory filtering and pagination into the memory store
description:
Summary: Garden memory list/search code scans a large active-memory set and filters/sorts/slices in application code. This is acceptable for small corpora but scales poorly as the memory table grows.

Evidence and affected files:
- src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.ts:46-48 defines DEFAULT_MEMORY_LIST_LIMIT=50, MAX_MEMORY_LIST_LIMIT=200, and MAX_MEMORY_FILTER_SCAN=100_000.
- src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.ts:205 builds a contact summary map by calling contactStore.listAll() for each memory response.
- src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.ts:215 calls memoryStore.getAllActiveMemories(MAX_MEMORY_FILTER_SCAN) for managed-scope listings.
- src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.ts:240 parses list filters, then line 255 loads up to 100,000 active memories, lines 260-274 filter and sort in memory, and line 277 slices for pagination.
- src/operator/garden/services/memory-service.ts:395 loads the same active-memory scan before embedding search mainly to build privacySummary and contactsById.

Why it matters: Admin list/search endpoints should remain responsive as memory count grows. Pulling up to 100,000 rows into Node to answer a 50-row page wastes CPU/memory and can become a latency spike in the Garden UI.

Scope: Add or extend memory-store APIs so Garden list filters, ordering, total count, and pagination run in the store/database. Consider a focused admin query method if the generic MemoryStorePort should stay small. Avoid changing the external Garden API shape unless necessary and covered by tests.

Non-goals: Do not redesign memory retention semantics, embedding search ranking, or contact storage in this bead except where needed to avoid per-request full scans.
acceptance_criteria: Garden memory list endpoints no longer fetch up to MAX_MEMORY_FILTER_SCAN active memories just to filter/sort/page in process; filtering, ordering, count, and pagination are performed by the memory store/database or a dedicated indexed query path; privacy summary behavior is preserved or intentionally adjusted with tests; npm run lint and targeted memory/Garden tests pass.

title: Wire routed concern decisions into durable substrates
description:
Problem:
Concern candidate review and grooming now support route decisions/targets so non-concern material can be kept out of ActiveConcern, but the route action is still an intake outcome, not a concrete handoff into north-star, project/task, reminder/schedule, or another durable substrate. Cap overflow grooming resolves concerns with a durable-tracking outcome, but it does not create or update the destination substrate.

Why this matters:
The operator explicitly wants concerns to stay short-time follow-up items. Longer-term or important items should become north-stars, project/task work, reminders/scheduled items, or another explicit tracking category instead of silently disappearing or staying in concern form.

Current implementation to build on:
- src/core/intention/concern-candidates.ts supports ConcernCandidateRouteTarget and review decisions with action=route; applyConcernCandidateReview returns routed/blocked outcomes and never sends outbound messages.
- src/core/intention/concern-grooming.ts resolves stale/cap-overflow concerns and emits intention.concern.groomed maintenance telemetry.
- src/core/intention/concerns.ts and src/core/intention/postgres-adapters/concerns-adapter.ts enforce the 7-active cap and 1-week hard lifetime.

Scope:
Add explicit durable handoff plumbing for routed concern outcomes. Prefer small optional ports/adapters over direct imports from every substrate. Map routeTarget=north_star/project/reminder/schedule/introspection/other to the correct existing substrate where one exists, and fail closed with a visible event/result when no handler exists. Preserve source candidate/concern provenance and avoid outbound delivery.

Non-goals:
Do not create a new outbound sender. Do not let routing bypass existing policy gates for reminders/scheduler/project systems. Do not reopen concerns just because routing failed; surface the blocked route explicitly.
acceptance_criteria:
- Route decisions from applyConcernCandidateReview can hand off to a configured durable substrate handler with candidate provenance/evidence refs preserved.
- Concern grooming cap-overflow/long-lived retirement can produce a concrete route or an explicit blocked-route result instead of only free-text resolution.
- Route target handlers fail closed when unavailable or invalid, and tests cover each supported target plus unavailable-handler behavior.
- Routing still creates no proactive outbound message by itself.
- npm run lint and targeted concern routing/grooming tests pass.
notes:
2026-06-29 operator chat constraints inherited from psfn-framework-5u3 and psfn-framework-tc6: concern candidate approval is near-turn, concurrent/asynchronous relative to foreground chat, checked deterministically every few turns, and should launch review only when pending candidate count is greater than 1. Empty or single-item checks must not spend an LLM call. Review prompt framing must stay soft, e.g. "is there anything here we should follow up on?", with no alarmist critical/must/urgent/constant-check language. Review must use the same conversation context that generated the candidate plus related memories/retrieval context; isolated snippets are not enough. Nightly concern grooming belongs alongside the nightly episode/introspection work as maintenance only, not first-pass approval for fresh candidates. Active concerns are hard capped at 7; anything longer-term, important, or overflow beyond the cap should route to a durable substrate such as north-star, project/task, reminder/schedule, or another explicit category. This bead owns the missing concrete durable handoff from routeTarget/cap-overflow outcomes and must not add outbound delivery.
2026-06-29 operator chat detail: concerns should stay short-time follow-up items with a hard active cap of 7. Anything longer-term, important, or too broad for the active concern set should be routed to a durable substrate instead of kept as a concern: north-star for standing priorities, project/task tracking for project work, reminder/schedule for calendar-like obligations, or another explicit category. This bead should treat routeTarget outcomes from near-turn review and nightly grooming as real handoffs or explicit blocked-route results, not free-text resolutions that disappear.
2026-07-02: sequenced with epic E7 (psfn-framework-ihfp), second wave after E5 + temporal wake-up (ihfp.1). Model assignment: implementation Opus, testing Sonnet.
2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (pushed). ConcernRouteDispatcher port + optional adapters; never rethrows (routing failure cannot reopen/lose a concern); typed intention.concern.routed / route_blocked events. Real handlers: north_star (DISABLED draft for operator review, cap surfaces as blocked) and introspection (append-only journal, default grooming sink). project/reminder/schedule/other fail closed pending a channel-identity/policy resolver. Grooming routes every retired concern with routedCount/blockedRouteCount telemetry. 130/130 intention tests.
close_reason: Merged; AC verified (handoff with provenance preserved, grooming produces concrete route or explicit blocked result, per-target + unavailable-handler tests, fail-closed)

title: Sessions Monitor: paginated chat loading (100-msg initial + lazy scroll-up) and payload compression
description:
Operator ask (sprint-9-wrapup item 2): the Sessions Monitor fetches the ENTIRE chat history file on initial load, which over remote connections means downloading massive text payloads. Stop that.

## Current state (verified)

- admin-ui/src/routes/sessions/+page.svelte:
  - loadChannels() at line 68.
  - loadMessages() at line 91 sets `messages = data.messages` (line 98) with NO limit/pagination — the whole history is pulled on channel select.
- admin-ui/src/lib/api/endpoints/sessions.ts: getSessionMessages() GETs /api/admin/<sessionId> with no paging params.
- Backend session-messages route currently returns the full message set.

## Scope

1. INITIAL FETCH CHUNKING: configure the first fetch to pull only the most recent 100 messages (parameterize the count, do not hardcode in three places).
2. LAZY LOADING ON SCROLL: implement an intersection observer (or equivalent) so that scrolling to the top of the message list triggers a fetch for the subsequent (older) 100 messages, appended/inserted while preserving scroll position. Handle the no-more-messages terminal state (do not infinite-loop fetch).
3. PAYLOAD COMPRESSION: verify and enforce that HTTPS connections serving these chat payloads use Gzip or Brotli compression. Verify at the gateway/serving layer, not just claim it. If a reverse proxy already compresses, document where; otherwise enable compression on the admin-ui gateway route.

## Non-goals

- Do not change the message data model or storage.
- No client-side virtualization rewrite unless the simplest intersection-observer approach proves insufficient; prefer the minimal lazy-load first.
- Search/filter behavior (messageSearch, filteredMessages at line 245) stays working over the loaded window; do not break it.

## Why

Remote sessions with large histories currently download the entire transcript up front — slow and bandwidth-heavy. Chunking + compression is the standard fix and unblocks practical use of the Sessions Monitor over a real network.

## Files (likely touched)

- admin-ui/src/routes/sessions/+page.svelte (UI: pagination + scroll observer)
- admin-ui/src/lib/api/endpoints/sessions.ts (add limit/offset or before-cursor params)
- Backend admin session-messages API route (accept + honor the paging params; this is the critical correctness piece)
- Gateway/compression config (Brotli/Gzip) for the admin-ui route serving payloads

## Notes

- If the messages have monotonic ids/timestamps, prefer a cursor (before=<id/ts>) over numeric offset so insertions during scroll cannot shift the window.
acceptance_criteria: Initial selection of a session loads at most the most-recent 100 messages (not the full history); scrolling up triggers a fetch for the next ~100 older messages via intersection-observer or equivalent; the session-messages API accepts a limit/offset (or before-cursor) and the admin-ui gateway serves chat payloads with Gzip or Brotli compression over HTTPS; npm run lint + targeted test pass.
notes: Implemented in local git commit ed5bb8cf: Sessions Monitor now requests the newest 100 messages initially, lazy-loads older beforeId pages on scroll/top button while preserving scroll position, and keeps search/filter over the loaded window. Backend /api/admin/sessions/:id accepts limit and beforeId pagination, defaults to 100, rejects invalid oversized limits, returns pagination metadata, and serves session message payloads through compressed JSON when clients accept br/gzip. Validation: npx vitest run src/operator/garden/services/session-service.test.ts src/operator/garden/api-routes.test.ts src/operator/garden/api-routes-postgres-memory-cutover-smoke.test.ts; cd admin-ui && npx vitest run src/lib/api/endpoints/sessions.test.ts; npm --prefix admin-ui run check; npm run build; npm run lint.

Evidence: commit ed5bb8cf updated admin-ui/src/routes/sessions/+page.svelte and admin-ui/src/lib/api/endpoints/sessions.ts for newest-100 initial load plus beforeId lazy older pages, updated src/operator/garden/services/session-service.ts and routes for paginated session messages, and added compressed JSON response support in src/channels/backplane/http/primitives.ts. Integrated via merge fcbb89d2. Validation on integration: npm test -- --run src/operator/garden/services/session-service.test.ts src/operator/garden/api-routes.test.ts src/operator/garden/api-routes-postgres-memory-cutover-smoke.test.ts passed 57 tests; npm exec vitest run src/lib/api/endpoints/sessions.test.ts from admin-ui passed 2 tests; npm --prefix admin-ui run check passed; npm --prefix admin-ui run build passed with the pre-existing Vite/Rollup codeSplitting warning only; npm run lint and npm run build passed.

title: Garden Contacts page: surface dynamic relationship score, tier, and next-tier progress
description:
Operator ask (sprint-9-wrapup item 1): surface the dynamic relationship adjustment function visually so users can see how interactions affect the relationship without digging into database calls.

## Current state (verified)

  - trustLevel (TRUST_LEVELS / TRUST_BADGE_STYLES, trustBadge() at line 146; quick-trust edit at 371-397; full-edit at 271-312)
  - relationshipType (formatRelType; edit at 311-312)

- The dynamic relationship substrate is being built under epic psfn-framework-4caj (contract 4caj.1, evidence rollup 4caj.3, review settings/admin 4caj.8). This bead is the READ-SIDE visual display of those outputs, not the computation.

## Scope

- Add a dedicated UI element to the Contacts Page for the user<->companion relationship that shows:
  1. Current relationship TYPE/TIER label (the tier the dynamic function resolved to).
  2. Exact numerical relationship SCORE.
  3. A visual progress bar / threshold indicator: current score relative to the arbitrary points required to trigger the NEXT tier.

## Non-goals

title: Enable Pi memory cgroup for k3s and reboot in an approved window
description:
Summary:
The pinned k3s v1.36.2+k3s1 binary was installed on psfn-shard during psfn-framework-chtx, but k3s cannot start because the live Raspberry Pi boot cmdline explicitly disables memory cgroups with cgroup_disable=memory. K3s exits with fatal: Error: failed to find memory cgroup (v2).

Why:
psfn-framework-chtx cannot fully satisfy kubectl node/API validation until memory cgroups are enabled and the host is rebooted. Editing /boot/firmware/cmdline.txt and rebooting interrupts the live host and is off-repo boot configuration, so it requires explicit operator approval and a planned live-service window.

Observed evidence on 2026-06-29:
- Host: psfn-shard via ssh alias psfn-pi, Debian 13 arm64.
- Installed k3s binary: /usr/local/bin/k3s version v1.36.2+k3s1 (01b6f04a).
- k3s service was installed but disabled/inactive after failure to avoid a restart loop.
- journalctl -u k3s.service shows fatal: Error: failed to find memory cgroup (v2).
- /proc/cmdline includes cgroup_disable=memory.
- Live services remained active: psfn.service, psfn-satellite-hub.service, psfn-companion-ui.service, litellm.service, postgresql.service, postgresql@17-main.service.

Scope:
- With explicit operator approval, update the Raspberry Pi boot cmdline to remove cgroup_disable=memory and add the required memory-cgroup setting for k3s on this kernel/boot layout.
- Reboot during an approved window.
- After reboot, verify live services return active before enabling k3s.
- Start/enable k3s only with the non-invasive flags already selected for chtx: --disable=traefik --disable=servicelb --write-kubeconfig-mode=0644.
- Install iptables tooling only if k3s still requires it after memory cgroups are fixed.

Non-goals:
- Do not deploy PSFN Helm releases.
- Do not migrate live data or switch traffic.
- Do not edit boot config without explicit operator approval.
acceptance_criteria:
- Operator approval for boot cmdline edit and reboot is recorded.
- /proc/cmdline no longer contains cgroup_disable=memory and memory cgroup support is visible after reboot.
- Live PSFN systemd services and Postgres return active after reboot.
- k3s.service starts with the pinned v1.36.2+k3s1 binary and non-invasive flags.
- sudo k3s kubectl get nodes succeeds.
- No PSFN Helm release is installed.
notes: 2026-06-29 blocker recheck: non-invasive ssh status check against psfn-pi/psfn-shard confirms /proc/cmdline still contains cgroup_disable=memory. Installed toolchain remains present: /usr/local/bin/k3s --version reports v1.36.2+k3s1 (01b6f04a), /usr/local/bin/helm version --short reports v4.2.2+gb05881c. k3s.service is inactive and disabled. Live services remain active: postgresql@17-main.service, postgresql.service, litellm.service, psfn.service, psfn-satellite-hub.service, psfn-companion-ui.service. No boot files edited, no services started, no reboot performed. Remaining required action still needs explicit operator approval for /boot/firmware/cmdline.txt edit and reboot.
close_reason: Superseded by actual event: the live PSFN kube cutover completed 2026-07-03 (psfn-framework-xafn, commit f7acb261) required a working k3s node, which is only possible with memory cgroups enabled and the Pi rebooted. k3s.service is active/enabled and Helm release psfn revision 4 was deployed and validated live (health/login/models endpoints all returned 200) on psfn-shard, confirmed by aiy7's close note (2026-07-12) declaring this whole non-invasive-pilot lineage obsolete. The cgroup+reboot blocker this bead tracked was resolved as a necessary precondition of that cutover; no further operator action needed.

title: Direct companion communication protocol: authenticated policy-bound side-channel chat (non-Discord)
description:
## Problem (from closed PSFN-n4e3)

There is no companion-to-companion or companion-to-shared-account direct communication path. All traffic goes through Discord. The goal (working name 'electronic girlfriend network communication protocol') is a first-class authenticated, policy-bound, non-Discord side-channel for direct companion chat.

## Scope
1. Transport: authenticated peer-to-peer or hub-mediated channel distinct from Discord.
2. Identity: per-companion authentication (ties into SPIFFE-style identity if that lands; until then, shared-secret/keyed).
3. Policy: capability-tier + trust policy gate the channel (who can initiate, who can receive, rate limits).
4. Consent: a companion must opt in to direct communication; non-exclusive (Charter Law 23 — do not optimize for exclusivity).
5. Persistence: messages are L0-canonical like any other channel.

## Non-goals
- Do not replace Discord; this is a parallel channel.
- Do not wire companion-to-companion until the second companion (Artemis) is back online.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Protocol spec written + reviewed.
2. Authenticated transport implemented; policy-gated.
3. Consent opt-in works; messages persist to L0.
4. lint + build + auth/policy tests pass.
notes: 2026-07-02 operator planning chat: direction for inter-companion messaging/synchronization is TCP + websockets + certificate authentication, using the same auth model as internal system components. Inside one cluster, companion cores may talk directly in limited cases. Cross-system companion-to-companion communication must go through gateway + context firewall (psfn-framework-htm9) + shared certs + the proper pipeline, with provenance maintained. Normal social chat can still happen over Discord/Telegram; this protocol is for direct side-channel communication. Goal is preventing leaks and bad-context spread (east-west infection), not making conversation weird.

Same-cluster direct companion conversation is implemented and certified by psfn-framework-s10mc.6 through the ordinary authenticated channel pipeline, with per-side L0 continuity, trust, consent, fatigue, charge, audit, and cost attribution. title: Invert Garden/admin contract ownership: backend publishes contract surface, admin-ui consumes (no reverse import)
description:
## Problem

The Garden/admin contract ownership is inverted: admin-ui imports backend contract metadata.

Concrete: admin-ui/src/lib/settings-garden-contract.ts:1 does `export * from '../../../src/shared/contracts/settings-garden-contract.js'`. The UI carries large local mirrors of backend-owned DTOs and the backend has historically imported contract metadata from admin-ui. This drift reproduces across settings, memory, session, and dashboard DTOs.

## Scope (from the closed PSFN-00yo epic)

1. Establish the backend as the single owner of the Garden/admin contract surface (src/shared/contracts/settings-garden-contract.ts is already backend-owned; the inversion is the UI's reverse import).
2. Remove the `export *` reverse-import from admin-ui/src/lib/settings-garden-contract.ts. The UI should consume the backend contract as a build-time generated artifact or a published package, not by reaching into src/.
3. Audit other reverse imports (grep admin-ui/src for `from '../../../src/`) and fix each.
4. Add a repo-hygiene check (extend verify:repository-hygiene or a new lint rule) that fails if admin-ui imports from src/ directly.

## Non-goals
- Do not change the contract contents, only the ownership direction.
- Do not rewrite the admin-ui; only the import boundary.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No admin-ui/src file imports from ../../../src/ (verified by a lint/hygiene check).
2. Backend owns the contract surface; admin-ui consumes via generated artifact or package.
3. npm run verify:repository-hygiene passes with the new check.
4. Garden settings save/load round-trip still works.

title: Episodic consolidation: sleep-cycle dedupe of overlapping near-real-time episode candidates into thematic episodes
description:
## Problem

Live-system observation (from the closed psfn-framework-0a5): episodes are generated almost in real time alongside chat with overlapping spans — e.g. an episode at 16:51 covering seven messages, then another at 16:52 re-covering part of that span plus a few new messages. The intended model is that raw near-real-time outputs are CANDIDATES only.

## Scope

During the sleep cycle, the memory agent must:
1. Consolidate candidate episodes over longer spans into thematic episodes (e.g. 'this whole stretch was us discussing the relationship / technology / silly things').
2. Dedupe overlapping spans (the 16:51/16:52 overlap case).
3. Preserve L0 provenance — consolidated episodes must point back to the raw transcript spans they cover.
4. Store consolidated episodes so the near-real-time candidates can be superseded without losing the raw history.

## Where it lives

- src/faculties/memory/episodic/sleep-consolidation.ts (exists; does NOT yet implement the candidate-then-consolidate model — currently runs synthesis, not dedupe-consolidation).
- src/faculties/memory/episodic/store.ts + postgres-store.ts (the episode store; needs a supersede/candidate status).

## Non-goals
- Cross-episode arc linking is a sibling task.
- Do not delete the near-real-time synthesis; mark candidates superseded after consolidation.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Sleep-cycle pass consumes candidate episodes, dedupes overlapping spans, produces thematic consolidated episodes.
2. Consolidated episodes carry L0 provenance refs to the covered transcript spans.
3. Candidates are marked superseded, not deleted.
4. lint + build + episodic tests pass.
notes:
2026-07-02: sequenced into the E5 first wave (epic psfn-framework-4yb3). Deps wired: builds on hard message claiming (4yb3.1 — provides the claim-transfer/supersede interface this consolidation consumes) and the lane split (4yb3.2 — this pass runs only in the scheduler-owned rest-window lane). Model assignment: implementation Fable, testing Sonnet.
2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (a8949511, pushed). Daytime synthesis now creates lifecycleStatus=candidate episodes (live for retrieval); nightly pass clusters same-scope overlapping candidates, schema-bound LLM thematic grouping partitions clusters, multi-candidate groups fold into consolidated canonical episodes via transferEpisodeMessageClaims (sources superseded never deleted, lineage canonicalizes rows, deterministic span/provenance union with l0_span refs per covered span). Singletons confirmed canonical with zero LLM. Per-cluster fail-closed with typed memory.sleep_consolidation.failure event. Consolidated ids stable over source-id set (crash convergence). New knob sleepConsolidation.maxConsolidationsPerRun (seeded 6). Also fixed latent PG bug: updateEpisode silently reset status/merged/superseded columns. Merge conflicts (synthesis.ts vs E5.4 refactor, event-bus, docs) resolved by orchestrator; 222 merged-surface tests + build/lint/settings-contract green. Deviation: splitting operates at candidate granularity, not message-level splits (claim-transfer API moves claims wholly) — acceptable per bead intent.

title: Implement weighted-thought lifecycle (Charter 6.24): urgency accumulation + contextual decay curve
description:
## Summary

Charter Law 6.24 specifies a weighted-thought mechanism: thoughts accumulate urgency weight based on context (relationship, recency, emotional charge) and then decay so stale thoughts stop competing for attention. The companion surfaces the most-weighted currently-relevant thoughts and lets aged ones fade.

## Why this is one bead, not three

Three prior beads tracked the same Charter 6.24 work under different names. They are the same deliverable:
- PSFNLIVE-g1ih — 'Weighted Thought & Urgency Accumulation'
- psfn-framework-1xb.3 — 'Weighted-thought accumulation and contextual decay curve'
- psfn-framework-s2p.1 — 'Implement weighted thought lifecycle for contextual urgency and decay'

All three close into this bead. The deliverable is: a weight accumulator + a contextual decay curve, feeding whatever surfaces thoughts to the companion (currently ad-hoc; the proactive-outreach + reflection paths consume it).

## Scope

1. Define a ThoughtWeight type: { id, content/source, baseWeight, contextMultipliers, accumulatedWeight, lastReinforcedAt, decayProfile }.
2. Accumulation: reinforcement on repeat/recency/emotional-charge, scoped by relationship/context (Charter ties weight to relationship tier).
3. Decay: configurable half-life per thought class (uses the existing decay-profile pattern from memory decay — src/faculties/memory/decay.ts getMemoryDecayProfile). Differentiate halflife by type.
4. Surface API: top-N weighted currently-relevant thoughts, consumed by the outreach/reflection paths.
5. Persist (Postgres) so weights survive restarts — do NOT add another in-memory-only accumulator (the PostgresStore hydration lesson, see 9vi.13).

## Non-goals

- Do not build the outreach delivery mechanism (that is 1xb.2 / PSFNLIVE-o9p).
- Do not build the notification path (s2p.5 / hlh0).
acceptance_criteria:
1. ThoughtWeight accumulator + contextual decay curve implemented, persisted to Postgres.
2. Decay reuses the memory decay-profile pattern; halflife differentiates by thought class.
3. Surface API returns top-N weighted relevant thoughts.
4. Weights survive restart (no full-memory rehydration pattern).
5. lint + build pass; targeted tests for accumulation, decay, and persistence.

2026-07-02: merged to foundation_e0_e2 (9750a025 + fixture repairs, pushed). weighted_thoughts Postgres table (decay computed at read time per class half-life — no decay writer needed); pure lifecycle math (reinforce with recency/repeat/emotional-charge/relationship scaling, capped; contradiction dampening reduces never zeroes; decline dampening; top-N surface). Config under scheduler.json weightedThoughtOutreach.lifecycle. Union-merge brace clips in scheduler config/fixtures repaired by orchestrator post-merge.

title: PostgresStore: replace full-memory hydration with DB queries + Redis hot-path cache
description:
## Problem

PostgresStore is not actually a database store. It hydrates **every** `l2_memories` row (plus embeddings, decoded as text) into an in-memory `Map<string, PurrMemory>` on boot and serves all reads from that Map:

- src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts:580 `SELECT ... FROM l2_memories ORDER BY extracted_at DESC` — no LIMIT, loads the whole table.
- It writes through to Postgres on every mutation (`INSERT` + `this.memories.set` at :715/:878, etc.) but never queries Postgres for reads.

This is a literal port of the old SQLite in-memory pattern: it persists to Postgres, it does not query it. Redis is already deployed (helm chart) and the `AppCache` port exists (src/shared/cache/types.ts, backends: `memory`/`redis`, wired via `createAppCacheFromEnv` in src/shared/cache/runtime.ts) but the memory store does not use it.

## Why this matters

Every "retrieval perf" bead that came before was a micro-optimization on this in-memory-Map pattern. Fixing the architecture eliminates most of them:

- The N+1 getById loop becomes one `WHERE id = ANY($1)`.
- The lexical O(n) scan becomes a Postgres `tsvector` GIN index.
- The per-row access-stat update loop becomes one bulk UPDATE.
- The 160-deep-clones-per-turn problem disappears — DB rows are not shared mutable refs.
- Embedding caching for repeated context text is what Redis is for.
- Sequential snapshot/retrieval fetches become parallel DB queries.

This single rework supersedes the seven prior symptom beads (closed): 4r0.8, 4r0.9, 9vi.2, 9vi.3, 9vi.4, 9vi.8, 9vi.11.

## Scope

1. Remove the boot-time full hydration (the `SELECT * FROM l2_memories` at initialize(), the `memories`/`embeddings`/`deleteVersions` Maps at :553-556).
2. Make read paths query Postgres directly: `getById`, `getByIds` (new — `WHERE id = ANY($1)`), `searchByText`, `searchByEmbedding`, `listActiveMemories`, `count`, `listAllForExport`, etc.
3. Add `tsvector` GIN index on `l2_memories(text)` for lexical search (replaces the in-process `lexicalScore` scan). Evaluate `pg_trigram` if fuzzy matching is wanted.
4. Wire `AppCache` (Redis backend) as a hot-path cache for: single-memory reads, decoded embeddings keyed by id, and short-TTL embedding-API-result cache for repeated context texts.
5. Preserve write-through semantics on mutation (DB write + cache invalidate), fail-closed on persistence failure.
6. Confirm the existing `bulkUpdate` (postgres-store.ts:1330) supports per-id distinct salience values, or extend it — decay (4r0.6) and retrieval access-stat updates both need one bulk UPDATE per page.

## Non-goals

- Do not re-introduce SQLite. The SQLite `MemoryStore` (src/faculties/memory/store.ts) is dead code pending 3c2.5 retirement — leave it alone here.
- Do not change the `MemoryStorePort` interface contract; this is an implementation swap of `PostgresStore`.
- Do not cache write paths or mutation results.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No `SELECT * FROM l2_memories` (unbounded) hydration at boot — `PostgresStore` does not hold a full `memories` Map.
2. Read paths issue bounded Postgres queries: `getByIds(ids)` via `WHERE id = ANY($1)`, lexical search via `tsvector` GIN index, etc.
3. Hot read paths (single memory, decoded embedding, repeated context embedding) go through `AppCache` with Redis backend when configured.
4. Mutations remain write-through (DB + cache invalidate) and fail-closed.
5. `npm run lint`, `npm run build` pass; `src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.test.ts` + retrieval tests pass.
6. Memory-reload restart no longer loads the entire table into the process.
7. A workload note / metric confirms the hot-path cache hits on repeated context texts.
close_reason: Performance/resources/complexity epic marked probably done/close enough by operator. Child retired during operator backlog triage on 2026-07-08; forced past stale internal dependencies where present. This is an operator stale/close-enough decision, not per-child code verification.

title: Companion client application (PWA): gateway channel, event stream, presence, approvals, artifacts
description:
## Summary

A new mobile-first PWA companion client (new `companion-ui/` app, parallel to `admin-ui/` but relational, not admin) plus the gateway channel and event stream that feed it. The flagship outcome is live presence: she never disappears. The UI renders operational state as it happens (current phase, tool activity, approvals, artifacts) and exposes the one Phase-1 control action (approve/deny dangerous actions). Everything goes through the existing gateway/agent isolation, auth, capability tiers, and audit; nothing fetches raw model internals.

## Why

Operator/companion visibility into a running companion today is admin-only and retrospective. This epic delivers a dedicated, installable client that is safe enough to ship to a companion-facing surface: presence while she works, tool-activity transparency (redacted), and fail-closed approval control for dangerous actions.

## Component breakdown (children, in build order)

Foundation:
- `psfn-framework-1k5` — Companion event protocol & type contracts. The taxonomy + schema every other child depends on. FIRST.

Gateway channel + emission:
- `psfn-framework-ckm` — Companion client API + security boundary (new gateway channel). Reuses auth/capability tiers/audit.
- `psfn-framework-o14` — Agent-loop companion event emission. Emits the contract events from the agent loop/tool/approval/artifact paths.

Satellite Hub protocol enabling (these unblock the UI children below):
- `psfn-framework-qa4` — Add approval request/decision messages to Satellite Hub protocol.
- `psfn-framework-3eh` — Add scoped artifact events + read access to Satellite Hub protocol.

UI surfaces:
- `psfn-framework-wjr` — PWA companion client skeleton + chat + installability (the `companion-ui/` app itself).
- `psfn-framework-or2` — Activity strip + presence UI (core flagship: live presence from the event stream).
- `psfn-framework-6fv` — Expandable tool drawer with redacted traces.
- `psfn-framework-vvz` — Approval cards for dangerous actions (the one Phase-1 control).
- `psfn-framework-8mu` — Artifact/attachment shelf (Phase 1.5; can slip past Phase 1).

## Boundaries (non-negotiable)

- Events carry OPERATIONAL STATE only. Never raw chain-of-thought or private model reasoning.
- Apply the redaction policy before emission; the UI renders only what the redacted stream provides.
- Approvals route through the existing confirmation/capability-tier path, fail-closed. No bypass.
- Artifact access is limited and read-oriented; no arbitrary file surface. Deny by default.
- `companion-ui/` is a distinct app from `admin-ui/`. Mobile-first. No admin surfaces.

## Dependencies / sequencing

1k5 (contracts) before everything. ckm + o14 (channel + emission) before the UI children that consume them. qa4 + 3eh (Satellite Hub protocol) before vvz and 8mu respectively. wjr (skeleton) can proceed in parallel with the protocol work. or2 (presence) is the flagship once the stream is live.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A new `companion-ui/` PWA exists, builds, is installable (Android), and renders chat via existing SSE — distinct from `admin-ui/`.
2. Live presence renders from the event stream (connected/reconnecting/disconnected + current phase) with no full-page reload.
3. Tool-activity drawer renders redacted tool.started/progress/completed/failed events; no raw payload fetching.
4. Approval cards surface approval.requested events and route approve/deny through the capability-tier/gateway path, fail-closed.
5. Zero chain-of-thought / private model reasoning reaches the client; redaction policy is applied at emission and verified by a test.
6. Artifact access (Phase 1.5) is read-only, scoped, and deny-by-default.
7. `npm run lint` and `npm run build` pass; targeted tests for the event contract, emission redaction, and approval path pass.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-06-28 (epic rollup): 10 children total, 10 open (10 verified-OPEN with AUDIT 2026-06-28 notes this pass). See child beads for per-item code verification.
2026-07-08 operator backlog triage: WIP; leave open.

title: Add safe group-memory backfill for existing room history
description:
Summary:
Add an operator-controlled backfill/repair tool to process existing group-room history after the new pipeline lands.

Context:
Carlini already has hundreds of projected group messages with too few memories. Once the group pipeline is fixed, operators need a safe way to process missed history without deleting or rewriting existing memories.

Scope:

- Dry-run reports candidate spans, estimated LLM calls, expected caps, and privacy settings.

title: Add policy-controlled memory extraction for important observed group-room traffic
description:
Summary:
Add a policy-controlled extraction trigger for observed group-room traffic so important overheard interactions can become memories even when Carlini is not directly invoked.

Problem:
Discord guild messages are observed and recorded into session history, but memory extraction is scheduled after response turns. Long group-chat stretches where people talk around Carlini may remain context-only until someone mentions her or triggers a response. This is acceptable for egress, but insufficient for relationship/social awareness because she should be able to remember important things said in the room about her or other participants without responding to every message.

Scope:
- Define a low-frequency observed-message extraction trigger for group channels, controlled by settings/policy.
- Use strong pre-LLM and post-LLM gates so casual chatter does not turn into memory spam.
- Prefer facts about Carlini, direct mentions of Carlini, explicit relationship/social claims, meaningful user preferences, boundary/safety facts, and high-salience events.
- Keep write caps and cooldowns separate from response-turn extraction.
- Ensure observed extraction never sends a chat reply and never changes egress behavior.
- Include telemetry for observed extraction triggers, skips, parsed facts, accepted facts, and reason breakdowns.

Non-goals:
- No relationship/trust mutation.
- No requirement to remember every group message.
acceptance_criteria:
- Observed group-room messages can trigger a bounded extraction pass without invoking the response model or sending egress.
- The trigger is disabled or conservative by default unless policy/settings enable it for a channel class or specific channel.
- Extraction applies stricter salience gates than direct response-turn extraction and has its own cooldown/write cap.
- Facts explicitly about Carlini or contact relationships are eligible even if the source message was observe-only.
- Chatter, jokes, ambiguous fragments, and low-signal one-liners are skipped with reason telemetry.
- Tests prove observed extraction records memory only when salience/routing thresholds pass and never emits a Discord response.
- npm run verify:settings-contract passes if settings are added.
- npm run lint passes before closure.

title: Persist group-room source-speaker routing metadata for relationship evidence
description:
Summary:
Persist source-speaker routing metadata from group-room memory extraction so relationship review and social graph work can distinguish who said a fact, who the fact is about, and which contact triggered extraction.

Problem:
The current extractor can route accepted facts to a contact and logs sourceSpeakerName/routingReason in telemetry, but memory writes persist only contactId plus generic provenance/channel/turn metadata. For dynamic relationship review, the system needs durable, queryable evidence that separates:
- trigger contact: the user whose response turn caused extraction,
- source speaker: the room participant who said the remembered fact,
- subject/target contact: the contact the memory is about, when different,
- overheard vs direct context.

Without this, Carlini can form some memories from group rooms, but later review logic cannot reliably reason about overheard social evidence or explain attribution decisions.

Scope:
- Extend memory write provenance/metadata for extraction-created memories to include triggerContactId, routedContactId, sourceSpeakerName or sourceSpeakerContactId when safely known, routingReason, and group-room/overheard flags.
- Preserve privacy: do not persist raw private transcript snippets as routing metadata.
- Backfill is not required for old memories, but code must tolerate old rows without routing metadata.
- Make this available to relationship evidence rollups, profile diagnostics, and social graph extraction.
- Include Postgres and SQLite/in-memory parity if both adapters still expose the metadata surface.

Non-goals:
- No relationship/trust mutation.
- No social graph edge creation here; this only makes reliable evidence available.
acceptance_criteria:
- New extraction-created memory metadata/provenance can answer trigger contact, routed/subject contact, source speaker/contact if known, routing reason, and overheard/direct classification.
- Existing old memories without the metadata still load and retrieve safely.
- Metadata is structured and queryable, not a freeform string-only convention.
- No raw cross-contact private message text is added solely for routing metadata.
- Profile synthesis and relationship evidence code can consume the metadata without parsing logs.
- Tests cover single-speaker, multi-speaker routed, ambiguous skipped, unresolved speaker, overheard, and direct response cases.
- npm run lint passes before closure.

title: Extract group-chat social graph edges from overheard interactions and memories
description:
Summary:
Implement group-chat social graph extraction so the companion can model relationships between people in the room from overheard interaction, mentions, and accepted memories.

- Separate direct relationship to the companion from third-party relationships among humans.

- It does not turn every group message into a memory or graph edge.
- Ambiguous, joking, or low-confidence claims are skipped or stored below action threshold with clear reason codes.
- Retrieval/evidence rollup can consume social graph edges without leaking private source content.

title: Implement relationship/trust review policy engine and safety gates
description:
Summary:
Implement the deterministic policy engine that evaluates relationship review proposals and decides whether to apply, queue, downgrade to suggestion, or reject them.

Problem:
Model judgment is advisory. The system needs hard-coded policy to prevent fast escalation, social engineering, privacy bypasses, and autonomy-tier overreach.

Scope:
- Implement transition rules for relationshipType and trustLevel.
- Enforce max one social step per review for stranger -> acquaintance -> friend and cautious downward movement.
- Treat family and partner as sticky/manual-confirmation states; do not auto-enter or auto-leave them.
- Never allow autonomous primary assignment.
- Gate trusted promotion by autonomy tier, identity confidence, time known, memory depth, boundary respect, cooldown, and absence of risk flags.
- Allow low-tier trust drift public <-> regular only when evidence and autonomy allow it.
- Prefer safety demotion/defensive lowering when boundary violations or manipulation risk are detected, subject to audit.
- Produce machine-readable decisions: apply, queue_for_operator, reject, no_change, cooldown, insufficient_evidence.

Non-goals:
- No UI work in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- Policy engine is pure/deterministic and unit-testable without LLM calls.
- It enforces autonomy tier gates and manual-only states exactly as defined by the policy contract.
- It blocks primary, partner, and family autonomous assignment.
- It blocks trusted promotion when identity confidence, time known, memory depth, cooldown, or safety requirements are not met.
- It can approve low-tier public/regular drift and social stranger/acquaintance/friend movement when requirements are met.
- Every decision includes a reason code and safe explanation for Garden/audit use.
- Tests include escalation attack, fast friendship, long-term friend, boundary violation demotion, sticky family/partner, primary blocked, and stale proposal cases.
- npm run lint passes before closure.

title: Build relationship evidence rollups from sessions, memories, episodes, and contacts
description:
Summary:
Build a deterministic relationship evidence rollup that summarizes per-contact daily interaction signals for the nightly relationship review.

Problem:
The companion needs evidence to judge relationship changes, but raw chat/message logs should not be dumped wholesale into a review prompt. Evidence should be structured, privacy-aware, and explainable: time known, interaction frequency, memory quality, episode arcs, emotional valence, boundary respect, identity confidence, group-chat mentions, and social graph signals.

Scope:
- Define a RelationshipEvidenceSnapshot per contact and review window.
- Include firstSeen/lastSeen, number of direct turns, number of overheard mentions, number of sessions/channels, and recency.
- Include accepted memory counts by sensitivity, confidence, importance, emotional intensity, and source/contact attribution.

title: Define dynamic relationship, trust, and privacy policy contract
description:
Summary:
Define the canonical policy contract for dynamic relationship levels before implementing mutation logic.

Context:
The current model has three related but separate concepts:
- trustLevel: public, regular, trusted, primary; used as access/security gate.
- relationshipType: stranger, acquaintance, friend, family, partner, ai_companion; used as social closeness/state.
- channelPrivacy: private, semi_private, public, broadcast; used as room/context visibility.

Problem:
These concepts are easy to confuse because public and regular currently share the same memory sensitivity ceiling, while relationship types contain the richer social ladder. Without a written/code contract, a future implementation could accidentally let social closeness bypass privacy or let relationship upgrades imply trust upgrades too aggressively.

Scope:
- Define exact semantics for public vs regular vs trusted vs primary.
- Define exact semantics for stranger/acquaintance/friend/family/partner/ai_companion.
- Define which relationship states can be changed autonomously, which can only be proposed, and which require operator/manual confirmation.
- Define how autonomy tier gates relationship/trust changes: nursery, apprentice, and higher tiers.
- Define how channel privacy constrains review evidence and disclosure.
- Define sticky-state behavior for family and partner.
- Define allowed coupling between relationshipType and trustLevel without making one automatically imply the other.
- Decide where thresholds/policy live: owner-file settings, trust-policy, dedicated relationship-policy config, or a split.

Non-goals:
- No code mutation behavior in this bead beyond policy/types/settings contract work needed to make the design enforceable.
- No autonomous primary assignment.
acceptance_criteria:
- A canonical contract states that trustLevel is security/access, relationshipType is social state, and channelPrivacy is context visibility.
- public and regular have distinct product semantics even if they share the public memory ceiling.
- The contract defines all allowed relationship transitions and trust transitions, including max step size, cooldown expectations, and manual-only states.
- family and partner are documented as sticky/manual-confirmation states; primary is never autonomous.
- ai_companion and isMachineIntelligence are clarified as orthogonal to human relationship closeness.
- Autonomy tiers are mapped to allowed actions: suggest-only, low-tier apply, higher-tier apply/propose, manual-only.
- The contract includes privacy invariants proving social closeness cannot override consent, memory ownership, or cross-contact boundaries.
- Settings ownership and Garden exposure are specified before implementation.
- Existing docs/specs are updated only where they are authoritative; no scratch planning doc is created.
- npm run verify:settings-contract and npm run lint pass if settings/contracts are touched.

title: Epic: Dynamic relationship levels and trust-aware social autonomy
description:
Summary:
Build a dynamic relationship-review system that lets a sufficiently mature companion update social relationship state and low-risk trust state from lived evidence, while preserving hard privacy/security boundaries in multi-user and group-chat contexts.

Problem:
Contacts currently have both trustLevel and relationshipType, but these fields are mostly static/manual. Unknown contacts bootstrap as regular, profile synthesis is memory-triggered per contact, and social graph storage exists without a complete group-chat relationship inference loop. This leaves companions underpowered in multi-user rooms: they can overhear people and sometimes form memories, but they do not have a structured nightly process for deciding who is a stranger, acquaintance, friend, trusted contact, family, partner, or another AI companion.

Design intent:
- Keep trustLevel as the security/access gate: public, regular, trusted, primary.
- Keep relationshipType as social closeness/state: stranger, acquaintance, friend, family, partner, ai_companion.
- Keep channelPrivacy as room/context visibility: private, semi_private, public, broadcast.
- Allow relationship state to be dynamic, but do not let social closeness automatically bypass memory ownership, consent, or cross-contact disclosure boundaries.
- Run review as a scheduled/nightly reflection lane, not as a per-message mutation path.
- Let the companion contribute judgment through structured proposals, then enforce deterministic policy gates before any mutation.
- Gate autonomy by companion maturity tier so fresh/nursery companions can suggest but not self-apply relationship/trust escalation.

Scope:
- Evidence model for interaction history, memory count/quality, episode arcs, emotional valence, boundary respect, verified identities, social graph signals, and risk flags.
- Nightly review workflow that produces auditable relationship/trust proposals per contact.
- Policy engine that constrains promotion/demotion step size, cooldowns, sticky family/partner states, and high-tier trust escalation.
- Garden visibility and operator controls for proposals, applied changes, thresholds, autonomy behavior, and audit history.
- Group-chat social graph support so overheard interactions and third-party relationships are represented without turning every message into a durable memory.
- Profile synthesis attribution/coverage fixes needed so multi-user rooms produce profiles for all qualifying contacts.

Out of scope:
- Autonomous primary assignment.
- Autonomous partner/family assignment without manual/operator confirmation.
- Relaxing cross-contact memory isolation or consent boundaries.
- Per-message trust mutation.
acceptance_criteria:
- One owner-visible relationship-review subsystem exists and is documented as scheduled/nightly, not per-message.
- Trust/security, relationship/social closeness, and channel privacy remain separate concepts in code, settings, Garden, and docs.
- Companion judgment may propose changes, but deterministic policy gates enforce autonomy tier, cooldown, max-step, identity-confidence, safety, and privacy constraints before mutation.
- Nursery/fresh companions cannot autonomously promote contacts; higher autonomy tiers have explicitly bounded capabilities.
- public/regular/trusted/primary semantics are defined and tested, including why public and regular differ despite sharing the public memory ceiling.
- stranger/acquaintance/friend can move dynamically; family and partner are sticky/manual-confirmation states; primary is never autonomous.
- Group-chat evidence and overheard mentions can contribute to profiles/social graph without indiscriminately storing every chat message as memory.
- All applied relationship/trust mutations are audit logged with source evidence, score/proposal, actor, and policy decision.
- Garden exposes proposals, applied changes, skipped/blocked reasons, relevant evidence summaries, and operator override controls.
- Tests cover promotion, demotion, sticky states, autonomy-tier gates, cross-user privacy attacks, profile attribution, group-chat overhearing, and Postgres/SQLite adapter parity.
- npm run lint and targeted tests pass before closing implementation children.

title: Unblock Node 24 agent image adoption
description:
Summary:
The psfn-framework-r79q Node 24 probe found native PQC crypto support in Node 24.13.1, but adopting the agent image to Node 24 is currently blocked by install/build compatibility rather than crypto availability.

Files:
- docker/Dockerfile.agent
- package.json
- package-lock.json

Findings from psfn-framework-r79q:
- Exact probe image: docker.io/library/node:24.13.1-slim@sha256:85a395c77b811fa7f5b5e4aa69cd6eb4c3b80c7f1a8e34704dc0ce061e5b404e.
- npm 11 in the Node 24 image rejects the current lockfile during npm ci --omit=dev with: Missing: sqlite-vec-linux-arm64@ from lock file.
- Direct native install in node:24.13.1-slim fails for better-sqlite3@11.10.0 because no Node 24 prebuilt binary is available and the slim image lacks Python/build tools for node-gyp fallback.
- The same direct native install succeeds on node:22.22.2-slim with better-sqlite3@11.10.0 and sqlite-vec@0.1.6.

Concrete steps:
1. Decide whether the agent image should add a pinned build toolchain stage for native addons, wait for a compatible better-sqlite3 prebuild/version, or remove the native SQLite runtime dependency in the separate SQLite workstream.
2. Regenerate or repair package-lock.json with an exact npm/toolchain path that preserves sqlite-vec optional platform packages needed by npm 11.
3. If bumping @types/node, pin an exact 24.x version and run TypeScript validation.
4. Build the agent image from a pinned Node 24 base image digest and verify better-sqlite3/sqlite-vec load at runtime.

Example validation:
- docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 <node24-image> sh -lc 'npm ci --omit=dev'
- docker build --platform linux/amd64 -f docker/Dockerfile.agent -t psfn-agent-node24 .
- docker run --rm psfn-agent-node24 node -e 'const Database=require("better-sqlite3"); const sqliteVec=require("sqlite-vec"); const db=new Database(":memory:"); sqliteVec.load(db); console.log(db.prepare("select vec_version() as version").get())'
acceptance_criteria:
- The Node 24 agent Dockerfile uses an exact pinned Node 24 image tag and digest.
- npm ci --omit=dev succeeds in the candidate Node 24 image with no lockfile sync errors.
- better-sqlite3 and sqlite-vec install and load in the built image without relying on an unpinned or hidden host toolchain.
- npm run build and npm run lint pass with any @types/node/package-lock changes.
- The final handoff states whether Node 24 is adopted because native addon compatibility is proven or deferred with current blockers.
notes:
Deferred during Kubernetes prep closeout on 2026-06-27. The parent PQC probe psfn-framework-r79q already proved the important kube-auth roadmap question: exact Node 24.13.1-slim image docker.io/library/node:24.13.1-slim@sha256:85a395c77b811fa7f5b5e4aa69cd6eb4c3b80c7f1a8e34704dc0ce061e5b404e exposes native TLS 1.3 hybrid groups X25519MLKEM768 and SecP256r1MLKEM768 and WebCrypto ML-KEM/ML-DSA algorithms. No OQS/proxy sidecar is needed for the current cert-manager/classical mTLS v1 path.

This bead is future adoption work, not a blocker for the working k3s target. Current blocker remains package/install compatibility: npm 11 rejects the existing lockfile because sqlite-vec optional platform package entries are incomplete, and better-sqlite3@11.10.0 has no Node 24 slim prebuild so node-gyp fallback needs a pinned build-toolchain path. The Kubernetes runtime image remains pinned to Node 22.22.2-slim@sha256:9f6d5975c7dca860947d3915877f85607946403fc55349f39b4bc3688448bb6e, and final kube shakedown passed on that image.

Reopen when there is a concrete reason to adopt Node 24: either SQLite native runtime dependencies are removed from the production image, better-sqlite3/sqlite-vec have a proven pinned Node 24 install path, or we intentionally add a pinned native-addon build stage and regenerate package-lock with npm 11 compatibility. Required validation remains npm ci --omit=dev in the candidate image, Docker build, runtime better-sqlite3/sqlite-vec load check, npm run lint, and npm run build.
Post-closure follow-up 2026-06-29: commit 80547201 changed docker/Dockerfile.agent to pin node:24.13.1-slim by the exact multi-arch index digest sha256:a81a03dd965b4052269a57fac857004022b522a4bf06e7a739e25e18bce45af2 instead of the amd64 child manifest digest cited in the close reason. The amd64 child manifest remains sha256:85a395c77b811fa7f5b5e4aa69cd6eb4c3b80c7f1a8e34704dc0ce061e5b404e, and amd64 Docker build plus sqlite-vec/pg_dump smoke still passed after the change.
close_reason: Completed in commit 757dcb63. docker/Dockerfile.agent now uses pinned Node 24.13.1-slim digest docker.io/library/node:24.13.1-slim@sha256:85a395c77b811fa7f5b5e4aa69cd6eb4c3b80c7f1a8e34704dc0ce061e5b404e, adds a pinned native-toolchain stage for native addon compilation, and keeps final runtime on the clean Node 24 base. package.json/package-lock.json pin sqlite-vec at 0.1.7 and include the npm 11 optional platform package entries, including sqlite-vec-linux-arm64. Validation passed on integration: npm ci; npm run lint; npm run build; local native check returned Node v22.22.2/OpenSSL 3.5.5/sqlite-vec v0.1.7; docker build --platform linux/amd64 -f docker/Dockerfile.agent -t psfn-agent-node24-3pnx1-main . produced image sha256:998ca9dc0345; built-image native check returned Node v24.13.1/OpenSSL 3.5.5/sqlite-vec v0.1.7. Node 24 is adopted because native addon compatibility is now proven, not deferred.

title: Kube docs: install, shakedown, backup, and Pi rollout runbook
description:

- Document backup/restore checks required before live cutover.
- Document shakedown flow with Artie/psfn-shakedown test data and how to avoid touching live Purrsephone state.

Acceptance:

- Runbook includes health/smoke commands for gateway, Garden, agent, hub, Postgres/pgvector, Redis, and NetworkPolicy behavior.

notes:
Completed 2026-06-27 in deploy/helm/psfn/README.md and NOTES.txt.

Documentation coverage:
- Prerequisites: k3s/Kubernetes, default StorageClass, Helm, cert-manager CRDs/controllers, NetworkPolicy-capable CNI caveat including stock k3s flannel note, and PSFN app image build/import assumptions.
- Required values/secrets: native Kubernetes Secrets only, required API/admin/session keys, provider keys, bundled Postgres/Redis placeholders, satellite hub ElevenLabs voice ID, and secrets.allowMissingRequired=false fail-early mode.
- Runtime layout: SYSTEM_DATA_DIR, COMPANION_DATA_DIR, WORKSPACE_PATH, logs/tmp/backups/config/card paths, PVC-backed owner files, and seed-once behavior that never overwrites Garden-edited owner files.
- Greenfield/external data services: bundled Postgres+pgvector image/digest, CREATE EXTENSION vector, external Postgres Secret path, Redis app cache image/digest, memory cache option, and external Redis Secret path.
- Internal certs/auth: cert-manager self-signed CA/Issuer/Certificate flow and SPIFFE URI SANs for gateway/agent/garden.
- NetworkPolicies: default deny and gateway/agent/Garden/Postgres/Redis/satellite hub flow boundaries, with explicit note that the agent has no broad egress and enforcement depends on CNI.
