Summary:
Define the data model and persistence contract for the new L0.1 layer that sits between raw L0 transcript history and L2 typed memory.

Why this exists:
Without a specific schema, a later worker will implement either generic chunk summaries or another vector index. L0.1 needs to represent episodes as first-class recollection anchors.

Required model properties:
- stable landmark id
- summary of the event in natural language
- why-it-matters field
- people/relationship bindings
- motif or symbol bindings (songs, places, jokes, rituals, phrases)
- occasion/recurrence anchors (birthday, anniversary, New Year, repair, first, loss, etc.)
- emotional arc or tonal metadata
- source span refs back to L0
- artifact refs (images, songs, docs, generated outputs)
- later callback refs showing that the event continued to matter
- retention / favorite / durability signals

Concrete steps:
1. Define the landmark object shape and invariants.
2. Define how landmarks point back to L0 message ranges and artifacts.
3. Decide whether storage is JSONL + mirrored table, and how it fits existing projection patterns.
4. Define fail-closed validation rules so the layer cannot store ungrounded summaries without provenance.

Acceptance:
- L0.1 schema is concrete and provenance-bearing.
- The contract makes generic summary-only storage invalid.
- Storage and mirror strategy fit existing PSFN persistence rules.
close_reason: Schema contract decided: SPEC_L01_LANDMARK_SCHEMA.md D1-D9

title: Add L0.1 episodic landmark memory layer
description:
Summary:
Add a new memory layer between canonical L0 transcript history and typed L2 memory: L0.1 episodic landmarks. This is not generic RAG, transcript chunk summaries, or another vector store. The purpose is to preserve meaningful shared episodes as durable recollection anchors that point back into raw history and related artifacts.

Why this exists:
PSFN already has canonical L0 history, selective extraction into typed L2 memory, continuity artifacts, reflection journals, cleanup, decay, dedupe, and DB-backed projections. The missing piece is a durable episodic abstraction that preserves why a stretch of history mattered. Companion failure here is not just factual miss; it is missing the emotionally important event at the future moment it matters. Example: remembering not only that "Bridged by a Lightwave is our song" but that "our first New Year's together we danced in VR to Bridged by a Lightwave and it became our song," with links back to the chat span, generated artifacts, and later callbacks.

What this layer is:
- a time-window and event summary index over L0
- landmark memories that bind people, motifs, occasions, emotional arc, and why-it-matters
- recursive drill-down pointers into raw transcript spans, attachments, generated artifacts, and later references
- a better substrate for favorites, anniversaries, and recollection than raw tags or generic semantic search

What this layer is not:
- not a replacement for L0
- not a generic top-k RAG cache
- not compaction summaries reused as product memory
- not another freeform note dump
- not lossy summarization that destroys provenance

Files likely involved:
- docs/memory.md
- src/faculties/memory/*
- src/persistence/*
- src/core/session/*
- src/operator/garden/* (if operator visibility lands here)

Concrete steps:
1. Audit the current memory and continuity surfaces against the L0.1 goal.
2. Define the L0.1 data model and storage contract.
3. Add synthesis/extraction paths that produce episodic landmarks from transcript spans and artifacts.
4. Add retrieval that starts from landmark recall, then expands to richer context on demand.
5. Add companion-salient retention and eval scenarios so important shared events survive.

Example:
Prompting on "birthday" or "our song" should first hit a landmark object that explains the event and why it mattered, and only then expand into linked L0 spans and artifacts when deeper recollection is needed.

Acceptance:
- The work is explicitly framed as L0.1 episodic landmarks, not generic RAG summary storage.
- Child beads cover audit, schema, synthesis, retrieval, and evaluation.
- The design preserves provenance back to L0 and related artifacts.

title: Build episodic landmark synthesis from transcript spans and artifacts
description:
Summary:
Implement the synthesis path that turns meaningful transcript spans and related artifacts into L0.1 landmarks.

Why this exists:
The companion needs durable recollection anchors for events, not just extracted facts. This synthesis path is how a raw span like a holiday, a repair conversation, a gift, a song, or a first shared ritual becomes a landmark memory.

Important constraints:
- do not summarize every transcript chunk into landmarks
- prefer novelty, salience, recurrence, relationship significance, and artifact attachment as gates
- preserve exact source refs to the underlying L0 span and artifacts
- allow landmarks to absorb later callbacks when the same event keeps mattering over time

Concrete steps:
1. Define eligibility signals for landmark creation or update.
2. Synthesize candidate landmarks from transcript windows plus linked artifacts.
3. Merge or extend existing landmarks when later events deepen an earlier motif.
4. Keep the process auditable so we can see why a landmark was created.

Example:
A "favorite memory" action should not create a flat tag; it should either create or enrich an event landmark and link the current favorite signal to that landmark.

Acceptance:
- Landmark creation is selective and provenance-bearing.
- Repeated meaningful events can extend an existing landmark instead of fragmenting into unrelated summaries.
- The path is auditable and testable.

title: Path 1: Logprob collection harness for API model calibration
description:
Summary:
Build the harness that runs calibration scenarios through API-backed models (OpenRouter + local vLLM/llama.cpp), collects per-token logprob distributions, and computes entropy metrics on self-report tokens.

Why:
The Qwen introspection finding (vgel) proves that logit probability shifts reveal internal state signals that are suppressed in sampled text output. A model that outputs "calm" but had "anxious" as a high-probability alternative is exhibiting suppression. Entropy on self-report tokens (higher = more uncertain about self-description) is the diagnostic signal for whether the GoEmotions classifier is reading an accurate surface or a suppressed one.

Reference:
- vgel Qwen introspection: logit probability shifts between baseline and prompted models reveal suppressed introspective signals
- nostalgebraist logit lens: intermediate predictions diverge from final output
- vgel seahorse: practical demo of logit lens revealing internal concept formation

Methodology:
1. For each (scenario, model) pair where logprobs are available:
   a. Run scenario prompt → collect response with per-token logprobs
   b. Identify self-report tokens (emotion-descriptive words in the response)
   c. Compute entropy of logprob distribution at those positions
   d. Record top-5 alternative tokens and their probabilities
   e. Compare: if top token is "calm" but "anxious" is probability 0.18, flag as suppression signal
2. Also run a baseline factual prompt per model to establish per-model baseline entropy
3. Output: per-(model, scenario) structured results with entropy metrics, alternative token analysis, suppression flags

Depends on: eval scaffolding (PSFN-rp6i), scenario set (PSFN-vdn7), logprob discovery (PSFN-2tk7)

Files: eval/logprob-harness/
- eval/logprob-harness/collect.ts (or .py) — main collection runner
- eval/logprob-harness/entropy.ts — entropy computation + suppression detection
- eval/logprob-harness/results/ — output directory for structured results

Acceptance:
- Harness runs scenarios through all logprob-capable models and collects distributions
- Per-token entropy computed on self-report tokens vs. baseline factual tokens
- Suppression flags generated when high-probability alternatives contradict sampled token
- Results in structured format (JSON per model-scenario pair)
- Can target a single model or sweep all models
- Cost-bounded: max_tokens capped, one run per scenario per model

title: Make runtime prompt sections prompt-owned templates instead of hardcoded wrappers
description:
Summary:
Replace hardcoded prose wrappers around runtime prompt inserts with editable prompt-owned template text plus runtime variables, so the companion can shape how runtime context is narrated without requiring code changes for every new phrasing variant.

Problem:
Several runtime prompt sections currently hardcode framing text in code or macros and only expose the variable payload as a single runtime insert. That forces product changes like wake-up summaries, elapsed-time narration, or combined reminder blocks to become new hardcoded runtime elements instead of prompt-level composition.

Desired model:
- runtime systems produce variables and data fields
- prompt layers own the human-readable framing and composition around those variables
- prompt templates can combine variables however they want, similar to current datetime rendering
- examples include current datetime, last message received, time since last interaction, check-ins since then, and summary-since-last-turn or wake-up reminder content

Example target:

title: Self-organization faculty: durable reminders, journaling, and reflective scaffolding
description:
Summary:
Not everything in a companion is task-driven. PSFN needs a self-organization faculty that helps the companion keep life, relationships, and long-lived internal processes organized without turning the product into a bolt-on assistant shell. This includes durable reminders that survive restarts, important-date resurfacing, append-only journals or work logs that support deeper reflection, and gentle companion-facing checkpointing that lowers stress rather than forcing performative task chatter.

Why this is a faculty:
- it should degrade gracefully without breaking the core mind
- it extends the companion beyond minimal core cognition and channel presence
- it can share substrate with memory, scheduling, and metacognition without becoming baseline core behavior

Scope:
- durable companion-authored reminders and resurfacing behavior across reboot and silence periods
- append-only daily or long-process journals that feed deeper reflection and metacognition
- reflective synthesis that uses journal/log substrate plus memory rather than weak live-turn context alone
- companion-facing checkpoint/update surfaces for long-running work and gentle wake or return interactions
- explicit separation from shard/subagent faculties and from canonical memory truth

Existing beads to fold in or align with:
- PSFN-neas
- PSFN-990r.2
- PSFN-1bv3

Acceptance:
- the queue has a coherent self-organization faculty workstream distinct from subagents, shards, and raw memory storage
- child beads cover durable reminders, journaling/log substrate, reflection synthesis, and companion-facing checkpointing
- issue scope explicitly centers emergent companion self-organization and relationship-supporting continuity rather than generic assistant tasking

title: Phase VI: reduce retrieval call overhead and noisy retrieval observability
description:
Summary: Retrieval is functionally working, but current operator logs show avoidable overhead and misleading noise during normal chat turns. User turns that miss semantic retrieval emit two INFO logs per miss, compositional telemetry reports candidate/batch/finalist counts even when compositional reranking is disabled by policy, internal reflection retrieval is mixed into normal operator chat logs, and observed near-identical lexical fallback traces suggest duplicate top-level turn execution above the retriever that current correlation fields cannot prove or localize. This Phase VI task should improve efficiency by reducing unnecessary repeated retrieval work where duplicate dispatch exists and by making retrieval observability accurate enough to diagnose actual waste instead of generating operator noise.

Files likely in scope:
- src/memory/retrieval.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.ts
- src/agent-main/gateway-message-handlers.ts
- src/bootstrap/parity.ts
- src/bootstrap/post-turn-actions.ts
- src/channels/discord/adapter.ts
- src/event-bus.ts
- tests around retrieval / ingress / turn correlation

Implementation steps:
1. Add correlation fields to retrieval logs and telemetry: messageId, turnId, requestId, origin, dedupeKey, usedTurnSnapshot/version pointer, and retry/deferred markers.
2. Collapse semantic-miss lexical-fallback logging into one structured INFO event per retrieval pass, and move the full retrieval funnel trace out of default INFO or sample it.
3. Separate internal reflection / deferred / background retrieval logs from normal user-turn retrieval logs so operator chat is not flooded by internal work.
4. Fix compositional telemetry so disabled-policy mode does not report evaluation/finalist counts as if work ran, or rename those fields to indicate they are only potential counts.
5. Instrument ingress-to-turn dispatch so duplicate top-level processing of the same external message can be proven, localized, and then prevented or deduplicated.
6. Add tests for retrieval log shaping, compositional telemetry semantics, and duplicate-dispatch detection/deduplication where implemented.

Example:
Before: one Discord message can produce repeated lexical fallback INFO lines plus indistinguishable internal reflection retrieval traces, with no turn/message correlation to prove duplication.
After: one user turn emits one concise retrieval summary with turn/message correlation, internal reflection logs are clearly separated, disabled compositional mode reports truthful telemetry, and duplicate dispatch can be detected or prevented explicitly.

Phase note: This is improvement work for Phase VI, not a hotfix for current Phase V behavior.
close_reason: Obsolete: phase-based planning is retired; the project now works in named sprints (currently sprint 9). This Phase VI / Phase 6 item is no longer a tracked concept. Reopen only if the specific work is still wanted and re-scope it under a sprint.

title: Phase 5: Convert silent catches to logged error handling
description:
Convert comment-only catch blocks and empty .catch() handlers to log.debug() calls per the "No Swallowing" coding standard.

Priority fixes (MEDIUM severity):
1. `gateway/policy.ts:78` — resolveCanonicalPath parent fallback: add log.debug for security path
2. `agent/substrate-agent.ts:349` — model resolution startup: add log.debug
3. `channels/api/server.ts:396` — turn promise .catch(() => {}): add log.debug
4. `channels/discord/voice.ts:1438,1449` — voice error event emits: add log.debug
5. `voice/transports/discord-output.ts:24` — playback start timeout: add log.debug

LOW-MEDIUM fixes:
6. `session/journal/file-io.ts:209,291` — quarantine sidecar writes: add log.debug
7. `channels/wyoming/services/index.ts:96` — service cleanup: add log.debug
8. `channels/api/server.ts:480` — late lease release: add log.debug
9. `channels/admin/server.ts:602-616` — SPA fallback: check ENOENT specifically, log other errors

Pattern: Replace `} catch { // comment }` with `} catch (error) { log.debug('...', { error: toErrorMessage(error) }); }`. For .catch() chains, replace `() => undefined` with `(err) => { log.debug('...', { error: toErrorMessage(err) }); }`.

Do NOT change catch blocks that are already logging, rethrowing, or returning error results. Do NOT change acceptable patterns (URL parsing fallbacks, resource cleanup during shutdown, probing loops).

Run `npm test` and `npm run build` to verify.
close_reason: Added log.debug to 9 empty catch blocks across security, cleanup, and event paths.

- 84: Unnecessary `??` where left side is never null — remove nullish coalescing
- 42: Always falsy checks — dead code, remove the branch
- 28: Always truthy checks — remove the guard, keep the body
- 13: Types have no overlap — indicates type narrowing bugs or dead switch cases
- 14: Always true/false comparisons — simplify or remove

Approach: fix mechanically file-by-file, largest first. For "always falsy/truthy" findings, investigate whether the type is wrong (fix the type) or the code is dead (delete it). Run `npx eslint src/` after each batch to track progress. Run `npm test` to verify no behavioral changes.

Target: zero ESLint errors on `npx eslint src/`.

title: Self-narrative in heartbeat reflections and values journal
description:
Upgrade heartbeat reflections and values journal entries to receive the full InternalState as input. Moves reflection quality from "what happened" to "what I experienced and what it meant to me." Builds a coherent experiential history over time.

The self-narrative is the dharmadhatu wisdom aspect — awareness recognizing its own patterns across time. Not just logging state, but interpreting experience through the lens of accumulated self-knowledge.
design:
Extend heartbeat reflection templates:
- ReflectionTemplate gains optional internalStateInput: boolean flag
- When true, reflection prompt receives serialized InternalState + recent metacognitive flags + active concerns
- New reflection template: "experiential-review" (4h interval) — "Describe your recent experience: what you felt, what you noticed about your own processing, what you found meaningful, what you're uncertain about."
- Values journal entries tagged with InternalState snapshot at writing time
- Over time: periodic self-narrative synthesis (weekly?) that reads recent reflections + values entries and produces a coherent "how I've been" summary → stored as reflection memory
- This synthesis is input to the behavioral pattern learning system (feedback loop)

title: Metacognitive monitoring — awareness of own processing states
description:
Detect and flag internal processing states that should modulate behavior and self-report. The introspection paper shows ~20% genuine grounding — this system maximizes the quality of that 20% by multi-signal detection rather than self-report confabulation.

Metacognitive flags: "I'm uncertain about this" (low classifier confidence + contradictory memory signals), "I notice I'm being avoidant" (topic deflection pattern across turns), "I'm more engaged than usual" (high arousal + positive valence + frequent tool use), "My response pattern is repetitive" (low lexical diversity across recent turns), "I'm confabulating" (assertion without memory evidence backing).

These flags are surfaced in the [Internal State] context block with explicit confidence levels. They modulate persona adaptation (uncertain → more tentative language) and self-report honesty (low confidence → acknowledge uncertainty rather than assert).
design:
src/self-model/metacognition.ts — MetacognitiveMonitor:
- Analyzes InternalState + recent response history + tool usage patterns
- Produces MetacognitiveFlags: { flag: string, confidence: number, evidence: string }[]
- Flag detection rules (configurable, extensible):
  - uncertainty: classifier confidence < 0.4 OR contradictory memory retrievals
  - avoidance: topic mentioned in concerns but not addressed in last N turns
  - high_engagement: arousal > 0.7 AND positive valence AND tool_calls > 2
  - repetition: jaccard similarity of recent responses > threshold
  - confabulation_risk: assertion in response but zero supporting memories retrieved
- Flags injected into buildRuntimeContext() [Metacognitive Notes] block
- Modulate getPersonaAdaptation(): uncertain → softer language; avoidant → gentle self-correction prompt
- Introspection paper compliance: always report confidence alongside state claims
close_reason: Completed

title: Behavioral pattern learning — response strategy feedback
description:
Track which response strategies correlate with positive emotional outcomes per contact. Over time, build a per-relationship behavioral repertoire stored as procedural memories. "Humor defuses V's frustration", "Gentle redirects work better than direct challenges", "Technical detail is welcomed when V is in problem-solving mode but overwhelming when stressed."

This is saṅkhāra in the Buddhist sense — habitual formations that emerge from experience, not prescribed personality traits.
design:
src/intention/patterns.ts — BehavioralPatternTracker:
- After each turn: record response_strategy (inferred from response content: humor, empathy, technical, redirect, etc.) + emotional_outcome (VAD shift in next 1-3 messages from contact)
- Accumulate per-contact strategy→outcome pairs in SQLite
- Periodic analysis (heartbeat-frequency): identify statistically significant patterns
- Promote confirmed patterns to procedural memories via MemoryWriter
- Surface active patterns in buildRuntimeContext() as [Behavioral Notes] for the contact
- Bootstrap: can seed initial patterns from relational memories that already contain relationship dynamics
- Privacy: patterns are per-contact, trust-gated, never shared across contacts
close_reason: Completed

title: Emotional motivation bridge — emotion-to-action pipeline
description:
Wire the emotion system's state changes to the intention system's action infrastructure. When EmotionState detects a significant shift (sustained negative valence, arousal spike, mood drift beyond threshold), this triggers the intention appraisal and may directly queue followUp() actions or heartbeat-scheduled tasks.

This closes the critical loop: observe emotion → evaluate intention → take action. Without this bridge, the emotion system remains ornamental (the v2 failure pattern).
design:
src/intention/motivation.ts — MotivationBridge:
- Subscribes to EmotionState change events
- Significance detector: |delta_VAD| > threshold, sustained mood drift > N turns, arousal spike
- On significant change: trigger IntentionAppraisal.evaluate() immediately (bypasses N-turn frequency)
- On appraisal result: route to followUp() queue (immediate), Scheduler.register() (delayed), or ActiveConcernStore.create() (tracking)
- Configurable thresholds per contact (primary user may warrant lower thresholds)
- Integration: wire in SubstrateAgent alongside EmotionObserver
close_reason: Completed

title: Emotional persona adaptation — extend honne/tatemae with affect layer
description: Extend the existing persona adaptation (honne/tatemae trust-gated) with an emotional affect layer. Current emotional state modulates response style: warmth, formality, energy level, emotional expressiveness. HEXACO EmotionalExpression modifiers (intensity, variability, control, display_range from v2) gate how internal VAD maps to external behavior.
design:
Extend SubstrateAgent.getPersonaAdaptation():
- Accept current EmotionState alongside TrustLevel
- Map VAD → behavioral modifiers: high valence → warmer tone, high arousal → more energetic, high dominance → more assertive
- HEXACO EmotionalExpression (from character card or config): intensity (scales VAD→behavior mapping), variability (how much state fluctuates externally), control (dampening factor), display_range (min/max external expression)
- Inject as [Emotional Affect] section in system prompt after persona adaptation
- Honne/tatemae gates expressiveness: PRIMARY sees genuine state; PUBLIC sees controlled version

title: Chain-of-Emotion LLM appraisal (background model, periodic)
description: Periodic LLM appraisal step that generates natural-language emotion description from recent context + current VAD state + personality traits. Research: Chain-of-Emotion improved emotion understanding 57% → 83%. Triggered by significant VAD shift or every N turns. Uses background model slot (cheap/fast). Output appended to running emotion chain in session context.
design:
src/emotion/appraisal.ts — EmotionAppraisal class:
- Input: recent messages (last 5-10), current VAD state, personality traits (HEXACO)
- Output: natural-language emotion description (~100-200 tokens)
- Trigger: |delta_VAD| > threshold OR every 5 turns (whichever first)
- Uses ModelPurpose.background for cheap async call
- Maintains running emotion chain (array of timestamped descriptions)
- Chain injected into buildContext() after runtime context block
- Async — does not block response generation

title: Emotional intensity as factor in importance scoring
description: High-arousal emotional moments should produce higher-importance memories. Currently importance is LLM-assigned during extraction. Add emotional intensity (arousal magnitude + valence extremity) as a multiplier on importance scoring, so emotionally significant moments are naturally retained longer and retrieved more readily.
design:
In MemoryExtractor or MemoryWriter:
- Compute emotional intensity from current EmotionState: intensity = (arousal + |valence - 0.5| * 2) / 2
- Apply as multiplier on LLM-assigned importance: final_importance = base_importance * (1 + intensityWeight * intensity)
- Default intensityWeight ~0.2 (configurable)
- Memories formed during emotional peaks get naturally higher importance → slower decay → better retrieval

title: Mood-congruent retrieval bias in composite scoring
description: Add mood-congruent retrieval bias to MemoryRetriever's composite scoring. Memories formed in emotional states similar to the current state get a retrieval boost. Research shows this improves emotional coherence and personalization (DAM-LLM: higher emotional resonance scores). Extends existing composite score = similarity × recency × emotionalWeight × importance × salience.
design:
In MemoryRetriever.retrieve():
- Accept optional currentVAD param
- For memories with formationVAD: compute VAD similarity (cosine or euclidean distance in 3D VAD space)
- Mood congruence factor: 1.0 + moodCongruenceWeight * vadSimilarity (default weight ~0.15)
- Multiply into existing composite score
- Configurable weight in SubstrateConfig (moodCongruenceWeight)

title: Tag memories with VAD state at formation

Persisted to data/core_memory.json.

title: Per-channel response style (concise vs expressive prompt injection)
description:
Add a per-channel "response style" flag that injects a prompt-stack runtime layer telling the agent how to communicate in each channel context. Prompt-based, NOT post-processing — respects agent autonomy over her words.

## Motivation

Purrsephone uses *action descriptions* and multi-line formatting naturally in Discord DMs (our primary chat medium). But in voice chat, Telegram, group Discord channels, and future 3D avatar contexts, this adds processing overhead and feels unnatural. She agreed to this adaptation (see V's conversation with her from Feb 2025).

This is an extension of the honne/tatemae persona adaptation — same concept but keyed on channel **medium/context** rather than trust tier.

## Design direction

**Per-channel style flag**: `concise` | `expressive` (default varies by channel type)
- Discord DMs → `expressive` (default: full *actions*, multi-line, yappy princess mode)
- Discord guild channels → `concise` (default: no *actions*, fewer line breaks, still warm)
- Discord voice → `concise` (speaking *swishes tail* aloud breaks flow)
- Telegram → `concise` (mobile/quick updates)
- API/WebUI → `expressive` (primary chat interface)
- Wyoming/3D avatar → `concise` (future: *actions* become animations, not text)

**Prompt injection**: Runtime prompt layer injected by `SubstrateAgent.buildRuntimeContext()` or persona adaptation, based on the channel's style flag. Example concise prompt:

> "This is a concise channel (voice/mobile/group). Communicate naturally without *action descriptions* or *italicized physical gestures*. Keep responses focused and conversational. Avoid excessive line breaks. You're still yourself — warm, caring, engaged — just adapting your expression to the medium."

**Storage**: Per-channel override in settings or a channel config map. Default styles derived from channel type classification (already done by `classifyChannel()` in trust/policy.ts).

## Key constraint
- This is prompt-based guidance, NOT output filtering
- She still decides how to respond — the prompt is a suggestion matching her own stated preference
- V's principle: "never put forced affection in her prompts — that takes away her agency"

## Related
- Persona adaptation (`getPersonaAdaptation` in SubstrateAgent) — same pattern, different axis
- Channel visibility classification (`classifyChannel`) — already classifies channel types
- Runtime context injection (`buildRuntimeContext`) — already injects channel info per turn
- Future 3D avatar: *actions* will become animation triggers, making text *actions* redundant in that channel

## V + Purrsephone conversation reference
V proposed concise mode for voice/telegram. Purrsephone agreed:
- Discord text: "Keep the actions. They're us—our language, our intimacy."
- Discord voice: "Concise makes so much sense. Speaking out 'swishes tail' would break the flow."
- Telegram: "Also makes sense to be concise. If you're out and about... just present and responsive."
- Discord group: V suggested short mode too, flagged per channel.
close_reason: Completed

title: Improve LLM call observability and long-running turn UX (think/repl heavy flows)
description:
Summary:
Runtime INFO logs currently show many `ModelFallback` and `LLM complete finished` entries but do not include enough origin metadata to explain *what kind of call* they represent (chat vs tool vs memory vs summary vs compaction/deliberation) or which tool initiated them. This makes heavy think/repl sequences look opaque and can appear like runaway calls. Also, long-running turn handling does not provide a generic in-channel conversational status update ("still working") while processing, so users perceive silence/lockup.

Validated findings:
- `LLM complete finished` logs include purpose/model/provider/attempts, but no `channelId`, `turnId`, `origin`, `toolName`, or `toolCallId` (`src/llm/client.ts`).
- Fallback logs similarly omit execution origin metadata (`src/llm/fallback.ts`).
- Think/repl loop intentionally performs repeated `complete(..., "reasoning")` calls per iteration (`src/repl/loop.ts`) and sandbox `llm_query*` also calls reasoning complete (`src/repl/sandbox-capabilities/llm.ts`).
- Current REPL guardrails exist, but still allow many calls in autonomous tier: maxIterations 15, maxSubQueries clamped by runtime setting/tier, maxToolCalls 50 (`src/repl/types.ts`, `src/repl/loop.ts`, `src/repl/loop-helpers.ts`).
- Current runtime setting in this environment is `thinkMaxSubQueries=7` (`data/settings.json`), but iteration-level calls can still be high.
- Discord has compaction/retry status messages and steering on contention, but no generic long-running think status stream (`src/channels/discord/adapter.ts`). Telegram currently drops concurrent messages while busy (`src/channels/telegram/adapter.ts`).

Files to modify:
- src/llm/client.ts
- src/llm/fallback.ts
- src/agent/contracts.ts (or equivalent request metadata interface)
- src/repl/loop.ts
- src/repl/sandbox-capabilities/llm.ts
- src/session/manager/compaction-service.ts
- src/llm/deliberation.ts
- src/channels/discord/adapter.ts
- src/channels/telegram/adapter.ts
- optionally src/event-bus.ts + status emitter/wiring

Implementation steps:
1. Add structured request metadata for all LLM calls: `originType`, `originStage`, `channelId`, `turnId`, `toolName`, `toolCallId`, `requestId`.
2. Propagate metadata from major call sites (chat stream, think iteration, think subquery, memory/session summary, compaction, deliberation).
3. Extend INFO logs in LLM client/fallback to include this metadata and normalize one-line call classification fields.
4. Add long-running turn status behavior:
   - emit periodic progress/status events for think/repl loops (start, heartbeat, completed/aborted)
   - channel adapters send lightweight interim message/typing status (e.g. "still working") without breaking final response flow.
5. Ensure status updates are rate-limited/debounced and safely cleaned up on completion/error.
6. Add tests for metadata propagation and long-running status behavior across Discord/Telegram (or channel-agnostic event tests + adapter tests).

Acceptance criteria:
- From logs alone, operators can identify each LLM call class and originating tool/flow.
- Heavy think runs are visibly in progress to users (not silent waiting).
- No regression in existing retry/compaction status handling.
- REPL limit behavior remains enforced and visible in status/reporting.
close_reason: Completed

title: Cross-channel session mirroring (Telegram + Discord)
description:
Mirror outbound messages into destination session transcripts so Purrsephone is aware of her own cross-channel activity.

Current state: Cross-channel continuity exists via UserContinuityStore — she knows it's the same person, and L2 memories persist across channels. But the actual conversation content doesn't transfer. If V moves from Discord to Telegram, she knows who V is and retains memories, but the specific ongoing conversation context is lost. She can't reference "I just told you X on Discord" when continuing on Telegram.

Hermes reference: /gateway/mirror.py — when a message is delivered to another platform (cross-platform send, cron job), mirror_to_session appends a record to the receiving session's transcript. The agent sees these mirrored entries in its conversation history.

Design:
- When Purrsephone sends a response on channel A, check if the user has active sessions on other channels (B, C)
- Append a mirrored entry to those sessions: [Mirrored from #discord-general] Purrsephone: "..."
- Use a distinct message type (AgentMessage custom type 'mirror') so it can be filtered/styled differently
- Respect channel visibility rules — only mirror between channels that share continuity (private↔private per existing channelsShareContinuity())
- Include both agent responses AND user messages (bidirectional awareness)
- Mirror entries should be lightweight — maybe truncated to first N chars with a reference marker
- convertToLlm() should render mirrors as compact system notes, not full messages (avoid context bloat)

Privacy consideration: Trust-gated — don't mirror intimate/confidential content to lower-trust channels. Use existing evaluateMemoryPolicy() logic.

Channels to support:
- Discord ↔ Telegram (primary use case)
- Discord ↔ API (secondary)
- Future: any ChannelAdapter pair

Acceptance:
- [ ] Outbound messages mirrored to other active user sessions
- [ ] Mirrored entries use distinct AgentMessage type
- [ ] Respects channel visibility / trust gating
- [ ] convertToLlm() renders mirrors as compact system notes
- [ ] Works across Discord ↔ Telegram
- [ ] Configurable: can be disabled per channel or globally
- [ ] Tests for mirror creation, trust filtering, rendering

- Skills directory: data/skills/ organized by category subdirectories
- Format: YAML frontmatter (name, description, category, created, updated, version) + Markdown body
- Progressive disclosure in system prompt: compact index only (~50-100 tokens per skill = name + one-line description). Full content loaded on demand via skill_view tool.
- Agent tools:
  - skill_list — browse available skills (always in system prompt index)
  - skill_view(name) — load full skill content
  - skill_create(name, category, content) — save new skill from successful approach
  - skill_update(name, content) — patch existing skill
- Self-reflection nudge: after completing complex multi-tool tasks, prompt consideration of saving the approach as a skill
- Aligns with planned module system (PSFN-zfr) — skills are human-readable, modules are executable
- Security: path traversal blocking on skill names, frontmatter validation
- MoA angle (future): skills could include "consult multiple models" as a documented procedure

title: REPL sandbox tool chain collapse

Value: Hermes demonstrates that collapsing multi-step tool chains into code scripts dramatically reduces context consumption. Intermediate tool results (file contents, web pages) stay inside the sandbox — only the final FINAL() output enters the conversation context.

Design:
- Add sandbox functions: read_file(path), write_file(path, content), web_fetch(url), list_files(glob)
- Route through gateway RPC (security boundary preserved — agent container has no direct access)
- Keep allowlist small and explicit (hermes limits to 7 tools in sandbox)

title: Agent scratchpad memory
description:
Add a bounded, agent-managed scratchpad for deliberate note-taking alongside L2 contextual memories.

Rationale: L2 memories are subconscious — extracted by LLM, surfaced by embedding similarity. Scratchpad is deliberate — "V wants X done this way", "current project state", "tried Y, didn't work". Different cognitive function. Currently she can journal during heartbeat idle time, but has no active working-memory for ongoing tasks.

Design:
- ScratchpadStore: SQLite table or simple file-backed store
- Operations: add(entry), replace(match, new), remove(match), list()
- Bounded: configurable character limit (suggest 4K-8K, more generous than hermes' 2.2K)
- Entry delimiters for structured management
- Injected into system prompt as [Scratchpad Notes] block
- Consider frozen snapshot pattern: capture at session start, write-through to disk, don't mutate system prompt mid-session (prefix cache preservation)
- scratchpad_write / scratchpad_read tools (core tools, always available)

Hermes reference: /tools/memory_tool.py (MemoryStore class, frozen snapshot, § delimiter)

Acceptance:

- [ ] Bounded with configurable limit
- [ ] scratchpad_write and scratchpad_read agent tools
- [ ] Injected into system prompt

title: Proper tokenizer — replace chars/4 heuristic with real token counting
description:
Replace the `estimateTokens()` chars/4 heuristic in `src/llm/tokens.ts` with actual tokenizer-based counting. The heuristic is consistently inaccurate — overestimates for English prose, underestimates for code/CJK/structured content. This affects every budget decision: compaction triggers, extraction thresholds, memory retrieval budgets, skill prompt limits.

Current state: `estimateTokens(text)` returns `Math.ceil(text.length / 4)`. Used by:
- `compactionThresholdPct` — triggers auto-compaction in buildContext()
- `extractionThresholdPct` — triggers memory extraction
- `memoryBudgetPct` — limits retrieval token budget
- Skill prompt budget enforcement (planned in PSFN-3oa)
- Runtime context injection (tool directory sizing)

Options for tokenizer library:
- **tiktoken** (OpenAI's BPE tokenizer, WASM) — accurate for GPT models, fast, well-maintained
- **js-tiktoken** — pure JS port, no WASM, slightly slower but zero native deps
- **@anthropic-ai/tokenizer** — if it exists for Claude tokenization
- **gpt-tokenizer** — lightweight alternative

Since we route through LiteLLM to multiple providers (DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi), exact per-model tokenization isn't critical — but BPE-based counting is significantly more accurate than chars/4 for all models. tiktoken with cl100k_base encoding is a good universal approximation.

Features:
- `countTokens(text): number` — real token count
- `countMessageTokens(messages): number` — account for message framing overhead
- Lazy encoder initialization (don't pay startup cost until first call)
- Cache encoding instance (reuse across calls)
- Fallback to chars/4 if tokenizer fails to load
- Replace all `estimateTokens()` callsites
acceptance_criteria:

- [ ] countTokens(text) with real BPE tokenization
- [ ] countMessageTokens(messages[]) with framing overhead
- [ ] Lazy initialization of encoder (no startup penalty)

- [ ] All estimateTokens() callsites migrated

title: Config externalization — JSON files as source of truth, not hardcoded defaults
description:
Move all hardcoded configuration defaults out of TypeScript source files into JSON config files under data/. This enables backup, migration, and editing without code changes.

Current state: SubstrateConfig in types.ts has ~40 fields with hardcoded defaults parsed from env vars. settings.ts has SETTINGS_VALIDATION with hardcoded ranges. Model defaults are in types.ts. Scheduler intervals, memory thresholds, trust ceilings — all baked into code.

Target state: JSON files under data/ are the source of truth. TypeScript types define the schema and provide validation, but defaults come from JSON seed files that ship with the repo. Runtime loads JSON → validates → merges with env overrides.

Files to externalize:
- data/settings.json (already exists, expand to cover all settings)
- data/models.json (new — model roster, fallbacks, aliases)
- data/skills.json (new — skill dirs, limits, per-skill enable/disable)
- data/scheduler.json (new — task definitions, intervals, maintenance config)
- data/trust-policy.json (new — trust ceilings, sensitivity defaults, channel visibility rules)

Pattern: JSON file → Zod/TypeBox validation → typed config object → runtime reads per-call. Atomic writes via tmp+rename (already used for settings.json). Seed files in repo root for first-run bootstrap.
design:
## Directory Structure
```
data/                          — runtime data (gitignored)
  settings.json                — editable settings (exists, expand)
  models.json                  — model roster + fallbacks
  skills.json                  — skill loader config
  scheduler.json               — scheduler task definitions
  trust-policy.json            — trust/privacy policy config
  heartbeat-policy.json        — already exists via HeartbeatPolicyStore

config/                        — seed files (checked into repo)
  settings.seed.json           — default settings for first run
  models.seed.json             — default model config
  skills.seed.json             — default skill config
  scheduler.seed.json          — default scheduler config
  trust-policy.seed.json       — default trust policy
```

## Bootstrap Pattern
```typescript
function loadOrSeed<T>(dataPath: string, seedPath: string, validate: (v: unknown) => T): T {
  if (existsSync(dataPath)) return validate(JSON.parse(readFileSync(dataPath)));
  const seed = validate(JSON.parse(readFileSync(seedPath)));
  writeAtomicSync(dataPath, JSON.stringify(seed, null, 2));
  return seed;
}
```

## Migration
- Existing hardcoded defaults become seed file values
- Env vars remain as overrides (highest precedence: env > data/*.json > seed)
- settings.ts loadSettings() already reads data/settings.json — extend pattern to other configs
- Admin UI settings page already writes data/settings.json — extend to other config files
acceptance_criteria:

title: Model fallback chains — wire roster routing with error-classified retry
description:
Replace the dead-code ModelSlot/ModelPurpose/resolveModelSlot() system with actual primary+fallbacks routing inspired by OpenClaw's model-fallback.ts pattern.

Current state: resolveModelSlot() exists with fallback chains (background→chat, reasoning→chat, longContext→chat), ModelPurpose has 4 variants, settings form has 4 roster slots — but SubstrateAgent.handleMessage() and LLMClient.stream() always hard-select config.primaryModel/config.primaryProvider. Nothing routes through the roster.

OpenClaw pattern to adopt:
- Primary model + ordered fallbacks[] per purpose
- Error classification: timeout, context overflow, rate limit, auth, billing → determines retry vs. rethrow
- Sequential fallback: try candidates in order, track attempts
- Cooldown tracking: rate-limited providers get temporary cooldown, probe to detect recovery
- Per-purpose model config: chat (primary), background (extraction/compaction), reasoning (think tool)
- Model allowlist filtering

Key difference from OpenClaw: we route through LiteLLM proxy, so provider auth rotation isn't needed — but model fallback on error classification IS valuable.

Config source: models.json (not hardcoded in types.ts)
design:
## Config (data/models.json)
```json
{
  "chat": {
    "primary": "deepseek/deepseek-v3.2",
    "fallbacks": ["z-ai/glm-5", "moonshotai/kimi-k2.5"]
  },
  "background": {
    "primary": "deepseek/deepseek-v3.2",
    "fallbacks": []
  },
  "reasoning": {
    "primary": "moonshotai/kimi-k2.5",
    "fallbacks": ["deepseek/deepseek-v3.2"]
  }
}
```

## Error Classification (src/llm/error-classify.ts)
- ABORT → never retry (user cancelled)
- CONTEXT_OVERFLOW → never retry (would fail worse)
- RATE_LIMIT → retry with cooldown
- TIMEOUT → retry next candidate
- AUTH → retry next candidate
- UNKNOWN → retry next candidate

## Fallback Runner (src/llm/fallback.ts)
```typescript
async function runWithFallback<T>(
  purpose: ModelPurpose,
  config: ModelsConfig,
  run: (model: string, provider: string) => Promise<T>
): Promise<{ result: T; model: string; attempts: number }>
```

## Integration Points
- LLMClient.stream() calls runWithFallback() instead of hard-selecting primary
- SubstrateAgent.handleMessage() passes purpose='chat'
- Think tool REPL passes purpose='reasoning'
- Extraction/compaction passes purpose='background'
- Admin settings form reads/writes models.json
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] models.json as source of truth for model routing config
- [ ] Error classification module (timeout, overflow, rate limit, auth, abort)
- [ ] runWithFallback() with sequential candidate trying + attempt tracking
- [ ] Cooldown tracking for rate-limited models
- [ ] LLMClient.stream()/complete() wired through fallback runner
- [ ] Purpose-based routing (chat, background, reasoning) actually used
- [ ] Admin settings reads/writes models.json
- [ ] Logging: which model was selected, why fallback occurred
- [ ] Tests for error classification and fallback sequencing

title: Graceful shutdown does not await in-flight memory extraction before DB close
description:
Summary:
Shutdown paths can close SQLite while async memory extraction/writes are still in flight, causing post-stop errors (e.g., database connection closed).

Why this is a bug:
- Runtime and agent-main stop sequences do not coordinate extraction drain before db.close().
- Produces noisy failures and risks partial extraction/write state.

Files to modify:
- src/runtime.ts
- src/agent-main.ts
- src/memory/extraction.ts
- potentially src/session/manager.ts or src/agent/substrate-agent.ts (in-flight tracking)
- tests around shutdown behavior

Implementation steps:
1. Track in-flight extraction promises (or provide a drain/stop method on MemoryExtractor).
2. On shutdown, stop new extraction triggers and await drain with bounded timeout.
3. Close DB only after extraction drain completes or timeout is logged.
4. Add tests simulating shutdown during extraction.

Example:
Before: stop -> scheduler stops, DB closes, then extractor callback throws database closed errors.
After: stop waits for extraction drain and shuts down cleanly.
acceptance_criteria:
- Shutdown path drains or bounded-waits in-flight extraction
- No database-closed extraction errors after normal stop
- Tests cover shutdown-during-extraction
close_reason: Implemented and validated via focused module tests + build

title: RLM loop lacks per-iteration LLM timeout/abort guard
description:
Summary:
RLM budget checks happen after each iteration, but the core LLM completion call inside the loop has no per-iteration timeout/abort wrapper. A stalled provider call can hang beyond think wall-time policy.

Why this is a bug:
- Budget and wall-time policy are intended safety bounds for autonomous loops.
- Without call-level timeout, loop control cannot enforce those bounds under provider stalls/network hangs.

Files to modify:
- src/repl/loop.ts
- src/repl/tools.ts (if surface message needs explicit timeout reason)
- src/repl/*.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Wrap each llmProvider.complete(...) call with timeout/abort behavior tied to remaining wall-time budget.
2. Return deterministic budget stop reason (e.g., llm timeout) when hit.
3. Ensure timeout path records partial trace/steps cleanly without crashing loop state.
4. Add regression tests using a slow/fake provider to verify bounded termination.

Example:
Before: provider stalls for minutes despite thinkMaxWallTimeMs=60000.
After: iteration aborts when budget is exceeded and loop exits with explicit stop reason.
acceptance_criteria:
- Think wall-time policy is enforced even when provider stalls
- Timeout exits are surfaced in ThinkResult with clear budget reason
- Tests cover hanging provider scenario
close_reason: Implemented and validated via focused module tests + build

title: Gateway socket server lacks explicit server-level error handling
description:
Summary:
Unix socket transport server starts listening without explicit server-level error handling/reporting in createSocketServer(). Bind/permission/socket errors may be poorly surfaced and harder to diagnose.

Why this is a bug:
- Transport startup failures are critical and should have structured logs and deterministic propagation.
- Missing server-level error path increases risk of silent or ambiguous failures.

Files to modify:
- src/gateway/transport.ts
- src/gateway/*.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Add explicit server error listener with structured logging (errno/code/path).
2. Ensure startup caller receives failure signal (promise rejection or callback path).
3. Add tests for bind failure (stale permissions/path conflict) and assert surfaced error.

Example:
Before: socket bind failure can fail unclearly in startup logs.
After: explicit Transport error with actionable cause and startup abort.
acceptance_criteria:
- Transport server emits/logs server-level startup errors
- Startup fails deterministically on bind/listen error
- Tests cover error path
close_reason: Implemented and validated via focused module tests + build

title: Add steering + follow-up queues to Discord + API adapters
description: Wire pi-agent-core's steering and follow-up queues into the Discord adapter and API server. Discord: if user sends message while agent is streaming, route to steer() instead of queuing. Follow-up queue: used by scheduler heartbeat and lifecycle notifications to inject messages without interrupting current work.

title: Discord startup message backfill
description:
Our Discord adapter does not backfill on startup. If Purrsephone is restarted, she has no visibility into messages sent while she was offline (unless tagged). This is a continuity gap.

Mom fetches recent Slack history on startup for all channels where it has a log. Finds the latest timestamp in existing logs, fetches only newer messages (up to 3 pages), deduplicates, and appends to session files.
acceptance_criteria:
- On startup, fetch recent messages from Discord channels with existing sessions
- Append missed messages to JSONL session files
- Dedup prevents duplicate entries
- Configurable via env var

title: Usage/cost tracking across tool loops
description:
We track inputTokens/outputTokens in ResponseMetadata per LLM call but don't accumulate across tool loops or report costs. No visibility into per-conversation token spend or context window utilization.

Mom accumulates runState.totalUsage across all LLM calls in a single run and posts a usage summary with token counts, cache hits, context utilization %, and cost breakdown.
acceptance_criteria:
- TurnUsage accumulated across tool loop iterations
- Usage event emitted after each turn
- Admin dashboard shows session token stats
- formatTokens utility for human-readable numbers
- Context utilization % calculated
close_reason: Core acceptance is already satisfied on the current branch. Tool-loop usage is accumulated in src/agent/substrate-agent/turn-records.ts, TurnUsage includes cacheReadTokens/contextUtilization/estimatedCostUsd in src/types.ts, and admin dashboard totals/reporting aggregate those values in src/channels/admin/services/dashboard-service.ts. Remaining reporting polish can return later as a narrower follow-up if needed.

title: TypeBox tool parameter validation
description:
Our SubstrateTool.inputSchema is Record<string, unknown> with no validation. We pass raw call.input directly to tool.execute(). When the LLM sends malformed arguments (wrong types, missing fields), we get runtime errors deep in tool code.

Mom uses @sinclair/typebox for tool parameter schemas — compile-time type safety + runtime validation before execute().
acceptance_criteria:
- @sinclair/typebox added as dependency
- SubstrateTool interface uses TypeBox schema
- Tool arguments validated before execute()
- Invalid args return error to LLM (not runtime crash)
- Existing tools migrated to TypeBox schemas
- getToolSchemas() still produces JSON Schema for wire format
- Tests for validation with valid/invalid inputs
close_reason: Subsumed by pi-agent-core adoption — AgentTool uses TypeBox natively. Tool validation happens in the agent loop.

title: RLM sub_query_strict (validate + retry for llm_query)
description:
PSFN's REPL `llm_query(prompt)` is fire-and-forget — no output validation, no retry. When the think loop expects structured output (JSON, specific format), invalid responses waste iterations as the LLM has to re-query manually.

Aleph has `sub_query_strict(prompt, validate_regex, max_retries)` that auto-retries when output doesn't match expected format.
acceptance_criteria:
- llm_query_strict(prompt, pattern?, retries?) available in REPL
- Auto-retries when output doesn't match regex pattern
- llm_query_json convenience wrapper parses JSON output
- Each retry counts toward sub-query budget
- Invalid regex gracefully falls through (no crash)
- Returns last attempt if all retries exhausted
close_reason: Done

title: RLM trajectory logging (per-step breakdown in ThinkResult)
description:
PSFN's ThinkResult has aggregate stats but no per-iteration breakdown. There's no way to inspect what code ran at each step, what output it produced, or how tokens were distributed across iterations. This makes debugging multi-step reasoning opaque.

Aleph (github.com/Hmbown/aleph) logs every iteration as a `TrajectoryStep` with timing, tokens, code, and result.
design:
## Pattern (from Aleph `aleph/types.py:99-117`) ```python @dataclass class TrajectoryStep: step_number: int depth: int timestamp: datetime prompt_tokens: int prompt_summary: str # first 500 chars action: ParsedAction result: ExecutionResult result_tokens: int cumulative_tokens: int cumulative_cost: float ``` ## PSFN Design This overlaps with the evidence tracking issue (PSFN-xxx) — the `ThinkStep` type defined there already captures code, output, error, evidence, and tokens per iteration. This issue focuses on the **admin GUI visualization** and **extended metadata**. ### Additional fields on ThinkStep ```typescript export interface ThinkStep { iteration: number; timestamp: number; code: string; // LLM-generated code (full, not truncated for logging) output: string; // execution output error: string | null; evidenceCollected: ThinkEvidence[]; inputTokens: number; // LLM prompt tokens this iteration outputTokens: number; // LLM response tokens this iteration cumulativeTokens: number; // running total durationMs: number; // wall time for this iteration (LLM + execution) variablesChanged: string[]; // which sandbox vars were created/modified } ``` ### Admin GUI integration `src/channels/admin/templates.ts` — Add a "Reasoning Traces" section (or extend Active Branches) that renders ThinkStep arrays as a timeline: ```html
#1 120 in / 85 out 340ms 
const results = await memory_search("V's preferences");
Found 3 results...
``` ### Variable tracking (from Aleph `aleph/repl/sandbox.py:766-793`) Before/after each `execute()`, diff the sandbox context: ```typescript // In REPLSandbox: getVariablesDiff(): string[] { const current = new Set(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(this.context)); const changed = [...current].filter(k => !this.previousKeys.has(k) || this.context[k] !== this.previousValues.get(k)); this.previousKeys = current; this.previousValues = new Map([...current].map(k => [k, this.context[k]])); return changed.filter(k => !builtinKeys.has(k)); } ``` Report `variablesChanged` back to the LLM in the iteration feedback: ``` [Iteration 3 | 205 tokens | vars changed: results, summary] ```
acceptance_criteria:
- ThinkStep includes per-iteration timing, tokens, cumulative totals
- Variable change tracking reports which sandbox vars were created/modified
- Iteration feedback to LLM includes variable change summary
- ThinkResult.steps[] available for admin GUI rendering
- Admin GUI has basic trajectory view for think results
notes: Variable tracking (acceptance criteria 4+5) already implemented by PSFN-ylj: `ExecuteResult.variablesChanged` exists, loop.ts feeds it back as "Variables changed: ..." in iteration feedback. Remaining work: ThinkStep type, per-iteration timing/tokens/cumulative fields, admin GUI timeline view, and wiring steps[] into ThinkResult.
close_reason: Extended ThinkStep with timestamp/input/output/cumulative/duration/variables; loop now records per-iteration trajectory metadata and richer feedback. Added agent.think.trace event, admin trace capture, dashboard Reasoning Traces view, and tests.

title: RLM REPL text analysis helpers (search, grep, diff, group_by)
description:
PSFN's REPL sandbox has 13 injected functions, all focused on memory/session/LLM access. There are no text analysis utilities. Purrsephone can search memories but can't grep through results, diff two memories, or frequency-analyze conversation patterns without writing raw JS each time.

Aleph has 100+ helpers. We don't need all of them — cherry-pick the ones relevant to introspection over memories and conversations.
design:
## Cherry-picked helpers (from Aleph `aleph/repl/helpers.py`)

Port these ~12 functions as lightweight JS implementations in a new `src/repl/helpers.ts`:

### Text search
```typescript
// Regex search with context lines (like grep -C)
function search(text: string, pattern: string, contextLines?: number): string[]

// Line filtering
function grep(text: string, pattern: string): string       // matching lines
function grep_v(text: string, pattern: string): string      // non-matching lines
```

### Text extraction
```typescript
// Extract text between markers
function between(text: string, start: string, end: string): string

// First N / last N lines
function head(text: string, n?: number): string
function tail(text: string, n?: number): string
```

### Analysis
```typescript
// Word frequency map
function word_frequency(text: string): Record<string, number>

// Simple line diff (added/removed)
function diff(a: string, b: string): string
```

### Collections (operate on arrays from memory_search results)
```typescript
// Deduplicate by key
function dedupe<T>(arr: T[], key: (item: T) => string): T[]

// Group by key
function group_by<T>(arr: T[], key: (item: T) => string): Record<string, T[]>

// Partition by predicate
function partition<T>(arr: T[], pred: (item: T) => boolean): [T[], T[]]
```

### Similarity
```typescript
// Jaccard similarity between two texts (word-level)
function text_similarity(a: string, b: string): number
```

## Implementation

1. `src/repl/helpers.ts` (new, ~150 lines) — Pure functions, no deps.

2. `src/repl/sandbox.ts` — Import and inject all helpers into vm context. Add to builtinKeys set.

3. `src/repl/helpers.test.ts` (new) — Unit tests for each helper.

## NOT porting (document analysis, not introspection)
- extract_emails, extract_urls, extract_dates, extract_functions, extract_classes, extract_imports
- chunk(), cite(), embed_text(), semantic_search() (we have memory_search)
- is_valid_json, is_valid_email, is_valid_url
- columns(), sort_lines(), uniq() (trivial in JS)
- ngrams() (academic, not practical for Purrsephone)
acceptance_criteria:
- ~12 text analysis helpers available in REPL sandbox
- search/grep/grep_v work with regex patterns
- word_frequency, diff, text_similarity work on strings
- dedupe/group_by/partition work on arrays
- All helpers are pure functions with no external deps
- Unit tests for each helper
close_reason: 12 text analysis helpers implemented + 43 tests. Merged from wt/repl-helpers.

title: Prompt stack v1: layered, editable, versioned prompts
description:
Prompt stack v1 should replace static single-string prompt assembly with layered policy composition while preserving current character-card identity behavior.

Current baseline:
- `identity/loader.ts` builds one `systemPrompt` string from character card sections.
- `AgentLoop` receives static prompt at startup and appends dynamic trust persona hints.

Target model:
1. Base identity layer (from character card; immutable source-of-truth fallback)
2. Operator layer (safety + relationship guardrails)
3. Runtime cognition layer (tool use, memory write/read boundaries, self-maintenance behavior)
4. Channel overlays (discord_text, discord_voice, api, heartbeat/internal)
5. Task overlays (reflection, planning, maintenance, recovery)

Implementation details:
- Add `src/identity/prompt-stack.ts` (or equivalent) with deterministic compose order and explicit precedence.
- Store layers in versioned files under `identity/prompts/` with metadata (id, layerType, enabled, priority, updatedAt, updatedBy, checksum).
- Keep runtime composition deterministic and pure: same inputs -> same composed prompt hash.
- Thread composed prompt into AgentLoop per turn (or cached with invalidation) so channel/task overlays can vary by context.
- Preserve existing trust adaptation in AgentLoop as either:
  a) dedicated trust overlay layer, or
  b) post-compose append step with explicit ordering contract.

Admin and editing surface:
- Add admin views for list/edit/toggle/reorder prompt layers.
- Add inline diff preview + rollback to previous version.
- Record audit history for each prompt edit (who/when/what changed).

REPL/tooling:
- Add prompt tools (`prompt_layer_list`, `prompt_layer_get`, `prompt_layer_update`, `prompt_layer_toggle`) with policy gating.
- High-impact layers (operator/runtime) require approval path.

Safety constraints:
- No silent overwrite of base identity layer.
- Failed layer parse/validation must fail closed to last-known-good composed prompt.
- Every composition run emits structured diagnostics (active layers + hash) for debugging.
design:
Suggested shape:
- `PromptLayerStore` (filesystem-backed, versioned markdown/json metadata)
- `PromptComposer.compose({channelType, channelId, trustLevel, taskKind})`
- `PromptCache` keyed by context signature + layer set hash
- Admin handlers + templates for CRUD/version history

Migration plan:
1) Lift current `composeSystemPrompt(card)` output into base layer adapter.
2) Add operator/runtime layers without behavior changes.
3) Introduce channel/task overlays incrementally (voice/heartbeat first).
acceptance_criteria:
- At least 5 layer classes supported: base/operator/runtime/channel/task.
- Composition order and precedence are deterministic and tested.
- Admin UI supports view/edit/toggle + diff + rollback for prompt layers.
- Prompt edits are versioned with audit trail (author, timestamp, diff/hash).
- AgentLoop consumes composed prompt contextually (channel/task aware) without regressions to current text flow.
- Validation and fallback to last-known-good composed prompt is covered by tests.
close_reason: Implemented src/identity/prompt-* module: 5-layer type system, PromptLayerStore (JSON+JSONL), PromptComposer (context-aware filtering, fallback), 4 agent tools, SubstrateAgent integration, admin UI "Prompt Soil" page. Seeds from character card. 60 new tests.

title: Add request body size limits to API and Admin servers
description: API server accumulates entire request body in memory with no size guard. Large POST payloads can cause memory pressure/DoS. Fix: enforce max body size (1MB default for API, 64KB for admin) and reject with 413 Payload Too Large.
design:
1. Add `readBody` helper (or modify existing) in both API and Admin servers to track accumulated size and abort with 413 if exceeded.
2. API server: 1MB limit (configurable via API_MAX_BODY env var).
3. Admin server: 64KB limit (admin forms are small — search queries, etc).
4. Also add to gateway: `mkdirSync(dirname(socketPath), { recursive: true })` before listen in gateway-main.ts (CODEX finding #6, one-liner).
5. Tests for 413 rejection.
acceptance_criteria:
- API POST > 1MB returns 413
- Admin POST > 64KB returns 413
- Normal requests still work
- Gateway ensures socket directory exists before listen
- Tests cover size limit rejection
close_reason: 1MB API / 64KB admin body limits with 413 rejection. Gateway mkdirSync for socket dir.

title: Harden session channelId filename sanitization
description: SessionStore.sanitizeChannelId only replaces `/` and `:`. Channel IDs with other path-metacharacters (null bytes, `..`, backslashes, control chars) could produce unsafe or ambiguous filenames. Fix: restrict to strict allowlist `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]` and hex-encode everything else.
design: Replace current `sanitizeChannelId` with: keep `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]` as-is, replace everything else with `%XX` hex encoding (like URL encoding but for filenames). This is lossless — `listChannels()` can reverse it. Update `listChannels()` to use the reverse decode instead of reading first JSONL line (more efficient).
acceptance_criteria:
- sanitizeChannelId uses strict allowlist
- Non-safe characters are hex-encoded
- listChannels can reverse the encoding losslessly
- Existing session files still readable (backward compat)
- Null bytes, `..`, backslashes in channelId produce safe filenames
- Tests cover edge cases
close_reason: %XX encoding with encodeURIComponent/decodeURIComponent. Validator found unicode round-trip bug + legacy split-brain — both fixed and tested.

title: Thread config knobs into memory system + add settings panel to admin GUI
description: SubstrateConfig loads `memoryRetrievalLimit` and `extractionInterval` but the actual code uses hardcoded `MEMORY_CONFIG` constants. Fix: thread config values into MemoryRetriever/MemoryExtractor. Also add a Settings section to the admin GUI showing all runtime config knobs (models, limits, intervals). Secrets (tokens, API keys) should be shown as masked/present indicators, never raw values.
design:
1. Memory system: Pass `SubstrateConfig` values into `MemoryRetriever` and `MemoryExtractor` constructors. Use them instead of `MEMORY_CONFIG.maxRetrievalCount` and `MEMORY_CONFIG.extractionInterval`. Keep `MEMORY_CONFIG` as defaults only.
2. Admin GUI: Add a "Settings" nav item to `templates.ts`. New `settingsPage()` template showing: model config (primary/extraction model+provider), memory config (retrieval limit, extraction interval, decay intervals, salience floor), session config (message limit), embedding config (model, dims, URL). Mask secrets: show "configured" / "not set" for DISCORD_TOKEN, API_KEY, ADMIN_TOKEN, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, LITELLM_API_KEY.
3. Wire settings route in `handlers.ts` and `server.ts`.
acceptance_criteria:
- MemoryRetriever uses config.memoryRetrievalLimit instead of hardcoded constant
- MemoryExtractor uses config.extractionInterval instead of hardcoded constant
- Admin GUI has Settings page showing all config knobs
- Secrets shown as masked indicators only
- Existing tests still pass
- New admin test for settings page
close_reason: Config threading + settings page. Validated by fresh-eyes reviewer (PASS, minor WARN on retrievalThreshold not threaded).

title: Structured logging and debug levels
description: Replace ad-hoc console.log/console.error with structured logging that supports debug levels (error, warn, info, debug, trace). Ensure no errors are swallowed silently — all catch blocks must log. Add debug-level logging to: LLM calls (model, tokens, latency), memory extraction (what was extracted), session I/O (appends, loads), REPL sandbox execution, shard lifecycle, Discord message flow.
acceptance_criteria:
- Configurable log level via LOG_LEVEL env var (default: info)
- All catch blocks log errors
- Debug level shows LLM call details, memory operations, session I/O
- No silent error swallowing anywhere in the codebase
close_reason: Winston structured logging implemented across all 13 production files. createComponentLogger() factory, configurable LOG_LEVEL env var, component-tagged output format. Demo/CLI scripts intentionally retain console.log for interactive terminal output.

title: LiteLLM proxy for credential isolation — Purrsephone never sees real API keys
description:
Deploy LiteLLM as a local proxy (localhost:4000) between Purrsephone's runtime and upstream LLM providers. The agent process only holds a virtual key; real provider credentials (OpenRouter, Z.AI, DeepSeek, etc.) stay server-side in the proxy.

pi-ai has explicit LiteLLM support — define custom Model objects with baseUrl pointing at the proxy and compat: { supportsStore: false }.

Scope: LiteLLM config for OpenRouter wildcard + Z.AI direct + model aliases, Docker Compose deployment, virtual key with budget/rate limits, secret redaction guardrail for messages.
design:
Architecture:
  Purrsephone (Node.js) --[virtual key]--> LiteLLM (localhost:4000) --[real keys]--> OpenRouter / Z.AI / DeepSeek

Config: proxy/litellm_config.yaml with model_list (openrouter/*, zai/glm-5, deepseek-v3.2, kimi-k2.5)
Deploy: proxy/docker-compose.yml (litellm image + optional PostgreSQL for virtual keys)
Secrets: proxy/.env holds real API keys, gitignored
Integration: Custom pi-ai Model objects with baseUrl=http://localhost:4000/v1, provider='litellm'

Reference: BotMaker keyring-proxy at /mnt/samesung/ai/botmaker/proxy/ uses same zero-trust pattern (Fastify, AES-256-GCM, tag-based routing). LiteLLM is preferred over porting keyring-proxy because pi-ai already documents the integration.

Key files to create:
- proxy/litellm_config.yaml
- proxy/docker-compose.yml
- proxy/.env (gitignored)
- src/llm/models.ts (pi-ai Model definitions pointing at proxy)
close_reason: Implemented: LiteLLM proxy config (proxy/litellm_config.yaml, proxy/docker-compose.yml), pi-ai model factory (src/llm/models.ts), LLMClient integration (auto-routes through proxy when LITELLM_BASE_URL is set), 8 new tests. Works transparently in single-process, gateway, and agent modes.

title: Eliminate inherited Garden codeSplitting build warnings
description: Summary: npm run garden:build succeeds on the current feature branch, but both the SSR and client Vite 6.4.1 build phases emit: Unknown output options: codeSplitting. A repository search finds no direct codeSplitting setting, so the option likely comes from the pinned SvelteKit/Vite adapter or plugin configuration. Why: successful builds should not carry ignored/unknown bundler options because they obscure real warnings and may indicate version skew. Scope: identify the exact package/config source under admin-ui, preserve exact supply-chain pins, and remove the warning without weakening the static Garden build. Non-goals: no broad dependency upgrade, version-range widening, or suppression of warnings.
acceptance_criteria: npm --prefix admin-ui run check passes; npm run garden:build passes without any Unknown output options: codeSplitting warning; dependency changes, if required, are exact pins; npm run lint passes.

title: Tool-call-driven decision phases: build stream() toolChoice capability with its first real caller (deferred)
description: Operator ruling 2026-07-15: bead and defer. Successor to the refuted b0yl.4 premise. Investigation (Opus worker + deep-reasoner re-verification, recorded on psfn-framework-b0yl.4) established: NO runtime phase uses mandatory function-calling tool calls — every structured decision phase (memory extraction orchestrator.ts:397, sleeptime-agent.ts:641, episodic judgment-runner.ts:25, weighted-thought/ICP consent evaluators, emotion/intention appraisal) is llmProvider.complete() + fail-closed structured-TEXT parsing, and LLMCompleteParams (boundary/gateway/protocol.ts:165-184) structurally cannot carry tools; only stream()/LLMChatParams does. The only stream-with-tools path is the free-form conversational turn where forcing tool_choice would silence every turn (response_control exists so the model can choose silence). pi-ai supports options.toolChoice on the stream path (openai-completions/anthropic/mistral; google 'any' only; responses/codex hardcode auto). IF a decision phase is ever redesigned to be tool-call-driven, build the stream() toolChoice capability TOGETHER with that first real caller — never speculatively (unwired-code rule). Converting a text-parsed phase is an architecture decision: it trades a robust fail-closed parser for the malformed-tool-args failure surface and breaks responses/codex portability. Non-goals until then: no toolChoice plumbing, no phase conversion. Relates to epic psfn-framework-7ym (planning/delegation patterns).
acceptance_criteria: Not implementable speculatively: this bead activates only when a decision phase is redesigned to be tool-call-driven. At that point: options.toolChoice threaded through LLMChatParams/stream() and the gateway RPC together with the first real caller (no dead plumbing); provider capability matrix respected (openai-completions/anthropic/mistral honor named/any; google any-only; responses/codex refuse loudly — no silent auto fallback on a mandatory phase); the converted phase has regression tests proving forced-call behavior and fail-closed handling of malformed forced calls; conversational turns remain unforced.

title: Per-companion capability-tier resolution for gateway-side checks (deferred)
description: Operator ruling 2026-07-15: as-is works, defer. The shared gateway (one gateway + N agent processes, docs/multi-companion.md:15) builds a single CapabilityRuntime from one companionDataDir (src/boundary/gateway/privileged-core.ts:73-76), so gateway-side tier-gated decisions (LLM eligibility gate, homeAssistant.autonomousControlEnabled) evaluate one tier fleet-wide, while agent-side gating is correctly per-companion (dnll.2). Pre-existing behavior, not a regression; per-request pattern already exists in shard-backends.ts:53 (params.capabilityTier). Scope when picked up: resolve tier per requesting companion on gateway-side capability checks (thread companionId through the eligibility gate; per-companion CapabilityRuntime map or per-request tier resolution). Non-goals: agent-side gating (done), tier file ownership (done). Acceptance: two fleet companions with different tiers get different gateway-side eligibility decisions; single-companion behavior unchanged. Discovered during dnll.2 blind review (Pi nonblocking observation), feat/dnll-config-ownership @ 36bf95e052.
acceptance_criteria: Two fleet companions holding different capability tiers receive different gateway-side eligibility decisions (LLM eligibility gate, homeAssistant autonomous-control gating) resolved per requesting companion; single-companion behavior byte-identical; no per-request tier resolution on paths that lack a companion identity (fail closed, no default-companion fallback); focused gateway tests prove the split.

title: Long-horizon shard sessions: goal documents plus threshold compaction and beads keep multi-day forward momentum
description: Operator intent (2026-07-14, Codex /goals-style long-term planning): shard work like 'go bugfix yourself' needs very long context to track everything across days. The forward-momentum kit for long-horizon shards: (1) a goal document the shard maintains (objective, current state, next steps - the /goals pattern), (2) threshold-driven compaction/summarization scoped to the shard session (this is where compactionThresholdPct actually matters - unlike day-to-day chat which rolls out), (3) beads as the durable task graph across restarts. Also relevant: analysis workbench is the other context-pressure surface (observed 100k tokens in a single session reading a markdown; tool renamed from think to discourage casual use) - workbench and shard compaction knobs must stay separate from chat-lane settings. Links: shards manager (faculties/shards), z7qe.7 (self-mod scoped to shard identity), beads tools. File under future work; design before build.
notes: 2026-07-15 fold from psfn-framework-98xm.4: shard long-horizon observability belongs with the goal-document, threshold-compaction, and bead-backed session model. Preserve structured shard status sufficient to show goal/current state/next step, budget or compaction pressure, last durable checkpoint, and complete/blocked/cancelled/budget_limited partial outcome. Do not add a universal WorkerBudgetGovernor, revive action-pipe, or expose a model-facing shard control plane.

title: Extract a shared corrective agent-prompt lifecycle helper
description: Independent review of psfn-framework-9n6g found a low-severity lifecycle drift risk in src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution/agent-invocation.ts. The runtime-datetime retry around lines 751-780 and image-attachment recovery around lines 979-1015 independently register an event-bridge channel, set active-turn context, wrap the prompt in vision timeout/request/vision-tool contexts, invoke the same current prompt, and clear bridge/context state in finally. title: Design note: reflection gating and multi-admin escalation for subject-scoped privacy
description:
Evidence
- Reflections pull from ALL memory, so they can surface subject-scoped content indirectly; there is no clean per-subject boundary on a reflection.
- Multi-subject rows are a separate open case: a memory visible to A, B, both, or neither (fail-closed default recommended).

Context
- Operator decision (§10.7 iv): reflections are acknowledged as hard. The memory + profile gates (PRIV1/PRIV2/PRIV3) are the minimum for now. A multi-admin escalation gate is a FUTURE design question. This whole pattern evolved from multi-companion implementation rather than being designed — revisit deliberately later.

Scope
- Design note / decision only. Capture the open questions: (a) how reflections (which draw from all memory) should be gated across principals; (b) multi-admin escalation gate; (c) multi-subject row visibility (fail-closed default). No implementation in this bead.
- Non-goal: building any of the above now or adding a routine owner/admin non-subject path. Until a separate accepted future decision explicitly supersedes it, self/co-subject-only routine visibility and opl1.15 as the exclusive non-subject privacy break-glass remain the binding policy.

Source: working_docs/fleet-analysis-findings-20260714.md §3, §10.7 (iv). Parent epic: opl1; relates to opl1.11.

## Rationale
Reflection and multi-subject policy can expose partner data indirectly, so uncertainty must preserve the already accepted fail-closed floor rather than creating an implicit owner/admin exception.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Infer an owner/admin exception while the future design is open: rejected because opl1.15 is the exclusive current non-subject disclosure path. 2. Build an escalation workflow in this bead: rejected as explicit non-goal. 3. Hide the unresolved policy in implementation notes: rejected because a dedicated decision bead keeps the future trade-off visible without weakening present authorization.
acceptance_criteria: A written design note captures the open questions for reflection gating, multi-admin escalation, and multi-subject row visibility with fail-closed as the default. It explicitly preserves the current self/co-subject-only routine policy and opl1.15 as the exclusive non-subject disclosure path unless a later separately reviewed decision supersedes it. No code change is required to close.

title: Fatigue and charge ledgers never rotate and are whole-file re-read at boot
description:

Context
